d03ed1cd-d551-47ee-a8d2-6c2067bab8b4.title: Print Vouchers - Activity Log > Print Log > Print Log does not exist for this activity.
d03ed1cd-d551-47ee-a8d2-6c2067bab8b4.content:
Problem
There appears to be a way through the menu item "PA Print Vouchers" if we click on the "Activity" tab. Up pops an "Activity Log" similar to what we are familiar with for other reports, for example within "Post Checks" near the end of the "Payday Work" sub-menu. However, then up pops this comment: "Print Log does not exist for this activity." Why have a "Print Log" column within the "Activity Log" window if no Print Log exists? Is there a toggle within Business Rules that we need to flip to be able to see these print logs?

Resolution
Print Log Not Available in PA Print Vouchers

Issue:
Users attempting to reprint payroll vouchers through PA Print Vouchers → Activity tab encounter the message: “Print Log does not exist for this activity.” Additionally, the Print Log column is visible in the Activity Log window, leading to confusion about its availability.

Description:
Within the PA Print Vouchers screen, users can access the Activity Log similar to other processes (e.g., Post Checks). However, when attempting to use the Print Log option, the system displays a message indicating that no print log exists.

Cause:
This is expected system behavior.
- The Print Log column is part of a standard UI layout used across multiple modules.
- Not all activities generate print logs.
- PA Print Vouchers does not support print log generation, even though the column is displayed.
Resolution / Clarification:
- There is no Business Rule or configuration setting available to enable print logs for this activity.
- The system will continue to show the Print Log column, but it is non-functional for PA Print Vouchers.
Enhancement Option:
If print log functionality is required:
- It would need to be implemented via customization.
- Contact your support or development team to explore custom solutions.
Summary:
The absence of a print log in PA Print Vouchers is by design. The presence of the column does not indicate functionality for this specific activity.

a0b1edc1-24d1-4ef4-a992-8ea36fa4b564.content:
Problem
When Trying to Log In to Traverse, User Encounters “RemoteApp Disconnected” Pop-Up

Resolution
Issue:

User was unable to access/connect through RDP/application access.

Troubleshooting Performed:

- Asked the user to verify network stability/connectivity.
- Shared a new RDP file to test the same.

Customer-side IT/network restriction blocked the required access.

If similar issues occur in the future, confirm with the customer’s internal IT team whether any firewall, VPN, security policy, or access restriction is blocking the connection/application access.

dc201b07-ed66-4f0d-b162-044cc86af701.title: Multiple local tax withholdings on a salaried employee
dc201b07-ed66-4f0d-b162-044cc86af701.content:
Problem
We have recently hired a new employee that is going to be a "hybrid" employee. They are going to work 2 days a week in our physical office in one city, and the other 3 days working from home in a different city. They are going to be a salaried employee. How can I make Traverse pull one local tax for 2 days of the week and a different local tax for the other 3 days of the week? What are the steps for setting that up?

Resolution
There are two possible solutions.

- Continue to import the time as Transaction from OTW and then go into the Transactions screen and edit the Tax Group for each time ticket as necessary. It might also be possible to change the import from OTW to set this tax group id automatically.
- Don't import or use transactions, and instead set up the employee to have a special Tax Group ID composed of special tax locations where the rate is prorated based on the number of days in each location, and then let the system automatically calculate Salary.

54a5fa23-4469-4da0-8e75-b104d0cbc1d5.title: SO Module - Lock Issue
54a5fa23-4469-4da0-8e75-b104d0cbc1d5.content:
Problem
Lock Issue

Resolution
- Log in to PMTTRAVDB07
- Log in to SSMS
- Click on New Query

SELECT
blocking_session_id AS BlockingSessionID,
session_id AS BlockedSessionID,
wait_type,
wait_time,
wait_resource,
text AS QueryText
FROM sys.dm_exec_requests
CROSS APPLY sys.dm_exec_sql_text(sql_handle)
WHERE blocking_session_id <> 0;

- No need to select any database. Paste the above script in SSMS and execute it.
- It will show the locked session IDs.

- Note down the ID number and kill the locked session.
- For example, if the locked session ID is 86, simply run "kill 86;" as shown below.
- Run the script repeatedly until all locked sessions are successfully unlocked.

54248134-f0b5-484b-ad99-a68e97ef6954.title: Error when importing Account Payable entries
54248134-f0b5-484b-ad99-a68e97ef6954.content:
Problem
When attempting to upload Accounts Payable entries as 'Disbursements' via Bank Reconciliation, users may encounter an import error if there is a conflict with existing transaction IDs in the system

Resolution
Import failures may occur when the transaction IDs in the import file are already associated with pending (unposted) transactions, even if they belong to a different Bank ID. In such cases, the conflicting transactions must be posted or cleared before the import can be completed successfully.

Troubleshooting Steps:
- Navigate to BR → BR Transactions.
- Search for existing transactions that use the same Transaction IDs as those in the import file.
- Check for any pending or unposted transactions under other Bank IDs that may be using the same transaction IDs.
- Post or clear the conflicting transactions.
- Retry the import.
Additional Considerations:
- If the error "Total Debit must equal Total Credit" is encountered, verify that the import map correctly maps the Header Amount field so that the GL debit entries are properly offset by the corresponding bank account outflow.
- If the issue persists, confirm that the source file format (for example, a bank or credit card statement) has not changed. Changes such as additional columns, reordered fields, or formatting updates can affect the import process.
- Review the import map under System Manager → Import → Import Map to ensure the field mappings remain aligned with the current structure of the source file.

f1536d41-d205-4926-a880-5a4a190247f4.title: Reporting Qualified Tips and Overtime on Form W-2 (2025–2026)
f1536d41-d205-4926-a880-5a4a190247f4.content:
Problem
Reporting Qualified Tips and Overtime on Form W-2 (2025–2026)

Resolution
One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA)
The One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) provides a new above-the-line tax deduction for:
- Qualified tips
- Qualified overtime compensation
for tax years 2025 through 2028.

The deduction applies to the portion of overtime pay above the regular rate (the “overtime premium”), and to voluntary tips in certain occupations.

Overview (Effective Tax Year 2026)
Starting with Tax Year 2026, the IRS requires clearer identification of qualified overtime amounts on Form W-2 as part of updated federal tax regulations. To support this reporting, payroll configurations in TRAVERSE must be updated accordingly.
These changes ensure that qualified overtime is properly identified and reported for employee tax purposes.

What Is Changing in 2026
- Qualified overtime must be separately identified on the employee’s Form W-2.
- This information is reported for informational and compliance purposes and supports employee tax filings.
- TRAVERSE relies on earning code configuration to determine which earnings qualify as overtime for W-2 reporting.


Required Action in TRAVERSE (PA Earning Code Screen)
To ensure qualified overtime is reported correctly for 2026, the overtime earning codes must be updated in the PA Earning Code setup.
Steps to Update the Earning Code
- Navigate to the PA Earning Codes screen under the path: Payroll -> Codes Maintenance -> Earning Codes
- Open the overtime-related earning code that should qualify.
- Update the following fields:
- W-2 Box: 14
- W-2 Description: TT
- Save the changes.

Important:
Only earning codes configured with W-2 Box = 14 and W-2 Description = TT will be treated as qualified overtime for 2026 W-2 reporting.

How TRAVERSE Determines Qualified Overtime
- TRAVERSE identifies qualified overtime based on:
- The earning code configuration
- The W-2 Box and Description values
- If the earning code is not updated as noted above, the overtime amount will not be reported as qualified overtime on the W-2.


Summary
- 2026 introduces updated W-2 reporting requirements for qualified overtime
- TRAVERSE requires manual configuration to support this change
- Customers must update overtime earning codes in the PA Earning Code screen:
- W-2 Box = 14
- W-2 Description = TT
- This configuration ensures accurate and compliant W-2 reporting for 2026

c74dfd91-425d-4e0b-ad7c-099557333968.title: SM Change ID Behavior with Leading and Trailing Spaces in IDs
c74dfd91-425d-4e0b-ad7c-099557333968.content:
Problem
In Traverse, certain master data records such as Vendor IDs, Customer IDs, and Item IDs may contain hidden leading or trailing spaces (for example, ' XXX' or '1 '). These invisible spaces can cause inconsistencies and unexpected behavior in reporting, integrations, and downstream processing (such as 1099 processing, lookups, posting, or filtering).



In older builds of Traverse, when attempting to correct these IDs using the SM Change ID function, the system did not allow changing an ID directly from a value with whitespace (e.g., '1 ') to the same value without the space (e.g., '1'). This was because Traverse internally treated '1 ' (with a trailing space) as equivalent to '1' during uniqueness validation, even though the underlying database value contained whitespace.



As a result, the system would block the change due to perceived duplication, preventing direct cleanup of leading or trailing spaces using a single Change ID operation, and the user would encounter an error indicating that the target ID already exists.



This behavior has been addressed in recent Traverse builds. In the latest versions, the SM Change ID function correctly differentiates IDs with hidden whitespace and allows direct cleanup without requiring intermediate ID changes. This enhancement improves data integrity handling and simplifies master data cleanup activities.

Resolution
SM Change ID Function Overview:

The SM Change ID function performs a global update of the selected ID across the database. To prevent data conflicts, the following precautions must be followed:

- Ensure all users are logged out of the company before running Change ID.
- The system checks for active users and will block the process if users are connected.

- Access the 'SM Change ID' function under the path: Applications -> System Manager -> setup and Maintenance -> Change IDs
- Select the appropriate ID Type.
- Enter the existing ID in the From field.
- Enter the new ID in the To field.
- Repeat for additional IDs if required.
- Click OK to apply the changes.
- Use Activity to review the Change ID activity log.
- Use Reset to clear the screen if needed.



Resolution (Example Overview – Removing Leading/Trailing Spaces):

Let us consider a Vendor ID containing hidden whitespace, for example: ' 1Test' (where a leading space exists before the Vendor ID).







In Traverse, IDs with leading or trailing spaces can be directly corrected using the SM Change ID function because the system

Example:

-
From: ' 1Test'

-
To: '1Test'



However, when there are instances, where Traverse blocks the process, we can follow the below to successfully remove the hidden space. A two-step Change ID process can be performed using a temporary unique value.



Step 1: Change the ID to a Temporary Unique Value:

Use the SM Change ID function to change the Vendor ID from the value containing whitespace to a temporary unique value.

Example:

-
From: ' 1Test'

-
To: '1TestX'

Note:

- The temporary character “X” is only an example.
- Any unique character, suffix, prefix, or completely different temporary ID can be used (e.g., 1Test_TMP, 1Test_New, 1Test123).
- The temporary ID must be unique and should not already exist in the system.



This step forces Traverse to treat the ID as a completely new value and removes the hidden space during the update.



Step 2: Revert the Temporary ID to the Correct Final ID:

Once the temporary change is completed successfully, run SM Change ID again to convert the temporary ID to the final corrected ID.

Example:

- From: '1TestX'
- To: '1Test'

This second step finalizes the cleanup and ensures the Vendor ID is stored without any leading or trailing spaces.

Why This Two-Step Process Is Required:

Traverse performs internal trimming and normalization when validating IDs. Because of this behavior:

- ' 1Test' (with leading space)
- '1Test' (without space)

are treated as logically identical during uniqueness checks [In the older Builds of Traverse. However, in the later Builds with both Traverse 11.0 and Traverse 11.2, Traverse allows direct conversion]. Therefore, if Traverse does not allow a direct Change ID operation to remove whitespace, this can be done by introducing a temporary unique ID. So that Traverse is forced to recognize the record as a different entity, allowing the hidden whitespace to be fully removed.



ID Types Available in SM Change ID:

The following master data IDs can be updated using the Change ID function:

- Item ID
- Vendor ID
- Customer ID
- Department ID
- Employee ID
- GL Account ID
- Asset ID
- Sales Rep ID

Recommendations / Best Practices:

- Always perform Change ID operations in a maintenance window with no active users.
- Avoid leading or trailing spaces when creating master records.
- Periodically audit IDs using SQL queries to detect hidden whitespace.
- Use a temporary unique ID (e.g., appending + or _TMP) when cleaning up whitespace issues.
- Validate downstream processes (AP, AR, reporting, integrations) after ID corrections.

3481aa0d-7021-4ece-b4e5-6abc61e6676a.title: 1099-nec Not Pulling For A Vendor
3481aa0d-7021-4ece-b4e5-6abc61e6676a.content:
Problem
A vendor does not appear on the 1099-NEC form during AP 1099 Processing, even though the vendor is correctly set up as a 1099 vendor and added to the 1099 Processing screen.

Resolution
The vendor’s total reportable payment amount does not meet the required monetary threshold for 1099-NEC reporting.
For 1099-NEC, the standard IRS reporting threshold is:
- $600 or more in total payments for the calendar year

If the vendor’s cumulative payments are below $600, the system will:
- Exclude the vendor from 1099-NEC output, or

- Display the vendor with blank / zero amounts, resulting in no 1099-NEC being printed

This is expected system behavior and aligns with IRS reporting rules.

dea23e50-a114-4c8d-9e27-cb7a75b78df8.title: How to find the list of 'Vendor' records with leading spaces through SQL Query?
dea23e50-a114-4c8d-9e27-cb7a75b78df8.content:
Problem
How to find the list of 'Vendor' records with leading spaces through SQL Query?

Resolution
In Traverse, master records such as Vendor IDs may sometimes contain hidden leading spaces (for example, ' 1Test'). These spaces are not visible in the UI but can cause multiple operational issues, including:
- Errors during 1099 processing
- Issues with lookups and filtering
- Duplicate or mismatched Vendor IDs
- Problems in integrations and reporting
- Unexpected behavior in posting and transactions
Since Traverse trims or normalizes IDs in some validations, these hidden spaces can be difficult to detect through the application interface. Therefore, a direct database-level method is required to identify Vendor records that contain leading spaces.

Identifying Vendor Records with Leading Spaces Using SQL:
To identify Vendor records that contain leading spaces in the Vendor ID, the following SQL query can be executed directly against the Traverse database:
SELECT *
FROM tblApVendor
WHERE VendorID LIKE ' %'

Explanation of the Query:
- tblApVendor → The Accounts Payable Vendor master table in Traverse.
- VendorID LIKE ' %' → This condition searches for Vendor IDs where the first character is a space, followed by any characters (% wildcard).
This query returns all Vendor records where the Vendor ID begins with one or more whitespace characters.


Post-Query Actions:
Once the affected Vendor records are identified:
- Review the Vendor IDs returned by the query.
- Confirm whether the leading spaces are unintended.
- Use the SM Change ID function to correct the Vendor IDs (Kindly refer the article #000113806, URL: SM-Change-ID-Behavior-with-Leading-and-Trailing-Spaces-in-IDs).
- Validate downstream processes such as: - 1099 processing
- AP transactions
- Reporting and integrations


Recommendation / Best Practices:
- Periodically audit master records using SQL queries to detect hidden whitespace.
- Avoid entering IDs with leading or trailing spaces during record creation.
- Perform cleanup activities in a maintenance window with all users logged out.
- Maintain documentation of ID corrections to avoid mismatches in historical data.

bb851640-aef2-495c-b9b3-be6ba8be6706.title: ACH File for US Vendors Not Loading Address Information
bb851640-aef2-495c-b9b3-be6ba8be6706.content:
Problem
The issue of ACH files for US vendors not including address information when generated from AP > Pay Invoice > Create ACH File is due to the use of a customized assembly (`Kal.Business.PayInvoice`) for the CIBC\_USD export layout

Overview
This article explains the difference between the CIBC_USD and CIBC_CAD export layouts in Traverse, specifically focusing on the assemblies used and the impact this has on support and change requests.
CIBC_USD Export Layout
In the CIBC_USD export layout, the Assembly configured is:
- Kal.Business.PayInvoice

This assembly is a customized assembly, meaning it is not part of the standard Traverse (base) application. Since this is a customization, any review, troubleshooting, or modification related to this layout requires deeper analysis.
As a result:
- The layout must be reviewed by the Services team

- Any changes or enhancements will be treated as a billable Services engagement

CIBC_CAD Export Layout
In comparison, the CIBC_CAD export layout uses the following assembly:
- Traverse.Business.PayInvoice

This is a standard (base) assembly provided by Traverse. Layouts using standard assemblies typically fall under normal product support, provided no additional customizations are involved.
Key Difference Summary
LayoutAssembly UsedTypeSupport HandlingCIBC_USDKal.Business.PayInvoiceCustomizedServices (Billable)CIBC_CADTraverse.Business.PayInvoiceStandardProduct Support
Conclusion
Because the CIBC_USD export layout relies on a customized assembly, any investigation or modification related to this layout must be handled by the Services team and will be considered a billable engagement.
The CIBC_CAD layout, on the other hand, uses a standard Traverse assembly and does not involve customization.

6989ecce-c4e5-4ebb-8852-2e04e154c68f.title: Resolving InstallerX (IX) Application Down Issue – Crew2
6989ecce-c4e5-4ebb-8852-2e04e154c68f.content:
Problem
[Huzaifa Bilal]
Hello,

Our users cannot log into IX application. If they sign out, it does not let them back in.

User have tried resetting their passwords and cleared their browser cache, but it did not work. It’s happening at a larger scale and is currently all our users. See the errors in the screenshot below.

Resolution
KB Article: Resolving InstallerX (IX) Application Down Issue – Crew2
Overview
This Knowledge Base article outlines the steps to troubleshoot and resolve an issue where the InstallerX (IX) application is down for the Crew2 customer. The issue is typically resolved by recycling the application pool and restarting the IIS site associated with InstallerX.
Prerequisites
- Access to the customer’s installation survey to identify IIS server details
- Administrative access to the Crew2 Application Server
- Access to Internet Information Services (IIS) Manager
Procedure
Step 1: Identify and Log in to the IIS Server
- Refer to the customer’s installation survey to obtain the IIS/Application Server details.
- Log in to the Crew2 Application Server using administrative credentials.
Step 2: Verify InstallerX Sites
- Open Internet Information Services (IIS) Manager.
- In the left navigation pane, expand the server name.
- Click on Sites.
- Locate the InstallerX sites for Crew2:
- installerx-crew2
- ix-crew2
- Note that both sites are mapped to the same InstallerX application.
Step 3: Validate Website Access
- Select one InstallerX sites.
- Click Browse (or “Browse Website”) to attempt to access the site.
- Try logging in to confirm whether the application is accessible.
- If the site does not load or login fails, proceed to the next step. And do the same with another site
Step 4: Recycle the Application Pool
- In IIS Manager, click on Application Pools.
- Locate the application pool of the site that is not working which is associated with the Crew2 InstallerX application.
- Right-click the application pool and select Recycle.
Step 5: Restart the IIS Site
- Navigate back to Sites.
- Select the InstallerX site (installerx-crew2 or ix-crew2).
- Click Restart.
Step 6: Validate Application Access
- After recycling the application pool and restarting the site, browse the InstallerX site again.
- Attempt to log in to confirm the application is accessible.
- In most cases, the issue is resolved after these steps.
Post-Resolution
- Confirm with the customer that InstallerX access has been restored.
- Update the support or Salesforce case with the actions performed and resolution details.

6ec4697c-1a41-4713-9d68-3328b8596361.title: Time Card Notification Emails Not Delivered to External Email Domains (Gmail/Comcast)
6ec4697c-1a41-4713-9d68-3328b8596361.content:
Problem
Customers reported that time card notification emails were not being delivered to employees using external personal email domains such as:
- Gmail

- Comcast

However:
- Emails were successfully delivered to company-domain email addresses.

- Previously affected users had been receiving notifications without issue.

- The issue started recently.

- Resetting employee email fields did not resolve the issue.

- Changing the employee email to a company-domain address immediately restored delivery.

This indicated that the notification process was functioning correctly, but emails sent to external domains were not being accepted.

Resolution
- All employees using personal external email addresses were affected.

- Only employees with company-hosted email accounts received notifications.

- Payroll/time tracking compliance was impacted because employees were not notified about submitted or required time cards.

- Workaround (switching to company email) was not viable long-term.

Root Cause :
The issue was caused by missing or improperly configured email authentication records in Azure DNS:
- SPF record not properly configured

- DKIM record not properly configured

Because external providers (Gmail, Comcast) enforce strict email authentication policies, they rejected or filtered messages that failed SPF/DKIM validation.
Company-domain mail systems were less restrictive, which is why internal emails continued to work.

Resolution:
The SaaS team updated the Azure DNS configuration by adding:
- Proper SPF records

- Proper DKIM records

After updating DNS:
- Test emails were successfully delivered to Gmail accounts.

- Customer confirmed external users received timecard notifications.

- Issue resolved.



Workaround (Prior to Resolution):
Changing the employee email address to a company-domain email temporarily restored delivery.
However, this was not a viable long-term solution.

80080068-7d0d-4089-810b-9afcfb5319be.title: Income Statement Prior Period Totals Displaying Incorrectly Due to Fiscal Period Configuration
80080068-7d0d-4089-810b-9afcfb5319be.content:
Problem
In some cases, the Income Statement (IS) may display incorrect or zero values for prior period totals. This issue can occur when the number of fiscal periods configured in the company setup does not align with the periods where transactions were actually posted.
When the report is run, the system references the configured fiscal periods, and if the report looks at a fiscal period that contains no transactions, prior period totals may appear as zero or incorrect values.

Resolution
Symptoms
Users may notice the following:
- Prior period totals on the Income Statement appear incorrect or zero

- Transactions exist for the expected period but are not reflected in the report

- The report appears correct for some companies but not others

- The report may be referencing a fiscal period with no posted transactions

Cause
The issue typically occurs when companies have different fiscal period configurations.
Example scenario:
- Some companies are configured with 12 fiscal periods

- Another company may be configured with 13 fiscal periods

If transactions were posted in Period 12, but the system expects Period 13, the report may attempt to retrieve prior period data from Period 13, which may not contain any transactions.
This results in incorrect or zero prior period totals.
Resolution
Step 1 – Verify Fiscal Period Configuration
Check the fiscal period setup for the company.
Navigate to:
System Manager → Company Setup → Period ConversionReview the number of fiscal periods configured for the company.
Step 2 – Confirm Posting Period
Verify which fiscal period contains the transactions.
This can be confirmed by reviewing:
- GL transaction history

- Journal entries

- Posting period information

Step 3 – Run the Report for the Correct Fiscal Period
When running the Income Statement, select the fiscal period where transactions were actually posted.
Example:
Fiscal Period: 12
Fiscal Year: 2025
Running the report for the correct fiscal period will display the expected totals.
Important Notes
- The Income Statement references configured fiscal periods, not only periods with transactions.

- If a fiscal period exists but has no transactions, reports referencing that period may display zero totals.

- Differences in fiscal period configurations across companies can lead to inconsistent reporting results.

d7c09e9a-7a11-4afb-a592-99d88c31aeb9.title: Two Records Displayed in Sales Order Detail After Pick and Pack in Warehouse Management
d7c09e9a-7a11-4afb-a592-99d88c31aeb9.content:
Problem
After creating a Sales Order and completing the Pick and Pack process in Warehouse Management (WM), users may notice that two records appear in the Sales Order Detail view instead of a single record.
At first glance, this may appear to be a duplicate entry or a system issue. However, this behavior is expected and part of the system design. The system intentionally creates two records to maintain an accurate history of inventory movement and order processing.

Resolution
Symptoms
Users may observe the following behavior:
- After completing Pick and Pack, two records appear in the Sales Order Detail popup window

- The first record displays:
- Quantity Filled = 0

- Default Bin

- The second record displays:
- Updated Filled Quantity

- Work Bin or Pack Bin

This may appear as if the system has created a duplicate record.
Cause
This behavior occurs due to the design of the Warehouse Management pick and pack process.
When a sales order is processed through WM:
- The system retains the original sales order record showing the initial state of the order.

- A second record is generated once the pick and pack process is completed to reflect the updated inventory movement.

This allows the system to:
- Track the original order state

- Record the actual picked and packed quantities

- Capture bin movement during the warehouse process

- Maintain a complete transaction history

Behavior Explanation
RecordDescriptionRecord 1Original Sales Order line with 0 Qty Filled and Default BinRecord 2Updated record created after Pick and Pack, showing Filled Qty and Work/Pack Bin
The second record reflects the actual warehouse activity, while the first record preserves the original order state.
Steps to Observe the Behavior
- Create a new Sales Order.

- Release the order for Warehouse Management processing.

- Complete the Pick and Pack process.

- Return to the Sales Order screen.

- Click the Detail button.

Two records will appear in the Detail popup view.
The second record will display the correct picked and packed information.


This behavior:
- Is working as designed

- Does not indicate a system defect

- Does not affect order processing

- Does not create additional workload

- Ensures accurate tracking of warehouse operations

Additional Notes
- The difference between the records typically reflects inventory movement between bins.

- The Work Bin or Pack Bin shown in the second record depends on how the pick and pack process was performed.

- This design helps maintain traceability of warehouse transactions.

1b1886b3-03ca-498d-a862-87a4f6796c48.title: Configuring Custom Clock-In / Clock-Out Rounding for Specific Employee Groups Using Punch Overrides (On-Time Web)
1b1886b3-03ca-498d-a862-87a4f6796c48.content:
Problem
In On-Time Web, rounding rules are typically configured at the company level under Punch Settings. Because of this, the system does not natively support assigning different rounding rules to different employee groups.
However, a similar outcome can be achieved by using Punch Overrides configured at the Supervisor Group or Employee level. These overrides allow administrators to define time-based rules that adjust punch times within specific ranges.
This approach can be used to simulate different rounding behaviors for selected employees or groups.

Resolution
Scenario
A customer requested the ability to configure different rounding rules for different groups of employees, for example:
GroupClock-In RuleClock-Out RuleClientsRound to previous quarter hourRound to next quarter hourStaffContinue using default company rounding rules
Since rounding rules are company-wide, this must be handled using Punch Overrides.
Resolution – Using Punch Overrides
Step 1 – Navigate to Punch Overrides
- Open On-Time Web.

- Navigate to:

Home → Settings → Punch OverridesThis page allows administrators to configure custom punch adjustment rules.
Step 2 – Select Policy Type
Choose where the override should apply.
Available options include:
- Employee

- Supervisor Group

- Department (if available in configuration)

Example:
Policy Type: Employee
Option: Select the specific employee
Step 3 – Configure the Punch Override Rule
Define the rule parameters.
Example configuration:
FieldExample ValuePunch TypeINStart Time07:55 AMEnd Time08:05 AMOverride Time08:00 AMStatusEnabled
This means:
- If an employee clocks in between 07:55 AM and 08:05 AM

- The system will override the punch time to 08:00 AM

Step 4 – Create Multiple Time Ranges
To replicate quarter-hour rounding, you must create multiple override ranges.
Example for Clock-In rounding to previous quarter hour:
Start TimeEnd TimeOverride Time07:4608:0007:4508:0108:1508:0008:1608:3008:15
Example for Clock-Out rounding to next quarter hour:
Start TimeEnd TimeOverride Time01:4602:0002:0002:0102:1502:1502:1602:3002:30
Each range must be configured as a separate Punch Override rule.
Step 5 – Enable the Override
- Ensure Status = Enabled

- Click Save

Repeat these steps for all required time intervals.

Result
After configuration:
- Selected employees or groups will follow custom rounding behavior.

- Other employees will continue using the default company rounding rules.

This allows organizations to simulate different rounding rules for different groups without modifying the global company rounding configuration.

2f0bc5d1-b7a2-4816-8570-ee5ed0596460.title: Why do we get the warning 'Reports have been printed for batch (<Batch>). Do you wish to continue?' while saving a Transaction?

------------------------------

Reports have been printed for batch (######). Do you wish to continue?

Resolution
Overview

The warning message: Reports have been printed for batch (######). Do you wish to continue?

typically appears while saving an Accounts Payable (AP) or Accounts Receivable (AR) transaction within an existing batch.



This message is informational in nature and is triggered because Traverse detects that reports (such as journals) associated with the specified batch have already been printed.



Why This Message Appears?

Traverse tracks whether required batch reports (e.g., Purchase Journal, Edit List, etc.) have been printed.

If we attempt to:

- Add new transactions
- Modify transactions
- Save changes

after reports for that batch have already been printed, the system generates this warning to alert the user that the batch has already undergone a reporting step.

This prevents accidental posting of modified data after reports have been finalized.

Is This an Error?

No. This is a warning message, not a system error. It does not indicate data corruption or transaction failure.

Recommended Action:

If changes to the batch are intentional, you may safely:

-
Click “Yes” to proceed with saving the transaction.

However, it is recommended that we:

-
Reprint the relevant journal (e.g., Purchase Journal)

-
Review the updated report before posting

This ensures that the printed documentation accurately reflects the final transaction data.

Exception Scenario:

There may be certain exceptional situations where this warning appears even when the transaction being created is the first entry in the batch.

In such cases, the warning may occur because the Journal status for that specific batch was previously marked as “Printed.” If the Traverse session did not properly end during the initial posting, there are chances, the 'Journal status' did not reset after the posting. This makes the journal status set to Printed (even without any transactions currently in the batch), and Traverse will still recognize it as having been reported and will trigger the warning message upon saving a new transaction.

Resolution Steps:

To resolve this condition:

-
Navigate to: Accounts Payable -> Setup and Maintenance -> AP Transaction Batch Codes

-
Locate the appropriate batch.

-
Review the journal status fields:

-
If the warning occurs while creating an Invoice, review the status of the Purchases Journal.

-
If the warning occurs while creating a Debit Memo, review the status of the Miscellaneous Debits Journal.

-
If the relevant journal status is marked as “Printed”, change (toggle) the status to “Unprinted.”

-
Click Save.

After updating the journal status to Unprinted, the user should no longer receive the warning message when saving the transaction.

803b459f-0fb9-46da-a911-e460b1bea55b.title: Resolving "Modifying a locked document is not allowed" Error for Sales Orders
803b459f-0fb9-46da-a911-e460b1bea55b.content:
Problem
Customers may encounter an error message "Modifying a locked document is not allowed" when attempting to save, update, or calculate taxes on a Sales Order

Resolution
Title: Error: “Modifying a locked document is not allowed” when saving Sales Order
Overview
Users may encounter an error when attempting to save, update, or calculate taxes on a Sales Order. The system prevents modifications because the document is locked.
This article explains the cause of the issue, how to verify the source of the lock, and the possible resolutions and workarounds.
Error Message
Users may see the following error when saving a Sales Order:
Modifying a locked document is not allowed.
Document 87084689164151 is locked. Modification is not allowed.
Edition = Global
Build = 25353
User = STERBallard
LicenseServer = pmttravrds09
Culture = English (United States)
DefaultCompID = STE
SysDb = SYSSTE
SessionID = STE-2W8WJD4
MachineName = PMTTRAVRDS09
Modifying a locked document is not allowed.
Document 87084689164151 is locked. Modification is not allowed. (TRAVERSE.Business.SalesOrder)
Program Location:
at TRAVERSE.Business.SalesOrder.TransactionHeader.CalculateTaxes()
at TRAVERSE.Business.SalesOrder.TransactionHeader.CalculateTotals(Boolean raiseEvent)
at TRAVERSE.Client.SalesOrder.TransactionHeaderControl.OnSavingRow(CancelEventArgs args)
Cause
This issue typically occurs when the transaction has already been committed or reported through Avalara for tax reporting.
When a document is committed in Avalara, it may become locked, preventing any further modifications from within TRAVERSE.
Because Avalara operates as an external tax service, TRAVERSE does not have visibility into the Avalara account to determine whether the document has been committed.
Verification Steps
To confirm if Avalara is causing the document lock:
- Log in to the Avalara Admin Console.

- Search for the document number referenced in the error message.

- Check the status of the transaction.

- Verify whether the document is marked as Committed.

Resolution Options
Option 1: Contact Avalara Support
If the document is committed in Avalara, the first step is to contact Avalara Support and request verification.
They may be able to determine whether the document can be unlocked or adjusted.
However, in many cases:
- If the transaction has already been reported and filed, Avalara may not allow it to be unlocked or modified.

Option 2: TRAVERSE Workaround
If Avalara confirms the document cannot be unlocked, a workaround may be required within TRAVERSE.
In previous cases, this was addressed by implementing:
- Custom scripting (TSMX)

- Additional processing steps to allow the order to be recreated and processed

If needed, support can assist with evaluating and implementing this workaround.
Additional Workaround (Deleting the Sales Order)
If the Sales Order needs to be removed, you can attempt to delete it through the user interface by following these steps:
Steps to Delete the Sales Order
- Navigate to:  Sales Order → Transactions → SO

- Query and open the relevant Sales Order.

- Go to the Line tab.

- Open the Detail window for the specific line item.

- In the Detail window:
- Clear or remove the relevant fields (such as Bin or Lot)

- Use the (-) button at the bottom to remove the values.

- After clearing the fields, attempt to delete the line item.

- Once all line items are removed, you should then be able to delete the entire Sales Order.

f534e97e-6453-45a1-9f2e-9b89fb080bb6.title: CR – Global Design Studio Changes Not Reflected in Online Work Order Report
f534e97e-6453-45a1-9f2e-9b89fb080bb6.content:
Problem
In Traverse ERP (v11.2, Build 24138), changes made to the Work Order Report in Global Design Studio are only reflected in the batch printed report, but not in the online report.
Specifically:
- Modifications made via Design Studio → BM Work Order Report are visible when using:
- Bill of Material → Work Orders → Work Order Report → Preview

- However, the same changes are not reflected when using:
- Bill of Material → Work Orders → Issue Work Order (Online Report)


Bug reference:
Bug 85362: CR - Changes made in Global Design Studio affect only the Batch Printed Report and not the online report - 03777310 - DEV-221901
Bug 85362: CR - Changes made in Global Design Studio affect only the Batch Printed Report and not the online report - 03777310 - DEV-221901

Resolution
Cause
The issue was due to a design inconsistency in the application, where:
- The batch Work Order report and the online Work Order report were implemented as two separate report classes

- Although both reports appear identical, they are not linked to the same report definition

- Changes made in Global Design Studio apply only to the batch report, and do not propagate to the online report


Resolution
This issue has been resolved in Build 25031.
- The system has been updated to ensure that both batch and online Work Order reports utilize the same report definition

- Changes made in Global Design Studio are now consistently reflected across:
- Batch printed reports

- Online Work Order reports


Steps to Reproduce
- Navigate to Design Studio → Report Designer.

- Select BM → Work Order → Work Order Report and make changes.

- Go to Bill of Material → Work Orders → Work Order Report → Preview.
- Changes are reflected.

- Go to Bill of Material → Work Orders → Issue Work Order.

- Select Item ID, location, and quantity, and issue the Work Order.

Result:
- Online Work Order report does not reflect the changes made in Design Studio.



Action Required: Customers experiencing this issue in earlier builds (e.g., 24138) are advised to upgrade to Build 25031 or later to resolve the behavior.


Screenshots below,

In Design Studio, navigate to Report Designer → BM → Work Order → Work Order Report, and make the required changes, then save the report.



Navigate to Bill of Material → Work Orders → Work Order Report → Preview, where the changes made in Design Studio are correctly reflected.

However, when navigating to Bill of Material → Work Orders → Issue Work Order, selecting the Item ID, location, and quantity to build, and issuing the Work Order, the online Work Order report does not reflect the changes made in Design Studio.

c3bfd854-bca9-4381-9b61-f1c74ace6aed.title: AutoLunch Records in Piecework Report
c3bfd854-bca9-4381-9b61-f1c74ace6aed.content:
Problem
Users may observe incorrect lunch entries in the Piecework report, such as:
- AutoLunch appearing for clients who did not work through lunch (e.g., left at noon)

- Duplicate or multiple lunch entries for the same day

- Lunch entries persisting even after related time entries are deleted

Cause
This issue is caused by orphaned AutoLunch records in the tblItIndPiecework table.
Expected Behavior
- When a time entry crosses the lunch threshold, the system:
- Creates an AutoLunch record

- Links it to the time entry using:
- HasAutoLunch = 1

- AutoLunchIdent (reference to AutoLunch row)

- If the time entry is deleted, the corresponding AutoLunch record should also be deleted.

Problem Behavior
- The system (CRI process) deletes time entry records without deleting the linked AutoLunch record

- This leaves behind orphaned AutoLunch rows

- These orphaned rows:
- Have IsAutoLunch = 1

- Are not referenced by any time entry

- Cannot be deleted through the UI or standard processes

Resolution
Identification of Orphaned Records

Run the following query to identify orphaned AutoLunch records:

SELECT * FROM tblItIndPiecework WHERE pwdate > '2026-01-01' AND IsAutoLunch = 1 AND ident NOT IN ( SELECT AutoLunchIdent FROM tblItIndPiecework WHERE pwdate > '2026-01-01' AND HasAutoLunch = 1 );

Result
- Returns AutoLunch records that:
- Exist independently

- Are not linked to any valid time entry

Resolution
Important
- These records cannot be removed through the application

- Must be handled via SQL script

- Take a full database backup before proceeding

Step 1: Verify Records
Review the output of the identification query to confirm:
- Dates

- Users

- No valid parent time entry exists

Step 2: Delete Orphaned AutoLunch Records

DELETE FROM tblItIndPiecework WHERE pwdate > '2026-01-01' AND IsAutoLunch = 1 AND ident NOT IN ( SELECT AutoLunchIdent FROM tblItIndPiecework WHERE pwdate > '2026-01-01' AND HasAutoLunch = 1   );
Step 3: Validate Fix

- Re-run the identification query → should return zero rows

- Re-generate Piecework report → verify:
- No duplicate lunch entries

- No phantom AutoLunch entries

Prevention / Recommendation
- The underlying issue is caused by improper deletion logic in CRI

- Recommended actions:
- Review CRI process handling time entry deletions

- Ensure:
- When a time entry is deleted, its AutoLunchIdent record is also deleted

- Consider adding:
- A cleanup job to periodically remove orphaned AutoLunch records

Impact
- Affects reporting accuracy

- Does not impact raw data integrity outside lunch calculations

- Limited to records where improper deletion occurred

Summary
Orphaned AutoLunch records occur when linked time entries are deleted incorrectly. These records must be identified and removed via SQL to restore accurate Piecework reporting.

95fd467f-4048-47db-8b95-33a1e0bd6342.title: How to Address Kentucky State Unemployment Tax Table Wage Limit Updates

Kentucky State Unemployment Insurance (SUI) wage limit did not update to $12,000 for 2026. System continued using previous limit ($11,700), resulting in incorrect Q1 SUI calculations.


possible errors
- State tax not updated

KB Article: Updating Expired Azure Communication Service Secret for Email Integration in Traverse

This Knowledge Base article outlines the steps to resolve issues caused by an expired Azure Communication Service (ACS) secret used for email integration in Traverse. When the secret expires, email functionality within Traverse (Document Delivery) will fail.

Issue Description
Customer reports:
- Emails cannot be sent from Traverse
- Azure Communication Service (ACS) secret has expired

6e833682-8a11-4cf9-b9a7-1cc17356761b.content:
Problem
Overview
This article explains how to identify available Form IDs in Aptean Traverse and how to use them in API calls such as GET and PUT for Form Numbers.

Prerequisites
- Access to Traverse application

- Access to Traverse Global API (Swagger UI)

- Valid Company ID

Resolution
How to Identify Available Form IDs
Step 1: Navigate in Traverse Application
- Go to: System Manager (SM) → Form Numbers

Step 2: Review the Form ID List
The Form Numbers screen displays all configured Form IDs in the system.
Example Form IDs
Based on the system configuration, some available Form IDs include:
- AR INVOICE

- BACCDocNum

- BANK:AMPR

- BANK:MAIN

- PAChecks

- Po Order

- PROF INV

- SD INVOICE

- SO INVOICE

- SO PACK

- SO PICK

- SO QUOTE

- SO RMA

- WM Pack

- WMReceip

These Form IDs are used to control document numbering for different modules.
How to Use Form ID in API
Example: GET Form Number
Step 1: Open Swagger UI
- Navigate to: http://localhost/TraverseGlobalAPI/swagger/ui/index

Step 2: Select Form Numbers → GET
Step 3: Provide Parameters
- id: SO INVOICE (example)

- Company ID: Required

Step 4: Execute
Sample Response
[
{
"id": "SO INVOICE",
"next_number": 10500
}
]
How to Update Next Number (PUT)
Example Payload
[
{
"id": "SO INVOICE",
"next_number": 11000
}
]
Steps
- Select PUT method

- Click Try it out

- Enter Company ID

- Paste JSON payload

- Click Execute



Notes
- Form IDs must match exactly as shown in Traverse (case and spacing sensitive)

- If an invalid Form ID is passed, the API will return an empty response

- Changes to next_number impact document sequencing and should be tested in a non-production environment

- Not all Form IDs should be modified without understanding their usage

Example Use Case
Using Form ID: SO INVOICE
- Purpose: Controls numbering for Sales Invoices

- API Usage:
- GET → Retrieve current next number

- PUT → Update next number if required


Users who are already logged into the Traverse application may need to close and reopen the application for the updated Form Number changes to be reflected correctly in the UI. Existing sessions may continue displaying cached or previously loaded values until the application is restarted.

Impact on Users and Locked Forms
When a user modifies the "Locked" status or configuration of a Form Number within the System Manager module in Traverse, it can directly impact the ability of other users to perform tasks associated with that specific form.
Effect on Other Users
If a form (such as SO INVOICE or SO PACK) becomes locked, commonly due to an unexpected program termination, screen closure during processing, or a system interruption, other users may be unable to process related documents.
Since the Form Numbers configuration is maintained globally within Traverse, a lock on a specific form impacts all users across the environment, not only the user who originally accessed the form.
Recommended Resolution
If users encounter an "in use" error message, the issue is typically caused by a stale or stuck lock that must be cleared manually by an administrator or a user with sufficient permissions.
Steps to Clear the Lock
- Navigate to:

System Manager → Company Setup → Form Numbers

- Locate the affected Form ID.

- Verify whether the Locked checkbox is enabled.

- If enabled, uncheck the Locked option and save the changes.

- Once the lock is cleared, affected users should be able to resume processing immediately.

Resolution
Expand "System Databases"
You should see tempdb

Expand Types
Then User Defined data types

pDec will be missing

Issue Summary:
The report issue was traced to a missing user-defined datatype (pDec) in the tempdb database. While the report worked correctly against a local copy of the database, the Cloud environment was missing the required datatype under tempdb > Types > User Defined Data Types. This occurred because the SQL environment was not prepared correctly during the Cloud migration. The TRAVERSE databases were restored directly, but no SYS database was ever created in that environment, so the required TRAVERSE user-defined datatypes were never added to tempdb.
Resolution:
The fix should be straightforward. Using TRAVERSE Server Manager (TSM), log in to the SQL instance and attempt to connect using a SYS database name that does not currently exist (for example, SYSXXX). TSM will prompt to create the database—allow the process to complete. During SYS database creation, TSM checks tempdb for the required TRAVERSE user-defined datatypes and automatically creates any that are missing, including pDec.
Once the process is complete, the newly created SYS database can simply be deleted, as the primary goal is to populate tempdb with the necessary TRAVERSE datatypes.

02039457-8fc1-4232-b3bc-a254d0f357bd.title: Resolving Azure VM Login/Boot Issues Related to Missing Hyper-V ACPI Registry Entries
02039457-8fc1-4232-b3bc-a254d0f357bd.content:
Problem
This article documents the resolution steps used when an Azure Virtual Machine becomes inaccessible or experiences login/boot issues due to missing or corrupted Hyper-V virtual hardware registration entries within the Windows registry.

In this scenario, the server could not be accessed normally because required virtual device enumeration entries were missing under the ACPI registry structure.

Cause
The issue was caused by missing or improperly registered Hyper-V ACPI device entries within the Windows registry.

Specifically, the following registry entries were not being enumerated correctly:

- MSFT1000
- MSFT1002

These entries are required for proper initialization of certain virtual hardware components used by Azure virtual machines.

Resolution
1. Launch SYSTEM Command Prompt

Run:

psexec -i -s cmd.exe
This opens a command prompt running under the Local SYSTEM account.

2. Create Missing MSFT1000 Registry Entry

Run:

reg copy "HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Enum\ACPI\VMBus" "HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Enum\ACPI\MSFT1000" /s /f
3. Create Missing MSFT1002 Registry Entry

Run:

reg copy "HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Enum\ACPI\Hyper_V_Gen_Counter_V1" "HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Enum\ACPI\MSFT1002" /s
4. Reboot the Server

After the registry entries are created successfully, reboot the server.

Validation

After reboot:

- Verify RDP access is restored.
- Confirm the VM boots normally.
- Validate application services start successfully.
- Review Event Viewer for any remaining Hyper-V or ACPI-related errors.

a5c288ef-a3b9-4184-9bc7-4569442e5622.title: Creating and Configuring a Tax Location Group in TRAVERSE
a5c288ef-a3b9-4184-9bc7-4569442e5622.content:
Problem
This article explains how to create a new Tax Location Group and assign it to a vendor or customer. Tax Location Groups are used to group one or more Tax Locations for tax calculation and reporting.

Resolution
Prerequisites
Before creating a Tax Location Group, ensure the required Tax Location(s) have already been created.
Note: If you are adding a new state (for example, New York), you must first create the corresponding Tax Location before it can be added to a Tax Location Group.

Navigation
System Manager > Tax Setup > Tax Location Groups
Steps to Create a Tax Location Group
Navigate to:
System Manager > Tax Setup > Tax Location Groups
Click New on the toolbar to create a new Tax Location Group.
Enter the following information:
- Tax Group ID

- Description

- Type
- Regular

- Use

- Extended1

- Extended2


Reporting Method
- Combined

- Separate

(Optional) If you want to base the new group on an existing one, select a value from the Copy From dropdown.
Select the appropriate Tax Location ID for each tax authority level.
Note: Only Tax Location IDs that have already been created are available for selection.
If your tax structure requires Tax on Tax, enable the appropriate Tax on Level checkboxes.
If using Avalara Tax Service, enable Use with Tax Service and enter the appropriate Tax Location Account Number.
Click Save to save the Tax Location Group.

Assign the Tax Location Group
After creating the Tax Location Group:
- Open the appropriate Vendor or Customer record.

- Locate the Tax Location Group field.

- Select the newly created Tax Location Group.

- Save the record.

Editing a Tax Location Group
- Navigate to:

System Manager > Tax Setup > Tax Location Groups
- Select the Tax Group ID.

- Make the required changes.

- Click Save.


Deleting a Tax Location Group
- Open the Tax Location Group.

- Click Delete.

- Confirm the deletion.

Note: A Tax Location Group cannot be deleted if it is currently assigned to a customer or vendor.

Important Notes
- Tax Locations must exist before they can be added to a Tax Location Group.

- If only one Tax Location (e.g., NJ) is available, create the additional Tax Location (e.g., NY) first.

- A Tax Location cannot be deleted while it is associated with a Tax Location Group.

- A Tax Location Group cannot be deleted while assigned to customers or vendors.

9a7a4a03-71a4-4ecc-9910-8b246c54f806.title: How to bring Hidden Dialog Box Back to the Screen in an RDP Session
9a7a4a03-71a4-4ecc-9910-8b246c54f806.content:
Problem
While working in Traverse through a Remote Desktop (RDP) session, a dialog box (such as Save, Open, Print, or another pop-up window) may appear to be missing. The application becomes unresponsive because the hidden dialog box is waiting for user input.
Symptoms
- Traverse appears frozen or unresponsive.

- Clicking within Traverse does not have any effect.

- The application cannot be minimized or closed normally.

- A dialog box is open but not visible on the current screen.

Cause
This issue typically occurs when:
- Multiple monitors are used and the dialog box opens on a monitor that is no longer connected.

- The monitor arrangement has changed since the RDP session was established.

- Screen resolution or display scaling settings have changed.

- The RDP session was previously used with a different monitor configuration.

As a result, the dialog box opens outside the visible display area.

Resolution
Method 1: Move the Hidden Window Using Keyboard Shortcut
- Connect to Traverse using the downloaded RDP file.

- When the hidden dialog box is expected to be open, press:
Windows + Shift + Left Arrow
or
Windows + Shift + Right Arrow

- Continue pressing the shortcut until the hidden dialog box appears on the active monitor.

Method 2: Disconnect and Reconnect with Correct Display Configuration
- Close the RDP session.

- Ensure the desired monitors are connected and enabled.

- Reopen the downloaded RDP file.

- Log back into Traverse and retry the action.

Method 3: Adjust Screen Resolution
- Disconnect the RDP session.

- Edit the RDP display settings or resize the RDP window.

- Reconnect to the session.

- Verify whether the dialog box is now visible.

4124ad16-3fd1-470c-b4f0-886097b15212.content:

TITLE: Traverse Global Design Studio
------------------------------

You do not have permission to run Design Studio in company TST

&OK

fb648254-2434-414a-af23-362a82166cad.title: Converting an Existing Payroll Employee to an IPM/ITS Individual (Consumer)
fb648254-2434-414a-af23-362a82166cad.content:
Problem
A client may have an employee who was previously set up as a standard Payroll employee (for example, an hourly staff member) and later returns in a different capacity as an Individual/Consumer who will be paid through ITS/IPM (such as a piece-rate worker).
When attempting to create a new employee record for the individual, Traverse prevents the creation because the Social Security Number (SSN) already exists on another employee record.

Cause
Cause
Traverse allows only one Payroll Employee record per Social Security Number.
Since every Individual created in IPM/ITS must have a corresponding Payroll Employee record, attempting to create a second employee using the same SSN will result in a duplicate SSN restriction.

Resolution
Background
There is an important distinction between Payroll Employees and Individuals:
Every Individual in IPM/ITS has a corresponding Payroll Employee.
However, not every Payroll Employee is an Individual.
Standard employees are managed entirely within Payroll, while Individuals are managed through IPM/ITS, where time and piece work are entered before being transferred into Payroll for payroll processing.

Recommended Resolution (Option 1)
If the client wants to preserve the employee's payroll history, do not create a second Payroll Employee record.
Instead:
Leave the existing Payroll Employee record intact.
Create a corresponding Individual record in IPM/ITS linked to the existing Payroll Employee.
Continue entering the employee's time or piece work through ITS.
Payroll will continue processing using the existing employee record.

Benefits
Preserves payroll history.
Maintains historical reporting.
Avoids duplicate W-2s if the employee returns during the same tax year.
Recommended approach in most situations.

Alternative Resolution (Option 2)
If the client wants to treat the returning worker as a completely new employee and no longer needs the previous employee record:
Change the SSN on the existing Payroll Employee record (for example, to a placeholder value according to company policy).
Create a new Individual/Employee record using the employee's actual SSN.
Continue processing payroll using the new record.

Considerations
This approach is generally recommended only when:
The previous employee record is no longer required.
Historical continuity is not needed.
The client intentionally wants separate employee records.

Best Practice
Unless there is a business requirement to create a completely separate employee record, Option 1 is the recommended approach, as it preserves payroll history, maintains employee continuity, and avoids duplicate payroll records for the same individual.

7f5d8ce6-22c1-4438-b785-5b2098ebd556.title: Advantage Down - "Unable to connect to licensor server."
7f5d8ce6-22c1-4438-b785-5b2098ebd556.content:
Problem
Advantage has been down. It says, "Unable to connect to licensor server."

Resolution
New Licensor Service Download:
https://filetransfer.aptean.com/public/file/ye5l5vq-neyzhpukuoy1vq/AdVantage%20Licensor%20Service.zip
Download and extract this to get the new .EXE file needed.
Where is the Licensor Service hosted?
Identify where the licensor service is being hosted. Depending on the client's setup it may
be locally on the same machine, or on a separate host.
This is easily found by looking at the registry where these settings are stored.
The settings are all stored under HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Customware,
Inc.\Ad-Vantage. You’re looking for the LicensorServer value. This will tell you where the
service will be running.

Shutdown and Uninstall the Licensor Service
Once the location has been identified you will need to login to that host. You will need
admin credentials for this work.
Start the Windows Services app, and look for the Ad-Vantage Licensor Service. If it is
currently running then right-click it and choose Stop. Wait for the service to stop
completely. The status will change from Running to a blank.

Right-click the service and choose Properties to gather information.
Where is the service program?

Note down the location of the service as you will need to navigate there in a command
prompt later.
What user is the service running as?
Note down what user the service is running as. You will need the username and password
to re-install the service later.

After all information is gathered, click OK or Cancel to close the properties before
continuing.
Uninstall the Licensor Service
Open a command prompt with administrator privileges. From there, navigate to where the
Licensor Service is installed at noted above. You can use the ‘cd’ command to ‘change
directory’to that location and use tab completion to help you get there.

Once there you can run the service program with the /u flag to uninstall it. The program
name has spaces in it, so it will be quoted.

Press enter to run that and you should just get the prompt back. If you refresh the Services
screen (F5) afterwards, the service should be gone.
Install the new Licensor Service
Now you will want to take the new version of Ad-Vantage Licensor Service.exe and copy it
into place, replacing the existing one. You can do this on Windows File Explorer.

Once copied and replaced, go back to your command prompt and this time you will do the
install flag and provide the username and password that the service will run as. Depending
on how the user is setup you may need to prepend the username with .\, such as .\msams.

Once done you should be able to refresh Services again and see the newly installed
service. Right-click it and choose Start. After a few moments the status should change to
Running.
Verify Login
Have the customer attempt to login to Ad-Vantage again, and it should succeed

60460bc5-c73c-49a7-85ae-09e8d1f1533e.title: Why are Inventory Adjustment entries labeled as "COGS Adjustment" posting to GL Account 500000?
60460bc5-c73c-49a7-85ae-09e8d1f1533e.content:
Problem
Why are Inventory Adjustment entries labeled as "COGS Adjustment" posting to GL Account 500000?

Resolution
The Inventory Adjustment entries labeled as "COGS Adjustment" are posting to GL Account 5000 because the Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) account configured in the Inventory (IN) Account Codes setup is currently mapped to account 5000.
This is the system's expected behavior when an inventory adjustment results in a reduction of item quantity. During the posting process, the system references the account mappings defined in the Inventory Account Codes setup and generates the corresponding journal entries based on that configuration.

Step-by-Step Explanation:
- Navigate to Inventory > Setup and Maintenance > Account Codes.

- Review the account mappings configured for the IN account code.

- When an inventory adjustment reduces the quantity of an item, the system uses the configured accounts to create the journal entry.

- Based on the current setup, the system generates the following entry:
- Debit: 500000 – Cost of Goods Sold (COGS)

- Eg screenshot:


Important Notes:
- If inventory adjustment transactions should post to a different GL account, the COGS account configured in the IN Account Codes setup must be reviewed and updated accordingly.

c59e63a8-6d4a-47ea-b6aa-62ede14d53e1.title: Understanding Bins Auto Create and Containers Auto Create Settings in Business rules
c59e63a8-6d4a-47ea-b6aa-62ede14d53e1.content:
Problem
What do the Bins Auto Create and Containers Auto Create settings within the Miscellaneous section of the Warehouse module in Business rules setup control? How do they impact users when entering data?

Resolution
Overview
The Bins Auto Create and Containers Auto Create settings determine whether users must select from existing records or can create new ones on the fly while working in Warehouse Management Daily Work functions.
These settings help control data consistency and user flexibility when working with bins and containers.

Purpose
- Enforce use of predefined bins and containers

- Prevent or allow on-the-fly creation of new records

- Maintain data accuracy and standardization

Bins Auto Create
This setting controls how users interact with Bin IDs.
- Select Yes
- Users must select an existing bin from the lookup

- Cannot create new bin IDs during transaction entry

- Ensures strict control and consistency

- Select No
- Users can create new bin IDs on the fly

- Simply type a new bin ID directly into the field

- System will accept and create it automatically

Containers Auto Create
This setting controls how users interact with Container IDs.
- Select Yes
- Users must select an existing container from the lookup

- Prevents creation of new containers during entry

- Helps maintain controlled container usage

- Select No
- Users can create new container IDs on the fly

- Enter a new ID directly into the field

- System will create it automatically

Key Differences
When to Use
Set to Yes when:
- You want strict control over bin/container setup

- You want to avoid duplicate or incorrect entries

- Your warehouse follows a fixed structure

Set to No when:
- You need flexibility for users

- New bins/containers are frequently created

- You want faster data entry without pre-setup


Recommendation:
- Bins Auto Create It is recommended to set this to Yes to ensure users select only existing bins, helping maintain consistency and prevent duplicate or incorrect bin creation.

- Containers Auto Create It is recommended to set this to Yes to ensure users select only existing containers, maintaining standardized and controlled container usage.

8da82684-84fb-4abe-a44d-c9d352558dff.title: How to resolve the error "Insufficient Disk Space in PRIMARY Filegroup"?
8da82684-84fb-4abe-a44d-c9d352558dff.content:
Problem
The user was unable to process anything in Traverse, regardless of transaction size.



During posting, the system generated the following SQL Server error:



SQL Server error encountered. Please check the error details for more information.

Edition = Standard
Build = 25143
User = User_X
LicenseServer = XXXXXXX
Culture = English (United States)
DefaultCompID = CSM
SysDb = SYS
SessionID = #########
MachineName = ######

1101: Could not allocate a new page for database 'CSM' because of insufficient disk space in filegroup 'PRIMARY'. Create the necessary space by dropping objects in the filegroup, adding additional files to the filegroup, or setting autogrowth on for existing files in the filegroup.
Procedure {trav_BuildPostGlEntries_proc}

Uncommittable transaction is detected at the end of the batch. The transaction is rolled back. (.Net SqlClient Data Provider)

For help, click: http://go.microsoft.com/fwlink?ProdName=Microsoft+SQL+Server&ProdVer=13.00.5103&EvtSrc=MSSQLServer&EvtID=50000&LinkId=20476

Server Name: s2049942\TRAV11
Error Number: 50000
Severity: 17
State: 12
Procedure: trav_RaiseError_proc
Line Number: 17

Program Location:

at TRAVERSE.Client.ProcessControlBase.OnProcessCompleted()
at TRAVERSE.Client.SalesOrder.PostingControl.OnProcessCompleted()

Resolution
Root Cause Analysis:

The issue occurred because the SQL Server database size had reached the 10 GB limit (SQL Server Standard / Express size limitation).

Due to this limitation:

- SQL Server was unable to allocate additional pages in the PRIMARY filegroup.
- The posting process could not complete.
- The transaction was automatically rolled back.
- No partial data was saved.

This is a database storage limitation and not a Traverse application defect.



Resolution:

To resolve the issue:

- Connected to the SQL Server instance using SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS).
- Reviewed the database size and confirmed it had exceeded the permitted 10 GB threshold.
- Performed a transaction log shrink operation to reduce the database size within the allowed limit.
- Ensured sufficient free space was available in the PRIMARY filegroup.
- Requested the client to retry posting the Sales Order transactions in Traverse.

After completing these steps:

- The posting process completed successfully.
- The SQL error no longer occurred.
- The issue was confirmed as resolved.



Preventive Recommendation:

To avoid recurrence:

- Monitor database size regularly.
- Implement a database maintenance plan.
- Schedule periodic log backups (if in Full Recovery Mode).
- Consider upgrading SQL edition if database growth is expected to exceed current limits.
- Enable proper auto growth settings with sufficient disk space availability.

24062e8d-024d-43d4-94f2-55c59f7f1b9b.title: Why Are Expense Accounts Showing YTD Balances in January After Year-End Processing?
24062e8d-024d-43d4-94f2-55c59f7f1b9b.content:
Problem
Why are Expense Accounts Showing YTD Balances in January After Year-End Processing?

The User reported that one of their expense accounts displayed YTD balances in January, while all other expense accounts behaved correctly.

Upon investigation:
- The Activity Report confirmed the balances came from the Year-End processing
- The Update Current Year process had been executed properly

Resolution
Root Cause:
- The affected account was configured with Account Type IDs below 500
Because of this configuration:
- The system treated those accounts as Balance Sheet accounts
- Their balances were carried forward instead of cleared


Resolution:
To resolve this issue, the Account Type ID must be corrected so the system recognizes the account as an Income Statement account.
Step 1: Review the Account Type ID:
- Navigate to: General Ledger -> Setup and Maintenance -> Chart of Accounts
- Pull up the affected account ID and verify the Account Type ID.
- If the account is an Expense account, the Account Type ID should typically be greater than 500
- If the Account Type ID < 500: It will be treated like a Balance Sheet Account
- If the Account Type ID > 500: It will be treated like an Income Account

Step 2: Correct the Account Type ID:
Update the account configuration:
- Change the Account Type ID to a value greater than 500
- Ensure the balance type (Debit/Credit) aligns with the Balance Type associated with the 'Account Type ID' behavior
- Click on 'Save' to save the changes



Step 3: Re-run the 'GL Update Current Year':
After correcting the account configuration, the Update Current Year process must be run again.
- Navigate to: General Ledger -> Periodic Processing -> Update Current Year
- Run the process to allow the system to recalculate the year-end balances based on the corrected account configuration.

Step 4: Verify the Results:
After running the process:
- Review the Income Statement for January
- Confirm that:
- The affected accounts no longer carry forward prior year balances [As the MTD value is 0.00, they have been excluded from the report.]
- YTD balances align correctly


Key Takeaways:
- The Account Type ID determines how balances behave during year-end processing.
- Incorrect configuration of Account Type ID will cause balances to carry forward into the next fiscal year instead of clearing to Retained Earnings.
- After correcting the configuration, the Update Current Year process must be re-run to properly reset the balances.

10ce1b7d-72c5-44a8-af8f-ce312c0ce92a.title: How to add 'Additional Description' field to the 'PO Order View' in Traverse 11.2?
10ce1b7d-72c5-44a8-af8f-ce312c0ce92a.content:
Problem
How to add 'Additional Description' field to the 'PO Order View' in Traverse 11.2?

Resolution
Current System Limitation:

In the PO Order View, the following fields are currently available:

TransId, BatchId, VendorId, PostRun, VendorName, OrderedBy, TransDate, Notes, SourceType, ItemId, LocId, QtyOrd, Units, Descr, LineStatus, DocumentNo, DocumentDate, FiscalYear, GlPeriod, LotNum, Qty, UnitCost, ExtCost, UnitCostFgn, ExtCostFgn, DocumentType, ReqShipDate, ShippingID, ShippingName, EntryNum, ItemType, GLAcct, GLDesc, ProjID, ProjName, PhaseID, PhaseName, TaskID, TaskName, GLAcctAccrual, CurrencyId, VendorPartNumber, ExpReceiptDate, ShippingType



Resolution Overview:

The Additional Description field exists at the database level but is not added to the Orders View definition. To make it available for reporting, we need to expose this field through Design Studio by updating the Views Table.



This solution applies to Traverse Global.



Resolution Steps:

Step 1: Access Design Studio

i. Launch Design Studio

ii. Navigate to the following path: System Data -> Views Table

iii. In the Views Table, and locate the PO Orders View ID



NOTE: It is recommended to NOT modify the stock Views Table ID directly.



Step 2: Create a New Views Table Entry:

i. Create a new Views Table line entry (new ID) using the + icon:



ii. Copy the following from the existing PO Order View ID and paste it into the new record:

- Description [Can be updated for reference accordingly]
- Data Source
- Available Fields
- Default Columns
- Enumerated Columns
- Any other relevant configuration

This ensures the new record mirrors the stock configuration before customization.



Step 3: Replace the Stock ID (Critical Step):

In the newly created Views Table entry:

- Locate the “Replace ID” field
- Enter the stock 'PoOrder' View ID in this field

This ensures the new custom record replaces the stock ID during runtime.



Why This is Best Practice?

Using the “Replace ID” approach:

- Reduces the risk of custom changes being overwritten
- Protects modifications during future build updates
- Maintains upgrade-safe customization
- Avoids reverting to default/stock configurations

Direct modification of stock IDs is not recommended.





Step 4: Update the Data Source definition:

We need to update the 'Data Source' to include the 'Additional Description' field:

de47f8da-7a84-4141-b455-d1291d0e8ea7.title: Why Does Traverse EDI Continue Detecting a Duplicate PO Even After the Original PO Was Deleted?
de47f8da-7a84-4141-b455-d1291d0e8ea7.content:
Problem
The client reported that Purchase Order XXXX was failing validation within Traverse EDI because the system continued detecting the PO as a duplicate.



According to the client, a duplicate Purchase Order had previously existed within the system and was later deleted. However, when attempting to reprocess or validate the same Purchase Order again through EDI PO Processing, Traverse continued to return a duplicate PO validation error.



As a result, the Purchase Order could not proceed further, preventing the client from processing the order successfully.

Cause
Traverse EDI validates incoming Purchase Orders against previously processed PO numbers to prevent accidental duplicate order creation.



Even though the original Purchase Order may have been deleted, the Trading Partner configuration may still prevent the system from validating another PO with the same PO number when duplicate PO validation restrictions are enabled.



Because of this validation rule, the system continued blocking the Purchase Order during the EDI validation process.

Resolution
To allow the Purchase Order to validate successfully and proceed through processing, the duplicate PO restriction was temporarily disabled for the Trading Partner configuration.

Steps to follow:

i. Navigate to: EDI Connector -> Setup and Maintenance -> Partners

ii. Select the applicable Trading Partner: In this example, WALMART

iii. Click on the Options button.

iv. Locate the setting related to duplicate Purchase Order validation.

v. Change the setting: Allow Duplicate PO’s to Yes

vi. Save the changes.



Reprocessing the EDI Purchase Order:

After enabling duplicate PO processing, proceed with validating the PO and processing the same.



Important Post-Processing Step:

After the Order has been processed successfully, it is important to restore the original validation setting to prevent unintended duplicate PO processing in the future.

Steps to Revert the Setting:

i. Navigate to: EDI -> Setup and Maintenance -> Partners

ii. Select the applicable Trading Partner: In this example, WALMART

iii. Click on the Options button.

iv. Locate the setting related to duplicate Purchase Order validation.

v. Change the setting: Allow Duplicate PO’s to No

vi. Save the changes.





Outcome:

By temporarily enabling duplicate PO processing for the specific Trading Partner, the affected Purchase Order successfully validated within Traverse EDI and proceeded.

Once processing was completed, the duplicate PO restriction was restored to maintain standard validation controls and prevent future accidental duplicate order entries.

9d507454-b589-41cf-b258-b5143366bd7b.title: What causes the Picking Slip alignment to change after installing the WM module?
9d507454-b589-41cf-b258-b5143366bd7b.content:
Problem
Why does the alignment of Picking Slip changes when WM module is installed?



Picking Slip when WM is installed:



Picking Slip when WM is NOT installed:

Resolution
When WM is not installed, Traverse displays only basic item information on Picking Slips, such as the Item ID and Quantity, because the system is relying solely on the inventory records from the IN module. In this mode, Traverse does not track inventory at the bin or container level. As a result, the Picking Slip does not include bin, container, or bin-level quantity details, and the line items appear in standard Sales Order sequence.



However, when the Warehouse Management (WM) module is installed, Traverse switches to a more advanced warehouse-driven process. WM adds deeper functionality that includes:

- Bin-level inventory tracking
- Container tracking
- Quantity per bin



Because of these WM capabilities, Traverse automatically changes both the information shown on the Picking Slip and the order in which items appear.



Why the behavior differs with WM installed?

i. WM introduces bin-level inventory control:

With WM active, Traverse must display:

- Bin locations
- Container details
- Quantity available per bin

Because the warehouse staff is expected to pick items based on actual physical storage locations. Without WM, this data simply does not exist in the system.



ii. Alignment and ordering change due to bin-based sorting:

WM reorganizes the Picking Slip to optimize picking efficiency.

How WM reorders the lines:

- Items with no bin assigned appear at the top.
- Remaining items are sorted alphabetically by bin.
- Quantity and bin details appear to guide pickers through the warehouse efficiently.

This ensures pickers move through the warehouse in a logical path instead of jumping between random locations.

iii. This behavior is intentional, not an error:

The change in layout and sorting is part of the designed functionality of Traverse when WM is enabled.
WM is built specifically to:

- Reduce travel time
- Improve picking accuracy
- Streamline warehouse operations

So, the Picking Slip automatically adapts from a simple sales-order document to a warehouse-optimized picking document.

Summary:

FeatureWM Not InstalledWM InstalledBin information❌ Not shown (system does not track it)✔ DisplayedContainer details❌ Not available✔ DisplayedQuantity per bin❌ Not tracked✔ DisplayedPicking Slip orderStandard Sales OrderBin-based sequencePurposeSales documentationWarehouse picking optimization


WM changes the Picking Slip because the system starts using bin-level inventory and must reorganize the information to support warehouse workflows. Without WM, Traverse does not have this level of detail, so the Picking Slip remains basic.
