c6e13812-e6b1-400f-a7e5-81b0412fbe70.title: Why does a multi-currency bank transfer result in an out-of-balance transaction in Traverse?
c6e13812-e6b1-400f-a7e5-81b0412fbe70.content:
Problem
This issue was identified based on an actual client transaction involving a multi-currency bank transfer scenario.



Let us consider an example involving USD and JPY.

- The client intended to transfer funds from their USD bank account to their JPY bank account.
- The required amount on the receiving side was 558,060 JPY.
- To facilitate this, the bank deducted 3,605.67 USD from the USD bank account. And the same was entered in Traverse in USD.
- The applicable exchange rate for the transaction was 154.77289935.



When the client entered a Bank Reconciliation (BR) Transfer in Traverse from the USD bank account to the JPY bank account using 3,605.67 USD, the system calculated and credited the JPY bank account based on an equivalent of 3,606 USD, instead of the actual entered amount.

As a result:

- The transaction appeared out of balance when previewing the BR Transaction Journal.



However, when the same transaction was entered by specifying the amount in JPY (foreign currency), and changing the Currency ID accordingly, the transaction comes through successfully without any imbalance.



This behavior indicated an inconsistency, as the transaction should remain balanced regardless of whether the user enters the amount in USD or JPY.

Resolution
This issue was submitted as a bug under the Change Request DEV-229587.



TFS URL: https://dev.azure.com/TraverseERP/b746159b-5617-4616-8466-ae9d6a61d66f/_workitems/edit/88431



Upon investigation, the Engineering team identified the root cause as a rounding discrepancy in multi-currency bank transfers, where incorrect currency precision was being applied during the calculation. Specifically, the system was using the To-bank currency precision instead of the From-bank currency precision for rounding the foreign amount.



The issue has been resolved by updating the logic to ensure that rounding is consistently applied based on the From bank currency precision, which aligns with the currency in which the foreign amount is entered.



The fix has been successfully implemented by the Engineering team and is scheduled to be included in the June 2026 release. With this correction in place, multi-currency transfer transactions will now remain balanced irrespective of the currency used during entry.

911cc065-7eb2-4678-94b8-9125f287a238.title: Viewing Serial Numbers Associated with Sales Orders and Invoices in Traverse
911cc065-7eb2-4678-94b8-9125f287a238.content:
Problem
This article explains how to view serial numbers associated with Sales Orders and Invoices Traverse using the Serial History View. It also provides additional information regarding how serial numbers are stored and used within the system.

Users may need to identify or verify serial numbers associated with Sales Orders, Invoices, or Customers for purposes such as:
- Warranty tracking

- Item traceability

- Customer support

- Shipment verification

- Billing validation

- Regulatory or compliance requirements

By default, serial numbers are stored at the transaction detail level and may not always appear in standard reports or forms, making it difficult to locate the information directly from invoices or sales order documents

Resolution
How to View Serial Numbers
Step 1: Navigate to Serial History View
Go to:
Inventory → Interactive Views → Serial History View
Step 2: Add Required Columns
Within the Serial History View, use the Column Chooser to add the following fields to the grid:
- Transaction ID

- Type

- Serial Number

These fields will help display the relevant serial number information associated with transactions.
Step 3: Review Transaction Information
After adding the columns, users can review the serial number history and associated transaction details.
Using the Serial History View, users can trace both the Sales Order and Purchase Order activity associated with a specific serial number. This provides end-to-end visibility into the lifecycle of the serialized item, including purchasing, inventory movement, sales processing, and invoicing history.


Serial numbers help track individual inventory items throughout their lifecycle. They provide better visibility, accuracy, and control over serialized products.
Why Serial Numbers Are Important
Individual Item Tracking
Serial numbers allow users to track a specific item separately from other inventory items. This helps users identify:
- Where the item is located

- When it was purchased or sold

- Its transaction history

- Its cost and selling price

This is especially useful for high-value or regulated products.

Traverse automatically updates the status of serialized items based on transactions performed in the system.
Common serial number statuses include:
- Available – Item is in stock and ready to sell

- Sold – Item has been sold and the transaction has been posted

- Lost – Item was removed through an inventory adjustment

- In Transit – Item is being transferred between locations

The serial number status is controlled by the system and cannot be manually edited.

Each serial number maintains its own:
- Unit Cost

- Selling Price

- Transaction History

This helps ensure inventory and financial records remain accurate.

8accda83-f2eb-4d76-bc6d-daeb7b612566.title: Negative Inventory Valuation and Incorrect On-Hand Quantity After Inventory Adjustment
8accda83-f2eb-4d76-bc6d-daeb7b612566.content:
Problem
This article explains a scenario where Inventory Valuation becomes negative after an incorrect return process and how manual Inventory Transactions (INTRANS) can correct valuation but unintentionally create incorrect On-Hand quantities in Traverse.
The article also explains the root cause, business impact, and recommended resolution steps.

A customer returned product to a vendor, but the return was processed incorrectly using a description instead of the actual Item ID. As a result:
- Inventory was not properly relieved

- Inventory Valuation became negative

- Manual Inventory Increase Adjustments (INTRANS) were later entered to correct valuation

Although the Inventory Valuation and Inventory GL became accurate after the adjustment, the system then displayed incorrect positive On-Hand quantities and Item Availability values.
The customer confirmed that the physical stock quantity was actually zero.

Resolution
- Product: Traverse 11.2

- Build: 25031



The client observed the following behavior:
- Negative Inventory Valuation quantity and cost

- Inventory GL mismatch initially

- Inventory Increase Adjustment corrected valuation

- Inventory Valuation now equals zero and matches GL account 119020

- On-Hand Quantity became incorrectly positive

- Available Quantity displayed negative values due to open Sales Orders

- Physical inventory remained zero



The issue occurred because the return transaction was processed incorrectly.
Instead of processing the Credit Memo using the proper serialized or inventory Item ID, the transaction was entered using a description field.
As a result:
- FIFO inventory layers were not relieved correctly

- Inventory cost layers became inconsistent

- Inventory Valuation showed negative quantity and cost

To correct the valuation, manual Inventory Increase Adjustments (INTRANS) were entered.
However, Inventory Transactions affect both:
- Inventory valuation/cost

- On-Hand quantity

Because of this, correcting valuation through INTRANS also artificially increased inventory quantities in the system.


Resolution
Recommended Resolution Approach
Step 1: Identify Incorrect Inventory Transactions
Review:
- Inventory Transaction History

- IN Detail History

- FIFO cost layers

- Inventory Valuation Report

Identify:
- Incorrect Inventory Increase Adjustments (INTRANS)

- Transactions created solely to offset negative valuation


Step 2: Reverse Incorrect INTRANS Entries
The manually created Inventory Increase Adjustments should be reversed carefully to remove the artificially created On-Hand quantity.
This helps restore:
- Correct physical quantity

- Correct Item Availability

- Proper inventory balance


Step 3: Verify Correct Purchasing and Return Transactions Exist
Ensure the following transactions were entered correctly using the proper Item ID:
- Original PO Receipt

- Sales Order Shipment

- Vendor Return / Credit Memo

The Item ID must be used instead of descriptions to ensure FIFO layers update correctly.

Step 4: Rebuild and Validate Inventory Balances
After reversals:
- Re-run Inventory Valuation

- Validate Item Availability

- Validate On-Hand Quantity

- Confirm Inventory GL matches valuation

Expected result:
- Physical stock = 0

- On-Hand quantity = 0

- Inventory Valuation = 0

- GL balance = matched




For example, in this customer’s environment, it was observed that Purchase Order Receipts and PO Invoices were being future dated beyond the actual transaction entry date. This is considered an uncommon processing practice and can impact FIFO costing and Inventory Valuation reporting.
In the reported scenario:
- Inventory became available and was consumed through Sales Orders in an earlier fiscal period.

- However, the corresponding PO Receipt/Invoice cost was recognized only in a later fiscal period due to future dating.

- This caused negative Inventory Valuation balances for the earlier period even though the On-Hand quantity eventually balanced out in later periods.


In this scenario:
- Sales Order 00209418 was shipped and verified in Fiscal Period 4.

- Corresponding Purchase Order 00009711 was future dated into Fiscal Period 5.

- Inventory quantity became available and was consumed before the inventory cost layer was recognized.

- This caused a temporary negative Inventory Valuation balance in Period 4.

- When Inventory Valuation was later run for Period 5, the inventory quantity and valuation netted back to zero once the PO cost was recognized.

To correct the valuation discrepancy, manual Inventory Transactions were entered. However, because Inventory Transactions affect both quantity and valuation, this created incorrect positive On-Hand quantities in the system.
For example:
- Inventory Transaction XX1

- Inventory Transaction XX2

- Inventory Transaction XX3

were identified as adjustment entries used to correct valuation.

It is recommended to reverse Inventory Transactions XX1, XX2, and XX3 to remove the artificially created inventory quantities and restore accurate On-Hand balances.
After reversing these transactions:
- Re-run the Inventory Valuation report for the affected fiscal periods.

- Validate Inventory Valuation, On-Hand Quantity, and Item Availability.

- Confirm Inventory GL balances match the valuation reports.

In this example, reversing the adjustment transactions would reduce inventory by the corresponding quantity for Item ID 98-8304 and help restore accurate inventory balances.
However, due to the customer’s future-dated PO processing practice, temporary negative Inventory Valuation balances may still appear in earlier fiscal periods until the related PO costs are recognized in the later fiscal period.

2569c6fc-8080-4c22-a382-fb6e8301483e.title: Custom Fields Not Copying When Creating a New BOM from an Existing BOM
2569c6fc-8080-4c22-a382-fb6e8301483e.content:
Problem
This article explains an issue where custom fields assigned to BOM detail records are not copied when creating a new Bill of Materials (BOM) using the “Copy from Assembly ID” functionality in Traverse Manufacturing.
Although the BOM structure and component records are copied successfully, the custom field values entered on the BOM detail lines are not transferred to the newly created BOM.

Users have custom fields configured on BOM detail records through Aptean Design Studio. When creating a new BOM by copying an existing Assembly ID, the custom field values are not carried over to the new BOM.
As a result:
- The BOM copies successfully

- Component lines copy successfully

- Custom field values remain blank in the new BOM

- Users must manually re-enter the custom field information

This behavior impacts all users working with BOM customizations.

Resolution
Bug : Bug 89182: CR - Custom Fields don't copy from existing BOM - 01815338 - DEV-233405
Bug 89182: CR - Custom Fields don't copy from existing BOM - 01815338 - DEV-233405

For example, a customer configured a custom field called Invoice Comments and assigned it to the BOM detail table.
Users entered values into the custom field for an existing Assembly ID. However, when creating a new BOM using the Copy from Assembly ID feature, the custom field values were not copied into the new BOM, even though the BOM components themselves copied successfully.
This indicates that the standard BOM copy process does not include custom detail-level field values. Build Tested: 24242


This issue causes:
- Additional manual data entry

- Increased time when creating BOM revisions or duplicate BOMs

- Potential inconsistencies between BOM records

- Missing custom information in newly copied BOMs

Number of users impacted:
- All users creating or maintaining BOMs with custom fields


The “Copy from Assembly ID” functionality appears to copy:
- BOM Header information

- Standard component records

However, custom fields associated with BOM detail/component records are not included during the copy process.
The issue was successfully replicated in testing.


Steps to Reproduce
Note: Testing was performed using standard CPU sample data.
Step 1: Configure a Custom Field
- Open Aptean Design Studio.

- Create or locate a custom field.

- Assign the custom field to the BOM detail table.

- Save the customization.

Step 2: Populate the Custom Field in an Existing BOM
- Open Traverse.

- Navigate to:
- MFG → Bill Of Material

- Select an existing Assembly ID.

- Open the Component tab.

- Add the custom field column using the Column Chooser if necessary.

- Enter a value into the custom field for one or more component lines.

- Save the BOM.

Step 3: Create a New BOM Using Copy from Assembly ID
- Click New Record.

- Select an existing Assembly ID.

- Ensure the “Copy from Assembly ID” field references the existing BOM.

- Enter a Revision number.

- Save the new BOM.


Step 4: Validate the New BOM
- Reopen the newly created Assembly ID.

- Navigate to the Component tab.

- Review the custom field values.

Result:
- BOM components are copied successfully

- Custom field values are blank and not copied from the original BOM



Resolution :

The issue has been identified as a product defect where the standard BOM copy functionality does not copy custom field values associated with BOM detail records.
This behavior has been submitted as a bug for correction, and the fix is currently planned for inclusion in the upcoming June 2026 build release.
Until the fix is released:
- Users will need to manually re-enter custom field values after copying the BOM.

- Standard BOM fields and component records will continue to copy successfully, but custom detail-level field values will not transfer automatically.

fe575538-4bbd-46f3-be77-ec14e260072f.title: Why Does the Error “Payments Not Found in BR” Occur While Voiding AP Payments?
fe575538-4bbd-46f3-be77-ec14e260072f.content:
Problem
Users may encounter the error message “Payments not found in BR” while attempting to void historical Accounts Payable (AP) payments in Traverse.



This issue typically occurs in scenarios where the original AP payment was posted before the Bank Reconciliation (BR) module was licensed or enabled in the environment. Since the Bank Reconciliation module was not present at the time the payment was originally processed, the payment transaction did not create a corresponding record within the BR module.



At a later stage, once the Bank Reconciliation module is added to the license and activated, Traverse expects AP payments to have associated records in Bank Reconciliation during the voiding process. However, because the historical payment was created before the BR module existed in the environment, no corresponding BR transaction is available, resulting in the error: “Payments not found in BR”



This prevents the payment from being voided successfully through the standard process.

Resolution
To successfully void the historical AP payment, the interface between Accounts Payable and Bank Reconciliation must be temporarily disabled.

Steps to Resolve:

i. Navigate to the following path in Traverse: System Manager -> Company Setup -> Business Rules:



ii. Select: AP – Accounts Payable, and locate the Interface-Application section.



iii. Set the Bank Reconciliation option to: No [This temporarily disables the integration/interface between AP and Bank Reconciliation.]



iv. Save the changes.



v. Proceed with voiding the AP payment. and it should go through without any issues.





vi. Once the void process has been completed successfully, return to the same Business Rules screen and set the Bank Reconciliation option back to: Yes and save the changes [This restores the interface between Accounts Payable and Bank Reconciliation.]



Next Steps After Voiding:

The Invoice will now be available in the 'AP Hold/Release Invoices' screen for repreparing and issuing a Check and subsequently posting the same.



Once the interface has been turned back on:

- Re-prepare the payment.
- Print the check as needed.
- Post the payment.

Since the Bank Reconciliation module is now active and the interface has been restored, the newly posted payment will correctly create a 'Disbursement' entry within Bank Reconciliation.

This allows future voiding (of this Invoice) and reconciliation activities to function normally without encountering the “Payments not found in BR” error.



Important Note:

While the Bank Reconciliation interface is temporarily turned off:

- No users should process or post any AP payments.
- If any AP Payments are posted during this period, it will not hit the Bank Reconciliation

1e7eb0ee-49b1-4681-8321-2ab5e2ce9bff.title: How to resolve Unable to connect to Licensor server in Ad-Vantage
1e7eb0ee-49b1-4681-8321-2ab5e2ce9bff.content:
Problem
Users getting the below error when trying to login into Ad-Vantage

" Unable to connect to Licensor server"

Resolution
New Licensor Service Download

https://filetransfer.aptean.com/public/file/ye5l5vq-neyzhpukuoy1vq/Ad- Vantage%20Licensor%20Service.zip

Download and extract this to get the new .EXE file needed.



Where is the Licensor Service hosted?

Identify where the licensor service is being hosted. Depending on the client's setup it may be locally on the same machine, or on a separate host.

This is easily found by looking at the registry where these settings are stored.

The settings are all stored under HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Customware,

Inc.\Ad-Vantage. You’re looking for the LicensorServer value. This will tell you where the service will be running.







Shutdown and Uninstall the Licensor Service

Once the location has been identified you will need to login to that host. You will need admin credentials for this work.



Start the Windows Services app, and look for the Ad-Vantage Licensor Service. If it is currently running then right-click it and choose Stop. Wait for the service to stop completely. The status will change from Running to a blank.


Right-click the service and choose Properties to gather information.

Where is the service program?

Note down the location of the service as you will need to navigate there in a command prompt later.







What user is the service running as?

Note down what user the service is running as. You will need the username and password to re-install the service later.









After all information is gathered, click OK or Cancel to close the properties before continuing.





Uninstall the Licensor Service



Open a command prompt with administrator privileges. From there, navigate to where the Licensor Service is installed at noted above. You can use the ‘cd’ command to ‘change directory’ to that location and use tab completion to help you get there.




Once there you can run the service program with the /u flag to uninstall it. The program name has spaces in it, so it will be quoted.











Press enter to run that and you should just get the prompt back. If you refresh the Services screen (F5) afterwards, the service should be gone.



Install the new Licensor Service

Now you will want to take the new version of Ad-Vantage Licensor Service.exe and copy it into place, replacing the existing one. You can do this on Windows File Explorer.



Once copied and replaced, go back to your command prompt and this time you will do the install flag and provide the username and password that the service will run as. Depending on how the user is setup you may need to prepend the username with .\, such as .\msams.





Once done you should be able to refresh Services again and see the newly installed

service. Right-click it and choose Start. After a few moments the status should change to Running.



Verify Login

Have the customer attempt to login to Ad-Vantage again, and it should succeed.

4825ddf7-a829-4c12-a183-81dbd03d2f95.title: How to add new Delivery Location for an EDI Customer in Traverse?
4825ddf7-a829-4c12-a183-81dbd03d2f95.content:
Problem
How to add new Delivery Location for an EDI Customer in Traverse?

Resolution
To set up a new EDI Ship-To ID within the system, the required address must be added under the ‘Ship-To’ tab in the ‘AR Customers’ screen. This ensures that each delivery location is properly defined and can be referenced during EDI transactions.

While creating the Ship-To record, it is important to populate all relevant address details to maintain consistency and avoid any downstream issues in order processing or delivery.
In particular, please ensure that the EDI Ship To Code field is updated with the correct Ship-To code provided by the customer for that specific delivery location. This code is essential for EDI transactions, as it uniquely identifies the destination and ensures proper mapping between systems.

To complete this setup, please follow the steps below:
- Navigate to Accounts Receivable -> Setup and Maintenance -> Customers and open the ‘AR Customers’ screen.

- Locate and select the required customer record.

- Go to the ‘Ship-To’ tab within the customer screen.

- Create a new Ship-To address record and enter the relevant address details.

- In the 'EDI Ship To Code' field, input the corresponding Ship-To code provided by the customer.

Once completed, this configuration will enable accurate processing of EDI transactions for the specified delivery location.

e5cee416-af17-4f00-bec6-58f2393ba06a.title: How to Create 'ITS Programs' and What Is the Use of Them?
e5cee416-af17-4f00-bec6-58f2393ba06a.content:
Problem
How to create the 'IT Programs' in Individual Tracking?

Resolution
How to Create ITS Programs and What Is the Use of Them?

ITS (Individual Tracking System) Programs are used to define and manage the various programs, initiatives, or services that an organization offers and assigns to individuals within the system. Creating programs allows organizations to centrally track participation, maintain program details, and ensure accurate assignment and reporting across individuals.

This document explains what ITS Programs are, why they are important, and step-by-step instructions on how to create them in the system.



What are ITS Programs?

ITS Programs represent structured offerings within an organization, such as training programs, service initiatives, educational programs, or internal projects, that individuals can be associated with.

Each program record stores key information such as:

- Program identification details
- Program type and classification
- Contact and address information

Once created, these programs can be assigned to individuals through the IT Programs screen, allowing the organization to track involvement accurately.

Why Are ITS Programs Important?

Creating and maintaining ITS Programs helps organizations:

- Standardize how programs are defined across the system
- Easily assign individuals to specific programs
- Maintain consistent and centralized program information
- Improve reporting and tracking of individual participation
- Reduce manual tracking and data inconsistencies

Navigation Path to Create Programs

To create an ITS Program, we need to navigate to:

Individual Tracking Systems -> Setup and Maintenance -> Programs

This menu allows us to view existing programs, create new ones, and maintain program-related details.

Step-by-Step Instructions:

Step 1: Create a New Program Record

- Open the IT Programs screen
- Click the New button at the top of the screen

This opens a new record where program details can be entered.

Step 2: Enter the Program ID

- Enter a unique Program ID
- This ID is used to identify the program throughout the system

Best practice: Use a meaningful and standardized naming convention for easier identification.

Step 3: Select the Program Type

- Click the down arrow in the Program Type field
- Select the appropriate program type from the list

Note: Program types are predefined in the Type Codes Maintenance screen. This is where all valid program categories for your organization are maintained.



Step 4: Enter the Program Name

- Provide a clear and descriptive Program Name
- This name will be visible when assigning individuals to the program

Step 5: Enter Program Contact Details (Optional)

If applicable, fill in the following fields:

- Address
- Phone number
- Customer phone number
- Website

These details help store reference and contact information related to the program.

Step 6: Save the Program

-
Once all required and desired information is entered, click Save

The program is now successfully created and available for use.



Assigning Individuals to a Program

After the program is created:

- Navigate to the Individual Maintenance screen
- Assign individuals to the newly created program

This allows the system to track which individuals are associated with which programs.

Best Practices

- Ensure program types are properly set up before creating programs
- Use consistent naming conventions for Program IDs and Names
- Periodically review program records for accuracy
- Avoid creating duplicate programs with similar names

ITS Programs provide a structured way to manage and track organizational programs and individual participation. By properly setting up programs in the system, organizations can maintain accurate records, streamline assignments, and improve overall data consistency.

dc6c4a9b-1429-486a-98e4-e8c3e65a60c8.title: How to handle the SQL Connection Error: "Communication Link Failure" in DocUnity?
dc6c4a9b-1429-486a-98e4-e8c3e65a60c8.content:
Problem
How to resolve the below SQL connection error while saving Documents in Doc Unity?



The user encountered an error when executing a SQL query to retrieve blob data from the KMD_BATCH_BLOBS table using a specific KMD_UUID. The error message indicated a communication link failure caused by the SQL Server connection being forcibly closed by the remote host.



Error Message:
SELECT KMD_BLOB FROM KMD_BATCH_BLOBS WHERE KMD_UUID = 'XXXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXXXXXXXXXX'
[Microsoft][SQL Server Native Client 11.0][SQL Server]TCP Provider: An existing connection was forcibly closed by the remote host.
[Microsoft][SQL Server Native Client 11.0]Communication link failure.

Resolution
This is commonly associated with disruptions in the network layer or issues at the SQL Server service level that cause the active session to terminate unexpectedly.

The error specifically included:

-
TCP Provider error: Indicates that the existing connection to the SQL Server was terminated unexpectedly.

-
SQL Server Native Client 11.0: Identifies the client technology being used for the connection.

-
Communication Link Failure: A general connectivity error signaling that the client could not maintain a stable connection with the SQL Server instance.



To address the issue, it was recommended to reboot the SQL Server hosting the database. After the reboot:

-
The error message no longer appeared.

-
The query executed successfully.

-
No further communication link failures were observed during post-reboot monitoring.

This indicates that the server reboot resolved any transient issues impacting the SQL Server's ability to maintain stable connections with clients.

789fa417-291c-4f8d-8f50-f2f567c92c7f.title: APS Displays All Company Printers in Traverse
789fa417-291c-4f8d-8f50-f2f567c92c7f.content:
Problem
When using APS (Aptean Print Services) within Traverse, users may notice that the printer selection window displays a large number of printers instead of only their assigned or default printer.

Users may report:

- Seeing all company printers in the printer selection list
- Difficulty locating the correct printer
- Printer dropdown containing dozens or hundreds of entries
- Default printer not appearing automatically selected

Cause
APS (Aptean Print Services) is designed to enumerate and display all printers associated with the active APS session/account.

As a result:

- Traverse retrieves all mapped/available printers from the APS environment
- The application does not currently support filtering or restricting the visible printer list at the application level
- All available printers are presented to the user during printer selection

This is standard system behavior and not a malfunction.

Resolution
Although the printer list cannot currently be filtered, usability can be improved by configuring a default printer for users.

Configure Default Printer

Navigate to:

SM > Company Setup > User Defaults > System Manager

Specify the desired printer name as the user’s default printer.

This configuration:

- Prioritizes the selected printer
- Moves the preferred printer toward the top of the selection list
- Improves usability during printing operations

9dc1749f-17fd-45df-9cde-277dcd51cd72.title: Active Directory User Lookup Behavior Change – Security Enhancement
9dc1749f-17fd-45df-9cde-277dcd51cd72.content:
Problem
A recent security enhancement has changed how Active Directory (AD) user lookup behaves within the application environment. Customers may notice that the AD dropdown no longer displays a broad list of domain users as it did previously.

Cause
Previously, the AD lookup functionality was capable of returning a wide list of users across the domain.

This behavior was identified as a potential:

- Security concern
- Data exposure risk
- Unnecessary domain-wide user enumeration capability

To align with security best practices and reduce unintended visibility of user information, the functionality was modified to restrict user enumeration.

Resolution
Current Expected Behavior

Under the updated security model:

- The AD dropdown no longer performs unrestricted domain-wide browsing
- User visibility is now limited to organization-relevant scope
- Broad enumeration of domain users is intentionally blocked

This behavior is expected and working as designed.

How to Locate Users

Users can still locate valid users within their organization by:

- Clicking the dropdown (▼) icon next to the selection field
- Selecting from the filtered organization-specific user list

This method is designed to return only authorized and relevant users within the permitted scope.

Security Benefit

This enhancement helps:

- Prevent unintended exposure of domain user information
- Improve compliance with security best practices
- Restrict unnecessary Active Directory enumeration
- Maintain organization-level user isolation

da19aaaf-791d-4608-8d2f-4f4bfec1e0e0.title: How to resolve the 'Divide by Zero' error while trying to post Transactions?
da19aaaf-791d-4608-8d2f-4f4bfec1e0e0.content:
Problem
How to resolve the 'Divide by Zero' error while trying to post Transactions?



8134 : Divide by zero error encountered
(TRAVERSE.Report.PurchaseOrder.ReceiptsAndInvoices)

Procedure Details:
Procedure = dbo.trav_PoReceiveInvoiceReport_proc
Raised By = dbo.trav_RaiseError_proc
Line Number = 17

SQL Server Details:
Server Name = XXXXXXXXXXX
Error Number = 50000
Severity = 16
State = 1
Provider = .Net SqlClient Data Provider

Program Location:

at TRAVERSE.Report.PurchaseOrder.ReceiptsAndInvoicesData.Execute(String filter, Status status)
at TRAVERSE.Report.PurchaseOrder.ReceiptsAndInvoicesControl.AssignDataSet()
at TRAVERSE.Client.Report.PickScreenBase.RenderReport()

Resolution
Cause of the Issue:

This error occurs when a transaction within the invoice batch contains either:

- A Receipt with zero quantity, or
- A Return Authorization with zero quantity

During processing, these zero-quantity records lead to a divide-by-zero condition, which results in the reported error.

How to Identify the Problematic Transaction:

If the user is not aware of which specific transaction is causing the issue, they can review the transactions using the PO Open Order View.

- Apply a filter on the Received/Invoiced Quantity field
- Look for records where the quantity is zero

This will help isolate the receipt or return authorization that is triggering the error.

Alternative Approach:

As an alternative, the user may process the transactions in smaller batches. This can help narrow down and identify the exact transaction causing the issue more quickly.

Product Behavior:

This issue is observed in builds prior to 23386.

From Build 23386 onwards, the system has been updated to prevent the creation or processing of:

- Zero-dollar receipts
- Zero-quantity return authorizations

Resolution:

Once the identified transaction (either the zero-quantity receipt or return authorization) is removed or corrected, the user should be able to proceed with posting the invoice successfully in Traverse.

2e5f8888-526d-4126-b4be-44a7074402c2.title: How to apply multiple payments for a single AR Invoice?
2e5f8888-526d-4126-b4be-44a7074402c2.content:
Problem
How to apply multiple payments for a single AR Invoice?

Resolution
Let us take an illustrative example to understand this process in detail. Suppose there is an Invoice raised for a Customer with a total value of $200. The Customer, in this case, has already made a prior Cash Deposit of $60. Subsequently, an additional Cash Deposit of $140 is also received after a few days.



This document provides a step-by-step walkthrough of how these Cash Deposits, when received at different times, can be applied collectively against the same Invoice. The process will be demonstrated using the “AR Hold/Release Invoices” screen, highlighting how the system manages partial and full applications of payments to settle the outstanding Invoice balance.



The added Cash Deposit will be looking like this in the AR Hold/Release Invoices screen:



i. Navigate to the 'AR Hold of Release Invoices' screen under the path: Applications -> Accounts Receivable -> Pay Invoices -> Hold/Release Invoices:



ii. In the 'AR Hold/Release Invoices' screen, select the 'Payment' entry and click on the 'Split/Reapply' icon:



iii. At this point, we can either opt for 'Auto-Apply' or manually type in the 'Payment Amount' in the 'Applied Amount' field and click on 'OK':



iv. a. Once the Payment has been applied, the ‘AR Hold/Release Invoices’ screen will look as below:



NOTE: Even if part of the Invoice had already been paid, the 'Invoice' will only show the entire amount as the 'Gross Due.' So for better understanding, it is always advised to filter out with the 'Invoice Number' wand observe the totals accordingly.



Pending Due = Total Gross Due - Payment made





iv. b. Once the Payment has been applied, the ‘AR Cash Receipts’ screen will look as below, reflecting the 'Pending Due' amount for that Invoice:



v. Later on, a new Cash Receipt was created for the remaining amount as shown below and then posted:



vi. Now the ‘AR Hold/Release Invoices’ screen will look as below:



vii. Then, the remaining amount needs to be paid against the 'Invoice' as needed using the 'Split/Reapply' icon. This can be done by choosing the Payment entry and then clicking onto the 'Split/Reapply' icon:





viii. Once the process has been completed, the 'AR Hold/Release Invoices' screen looks as follow:



ix. Once the 'Payment' total corresponding to the 'Invoice number' matches with the 'Invoice Due', we can confirm that the Payment has been completely 'Paid':

NOTE: If the 'Payment' was not properly applied against the intended Invoice, even if the Payment was received from the Customer, the pending Payment will be showing up on the 'AR Cash Receipts' screen with the remaining Due Amount.

11e12291-f8bf-49ef-9f2e-03a8cbbddaee.title: How to Fix the SQL Permission Error 'VIEW SERVER PERFORMANCE STATE permission was denied' when Launching Traverse Server Manager on a New Server?
11e12291-f8bf-49ef-9f2e-03a8cbbddaee.content:
Problem
How to resolve the error below that appears while attempting to launch the Traverse Server Manager for a fresh install on the new Server?



===================================

An exception occurred while executing a Transact-SQL statement or batch.

===================================

An exception occurred while executing a Transact-SQL statement or batch. (Microsoft.SqlServer.ConnectionInfo)

------------------------------
Program Location:

at Microsoft.SqlServer.Management.Common.ServerConnection.GetExecuteReader(SqlCommand command)
at Microsoft.SqlServer.Management.Smo.ExecuteSql.GetDataReader(String query, SqlCommand& command)
at Microsoft.SqlServer.Management.Smo.DataProvider.SetConnectionAndQuery(ExecuteSql execSql, String query)
at Microsoft.SqlServer.Management.Smo.ExecuteSql.GetDataProvider(StringCollection query, Object con, StatementBuilder sb, RetriveMode rm)
at Microsoft.SqlServer.Management.Smo.SqlObjectBase.FillData(ResultType resultType, StringCollection sql, Object connectionInfo, StatementBuilder sb)
at Microsoft.SqlServer.Management.Smo.SqlObjectBase.FillDataWithUseFailure(SqlEnumResult sqlresult, ResultType resultType)
at Microsoft.SqlServer.Management.Smo.SqlObjectBase.BuildResult(EnumResult result)
at Microsoft.SqlServer.Management.Smo.SqlServer.GetData(EnumResult erParent)
at Microsoft.SqlServer.Management.Sdk.Sfc.Environment.GetData()
at Microsoft.SqlServer.Management.Sdk.Sfc.Environment.GetData(Request req, Object ci)
at Microsoft.SqlServer.Management.Sdk.Sfc.Enumerator.GetData(Object connectionInfo, Request request)
at Microsoft.SqlServer.Management.Smo.ExecutionManager.GetEnumeratorDataReader(Request req)
at Microsoft.SqlServer.Management.Smo.SqlSmoObject.GetInitDataReader(String[] fields, OrderBy[] orderby)
at Microsoft.SqlServer.Management.Smo.SqlSmoObject.ImplInitialize(String[] fields, OrderBy[] orderby)
at Microsoft.SqlServer.Management.Smo.SqlSmoObject.Initialize(Boolean allProperties)
at Microsoft.SqlServer.Management.Smo.SqlSmoObject.OnPropertyMissing(String propname, Boolean useDefaultValue)
at Microsoft.SqlServer.Management.Smo.PropertyCollection.RetrieveProperty(Int32 index, Boolean useDefaultOnMissingValue)
at Microsoft.SqlServer.Management.Smo.PropertyCollection.GetValueWithNullReplacement(String propertyName, Boolean throwOnNullValue, Boolean useDefaultOnMissingValue)
at Microsoft.SqlServer.Management.Smo.Server.get_Collation()
at TRAVERSE.Business.ServerManager.DatabaseMaster..ctor()
at TRAVERSE.Business.ServerManager.SystemDB..ctor()
at TRAVERSE.Client.ServerManager.CreateDBControl.Initialize()

===================================

VIEW SERVER PERFORMANCE STATE permission was denied on object 'server', database 'master'. (.Net SqlClient Data Provider)

------------------------------
For help, click: http://go.microsoft.com/fwlink?ProdName=Microsoft+SQL+Server&ProdVer=16.00.1000&EvtSrc=MSSQLServer&EvtID=300&LinkId=20476

------------------------------
Server Name: LOCALHOST
Error Number: 300
Severity: 14
State: 1
Line Number: 142

------------------------------
Program Location:

at Microsoft.SqlServer.Management.Common.ConnectionManager.ExecuteTSql(ExecuteTSqlAction action, Object execObject, DataSet fillDataSet, Boolean catchException)
at Microsoft.SqlServer.Management.Common.ServerConnection.GetExecuteReader(SqlCommand command)

Resolution
This error occurs when a SQL Server user or login lacks the required permission to access server-level performance-related views or properties, such as when trying to view server collation, memory info, CPU usage, or similar metadata.

The application (Traverse Server Manager) is trying to retrieve server-level info (like collation) from the master database, but the SQL login used to connect does not have VIEW SERVER STATE permission.

Resolution Steps:

Option 1: Grant Permission to the SQL Login:

If we're a sysadmin we can follow the below steps:

-
Open SQL Server Management Studio

-
Connect to the corresponding SQL Server

-
Run this command against the 'master' DB:

GRANT VIEW SERVER STATE TO [YourLoginName];

NOTE: Replace [YourLoginName] with the actual SQL login or database user (e.g., TraverseUser, domain\user, etc.)



Option 2: Manually Grant 'VIEW SERVER STATE' Permission:

i. Open SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS)
Log in using a sysadmin account.



ii. Expand the SQL Server Instance
In the Object Explorer (left panel), expand your server's name.



iii. Go to Security > Logins

-
-
Expand Security

-
Expand Logins

-
Right-click the Login used by Traverse

-
Choose Properties

-
In the Login Properties window:

-
Select Securables from the left menu.

-
Click Search… → choose The server → click OK

-
In the Securables list, scroll down to find View server state

-
Check the box under Grant

-
Click OK to save the changes.





Option 3: Use an Account with Higher Permissions

Use a sysadmin or elevated account to perform this action if you cannot change permissions directly.

Use the 'sa' login information to launch the TSM.

Optional Check: Verify Current Permissions:

We can verify if the current login has the required permission by running:

sqlCopyEditSELECT HAS_PERMS_BY_NAME(NULL, NULL, 'VIEW SERVER STATE');

If the result is 0, the login lacks the permission.

Note: This does not apply to just one database; it's a server-level permission.

c4e42e1c-36aa-466f-8553-1cff9c4fc573.title: How to resolve the error: 'The zip code is invalid' while attempting to upload the 1099 XML file in the Nelco portal?

The error indicates that a specific Vendor record contains an invalid ZIP code format. From the error message displayed during the upload, we need to take note of the “Recipient ID.” In this context, the Recipient ID corresponds to the Vendor Name in the system.

[Here the first 5 digits are to be retained, and the last 4-digit extension section need to remain blank.]

-

6. Output the updated data:

-
- Export the XML file again.
