However, this change would apply only for that specific export and would not update the Vendor master record. As a result, the same correction may need to be made again in future years if the Vendor record itself is not updated.

We need to follow the below steps on this:
1. Locate the required Vendor Record:



2. Update the 'Postal Code' field to meet the format: ##### with no additional character's present. And then hit on the 'Tab' key on the keyboard:



3. Then we can use the 'Output' icon to regenerate a new XML file:

After regenerating and exporting the XML file, the file should upload to the Nelco site without encountering the previous ZIP code validation error.

833e96e8-0d59-4cfd-8bef-9247ebda242e.title: Why is no GL Accounts returned despite setting GL Account Ranges in 'GL Statement Contents' Traverse?
833e96e8-0d59-4cfd-8bef-9247ebda242e.content:
Problem
The user configured a report with multiple filter conditions on the Account ID (GL Account) as follows:

Even though valid records exist within each of these ranges individually, the report returned no results. This raised concerns about whether the data was missing or if there was an issue with the report configuration.

Output Report:

Resolution
Explanation:
When multiple conditions are applied to the same field in a report, the system evaluates how these conditions interact with each other.
In this case, both conditions define distinct and non-overlapping ranges of Account IDs. One range ends at 110500, while the other begins at 159300, leaving a clear gap between them.
Because of this separation, there is no single Account ID that falls within both ranges simultaneously. As a result, the system is unable to identify any records that satisfy the combined criteria, leading to an empty report output.

Resolution:
The behavior observed is due to the use of the AND operator between the conditions, which requires that a record satisfy both ranges at the same time.
To retrieve records from both ranges, the conditions should be modified to use the OR operator instead:
Account ID is between 011070 and 110500
OR
Account ID is between 159300 and 204000

This change will allow the report to return records that fall within either of the specified ranges, thereby displaying the expected results.



Output:

How Conditionals Work in Traverse Reports?
When setting up filters in Traverse reports, conditionals determine how multiple criteria are evaluated together. Understanding how these operators behave is key to ensuring accurate report results.

1. AND Condition (Intersection Logic)
The AND operator requires that all conditions must be true at the same time for a record to be included.
- Think of this as finding the overlap (intersection) between conditions.
- If there is no overlap, no records will be returned.
Example:
- Account ID between 1000–2000
- AND Account ID between 1500–2500
👉 Result: Only records between 1500–2000 (common range)
Important Note:
If the ranges do not overlap (e.g., 1000–1200 AND 1300–1500), the result will be empty, even though each range has valid data.

2. OR Condition (Union Logic)
The OR operator requires that at least one condition must be true.
- Think of this as combining multiple sets of data (union).
- It retrieves records that match any of the conditions.
Example:
- Account ID between 1000–1200
- OR Account ID between 1300–1500
👉 Result: Records from both ranges are returned

09a80ad4-c54f-47bf-92c2-358791c1ada6.title: Why are 'Productivity Reports' of MFG-Production is Not Working?
09a80ad4-c54f-47bf-92c2-358791c1ada6.content:
Problem
The user reported issues with accessing the Productivity Reports of MFG-Production. They have already reviewed the permissions on the 'SM Groups', and still the reports remain inaccessible.

[These reports are specifically custom Excel-based reports integrated with TRAVERSE]

Resolution
Overview:

A brief overview regarding the current status of Productivity Reports within TRAVERSE is, at present, the Productivity Reports are no longer actively supported, and there have been no recent updates or maintenance from the Engineering team for several years. While these reports may still be visible within the application for legacy purposes, they are not part of the actively supported feature set.

These reports have been replaced due to the fact that the same information is already available through 'Interactive Views' and can be exported in the 'Excel' format as and when needed.



Support Scope and Billing:
Given the above, any efforts to investigate, troubleshoot, or enhance these reports would be considered outside regular support coverage. Such requests would typically be handled as billable services, unless there is an active maintenance agreement in place that specifically includes support for these customizations.



Recommended Alternative:
As a supported alternative, we recommend exploring Interactive Views within TRAVERSE. These views can often provide similar data insights in a more flexible and supported manner, without relying on deprecated or custom reporting structures.



Also, to avoid such confusion, it is recommended to leave these reports as hidden using the 'Hide' option available in the 'SM Application Menus.'

110f5992-c2f3-4f92-9a67-4cc8ea7d9c2e.title: How to add the 'Sum' or 'Total' field in the Interactive Views?
110f5992-c2f3-4f92-9a67-4cc8ea7d9c2e.content:
Problem
How to add the 'Sum' or 'Total' field in the Interactive Views?



Users may encounter situations in Traverse where they want to view the totals (such as Sum, Count, or Average) for specific columns within an Interactive View. While existing fields may already display totals, newly added fields, introduced using the Column Chooser, do not automatically show totals at the bottom of the grid.



This can lead to confusion, as users may assume that the system is not calculating totals correctly. The issue is not with the data or system functionality, but rather with how totals need to be manually enabled for each column within the Interactive View interface.

Resolution
To display totals for a newly added or existing column in an Interactive View, users need to manually enable the aggregation option. After adding the desired field using the Column Chooser, right-click on the corresponding column header. From the context menu, select the appropriate aggregation option such as Sum to display the total value at the bottom of the column.



Result:



In addition to Sum, users can also choose other aggregation options like Minimum (Min), Maximum (Max), Count, and Average, depending on their requirement.

Once selected, the chosen calculation will appear in the footer of the column, allowing users to easily analyze the data. This approach ensures flexibility, as users can customize which fields display totals based on their specific needs.

751d9b7d-186e-4d0f-ba3b-e2144432dea9.title: How does FIFO Costing works in Traverse?
751d9b7d-186e-4d0f-ba3b-e2144432dea9.content:
Problem
How FIFO Costing works in Traverse?

Resolution
What is FIFO Costing?

FIFO (First-In, First-Out) is an inventory valuation method where the oldest inventory items (first purchased or produced) are assumed to be sold or used first.

In simple terms: The cost of the earliest inventory is assigned to the earliest sales.



How FIFO Works:

- Inventory is tracked in layers, based on purchase dates and costs.
- Each time inventory is purchased, a new cost layer is created.
- When a sale occurs:
- The system pulls the cost from the oldest available layer first
- Then moves to the next layer, and so on



Example of FIFO:

Purchases:

- Jan 1: 100 units @ ₹10 = ₹1,000
- Jan 5: 100 units @ ₹12 = ₹1,200

Sale:

- Jan 10: Sold 150 units

FIFO Calculation:

- First 100 units → from Jan 1 stock → 100 × ₹10 = ₹1,000
- Next 50 units → from Jan 5 stock → 50 × ₹12 = ₹600

Total Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) = ₹1,600

Remaining Inventory:

- 50 units from Jan 5 → 50 × ₹12 = ₹600





Key Components of FIFO:

a. Cost Layers:

- Each purchase creates a new layer
- Layers are consumed in chronological order

b. Cost of Goods Sold:

- Calculated using the oldest inventory costs first

c. Ending Inventory:

- Based on the most recent purchase costs





Advantages of FIFO:

- Realistic Inventory Valuation
Ending inventory reflects recent market prices
- Better Profit Reporting in Inflation
Older (cheaper) costs are used → higher profit margins
- Logical Flow
Matches actual physical movement in many businesses (e.g., perishables)
- Compliance Friendly
Accepted under most accounting standards (including IFRS)



Considerations for FIFO:

- Higher Tax Liability (in Inflation)
Higher profits → higher taxable income
- Not Always Matching Reality
Some businesses don’t physically use oldest stock first
- Complex Tracking
Requires maintaining multiple inventory layers

When to Use FIFO?

FIFO is best suited for:

- Retail businesses
- Food & perishable goods industries
- Businesses where stock rotation is important
- Companies wanting inventory close to market value

d5892785-5a6e-4051-be53-082aa1678252.title: Error in Ship-To Address View – Duplicate Column in Dataset
d5892785-5a6e-4051-be53-082aa1678252.content:
Problem
When accessing Accounts Receivable → Interactive Views → Ship-To Address View in Aptean Traverse, the following SQL Server error is encountered:


“The column 'EDIShipToCode' was specified multiple times for 'ds'.”
=================================== SQL Server error encountered.

Please check the error details for more information.
Edition = Global
Build = 25304
User = xxxxx
LicenseServer = xxxx
Culture = English (United States) DefaultCompID = xxx SysDb =xxxx SessionID =xxxx MachineName = xxxx ===================================
The column 'EDIShipToCode' was specified multiple times for 'ds'. (.Net SqlClient Data Provider)

For help, click: http://go.microsoft.com/fwlink?ProdName=Microsoft%20SQL%20Server&ProdVer=15.00.4326&EvtSrc=MSSQLServer&EvtID=8156&LinkId=20476

Server Name: xxxx
Error Number: xx
Severity: 16
State: 1
Line Number: 13 Program Location: at TRAVERSE.Client.ViewControlBase.OnProcessCompleted()
TRAVERSE.Client.ViewControlBase.TaskCompleted(Exception processError, Boolean cancelled)

This error prevents the Ship-To Address View from loading.

Resolution
The issue is caused by duplicate column definitions within the dataset (ds).
In the base environment, fields such as EDIShipToCode, EDIShipLeadDays, and EDIDfltLocId are standard fields already present in the view dbo.trav_tblArShipTo_view.
In the customer environment, these same fields have been configured as Custom Fields ({CF}) and assigned to tblArShipTo through Design Studio.
As a result, the dataset retrieves these fields both from the base view and from the custom field configuration, leading to duplication and the SQL Server error.



Perform the following steps to remove duplicate field definitions:
1. Verify Base View
- Confirm that the view dbo.trav_tblArShipTo_view contains the fields:
- EDIShipToCode

- EDIShipLeadDays

- EDIDfltLocId

Use the below query in the query builder to see the available columns,
SELECT COLUMN_NAME
FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS
WHERE TABLE_NAME = 'trav_tblArShipTo_view'
AND TABLE_SCHEMA = 'dbo';
2. Open Design Studio
- Launch Traverse Design Studio.

- Navigate to Custom Fields → Manage.

3. Remove Duplicate Custom Fields
- Identify whether the following fields exist as Custom Fields:
- EDIShipToCode

- EDIShipLeadDays

- EDIDfltLocId

- If present, delete these fields from the Manage section.

4. Remove Field Assignments
- Navigate to Custom Fields → Assign.

- Locate assignments for the table tblArShipTo.

- Remove any assignments related to the above fields.

5. Save Changes
- Save all changes in Design Studio.

- Close Design Studio.

6. Validate
- Open Traverse Global.

- Navigate to Accounts Receivable → Interactive Views → Ship-To Address View.

- Confirm that the view loads without error.

bff39d33-9e8d-4ba1-8de8-86d67bc812be.title: How to Create a New Inventory Item Using Traverse API (Required Fields)
bff39d33-9e8d-4ba1-8de8-86d67bc812be.content:
Problem
Overview
This article provides step-by-step instructions to create a new Inventory (IN) item using the API in Aptean Traverse with only the required fields.

Prerequisites
- A valid user account configured under System Manager (SM) → User Accounts

- Access to the Traverse Global API (Swagger UI)

- Company ID available from the Traverse application

Resolution
1. Access the Traverse API
- Open a web browser

- Navigate to: http://localhost/TraverseGlobalAPI/swagger/ui/index

- Log in using your Traverse credentials

2. Locate the Inventory Item Endpoint
- In Swagger UI, navigate to the IN Item section

- You will see the following available operations:
- GET

- POST

- PUT

- DELETE



3. Select the POST Method
- Click on the POST method (used to create a new item)

- Click “Try it out”

4. Provide Request Body
In the Request Body section, enter the following JSON with required fields:


{
"item_id": "TESTITEM001",
"description": "Test Item",
"item_type": "Nonserialized",
"item_status": "Active",
"base_uom": "EA",
"default_uom": "EA",
"units": [
{
"unit": "EA",
"conversion_factor": 1
}
],
"locations": [
{
"location_id": "MAIN",
"location_status": "Active",
"account_code": "01"
}
]
}


5. Provide Required Parameters
- Enter the Company ID (mandatory field)
- This can be obtained from the Traverse application

6. Execute the Request
- Click Execute

7. Validate the Result
- If successful, the API will return a success response

- Verify the item creation in Traverse:
- Navigate to IN → Setup and Maintenance → Items

- Search for TESTITEM001

Result
A new inventory item will be successfully created using the Traverse API with the minimum required fields.

7a1a12a6-77c8-4fff-9240-9cf73631ff8f.title: Why do we observe discrepancy between 'Postrun' Numbers in 'GL Transaction View' and 'GL Post to Master' Activities?
7a1a12a6-77c8-4fff-9240-9cf73631ff8f.content:
Problem
Users have observed that the ‘Postrun’ numbers appearing in the ‘GL Transaction View’ screen do not align with the ‘Postrun’ numbers displayed within the ‘Activity’ section of the ‘GL Post to Master’ process.

This discrepancy has caused confusion when reconciling postings and tracking the flow of journal entries from source modules into the General Ledger master records.

Resolution
The difference in ‘Postrun’ numbers occurs because the ‘Postrun’ value shown in the ‘GL Transaction View’ is specific to the individual module posting, not to the ‘GL Post to Master’ process. This means that:
- Each module (such as AR, AP, or Inventory) assigns its own Postrun ID when transactions are generated or posted.
- The GL Transaction View reflects the Postrun number corresponding to that module’s posting process, not the one from the final GL Post to Master posting.
- The ‘Source’ field in the transaction plays a key role in identifying where the transaction originated and must be reviewed to understand which module’s posting the Postrun pertains to.
- This is the reason we can locate 'Postrun' numbers even for entries that were not posted through the 'GL Post to Master'


In the case of manual postings, such as those with a source code beginning with “M” (e.g., M1, M0, MA, etc.), the Postrun number represents the posting event of writing manual journal entries from the ‘GL Transactions’ screen to the ‘GL Edit Transactions’ screen. These manual entries, along with their associated Postrun identifiers, remain in the ‘GL Edit Transactions’ screen until they are finally posted using ‘GL Post to Master’.


The ‘Posted’ field in the ‘GL Transaction View’ clearly indicates whether an entry has been successfully posted to the GL master table:
- Yes: The transaction has been posted to master.
- No: The transaction is still pending posting in master.

633c7feb-a815-4aa2-be96-73d46e646a61.title: Controlling Availability of Items in Receiving Bins
633c7feb-a815-4aa2-be96-73d46e646a61.content:
Problem
Why are items received into a receiving bin showing as available for picking or sales? How can I prevent items in a receiving bin from being used to satisfy demand?

Cause
By default, receiving bins do not restrict availability. As a result, any inventory placed in these bins is immediately treated as available for transactions such as sales orders or transfers.

Resolution
OVERVIEW:
In Warehouse Management, items received into a receiving-type bin are automatically considered in stock. This means they are:
- Included in on-hand quantities

- Available for picking/issuing to fulfill demand

This is standard system behavior.

SOLUTION:
If you do not want items in receiving bins to be available for demand, you can configure the bin type to place quantities on hold.
Steps to Configure:
- Navigate to WM Bin Type

- Locate and select the Receiving Bin Type

- Enable the Quantity On Hold (Y/N) checkbox

- Save the changes


RESULT:

Once the Quantity On Hold option is enabled:
- Items in receiving bins will still be:
- Included in on-hand quantities

- But will NOT be available for:
- Picking

- Issuing

- Sales fulfillment

Example: I have an Item in a receiving bin which is marked as On-hold.

Now, when I attempt to create a sales order with that item, I would get this error message. This message ideally means that the item is not available to be sold.
You can confirm that by looking at the Inventory > Item Availability view. The On-hand would contain the qty whereas the Available would be zero.
KEY NOTES:
- This setup is useful when inventory needs to be inspected or verified before being released for use

- It helps prevent premature allocation of inventory

- Ensure this setting aligns with your warehouse and receiving process


IMPORTANT BEHAVIOUR OF QTY ON HOLD:
Marking the Qty On Hold (Y/N) checkbox means that the contents of the bin type are unavailable. When a bin type is set to Qty On Hold = Yes, any items stored in that bin will not appear in the available on-hand quantities.
This behavior is reflected in Item Availability when viewed from the Sales Order screen Task Pane.
For example, if you have 10 units of an item in a receiving bin marked as Qty On Hold, and no stock is available in any other bins, the system will display a warning indicating that there are no available quantities when demand is entered.
However, in the Task Pane > Bins tab, you will still be able to see the 10 units in the bin, along with an indication that the bin is marked as Qty On Hold.

4f600af6-3c68-4688-a201-ba031ec3b79d.title: Increasing SQL Server Memory and Validating Performance
4f600af6-3c68-4688-a201-ba031ec3b79d.content:
Problem
This article outlines how to increase memory allocation for SQL Server and validate performance improvements from the SQL Server side.

Resolution
Step 1: Check Current Memory Configuration

Run the below query:



EXEC sp_configure 'show advanced options', 1;
RECONFIGURE;

EXEC sp_configure 'max server memory (MB)';
EXEC sp_configure 'min server memory (MB)';

Step 2: Decide Memory Allocation

General guideline:

- Leave 4–6 GB (or more depending on server size) for OS and other processes
- Allocate remaining memory to SQL Server

Example:

- Total RAM: 32 GB
- SQL allocation: ~24–26 GB

Step 3: Update Max Server Memory



EXEC sp_configure 'max server memory (MB)', 24576; -- Example: 24 GB
RECONFIGURE;



(Optional – usually not required)



EXEC sp_configure 'min server memory (MB)', 8192;
RECONFIGURE;



Step 4: Validate Memory Usage

Check SQL Server Memory Consumption



SELECT
total_physical_memory_kb/1024 AS TotalMemoryMB,
available_physical_memory_kb/1024 AS AvailableMemoryMB,
system_memory_state_desc
FROM sys.dm_os_sys_memory;





SELECT
physical_memory_in_use_kb/1024 AS SQLMemoryMB,
large_page_allocations_kb,
locked_page_allocations_kb
FROM sys.dm_os_process_memory;



Step 5: Check Buffer Cache Usage



SELECT
COUNT(*) * 8 / 1024 AS BufferCacheMB
FROM sys.dm_os_buffer_descriptors;



Step 6: Validate Performance Improvements

1. Page Life Expectancy (PLE)



SELECT cntr_value AS PageLifeExpectancy
FROM sys.dm_os_performance_counters
WHERE counter_name = 'Page life expectancy';



- Healthy: Generally > 300 (higher is better)

2. Memory Grants Pending



SELECT cntr_value AS MemoryGrantsPending
FROM sys.dm_os_performance_counters
WHERE counter_name = 'Memory Grants Pending';



- Should be 0 ideally

3. Buffer Cache Hit Ratio



SELECT
(a.cntr_value * 1.0 / b.cntr_value) * 100 AS BufferCacheHitRatio
FROM sys.dm_os_performance_counters a
JOIN sys.dm_os_performance_counters b
ON a.counter_name = 'Buffer cache hit ratio'
AND b.counter_name = 'Buffer cache hit ratio base';



- Healthy: > 90%

4. Wait Statistics (Memory Pressure Indicators)



SELECT TOP 10
wait_type, wait_time_ms, signal_wait_time_ms
FROM sys.dm_os_wait_stats
ORDER BY wait_time_ms DESC;



Watch for:

- RESOURCE_SEMAPHORE → memory pressure
- PAGEIOLATCH → disk bottleneck

Step 7: Monitor After Change

- Monitor for 24–48 hours
- Check:
- CPU usage
- Query performance
- Blocking/long-running queries
- Application response time

Best Practices

- Do NOT set memory equal to total RAM
- Always leave buffer for OS
- Avoid frequent changes unless required
- Combine with index/query optimization for best results

e7c45fd9-7298-4eb2-a5f1-09c2435f1484.title: Unable to Delete Confirmed Work Orders and Process to Reverse Using Unbuild Transaction
e7c45fd9-7298-4eb2-a5f1-09c2435f1484.content:
Problem
Users have identified that Work Orders listed under:
Bill of Materials > Work Orders > Post Work Orders
need to be deleted. However, these work orders are no longer available in the Confirm/Cancel Work Orders screen.

Resolution
Once a work order is confirmed, it transitions from a pending state to a ready for posting state and is moved to the Post Work Orders screen.
At this stage:
- The work order is considered processed within the system workflow.

- It cannot be deleted or cancelled using standard system functionality.



To reverse the impact of a confirmed work order, an Unbuild transaction must be performed. This process reverses the inventory changes by:
- Reducing the quantity of finished goods

- Returning the component items back into inventory



Steps to Perform an Unbuild Transaction
- Navigate to: Bill of Materials > Work Orders > Issue Work Orders

- In the Type field, change the selection to: "Unbuild"

- Enter the required details:
- Work Order Number (the one to be reversed)

- Quantity to Unbuild

- Transaction Date

- Fiscal Period

- Click Enter to load the work order details.

- Review the information and proceed to Issue the work order.

- After issuing, navigate to: Confirm/Cancel Work Orders
- Confirm the Unbuild work order

- Finally, navigate to: Post Work Orders
- Post the Unbuild transaction to complete the reversal

4deb68d7-a239-48b1-9565-7099ab3656f0.title: How to Generate a List of Top 10 Customers by Sales for a Fiscal Year?
4deb68d7-a239-48b1-9565-7099ab3656f0.content:
Problem
The User requested a method to identify the top 10 customers who generated the highest sales within a specific fiscal year.



The requirement is to:

- Analyse total sales per customer
- Filter results based on a selected fiscal year
- Identify and list the top 10 customers with the highest sales values



However, there is no direct out-of-the-box report or functionality available within the application that automatically provides a ranked “Top N” customer list based on total sales.

Resolution
Analysis:
The system provides access to customer sales data through the AR Summary History View, which contains aggregated sales information by customer.
While this view allows:
- Filtering by fiscal year
- Viewing customer-level totals
Traverse does not provide built-in functionality to:
- Sort by total sales within the application interface
- Automatically extract the top 10 customers
[NOTE: This feature of sorting based on Sales is not available until Build 26065]

Resolution:
To achieve the desired result, the following steps can be followed:
Step 1: Access AR Summary History View
- Navigate to the AR Summary History View
- Apply filters to select the required Fiscal Year

Step 2: Export Data
- Export the filtered data to Microsoft Excel

Step 3: Sort Data in Excel
- Open the exported file
- Convert the table of contents into a table:

- Identify the column representing Total Sales (Ext Price)
- Sort the data in descending order based on Total Sales

Step 4: Identify Top 10 Customers
- Select the top 10 rows after sorting
- These represent the customers with the highest sales for the selected fiscal year

Outcome:
Using this approach, the client can successfully identify the top 10 customers by total sales for any given fiscal year, despite the limitation within the application’s reporting capabilities.

Limitations:
- Requires manual export and processing in Excel
- No in-application ranking or Top N filtering available
- Dependent on user performing correct sorting externally

785d76ae-c1f1-4c8e-90a1-72463abaa84b.title: How Does 'Adjustment Base' and 'Type' affect Pricing in Sales Orders?
785d76ae-c1f1-4c8e-90a1-72463abaa84b.content:
Problem
How Does 'Adjustment Base' and 'Type' affect Pricing in Sales Orders?



Users observe that the price in the Sales Orders screen is different from the value entered in the Amount field within Customer Pricing. The final price appears to be either higher or lower than expected, depending on the configuration.

Resolution
Explanation:

The final Unit Price is calculated based on two key factors:

-
Adjustment Base

-
Adjustment Type



1. Adjustment Base:

This determines the starting value for calculation. Examples include:

- Standard Cost
- Base Cost
- Average Price
- Base Price
- List Price
- Minimum Price
- Last Cost
- Calculated Price

The Adjustment Base values can be observed from the 'IN Items' screen as shown below:



2. Adjustment Type:

a. Amount:

- Positive value: Added to the base
- Negative value: Subtracted from the base

Examples:

Example 1 (Amount – Positive):

- Adjustment Base (Standard Cost) = $2
- Adjustment Type = Amount
- Amount Entered = +$5

Final Price = $2 + $5 = $7



Example 2 (Amount – Negative):

- Adjustment Base = $5
- Amount Entered = -$2

Final Price = $5 - $2 = $3

b. Percent:

- Applied as a percentage increase or decrease
- System automatically divides by 100

Example:

- Adjustment Base = $10
- Adjustment Type = Percent
- Percent Entered = 50 (i.e., 50%)

Calculation: 50% of $10 = $5

Final Price = $10 + $5 = $15



Key Takeaway:

- The Adjustment Base provides the starting value
- The Adjustment Type (Amount or Percent) determines how the entered value is applied
- The final price is always calculated based on both, unless the Adjustment Base is set to “No Base”

e683e069-f732-43ce-9050-d0b8750206e6.title: How to ensure GL Account from 'AP Vendor-Defaults' populates in AP Transactions?
e683e069-f732-43ce-9050-d0b8750206e6.content:
Problem
The client observed that even after assigning a GL Account in the "Defaults tab" of 'AP Vendors', the GL Account was not automatically populating in AP Transactions when entering non-inventory purchases.

This led to confusion, as the expected behavior was for the system to default the configured GL Account during transaction entry.

Resolution
Let us consider the below 'Vendor' with the Default GL Account configured as follows:



The GL Account will not auto-populate immediately upon entering the header-level information in the AP Transaction.

For the system to populate the GL Account, at least one of the required line-level detail fields must be entered, such as Description, Location ID, Tax Class, Quantity, or Cost. If none of these fields are populated, Traverse interprets this as no transaction detail being entered and, therefore, does not default the GL Account.



If the none of these columns are visible by default, it can be added using the Column Chooser, as needed:



Once one of the mentioned columns is added and an appropriate value is entered (or other required fields are populated), the GL Account will populate automatically as expected.



In this example, the User can just enter the 'Ext Cost' and hit on the 'Tab' key on the keyboard to populate the corresponding 'GL Account':



This behavior is by design. The GL Account configured in the AP Vendor Defaults is intended to populate only when entering transactions for non-inventory items or items not selected from the System Manager Description list, and when sufficient transaction detail is provided.



The GL Account specified in the vendor record represents the account to be debited for such non-inventory purchases and is triggered based on the transaction details entered at the line level.

b0d8f4da-a99a-449d-b5fb-140c48645edf.title: Why are 'PC Distribution Codes' displayed instead of 'AR Distribution Codes' in the "PC Edit Billing Screen"?
b0d8f4da-a99a-449d-b5fb-140c48645edf.content:
Problem
The Users are encountering an issue in the PC Edit Billing screen within Traverse.



When navigating to: Applications -> Project Costing -> Billing -> Edit Billings, the Distribution Code dropdown is expected to display only AR Distribution Codes. However, the system is currently displaying both PC Distribution Codes and AR Distribution Codes in the dropdown list.



Although the system does not allow users to select these PC Distribution Codes, their presence in the dropdown creates confusion, making it difficult for users to identify and select the correct AR Distribution Code.



Impact on Client:

- Users are unable to easily identify the correct Distribution Code
- Presence of incorrect (PC) codes causes visual confusion
- Impacts efficiency during billing updates
- Increases risk of incorrect selection attempts or delays

Resolution
Root Cause:

The issue occurs because the Distribution Code dropdown in the PC Edit Billing screen is incorrectly referencing PC Distribution Codes and AR Distribution Codes instead of only AR Distribution Codes.

While the backend validation restricts selection to valid AR codes, the UI still displays PC codes, leading to inconsistency between display logic and selection logic.

Steps to Reproduce:

- Navigate to: Applications -> Project Costing -> Billing -> Edit Billings
- Open an existing transaction
- Click on Update
- Click on the Distribution Code dropdown
- Observe that:
- PC Distribution Codes are listed along with AR codes
- When PC codes are selected, Traverse would throw the below error, but still available for selection



Resolution:

A change has been implemented to correct the behavior of the Distribution Code field:

- The dropdown has been updated to only reference AR Distribution Codes
- The maintenance (double-click) functionality already correctly points to AR Distribution Codes
- The inconsistency between display and selection has been resolved



Fix Details:

- Change Request: DEV-289932
- Fix Availability: Included in Build 26065
- TFS URL: https://dev.azure.com/TraverseERP/b746159b-5617-4616-8466-ae9d6a61d66f/_workitems/edit/99440



Recommendation:

Customers experiencing this issue are advised to:

- Upgrade to Build 26065 or later, where the issue has been resolved
- Until then, proceed cautiously while selecting Distribution Codes, ensuring only valid AR codes are used

b5cddd98-32b9-4795-a8c8-8972c7149517.title: SO Transactions Ship to ID Lookup Not Saving Column Changes
b5cddd98-32b9-4795-a8c8-8972c7149517.content:
Problem
The Ship To lookup in SO transactions screen was not saving new columns added from the column chooser on the Ship to tab.

Resolution
The issue occurs when using Sales Order (SO) transactions, where any user-added columns on Ship To tab are not saved and the layout reverts to the default configuration.
Specifically, on the Ship To tab, clicking the ellipses (…) next to Ship-To ID normally displays two default columns: Ship-To ID and Name.

Users can add additional columns by right-clicking on the column header area, selecting Column Chooser, and dragging the desired columns into the layout.

Once saved, these custom column layouts are expected to persist across user logouts and logins.
This functionality was working as expected up to Build 25199. However, in Builds 25262 and 25304, the column layout changes were not retained, causing the layout to reset to default each time. This behavior has been identified as a product bug in those builds.
The issue has been fixed in Service Pack 7/ Build 25353. Customers experiencing this behavior should be advised to update to Build 25353 to resolve the issue and ensure that custom column layouts are saved and retained as expected.

04a9a1d9-4ef2-46c1-af14-c94ea3b573d6.title: RemoteApp Security Prompt & Drive Redirection Behavior After Windows Updates
04a9a1d9-4ef2-46c1-af14-c94ea3b573d6.content:
Problem
User getting below window when trying to Lauch rdp of traverse

Cause
This is due to recent Microsoft security enhancements introduced in Remote Desktop components.

As part of the April 2026 cumulative updates:

- Windows 10: KB5082200
- Windows 11: KB5083769, KB5082052

Microsoft has implemented additional protections to mitigate risks associated with malicious .rdp files.

Resolution
Option 1: User Action (Immediate)

Users can proceed by:

- Reviewing the security prompt
- Selecting required options (e.g., Drives)
- Continuing with the connection

Option 2: Registry Configuration (Client-Side)

To suppress the warning prompt, the following registry setting can be applied on client machines:

- Open Registry Editor
-
Navigate to:



HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Terminal Services\Client



-
Create or modify:



Name: RedirectionWarningDialogVersion
Type: REG_DWORD
Value: 1



Note: This change must be applied on each client machine.

95f9754e-707e-4397-b124-5ee660677548.title: Why does the 'Amount' entered in 'SO Customer Pricing' is different from the ones showing up in 'SO Orders' screen?
95f9754e-707e-4397-b124-5ee660677548.content:
Problem
Users have configured pricing in the Customer Pricing screen by entering a value in the Amount field, but the same value is not directly reflected as the Unit Price in the Sales Orders (SO Orders) screen.
Instead, the price appearing in the Sales Order is different from the value entered, leading to confusion regarding how pricing is calculated.

Let us consider an example, where the Pricing is configured as $7. However, in the 'SO Orders' screen, it shows a different value:

Resolution
Root Cause:
The final price in Sales Orders is not solely determined by the Amount field. It is influenced by:
- Adjustment Base
- Adjustment Type (Amount / Percent)
If the Adjustment Base is set to anything other than “No Base”, the system uses the selected base value (e.g., Standard Cost, Base Price, etc.) and then applies the adjustment on top of it.

In this example, we can see that the 'Adjustment Base' is set to 'Standard Cost':

With this setup, since the ‘Type’ is configured as ‘Amount’ and the value entered is $7, this amount is added to the Standard Cost of the Item ID as defined in the ‘IN Items’ screen.
As a result, the Sales Order reflects a total Unit Price of $15 (i.e., $8 Standard Cost + $7 adjustment).

Resolution:
To ensure that the value entered in the Amount field is directly reflected as the final Unit Price in the Sales Orders screen:
We need to Update the following:
- Adjustment Base = No Base
- Adjustment Type = Amount
Behavior:
- The system will ignore any price included in the 'Adjustment Base'
- The value entered in the Amount field becomes the final price


Outcome:
The price entered in Customer Pricing will now directly populate in the Sales Order without any additional calculations.

5aa2271b-3803-49be-92f4-ee57d8335645.title: How to Remove an Unwanted Entry from the ‘BR Cleared Transactions’ Screen?
5aa2271b-3803-49be-92f4-ee57d8335645.content:
Problem
Users may encounter situations where unwanted transactions appear in the Bank Reconciliation (BR) Cleared Transactions screen.

Resolution
Understanding the System Behavior:
In Traverse, cleared transactions are always linked to a specific reconciliation statement. Therefore:
- Individual cleared entries cannot be deleted directly
- The only way to remove them is by addressing the entire statement they belong to

Resolution Overview:
To remove unwanted entries, the recommended approach is:
- Create a temporary reconciliation statement
- Clear the unwanted entries into that statement
- Purge the temporary statement
Once the statement is purged, all associated cleared transactions are permanently removed from the system.

Important Warning (Before Proceeding):
The “Purge Cleared Transactions” feature is permanent and irreversible.
- The statement and all associated cleared transactions will be deleted
- There will be no recovery option
- No trace will remain unless Activity logs are reviewed
This should only be performed:
- After careful validation
- With proper approvals (Accounting/Audit teams)
- When data is confirmed to be unnecessary or incorrect

Step-by-Step Resolution:
Step 1: Create a Temporary Statement:
Navigation: Bank Reconciliation -> Reconciliation -> Cleared Transactions
- Create a temporary reconciliation statement. We can proceed with entering the 'Statement Date', Beginning Date and Ending Date of the Statement to create a temporary one.

- Clear only the unwanted transactions under this statement:


Step 2: Update Statement Status to Reconciled
Before purging, the statement must be in Reconciled status:
- Use Change Status option to do the same

Step 3: Purge the Statement
Navigation: Bank Reconciliation -> Reconciliation -> Purge Cleared Transactions
Apply Filters Carefully:
This is the most critical step
- For a specific unwanted entry: - Filter by Bank Account ID + Statement Date

Always double-check filters to avoid deleting valid data

Execute Purge:
- Select the confirmation checkbox
- Click OK

Outcome:
- The selected statement will be permanently deleted
- All unwanted cleared transactions within that statement will be removed
- Entries will no longer appear in the BR Cleared Transactions screen

When to Use This Approach:
- Incorrect reconciliation created
- Unwanted cleared entries need removal
- Cleanup of obsolete reconciliation data

When NOT to Use:
- If data is required for audit/compliance
- If unsure about impact
- Without proper approvals

Best Practices / Recommendation:
- Always test in a non-production environment first
- Take database backup before purge
- Confirm with Finance/Accounting teams
- Use precise filters to avoid accidental data loss

Summary:
Since cleared transactions cannot be removed individually, the correct approach is to isolate them within a statement and purge that statement. This ensures clean removal while maintaining system integrity.

e872cb92-dac2-4a32-b5c0-e251245d4046.title: RemoteApp Security Warning
e872cb92-dac2-4a32-b5c0-e251245d4046.content:
Problem
Multiple people are receiving the attached Microsoft RemoteApp security warning prompt that appears before launching a published remote application

Resolution
The message you are seeing is a standard Windows security prompt that appears when connecting to a RemoteApp (RDP) application. It is designed to verify the publisher of the remote connection before allowing access.
This is expected, especially when accessing the application from a different network than the one hosting the resource, as part of normal security validation.
There is no need to worry; the connection is safe, and users can proceed by clicking Connect to access the application.
If users would like to avoid seeing this prompt in future sessions, then they can select “Remember my choices” before connecting.

cf317fb2-8ce7-4ee4-a085-401620a88fa5.title: Sales/COGS Accounts Setup in Accounts Receivable
cf317fb2-8ce7-4ee4-a085-401620a88fa5.content:
Problem
How to setup Sales/COGS Accounts in Accounts Receivable?

Resolution
Overview
The Sales/COGS Accounts function is used to define account codes that link Sales and Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) accounts from the General Ledger to transactions in Accounts Receivable. When transactions are posted, the system uses these account codes to automatically distribute amounts to the appropriate GL accounts.
Purpose
Assigning Sales and COGS accounts to transactions ensures accurate financial posting to the General Ledger. It standardizes revenue and cost tracking across transactions
Navigation
Go to: Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup and Maintenance > Sales/COGS Accounts
Creating a Sales/COGS Account Code
Click New on the toolbar
Enter an Account Code in the Acct Code field
Enter a Description for the account code
If Accounts Receivable is interfaced with General Ledger, select the GL Sales Account and GL COGS Account from the chart of accounts
If Accounts Receivable is not interfaced with General Ledger, manually enter the GL Sales and GL COGS account numbers
Once done, Click Save to save the record.
Editing a Sales/COGS Account Code
Select the required Account Code
Modify the necessary fields
Click Save to apply changes
Deleting a Sales/COGS Account Code
Select the Account Code to delete
Click Delete or press F3 on the Keyboard.
Confirm the deletion when prompted
Note: Ensure the account code is not in use before deleting

Producing a Sales/COGS Accounts List
Click Print Preview, and you should be able to review the report in the preview screen
If you would like to print, you can use the Print option to generate a hard copy.
Key Notes
Sales/COGS Account Codes act as a bridge between AR transactions and GL accounts. They ensure accurate revenue and cost allocation. Proper setup helps maintain consistent financial reporting.

6d914da7-c3ed-4a99-9adb-0934e831ed03.title: How to Stop State Tax Withholding for an Employee in Traverse
6d914da7-c3ed-4a99-9adb-0934e831ed03.content:
Problem
The client needs to stop state tax withholding for a specific employee in Traverse. Resolution
Steps to Configure Exclusion:
- Navigate to the Employee Maintenance / Tax Setup section in Traverse.

- Open the relevant employee record.

- Go to the Tax Setup area.

- Click on the Exclusions button.

- Click the “+” (Add) button to create a new exclusion.

- Select the appropriate State Tax Code from the dropdown list.

- Save the record to apply the changes.

Validation Steps:
- Create a manual check for the employee.

- Verify that state tax is no longer being calculated.

- Delete the manual check after testing is complete.

Important Notes:
- Applying a tax exclusion may impact the employee’s W-2 reporting.

- Ensure that this change complies with your organization’s tax and legal requirements.

- It is recommended to validate the setup before processing live payroll.

264280f0-2349-47a5-8e29-1f5b4c414110.title: Backflush standard process

How to backflush, steps for standard backflush process

The backflush process is designed to automatically record material consumption, routing steps, and finished goods based on the Bill of Materials (BOM), assuming production occurred as planned.

ea02cd11-5d91-4608-a0fb-32ae42c3a8e1.title: how to add gl accounts are determined and validated in the system
ea02cd11-5d91-4608-a0fb-32ae42c3a8e1.content:
Problem
how can we check if GL accounts are set up correctly and how the system decides which GL account to use?

Resolution
The system determines GL accounts based on default configurations set in different modules, not from a single validation tool or report.
to understand and verify GL behavior, review the following areas:

- accounts receivable distribution codes → controls AR-related accounts

96c6b73e-df1a-4ddc-ac28-a54e8432502b.title: Understanding and Using Recurring Adjustments in BR
96c6b73e-df1a-4ddc-ac28-a54e8432502b.content:
Problem
How to set up the recurring adjustments in Bank reconciliation?

Resolution
Overview
Recurring Adjustments are routine bank-related transactions that occur regularly, such as:
- Monthly service charges

- Overdraft fees

- Stop payment fees

This feature allows you to automate these entries, saving time and ensuring consistency in your financial records.

Purpose
- The Recurring Adjustments function is used to:

- Set up frequently occurring bank transactions

- Automatically populate adjustment details during entry

- Ensure proper General Ledger (GL) posting with balanced entries


Key Concept
Every recurring adjustment must be balanced, meaning:
- It must include both debit and credit entries

You can split the offset across multiple accounts
- Example: A $100 adjustment can be distributed as:

- $40 to one GL account

- $60 to another GL account


How to Create a Recurring Adjustment
1. Initial Setup
- Select the appropriate Bank Account ID

- Click New (+) to create a new record


2. Enter Header Details
- Payment No: Enter a unique identifier (e.g., OVERDRAFT)

- Description: Enter a meaningful description (used in GL)

- Reference: Optional, for tracking/search purposes

- Currency ID (if applicable): Select the appropriate currency


3. Enter Adjustment Amount
- Input the amount in the Amount field:

- Use a negative value for charges against the bank account

- Use a positive value for additions

- Select the GL Account for the adjustment


4. Enter Distribution (Offset Entries)
In the detail section:
The system will auto-populate:
- Default GL account

- Description and reference

- Enter offsetting entries:

- If the main amount is negative (credit) → enter a Debit

- If the main amount is positive (debit) → enter a Credit

You can:
- Accept the suggested balancing amount

- Or split across multiple GL accounts


5. Validate Balancing
Ensure:
Total Debits = Total Credits
The system displays:
Debit Total
Credit Total
Balance differences (if any)
You cannot save an unbalanced recurring adjustment.

6. Save the Record
Click Save to finalize the recurring adjustment

Editing a Recurring Adjustment
Select the Bank Account ID
Modify required fields
Click Save
The changes will be saved automatically.

Deleting a Recurring Adjustment
Select the Bank Account ID
Choose the adjustment from Recur Adj ID
Click Delete
Confirm the prompt
Using Recurring Adjustments
Once the setup is configured,
- Navigate to the Transactions screen → Adjustments tab

- Manually select the recurring adjustment by pulling the Payment No from the list

- Once selected, the system will populate the predefined details into the transaction

Note: The recurring adjustment will not auto-populate unless it is explicitly selected via the Payment No.
Reporting
To view a list of recurring adjustments:
Use the Master Lists > Recurring Adjustments List function
Important Notes
Only active currencies can be used
Exchange rates are applied automatically (if multicurrency is enabled)
Descriptions and references are posted to the General Ledger
Unbalanced entries will be reset or require correction before saving

98c6d12f-0ffa-4e9e-a46f-0d8e7f69e863.title: Understanding Missing Bank Reconciliation Statements
98c6d12f-0ffa-4e9e-a46f-0d8e7f69e863.content:
Problem
Why are previously available bank reconciliation statements missing from the system?

Resolution
Cause:
This behavior occurs when the Purge Cleared Transactions process has been executed.
The purge process permanently removes:
- Reconciled bank statements

- Associated cleared transaction records

Once this process is completed, the purged data is no longer available for viewing within bank reconciliation screens.

How to Verify
To confirm whether a purge activity was performed:
- Navigate to the BR Purge Cleared Transactions section (Applications > Bank Reconciliation > Reconciliation > Purge Cleared Transactions)

- Open the Activity Log

- Review the details, including:

- User ID who performed the purge

- Date and time of execution

- Workstation information

This log will help identify when and by whom the purge was completed.
Important Notes
Only reconciled statements can be purged
Open (unreconciled) statements cannot be purged
For example:
Statements dated 6/30/2025 and 8/30/2025 remain in the system because they are still open and have not been reconciled

All previously reconciled statements were eligible for purge and were removed during the process.

Impact
Purged statements cannot be recovered from within the application
Historical reconciliation data associated with those statements will no longer be accessible

Recommendation / Best Practice
Before running the purge process, ensure that:
Historical records are no longer needed for reporting or auditing
Before purging cleared transactions, clear all the applicable transactions, then print and verify the Reconciliation Report.
Necessary backups or reports have been saved externally
Restrict access to the purge function to authorized users only to prevent unintended data loss

0aab3ed5-8787-4198-b513-47d7e16a7865.title: Incorrect Terms Discount Posting to Default GL Account in Cash Receipts
0aab3ed5-8787-4198-b513-47d7e16a7865.content:
Problem
Customers have reported that when posting payments through Cash Receipts, the terms discount amount is automatically being posted to an incorrect General Ledger (GL) account (e.g., 350179) instead of the desired account (e.g., 350171).
This behavior has been observed across multiple customers, where the system defaults to a predefined discount account during Accounts Receivable payment posting.

Resolution
To update the default GL account used for terms discounts during Cash Receipts posting, follow the steps below:
- Navigate to: System Manager > Business Rules > Accounts Receivable > Defaults – GL Accounts

- Locate the Discounts Account field.

- Update the GL account to the required value (e.g., change from 350179 to 350171).

- Save the changes.

After updating, all future payment postings with terms discounts will use the updated GL account.

b85d5918-246b-4cd8-8f12-6257329e8ca2.title: CR – Embedded Documents Require Save Before Opening in SaaS Environment
b85d5918-246b-4cd8-8f12-6257329e8ca2.content:
Problem
In Traverse (v11.2, Build 24138), users are unable to directly open embedded documents.
When attempting to open an embedded file (e.g., PDF) from within the application, the system prompts users to save the file locally before it can be opened, instead of opening it directly as expected.
Bug reference:
Bug 84755: CR - Not able to open embedded files now without saving the embedded documents. - 03768246 - DEV-218865
Bug 84755: CR - Not able to open embedded files now without saving the embedded documents. - 03768246 - DEV-218865

Resolution
Cause
This behavior is due to changes introduced for SaaS/Cloud environments in Build 24138.
- Embedded documents are now required to be saved locally before opening, instead of opening directly from a temporary location

- Previously, documents were automatically saved to a temporary folder, which was not visible to users

- With the updated design, document handling relies on User Default settings, including:
- Default Document Folder

- Prompt behavior for opening documents

This change ensures compatibility with SaaS architecture but introduced usability concerns when default paths are not configured.
Resolution
This issue has been addressed in a subsequent update and included as part of the November Service Pack (SP7).
- If a Default Document Folder is configured in User Defaults:
- The system will no longer prompt users to select a save location

- Documents will automatically save to the configured folder and open directly, restoring expected behavior


Action Required: Customers are advised to:
- Update to the latest build (post-24138 / SP7 or later)

- Configure the Default Document Folder in User settings for optimal behavior.

89f69049-788d-4f6f-b4bf-1a64c75f5af1.title: CR – COGS Adjustments from PO Receipts Posting to Closed Prior Periods
89f69049-788d-4f6f-b4bf-1a64c75f5af1.content:
Problem
Users observed that Purchase Order (PO) receipts processed in the current period were resulting in COGS adjustments being posted to prior (closed) accounting periods in Aptean Traverse ERP (v11.2).
Specifically, when goods were received and sold in one period and invoiced in a subsequent period, the system posted the corresponding COGS adjustment back to the original receipt period instead of the current invoicing period.

Bug reference:
Bug 72655: CR - PO receipts for this month are posting COGS adjustments. - 02278375 - DEV-157143
Bug 72655: CR - PO receipts for this month are posting COGS adjustments. - 02278375 - DEV-157143
Resolved in the build : 24355

Resolution
Cause
The issue was identified as a defect in Build 23139, where:
- The system incorrectly derived the posting date for COGS adjustments based on the original PO receipt date

- Instead of using the current transaction/invoice period, the adjustment logic referenced historical transaction data

- This caused COGS adjustments to be posted to prior periods, even when those periods were already closed


Resolution
This issue has been resolved in Build 24355.
- The COGS adjustment logic has been corrected to ensure that adjustments are posted in the current accounting period (invoice period)

- The system now aligns COGS adjustments with the appropriate financial period, preventing postings to closed periods

Action Required: Customers experiencing this issue on earlier builds (e.g., 23139) are required to upgrade to Build 24355 or later to resolve the behavior.

Screenshots below,

PO receipts were initially recorded in Period 1 but were not posted prior to month-end. Subsequently, the period was updated to Period 2, and all related reports reflected the updated period accordingly. However, during posting, the system required Period 1 to be reopened and proceeded to post the transaction back to Period 1 instead of the updated Period 2.
Additionally, users reported that the drill-down functionality from Inventory to Sales Order History is no longer working for certain records (e.g., 00048583).

92827c1e-6c31-4dd5-8cbe-d6a3c9314a00.title: CR – WMS Receiving Does Not Allow Service Item Type Inventory IDs to Be Received
92827c1e-6c31-4dd5-8cbe-d6a3c9314a00.content:
Problem
Users are unable to receive Inventory Item IDs configured as Service Item types through Warehouse Management in Aptean Traverse ERP (WMS module).
When processing Purchase Order receipts via Warehouse Management, Service-type items are not available for selection or receipt. As a result, users are required to perform receipts for such items directly through the Purchase Order module instead of WMS.

CR:
Bug 66151: CR - WMS Receiving - Cannot receive Inventory Item IDs that are Service Items - 02276380 - DEV-129537
Bug 66151: CR - WMS Receiving - Cannot receive Inventory Item IDs that are Service Items - 02276380 - DEV-129537Bug 66151: CR - WMS Receiving - Cannot receive Inventory Item IDs that are Service Items - 02276380 - DEV-129537

Resolution
Cause:
The issue was due to a limitation in the Warehouse Management receiving logic, where:
- WMS did not include or display Service Item type Inventory IDs during the receiving process

- The system filtered items based on item type, allowing only specific inventory types (e.g., serialized or non-serialized) to be received via WMS

- This behavior was not aligned with the Purchase Order functionality, where Service Items could be added (based on the “Allow Service Items in Purchases” business rule)

As a result, even when Service Items were valid and present on the Purchase Order, they were not exposed or available for receipt within WMS.
Resolution:
This issue has been addressed through a product enhancement implemented under DEV-129537 (Bug 66151).
- The WMS receiving functionality has been updated to allow Service Item type Inventory IDs to be received

- WMS now retrieves and displays items directly from the Purchase Order without restricting based on item type

- Service Items included in the Purchase Order are now available for receipt in Warehouse Management, ensuring consistency across modules.

f6c8b473-d077-47ec-8dd2-221a1059c87e.title: CR- Excluding Zero Shipped Line Items from Sales Order Invoice
f6c8b473-d077-47ec-8dd2-221a1059c87e.content:
Problem
Customers reported confusion during the Sales Order invoice process, as invoices were including line items with zero shipped quantity and/or zero price, which were not relevant for billing purposes.
Additionally, in scenarios where all line items had zero shipped quantities and no associated financial values (such as tax, freight, or miscellaneous charges), the system was still allowing the generation and posting of $0 invoices.

Cause
The issue was identified as a limitation in the existing system design and invoice processing logic:
- The invoice printing functionality did not include conditional filtering to exclude line items with zero shipped quantity or zero price

- The system treated all Sales Order line items equally during invoice generation, regardless of shipment status

- There were no validation checks in place to prevent invoice creation when there were no valid printable line items or financial values

- As a result, the system proceeded with invoice generation and posting even when the invoice effectively contained no meaningful data.

Resolution
Please find the resolution steps below,
- A new Sales Order Business Rule: “Print Zero Shipped Line Item” has been introduced, with a default value of Yes

- When this setting is changed to No, the system excludes line items with zero shipped quantity from invoice printing across:
- Sales Order Print Invoice

- Sales Order Online Invoice

- Sales Order Invoice from History

- Additional validation logic has been implemented to ensure:
- Invoices are not generated or posted if there are no printable line items

- Invoices are not created when there are no associated financial values such as tax, freight, or miscellaneous charges

- The system now displays a “Nothing to process” message in such cases, preventing the creation of blank or $0 invoices

This enhancement ensures improved invoice clarity, prevents unnecessary financial records, and aligns invoice output with actual shipped and billable items.

Later if we see reopen traverse it still exists,

This issue has been addressed through a product enhancement implemented in Build 25199.

f8b52b27-5919-4472-b891-106401b393bc.title: Why Does a Column Show Reversed Signs in 'GL Financial Statements' despite having right signs on the Sub-Column Values?
f8b52b27-5919-4472-b891-106401b393bc.content:
Problem
In Traverse, users may encounter a scenario where a calculated column in a GL Financial Statement displays values with reversed signs (negative instead of positive, or vice versa), even though the individual contributing columns or sub-values appear correct and positive.

This can be confusing because:
- The underlying account balances seem accurate
- Individual columns display expected values
- However, the final computed column shows opposite signs

This behavior often leads users to question whether:
- The formula logic is incorrect
- The layout configuration is wrong
- Or the data itself is inconsistent

Cause
The issue is typically related to the Formula Type used in the Statement Layout.

- The column is currently configured using Formula 1
- Formula 1 is designed for calculations where account balance signs (Debit/Credit) are not significant
- Examples: ratios, percentages, variance comparisons

However, in financial reporting:

- Account balances follow a Debit/Credit convention
- Debits → Positive
- Credits → Negative

- When this convention is not respected, calculated values may appear with incorrect signs

As a result, even if individual columns appear correct, the final computed column may display reversed signs due to the formula type used.

Resolution
In Traverse, Formula 1, Formula 2, and Formula 3 are used to create calculated columns in GL Financial Statements.
They differ primarily in:
- How they treat Debit/Credit signs
- Whether they respect accounting behavior
- How they calculate totals
- Whether they support cross-period/year reporting

Core Concept:
Before understanding formulas, we need to remember:
Traverse stores:
- Debit balances → Positive (+)
- Credit balances → Negative (−)
So, the formula type determines: How these signs are interpreted and displayed

Formula 1 – Sign-Insensitive Calculations:
When to Use:
- Ratios
- Percentages
- Variance %
- Any calculation where sign does NOT matter
Behavior:
- Ignores Debit/Credit nature
- Ignores “Reverse Sign to Print” setting
- Calculates both: - Account lines
- Total lines

Key Insight: Treats numbers more like mathematical values, not accounting values
Example:
- (Actual / Budget) * 100
- Profit margin %
- Variance %

Formula 2 – Accounting-Aware Calculations:
When to Use:
- Financial values where sign matters - Revenue percentages
- Currency variances
- GL-based calculations

Behavior:
- Respects Debit/Credit sign convention
- Uses “Reverse Sign to Print” setting
- Calculates: - Only at account level

- Totals are: - Sum of account lines (not recalculated)

Key Insight: This is the most commonly used formula for financial reporting
Example:
- (Actual - Budget)
- Totals of any actuals
- % of Revenue
- Expense comparisons

Formula 3 – Cross-Year / Time-Based Calculations:
When to Use:
- Reporting across: - Multiple periods
- Fiscal years

Behavior:
- Aggregates: - Actual
- Budget
- Forecast

- Works across date ranges
- Respects Reverse Sign to Print
- Excludes closing entries (important for accuracy)
Key Insight: Designed for historical comparisons and trend analysis
Example
- Year-over-year comparisons
- Multi-period summaries


In this example scenario, the user was using the 'Formula 1', which will not pay attention to the signs of the individual accounts.
To correct the sign behavior, the column should be updated to use Formula 2.
- Formula 2 is designed for financial calculations where: - Account balance signs are significant
- Debit/Credit behavior must be preserved

- It also respects the “Reverse Sign to Print” setting
- Ensures totals are calculated correctly based on account-level values

Steps to Update the Formula:
1.Navigate to the GL Statement Layout under the path: General Ledger -> Management Report Setup -> Statement Layout:
[NOTE: We should be aware of the GL Statement Layout beforehand, or we need to observe it from the 'GL Statements' screen]


2. Open the specific layout being used.

3. Go to the Column Detail section of the specific Column that is pulling the numbers with incorrect sign.

4. Update the formula type to Formula 2:

5. Save the changes:

6. Re-run or preview the statement:

Expected Outcome:
- The column will now display values with the correct sign convention
- Calculations will align with Debit/Credit accounting behavior
- The discrepancy between sub-columns and computed columns will be resolved

Note:
When working with formulas:
- Traverse stores: - Debit balances as positive values
- Credit balances as negative values

- Selecting the appropriate formula type is critical to ensure accurate financial representation

fc96c1d8-dbd8-433e-a031-b0edc0b64040.title: Understanding Item Vendors and Item Customers Views in Traverse
fc96c1d8-dbd8-433e-a031-b0edc0b64040.content:
Problem
How can I see which vendors are associated with my inventory items and track their related transactions? Also, is there a way to view which customers are linked to specific items along with their transaction history in Traverse

Resolution
1. Item Vendors View
The Item Vendors View provides visibility into all inventory items associated with specific vendors, including:
- Vendor-specific transactions.

- Item details such as description, unit of measure, and inventory location.

- Vendor setup information from Inventory > Setup and Maintenance > Item Vendors.

- Vendor aliases configured in inventory items.

Steps to Access and Use the View:
- Go to Inventory > Interactive Views > Item Vendors View.

- Filter or search for the desired vendor.

- Review the list of associated items and their transactions.

- Cross-check vendor setups and aliases via Item Vendors UI.

Example Use Case: A procurement manager wants to verify which items a new vendor supplies before creating a purchase order. This view provides a complete overview.




2. Item Customers View
The Item Customers View shows all inventory items linked to specific customers, including:
- Customer-specific inventory details and transactions.

- Item setup information from Inventory > Setup and Maintenance > Item Customers.

- Customer aliases configured in inventory items.

Steps to Access and Use the View:
- Navigate to Inventory > Interactive Views > Item Customers View.

- Filter or search for the customer.

- Review associated inventory items and transaction history.

- Verify Item Customers UI and Customer Aliases for accuracy.

Example Use Case: A sales analyst needs to report on items sold to a particular customer over the last quarter. This view provides the required transaction data quickly.

Feature Availability
The Item Vendors View and Item Customers View were introduced in Traverse build 24278 and later. Users must be on this build or a later version to access these views.

68f2c001-3ac4-4aff-8c49-ca5eb18ab888.title: Mobile WMS – Physical Inventory Menu Overview and Functionality
68f2c001-3ac4-4aff-8c49-ca5eb18ab888.content:
Problem
Warehouse users require a clear understanding of the Physical Inventory Menu options available in the mobile warehouse management application. Specifically, clarification is needed on how the Inventory Counts, Physical Inventory, and Inventory Dispose functions operate, when each should be used, and how inventory quantities are adjusted within the system while maintaining proper validation and audit controls.

Resolution
The Physical Inventory Menu in the mobile warehouse application provides access to three core inventory control functions: Inventory Counts, Physical Inventory, and Inventory Dispose. Each serves a distinct operational purpose while ensuring inventory accuracy and system traceability.
Inventory Counts
The Inventory Counts function supports spot counting without requiring a formal freeze process. It captures counted quantities by Item ID, Bin, Container (if applicable), Lot, and Serial Number. The current On Hand Quantity is displayed for reference during entry.
When a counted quantity is recorded, the system automatically adjusts the on-hand balance to match the entered value. This adjustment is logged in the WM Adjustments Journal for audit visibility. Serialized items require individual entries per serial number with a counted quantity of one. The unit of measure is displayed for verification.
This function is typically used for quick corrections, verification counts, or minor discrepancies that do not require a structured batch-based physical inventory.

Physical Inventory
The Physical Inventory function supports controlled, batch-based inventory processing. Before counts are entered, quantities must be frozen using the Freeze Quantities function, and inventory tags or worksheets must be generated. While counts are being entered, the selected batch remains locked to prevent edits or execution of the Update Perpetual Inventory function.
Counts may be entered by selecting items from the batch list or by scanning item barcodes directly. The system records Bin, Container (if enabled), Lot, Serial Number (if applicable), and Counted Quantity. Serialized items require separate entries per serial number with a quantity of one. The default counted unit of measure is displayed and may be adjusted as necessary.
When the Update Perpetual Inventory function is executed, the system adjusts inventory based on the difference between the frozen quantity and the counted quantity.
Field validation follows a defined sequence depending on the Use Container parameter:
- When Use Container = Yes: validation occurs in the order of Container, Bin, Lot, Serial.

- When Use Container = No: validation occurs in the order of Bin, Lot, Serial.

This function is intended for structured physical inventory events where quantities are frozen and reconciled in a controlled manner.

Inventory Dispose
The Inventory Dispose function is used to decrease inventory quantities for damaged, expired, or otherwise unusable items. It functions similarly to a WM Adjustment using a “Decrease” adjustment type.
The process records Item ID along with Container, Lot, Bin, and Serial Number (if applicable). Serialized items require individual entries per serial number with a disposal quantity of one. Entering a positive quantity in the Qty to Dispose field reduces the current On Hand Quantity accordingly. The unit of measure and On Hand Quantity are displayed for reference.
Validation follows the same configuration logic:
- With Use Container = Yes: validation sequence is Container, Bin, Lot, Serial.

- With Use Container = No: validation sequence is Bin, Lot, Serial.

This function ensures accurate and controlled reduction of inventory balances while maintaining system audit integrity.

269f9402-ad26-4f91-9ffb-967c9d9e2e12.title: Changing the Save Location for Magnetic Media File in AP 1099 Processing
269f9402-ad26-4f91-9ffb-967c9d9e2e12.content:
Problem
This article describes how to change the save location for the magnetic media file during AP 1099 Processing

Resolution
Title:
Solution Overview:
This article describes how to change the save location for the magnetic media file during AP 1099 Processing. The solution involves accessing the 1099 Processing screen, completing the header information, and then updating the file location.

Step-by-Step Instructions:
-
Go to the 1099 Processing screen.

- Click Generate.

- Click Header at the top of the screen and complete the Header information.

- Update the file location for the Magnetic Media file to the folder you prefer.

- Select Output > Magnetic Media to generate the file.

- The file will be created in the specified folder with the name IRSTAX.

- An audit report will appear in Print Preview. You can simply close it; Do not print it.

Important Notes:
The Magnetic Media file is saved in the folder specified on the right-hand side of the first 1099 Processing screen. When you first open the screen and click Generate, this field is greyed out. It only becomes editable after you click Header and complete the required header information (this step is mandatory before generating the Magnetic Media file).
When the Magnetic Media file is generated, it is created in that folder with the filename IRSTAX (with no file extension). The file name is hard-coded and cannot be changed.
After the file is created, Traverse automatically displays a Print Preview of the 1099 Magnetic Media Report (Audit Log). This is NOT the Magnetic Media file. This is a common point of confusion.
The Print Preview is simply an audit report that shows how the data was used to create the Magnetic Media file. It is intended only for troubleshooting purposes. If there are no errors in the file creation, this report does not need to be printed or saved and can be closed.

2727fcca-a257-4ebc-9ec7-6e8b0742056b.title: Ways to change the status of a Serial Number from Lost to Active.
2727fcca-a257-4ebc-9ec7-6e8b0742056b.content:
Problem
Serial Numbers that are marked as Lost need to be restored to an Available (Active) status when the item is physically located or incorrectly flagged as lost.

Resolution
There are two ways to change the status of a Serial Number from Lost to Available (Active).

Method 1: Inventory Adjustment (Increase Transaction)

Steps to Perform the Adjustment
- Navigate to:
- Inventory → Transactions → Inventory Transactions
- Create a new transaction with the following details:
- Type: Increase
- Item ID: Enter the relevant Item ID
- (Optional) Add Date, Fiscal Period, and Fiscal Year columns if you need the adjustment posted to a specific period.

- In the Serial Number Entry pop-up:
- Select the Lost Serial Number.
- Verify the Unit Cost and update it if required.

- Click Close on the Serial Number Entry pop-up.
- Save the Inventory Transaction.
At this point, the Serial Number status will change to Available.

Posting the Transaction
- Navigate to:
- Inventory → Transactions → Post Transactions
- Post the Inventory Adjustment to create the corresponding Journal Entries.
- (Optional) You may print the Transaction Journal beforehand via:- Inventory → Transactions → Transaction Journal for audit purposes.

Method 2: Physical Inventory Count
Steps to Perform Physical Inventory
- Navigate to:
- Inventory → Physical Inventory → Freeze Quantities
- Prepare and freeze a Physical Inventory Batch Code for the specific:
- Item ID
- Location ID
- Go to:
- Inventory → Physical Inventory → Physical Counts Entry
- Open the newly created Batch ID.
- It is recommended to select “Default Counted” to populate counted quantities for serial numbers with frozen quantities.

- Manually add the Lost Serial Number and mark it as Counted.

- Save and Verify the physical count.
Review & Post
- Review and print the following reports:
- Physical Inventory Variance Report
- Physical Counts Valuation Report
- Navigate to:
- Inventory → Physical Inventory → Update Perpetual Inventory
- This step will:
- Post the GL Entries
- This will update the Serial Number status from Lost to Available
