eec5cd26-a83b-49d6-a3b8-b0f8c517a4e1.title: InfoAlert Licensing – How to Generate and Apply the License Key
eec5cd26-a83b-49d6-a3b8-b0f8c517a4e1.content:
Problem
Users installing or reinstalling InfoAlert are unable to complete the licensing process, as they are unsure how to generate the Installation ID, request the Activation ID, and correctly apply the license within the application.

Resolution
Purpose
This article explains how to obtain the Installation ID from the InfoAlert application, provide it for licensing, and apply the returned Activation ID / License Key to complete the activation.
Applies To
- InfoAlert

- New installation

- Reinstallation

- Extended period / licensing renewal scenarios


Important Notes
- The Installation ID is generated from the specific machine/environment where InfoAlert is installed.

- The Activation ID / License Key is provided separately after the Installation ID is shared with the licensing/fulfillment team.

- The license process is generally for product activation purposes only.

Prerequisites
Before proceeding, ensure:
- InfoAlert is installed on the target machine.

- The user has access to open the InfoAlert application.

- The licensing key or activation details have been received from the appropriate team.

- The correct customer/environment is being used.

Step 1: Open the InfoAlert Application
- Log in to the machine where InfoAlert is installed.

- Launch the InfoAlert application.

- If the application opens in trial mode or prompts for licensing, continue to the licensing screen.

Step 2: Locate the Installation ID
- In the InfoAlert licensing window, locate the field labeled:
- Installation ID

- Copy the full Installation ID exactly as displayed.

- Save it in a secure place or share it with the licensing/fulfillment team.

Example
You may typically see:
- Installation ID

- Activation ID field

- License entry area

Step 3: Send the Installation ID for License Generation
- Share the Installation ID with the internal licensing / fulfillment team.

- Confirm the following details when requesting the key:
- Customer name

- Product name: InfoAlert

- Site ID or account reference, if applicable

- Reason for request:
- new installation

- reinstallation

- extended license

- renewal

- Wait for the corresponding Activation ID / License Key to be provided.

Step 4: Receive the Activation ID / License Key
Once the licensing team processes the request, they will provide one of the following:
- Activation ID

- License Key

- both, depending on the licensing format used

Carefully verify that the key provided belongs to the same customer/environment for which the Installation ID was generated.
Step 5: Enter the Activation ID / License Key
- Return to the InfoAlert licensing screen.

- In the appropriate field, enter or paste the provided:
- Activation ID

- Double-check for:
- missing characters

- extra spaces

- incorrect dashes

- copied line breaks

Step 6: Apply / Activate the License
- Click the appropriate button, such as:
- Activate

- Wait for the application to process the license.

- If successful, the application should confirm activation or proceed to normal usage.

Step 7: Validate the License
After activation:
- Close and reopen the InfoAlert application.

- Confirm that no licensing prompt appears.

- Verify the application opens normally.

- If there is an “About” or “License Information” screen, confirm the product now shows as activated.

Troubleshooting
Issue 1: Invalid Activation ID / License Key
Possible Causes
- Incorrect key entered

- Key copied with extra spaces

- Key does not match the Installation ID

- Key belongs to another environment

Resolution
- Re-copy the key carefully.

- Recheck the Installation ID used to generate the key.

- Confirm with licensing that the key was generated for the correct customer/environment.

Issue 2: Installation ID Changed
Possible Causes
- InfoAlert was reinstalled

- Machine/environment changed

- Hardware or system changes caused a new Installation ID

Resolution
- Re-open the application.

- Capture the new Installation ID.

- Request a new Activation ID / License Key based on the updated Installation ID.

Best Practices
- Always use the current Installation ID from the exact machine where InfoAlert is installed.

- Do not reuse an Activation ID from another customer or another server unless licensing confirms it is valid.

- Keep a record of:
- customer name

- Installation ID

- Activation ID

- date applied

- person who performed activation

InfoAlert licensing requires capturing the Installation ID from the application, sending it to the licensing/fulfillment team, receiving the corresponding Activation ID or License Key, and applying it within the InfoAlert licensing screen. After activation, reopen the application and verify that licensing prompts no longer appear.

a973e520-ce83-468a-b693-8fac0b58cbcf.title: Why Does “Cannot Insert NULL into RealGainAcct” Error Occur in AP Select Payables?
a973e520-ce83-468a-b693-8fac0b58cbcf.content:
Problem
Users may encounter the following SQL error in Traverse while dropping a payment through AP Select Payables:

“Cannot insert the value NULL into column 'RealGainAcct', table 'tempdb.dbo.#GainLossAccounts'; column does not allow nulls. INSERT fails.”

This error typically occurs after selecting an entry and clicking on the Write button. As a result, the system cannot proceed with dropping a specific Invoice from the payment process, blocking users from completing the specific Payment cycle.

Cause
This issue arises due to incomplete configuration of Gain and Loss accounts in the Active Currency setup.

Specifically, the following fields are either missing or not populated:
- Realized Gains Account
- Realized Losses Account
- Unrealized Gains Account
- Unrealized Losses Account

When these values are not defined, the system attempts to insert NULL values into a temporary Gain/Loss table (#GainLossAccounts) during processing. Since the table does not allow NULL entries for these columns, the operation fails and triggers the SQL error.

Resolution
Resolution:
To resolve this issue, we need to ensure that all required Gain and Loss account fields are properly configured for the active currency.
Steps to Resolve:
1.Navigate to: System Manager -> Setup and Maintenance -> Active Currency
2. Review the affected currency (for example, USD)


3. Verify and populate the following fields:
-
- Realized Gains Account
- Realized Losses Account
- Unrealized Gains Account
- Unrealized Losses Account

4. Save the changes


Expected Outcome:
Once the required Gain and Loss accounts are configured:
- The system will no longer attempt to insert NULL values
- The SQL error will be resolved
- And the 'Write' action will be executed without any issues


Best Practice:
- Always ensure that all Active Currency configurations are fully populated during setup
- Validate Gain/Loss account mappings when introducing new currencies or modifying financial configurations

Conclusion:
This issue is configuration-related and occurs when required financial account mappings are missing. By completing the Active Currency setup, the system can process Gain/Loss calculations correctly and avoid SQL errors during payment processing.

90205c4b-63db-43ad-a47a-5c83ce0227eb.title: How to reset the unposted depreciation that got calculated incorrectly in Fixed Assets?
90205c4b-63db-43ad-a47a-5c83ce0227eb.content:
Problem
How to reset the unposted depreciation that got calculated incorrectly in Fixed Assets?



In Traverse, users may encounter situations where depreciation is calculated for an unintended range of periods in Fixed Assets.

For example:

- A user may intend to calculate depreciation only for a specific period (e.g., Period 3)
- However, depreciation may get calculated for multiple periods (e.g., up to Period 12)

In such cases, attempting to use the “Reset” option does not clear or reverse the calculated (unposted) depreciation. This can lead to confusion and incorrect financial data if not addressed properly.



Report:

Resolution
Resolution

To reset or clear incorrectly calculated unposted depreciation, please follow the steps below:

- Navigate to: Fixed Assets -> Daily Work -> Compute Period Depreciation
- In the lower section of the screen, identify the range of periods for which depreciation has been calculated



- Locate the Depreciation Type entry (that was previously selected for the depreciation calculation)
- Uncheck the selected Depreciation Type



- Click on the “Calculate” button
- A confirmation pop-up will appear asking if we want to clear the calculated depreciation
- Click Yes to confirm the same

- Once done, the confirmation pop-up will appear as below:



Expected Outcome:

- The previously calculated (unposted) depreciation will be successfully cleared. We can confirm this by hitting the 'Report' icon at the top, and it would confirm us that the depreciation has not been calculated
- The user can then recalculate depreciation for the correct period as intended



Note:

- The Reset option alone does not remove calculated depreciation
- Clearing must be done through the Compute Period Depreciation screen using the steps above

07de396c-9b16-4857-afbd-6a6c142e0ada.title: Unable to Load Database in Design Studio - On Prem environment
07de396c-9b16-4857-afbd-6a6c142e0ada.content:
Problem
The client is experiencing issues launching the Traverse Global Design Studio application on a workstation. The application fails to load properly and prevents users from accessing the system due to repeated login and connectivity errors.

Observed Issues:
- Upon launching the application and attempting to log in, users encounter the following error:

------------------------------
Login failed..
Cannot connect to License Server: localhost :
Error: No connection could be made because the target machine actively refused it 127.0.0.1:2003
------------------------------
BUTTONS:
OK
------------------------------
- After dismissing the above error and retrying login, a second error appears:

------------------------------
Login failed..
Object reference not set to an instance of an object.
------------------------------
BUTTONS:
OK
------------------------------

- In another scenario:
- Users are prompted to select a database.

- After selecting the database and clicking “OK,” the application closes or disappears without logging in.

- This behavior repeats in a continuous loop, preventing access to the application.



Impact:
- Users are unable to successfully launch or log into the application.

- The issue blocks access to the Design Studio entirely, impacting productivity and operations.

Cause
- The Design Studio configuration file was missing or incorrectly configured.

- Configuration values (company database, SYS database, license server name, port) did not match the TRAVERSE License Server Manager settings.

- In some cases, cached application data caused looping or prevented the database list from loading.

Resolution
Step 1: Launch with Appropriate Credentials
- Attempt to launch Design Studio using either Administrator or TRAVERSE credentials.

Step 2: Check for Configuration File
- Navigate to the Traverse installation directory (typically the client folder).

- Look for the configuration file named:
TRAVERSE.DesignStudio.exe.config
-  Verify that the file is present.

Step 3: Replace Missing Configuration File (Primary Fix)
-  If the configuration file is missing, copy it from a working workstation.

-  Place the file in the correct directory on the affected machine.

Step 4: Validate Configuration Settings
-  Open the configuration file and confirm the following values:
-  Company database name

-  SYS database

-  License server name

-  Port number

-  Ensure all values match those in the TRAVERSE License Server Manager.

Step 5: Retry Application Login
-  Relaunch Design Studio and attempt to log in again.

Step 6: Resolve Looping Issue (Third Scenario)
-  If the application loops after selecting the database:
-  Clear the application cache and temporary data.

-  Restart the application and try logging in again.

Step 7: Final Verification
-  Confirm that Design Studio loads successfully and allows login without any errors.

12098bd5-d494-4c67-900a-357be097e02b.title: How to track Inventory at the Bin Level Without Warehouse Management (WM) in Traverse?
12098bd5-d494-4c67-900a-357be097e02b.content:
Problem
How to track Inventory at the Bin Level Without Warehouse Management (WM) in Traverse?



Organizations that do not have the Warehouse Management (WM) module installed may still have a business need to identify or associate inventory with specific bins within a warehouse. However, in such environments, Traverse does not natively support true bin-level inventory tracking.

This often leads to confusion around:

- Whether inventory quantities can be tracked per bin
- How to utilize the Default Bin functionality
- How the “Default/No Bins Only” setting impacts inventory behavior

Users may expect the system to reflect exact quantities across multiple bins, similar to WM functionality, but instead find that inventory is only tracked at the item-location level.

Resolution
There is a Business Rule setting available for 'Inventory' in Traverse named as “Default/No Bins Only”, and this option determines how inventory quantities are interpreted in environments where bin-level tracking is not actively managed.



When Warehouse Management is NOT installed:

- Traverse does not track inventory at the bin or container level
- Inventory is maintained only at the item-location level



However, “Default/No Bins Only” option provides an additional behavior:

- If set to “Yes”:
- A default bin is assigned to the item/location
- The system will assume that all inventory quantity resides in that default bin
- This is only a logical assumption for reporting or reference, it does not enable true bin tracking

- If set to “No” (default behavior):
- Traverse will not associate inventory with any bin
- Inventory remains strictly at the location level, without bin-level visibility



When Warehouse Management (WM) IS installed:

- This option is always set to “No”
- Bin-level tracking is fully handled by the Warehouse Management module
- Inventory is tracked accurately across bins/containers, making this setting irrelevant





Resolution:

To simulate bin-level tracking without WM, follow the steps below:

Step 1: Assign a Default Bin to the Item Location

- Navigate to the Item Location setup
- Assign a Default Bin for the item (e.g., 13)



Step 2: Enable “Default/No Bins Only”

- Locate the “Default/No Bins Only” setting under Business Rules in the path: System Manager -> Company Setup -> Business Rules: IN - Inventory -> Physical Inventory
- Set this option to “Yes”



Step 3: Understand System Behavior

Once enabled:

- Traverse will assume all inventory for that item/location resides in the Default Bin
- This is a logical assignment, not physical tracking
- The system will not track movement across multiple bins

Example Scenario

- Item: Item A
- Location: Main Warehouse
- Default Bin: BIN-01
- Quantity on Hand: 100 units

With “Default/No Bins Only” = Yes

- System assumes:
- All 100 units are in BIN-01

With “Default/No Bins Only” = No

- System shows:
- 100 units at the location level only
- No bin association





Key Notes:

- This option is primarily relevant only when Warehouse Management is not installed
- Setting it to Yes provides a default bin assumption, not true bin tracking
- Setting it to No keeps inventory strictly at the location level
- When Warehouse Management is installed, bin tracking is handled separately, and this option is not applicable

d7f7f549-6ed1-4898-8204-29a316da294a.title: Picking Slips & Packing Lists Printing Per Location
d7f7f549-6ed1-4898-8204-29a316da294a.content:
Problem
Customers may notice that Picking Slips and Packing Lists print on separate pages when an order contains items from multiple inventory locations. This article explains why this occurs and what options are available.

Resolution
System Behavior
The system processes each inventory location independently
Picking Slips and Packing Lists are generated per location
Items from the same location are grouped and printed on one page
Items from different locations are printed on separate pages

Why This Happens
This is standard system behavior designed to ensure:
Accurate inventory tracking by location
Clear separation of fulfillment responsibilities
Reduced confusion when locations represent different warehouses or physical areas

Limitations
There is no out-of-the-box option to combine multiple locations into a single Picking Slip or Packing List
Printing all items on one page across locations is not supported in the base system

Available Options
If the business requires combining multiple locations into a single document:
A custom report modification can be implemented
This involves changes to the report design/layout
Customizations are handled by the Professional Services team
This would be a billable service

Recommendation
Continue using the standard functionality for accurate, location-based fulfillment
Consider customization only if operational needs require consolidated printing

Summary
Printing Picking Slips and Packing Lists per location is expected system behavior. Combining multiple locations into a single document requires customization through Professional Services.

2ccf2a6a-bbc2-4a8f-b05f-77f7a3b956a9.title: How can the posting level (detail vs summary) be configured for applications interfacing with GL?
2ccf2a6a-bbc2-4a8f-b05f-77f7a3b956a9.content:
Problem
Users may need to control the level of Journal Entry details that transaction postings from various applications write to the General Ledger during the corresponding applications Transaction Posting  process.

In some cases, organizations require detailed journal entries for every transaction to support auditing, reconciliation, and traceability. In other cases, they may prefer summarized postings to reduce the number of journal entries in the GL and simplify financial reporting.

When multiple applications (such as Accounts Receivable, Accounts Payable, Inventory, Sales Order, Purchase Order etc.) interface with the General Ledger, users may be unsure how to configure whether each application writes detailed entries or summarized entries during the posting process.

This can lead to confusion regarding why the GL contains many individual entries for each transaction or only a single summarized entry per account or batch.

As a result, users seek clarification on how the posting level for interfacing applications can be configured, so that the GL reflects either detailed or summarized journal entries based on the organization’s operational, reporting, and audit requirements.

Resolution
In Traverse, the level of details that write to the General Ledger (GL) from interfacing applications is controlled through a setting in the SM Business Rules.

This configuration is available under the “Post Detail to General Ledger” setting, located in the Configuration Group section of the SM Business Rules. The setting determines whether posted transactions from integrated applications will have the Journal Entries written to General Ledger as detailed entries or as summarized entries.

Navigation Path:
To access this configuration:
System Manager -> Company Setup -> Business Rules:
- Expand the “Configuration Group” section -> Locate “Post Detail to General Ledger.”


Setting Options:
Yes – Post Detailed Entries:
When this option is enabled (set to 'Yes'), the system will write one GL entry for each account number for every individual transaction from the selected applications during the applications transaction posting process. This results in a highly detailed GL journal, which may contain many journal entries. Once the posting has been completed in individual modules, we can review them under the 'GL Edit Transactions' screen as shown below. In this example, each transaction has an individual Line entry.
With detailed posting enabled, users can drill down from the GL Transactions View to view the exact originating transaction that generated the entry, provided that detail history will also be retained in the source application.
In the below example, even though, they got posted to the same GL Account, we have 2 separate entries created, pointing to different transactions:


No – Post Summarized Entries:
When this option is disabled (set to 'No'), the system will write one summarized GL entry for the total amount per account number for each batch being posted in the corresponding application. If batch processing is not used in the application, the system will generate one summarized entry per account for all transactions being posted.
This approach results in a more concise GL journal with fewer entries, while still allowing users to drill down to the originating transactions through the GL Transaction Inquiry, provided the detail history is stored in the respective application.
In the below example, all the entries have the reference as 'AR', and the individual entries belonging to different customers are summarized under each 'GL Account':



Purpose of the Setting:
This configuration allows organizations to choose between:
- Detailed financial traceability, where each transaction is reflected individually in the General Ledger, or
- Simplified GL posting, where transactions are summarized to reduce the number of journal entries.
Once the setting has been updated, the User needs to hit on 'Apply' and 'OK' to save the changes. Organizations can configure this setting per individual application, depending on their operational, reporting, and auditing requirements. Once the configuration is updated and saved, the change is applied at the company level and will affect all users within that company environment.

6db57bb6-90ec-46e2-82f2-2bb10ecd264b.title: How to resolve the error 'The specified string is not in the form required for an e-mail address' for Traverse Actions?
6db57bb6-90ec-46e2-82f2-2bb10ecd264b.content:
Problem
How to resolve the error 'The specified string is not in the form required for an e-mail address' for Traverse Actions?

Resolution
In Traverse, to configure email settings for alerts, please follow the steps below:
- Navigate to: System Manager -> Actions -> Actions
- Pull up the required alert that is encountering the specific error
- Navigate to the Email tab

Overview of Email Configuration:
Within this tab, we can configure how and where email notifications are sent. The system provides flexibility in defining recipients and email content based on the alert configuration.
We have the option to:
- Send emails dynamically using email addresses retrieved from the result set
- Specify static email addresses manually for designated recipients

Additionally, we can configure the email by:
- Including the output file as an attachment
- Adding any additional attachments, if required
- Defining the email subject and body, with the ability to include fields derived from the alert
Note: To enable email delivery, ensure that the SMTP configuration is properly set up within the Document Delivery settings.

Dynamic Email Selection:
To send emails using addresses retrieved from the result set:
- Use the lookup option available in the Email field
- Select the appropriate field that contains valid email addresses
For example, if the alert is configured for Customers, selecting the corresponding email field ensures that each customer receives an email containing their relevant data, along with the output file if configured.

Validation and Error Handling:
It is important to ensure that the selected field contains valid email address values.

If a field is selected that does not contain properly formatted email addresses, the system will treat this as an error and display the following message:
"The specified string is not in the form required for an e-mail address"

This occurs because the system expects the selected field to strictly contain valid email formats.

In this case, the user had configured the 'CustId' field in the 'Email' field. As a result, the Action attempted to retrieve email addresses using the Customer IDs returned by the Alert. However, since the Customer ID field only contains a list of customer ID records and does not hold any values that meet the criteria of a valid email address, the process resulted in an error.
This behavior would apply to any field that does not contain valid email address values.

Best Practices and Resolution:
- Ensure the selected email field contains only valid and properly formatted email addresses
- Remove or correct any invalid entries within the dataset
If a valid email field is not available within the alert result set:
- Specify a static recipient email address directly in the "Send To" field.
[NOTE: Kindly ensure that only a valid email address is entered in the 'Send To' field. Providing any text or invalid string in this field will result in the same error when the alert/action is executed.]

This will ensure successful email delivery without encountering validation errors.


Output:

965c149b-355b-4d87-abef-b3dd2c47afbf.title: A specific User is stuck while launching Traverse
965c149b-355b-4d87-abef-b3dd2c47afbf.content:
Problem
A specific User is stuck while launching Traverse. It keeps spinning, and the session did not launch.

Resolution
The server experienced a critical spike in memory usage, reaching approximately 99% utilization, which led to noticeable system instability and degraded performance. This unusually high consumption of resources prompted further investigation into the processes running on the server.

Upon reviewing the details in Task Manager, we observed that a user had interacted with the services.exe process and subsequently closed it. However, despite being closed from the user interface, the process continued to run in the background and kept consuming a significant amount of memory. This behavior contributed directly to the resource exhaustion on the server.

To resolve the issue, we manually terminated the process under the respective user session. Following this action, the server’s memory usage returned to normal levels, and system stability was successfully restored.

d8ed7094-927d-4357-9358-0cbd23100fea.title: Why Does TRAVERSE Crash When Exporting Multiple PDFs Sequentially?
d8ed7094-927d-4357-9358-0cbd23100fea.content:
Problem
Users may experience intermittent application crashes in Traverse while attempting to export documents, such as sales quotes, to PDF format. This behavior is typically observed when multiple PDF exports are performed consecutively in a short span of time (back-to-back processing).

The issue does not occur consistently with every attempt, but it happens frequently enough to impact user productivity and disrupt normal workflow. Users may notice that the application becomes unresponsive or unexpectedly closes during or after repeated export operations.

This behavior is more commonly observed in environments where TRAVERSE is accessed via Remote Desktop Services (RDS) or similar remote sessions, where system resources and network conditions play a critical role in application performance.

Cause
Cause / Analysis
When multiple PDF files are generated consecutively:
- The application temporarily consumes higher memory and system resources
- Large amounts of data are processed and transmitted over the remote session (RDP)
- Any network latency, bandwidth fluctuation, or brief instability can impact performance
As a result:
- The application may become unresponsive
- In some cases, it may lead to an application crash
Since this behavior depends on environmental factors such as system load and network stability, it may appear intermittent rather than consistent.

Resolution
Resolution / Recommended Actions
The following steps have been suggested and observed to help mitigate the issue:
- Clear application cache to remove temporary data that may impact performance
- Adjust timeout settings to better handle longer processing durations during multiple exports
- Avoid exporting a large number of PDFs in rapid succession where possible
- Monitor system resource utilization (especially memory) during export operations
- Ensure stable network connectivity, particularly in RDS environments
The suggested solution appears to be effective in reducing the occurrence of the issue.

dd155ad5-cfc7-46b6-9110-3be6632f363a.title: How to resolve the error when a SaaS user is getting the error 'Unable to switch Database'?
dd155ad5-cfc7-46b6-9110-3be6632f363a.content:
Problem
TITLE: TRAVERSE
------------------------------
Unable to switch database.
Check detail.
------------------------------
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION:
Unable to switch database. Check detail. (TRAVERSE)
------------------------------
The server principal "traverseSYS" is not able to access the database "SYS" under the current security context. (Microsoft SQL Server, Error: 916) For help, click: http://go.microsoft.com/fwlink?ProdName=Microsoft+SQL+Server&ProdVer=15.00.4326&EvtSrc=MSSQLServer&EvtID=916&LinkId=20476
------------------------------
BUTTONS: OK
------------------------------

Resolution
Possible Causes and Troubleshooting for TRAVERSE Login/Connection Issues
The issue may occur due to mismatches in configuration, missing associations, or network-related settings. Please review the following potential causes and corresponding checks:

1. Mismatch in Login Credentials
The login ID and password entered in the TRAVERSE Database section of License Manager may not match the Master Login credentials configured in Server Manager.
Ensure that both configurations use the same credentials to establish a successful connection.

2. Company Not Associated with Master Login
The company you are attempting to access may not be linked to the selected Master Login in Server Manager.
Verify that the company is properly assigned to the Master Login to allow access.
3. Missing Company Record in SYS Database
The company may not have a valid entry in the
tblSmCompInfo table within the SYS database.
Confirm that the company record exists and is correctly configured in this table.

4. Incorrect System Database Configuration
The SysDbName value specified in the TRAVERSE.exe.config file may be incorrect.
Ensure that the value accurately points to the correct SYS database.

5. SQL Server Protocols Not Enabled
Required SQL Server protocols, such as TCP/IP, may not be enabled.
Check the SQL Server configuration to ensure all necessary protocols are active.

6. SQL Browser Service Not Running
The SQL Browser service may not be running on the server.
Verify that the service is started, as it is essential for client connections to named instances.

7. Firewall Restrictions
Firewall settings on the SQL Server may be blocking communication.
In some cases, even after a timeout, users may still be able to select the company and connect.
To prevent such issues:
- Add firewall exceptions for:- sqlservr.exe
- sqlbrowser.exe

8. Issues After Client Update
If the issue occurs after applying an update:
- Manually copy the update files to the client’s TRAVERSE installation folder
- Alternatively, download and apply the latest available updates to ensure compatibility
9. SQL Server Protocol Configuration Check
Launch
SQL Server Configuration Manager and navigate to:
- SQL Server Network Configuration
Ensure that:
- All required protocols are enabled on the server
- If the application works on the server but not on workstations, it may indicate that:- Native Client protocols are enabled
- Network protocols are not enabled

In such cases, enable the necessary network protocols to allow workstation connectivity.

Resolution:
In this case, the issue was resolved by deleting the master login on the specific Database, and re-adding the same

d9539909-d764-4baf-b7c6-3e878d6a92b3.title: Where do we check which GL Account a Earning code is associated to?

41984202-2ef5-4d01-ac93-634b78895faf.title: How to Ensure Alerts/Actions Return Valid Results Before Configuring in Traverse?
41984202-2ef5-4d01-ac93-634b78895faf.content:
Problem
How to Ensure Alerts/Actions Return Valid Results Before Configuring in Traverse?

Resolution
Overview:

In Traverse, Alerts/Actions configured through the Actions Designer become available for users to execute within the application. However, there may be scenarios where the Actions Service is running, but no output is generated.

In such cases, it is important to determine whether the issue lies with:

- Output configuration
- Email setup
- Scheduling
- Or the underlying logic/query itself

Before investigating other configurations, we must first confirm that the Alert/Action actually returns valid results based on the defined criteria.



Why This Validation is Important?

An Alert/Action will only trigger when:

- The defined query returns records
- The conditions specified in the logic are met

If no records satisfy the criteria, the system will not generate output, send emails, or execute further steps, even if everything else is configured correctly.



Steps to Validate Alerts/Actions Results:

Step 1: Open Design Studio:

Launch the Design Studio application.



Step 2: Navigate to Actions Designer:

- Open Actions Designer under the 'Designers' section
- Locate and select the specific Alert/Action we want to validate



Step 3: Access the Data Source:

- Navigate to the Data Source tab
- Open the Query Builder



Step 4: Preview Results:

- On the 'Query Builder' pop-up dialog box, we need to click on “Preview Results”
- Enter all mandatory parameters required for the query
- Click OK





Output:

Scenario 1: Records are Returned:

If records appear in the Preview Results section:

- This confirms that the Alert/Action logic and the 'Parameters' are valid
- The alert has qualifying data that can trigger execution
- We can proceed to verify other configurations (Email, Output, Schedule)



Scenario 2: No Records Returned:

If the Preview Results section is blank:

- No records meet the defined criteria either in the Query, or in the 'Parameters' defined.
- The Alert/Action will not trigger in Traverse
- This is the primary reason why no output is being generated

In this case, the user needs to re-work on the query to achieve the required Alert/Action working

80778ced-ad0c-4cde-902c-bde221e1c3c8.title: Why Labor Account Codes Are Required for BOM Posting in Traverse
80778ced-ad0c-4cde-902c-bde221e1c3c8.content:
Problem
Users may question why Labor Account Codes need to be configured when posting a Bill of Materials (BOM), especially if they have not explicitly set up or intended to use labor-related accounts.

Resolution
In Traverse, Labor Account Codes are required only when a BOM includes labor cost values. Even if users have not manually configured labor accounts, the system automatically expects them if any labor component exists within the BOM structure.
A BOM is not limited to material costs - it can also include labor costs associated with production or assembly. When such labor costs are present, the system must determine how to properly record these costs in the General Ledger. This is where Labor Account Codes become essential.
Without configured Labor Account Codes:
- The system has no defined GL accounts to post labor-related costs

- This creates a gap in financial tracking

- As a result, posting is blocked to maintain accounting integrity

Key Concept: Traverse enforces Labor Account Code configuration to ensure that all cost components (materials and labor) are accurately captured in financial reporting.

When Are Labor Account Codes Required?
Labor Account Codes are required only if labor costs exist in the BOM.
This can be validated by:
- Navigating to Bill of Materials > Setup and Maintenance > Bill of Materials

- Opening the relevant assembly

- Checking if any labor cost fields are populated

- If labor cost exists, Labor Account Codes are mandatory

- If no labor cost exists, Labor Account Codes are not required

Why This Design Exists
This behavior is intentional and ensures:
- Accurate Costing: Labor is treated as part of the total production cost

- Proper GL Posting: Every cost component must map to a valid GL account

- Financial Integrity: Prevents incomplete or unbalanced financial entries

- Audit Compliance: Ensures traceability of all production-related costs

If the system allowed posting without Labor Account Codes when labor costs exist, it would result in incomplete or incorrect financial data.

Summary
Labor Account Codes are not universally required - they become mandatory only when labor costs are present in a BOM. Their purpose is to ensure that all labor-related expenses are properly recorded in the General Ledger. This requirement is part of Traverse’s design to maintain accurate costing and financial integrity during BOM posting.

47844540-b3eb-4ee8-91f7-5083c03fe7aa.title: Why is the User Receiving Duplicate Alert Emails in Traverse?
47844540-b3eb-4ee8-91f7-5083c03fe7aa.content:
Problem
Users have reported receiving repeated alert emails in Traverse for the same records, even when there have been no changes to the underlying data. This has raised questions about how to control the frequency and conditions under which alerts are triggered and sent.
Specifically, users are seeking clarity on how to configure the Traverse Alerts to handle the following scenarios:
Weekly Alerts for New Records Only:
- The user wants the alert to run once every week, but it should include only new or updated records that were not reported in previous runs. Any records already notified in the last alert should not trigger another email unless new activity is detected.
Daily Alerts for All Records:
- The user wants the alert to run every day, regardless of whether the records have changed or remain the same. In this case, the system should send an email notification daily, including all applicable records without filtering based on prior notifications.

Resolution
This issue generally arises when the Renotification Period in Traverse is not configured appropriately, or when the dataset used in the alert does not exclude records that have already been reported. The Renotification Period plays a crucial role in determining how Traverse manages and filters data that has appeared in prior alerts, helping to prevent duplicate notifications for the same records within a defined time frame.
When setting up alerts, users should configure the Renotification Period according to their business requirement:

For Alerts to avoid duplicate Notifications/Emails (New Records Only):
To ensure that alerts are triggered only for new or updated records, set an appropriate Renotification Period aligned with the alert frequency.
- For example, if the alert runs weekly and we want to avoid repeating previously notified records, set the renotification period to 7 days.
- This ensures that if a customer or record (e.g., Customer 00001 with overdue invoices) was included in this week’s alert, it will not reappear in the next alert unless the condition still persists after 7 days.
- This configuration helps maintain a clean and relevant alert history while still capturing recurring issues at the right intervals.



For Alerts to include All Records:
In scenarios where users wish to receive alerts every time regardless of whether the data has changed, the Renotification Period should be set to 0.
- Setting it to 0 instructs Traverse to include all qualifying records in every alert run, effectively bypassing the exclusion filter for previously reported data.
- This setup is useful for daily monitoring reports, compliance checks, or operational summaries where consistent visibility is needed without waiting for a time lapse.



The Renotification Period can be defined in minutes, hours, days, or months, depending on the frequency of the alert’s schedule. By properly adjusting this setting, users can eliminate unnecessary duplicate alerts while ensuring timely and meaningful notifications that match their desired reporting cadence.
This configuration ensures that Traverse alerts remain relevant, accurate, and aligned with operational needs, providing clear visibility without overwhelming users with redundant information.

3d695783-7f1a-4e9e-a77a-bef032334295.title: How to resolve the error: "515 : Cannot insert the value NULL into column 'FiscalPeriod', table 'tempdb.dbo.#PaymentDetail"?
3d695783-7f1a-4e9e-a77a-bef032334295.content:
Problem
How to resolve the error: "515 : Cannot insert the value NULL into column 'FiscalPeriod', table 'tempdb.dbo.#PaymentDetail" while preparing the AP Payments?



Detailed Error message:

===================================

SQL Server error encountered. Please check the error details for more information.

------------------------------
Edition = Global
Build = 2XXXX
User = XXXXX
LicenseServer = XXXXXX
Culture = English (United States)
DefaultCompID = CPU
SysDb = SYS
SessionID = ###########
MachineName = YYYYYYYYYYYY

===================================

515 : Cannot insert the value NULL into column 'FiscalPeriod', table 'tempdb.dbo.#PaymentDetail______________________________________________________________________________________________________0000000000CD'; column does not allow nulls. INSERT fails. : Procedure{dbo.trav_ApPreparePayment_proc} (.Net SqlClient Data Provider)

------------------------------
For help, click: http://go.microsoft.com/fwlink?ProdName=Microsoft%20SQL%20Server&ProdVer=15.00.4365&EvtSrc=MSSQLServer&EvtID=50000&LinkId=20476

------------------------------
Server Name: $$$$$$$$$$$$\########
Error Number: 50000
Severity: 16
State: 2
Procedure: dbo.trav_RaiseError_proc
Line Number: 17

------------------------------
Program Location:

at TRAVERSE.Client.ProcessControlBase.OnProcessCompleted()
at TRAVERSE.Client.AccountsPayable.PreparePaymentsControl.OnProcessCompleted()

Resolution
Root Cause:

The issue occurs due to data inconsistency in AP Open Invoice records, where:

- Invoices are marked as Paid/Prepaid (Status = 3)
- But Check Period values are not populated
- This violates the expected lifecycle of invoice processing

Normally:

- Prepaid invoices: Should already have Fiscal Period & Year
- Other statuses (Released / Hold / Temp): Can have NULL values initially and get updated during payment preparation



Recommended Approach:

Step 1: Identify affected records:

Run the query to isolate all prepaid invoices with missing period details:



SELECT *
FROM dbo.tblApOpenInvoice
WHERE Status = 3
AND CheckPeriod IS NULL







Step 2: Correct the data:

The correction can be handled using one of the following approaches:

Option 1: Reset status to ‘Released’ and reprocess payment (Recommended)

- Update the invoice Status from ‘Paid’ (3) to ‘Released’
- Re-run the payment preparation process

Reason: Traverse allows NULL Check Period values for Released invoices, and the system will correctly populate them during payment preparation.

Option 2: Recreate payment using Prepay option

- Update the invoice status to something other than ‘Paid’ (to clear corrupted payment data)
- Recreate the payment using the Prepay option in Traverse

While re-entering, ensure all mandatory fields are populated:

- Payment Number
- Payment Date
- Payment Period
- Payment Year
- Bank Account ID

This ensures the invoice is properly marked as prepaid with complete data.



Option 3: Direct SQL update (Last resort)

If UI-based correction is not feasible:

-
Update the missing fields directly in dbo.tblApOpenInvoice

Populate:

- Check Period
- Check Year

Ensure:

- Values align with the Check Date

Note: This approach is not recommended as the first option, as it bypasses application-level validations.

SQL Query:

UPDATE dbo.tblApOpenInvoice
SET
CheckPeriod = GLPeriod,
WHERE Status = 3
AND CheckPeriod IS NULL



Summary:

- The issue is caused by prepaid invoices missing required Check Period values, leading to failures during payment preparation.
- Correcting the invoice status or reprocessing the payment ensures that all required fields are properly populated and prevents the error.

4d49603a-1966-4059-8126-1033e005ac96.title: How is Form Printer setup configured and used in Traverse?
4d49603a-1966-4059-8126-1033e005ac96.content:
Problem
What is the Form Printers function in Traverse, and how is it configured? A basic understanding is required.

Resolution
The Form Printers function in Traverse is used to control how system forms -such as invoices, receipts, picking slips, purchase orders, and checks- are printed. It allows users to define multiple copies of a form, assign different printers for each copy, and control the order and formatting of printed output.
This setup is workstation-specific, meaning it must be configured individually on each workstation.
1. Configure Form Printer Setup Mode (Business Rules)
Before setting up form printers, define how the configuration should be applied:
- Navigate to: Company Setup > Business Rules > Application > System Manager > Miscellaneous

- Locate Form Printer Setup Mode and select one of the following:
- By Workstation

- By UserID

- By Both

This determines whether printer settings are applied based on workstation, user, or both.
2. Understand Form Printers Page Fields
- Workstation Name Displays when setup mode includes workstation.

- Device Host ID Determined in the following order:
- From User Defaults

- From Service Integration configuration

- Defaults to current workstation name if none is specified

- Printer
- Lists printers from the Device Host ID when cloud print is enabled

- Otherwise, uses printers installed on the workstation

- User Name Displays when setup mode includes UserID

3. Create Form Printer Configuration
- Open the Form Printers screen

- Click New to create a record

- Select a Form from the drop-down list

- Enter Copy Text (e.g., Customer Copy, Office Copy)

- Enter the Order value
- Order numbers must be sequential and unique (e.g., 1, 2, 3…)

- If not sequential, multiple copies will not print

- Select a Printer
- Printers are based on Windows setup for the workstation or Device Host ID

- (Optional) Select a Tray if the printer supports multiple trays

- Check the Active option to enable printing

- Close the screen to save the configuration

4. Configure Multiple Copies of a Form
To print multiple copies:
- Add multiple rows for the same form

- Assign:
- Different Order numbers (must be sequential)

- Same or different printers as needed

Example:
- Order 1 → Customer Copy

- Order 2 → Office Copy


5. Edit Existing Configuration
- Select the form record

- Update fields as needed

- Close the screen to save changes


6. Delete Configuration
- Select the form record

- Click Delete

- Confirm the prompt to remove the record


Additional Notes:
- Traverse forms are designed to print on laser printers

- Dot matrix printers are generally used only for reports unless customized

- In cloud-hosted environments, local printers can be accessed without a VPN

- If no configuration exists at the user level, Business Rules settings are applied

b228e829-70af-4922-98a4-730fa77f8e05.title: Out-of-Order Check Printing in APS (Aptean Print Agent)
b228e829-70af-4922-98a4-730fa77f8e05.content:
Problem
Checks are printing out of order when using APS (Aptean Print Agent), especially in environments where printing is routed through a centralized print server instead of individual workstations.

Resolution
To enforce sequential processing and improve queue handling, update the APS configuration to limit concurrent jobs and control queue size.

Steps to Apply Fix

-
Access the APS workstaion
Log in to the workstation where Aptean Print Agent is installed.

-
Navigate to Configuration File
Go to the following path:



C:\Program Files (x86)\Aptean Print Agent\application.yaml

-
Edit the Configuration File

-
Right-click on application.yaml

-
Open with Notepad or Notepad++ (Run as Administrator if required)

-
Update Configuration
Add the following lines at the end of the existing configuration:



max-jobs: 1

max-queued-jobs: 400

Important:

-
Ensure there are two spaces of indentation before each line

-
YAML is indentation-sensitive; incorrect spacing may cause the service to fail

-
Save Changes

-
Restart APS Service

-
Open Services (services.msc)

-
Locate Aptean Print Agent

-
Restart the service

Expected Outcome

-
Print jobs will be processed one at a time (sequentially)

-
Check printing will follow the correct order

-
Reduced risk of job overlap or mis-sequencing

744a8723-cf74-41ea-a5d2-72eaf7874ecc.title: How to clear Traverse Cache in SaaS
744a8723-cf74-41ea-a5d2-72eaf7874ecc.content:
Problem
Users report that vertical grid lines are missing in tables within the application, making data difficult to read.

-
The issue appears inconsistent and affects only some users.

-
All user settings under View → Preferences are confirmed to be identical.

Cause
The issue is typically caused by corrupted or stale user-specific cache/configuration files stored locally on the SaaS/RDS server.

Resolution
Clear the affected user’s application cache from the server.

Steps:

-
Log in to the SaaS server.

-
Navigate to the following path:



C:\Users\<Username>\AppData\Roaming\Open Systems, Inc



-
Delete or rename the Open Systems, Inc folder.

-
Ask the user to log out and log back in to the application.

Result

-
The application recreates fresh cache/configuration files.

-
Vertical lines in tables are restored.

-
UI rendering returns to normal.

Additional Notes

-
This issue is user-specific and does not impact all users.

-
Safe to perform; no application data is lost (only cached UI/config files are removed).

-
If multiple users report similar behavior, repeat the steps for each affected user.

d4f2fabc-62b0-4f87-b507-8994c5764922.title: Document Code in Avalara Sales Tax Report Displays Transaction ID Instead of Invoice Number After Build 25304 Upgrade
d4f2fabc-62b0-4f87-b507-8994c5764922.content:
Problem
After upgrading from build 23198 to build 25304, users observe a change in the Document Code field within the Avalara Sales Tax Document report.
Previously, the Document Code for Sales Order (SO) transactions was generated using the Invoice Number. However, post-upgrade, the Document Code is now generated using the Transaction ID.
This change creates challenges in scenarios where a single Sales Order contains multiple shipments, as multiple records are generated with the same Transaction ID and different trailing values, without any reference to the corresponding Invoice Numbers. Additionally, the Invoice Number is not visible when reviewing the transaction in the Avalara console.

Resolution
This behavior has been reviewed by the development team and is confirmed to be a product issue in the current build.
Bug Reference: Bug 103933: CR - Avalara Integration: Document Code Changed from Invoice Number to Transaction ID After Upgrade - 06006790 - DEV-321969
The current system logic generates the Document Code based on the Transaction ID, which does not include or reference the Invoice Number.
At this time, there is no available workaround to modify the Document Code to display the Invoice Number instead of the Transaction ID.
This issue has been reported to the development team for further evaluation and potential resolution in a future release.

960533c6-0a6b-4e2a-8ad6-3e62cb4bc577.title: Positive Pay File Not Generating Due to Reused Check Numbers
960533c6-0a6b-4e2a-8ad6-3e62cb4bc577.content:
Problem
A user processed weekly payments in Traverse and generated the checks but the Positive Pay (POSPAY) file was not created. The Positive Pay file is required to upload check payment details to the bank.
How to correct this?

Cause
Positive Pay is a bank fraud-prevention process where the bank keeps a record of every check included in a Positive Pay file. The file typically contains:
- Check Number

- Check Amount

- Check Date

- Payee Name

The layout may vary from bank to bank depending on its own requirements.
If a check number appears again after it has already been reported to the bank, the system or bank will reject it because check numbers cannot be reused once they have been submitted in a Positive Pay file.

Resolution
This issue can occur when check numbers used in the current payment batch were already used previously and included in an earlier Positive Pay file. When duplicate check numbers are detected, the Positive Pay process will not generate a new file for those checks.

Resolution
The steps to resolve the issue depend on whether the payments have been posted or not.
Scenario 1: Payments Have NOT Been Posted
If the payment batch has been prepared but not yet posted, the payments can be re-prepared and issued with new check numbers.
Steps:
- Navigate to Accounts Payable.

- Locate the payment batch that was prepared.

- Re-prepare the payment.

- Assign a new starting check number that has not been used previously.

- Run the Print Checks process using the updated check numbers.

- Generate the Check PDF.

- Run the Positive Pay (POSPAY) file output again.

- Verify that the file includes the new check numbers.

- Once confirmed, post the payment batch.

Scenario 2: Payments Have Already Been Posted
If the payment batch has already been posted, the existing checks must first be voided before issuing new checks.
Steps:
- Navigate to Accounts Payable.

- Open Payment History View.

- Locate the checks that were created with duplicate check numbers.

- Void the checks that were already posted.

- Prepare the payments again.

- Run the Print Checks process using a new starting check number that has not been used previously.

- Generate the new Check PDF with updated check numbers.

- Run the Positive Pay (POSPAY) file output.

- Verify that the file is generated correctly.

- Post the payment batch.

Example screenshots.
Screenshot 1: Payment History View showing the two checks with the same check number

Screenshot 2: AP Create positive pay file showing the first used check.

671a2cc7-4a10-49f9-83f2-77f721a7a820.title: Resolving Drag-and-Drop Issues in DocUnity After Updates
671a2cc7-4a10-49f9-83f2-77f721a7a820.content:
Problem
After a recent update to DocUnity, users experienced issues with the drag-and-drop functionality. This issue was particularly noticeable when importing files from shared network locations such as OneDrive and SharePoint.
When attempting to import documents, the files appeared incomplete—displaying headers and images but missing the main text content. The issue was not limited to network locations, as it also persisted when dragging and dropping files from local folders.
It was also tested and confirmed that drag-and-drop functionality does not work in DocUnity version 2.6.0.4.

Resolution
The issue was identified as a problem with the DocUnity application following the update. An updated version of the DocUnity installer was provided to resolve the import inconsistencies.

Steps to Resolve
Download the updated DocUnity installer: installdocunity.2521.exe Link: https://filetransfer.aptean.com/public/file/7diaz3fk0uq2zr1t-5z4tq/installdocunity.2521.exe
Run the installer on the affected systems to update DocUnity.
After installation, test the drag-and-drop functionality:
- Import files from local folders

- Import files from shared locations (OneDrive, SharePoint)

- Confirm that documents are fully imported with text, images, and headers intact

Additional Notes
- If the issue persists after the update, it may be related to network access or permission settings on shared locations.

- Ensure that DocUnity version 2.5.2.1 (or the latest version provided by support) is installed.

- Verify that any configured capture profiles for specific folders are set up correctly and not impacting document visibility.

Important Note
Although this knowledge base indicates that a version update resolved the issue, this may not apply to all clients upgrading to version 2.6. This conclusion is based on testing conducted across three different workstations within a company, where the drag-and-drop feature remained unavailable.

92898b8e-a5ea-4e63-a1ec-c979af552d58.title: How to create an Item in Inventory
92898b8e-a5ea-4e63-a1ec-c979af552d58.content:
Problem
How do we create a new Item ID in the Inventory?

Resolution
This guide explains how to set up and maintain a new inventory item using the Items function.
Step 1: Create a New Item
Navigation: Applications > Inventory > Setup and Maintenance > Items
- Open the Items screen.

- Click New to open a blank record.

- Enter an Item ID.

- Do not use these characters in the Item ID: | " ' & # *
- You can copy over the following details using the Copy From function.

- Enter an Item Description.

Step 2: Item Tab Setup
- Select the Item Type and Item Status.

Item Types:
- Serialized
- Used for items that require a serial number when purchasing or selling.

- Nonserialized
- Used for standard items that do not require a serial number. Can include lot-controlled items.

- Service
- Used for non-physical items such as training or consulting.

- No quantities are stocked; used mainly for pricing and reporting.

Item Status Options:
- Active – Can be purchased and sold.

- Discontinued – Can be sold but not purchased.

- Superseded – Can be sold but not purchased and requires a replacement item.

- Obsolete – Cannot be purchased or sold.

- If the item status is Superseded, select the Superseded Alternate Item ID.


- Select any applicable item attributes such as: Kitted, Lotted Automatically Reorder


If the item is serialized, choose a Costing Method (General or Specific Item).
- Enter the Base Unit of Measure (note: this cannot be changed after saving).

- Populate any additional fields as applicable:
- Sales Category

- Commodity Code

- Product Line

- Price ID

- Tax Class

- HazMat Code

- Picture ID

- Enter additional descriptive text in the Additional Description field if required.

- Click Save to complete the setup.

Step 3: Units Tab
- Enter a Unit of Measure (example: CARTON, DOZEN).

- Enter a Conversion Factor (Base unit must always be 1).

- If needed, select a penalty method (Percent or Amount) for fractional quantities.

- Enter optional values such as UPC, Weight, and Minimum Sale Quantity.

- Click Append to add more units.

Step 4: Unit Defaults Tab
- Assign default units for various transaction types such as sales, purchases, manufacturing, reporting, service, or physical counts.

- If no defaults are required, leave the fields blank.

Step 5: Alternates and Aliases (Optional)
- Use the Alternates tab to add substitute items.

- Add optional start and end dates for alternate items.

- Use the Aliases tab to assign alternate identifiers per vendor, user, or customer.

- Use an asterisk (*) to apply the alias to all.

Step 6: Location Setup
- Select the Location tab.

Click Add to assign storage locations.
You can see the Add Item Location dialog box, where you can add one or multiple locations. You may use the Copy From Item function, if needed, as well as the Copy From Location function. You can also assign the appropriate account code and review the details to determine which information should be copied using the Copy From Item option.
- Configure any forecasting or reorder settings such as:
- Order Point

- Safety Stock

- Maximum Quantity

- EOQ

- Minimum Order Quantity

- Assign a buyer or planner if applicable.

Step 7: Price Setup
- Open the Price Info tab.

- Enter the Base Price, List Price, Minimum Price, and Average Price.

- If required, assign a quantity break ID for price tiers.

- If the system supports multiple currencies, enter international price details as needed.

Step 8: Vendor Information
- Open the Vendor tab.

- Add or review vendor details such as:
- Vendor

- Last purchase cost and order quantity

- Lead time

- Last order number

- Landed cost ID (optional)

- Vendor links can also populate automatically through purchasing activity.

Step 9: View-Only Tabs
These are updated by the system and cannot be edited:
- Cost Detail

- Loc History

- Quantity Info

- Serial Info

- Bin Info

Step 10: Editing or Deleting Items
- To edit an item, select it, make changes, and click Save.

- To delete an item, ensure:
- The item has no transaction history

- The quantity on hand is zero

- Click Delete to remove the item if allowed.

- Items with history cannot be deleted.

Additional Tools
- Update Price opens the Item Price Change window.

- Assign Labels allows label assignment.

- Import allows batch importing or updating item prices.


We have now completed item creation and setup.

309ae2db-3577-4050-97ff-d3a9b56cf620.title: SO Transactions Ship to ID Lookup Not Saving Column Changes
309ae2db-3577-4050-97ff-d3a9b56cf620.content:
Problem
The Ship To lookup in SO transactions screen was not saving new columns added from the column chooser on the Ship to tab.

Resolution
The issue occurs when using Sales Order (SO) transactions, where any user-added columns on Ship To tab are not saved and the layout reverts to the default configuration.
Specifically, on the Ship To tab, clicking the ellipses (…) next to Ship-To ID normally displays two default columns: Ship-To ID and Name.

Users can add additional columns by right-clicking on the column header area, selecting Column Chooser, and dragging the desired columns into the layout.

Once saved, these custom column layouts are expected to persist across user logouts and logins.
This functionality was working as expected up to Build 25199. However, in Builds 25262 and 25304, the column layout changes were not retained, causing the layout to reset to default each time. This behavior has been identified as a product bug in those builds.
The issue has been fixed in Service Pack 7/ Build 25353. Customers experiencing this behavior should be advised to update to Build 25353 to resolve the issue and ensure that custom column layouts are saved and retained as expected.

69f479a7-8c4d-4d40-83a7-e42e6cdda076.title: Issues Processing Payroll After Switching to New Year
69f479a7-8c4d-4d40-83a7-e42e6cdda076.content:
Problem
The user has set up and switched to the new payroll year. While attempting to process the first payroll of the year, they encounter the following error message.
Also, when looking at the employee records on the PA Employee Information screen, the Earnings Code and certain setups that were earlier available are missing.

Resolution
Payroll Processing Issue – Possible Causes and Resolution:
This issue commonly occurs due to one of the following two scenarios:
Scenario 1: Payroll/Compliance Update Not Run (Most Common)
The most frequent cause is that the payroll or compliance update has not been executed for the new payroll year.
For example:
Payroll may have processed successfully through the end of the 2025 payroll year, but errors begin when attempting to process the first payroll for 2026. This typically indicates that the required update has not been completed.
How to Validate
- Navigate to:
-  Payroll → Setup and Maintenance → Formula Tables
- Select the new payroll year (e.g., 2026)
- Check if data exists for that year
- If no data is available, it strongly indicates that the payroll/compliance update has not been run.
Resolution
Run the payroll/compliance update for the new payroll year.
This should resolve the issue in most cases.

Scenario 2: Payroll Year Created Without Copying Previous Values
This occurs when the new payroll year is manually created without copying values from the previous year.
How to Validate
- Confirm with the customer how the payroll year was created
- If they confirm that previous year values were not copied, this scenario is validated

Resolution Options:
Option 1: Delete and Recreate Payroll Year (Use with Caution)
- Payroll years cannot be deleted via the Traverse UI
- Deletion is only possible through Traverse Server Manager (TSM)
⚠️ Important Considerations:
- Deleting a payroll year via TSM may impact backend database tables
- It can lead to unintended consequences
- This approach must be reviewed and approved by the appropriate internal team before proceeding
hOption 2: Manual Update (Recommended Workaround)
As a safer alternative, users can manually update missing information:
- Open the Employee Information screen
- Enter the missing details for each employee
- Save the changes
- Retry payroll processing
This approach allows payroll processing to continue without deleting and recreating the payroll year.

352640bd-2d8b-41e0-9b91-ffa05978fc6b.title: Resolving "SqlTransaction has been completed" Error During 1099 Processing
352640bd-2d8b-41e0-9b91-ffa05978fc6b.content:
Problem
This article addresses the error "This SqlTransaction has been completed; it is no longer usable" encountered during 1099 processing

Cause
Root Cause
The issue was caused by a hidden leading space in the Vendor ID. Although the Vendor ID appeared correct visually, the preceding whitespace caused the vendor record to fail during 1099 processing.

Resolution
Step 1: Identify Vendor IDs with Leading or Trailing Spaces
You can identify by looking at the individual vendor records. or
You can run the following SQL query to locate Vendor IDs that contain hidden whitespace characters:

SELECT * FROM tblApVendor
WHERE VendorID LIKE ' %'
OR VendorID LIKE '% ';
Explanation:
LIKE ' %' identifies Vendor IDs with a leading space
This query will list vendor records that contain leading or trailing spaces in the Vendor ID.
Step 2: Correct the Vendor ID Using SM Change ID
Once the affected Vendor ID is identified, use the SM Change ID utility to remove the hidden space.
- Open SM Change ID (Applications > System Manager > Setup and Maintenance > Change IDs)

- Select Vendor as the entity

- Change the Vendor ID as follows:


Step 3: Reattempt 1099 Processing
After the Vendor ID is corrected:
- Regenerate the 1099 information.

- It should let you regenerate successfully.

138d545f-b73d-431a-bd88-1b5e975b56fa.title: Setup of check sort function in Payroll
138d545f-b73d-431a-bd88-1b5e975b56fa.content:
Problem
What is Check Sort, and how do I create and manage Check Sort IDs for payroll checks?

Resolution
The Check Sort function is used to set up and maintain Check Sort IDs, which allow payroll checks to be printed in specific groups. This is useful when checks need to be organized or printed separately based on departments, locations, employee groups, or any other internal requirement.
Once a Check Sort ID is created, it must be assigned to employees using the Employee Information screen on the Pay tab.
During payroll processing, the Print Checks function uses the assigned Check Sort IDs to group and print payroll checks accordingly.
Creating a Sort ID
- Click the New button on the toolbar to open a blank Check Sort record.

- Enter a Check Sort ID. This ID will be used to group employee payroll checks.

- Assign this Check Sort ID to employees on the Pay tab in the Employee Information function.

- Enter a description in the Description field to clearly identify the purpose of the Check Sort ID.

- Click Save on the toolbar to save the new Check Sort ID.

Editing a Sort ID
- Select the Check Sort ID you want to update from the Check Sort field.

- Modify the required fields as needed.

- Click Save on the toolbar to apply the changes.

Deleting a Sort ID
- Select the Check Sort ID you want to delete from the Check Sort field.

- Click Delete on the toolbar.

- Click Yes when prompted with "Are you sure you want to delete selected record(s)?" to confirm the deletion.

Using Check Sort IDs helps ensure payroll checks are printed in an organized and controlled manner, making payroll distribution easier and more efficient.

67aa705a-d5e1-4095-912e-edd8481acb2f.title: How to create Leave codes in Payroll
67aa705a-d5e1-4095-912e-edd8481acb2f.content:
Problem
How do Leave Codes work, and how do I create and manage them for leave accrual in Payroll?

Resolution
The Leave Codes function is used to set up and maintain leave accrual codes in the Payroll module. A leave code represents any type of exclusion from work, such as sick pay, vacation pay, paid-time-off (PTO), maternity leave, or similar leave types. There is no distinction between sick leave and vacation leave in the system -both are created and managed using the same Leave Codes form.
Leave codes are used only if Automatic Accrual of Leave Time is enabled in the PA Business Rules.
When entering a Daily Work Payroll Transaction, a leave code must be selected for any earning code that has a leave type. This determines which leave balance the accrued or used hours will be applied to.
Open Leave Accrual
If the system is set to accrue leave hours and you need to change the number of leave hours accrued per hour in a new year, you must switch to the current payroll year before making updates.
- For hourly employees, leave accrual is calculated using the number of hours entered on posted time tickets for the pay period.

- For salary employees, leave accrual is calculated using the number of hours defined in their Group Code.

The Max Hours field on the Leave Codes screen defines the maximum number of hours worked per pay period that can be used to calculate leave accrual.
The Min Accrual field specifies the minimum number of leave hours that must be accrued per pay period. If the system calculates fewer hours than this value, the Min Accrual amount is used instead.
The Maximum Accrual field limits the total number of leave hours an employee can accumulate. During check calculation, the system ensures that the accrued leave hours do not exceed this limit. Any excess leave hours are not accrued until the employee uses some of their existing balance.
If you choose not to have the system accrue leave automatically, these fields must still be set up.
Notes
- If Automatic Accrual of Leave Time is set to Yes in PA Business Rules, leave time is calculated for each pay period automatically.

- If leave time is granted as a lump sum (for example, at the beginning of the year), use the Leave Adjustments function under Periodic Processing to add leave hours to each employee’s balance.

- To change the maximum number of leave hours an employee can accumulate, update the Maximum Accrual field in the Leave Codes function.

Creating a Leave Code
Navigation: payroll -> Codes Maintenance -> Leave Codes
- Click the New button on the toolbar to open a blank leave record.

- Enter a new leave code in the Code field.

- (Optional) Use the Copy From field to copy settings from an existing leave code. This option is available only when creating a new leave code.

- Enter a description in the Description field.

- Enter the maximum leave hours allowed in the Maximum Accrual field, or leave it at 0.000 if there is no limit.

- Select Include Leave Hours in Accrual Calculation if leave hours should accrue when leave is taken for this code (applicable for per-hour accruals).

- Enter the required years of employment in the Up To Year field.

- Enter the leave hours accrued per hour worked in the Hrs/HrsWkd field.

- Enter the maximum hours per pay period used for accrual in the Max Hours field.

- Enter the minimum leave hours accrued per pay period in the Min Accrual field. This field may also be used to define accrual for salaried employees.

- Click Save to store the new leave code.

Editing a Leave Code
- Select the leave code from the Code field.

- Update the required fields.

- Click Save to apply the changes.

Deleting a Leave Code
- Select the leave code from the Code field.

- Click Delete on the toolbar.

- Click Yes to confirm the deletion when prompted.

This setup ensures accurate leave accrual, proper tracking of leave balances, and consistency across payroll processing.

44242d33-84e8-48c3-85a9-a37f23b16065.title: Converting SM Items to Inventory Items
44242d33-84e8-48c3-85a9-a37f23b16065.content:
Problem
How to convert System Manager Description items to Inventory Items?

Resolution
- Open the Convert SM Items function to begin converting SM description items to Inventory items.

- Navigation: Applications > Inventory > Setup and Maintenance > Convert SM Items.

- Use the Items function to verify that item details such as location and unit of measure are correct. Add any missing information as needed.

- Select the Default Location ID to assign the items' location.

- Select the Default Account Code to assign the GL account. Note: Items without a default account will be assigned this account code.

- Enter the item’s default unit of measure in the Default UOM field.

- Select the Maintain Item GL Accounts checkbox if you want GL accounts to be generated and maintained automatically. When selected, the system will auto-generate new account codes with the description set as Auto Gen based on the SM item combinations.

Note: Auto-generated accounts may not include all account numbers. You must go to the Account Codes function and manually assign any missing fields.
Click OK to process items. You may also click:
- Activity to view the activity log

- Reset to clear selected values

If any of the items already exist in Inventory, a message will display listing those items. Click OK to continue.
Use the Convert Items Skip List to review any items that were not converted.

e32b439d-c0b2-4d44-8ec4-596f96cdca97.title: Understanding Data Included in IT Weekly Piece Rate Summary Report and How to Retrieve Monthly Average Percentage
e32b439d-c0b2-4d44-8ec4-596f96cdca97.content:
Problem
The customer is running the IT Weekly Piece Rate Summary report and requires clarification on the following:
- Whether the report includes only piece rate jobs or also hourly work codes.

- How to generate report data for a longer duration (e.g., monthly instead of weekly).

- Where to find the average percentage for an individual over a month.

Resolution
1. Data Included in IT Weekly Piece Rate Summary Report
- The report includes only jobs configured with a Piece Rate.

- Jobs or work codes set up as hourly (non–piece rate) are not included.

- Hourly work entries can instead be reviewed in the IT Weekly Hours Summary report.

Additional Conditions:
- Only individuals with Employee Type = “Disabled” (under Diagnostic Information) are included.

- A Location must be assigned to the individual for the data to appear.

2. Running Data for a Longer Period (e.g., Monthly)
The IT Weekly Piece Rate Summary report is designed for weekly data only and cannot be directly run for a full month.
Alternative Approach: Use the Piece Work Interactive View:
- Navigate to the Interactive View.

- Apply a date filter for the required range (e.g., February 1 to February 29).

- Group by Date to organize results similarly to weekly output.

- Apply a filter:
- Pieces <> 0 (to include only piecework-related entries).

- Optionally filter for individuals with Disabled Diagnosis, depending on system configuration.

3. Finding Monthly Average Percentage for an Individual
To retrieve the average percentage for a month, use the Averages Report:
- Navigate to: ITS → Management Reports → Averages Report

- Run the report for the required date range (e.g., full month).

- This report provides:
- Average Pay

- Average Percentage

- Other related metrics per individual

-

14d3093a-d896-4551-8621-52f001d48e1f.title: Configure User-Specific PIN and Signature for AP Payment Approval
14d3093a-d896-4551-8621-52f001d48e1f.content:
Problem
Users are unable to proceed with the AP Payment Approval process because the required user-specific PIN and signature have not been configured.

Resolution
This issue occurs when the user’s PIN and signature are not set up in the AP Signature Setup screen. Each user must configure their own approval credentials while logged in with their individual account.
Steps to Configure PIN and Signature:
- Log in to the application using your own user credentials.

- Navigate to the AP Signature Setup screen.

- Enter your desired PIN.

- Enter or upload your signature.

- Click Save to store the changes.
