e55783f7-608f-4dc1-8e9d-7d2c5e226241.title: Understanding the need and use of batch codes in Traverse
e55783f7-608f-4dc1-8e9d-7d2c5e226241.content:
Problem
Understanding the need and use of batch codes in Traverse

Resolution
Overview
Batch codes in Traverse are used to group transactions together for easier processing, reporting, posting, and workflow management. Every transaction must be assigned to a batch code, allowing users to organize work efficiently and control how transactions move through the system.
Batch codes function like virtual folders, helping teams separate tasks, manage workflow hand-offs, and maintain clear historical records. This feature is particularly valuable in multi-user or network environments, where several users may be entering or processing transactions simultaneously.
What is a Batch Code?
A batch code is a transactional grouping mechanism that allows users to organize transactions for activities such as:
- Posting transactions

- Printing journals and reports

- Reviewing and editing entries

- Managing workflow between departments

- Tracking historical transaction activity

Each transaction must be assigned to a batch code before it can be processed or posted.

Benefits of Using Batch Codes
Batch codes help organizations manage operational workflows and prevent users from interfering with each other's work.
Key benefits include:
- Workflow control

- Separation of work between users

- Controlled transaction posting

- Improved reporting and tracking

- Historical reference of transaction activity


Setting Up Batch Codes
Follow these steps to create a new batch code:
- Click the New Record button on the toolbar, or select the blank record at the bottom of the batch list.

- Enter a Batch Code (maximum of 6 characters).

- Enter a Description for the batch.

- Select the Permanent checkbox if the batch should remain after transactions are posted.
- If unchecked, the batch will be deleted after posting.

- Review the Journal Status, which may show:
- Not Applicable – No transactions exist in the batch.

- Unprinted – Transactions exist but the journal has not been printed.

- Printed – Journal printed and ready for posting.

- Reprint – Changes were made and the journal needs to be printed again.

- Select Company Default if this batch should be the default batch for the company.


Why Use Batch Codes?
1. Workflow Management
Batch codes help manage operational hand-offs between users.
Example workflow batches:
- RDYINV – Sales Orders ready to invoice

- GDSREC – Purchase Orders received but waiting for vendor invoice

- FRQ – Request for quote batch

These batches help teams easily identify the current status of transactions and pass work between departments.

2. Separating Work Between Users
Only one user can have a transaction active at a time, and batch reports or posting cannot occur while a transaction is active.
Batch codes allow users to separate work and avoid conflicts.
Examples:
- JASON – Jason’s Purchase Orders

- APCHK1 – AP Check Batch 1

- APCHK2 – AP Check Batch 2

- SLS-JB – Sales orders for Sales Rep JB

- CLOSE – Work orders ready for closing


3. Group Posting
Transactions can be posted together by batch.
Each posting creates a unique Post Run number, and only transactions in the selected batch will be included.
Example uses:
- Daily Cash Receipts

- GL Transactions

- Inventory Transfers

- Invoice Posting

For example, in Accounts Receivable, the batch ID may represent a bank deposit ID, allowing the batch total to match the deposit total.

4. Historical Reference
Batch codes are stored in transaction history for reference.
Examples:
- Inventory adjustments store batch codes in inventory detail history.

- Sales Order transactions retain batch codes in historical records.

This allows users to track when and how transactions were processed.

Batch Management Features
Batch Activity
Administrators with permissions can view which users currently have transactions active in a batch.
The Activity button allows administrators to:
- View active users

- Refresh the activity list

- Remove users if a transaction becomes locked

This is commonly used when:
- A user loses connection

- A workstation crashes

- A transaction becomes locked

Note: Removing the user will unlock the transaction, but any unsaved work will be lost.

Locking a Batch
Users with appropriate permissions can lock a batch to prevent further changes.
When a batch is locked:
- Users cannot add transactions

- Users cannot edit transactions

- The batch cannot be posted

This is commonly done when preparing a batch for posting.
The system will also lock a batch when:
- A journal is printed

- A posting attempt fails

The Lock Date and Locked By fields will show who locked the batch.
To unlock a batch:
- Click the Lock button again.


Post and Move Batch
Traverse allows users to post transactions while moving remaining transactions to a new batch.
Common scenarios include:
- Posting invoiced sales orders and moving remaining orders to a Backorder batch

- Posting Purchase Order receipts and moving transactions to a Waiting for Invoice batch

This feature helps maintain clean transaction workflows.

Summary
Batch codes are a powerful organizational tool in Traverse that help manage transaction workflows, improve collaboration in multi-user environments, and maintain clear transaction history.

Using batch codes effectively allows organizations to:
- Improve workflow management

- Prevent user conflicts

- Streamline posting processes

- Maintain accurate transaction history

6fe08e57-cae6-4e92-856a-8bd1cdba25d7.title: How to Change or Verify the Company’s Base Currency in Traverse
6fe08e57-cae6-4e92-856a-8bd1cdba25d7.content:
Problem
When setting up a new company database, users may need to confirm or configure the Base Currency used for all financial processing. For example, a company may require CAD (Canadian Dollar) as the base currency. Users may be unsure where to verify or update this configuration in the system.

Resolution
The Base Currency is configured in the Company Setup section within Company Information. Follow the steps below to verify or change the base currency:
- Choose Applications. Navigate to System Manager.

- Select Company Information.

- Click Company Setup.

- Open the General tab to review the company’s general details.
- For example, if the company is located in Canada, you can select CAN as the Country from the dropdown list.

- If the company location needs to remain as another country (e.g., USA) but the financial transactions must use Canadian Dollars, proceed to the Defaults tab (located to the right of the General tab).

- In the Base Currency dropdown, select CAD – Canadian Dollar.

- Save the record to apply the changes.

00e494a7-d6fd-460d-b74d-0e9aee224b6d.title: How to Revert a Public View Back to Private in Traverse When Permission Error Occurs
00e494a7-d6fd-460d-b74d-0e9aee224b6d.content:
Problem
A user may accidentally change a saved Private View to Public while editing views in Traverse. When attempting to revert the view back to Private, the system displays the following error message:

"TITLE: TRAVERSE
You do not have permissions to edit public views. Please check the business rules. BUTTONS: &OK "

Resolution
This occurs because Traverse has a safety configuration that prevents users from editing Public Views, as these views may be used by multiple users or configured by administrators.
Resolution:
If the Public View was created by you and was made public accidentally, you can temporarily modify the business rule that restricts editing public views and revert it back to private.
Follow the steps below:
- Navigate to System Manager.

- Open Business Rules.

- From the available menus, select System Manager.

- In the list of rule categories, locate the Miscellaneous section.

- Find the rule "Allow editing public view".

- By default, this setting will be set to No. Change it to Yes.

- Apply or save the changes.

Before:
After:
After updating the rule:
- Go back to the Views screen.

- Navigate to Views → Edit Views.

- Locate the view that was accidentally made public.

- Click the Public icon corresponding to that view.

- The Public checkbox will now be disabled, indicating that the view is no longer public and has been reverted to private.

490957f1-7a34-45ba-ba91-f50edd0217a4.title: Using Bank Reconciliation and Accounts Payable to Manage Credit Card Payments in TRAVERSE
490957f1-7a34-45ba-ba91-f50edd0217a4.content:
Problem
This article explains how to manage credit card purchases and payments in TRAVERSE using Bank Reconciliation (BR) and Accounts Payable (AP). This approach allows the system to track credit card expenses, reconcile credit card statements, and properly record payments to the credit card vendor.
Using this method helps avoid manually tracking invoices and ensures that transactions are properly recorded in the General Ledger

Resolution
Step 1 – Create a Liability GL Account
Create a General Ledger liability account for each credit card.
Example:
Account Name: Visa Credit Card Liability
Account Type: Liability
This account represents the balance owed to the credit card company.
Step 2 – Create a Credit Card Bank Account
Navigate to:
Bank Reconciliation → Setup and Maintenance → Bank AccountsUnder the General Tab:
Configure the following:
- Account Type → Credit Card

- GL Account → Credit Card Liability Account

- Credit Card Expiration Date

- Vendor ID → Credit Card Vendor

This bank account will track credit card activity.
Step 3 – Create a Credit Card Vendor
Navigate to:
Accounts Payable → Setup and Maintenance → VendorsCreate a vendor representing the credit card company.
Example:
Vendor ID: VISA
Vendor Name: Visa Credit Card
Important:
The GL Account on the vendor must match the GL account used in the credit card bank account.
Paying Invoices Using the Credit Card
Method 1 – Using AP Hold/Release Invoices
Navigate to:
AP → Pay Invoices → Hold/Release InvoicesSteps:
- Select the Vendor

- Choose the Invoice

- Click Prepay

- Enter the Payment Number (confirmation number)

- Enter the Payment Date

- Select the Credit Card Bank Account

- Click OK

The invoice will now show as paid using the credit card bank account.
Entering Credit Card Payments Through AP Transactions
Navigate to:
AP → Transactions → TransactionsSteps:
- Enter the AP Transaction

- Go to the Payments Tab

- Enter:
- Payment Number

- Payment Date

- Credit Card Bank Account

- Post the transaction

The invoice will move into Open Invoices as a prepaid transaction.
Paying PO Invoices Using a Credit Card
- Enter the Purchase Order

- Receive the goods

- Apply the invoice

- Navigate to Totals → Invoice Totals

- Select the invoice and open Detail

- Go to the Payments Tab

- Enter:
- Payment Amount

- Payment Number

- Payment Date

- Credit Card Bank Account

Post the invoice to move it to Open Invoices as prepaid.
Processing Credit Card Payments
Navigate to:
AP → Pay Invoices → Prepare PaymentsSteps:
- Select the Credit Card Bank Account

- Confirm Prepaid Payments appear

- Print the Prepare Payments Report

- Click Post Payments

Posting payments will update Bank Reconciliation records.
Bank Reconciliation for Credit Card Statements
Navigate to:
BR → Reconciliation → Cleared TransactionsSteps:
- Enter the Statement Date

- Enter the Beginning Date

- Enter the Ending Date

- Enter the Statement Balance

- Mark transactions as Cleared

- Click Save

Print the Reconciliation Report for confirmation.
Entering the Credit Card Payment
After reconciliation:
Navigate to:
AP → Transactions → TransactionsSteps:
- Create an AP Transaction

- Select the Credit Card Vendor

- Enter the Amount from the Reconciliation Report

- Select the Credit Card Liability GL Account

- Post the transaction

The invoice will move to Open Invoices ready for payment.
Final Payment
Navigate to:
AP → Pay Invoices → Prepare PaymentsSteps:
- Select the Checking Account Bank Account

- Process payment normally

- Print Check

- Post Payment

The system will:
- Debit Accounts Payable

- Credit Cash

The credit card liability will be cleared.

76a640b6-5aa3-434b-9b99-75c6efd65901.title: How to change or update the Payroll Year in Traverse?
76a640b6-5aa3-434b-9b99-75c6efd65901.content:
Problem
How can we change or update the Payroll Year in Traverse?



During Year-end processing, once everything is completed, for the old year (for example, 2025), the Payroll person might want to switch to the new Payroll year (for example, 2026), completely moving forward. Or there might be a need to perform an adjustment through Manual Checks on the old year, and want to switch the Payroll year only for one session.



How can we switch Payroll Year under both of these instances?

Resolution
Identifying the Current Payroll Year:

The current payroll year is displayed at the bottom of the Traverse screen in the footer area. This allows us to quickly verify which payroll year is currently active before performing payroll-related tasks.



Accessing the Change Payroll Year Function:

To change the payroll year:

- Double-click the Payroll Year displayed in the footer.

[OR]

- Navigate to PA Change Payroll Year under the Path: Payroll -> Periodic Processing -> Change Payroll Year:

Selecting the Payroll Year:

Within the Change Payroll Year screen:

- Use the Change Year field to select the payroll year that we want to make active.
- This allows us to switch between the current payroll year and prior payroll years, depending on the task being performed.

Changing the Payroll Year for a Single Workstation or Entire System:

Traverse provides two options when changing the payroll year:

- This Workstation Only (Temporary Change):
If we select the “This workstation only” checkbox, the payroll year change will apply only to the current workstation. This is a temporary change that applies only for the current session, allowing us to review or correct prior-year payroll data without affecting other users.
- All Workstations (System-Wide Change)
If we leave the “This workstation only” checkbox unchecked, the payroll year will be updated for the entire system, making the selected payroll year active for all users until it is changed again.



Key Notes:

- Users can temporarily switch to a prior payroll year to review historical data or perform specific corrections. In such situations, it is recommended to use the “This workstation only” option so that other users can continue working in the current payroll year without disruption.
-
A system-wide change should only be used when it is necessary for all users to work within the same payroll year.

1ac39c0f-f69e-41f0-a196-c378719104c3.title: How to Check Who Voided or Deleted a Sales Order in Traverse
1ac39c0f-f69e-41f0-a196-c378719104c3.content:
Problem
A customer reported that some Sales Orders entered in Traverse appear to have been deleted and requested assistance in determining what happened to them. The customer would like to know whether the orders were removed and which user performed the action.

Resolution
In Traverse, Sales Orders are generally voided rather than permanently deleted. To determine if an order was voided and identify the user who performed the action, review the audit/change log for the Sales Order header.
Look for a change in the VoidYn field.
- Old Value: False

- New Value: True

To determine if an order was voided and identify the user who performed the action, review the SM audit explorer for the Sales Order header.
Note that multiple fields may appear in the change log if other updates were made at the same time, but the key indicator is the VoidYn field changing from False to True.

626404f5-879a-4f54-9365-0c9805c40ada.title: Aptean Print Agent Not Running
626404f5-879a-4f54-9365-0c9805c40ada.content:

Issue: The Aptean Print Agent is not running as a Windows service, preventing print jobs from being processed.

b98e35ce-2cf2-41bc-a8e0-eca48b1c8bd4.title: How to resolve the error: 'Current record cannot be deleted' while deleting a MP Production Order?
b98e35ce-2cf2-41bc-a8e0-eca48b1c8bd4.content:
Problem
How to resolve the error: 'Current record cannot be deleted' while deleting a MP Production Order?

Resolution
In cases where an MP Production Order cannot be deleted, it is typically due to existing component entries that are still associated with the order. And we need to delete the entries tied to it. In order to get this done, navigate to the MP Record Production Activity, and review each component.

Kindly follow the below steps to get this done:

i. Access the MP Record Production Activity Screen:
Navigate through the application using the following path: Applications → MFG-Production → Production Orders → MP Record Production Activity


ii. Retrieve the required Production Order:
In the MP Record Production Activity screen, enter the specific Production Order that we wish to delete.


iii. Review and Delete Component Line Entries:
For each component listed under the selected Production Order:
-
- Expand the components tied to the Production Order
- In the Detail section, review all associated line entries.
- Delete each line entry individually to remove the component transactions tied to the Production Order.


iv. Handling Already Posted Entries:
If any of the component entries have already been posted, they cannot be deleted directly. In such cases, we will need to reverse the transactions.
Please refer to the following article on the same: 000094573


v. Save the MP Record Production Activity:
Once all the relevant component entries have been deleted (or reversed and then deleted), click Save to ensure the changes are committed.



vi. Delete the 'Detail' in Production Order:
- Now return to the MP Production Orders screen under the path: Applications → MFG-Production → Production Orders → Production Orders
- Toggle to the 'Detail' section, and then delete the record tied to the 'Production Order' using the below highlighted icon:


vi. Delete the entire Production Order:
- Attempt to delete the Production Order. With all component records removed, the system will now allow the deletion of the Production Order successfully.

b356cd89-c416-4fea-ba92-6cc9b4f286a9.title: How to create Distribution code in AR
b356cd89-c416-4fea-ba92-6cc9b4f286a9.content:
Problem
The customer need assistance with the creating new distribution code so that they can assign to customers.

Resolution
AR - Setup and Maintenance - Distribution Codes
Use the Distribution Codes function to add, change, and delete distribution codes for your general ledger distribution accounts or to set up a selection of different receivable accounts. These general ledger accounts are used when transactions are posted for the customer.
During customer setup, you assign each customer a distribution code to associate the customer with a predefined set of General Ledger accounts. When you post transactions that involve the customers, transaction information moves directly to the accounts you specify for the associated distribution code. This ensures that the same General Ledger accounts debited during invoice entry will be credited during payment or credit entry.
You would also want to set up multiple distribution codes if you want your Aged Trial Balance to be sorted by distribution code grouped by customer.
If you use multicurrency, it's important to remember that Traverse validates the currency assigned to the Receivables account in the distribution codes you set up against the customer's and the base currency. That is, the currency for the Receivables account in the distribution code must match either the customer's currency or the base currency when you assign a distribution code to a customer record. The system validates only the Receivables currency because it assumes that the Freight and Miscellaneous accounts use base currency.
Distribution Codes screen


Creating a Distribution Code
- Click the New button, on the toolbar, to open a blank distribution codes record.

- Enter a new code in the Distribution Code field.

- Enter a description of the new code in the Description field.

- If Accounts Receivable is interfaced with General Ledger, select the following GL accounts:
- Receivables - this account will be debited when posting invoices and credited when posting cash receipts or credit memos.

- Freight - this account is credited for the amount you enter into the freight field on the totals tab when entering transactions.

- Miscellaneous - this account is credited for the amount you enter into the miscellaneous field on the totals tab when entering transactions.

- Deposit Receivables - this account is used when a Project Costing deposit is entered and posted, in place of the Receivables account in the distribution code. This account will get Debited when the deposit is posted and Credited when the cash receipt has been applied to the deposit.

- Deposit Receivables Contra - this account is used when a Project Costing deposit is entered and posted, it will get the credit transaction to off set the debit used in the deposit receivables account. This account will get Credited when the deposit is posted and Debited when the cash receipt has been applied to the deposit.

- If Accounts Receivable is not interfaced with General Ledger, you may enter accounts of your own choosing, but you must have entries in all fields.

- Click the Save button, on the toolbar, to save the new distribution code.

Editing a Distribution Code
- Select a code to edit from the Distribution Code field.

- Edit the fields as necessary.

- Click the Save button, on the toolbar, to save any changes made to the distribution code.

Deleting a Distribution Code
- Select a code to delete from the Distribution Code field.

- Click the Delete button, on the toolbar, to delete the selected distribution code.

- Click Yes at the "Are you sure you want to delete selected record(s)?" prompt.

Produce a Distribution Codes List
Select the print preview button to preview the list .
- The preview report screen appears.

Select the print button in the toolbar to print your list.

b0e56639-6253-4aa2-bfe6-65fc9713bc0b.title: How to Generate Unique Positive Pay Files Without Overwriting Previous Files?
b0e56639-6253-4aa2-bfe6-65fc9713bc0b.content:
Problem
When generating positive pay files for the bank, the system currently overwrites the existing file with the same name, causing loss of historical data. Is there a way to automatically create new files with unique names each time, ensuring previous files remain intact for record-keeping and audit purposes?

Resolution
You can configure the SM Export Layout Definition to automatically generate unique Positive Pay file names by including an asterisk (*) in the File Name. The asterisk will automatically be replaced with a timestamp or run ID each time a file is created.
You should have already set up a file path for the Excel CSV in the Export Layout Definition, as shown below.

Locate the File Name field for the Positive Pay layout.
Include an asterisk (*) in the file name where you want the timestamp or run ID to appear.
Example:
C:\Work\POSPAY_*.csv
Save the Export Layout Definition.

When you go to AP > Create Positive Pay File, the layout will automatically use this path.
Select the checks for which you want to create the Positive Pay file and click Create.
The generated file will automatically have a unique name with the timestamp replacing the asterisk as shown below
This process will generate a new file in the specified destination without overwriting the original file.

6b70dba3-c03f-4ede-9b51-e12beac7c4f4.title: How to display Company Name in the Traverse Title Bar
6b70dba3-c03f-4ede-9b51-e12beac7c4f4.content:
Problem
Users may find it difficult to identify which company they are currently working in within the Traverse application. By default, Traverse only displays small three-letter company initials in the bottom-left corner of the screen, which can sometimes be overlooked. This may lead to confusion when users are switching between multiple companies while processing transactions.

Resolution
We should be able to display the company name in the Title bar by following the below steps:
Enable the setting to display the full company name in the Traverse title bar.
Steps:

-

1dea8a96-8941-4e49-81cb-98657df5fd94.title: Why is the User unable to print the 'Order Status' from the 'MP Record Production Activity' screen?
1dea8a96-8941-4e49-81cb-98657df5fd94.content:
Problem
Why is the User unable to print the 'Order Status' from the 'MP Record Production Activity' screen?



Users may encounter a situation where they are unable to print the “Order Status” report directly from the “MP Record Production Activity” screen within the MFG-Production module.



When attempting to print the report, the Print option is greyed out and as a result, it does not allow the Order Status report to be generated from that screen, preventing users from producing the report while recording production activity.

Resolution
This behavior is typically controlled by a system business rule configuration, which determines whether the Order Status report can be printed online from the Record Production Activity screen.



Cause:

The issue occurs when the “Print Online Order Status” Business Rule is configured to No.

This rule controls whether the Order Status Report can be printed directly from the Record Production Activity screen.

-
Yes –> Allows the Order Status Report to be printed online directly from the Record Production Activity screen.

-
No –> Disables online printing from this screen. In this case, the report must be printed from the MP Order Status screen instead.

If the rule is set to No, the system will not allow printing of the Order Status report from the Record Production Activity screen.



Resolution:

To enable printing of the Order Status Report from the Record Production Activity screen, we need to update the relevant Business Rule setting by following the below steps:

Step 1: Navigate to SM Business Rules:

Access the 'SM Business Rules' by accessing the following path: Applications -> System Manager -> Company Setup -> Business Rules:



Step 2: Locate the Business Rule Setting:

Within Business Rules:

- Select the MP Production Order application.
- Navigate to the Miscellaneous section.
- Locate the rule titled: Print Online Order Status



Step 3: Update the Rule:

Set the rule value to: Yes

This setting enables the system to print the Order Status Report online directly from the 'MP Record Production Activity' screen:

Step 4: Save the Changes

After updating the rule, we need to click Apply and OK to save the configuration changes.



Step 5: Observe the Output:

After enabling the rule:

- Navigate to Applications -> MFG-Production -> Production Orders -> Record Production Activity.
- Select the required Production Order.
- Click the Print button, and we can observe that the 'Order Status' option is enabled now and allowing the report to be printed directly from this screen.







Notes:

If the organization prefers to restrict printing of the Order Status report to the MP Order Status screen only, the Business Rule 'Print Online Order Status' should remain set to: No

In this case, users must generate the report only from MP Order Status screen (filters can be applied as needed)

2c997170-e2c1-45da-b6bf-91a073c8d50b.title: How to Trace the Source Transaction of a General Ledger Entry
2c997170-e2c1-45da-b6bf-91a073c8d50b.content:
Problem
A user reviewing a transaction in the Traverse General Ledger Transaction View may need guidance on how to trace the originating transaction associated with a GL Entry Number.

Resolution
The Entry Number displayed in the General Ledger Transaction View represents the journal entry identifier used to group multiple GL lines that belong to the same posting entry. This number is generated during the posting process and typically does not correspond directly to the originating transaction number in the source module (such as Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, or Inventory).
Because of this, searching for the Entry Number directly within other modules may not return any results. Instead, the originating transaction can be identified using the following methods.
Method 1: Use Fiscal Period and Fiscal Year
- Navigate to GL Transaction View.

- Use the Column Chooser to display additional fields such as:
- Fiscal Period

- Fiscal Year

- Reference

- Note the Fiscal Period and Fiscal Year associated with the entry.

- Navigate to the history or detail view of the module where the transaction likely originated.

- Apply the same Fiscal Period and Fiscal Year filters.

- Review the transactions and match them using identifiers such as:
- Reference

- Transaction amount

- Open the matching record to review the full transaction details.

Example: For a debit of $-18,972.00, the GL Transaction View shows Fiscal Period 2, Year 2026. Using these filters in AP Detail History will reveal the related AP entry and invoice.

Method 2: Use the Post Run Number
- In GL Transaction View, identify the Post Run number associated with the entry.

- Navigate to the history view of the relevant module.

- Filter the results using the same Post Run number.

- Review the transactions included in that posting run to identify the source entry.

- Open the record to review the transaction details.

Key Notes
- The Entry Number in General Ledger is a journal entry grouping identifier, not the originating transaction number.

- Tracing the source transaction typically requires using Fiscal Period/Year, Post Run, or Reference information to locate the related record in the originating module.

b9f5766e-163c-41cd-a3ba-ac70ec08d876.title: Improving Application Performance by Adjusting SQL Server Memory Allocation
b9f5766e-163c-41cd-a3ba-ac70ec08d876.content:
Problem
Users reported application slowness and inconsistent performance. Initial server provisioning was done with minimal resource allocation due to a small user base. Over time, workload demand increased, leading to memory pressure on SQL Server.

Resolution
Microsoft SQL Server was configured with a lower Max Server Memory setting than required for the current workload. This caused:

-
Increased disk I/O

-
Higher PAGEIOLATCH waits

-
Buffer cache pressure

-
Query performance degradation

When SQL Server does not have sufficient memory, it frequently reads data from disk instead of serving it from memory (buffer pool), which significantly impacts performance.



Step 1: Verify Current SQL Memory Configuration

Run the following query:



EXEC sp_configure 'show advanced options', 1;
RECONFIGURE;

EXEC sp_configure 'max server memory (MB)';



Alternatively:



SELECT
name,
value_in_use
FROM sys.configurations
WHERE name = 'max server memory (MB)';

Step 2: Determine Recommended Memory Allocation

General best practice:

-
Leave 4–6 GB for OS (minimum)

-
Allocate remaining memory to SQL Server

-
On dedicated SQL servers, SQL can use ~75–85% of total RAM

Example:

If server has 32 GB RAM:

-
Reserve 4 GB for OS

-
Allocate ~28 GB (28672 MB) to SQL

Step 3: Update Max Server Memory



EXEC sp_configure 'max server memory (MB)', 28672;
RECONFIGURE;



No restart required.

Step 4: Validate Improvement

Monitor:



SELECT
total_physical_memory_kb/1024 AS TotalMemoryMB,
available_physical_memory_kb/1024 AS AvailableMemoryMB
FROM sys.dm_os_sys_memory;



Also check wait stats:



SELECT *
FROM sys.dm_os_wait_stats
WHERE wait_type LIKE 'PAGEIOLATCH%';

754a2339-173c-4b15-99fb-80b67751f040.title: Bin Locations Not Displaying and Not Editable During Physical Inventory
754a2339-173c-4b15-99fb-80b67751f040.content:
Problem
Users reported the following issues during physical inventory processing:

-
Bin locations were missing from the count worksheet, even when "Show Null Bins" was enabled.

-
BIN numbers no longer auto-populated, affecting inventory tracking accuracy.

-
In Physical Count Entry, the bin number field was not editable.

-
The "Full Expand" feature was not functioning as before, requiring manual expansion of entries.

-
Right-click > Bin Number no longer populated bin details.

-
Manual data entry was restricted to the default BIN only, preventing full bin-level tracking.

These issues created significant challenges in validating and completing accurate physical counts.

Resolution
The issue was traced to the Business Rule setting:
“Physical Inventory – Default/No Bins Only”, which was set to Yes.

-
This setting is meant for environments without Warehouse Management installed.

-
When set to Yes, Traverse assumes inventory is stored only in the default bin, disabling bin-level tracking.

-
To restore full bin functionality, the setting was changed to No.

After this change:

-
Bin locations reappeared in the count worksheet.

-
Users were able to enter and edit bin numbers during physical count entry.

-
All related features (e.g., full expand, right-click to populate bin) functioned as expected.

The issue is now resolved.

ba4055b2-4eff-46b9-95e0-43925fa5150f.title: Opening Embedded Document Attachments Without Being Required to select a Download Folder Path. Traverse Global Version 11.2.
ba4055b2-4eff-46b9-95e0-43925fa5150f.content:
Problem
When a user attempts to open or view an embedded document attachment in Traverse Global Version 11.2 by selecting the Attachments feature in AR Transactions, (or in another applicable application transaction entry feature that support the attachments function) then selecting the attached embedded document in the popup window to view the attached documents, they are being required to select a folder to download the document to before they can view it. Is there a way to bypass being required to select a folder path to download the attachment to before it can be reviewed?

Resolution
The solution involves setting a "Default Document folder" path in User Defaults under System Manager.

Note: Embedded Document Attachments are required to be downloaded before they may be viewed or opened. Linked Document Attachments are not required to be downloaded to open, however, the user must have access or permission to the network folder path the document was linked to. If that document is ever removed or the file path changes, that link will no longer work.

Step-by-Step Instructions:
- Navigate to System Manager -> Company Setup -> User Defaults.
- Select the Application SM-System Manager.
- Select the Ellipse in the "Default Document folder" field and select a file path in which you want the attachment to download to. - Setting a Default Document Folder file path in the User Defaults will allow the users to no longer be prompted to select a folder to download the embedded attached document to before it may be viewed. With a default folder path being set, the system will automatically download the document to the Default Document Folder path when the embedded attachment is selected to be viewed.

- Select as applicable the "Open Document After Download" setting [Yes, No, or Prompt].- For Embedded Document Attachments the selections will function as followed for the corresponding selection: - 'Yes', will allow the attachment download automatically to the "Default Document Folder" and will open after it downloads.
- 'Prompt' or leaving field blank, will allow the attachment to automatically download to the "Default Document Folder" and once the download is complete the user will be prompted to either open the attachment or not.
- 'No', will allow the attachment to download automatically to the "Default Document Folder" and the download will not automatically open once the download is complete and the user will not be prompted to either open the attachment or not.

d4f74890-2348-4899-98d1-56a6fea1f016.title: Difference Inactive vs Discontinued GL Accounts
d4f74890-2348-4899-98d1-56a6fea1f016.content:
Problem
The customer requested clarification on the difference between inactive and discontinued general ledger accounts. They highlighted that some accounts will never be used again due to department closures and company policy prohibits reuse of those departments.

Resolution
You can select the account status from the Status field: Active, Inactive, or Discontinued. This status is displayed in all account selection fields throughout Traverse and determines whether transactions associated with the account are posted to the GL Journal. Only accounts with an Active status post to the GL Journal; accounts marked as Inactive or Discontinued do not.
The Inactive and Discontinued statuses prevent entries to accounts that are no longer in use while retaining historical data and maintaining a complete audit trail. If an account will no longer be used in the future, it should be assigned a status of Discontinued.
During processing, the system treats Inactive and Discontinued accounts as invalid. If transactions include amounts for such accounts at the time of posting, the system will not post those amounts to the GL Journal and will display an error message indicating that invalid accounts exist.
To identify invalid, inactive, or discontinued accounts, you can print the Invalid GL Accounts List (available under System Manager > System Audits > Invalid GL Accounts List). Within the General Ledger (GL) module, you can also print the Chart of Accounts List to view inactive or discontinued accounts.
Note: The account status determines whether transactions for that account post to the GL Journal. Only accounts with an Active status are eligible for posting.

bf2cccd3-d7d2-436d-8101-a8b8697c5357.title: Earning Types in Payroll
bf2cccd3-d7d2-436d-8101-a8b8697c5357.content:
Problem
What is the use of Earning Type function in Payroll?

Resolution
Purpose
The Earning Types function is used to set up and maintain the different types of pay employees can receive in Traverse Payroll. Earning types must be set up before earning codes, as earning codes rely on earning types for payroll calculation and reporting.
Important Notes
Earning types must be created before earning codes are set up. All user-defined earning types are treated as regular pay. The Multiplier and Add to Base fields on the Earning Codes screen determine how pay is calculated. Certain earning types are preset in Traverse and have limited edit options.
Preset Earning Types
The following earning types are predefined in Traverse and cannot be deleted or fully modified.
B – Bonus pay C – Commission pay F – Fringe pay. Earning codes with type F are reported in box 12 of the W-2 form. L – Leave pay. This includes sick pay, vacation pay, paid time off, maternity leave, and similar leave types. If Automatic Accrual of Leave Time is enabled in Business Rules, earning codes used to record leave pay must use earning type L. Transactions using earning type L reduce the Remaining Leave Hours shown on the Pay tab in Employee Information. M – Miscellaneous pay O – Overtime pay R – Regular earnings T – Tips reported as federal earnings. These amounts accumulate in the FICA Tips field on the Employee History screen, Miscellaneous tab, and print on W-2 forms and magnetic media files.
User-Defined Earning Types
All user-defined earning types are treated as regular pay. The Multiplier and Add to Base fields on the Earning Codes screen determine how the pay is calculated.
Creating an Earning Type
Click the New button on the toolbar to open a blank earning type record.
Enter a new earning type ID in the Earning Type field.
Enter a description in the Description field.
Decide how the earning code pay affects employee pay.
Leave the Replace checkbox clear to add the earning code pay to the employee’s regular pay.
Select the Replace checkbox to replace the employee’s regular pay with the earning code pay.
For salaried employees, clearing Replace adds the earning code pay to the regular salary.
Selecting Replace replaces the salary with the earning code pay.
Close the screen to save the new earning type.
Editing an Earning Type
Select the earning type from the Earning Type field.
Edit the fields as needed. Earning types B, C, F, L, M, O, R, and T can only have the Description and Replace fields edited.
Close the screen to save the changes.

Deleting an Earning Type
Select the earning type from the Earning Type field.
Preset earning types B, C, F, L, M, O, R, and T cannot be deleted.
Click the Delete button on the toolbar.
Click Yes when prompted to confirm deletion.

42951d1c-0518-4e55-ba00-e135142d3d48.title: Ensuring Correct Cell Formatting When Exporting Data from Interactive Views to Excel
42951d1c-0518-4e55-ba00-e135142d3d48.content:
Problem
When exporting data from an Interactive View to Excel, numeric values may be exported as text instead of numbers. As a result, Excel formulas such as SUM do not calculate correctly, and column totals may appear incorrect. This occurs because the cell formatting is not preserved in a way that Excel recognizes as numeric data.
Reference Screenshot:

Resolution
Interactive Views provide a configuration setting that allows users to control how cells are exported to Excel. This setting ensures that the exported spreadsheet behaves correctly in Excel and that numeric values can be used in formulas without additional conversion.
Steps to Export Cells Properly to Excel:
- Open the Interactive View: Navigate to the view you wish to export in your application. Ensure that the data is displayed correctly on the screen.

- Access Preferences:
- In the menu bar, click on View -> Preferences.

- This opens a configuration window with multiple options.

- Locate Export Setting:
- Look for the option labeled “Export Cells as Displayed.”

- This setting controls how cell values are exported to Excel.

- Understand the Option:
- Enabled / Checked: When this option is enabled, the export process will export the cells exactly as they appear in the Interactive View. This includes formatting, alignment, and display options.

- Disabled / Unchecked: When this option is disabled, the export will attempt to make the spreadsheet act like a native Excel file, preserving numeric types for calculations.

- Choose the Appropriate Setting:

- For scenarios where you need Excel to perform calculations (SUM, AVERAGE, etc.) correctly, ensure that the cells are exported in a true numeric format, not as text.

- If the primary goal is visual fidelity (to match exactly what is displayed in the Interactive View), you may choose to export as displayed, but note that numeric calculations in Excel may require conversion.

- Export the Data:

- After configuring the preference, proceed to export the data to Excel.

- Verify in Excel that numeric columns are recognized correctly. You can test by applying the SUM function or using Excel’s ISNUMBER() function to confirm numeric integrity.

By properly configuring the Export Cells as Displayed option, users can ensure that exported spreadsheets behave predictably in Excel, allowing formulas and calculations to work correctly while maintaining data integrity and appearance. This approach eliminates the need for time-consuming manual conversion of text to numbers and ensures that reports are accurate and ready for analysis immediately upon export.

a3d7c1a9-762d-440c-971b-03bce404d87f.title: Correcting Salaried Employee Hours on Payroll Edit Register
a3d7c1a9-762d-440c-971b-03bce404d87f.content:
Problem
The issue stemmed from salaried employees being assigned to a payroll group with a default of 20 hours, causing the Payroll Edit Register to display 20 hours even for employees who work 40 hours

Resolution
Overview
When payroll checks are calculated for a salaried employee, the system assigns pay information from two primary sources:
- Salary Amount – Entered in the Employee Information screen under the Pay tab.

- Hours Worked – Determined by the employee’s assigned Pay Group Code.

The default hours for each Pay Group are configured in Business Rules → Payroll.
Why This Happens
In the current configuration:
- Employees are assigned to Pay Group 2.

- Pay Group 2 has default hours set to 20 hours.

- As a result, even though the salary amount is correct, the Payroll Edit Register reflects 20 hours, based on the group’s configuration.

This behavior is system-driven and working as designed.
Recommended Long-Term Solution
The simplest and most effective solution is:
- Create a new Pay Group (for example, Pay Group 3 or Pay Group 4).

- Configure it the same as Pay Group 2.

- Set the Default Hours to 40 hours.

- Reassign applicable salaried employees to the new Pay Group.

Once completed:
- Payroll can be calculated for both Pay Group 2 and the new Pay Group simultaneously.

- Correct hours (40) will reflect automatically.

- No weekly manual adjustments will be required.

Alternative (Not Recommended for Ongoing Use)
It is possible to manually enter salary amounts and hours directly in Payroll Transactions prior to calculating checks.
However, this approach:
- Requires specific earning code configurations.

- Involves additional setup.

- Is more time-consuming.

- Is not efficient for long-term processing.

How to Set Default Hours to 40 for a New Pay Group
- Navigate to: System Manager → Company Setup → Business Rules

- Select: Application → PA – Payroll

- Locate the section: Defaults – Hours Per Pay Period

- Identify an unused Group Code (e.g., Group Code 3 or 4).

- Enter the desired default hours:
40.000

- Click Apply and OK to save changes.

- Update the employee records to assign them to the new Pay Group.

04e7daa4-c322-4bd5-acb5-9972d78b2a4d.title: Credit Card Processing Fee Cannot Be Automatically Applied to Invoices
04e7daa4-c322-4bd5-acb5-9972d78b2a4d.content:
Problem
The customer requested guidance on whether Traverse supports automatically applying a 3% credit card processing fee to invoices when customers pay using a credit card, or if the fee must be added manually during invoice entry.

Resolution
The customer inquired about applying a credit card processing fee automatically on invoices in Traverse. Upon review, it was confirmed that Traverse does not currently support an automated calculation or application of credit card processing fees on invoices. As a workaround, the recommended approach is to manually add the 3% credit card processing fee as a separate line item on the invoice when applicable. This limitation and the manual workaround were explained to the customer, who confirmed they are comfortable proceeding with this option.

4893ea6b-bae8-49ab-852d-18341fc34c08.title: W-2 Forms Not Aligning Correctly When Printing (4 Per Page)

-
Use the incorrect W-2 layout provided by the customer as a reference.

d2fe9f20-2b2e-4216-9562-5b7425bbab03.title: How to Create a New 'Views Table ID' without modifying the existing Views?
d2fe9f20-2b2e-4216-9562-5b7425bbab03.content:
Problem
How to create a New Views Table ID without modifying the existing stock 'View' entries in the Views Table of Design Studio?

Resolution
In Traverse (both Standard and Global), modifications to existing Views Table IDs are sometimes required to expose additional fields or adjust view behavior. However, directly editing a stock (default) Views Table ID is not recommended.
Direct modifications to stock IDs may:
- Be overwritten during future build or version updates
- Revert back to default values
- Cause upgrade inconsistencies
- Increase risk during patch deployments
To ensure upgrade-safe customization, changes must be made using a new Views Table ID while preserving the original stock configuration.

This document applies to both Traverse Standard and Traverse Global.
- For Traverse Standard, the changes should be made in the TRAVERSE Design Studio.

- For Traverse Global, the changes should be made in the Traverse Global Design Studio.


Column Definitions (For Reference):
ID:
- The name assigned to the view.
Description:
- Explains what the view displays.
Data Source:
- The SQL query used to retrieve data for the view ID.
- The script may be edited to include:
-
- New columns
- Columns from additional tables
- Custom logic


Available:
- Defines which columns are available: - For server filtering
- In the Column Chooser

Only columns included in the Data Source can be added here.
Default Columns:
Defines which columns appear by default when the view is opened.
- Clicking Reset in the Interactive View restores these columns.
Enumerated Columns:
Used to translate stored numeric values into readable descriptions.
Example:
- 1, 2, 3, 4 → Active, Discontinued, Superseded, Obsolete
Replace ID (Critical for Best Practice):
The Replace ID field is used when copying an existing stock View ID to a new record.
If you are modifying a stock view:
- Enter the original stock View ID in the Replace ID field of your new record.
- This ensures the system uses your customized View ID instead of the stock version.
Using Replace ID:
- Protects customizations from being overwritten during updates
- Maintains upgrade safety
- Preserves original stock configuration
- Ensures system stability

We need to follow the steps below to safely create a new Views Table ID without disturbing the stock configuration:
Step 1: Access the Views Table
- Open TRAVERSE Design Studio
- Navigate to: System Data → Views Table
- Locate the stock Views Table ID that requires customization
NOTE: Do NOT modify the existing stock ID directly.


Step 2: Create a New Views Table Entry
1. Create a new Views Table line entry (assign a new unique ID).

2. Enter the following details (or) Copy from the existing stock ID and paste these values into the newly created record:
-
- Description
- Data Source
- Available
- Default Columns
- Enumerated Columns
- Formats (if applicable)

This ensures the new entry mirrors the stock configuration before customization.


Step 3: Apply Required Customizations and add the 'Replace ID':
Make necessary updates only in the new Views Table ID, such as:
- Adding new columns in the Data Source script
- Adding field names in Available
- Adjusting Default Columns
- Modifying enumerated values
Add the original stock View ID in the Replace ID field of your new record, which needs to be replaced with the new record with the changes:


Step 4: Save Changes
- Click Save to apply changes.
- Close the Views Table screen.
- Log out and relaunch TRAVERSE to refresh metadata.

d72a78f2-4676-45b2-9b2e-c5f394eb6463.title: Running a Daily AR Aging Report in Traverse
d72a78f2-4676-45b2-9b2e-c5f394eb6463.content:
Problem
The Aged Trial Balance Report in Traverse provides a detailed breakdown of invoice balances across five aging periods

Resolution
Aged Trial Balance Report – Overview and Configuration Guide
Overview
The Aged Trial Balance Report displays outstanding invoice balances categorized into five aging periods. The report can be customized based on sorting preferences, aging method, customer type, invoice source, language, currency, and formatting options.
The report includes:
- Unpaid invoices

- Recently paid invoices (based on cutoff settings)

- Optional zero-balance and balance-forward customers

Understanding Cutoff Dates
Transaction Cutoff
The Transaction Cutoff determines which unpaid invoices appear in the report.
You can select either:
- To Date: Includes unpaid invoices with an invoice date on or before the selected date.

- Fiscal Period: Includes unpaid invoices within or before the selected fiscal period and year.

All invoices not fully paid before the transaction cutoff will appear in the report.
Payment Cutoff
The Payment Cutoff determines whether fully paid invoices appear with payment details.
You can select either:
- To Date: Includes payment information for fully paid invoices dated between the selected date and the Transaction Cutoff date.

- Fiscal Period: Includes payment information for fully paid invoices within or after the selected period but before the Transaction Cutoff.

Think of the time between the Payment Cutoff and the Transaction Cutoff as a reporting window that includes:
- Open invoices

- Recently paid invoices

Invoice Source Selection
You can choose which invoice sources to include:
- Sales – Includes invoices from Accounts Receivable, Sales Order, Point-of-Sale, eBusiness, and Mobile Order.

- Projects – Includes project-related billing invoices.

- Service – Includes invoices from the Service Director application.

Invoice Type Selection
Select which invoice types to include:
- Regular – Standard invoices.

- Pro Forma – Pro forma invoices.

Filtering and Report Options
Data Filter
Use the Data Filter to limit report results. Leave blank to include all available data.
Distribution Codes
Select a range of distribution codes to include. Leave blank to include all.
Customer View Options
View Customer
- Detail – Displays full customer transaction details (required to view customer currency).

- Summary – Displays summarized balances only.

Zero Balance Customers
Include customers whose balances are zero.
Current Customers
Include customers with balances only in the Current column.
Balance Forward Customers
Include balance forward customers:
- Displays summarized balances across aging periods.

- Does not show detailed transaction information.

- Open invoice customers will show detailed transactions, including invoices, credits, and receipts.

Sorting and Formatting
Sort By
Choose how to sort the report. Select With Page Breaks to insert page breaks by sort criteria. Leave unchecked for continuous formatting.
View Invoice
Choose how invoice information is displayed:
- Detail

- Summary

- Hidden

Currency Options
If no currency is selected, the report groups and subtotals data by transaction currency.
If a currency is selected in the Report Currency dropdown, the report will convert and display data based on the selected currency.
Aging Configuration
Age By Date
Select how aging should be calculated.
Aging Buckets
- Enter aging days or date ranges.

- Define the starting point for the Current period.

- Enter values in the Past Due fields to define aging categories.

These values determine how invoices are grouped into aging buckets.
Generating the Report
Once all selections are complete, choose one of the following options:
- Print – Prints the Aged Trial Balance Report.

- Output – Saves the report as a PDF.

- Send – Saves as PDF and attaches to an email using your default mail client.

- Preview – Displays a preview before printing.

- Reset – Restores all fields to default values.

4ee033a2-ddbf-4b0d-897f-5525fe6cf24c.title: How to add attachments in 'AP Transactions' of Traverse 11.0?
4ee033a2-ddbf-4b0d-897f-5525fe6cf24c.content:
Problem
How to add attachments to 'AP Transactions' in Traverse Standard version 11.0?

Resolution
In Traverse, we can Embed Documents to a Sales Order, Purchase Order, AP Transaction, or AR Transaction.

For instance, let us take an example of an AP Transaction. Create a Transaction in Accounts Payable -> Transactions -> Transactions, or pull up an existing Transaction:

1. We can observe the attachments icon on the right top of the screen (), and this can be used to enter comments or attach documents corresponding to this record.

2. Click on the Attachments icon () and we can observe a dialog box appear (shown below):



3. In the dialogue box the Priority field: Indicates the importance level of the attachment, such as Regular, High, or Low. The Status field shows the current status of the attachment, such as Public or Private. The Expires field allows a date to be entered to indicate whether the attachment has an expiration date. The Notes field may be updated with information related to the attachment or any additional comments.

4. Browse the Document to attach as a Link in the Link Document field. To view the Document that is attached here, the other users must have access to read the folder where the Document is stored.

5. In order to place a document into the attachment, we can use Embed Document. [That is, this document will be stored in the Database and the other users need not have the folder access to view the document]

6. Click on Save icon to save the attachment in the internal pop-up window. Subsequently, 'Save' the Transaction record to save the changes.

35f9ed82-f14f-4af0-b00e-afe39e063f4f.title: How to resolve the error: "Failed::Value cannot be null." while sending a 'Form' as an Email?
35f9ed82-f14f-4af0-b00e-afe39e063f4f.content:
Problem
How to resolve the error: "Failed::Value cannot be null." while sending a 'Form' as an Email?


The Form ID can be anything as listed below:
- AP Voucher
- AR invoice
- AR Statement
- PA Voucher
- PO Order
- PO Request
- PO Approval Request
- PC Professional Invoice
- PS Invoice
- PS Receipt
- SD Invoice
- SM API Password Reset Notification
- SO Acknowledgement
- SO Invoice
- SO Quote
- SO RMA
- TPS Receipt

Resolution
Overview:

To ensure successful email transmission from the system, proper configuration must be completed in both the SM Document Settings and SM Form Printers screens. These configurations work together to allow the system to generate printed copies as well as send email copies without errors.

It is essential that all related settings are accurately configured for the respective Form ID.



Prerequisites:

Before proceeding with the configuration, please ensure the following requirements are met:

- A valid and working SMTP ID must be created by the Client’s IT team to enable communication with the Mail Server.
- Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) must be disabled for the SMTP ID used for system email transmission.

The following Mail Server details will be required:

- SMTP Name
- SMTP Port
- Server Name
- Username
- Password

These details must be verified with the Client’s IT team prior to configuration.



Configuration Steps:

I. Updating the SMTP ID in SM Document Settings:

This step ensures that the correct SMTP configuration is linked to the appropriate Form ID.

-
Navigate to: Applications → System Manager → Document Delivery → Document Settings

-
In the SM Document Settings screen, we need to retrieve the required Form ID.

-
Assign the appropriate SMTP ID, as defined in the SMTP Settings screen.

-
Save the changes.

This configuration enables the system to use the specified SMTP credentials when sending email copies of the document.



II. Configuring SM Form Printers:

Proper printer configuration is equally important to ensure both printed and emailed copies function correctly.

-
Navigate to: Applications → System Manager → Company Setup → Form Printers

-
Open the SM Form Printers screen.

-
For the same Form ID, ensure that two separate line entries are configured using the appropriate printer:

-
- One entry designated for generating the physical (paper) copy.
- One entry configured for the Email copy.

-
Verify that both entries are correctly assigned and active.

-
Click Save to commit the changes.



Expected Outcome

Once:

-
The correct SMTP ID is configured in SM Document Settings, and

-
Two corresponding entries (Paper and Email) are properly set up in SM Form Printers,

the system will be able to:

-
Generate printed copies as required

-
Successfully process and send email copies without errors

Proper completion of these steps ensures smooth and consistent email transmission functionality.

b7c78774-f0de-47dc-b52b-7a0c2ae4c6c4.title: Unhandled Exception Error in Individual Tracking on PC with Traverse Recently Installed.
b7c78774-f0de-47dc-b52b-7a0c2ae4c6c4.content:
Problem
After installing Traverse on a new workstation, the user is receiving an Unhandled Exception error (shown below), while trying to access the Individual Tracking module.

Cause
The root cause appeared to be that when the Traverse Client Updater was ran after the new installation, it either wasn't pointed to the correct Client Updates Folder, or Windows Security may not have allowed all necessary files download to the Traverse Client folder install.

Resolution
First, checked which build was present from Help and About of the recently installed Traverse Client. Confirmed that this build number matched the build of what other Traverse Client installs were running on and it matched what the Company databases where updated to in the Traverse Server Manager.

Next, tried manually updating TRAVERSE Client folder, by coping the contents from shared Client Updates Folder directly into C:\Program Files\ Open System, Inc\Traverse (Traverse Client install folder). Overwriting all files. After this was done, the Individual Tracking module was able to be accessed from the Traverse installation.

0b14c7e0-0aa5-4c9b-a15c-b4b5904e3ddf.title: CRM Sales History Sync – “Object Ref” Error & Re-Syncing of Historical Data
0b14c7e0-0aa5-4c9b-a15c-b4b5904e3ddf.content:
Problem
The customer reported that the automated Sales History Sync action was failing with an “Object Ref” (Object Reference) error under:
System Manager → Actions → Activity AlertID: CRM Sales History Sync – Automation
Additionally, when performing a manual sync via:
System Manager → CRM Connector → Sales History Sync
The sync completed successfully. However, after clicking APPLY to load data, additional historical data continued to be pushed—even though it should have already been synced.
The expectation was that once historical data was successfully synced, no further data would be queued unless new transactions were created.

Resolution
Impact:
- All users impacted

- Delays in CRM Sales History updates

- Risk of duplicate or repeated historical data syncing

- Reporting and operational inconsistencies

- Manual sync required as temporary workaround.



Steps to Reproduce:
- Navigate to: System Manager → Actions → Activity Locate AlertID: CRM Sales History Sync – Automation Observe “Object Ref” error.

- Navigate to: System Manager → CRM Connector → Sales History Sync

- Perform a manual sync.

- After successful sync, click APPLY to load data.

- Observe additional historical data being pushed again.


Root Cause:
The issue was introduced after upgrading to Build 25031.
A defect in the automated Sales History Sync process caused:
- Object reference errors in the Action automation.

- Previously synced historical records to be re-queued for syncing.

- The system to fail to properly mark records as completed.



Resolution:
This issue has been resolved in Build 25143.
The fix corrects:
- The Object Reference error in the automated Sales History Sync action.

- The logic that determines which records have already been synced.

- The unexpected reprocessing of historical data after manual sync.



Recommendation:
Customers experiencing this issue should upgrade to Build 25143 or later.
After upgrading:
- Re-run the Sales History Sync.

- Verify no Object Ref errors occur.

- Confirm no additional historical data is re-queued after clicking APPLY.

be19de91-10ee-4566-9707-ba458a497130.title: Accounting for Scrap % in Inventory – Manufacturing
be19de91-10ee-4566-9707-ba458a497130.content:
Problem
The customer is seeking clarification on how Scrap % is accounted for in inventory during production.
In the example provided:
- Component item on BOM: Salt

- BOM Quantity: 10

- Scrap %: 2%

The expectation was that the user would enter 10 as the quantity used, and the system would calculate 2% scrap separately.
However, when generating the production order, the system calculates a required quantity of 10.2041 to account for the 2% scrap loss. When recording production activity, the full quantity of 10.2041 is consumed from inventory, and this entire amount is included in the finished good costing.
The customer is questioning whether this is functioning correctly or if it is a system issue.

Resolution
This is not a functionality issue. The system is working as designed.
When a Scrap % is defined on the BOM:
- The system increases the required material quantity during Production Order generation.

- The calculated quantity (e.g., 10.2041) represents the total material required, including expected scrap loss.

- The full calculated quantity is removed from inventory.

- The full quantity is included in finished good costing.

During production activity entry under:
MFG → Production → Production Orders → Record Production Activity
- The Quantity field should reflect the full quantity used (including scrap).

- The Qty Scrapped field can reflect the scrap portion separately.

- Inventory reduction equals the total quantity entered.

Backflush processing follows the same logic.
This behavior ensures accurate material planning, inventory valuation, and production costing. It is considered a training/process clarification, not a defect.

0214dfb2-5e75-4862-a037-9a6e0e8814fd.content:
Problem
How to add the 'Tax Exempt ID' to 'Customers View' for efficient reporting?



The client would like to report customers’ Sales Tax Exemption IDs that are maintained in the following location: Accounts Receivable -> Setup and Maintenance -> Customers: Default Tab: Exempt ID



Currently, the client maintains these exemption IDs at the customer level and would like to include this information in reports for efficient and centralized reporting.



The only standard report available in Traverse for customer master data is the AR Customer Detail List (under Master Lists). But, it is not efficient for reviewing in the table format.



However, the Tax Exempt ID field is not available in the Customers View or the Column Chooser, which prevents the client from including this field in reports.



As a result, the client is unable to generate a comprehensive customer report that includes Tax Exempt IDs for all customer records.

Resolution
Current System Limitation:
In the AR Customer View, the following fields are currently available:
CustId, CustName, Attn, Contact, Addr1, Addr2, City, Region, Country, PostalCode, Phone, Email, Internet, Status, BillToId, ClassId, GroupCode, AcctType, PriceCode, DistCode, TerrId, CustLevel, SalesRepId1, SalesRepId2, CurrencyId, TermsCode, Fax, CreditLimit, CreditHold, TaxCertExpDate, TaxLocId, Taxable, TSCustomerEntityCode, ValidAddress, TaxPayerType1, TaxPayerType2, TaxID1, TaxID2

Although several tax-related fields are available, Tax Exempt ID is not exposed in the view and therefore does not appear in the Column Chooser for reporting.

Resolution Overview:
The Tax Exempt ID field exists at the database level but is not added to the Customers View definition. To make it available for reporting, we need to expose this field through Design Studio by updating the Views Table.

This solution applies to both Traverse Standard and Traverse Global.


Resolution Steps:
Step 1: Access Design Studio
i. Launch Design Studio
ii. Navigate to the following path: System Data -> Views Table
iii. In the Views Table, and locate the Customers View ID

NOTE: It is recommended to NOT modify the stock Views Table ID directly.


Step 2: Create a New Views Table Entry:
i. Create a new Views Table line entry (new ID) using the + icon:

ii. Copy the following from the existing Customers View ID and paste it into the new record:
- Description
- Data Source
- Available Fields
- Default Columns
- Enumerated Columns
- Any other relevant configuration
This ensures the new record mirrors the stock configuration before customization.

Step 3: Replace the Stock ID (Critical Step):
In the newly created Views Table entry:
- Locate the “Replace ID” field
- Enter the stock Customers View ID in this field
This ensures the new custom record replaces the stock ID during runtime.

Why This is Best Practice?
Using the “Replace ID” approach:
- Reduces the risk of custom changes being overwritten
- Protects modifications during future build updates
- Maintains upgrade-safe customization
- Avoids reverting to default/stock configurations
Direct modification of stock IDs is not recommended.


Step 4: Review the Data Source definition:
SELECT * FROM (SELECT p.[CustId], p.[CustName], p.[Contact], p.[Addr1], p.[Addr2], p.[City], p.[Region], p.[Country], p.[PostalCode], p.[ShipZone], p.[IntlPrefix], p.[Phone], p.[Fax], p.[Attn], p.[ClassId], p.[SalesRepId1], p.[SalesRepId2], p.[Rep1PctInvc], p.[Rep2PctInvc], p.[TermsCode], p.[PmtMethod], p.[GroupCode], p.[StmtInvcCode], p.[AcctType], p.[PriceCode], p.[DistCode], p.[CalcFinch], p.[CreditLimit], p.[CreditHold], p.[PartialShip], p.[AutoCreditHold], p.[TaxLocId], p.[Taxable], p.[TaxExemptId], p.[CurrencyId], p.[TerrId], p.[CcCompYn], p.[CustLevel], p.[Email], p.[Internet], p.[Phone1], p.[Phone2], p.[AllowCharge], p.[Status], p.[BillToId], p.[TaxCertExpDate], p.[TSCustomerEntityCode], p.[ValidAddress], p.TaxPayerType1, p.TaxPayerType2, p.TaxID1, p.TaxID2 {CF} FROM dbo.trav_tblArCust_view p) ds


Step 5: Add Tax Exempt ID to Available Fields:

305817b2-6366-485c-a845-fc8e4687eb96.title: GL Trial Balance and AP Aged Trial Balance Variance After Update Current Year
305817b2-6366-485c-a845-fc8e4687eb96.content:
Problem
After completing the Update Current Year process, the client notices that the AP Control Account balance in the GL Trial Balance does not match the AP Aged Trial Balance.
This mismatch is usually discovered during post–year-end validation or when reviewing balances in the new fiscal year. Re-running the Update Current Year process often does not resolve the issue, which can cause confusion about whether the rollover itself failed.

Resolution
The Update Current Year process only carries forward the balances that exist at the moment it is run.
If any AP-related transaction (such as a Debit Memo or adjustment) is posted after the rollover, especially into a prior fiscal year, that transaction will not automatically be reflected in future-year beginning balances.
As a result, the GL and AP subledger can drift out of sync, even though the rollover technically completed successfully.

Follow the steps below in order. These checks usually identify the cause without requiring corrective action right away.

1. Confirm Year-to-Year Balance Carryforward
Start by reviewing the GL Account Balance View for the AP Control Account.
You are looking to confirm:
- The ending balance of one fiscal year matches the beginning balance of the next

- This holds true for each year up to the current fiscal year

If balances match across years, the Update Current Year process most likely worked as expected.


2. Look for Late Prior-Year Postings
Check whether any AP activity was posted after the Update Current Year process was completed, such as:
- Debit Memos

- AP invoices

- Adjustments posted into a closed or prior fiscal year

Late postings are a very common reason for variances and are easy to miss during year-end processing.

3. Check for Manual Entries to the AP Control Account
Review the GL detail for the AP Control Account.
Look specifically for:
- Manual journal entries posted directly to the AP Control Account

- Entries that did not originate from the AP module

Since the AP Aged Trial Balance only reflects AP subledger activity, manual GL postings will cause a mismatch.
4. Validate Account Usage and Mapping
Ensure that:
- AP transactions are posting to the correct AP Control Account

- Non-AP transactions are not hitting the AP Control Account

- Prepaid or asset accounts are being used correctly

Misposted transactions can shift balances out of AP while still appearing valid in the GL.

5. Review Posting Dates vs Invoice Dates
Check for timing differences where:
- The AP invoice date is in one period

- The GL posting date falls in another


6. Investigate Small Remaining Differences
If most of the variance is explained but a small amount remains:
- Review tax amounts

- Freight charges

- Rounding differences

These often account for minor residual variances once the main issue is identified.

471a8ace-05c2-40a1-8de6-77d4f24adfe5.title: APS Printer Visibility Limitation – Local and Print Server Printers Cannot Be Viewed Simultaneously
471a8ace-05c2-40a1-8de6-77d4f24adfe5.content:
Problem
A bug request has been submitted for the SaaS environment affecting product versions 11.0 and 11.2, and the issue remains unresolved in all versions at the time of writing.

Resolution
Issue:
Determine whether it is possible for both Print Server printers and locally installed printers to appear simultaneously in the user’s print queue in APS without using redirected printing.
Currently, this is not possible.

Problem Description:
The client is using APS and printer visibility depends entirely on how APS is configured:
- When APS is configured to the user’s local PC, only locally installed printers are visible.

- Printers shared from another device (Print Server printers) are not visible.

- When APS is configured to the Print Server, only shared printers are visible.

- Locally installed printers are not visible in this configuration.

The client requires both locally installed printers and shared Print Server printers to appear together in the print selection list without relying on redirected printing.

Impact:
- Users cannot access all required printers in a single configuration.

- They must switch configuration settings depending on printing needs.

- This disrupts workflow and reduces efficiency.

- There is no seamless printer selection experience.


Replication:
This issue is consistently reproducible.
Steps to Reproduce:
- Configure APS printer settings to the user’s local machine.
- Observe that only locally installed printers are visible.

- Reconfigure APS printer settings to the Print Server.
- Observe that only shared Print Server printers are visible.

- Attempt to view both printer types simultaneously.

Result:
Only one printer source (local or print server) can be visible at a time.


Workaround:
There is currently no direct workaround.
The only available option is to configure APS to either:
- The local PC, or

- The Print Server

Both cannot be used simultaneously without redirected printing.

Current Status:
This has been submitted as a bug request under . As of now, the issue is present in versions 11.0 and 11.2 and remains unresolved.
Note: Print Server configuration testing was confirmed based on environment behavior. Only one printer source is visible at a time depending on APS configuration.

0fde9f26-9a6a-4c1d-9703-b73b99c21562.title: Unable to Void Payments Without a Payment Number
0fde9f26-9a6a-4c1d-9703-b73b99c21562.content:
Problem
Users are unable to void payments that were posted without a payment/check number in:
AP → Pay Invoices → Void Payment
When attempting to void the payment, the system flags the transaction as an exception, and the standard void process cannot be completed.
This typically occurs when the Business Rule “Allow posting without check numbers” is enabled and a payment has been posted without a payment number.

Resolution
Steps to Reproduce
- Navigate to: Accounts Payable (AP) → Pay Invoices

- Create and post a payment without assigning a payment/check number
- Ensure the setting is enabled: Business Rules → Accounts Payable → Allow posting without check numbers = Yes

- Post the payment against one or more invoices.

- Go to: AP → Pay Invoices → Void Payment

- Attempt to void the payment.

- Result: The transaction is flagged as an exception and cannot be voided using the standard void process.


Uploading image...


Void via BR
- Navigate to: BR → Transactions → Void Checks and Stop Payments

- Locate the payment.

- Change status from Paid → Voided

- Save.


Post the BR transaction.
The payment will be reinstated in: AP → Hold/Release Invoices.

625b2e78-366d-4cc9-abdc-ecc3e9dfca71.title: Resolving Email Alert Delivery Issues Due to Incorrect Email Formatting
625b2e78-366d-4cc9-abdc-ecc3e9dfca71.content:
Problem
The customer reported that emails configured through Alerts (e.g., Employee Birthday alert) were not being received.
Initial troubleshooting included updating the SMTP password under:
System Manager → Document Delivery → SMTP Settings
However, changing the SMTP password did not resolve the issue.

Resolution
The issue was caused by incorrect formatting in the "Send To Email" field within the Alert configuration.
Specifically:
- Multiple email addresses were entered.

- There were spaces after the semicolon (;) separator.

- Email addresses must:
- End with a semicolon (;)

- Have no spaces between email addresses

- Start immediately after the semicolon

The extra spaces prevented the system from sending the email.


Step 1: Verify SMTP Settings (Initial Troubleshooting)
Navigate to:
System Manager → Document Delivery → SMTP Settings
- Confirm SMTP credentials are correct.

- Re-enter and update the password if necessary.

- Save changes.

Step 2: Test Alert Trigger
To confirm alert functionality:
- Navigate to: Payroll → Setup and Maintenance → Employee Information

- Create or modify an employee record.

- Set the Date of Birth to today’s date.

- Save the record.

This should trigger the Birthday Alert email.

Step 3: Verify Alert Email Configuration
- Navigate to: System Manager → Actions → Actions

- Select the alert that is not sending emails (e.g., Employee Birthday).

- Go to the Email section.

- Review the Send To Email field.

Correct Format Example:
email1@domain.com;email2@domain.com;Incorrect Format Example:
email1@domain.com; email2@domain.com;Do NOT include spaces after semicolons.
- Remove any spaces between email addresses.

- Save the changes.


After correcting the email formatting (removing spaces after semicolons), the alert emails were successfully triggered and received.
