a293a69c-97cf-4dd7-a761-bf32055ef6e9.title: How to Compare Two Columns in an Interactive View Using Filter Editor
a293a69c-97cf-4dd7-a761-bf32055ef6e9.content:
Problem
Users may need to compare values between two columns within an Interactive View (for example, in the Inventory Item View).
A common requirement is to filter records where:
Qty On Hand < Safety Stock
By default, standard filters typically compare a column to a fixed value. However, users may need to compare one column directly against another column within the same view.
How to achieve this behavior?

Resolution
It is possible to compare two columns within an Interactive View by using the Filter Editor.
Follow the steps below:
Example Scenario
Filter the Inventory Item View to display items where: Qty On Hand is less than Safety Stock

Steps to Create the Filter
- Open the Inventory Item View (or the required Interactive View).

- Locate the Qty On Hand column.

- Right-click on the Qty On Hand column header.

- From the pop-up menu, select the Filter Editor (Funnel icon).


- In the Create Filter Criteria window:
- Select Qty On Hand as the field.

- Choose the operator Less Than.

- Click on the Pencil icon (value selector).


- From the list of available column headers, select Safety Stock.


- Click Apply.

- Click OK to confirm.



Result
The Interactive View will now display only the records where:
Qty On Hand < Safety Stock


This method allows dynamic column-to-column comparison without exporting data or using external tools.

bb1a210d-8075-4ae1-a8f2-d819fcc9c19d.title: Mobile WMS – Pick/Pack/Ship Menu Overview and Functionality
bb1a210d-8075-4ae1-a8f2-d819fcc9c19d.content:
Problem
How does the Pick/Pack/Ship Menu in the mobile warehouse management application function, and how do the Pick Items, Pick Raw Material, Pack Orders, Ship, and Record Labor Time options impact inventory quantities, transaction statuses, production processing, and shipping updates?

Resolution
The Pick/Pack/Ship Menu within the mobile warehouse application provides operational control over outbound order fulfillment, production material issuance, packing, shipping updates, and labor tracking. These functions interact with released transactions created in the desktop system and ensure inventory accuracy, transaction status updates, and audit traceability.
- Pick Items

The Pick Items function records inventory issued against sales orders (New order type), PO returns, PC material requisitions, WM material requisitions, and WM transfers (From location). Transactions must first be released through the WM Release Items function in the desktop client before they are available for mobile processing.
When items are picked, committed quantities are allocated from inventory and the transaction status changes to Picked. Inventory is reserved for the order and cannot be used elsewhere; however, the On Hand quantity is not yet reduced.
Picking may be initiated by entering a Pick ID or an Order Number. The system displays items associated with the transaction and allows entry of Container (if enabled), Lot, Bin, Serial Number (if applicable), and Qty Picked. Serialized items require individual entries per serial number with a quantity of one. The Unit of Measure and Qty Remaining are displayed for reference.
Picking begins by entering a Pick ID or Order Number.
List Tab
The List tab displays all line items associated with the selected pick list or order. Line-level details can be expanded for additional visibility.
Selecting a line item opens the Detail tab.

Detail Tab
The Detail tab captures item-level picking information, including:
- Item ID

- Container (if the WM Use Containers rule is enabled)

- Lot Number (if applicable)

- Bin Number

- Serial Number (if applicable; serialized items require one entry per serial number with Qty Picked = 1)

- Qty Picked

The Unit of Measure and Qty Remaining are displayed for reference.
When items are picked, committed quantities are allocated and the transaction status changes to Picked. Inventory is reserved for the order and cannot be used elsewhere; however, the On Hand quantity is not reduced at this stage unless the Pick and Pack Together rule is enabled.
Validation follows system configuration:
- When Use Container = Yes: validation sequence is Container, Bin, Lot, Serial, and Qty.

- When Use Container = No: validation sequence is Bin, Lot, Serial, and Qty.

Picked Tab
The Picked tab lists all items picked during the current session. Entries may be reviewed or removed prior to completion.
If the Pick and Pack Together rule is enabled, inventory is removed from On Hand once picking is finished. If disabled, items are staged to a packing bin and removed during the Pack process.
For sales orders, a Shipping Information section may be available to record Ship Number, Ship Method, and Ship Date before completing the pick.
- Pick Raw Material

The Pick Raw Material function records issuance of raw material components to production orders or releases that are in In Process status. Orders must be released through the WM Release Orders function before they are available for mobile processing.
When raw materials are picked, On Hand quantities are decreased, committed quantities are removed, and interim general ledger entries are created to track production costs.
Users select a Pick ID or Production Order/Release and issue materials by recording Container (if enabled), Lot, Bin, Serial Number (if applicable), and Qty Picked. Serialized components require separate entries per serial number with a quantity of one.
List Tab
The List tab displays raw material line items associated with the selected production order or release. Bin and On Hand information may be expanded for visibility.
Selecting a line item opens the Detail tab.
Detail Tab
The Detail tab records:
- Container (if enabled)

- Lot Number (if applicable)

- Bin Number

- Serial Number (if applicable; serialized items require one entry per serial number with Qty Picked = 1)

- Qty Picked

The Unit of Measure and Qty Remaining are displayed.
Validation sequencing follows the same configuration logic:
- With Use Container = Yes: Container, Bin, Lot, Serial, Qty

- With Use Container = No: Bin, Lot, Serial, Qty

Picked Tab
The Picked tab lists all raw materials issued during the session. Items may be reviewed before finalizing the pick.
The Pick and Pack Together rule determines whether material is removed immediately from inventory or staged prior to final issue.
- Pack Orders


Pack Orders
The Pack Orders function applies previously picked items to orders and is equivalent to the desktop WM Pack Orders function. It is used after picking is completed when the Pick and Pack Together business rule is not enabled.
When items are packed, committed quantities remain allocated and the transaction status changes to Staged. Inventory is reserved for the order and cannot be used elsewhere. On Hand quantities are reduced when the pack/issue process is confirmed.
If the Pick and Pack Together business rule is set to Yes, the Pack function is not used. Once picking is finished and confirmed, the items are automatically packed/issued to the order.
A released transaction must exist before items are available for packing.

Packing List Printing
Packing lists can be printed automatically from either:
- The Pick Items function, on the Picked tab, when Pick and Pack Together is selected and Finish Pick is tapped.

- The Pack Orders function, on the Packed tab, when Confirm is tapped.

This functionality is controlled by the ‘Print Packing List’ WM business rule. The rule must be set to Yes for Mobile WMS to print a packing list.
The packing list is sent directly to the configured printer. Before printing is available, a default printer must be configured through:
- SM User Defaults, or

- SM User Defaults – Admin

If no default printer is defined in either location, the packing list will not print.
Additional packing list behavior:
- Additional descriptions for IN items print by default

- Kit details print by default

- Drop ship items print by default

- Barcodes do not print by default

- No activity log is generated


Pack Orders Processing Flow
A default packing bin is automatically populated in the Bin Number field. The bin may be changed if necessary.
Entering the Order Number loads associated line items.
List Tab
The List tab displays all items available for packing. Line details can be expanded for visibility.
Kitted items are indicated with an icon. When a kit parent item is selected, lot and serial number fields are disabled.
A Fill All option allows all remaining quantities to be packed simultaneously.
Detail Tab
Selecting a line item opens the Detail tab, where packing information is recorded:
- Item ID

- Container (if applicable)

- Lot Number (if applicable)

- Serial Number (if applicable; serialized items require separate entry per serial with packed quantity = 1)

- Qty Packing

The Unit of Measure and Qty Remaining are displayed.
Packed Tab
The Packed tab lists all items packed in the current session. Entries may be reviewed or removed prior to confirmation.
If the source document is a sales order (SO), a Ship Information section is visible. This allows entry of:
- Ship Number

- Ship Method

Selecting Update sends this shipping information to the sales order record. This action updates shipping details only and does not complete shipment processing.
Selecting Confirm completes the packing process and returns to the Pack Orders screen for the next order. If the Print Packing List rule is enabled, a packing list prints automatically at this point.

Ship
The Ship function updates shipping information on the source order after packing is complete. Users enter the Order Number, Ship Number, and Ship Method. The selected method description appears in the Ship Via field.
The Update action applies shipping information to the order record. Final shipment processing is completed through the desktop system.
Record Labor Time
The Record Labor Time function tracks labor activity against production operations. Users select the applicable Order/Release and choose the operation associated with the work performed.
The function captures Requirement ID, start and finish times or total hours and minutes, production date, quantity produced, quantity scrapped (if applicable), variance code, setup indicator, and notes. Variance codes are stored in production history for reporting and analysis.
Recorded operations may be reviewed, edited, or completed within the session. Completing an operation finalizes the labor time entry for that transaction.
List Tab
The List tab displays operations associated with the selected Order/Release.
Selecting an operation opens the Detail tab.
Detail Tab
The Detail tab records:
- Requirement ID

- Start and Finish Time OR Hours and Minutes

- Date

- Qty Produced

- Qty Scrapped (if applicable)

- Variance Code (stored in production history for reporting)

- Setup indicator

- Notes

Entries may be reviewed in the Recorded tab, where operations can be finalized. Completing an operation finalizes labor time recording for that transaction.

8205ff77-cb3b-47e8-9c76-6076f3126597.title: Invoices Sent with Incorrect Details Due to Post-Printing Adjustments
8205ff77-cb3b-47e8-9c76-6076f3126597.content:
Problem
Invoices sent through Traverse Global may contain incorrect details if modifications to non-taxable amounts, freight charges, or other financial data are made after the invoice has been printed and automatically emailed.

Resolution
When Auto Send Document Delivery is enabled in Traverse Global, the system automatically emails the invoice immediately after it is printed.

If changes are made to the order after the invoice is printed and sent, the system updates the order totals internally — but the customer has already received the original version of the invoice.

This results in a mismatch between:

1.The emailed invoice total
2.The updated order total in the system.

This happens due to Auto Send Document Delivery enabled:

1.Printing the invoice triggers automatic email delivery.
2.The invoice reflects the values at the exact time of printing.
3.Any edits made afterward update the order but do not recall or update the already-sent invoice.
The system is functioning as designed.

Recommended Best Practice to prevent future discrepancies:

1.Ensure all pricing adjustments are completed before printing the invoice.
2.Verify freight amounts are finalized.
3.Confirm tax and non-taxable values are accurate.
4.Only print the invoice once all changes are complete when Auto Send is enabled.

Optional control measure:

Consider temporarily disabling Auto Send Document Delivery if invoices may require post-print adjustments.

c98f5041-e46a-4d48-b7e5-0387322a4415.title: Using the Containers Menu in Mobile WMS (Make, Move, Combine, Undo)
c98f5041-e46a-4d48-b7e5-0387322a4415.content:
Problem
How do users create, move, combine, or undo containers within Mobile WMS to accurately manage item movement at the bin and container level inside the warehouse?

Resolution
The Containers menu in Mobile WMS allows users to manage item movement within bins and containers inside a warehouse location.
Key Concepts:
- Containers exist within bins.

- A bin can exist without a container.

- A container cannot exist outside of a bin.

- Container IDs must be unique within a company.

- A container cannot exist in more than one bin at the same time.

- Containers can be moved across Inventory (IN) locations.

Warehouse Management ensures accurate tracking of inventory at a more detailed level than standard Inventory processing, which is essential for efficient picking, receiving, and internal transfers.
The Containers menu includes four functions:
- Make Container

- Move Container

- Combine Container

- Container Undo


1. Make Container
Purpose
The Make Container function allows users to:
- Create a new container (if it does not already exist).

- Move selected quantities of items into a working container.

- Stage items in a working bin before dropping them into a final bin/container.

If a container is auto-generated and does not already exist, it is created in the default bin of the IN location.
Important Behavior
- When moving a full container into a bin that is not the user’s working bin, the entire quantity moves.

- When moving from a non-default bin into the working bin, you can specify the quantity to move.

- The Lot Number Behavior business rule determines whether lot numbers can be changed during movement.

Steps to Make a Container
Pick Tab
- Scan or enter the Item ID.

- Scan or enter the Container (if applicable).

- Scan or enter the Lot Number, if required.

- Scan or enter the Bin Number.

- Scan or enter the Serial Number, if applicable.
- Serialized items require separate entries for each serial number with a quantity of 1.

- Enter the Qty to Move.

- Adjust the Unit of Measure if needed.

- Repeat for additional items as required.

Validation Notes:
- If Use Container = Yes, validation occurs in this order:
- Container → Bin Number

- If Use Container = No:
- Only Bin Number is validated.

- For serialized items, data entry sequence:
- Item ID → Bin Number → Container → Serial Number

- For serialized lotted items:
- Item ID → Bin Number → Container → Lot Number → Serial Number

Drop Tab
- Enter the destination Container.

- Enter the destination Bin.

- Confirm to complete the process.

Use Menu to return to the main menu.

2. Move Container
Purpose
The Move Container function allows users to move an entire container and all of its contents from one bin to another.
This function is used when:
- Relocating stored inventory.

- Reorganizing warehouse layout.

- Moving containers between bins or locations.

Steps to Move a Container
- Scan or enter the source Bin From.

- Scan or enter the Container From.

- Scan or enter the destination Bin To.
- The contents of the container will display in the grid.

- Tap Confirm to complete the move.

Use:
- Clear to reset fields.

- Menu to return to the main menu.

All contents of the container move together; partial movement is not allowed in this function.

3. Combine Container
Purpose
The Combine Container function moves all items and quantities from one bin/container into another bin/container.
This is useful when:
- Consolidating inventory.

- Reducing the number of containers.

- Preparing shipments.

The entire contents of the source container are merged into the destination container.
Steps to Combine Containers
- Scan or enter the source Bin From.

- Scan or enter the source Container From.

- Scan or enter the destination Bin To.
- The destination bin must be different from the source bin.

- Scan or enter the destination Container To.
- All items in the source container will be listed.

- Tap Confirm to complete the combination.

Use:
- Clear to reset fields.

- Menu to return to the main menu.


4. Container Undo
Purpose
The Container Undo function removes all items from a container and places them directly back into the bin, leaving the container empty.
This is used when:
- A container was created in error.

- Items need to be de-containerized.

- Warehouse restructuring is required.

Important Note: If the WM business rule requires containers, this function will not be available and a system message will appear.
Steps to Undo a Container
- Scan or enter the Bin Number containing the container.

- Scan or enter the Container to empty.
- The system will display all items currently inside.

- Tap Confirm to complete the process.

Use:
- Clear to reset fields.

- Menu to return to the main menu.

f4d4f75d-c512-4f01-9dd3-0ab988d4faad.title: How to Configure Company, Location, Theme, and Default Printer in Mobile WMS
f4d4f75d-c512-4f01-9dd3-0ab988d4faad.content:
Problem
How can users configure session-level settings in Mobile WMS, such as Company, Location, Theme, and Default Printer, to ensure transactions and preferences align with their operational needs?

Resolution
The Settings menu in Mobile WMS allows users to control key session-level preferences that affect how the system behaves during their login. These settings determine which company and location transactions are processed under, how the interface appears visually, and which printer is used for label printing.
All changes made in the Settings menu apply to the currently logged-on user and, in certain cases, are retained for future sessions.

Company
The Company setting allows users to switch the active company within Mobile WMS for the current session. This option is available only if the logged-on Traverse user has access to multiple companies in System Manager (SM Users), and if proper WM user mapping exists within those companies.
The Company field displayed in the Settings screen reflects the company currently in use. Changing this setting updates the default company for the active session. Once updated, all Mobile WMS transactions will be processed under the selected company.
If needed, the Clear option restores the field to its default value. The Menu option returns the user to the main menu.

Location
The Location setting controls which inventory location Mobile WMS uses during the session. Transactions within Mobile WMS are location-specific, meaning users will only see and process transactions for the selected location.
The Location displayed on the Settings screen indicates the location currently active for the session. When the location is changed, Mobile WMS immediately limits all transaction visibility and processing to that selected inventory Location ID.
The selected location is saved and becomes the default location the next time the user logs into Mobile WMS.
The Clear option resets the field to its default value, and the Menu option returns to the main menu.

Theme
The Theme setting allows users to control the visual appearance of the Mobile WMS interface.
The system provides multiple theme options, with the Light theme set as the default.
Users can select an alternate theme, such as Dark mode, for their current session. The selected theme changes the overall display style of the application but does not impact system functionality or transaction processing.
The Clear option restores the default theme setting, and the Menu option returns to the main menu.

Default Printer
The Default Printer setting defines which label printer will be used for printing labels during Mobile WMS transactions. This setting applies to the currently logged-on user.
The selected printer must be installed on the server hosting Mobile WMS. Only installed or supported virtual printers will appear as selectable options.
Important limitations include:
- Redirected printers (such as those visible through Remote Desktop sessions) are not available.

- Microsoft Print to PDF and Microsoft XPS Writer cannot be selected.

Once selected, the printer becomes the default for label printing activities. The Clear option resets the selection to its default value, and the Menu option returns to the main menu.

def5d42d-610a-4d69-b9c9-ca36ba9a4317.title: How to Receive By-Products in Mobile WMS for a Production Order
def5d42d-610a-4d69-b9c9-ca36ba9a4317.content:
Problem
Users need to record and receive by-products generated during a production process into inventory using Mobile WMS. By-products are inventory items created as a secondary result of manufacturing (for example, sawdust from furniture production) and must be properly linked to a finished good in the Bill of Materials (BOM). This article explains the prerequisites, process steps, and system behavior when receiving by-products against a production order.

Resolution
The Receive By-Products function in Mobile WMS allows users to record by-products produced during the completion of a production order and move them into inventory.
By-products are:
- Defined as inventory items.

- Assigned a standard cost.

- Configured in the BOM with a Detail Type of By-Product.

- Associated with a finished good in Bill of Material Maintenance.

Unlike scrap, by-products have tangible value and are tracked as inventory.
To receive a by-product, the related manufacturing Production Order must already exist and be in In Process status.

Prerequisites
Before receiving by-products, ensure the following:
- The by-product item exists in the Inventory.

- The item has a standard cost assigned.

- The item is set up as a By-Product in the BOM and linked to a finished good.

- The production order for the by-product is created and is in In Process status.


Step-by-Step Process to Receive By-Products
1. Access the Production Order
- Scan or enter the Production Order and Release Number in the Order/Release No field.

- Navigate to the List tab to view available by-products for that order.

2. Select the By-Product
- Tap the item from the List tab, or

- Open the Detail tab and scan the item directly.

If receiving all by-products at once, use the Receive All button.

3. Enter Item Details (Detail Tab)
Provide the following information as applicable:
Lot/Serial/Expiration Information
- Enter Lot Number, Serial Number, and Expiration Date if required.

- For serialized items, each serial number must be entered individually with a quantity of 1.

Bin Selection
- The system defaults to:
- Item/location default bin (if defined), or

- Location default bin.

- You may select a different bin from the drop-down list.

Receiving process options:
- Two-Step Process: Receive into a receiving bin first, then use Put Away later.

- Single-Step Process: Receive directly into a stocking bin.

Business Rule Impact:
- If Default Bin on Receiving WM = No, the Bin field will be blank.

Container (If Applicable)
- If WM Use Containers = No, the field does not appear.

- If WM Containers Auto Create = Yes, you can create a new container using the Add button.

Label Printing
- Enter or adjust the number in the No. of Labels field.

Quantity
- Enter the quantity in Qty Received.

- If Default Quantity on Receiving WM = No, default quantity will be zero.

The unit of measure will display automatically.
Repeat the process for each by-product item as needed.

Reviewing Received Items
Received Tab
The Received tab displays all by-products received during the current session.
- Items received in the current session display a Delete icon.

- Receipt Number is auto-generated using the format <YearMonthDateTime>.

- Receipt date defaults to the workstation’s current date.

To remove items (before confirmation):
- Mark the checkbox next to the Delete icon.

- Confirmed items cannot be deleted.

Label Printing
From the Received tab:
- Adjust Label Qty if needed.

- Select checkboxes for items to print labels.

- Use Select All or Deselect All as required.

- Expand the Printer section to select a different printer if needed.

Important Notes:
- Only printers installed on the Mobile WMS server are available.

- Redirected printers (via RDP), Microsoft Print to PDF, and Microsoft XPS Writer are not supported.

Use the Printer icon to preview, print, or download labels.
Confirming the Receipt
Tap Confirm to finalize the receipt.
- A green confirmation message will appear indicating successful processing.

- Once confirmed, the receipt cannot be modified.

Receive and Putaway Options
At the time of confirmation:
- If Receive and Putaway Together is checked:
- Items are placed directly into stock in the selected bins.

- If unchecked:
- Items are moved to a receiving bin.

- You must later use the Put Away function to move items into stocking bins.

Additional Options
- Use the Clear button to reset the screen.

- Select Menu to return to the Receiving menu when finished.

634ffca2-202e-4bd4-8157-4273c7c662cf.title: How to access a SharePoint document library locally through Traverse while exporting
634ffca2-202e-4bd4-8157-4273c7c662cf.content:
Problem
This article explains how to access a SharePoint document library locally through OneDrive synchronization and use it as an export location when exporting data from Traverse. This approach leverages the redirected local drive available in the session.

Resolution
Prerequisites

Before proceeding, ensure the following:

-
OneDrive is installed and signed in on the local machine.

-
The required SharePoint document library is successfully synchronized via OneDrive.

-
You are connected to the remote session where local drives are redirected (RDP / TS session).

Accessing the SharePoint Library via UNC Path

Since the SharePoint library is synced locally through OneDrive, it is exposed as part of the local file system and accessible via the redirected drive.

Steps

-
Open File Explorer in the remote session.

-
Click on the address bar.

-
Enter the UNC path below (replace {username} with your local Windows username):



\\tsclient\C\Users\{username}\{User's Ondrive Sync Name}\{Desired Folder}

-
Press Enter.

-
Verify that the SharePoint document library opens successfully.

Why This Works

-
OneDrive synchronizes the SharePoint document library to the local user profile.

-
The \\tsclient\C path exposes the local C: drive inside the remote session.

-
This allows applications running in the remote environment to write directly to the OneDrive-synced SharePoint location.

Exporting Data from Traverse to SharePoint

When exporting data from Traverse:

-
Initiate the export process in Traverse.

-
When prompted to select a destination drive, choose:

C (via Network)

-
Navigate through the folder structure to the same OneDrive-synced SharePoint location:



C:\Users\{username}\{User's Ondrive Sync Name}\{Desired Folder}

-
Complete the export and confirm the file is created in the SharePoint library.

Recommended Optimization

To simplify future exports:

-
Right-click the SharePoint folder once accessed.

-
Select Pin to Quick Access.

This reduces navigation time and minimizes the risk of selecting an incorrect path during exports.

Troubleshooting

-
If the path does not open:

-
Confirm OneDrive is running and fully synced.

-
Verify the SharePoint library appears locally under the OneDrive folder.

-
If the export fails:

-
Ensure C (via Network) is selected, not a server-local drive.

-
Confirm sufficient permissions on the SharePoint library.

654a8fce-c99e-419c-995b-ab2b9a184892.title: How to Run SQL query against for customer environment
654a8fce-c99e-419c-995b-ab2b9a184892.content:
Problem
Purpose

This article explains how to execute a provided .sql file against a specific database using SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS).

Resolution
Step 1: Launch SQL Server Management Studio

-
Open SQL Server Management Studio

-
Wait for the Connect to Server window to appear

Step 2: Connect to the SQL Server

-
In Server type, select Database Engine

-

dfdf7d1d-542f-4b2d-b3aa-3e4abad7dfd5.title: Traverse RemoteApp crashes ~30 seconds after login
dfdf7d1d-542f-4b2d-b3aa-3e4abad7dfd5.content:
Problem
Users are able to launch Traverse (RemoteApp) successfully through RDS.
However, the application closes or becomes unresponsive approximately 20–40 seconds after login.

Resolution
Symptoms Observed

-
User launches RemoteApp → Login screen appears → Login succeeds

-
After ~30 seconds:

-
Application closes automatically OR

-
Window freezes and disappears

-
Session remains active in RDS Server

-
Issue occurs only for specific users / workstations

Root Cause (Typical Behavior)

This behavior almost always indicates a user profile–level corruption or configuration failure, not a server performance issue.

Traverse loads user-specific settings immediately after authentication.
When Windows fails to read required user registry components, the application crashes.

The crash occurs when the app tries to load:

User Regional Settings
User Calendar Configuration
User Locale Formatting Data
.NET user profile components

If these registry keys are damaged, RemoteApp terminates silently.

How to Diagnose (Event Viewer Review)

Step 1 — Check Application Crash

On the RDS Session Host:

Event Viewer
→ Windows Logs
→ Application
→ Filter Current Log
→ Event Sources:
Application Error
.NET Runtime
SideBySide
Windows Error Reporting

Typical Crash Event

Event ID 1000 — Application Error

Look for:

Faulting application name: mstsc.exe
Faulting module name: KERNELBASE.dll / ntdll.dll / clr.dll
Exception code: 0xe0434352 OR 0xc000041d

This indicates a .NET exception triggered by invalid user configuration data.

Step 2 — Check User Profile / Locale Failure

Go to:

Event Viewer
→ Applications and Services Logs
→ Microsoft
→ Windows
→ Shell-Core
→ Operational

You will typically see errors related to:

Failed to read user international settings
Failed to load calendar configuration
Locale data invalid
Step 3 — Confirm Registry Corruption

Load the affected user hive:

reg load HKU\TempHive C:\Users\<username>\NTUSER.DAT

Check:

HKU\TempHive\Control Panel\International\Calendars

Corrupted profiles will either:

-
Not open

-
Throw access denied

-
Contain invalid values

Unload hive after checking:

reg unload HKU\TempHive
Resolution Performed

The crash was caused by corrupted user calendar regional settings.

Traverse crashes because .NET cannot parse invalid calendar values during session initialization.

Fix Applied

Removed the corrupted calendar configuration for the affected user profile.

Deleted registry key:

HKCU\Control Panel\International\Calendars

(Performed for affected users only)

User logged in again → Windows recreated clean defaults → Traverse launched successfully.

d64dbe5a-2a87-4801-b6f6-3154b28896d1.title: Setting Up New Financial Statements with Updated Bank and GL Accounts
d64dbe5a-2a87-4801-b6f6-3154b28896d1.content:
Problem
When a new company is created by duplicating an existing application, financial statements may need to be updated to reflect new banking accounts and General Ledger (GL) account numbers

Resolution
Overview
This article explains how to modify customized Financial Statements in the GL module when unwanted GL accounts appear in the Income Statement or Balance Sheet.
This scenario occurred when a customer created new Statement Content IDs but the system was pulling accounts based on Account Type ID, which resulted in additional, unnecessary GL accounts appearing in the reports.
The resolution involved updating the filter criteria to use direct GL Account filtering instead of Account Type filtering.
Issue Summary
When generating customized financial statements:
- Unwanted GL accounts appeared in the report.

- Filtering was based on Account Type ID, not specific GL Account numbers.

- The setup made it difficult to control exactly which accounts were included.

Statement IDs involved:
- Income Statement – ACC New

- Balance Sheet – ACC New B

Root Cause
The GL Statement Content was configured to pull accounts using:
Account Type ID = [Specific Type]
This caused the system to automatically include all accounts under that Account Type.
Instead, the customer needed the report to include only specific GL account numbers.
Resolution
Step 1: Access GL Statement Content
- Navigate to:
General Ledger > Statements > Financial Statements

- Open the relevant Statement ID.

- Double-click the Content ID to open the GL Statement Content screen.

Step 2: Update Filter Criteria
Instead of using:
Account Type ID = [Value]
Update the filter to:
Account ID  →  Is Any Of  →  [List Specific GL Accounts]
This allows you to:
- Explicitly control which GL accounts appear

- Remove unwanted accounts

- Prevent automatic pulling of all accounts under an Account Type

Income Statement Adjustments
Under ACC New, the following sections were modified:
Removed Accounts From:
- Salaries & Wages

- Insurance Expense

Only required GL accounts were retained using direct filtering.
Balance Sheet Adjustments
Under ACC New B, updates included:
Removed Accounts From:
- Cash

- Employee Receivables

- Notes Receivable

- Visa Payable

- Long-Term Liabilities

- Notes Payable

- Distribution Tier

Additional Changes:
- Entire unused sections (e.g., Long-Term Liabilities and Notes Payable) were deleted.

- Only active and required accounts were retained.

Validation
After making updates:
- Saved changes.

- Closed and reopened the Financial Statement.

- Refreshed and previewed the report.

- Verified that only required accounts appeared.

The customer confirmed that:
- Reports were displaying correctly.

- Unwanted accounts were removed.

- No additional changes were required.

When creating customized Financial Statements:
- Avoid using broad Account Type ID filters unless all accounts in that category are required.

- Use “Is Any Of” with specific GL Account numbers when precise control is needed.

- Refresh and preview the report after every modification.

- Remove unused sections entirely to keep reports clean and accurate.

a8dd9dba-2a36-4aa9-8253-2a6ff243b7da.title: How to Use the “Receive Finished Goods” Function in the Warehouse Mobile App
a8dd9dba-2a36-4aa9-8253-2a6ff243b7da.content:
Problem
How can I move assembled items from the production floor into inventory using the Warehouse Mobile app?

Resolution
The Receive Finished Goods function in the Warehouse Mobile app allows you to move assembled items from production into inventory. This function is equivalent to the Traverse WM Receive or MP Record Production Activity function.
Prerequisites
- A manufacturing Production Order for the assembly item must be set up and marked as In Process.

- The WM Receive function (desktop Traverse) will not confirm entries made using the Mobile WMS app; confirmation must be done from the Receiving Finished Goods function in the mobile app.

Steps to Receive Finished Goods
1. Enter Order Information
- Scan or enter the Production Order number and Release number in the Order/Release No field.

2. Use the List Tab
- The List tab shows details of the finished goods.

- Use the ellipsis (…) to expand item details.

- Use the X to collapse item details.


3. Use the Detail Tab
- The assembly ID is displayed (item ID is not shown).

- If the finished good is lotted, serialized, or both, the Lot/Serial Number Information section will expand automatically.
- Enter or scan Lot Number, Serial Number, Initial Date, and Expiration Date as applicable.

- Serialized assemblies require separate entries for each serial number with a Received Qty of one.

- Accept or enter the Bin Number:
- The item/location default bin will populate if available.

- If no default bin exists, the location default bin will be used.

- You may select a different bin from the drop‑down list.

- For two‑step receiving, select a receiving bin.

- For single‑step receiving, select the stocking bin directly.

- Enter or scan the Container, if applicable.
- If WM Containers Auto Create is set to Yes, use the Add button to create a new container.

- If set to No, the Add button will not display.

- If WM Use Containers is set to No, the field will not appear.

- Enter the Qty Received.
- The unit of measure for the assembly is displayed.

- If Default Quantity on Receiving WM is set to No, the default will be zero.

- Enter the No. of Labels to print.

- Repeat these steps for each finished good, especially for serialized items.

- View received items on the Received tab. Items are not added to inventory until confirmed.

4. Use the Received Tab
- The Received tab lists finished goods added to the receiving list.

- Use the ellipsis (…) to expand details.

- Items received in the current session show a Delete icon (to remove before confirmation).

- Receipt Number is auto‑generated in the format YearMonthDate

- The date will be the current workstation date.

-
For labels:
- Accept or edit the Label Qty.

- Use Select All or Deselect All for label printing.

- Change printers by expanding the Printer section and selecting from available server‑installed printers.

- Note: Redirected printers (via RDP) and virtual printers like Microsoft Print to PDF or Microsoft XPS Writer are not supported.

- Use the Printer icon to preview, print, or download labels.

5. Confirm Receipt
- Use the Confirm button to finalize the receipt.

- If Receive and Putaway Together is checked, items go directly into stock bins.

- If unchecked, items go into a receiving bin and must later be put away using the Put Away function.

6. Finish Receiving
- Use the Clear button to reset the screen.

- When finished, select Menu to return to the Receiving menu.

- Use the Put Away function to move finished goods into stock if not already put away.

Notes & Business Rules
- Default Bin on Receiving WM:
- If set to No, the default Bin Number will be blank.

- Receiving Process:
- Two‑step: Receive into a receiving bin, then put away into stock.

- Single‑step: Receive directly into stock bins.

- WM Containers Auto Create:
- If set to Yes, the Add button is available to create new containers.

- If set to No, the Add button will not display.

- WM Use Containers:
- If set to No, the Container field will not appear.

- Default Quantity on Receiving WM:
- If set to No, the default Qty Received will be zero.

- Printers:
- Only installed or virtual printers on the server hosting Mobile WMS are available.

- Redirected printers (via RDP) and Microsoft Print to PDF/XPS Writer are not supported.

- Receipt Number:
- Auto‑generated in <YearMonthDate> format using the current workstation date.

b3dfdf17-6ccf-42c6-802a-fe426d4326fe.title: How to Use the “Put Away” Function in the Warehouse Mobile App
b3dfdf17-6ccf-42c6-802a-fe426d4326fe.content:
Problem
How can I move received items into inventory using the Warehouse Mobile app?

Resolution
The Put Away function in the Warehouse Mobile app allows you to move received items into inventory. This function is equivalent to the WM Put Away function and similar to the Traverse WM Move Quantities function.
The key difference is:
- Move Quantities lets you move entire containers or individual items regardless of location.

- Put Away allows you to move any or all items located in a single bin.

Prerequisites
- Items must first be received.

- If the Receive and Putaway Together checkbox was left blank during receiving, items will be placed into receiving-type bins. The Put Away function is then required to move them into stock.

- The Put Away process uses the unit of measure (UOM) from the receipt as the default when putting items into stock.

Steps to Put Away Items
1. Select the Source Bin
- If a default bin is set for the IN location in SM User Defaults – Admin, it will appear in the From Bin field.

- Accept or select the bin from which you want to put items away.

- Only bins with items eligible for put away will be listed.

2. Use the Item List Tab
-
The Item List tab shows items in the selected bin that can be put away.

- Use the ellipsis (…) to expand the record.

- Tap an item record to move to the Item Detail tab.

3. Use the Item Detail Tab
-
Select or scan the Item ID of the item to put away.

- If the item is lotted or serialized, the lot/serial number fields will be visible.

- To see the source transaction type, open the drop‑down list in the Order No field.

- Accept or select the destination bin in the Bin To field:
- For purchase orders: the bin from the PO line item is used.

- For other transactions: the default bin for the item/location is used.

- If no default is set, the system uses the default bin (WM) for the IN location (from SM User Defaults – Admin).

- If that is not set, the default bin for the inventory location is used.

- You can override and select a different bin if necessary.

- If applicable, scan or select the source container in the Container field.

- If applicable, scan or select the destination container in the Container To field.

- Enter the Quantity of the item to put away.

- Accept or select the Unit of Measure (base UOM is displayed).

- Tab through until the Put Away List tab opens.

4. Use the Put Away List Tab
-
The Put Away List tab shows items being put away into inventory.

- Use the ellipsis (…) to expand details.

- Scroll horizontally or vertically if needed to view all columns.

- Use the Delete icon to remove items from the list.

- Tap Write to complete the put away process.

5. Finish Put Away
- After completing the process, the Item Detail tab clears all fields so you can proceed to the next item.

- Use the Clear button to reset the screen.

- When finished, select Menu to return to the Receiving menu.

Notes & Business Rules
- Receive and Putaway Together:
- If checked during receiving, items are put directly into stock bins.

- If unchecked, items are placed into receiving bins and must be put away.

- Eligibility for Put Away:
- Only items in receiving bins are eligible.

- If items are picked for issue/shipment before put away, and the remaining quantity is less than the received quantity, the item will no longer appear in the Put Away function.

- On-Hand Quantities:
- If the receiving bin type is not flagged for Quantity on Hold, items in receiving bins are included in on-hand quantities and can fulfill demand.

- Batch Process:
- Put Away is a batch process; multiple items from a receipt can be put into stock together.

- Unit of Measure:
- The UOM from the receipt is used as the default when putting items into stock.

2bbe312e-5842-4118-a9dd-ac85522ff796.title: Traverse Credit Card Processing – Expiration Dates Beyond 2029 Not Accepted
2bbe312e-5842-4118-a9dd-ac85522ff796.content:
Problem
Why does Traverse reject credit card expiration dates in 2030 or later when adding cards in the AR Customers Payments section?

Cause
When using the legacy CCP (Credit Card Processing) solution in Traverse, users may encounter an issue where credit cards with expiration dates in the year 2030 or beyond are flagged as expired. This happens because the system relies on the .NET framework’s handling of two‑digit years. By default, the framework interprets:
- 00–29 as 2000–2029

- 30–99 as 1930–1999

As a result, an expiration year of “30” is read as 1930, causing Traverse to reject the card as expired.

Resolution
To resolve this issue, the two‑digit year cutoff must be adjusted in Windows regional settings and via the registry.
Step 1: Adjust Regional Settings
- Open Control Panel.

- Navigate to Clock and Region > Region.

- Click Additional settings….

- Go to the Date tab.

- Locate the setting: “When a two‑digit year is entered, interpret it as a year between:”.

- Adjust the range (e.g., set it to 1950–2049).

- Save the change.

Step 2: Update Registry (if regional settings fail)
- Create a .reg file with the following content:

Code
Windows Registry Editor Version 5.00

[HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Control Panel\International\Calendars\TwoDigitYearMax]
"1"="2049"

- Import the file into the Windows Registry by double‑clicking it or right‑clicking and selecting Merge. (Running the file means importing it into the registry.)

- Confirm the prompt to add the information.

- Close and reopen Traverse. (Restart the server if a server restart is required.)

- Test with a card expiring in 2030.

Note:
- The “1” key corresponds to the Gregorian calendar.

- The cutoff year “2049” ensures expiration dates up to 2049 are accepted.

- The change must be applied on the server where Traverse is running. For on‑premises setups, apply it on the workstation first; if unsuccessful, apply it on the server.

Step 3: Apply Settings for All Users (if needed)
If the issue persists in environments with RDP or multiple users:
- Ensure changes are applied under the affected user’s profile, not just the admin account.

- To enforce system‑wide settings:
- In Region settings, go to the Administrative tab.

- Click Copy settings.

- Check both Welcome screen and system accounts and New user accounts.

- Alternatively, use Group Policy or registry scripts to enforce the cutoff year for all users.

This article explains the root cause (two‑digit year interpretation in .NET) and provides clear steps to adjust settings so Traverse can accept credit card expiration dates in 2030 or later.

32a133f2-4232-41fa-9983-aaec6dfde12c.title: How the “Received Order” Function Works in the Receiving Menu of Warehouse Mobile
32a133f2-4232-41fa-9983-aaec6dfde12c.content:
Problem
How does the Received Order function operate within the Receiving menu of Warehouse Mobile, including the workflow steps, system validations, and its impact on inventory quantities and order status updates? Clear understanding of this process is required to ensure accurate receiving and to prevent inventory discrepancies.

Resolution
Overview
- The Receiving Menu in the Warehouse Mobile application provides access to all receiving-related processes performed on the warehouse floor.

- It enables users to receive inventory directly against order transactions using mobile devices.

- Inventory quantities are updated in real time as each line item is scanned or entered, making the items immediately available for allocation or use.

- Non-stock inventory items are supported within the receiving function.

- When receiving non-stock items, the system automatically processes them as a “Receive and Put Away Together” transaction.

- The standalone Put Away function does not support non-stock items.

Receive Orders Function
- The Receive Orders function is used to receive items tied to various transaction types, including:
- Purchase Orders (New order type)

- Sales Order RMAs (Return Merchandise Authorizations)

- Project Costing (PC) material returns

- Service Director (SD) part returns

- Warehouse Management (WM) material requisition returns

- WM transfers to a location

- As each item is processed, the system updates on-hand quantities immediately.

- This function mirrors the functionality of the Traverse WM Receive process.

Selecting an Order
- Scan or manually select the Order Number in the Order No field.

- Only open and partially received orders will appear; fully received orders are excluded.

- Upon selecting the order, the system automatically opens the List tab.

- The Filter Orders panel can be used to refine the list of open orders:
- Expand or collapse the filter panel using the arrow control.

- Choose a filter option from the Filter By dropdown list.


- Enter or select the appropriate value in the Filter Value field.

- After exiting the field, the Order No dropdown will display only orders matching the selected filter criteria.



Order Tab (Optional Header Information)
- Navigate to the Order tab if additional header information needs to be entered.

- Enter Shipper No. if applicable.

- Enter Notes as needed.

- This information updates the corresponding PO Receipt once the receipt is confirmed.

- The Clear button resets line-level data; selecting it again clears header-level information.



Receiving Items from the List Tab
- Use the Receive All button to process all line items on the order simultaneously.

- Alternatively, select individual line items to process them one at a time.


- Selecting a line item opens the Detail tab for entry.

Detail Tab – Line-Level Entry
- If the item is lotted, serialized, or both, the Lot/Serial Number Information section expands automatically.

- Required information may include:
- Lot Number

- Serial Number

- Expiration Date (if applicable)

- Initial Date (if required by configuration)

- For serialized assemblies:
- Each serial number must be entered separately.

- The received quantity must be one per serial number entry.

Data Validation Logic
- The system validates data in a specific sequence based on the Use Container parameter setting.

- If Use Container is set to Yes, validation occurs in the following order:
- Container

- Bin Number

- Lot Number

- Expiration Date

- Serial Number

- If Use Container is set to No, validation occurs in the following order:
- Bin Number

- Lot Number

- Expiration Date

- Serial Number

Container Handling
- If containers are enabled, scan or manually enter the Container ID.

- If the WM Containers Auto Create business rule is set to Yes:
- The Add button allows users to create a new container during receiving.

- If the rule is set to No:
- The Add button will not be available.

- If WM Use Containers is set to No:
- The Container field will not appear on the screen.

Bin Number Assignment
- For Purchase Orders:
- The bin defined on the PO line defaults into the Bin Number field.

- For other transaction types:
- The system defaults to the item/location bin if available.

- If not available, the location’s default bin is used.

- In a two-step receiving process:
- Select or accept a receiving bin.

- Items will later be moved to stocking bins using Put Away.

- In a single-step receiving process:
- Select the final stocking bin directly during receiving.

- If the Default Bin on Receiving WM business rule is set to No:
- The Bin Number field will remain blank and require manual selection.

Quantity Entry and Label Printing
- The Unit of Measure displays automatically based on item setup.

- Enter the quantity being received in the Qty Received field.

- If Default Quantity on Receiving WM is set to No:
- The Qty Received field defaults to zero.

- Enter the number of labels to print in the No. of Labels field.

- Select a Printer Name from the dropdown list.

- Only printers installed on the server hosting Mobile WMS are available.

- Redirected printers via Remote Desktop (RDP) and virtual printers such as Microsoft Print to PDF or Microsoft XPS Writer are not supported.


Received Tab
- The Received tab displays all items entered during the current receiving session.

- Items not yet confirmed display a Delete icon.

- The Receipt Number is automatically generated in YearMonthDate format.

- The receipt date reflects the current workstation date.

- Expand individual lines to review detailed information.

- Items cannot be deleted once confirmed.




Label Printing from the Received Tab
- Adjust the Label Qty field if changes are needed.

- Use Select All to mark all labels for printing.

- Use Deselect All to clear all selections.

- The default printer is used unless changed.

- Expand the Printer section to select a different printer if necessary.

- Use the Printer icon to preview, print, or download labels.

Confirming the Receipt
- Select Confirm to finalize the receipt.

- A green confirmation message appears at the top of the screen once completed.

- Shipment No is recorded and available in the Activity Log report for reference.

- Items are not officially received into inventory until confirmation is completed.

Receive and Put Away Together Option
- If the Receive and Put Away Together checkbox is selected:
- Items are placed directly into the specified stocking bins.

- If the checkbox is not selected:
- Items are placed into a receiving bin.

- The Put Away function must later be used to move items to stocking bins.

7c583339-3ae9-40b8-a755-fedf56e3d49b.title: Understanding Date Parameters in Traverse Reports (PO & AP) and Why YTD Totals Differ
7c583339-3ae9-40b8-a755-fedf56e3d49b.content:
Problem
Customers often report discrepancies in Year-to-Date (YTD) totals when running Purchase Order (PO) and Accounts Payable (AP) reports in Traverse using different date parameters such as Transaction Date, Document Date, Invoice Date, Payment Date, or Fiscal Period.
Even when the same date range is applied, totals may vary significantly across reports. This leads to confusion about which date parameter should be used for accurate reporting—especially when comparing Traverse data with manufacturer-provided sales totals based on order entry date.

Cause
Cause
Traverse tracks different stages of the purchasing and accounting lifecycle separately. Each stage is recorded using a different date field, and reports are designed to reflect specific business events rather than a single unified timeline.
Because of this design, the same purchase order can appear in different reports and reporting periods depending on the date parameter selected.

Resolution
Resolution
Understanding Date Parameters in Traverse
Each date parameter represents a distinct business event:
- Transaction Date (PO – Transaction Type = New Order) Represents the date the purchase order is originally created. This reflects order booking activity and aligns most closely with manufacturer “order entry date” totals.

- Document Date (PO Receipt / PO Invoice) Represents the date goods are received or the document is processed. This reflects operational activity, not order creation.

- AP Invoice Date Represents the date the vendor invoice is entered and the expense is recognized. This reflects accounting recognition timing.

- AP Payment Date Represents the date payment is issued to the vendor. This reflects cash disbursement timing.

- Fiscal Period Represents the accounting period in which transactions are posted for financial reporting.

Why YTD Totals Differ
A single purchase order progresses through multiple stages:
- Order creation

- Goods receipt

- Invoice posting

- Payment issuance

Each stage occurs on a different date and is reported separately. As a result, totals will naturally vary across reports even when the same calendar date range is used. This behavior is expected and by design.
Recommended Reporting Guidelines
Use the following approach based on reporting needs:
- For manufacturer comparisons based on order entry timing: PO Order View
- Transaction Type = New Order

- Filter by Transaction Date

- For expense recognition reporting: AP reports filtered by Invoice Date

- For cash activity reporting: AP reports filtered by Payment Date

- For financial statements and accounting periods: Reports filtered by Fiscal Period

Filtering PO Order View by Transaction Type = New Order is critical, as the view otherwise includes multiple entries per PO (New Order, Receipt, Invoice), which can inflate totals.

3230d38a-b34d-4519-a780-5e49ff61948b.title: How to configure folder preview pane feature no longer working for files on DocUnity network path.
3230d38a-b34d-4519-a780-5e49ff61948b.content:
Problem
When opening the file explorer, Windows has a feature called "Preview Pane" that you can use under the "View" option to easily preview PDFs that are being reviewed. The problem is that you may lose this feature when reviewing a folder from a network drive location shown in the 2nd image. When you click the "Preview" button, you will see a message that there is no image to display, as it is blocked.

Cause

1eab06ee-ca7a-4fc8-9ee8-7980cacea9c1.title: How to Email Monthly Customer Statements in Traverse When AR Is Imported from an External System
1eab06ee-ca7a-4fc8-9ee8-7980cacea9c1.content:
Problem
If a customer uses a separate system to generate invoices and then imports Accounts Receivable data into Traverse for AR management, can they email monthly customer statements directly from Traverse instead of printing and mailing them?
If so:
- What setup or configuration is required?

- Are there any limitations when invoices are imported from an external system?

- What steps are needed to enable emailing statements to customers?

Resolution
To set up emailing monthly Accounts Receivable statements from Traverse, you will need to configure both SMTP Settings and Document Settings within the System Manager. This allows you to define the email addresses used and how specific documents, like AR statements, are sent.
1. Configure SMTP Settings (System Manager > Document Delivery > SMTP Settings):
- Click the New button to create a new record.

- Select Microsoft for Microsoft Mail service or SMTP for basic authentication from the Mail Type drop-down menu.

- Enter an SMTP Name. This will be your reference when configuring document settings.

- Provide your SMTP Server name (e.g., smtp.live.com, smtp.gmail.com).

- Enter the SMTP Port (common ports are 25, 465, 587). Consult your system administrator if unsure.

- Mark the Enable SSL checkbox if your email server uses SSL.

- Enter the User Name and Password for the email account used to send mail.

- If SSL is enabled, enter the path to the SSL Certificate.

- Enter the Sender's Name and Sender's Email address.

- Optionally, enter a Reply To email address.

- Click the Save button.


2. Configure Document Settings (System Manager > Document Delivery > Document Settings):
- Click the New button to create a blank document setting record.

- Select the appropriate document type for AR statements from the Form ID drop-down list.

- To automate sending, mark the Auto Send check box. If you want to review statements before sending, clear this box; they will go to a document queue.

- Enter a Subject for the email. You can drag dynamic fields from the Fields tab into this field.

- Select the SMTP ID you configured in the previous step from the drop-down list. This links the document to the specific email address.

- If you want the email formatted as HTML, mark the Send as HTML check box. Otherwise, it will be plain text.

- In the Body section, create the email content. You can add static text and dynamic fields from the Fields tab.

- Define the file name for the document in the Document Name field.


- If applicable, add static attachments using the Append button.

- Click the Save button to save your changes.

After these configurations, you can find pending AR statements under Manage Queue if auto-send is not enabled. You can also set up an automatic monthly statement.

2df5350c-a2e6-41f0-8bb8-e0e8bd77d58e.title: How to perform 'AP Transactions' Import in Traverse?
2df5350c-a2e6-41f0-8bb8-e0e8bd77d58e.content:
Problem
How to perform AP Import in Traverse?

Resolution
The overview of the Import function can be found in the article: https://connect.aptean.com/s/article/How-does-Import-function-works-in-Traverse



The 'AP Import' is a 3-step process that comprises of the following:

I. Set up the SM Import Layout Definition:

- Go to the SM Import Layout definition under the path: Applications -> System Manager -> Company Setup -> Import Layout Definition
- Click on 'New' icon at the top to create a new Layout ID
- Layout ID: Enter the Layout ID as preferred
- Description: Enter the Description for the layout.
- File Type: Select a File Type that describes the plain-text source file. [The most common file type is ‘Delimited’].
- Number of rows: Enter the Number of rows the system should skip before importing the data. [Usually, we will have a title row for the columns, so we would enter ‘1’ to skip the first row].
- Field separator: Select the Field separator used in the source file to separate the fields. A Comma is the most common separator.
- Row separator: Select the Row separator used in the source file. The most common separator is the ‘CRLF' (carriage return line feed)
- Text qualifier: Select the Text qualifier that is used when a field separator occurs within a field. If there are no such entries, enter 'NONE'
- Filename: We can either enter the path and filename where the source file is located or browse to the source file under the 'Filename'. This enables us to use the 'Get Fields' function, which directs the system to read the column names from the source file and fill in the detail grid.
- Get Fields: The Get Fields function will only work if the first row of the source file contains column headings. If we do not have a path and filename selected, enter the column names from the source file into the detail grid with a data Type of ‘RawText’
- All the fields, including numeric or date fields, will be imported as a data type of ‘RawText’, and this needs to be later converted to the desired data type with the help of functions.
- ​​​​​​​Once everything is set up as desired, click on 'Save' at the top to save the Layout:



II. Set up the SM Import Map Definition:

- Go to the SM Import Map Definition under the path: Applications -> System Manager -> Company Setup -> Import Map Definition
- Click on the New icon to create a new Import Map ID
- Function ID: Select a Function ID for the map definition. In this case it will be 'Default'
- Description: Enter the Description for the Map ID.
- Assembly: Browse the assembly as TRAVERSE.Import.APTransaction
- Class ID: Use the Class ID as TRAVERSE.Business.AccountsPayable.TransactionImport for AP Transactions Import
- Expand the properties grid of the schema by clicking on the plus sign. Set up the necessary mappings for the AP import.
- Once everything is set up as desired, click on 'Save' at the top to save the Map ID.



III. Import the data into Traverse through SM Mapped data:

- Go to SM Import Mapped Data under the path: Applications -> System Manager -> Company Setup -> Import Mapped Data
- Map ID: Select the Map ID that was set under Import Map Definition.
- File Name: Choose the CSV file containing the AP Transactions. [It may appear by default, if it was already set up in the SM Import Layout Definition]
- Click on the "Read Data" button to Read the data from the File.



- Once the data was read successfully, click on 'Verify Data' button to check the data for errors. If the data has errors, those records will be flagged. If there are no errors, it will appear as follows, and then we can click on 'Import Data' to import the data into the AP Transactions screen.​​​​​​​



Now we can observe the transactions being imported into the AP Transactions screen under the path: Applications -> Accounts Payable -> Transactions -> Transactions:

9e13d8f6-10bc-4bee-a18e-b8e2d1b0d022.title: 'AR Customers' Screen Not Displaying All Customer Records by Default
9e13d8f6-10bc-4bee-a18e-b8e2d1b0d022.content:
Problem
The customer has a large number of AR Customer records in Traverse. However, when accessing the Customer Maintenance (Customers) screen (Accounts Receivable -> Setup and Maintenance -> Customers), Traverse displays “1 of 1” instead of the expected “1 of XX” (where XX is the total number of customer records). Additionally, the first customer record is not automatically displayed, which is different from the usual behavior where the first Customer ID is loaded by default.
This behavior causes confusion for users, as it appears that only one customer record exists, even though multiple customer records are present in the system.


However, when the user hits on the 'Lookups', the records are still intact.

Resolution
The issue is related to a Business Rule configuration in System Manager that controls whether all customers are loaded automatically when entering the Customer Maintenance screen.

Root Cause:
In Traverse, the behavior of the Customer Maintenance screen is controlled by the following Business Rule setting:
Path: System Manager -> Company Setup -> Business Rules : AR – Accounts Receivable -> 'Customer' Section
Setting:
Load All Customers in Setup:
- Yes: All customer records are loaded when entering the Customer Maintenance screen. The screen displays 1 of XX, and the first customer record is shown by default.
- No: Customers are not preloaded. The screen may display 1 of 1, and users must manually search or look up customer records.

In this case, the Load All Customers in Setup option was set to No, which prevented Traverse from loading the full customer list and caused the record counter to show only a single record.


Resolution
Step 1: Update the Business Rule Setting
- Navigate to: System Manager → Company Setup → Business Rules
- Expand AR – Accounts Receivable.
- Locate the Customer section.
- Find the setting Load All Customers in Setup.
- Change the value to Yes.
- Click on 'Apply' and 'OK' to Save the Business Rules configuration.


Result:
- After making the change to the above mentioned business rule, the next time accessing the Accounts Receivable -> Setup and Maintenance -> Customers screen, the actual number of Customer ID records appeared and the first Customer ID information loaded in the screen by default.

17264011-9b2e-473e-aeca-952231405502.title: How to create Rea-Only SQL account
17264011-9b2e-473e-aeca-952231405502.content:
Problem
This article explains how to create a read-only SQL login using SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS).
The account will be able to connect and read data but cannot insert, update, delete, or modify schema.

Resolution
Step 1: Create a SQL Login (Server Level)

-
Open SSMS

-
Connect to the target SQL Server

-
Expand Security → Logins

-
Right-click Logins → New Login…

Fill in:

-
Login name: readonly_user

-
Authentication: SQL Server authentication

-
Set a strong password

-
Uncheck Enforce password expiration (recommended for service/reporting accounts)

Click OK

Step 2: Map Login to Database

-
Right-click the new login → Properties

-
Go to User Mapping

-
Check the target database

-
Set Default Schema = dbo

Step 3: Assign Read-Only Permissions

Under Database role membership, select:

-
✅ db_datareader

Ensure NONE of the following are selected:

-
❌ db_datawriter

-
❌ db_owner

-
❌ db_ddladmin

Click OK

✅ This guarantees SELECT-only access.

Step 4: Validate Permissions

Test with SQL Login

-
Disconnect from SSMS

-
Reconnect using the readonly_user

-
Run:

SELECT TOP 10 * FROM dbo.YourTable;

950e052b-6649-42f3-a5b8-d15b715309ee.title: IN Items "Order Qty UOM is required" Error message is received when attempting to save a newly created Item.
950e052b-6649-42f3-a5b8-d15b715309ee.content:
Problem
The user is unable to save a newly created Inventory Item. Upon attempting to save, the system consistently displays the error message “Order Qty UOM is required,” preventing the Item from being saved.

Resolution
The issue was resolved by ensuring that the Unit of Measure (UOM) was correctly set at the location level for each location associated with the item. When an item is linked to multiple locations, the UOM must be specified for each location in the Location Defaults section.
Step-by-Step Instructions
- Navigate to the item creation screen: Applications → Inventory → Setup and Maintenance → Items
- Navigate to the Location tab.
- In the Loc Defaults section, verify that the UOM field has a UOM selected for each location assigned to the Item (Location field).
- Save the item.
Root Cause
In this case, the item was assigned to multiple locations, and the Loc Defaults - UOM field was not populated for one of the locations. This caused the system to display the error message “Order Qty UOM is required” when attempting to save the item.

Once the UOM was populated for all locations, the item saved successfully without any issues.
Important Notes
- The Loc Defaults - UOM field must be set for every location assigned to an item.
- If the UOM field is left blank at the location level, the system will prevent the item from being saved.

cdb3658b-bc9d-43d2-89b1-b08b7c645f7b.title: Bank Reconciliation Variance Due to Transactions Cleared in Incorrect Statement
cdb3658b-bc9d-43d2-89b1-b08b7c645f7b.content:
Problem
A user was unable to locate a prepayment in the current statement but the system indicated it was already cleared.

Resolution
Issue Description
During bank reconciliation, users may notice an unexplained variance where the cleared balance does not match the expected outstanding amount. In some cases, a transaction posted in a later fiscal year (e.g., 2025) appears to be missing from the current bank reconciliation and does not show as outstanding.
Root Cause
This issue occurs when a transaction is cleared against an incorrect bank statement, typically from a prior fiscal year that is still in an Open status. Even if the transaction was posted in the correct fiscal year, it can still be cleared on an older statement if that statement is not marked as Reconciled. Once cleared, the transaction no longer appears in future bank reconciliations, causing reconciliation differences.
How to Identify the Issue
- Run the Bank Reconciliation and note the variance amount.

- Review the Bank Register and confirm whether the transaction exists but is not available for clearing.

- Navigate to Bank Reconciliation → Clear Transactions.

- Use the Statement Date lookup to review prior-period statements (for example, December 2024).

- Check if the transaction is marked as Cleared under an incorrect statement.

Resolution Steps
- Go to Bank Reconciliation → Clear Transactions.

- Select the Bank Account ID.

- Use the Statement Date lookup and choose the incorrect prior-period statement.

- Navigate to the appropriate tab (Disbursements or Deposits).

- Uncheck the Cleared checkbox for the affected transaction and click OK.

- Re-run the bank reconciliation to confirm the variance is resolved.

- The transaction will now appear as Outstanding and can be cleared in the correct period.

Preventive steps
After completing a bank reconciliation for a period:
- Open Clear Transactions.

- Select the completed bank statement.

- Click Change Status and mark the statement as Reconciled.

Marking a statement as Reconciled prevents users from unintentionally clearing transactions in prior periods while still allowing the statement to be reopened if necessary.

5878261b-6516-4767-82ae-544e348ce451.title: How to use the Move Menu functionality in WM Mobile?
5878261b-6516-4767-82ae-544e348ce451.content:
Problem
How to use the Lookup Menu feature in WM Mobile?

Resolution
Overview
The Move function in the WM Mobile application allows you to move inventory within the warehouse. This helps track where items are stored and keeps inventory accurate.
The Move menu includes two options:
Internal Move – Move inventory within the same inventory location
(for example, bin to bin or bin/container to another bin/container)
Quick Transfer – Transfer inventory to another location within the same warehouse or campus
Internal Move
The Internal Move function is used to move items within the same inventory location.
This is comparable to the Traverse WM Move Quantities function.
If you need to move inventory between different inventory locations or warehouses, use the Location Transfers function instead.
Warehouse Management helps track item movement by temporarily placing items in a working bin before dropping them into their final destination.
Note: The Lot Number Behavior business rule controls whether the lot number can be changed during a move.
Pick Tab – Picking Items to Move
Use the Pick tab to select items and move them into a temporary (working) bin.
To pick an item:
Open the Move screen and select the Pick tab.
Scan or enter the Item ID.
Scan or enter the Container you are moving from, if applicable.
This field may not appear depending on configuration.
Scan or enter the Lot Number, if applicable.
Scan or enter the source Bin Number.
Once the bin (and container, if applicable) is entered, the quantity to move is temporarily placed into the default bin for the IN location, as defined in Location Maintenance.
Scan or enter the Serial Number, if applicable.
Serialized items must be entered one at a time with a Qty to Move of 1.
Enter the Qty to Move.
Accept or select the Unit of Measure.
Tab through the screen to complete the pick.
The selected quantity is moved to your working bin (or the IN location’s default bin if no working bin is assigned).
Repeat these steps for each item you want to move.
Additional options:
Select Clear to reset the fields.
Select Menu to return to the menu.
Drop Tab – Dropping Items into the Destination Bin
Use the Drop tab to move items from your temporary (working) bin into a final bin.
To drop items:
Select the Drop tab.
Scan or enter the destination To Bin.
Scan or enter the Container, if applicable.
If WM Containers Auto Create is set to Yes, you can use Add to create a new container.
If set to No, the Add button will not appear.
If WM Use Containers is set to No, the container field will not appear.
A list of items in your working bin will display.
Use the ellipsis (…) to view item details.
Select the check box for each item you want to move.
Use Select All or Unselect All as needed.
Update the Qty Received, if required.
Tap Drop to complete the move.
Additional options:
Select Clear to reset the fields.
Select Menu to return to the menu.



Quick Transfer
The Quick Transfer function is used to move inventory from one inventory location to another within the same warehouse or campus.
This function is comparable to the Traverse WM Quick Location Transfers function.
If inventory must be transferred between geographically separate locations where transit time is involved, use the Location Transfers function instead.
To transfer an item:
Scan or enter the Item ID.
Scan or enter the destination Location ID To.
Scan or enter the destination To Container, if applicable.
If WM Containers Auto Create is set to Yes, you may use Add to create a container.
If WM Use Containers is set to No, the container field will not appear.
Scan or enter the Lot Number, if applicable.
Scan or enter the source Bin Number.
Scan or enter the destination To Bin.
Scan or enter the Serial Number, if applicable.
Serialized items must be transferred one at a time with a Qty to Transfer of 1.
Enter the Qty to Transfer.
Accept or select the Unit of Measure.
Tab through the screen to complete the transfer.
The item quantity is transferred directly to the destination bin.
Repeat these steps for each item you want to transfer.
Validation Notes
Data validation is applied during Quick Transfer. The validation order depends on the Use Container setting:
Use Container = Yes
Validation order:
Item ID → Location To → Qty → Container → Bin Number → To Bin → To Container → Lot/Serial Number
Use Container = No
Validation order:
Item ID → Location To → Qty → Container → Bin Number → To Bin → Lot/Serial Number
Additional options:
Select Clear to reset all fields.
Select Menu to return to the menu.

d7c59f14-b717-4f50-b454-1ceb8a9d1a04.title: How does the Labels Menu function work in WM Mobile?

Additional options:
