d614a228-a7e0-4d8a-aef5-0c7c8e9a4d11.title: CR-95609 – Traverse Crash Opening Summary History View via Remote Desktop
d614a228-a7e0-4d8a-aef5-0c7c8e9a4d11.content:
Problem
An issue was identified where Traverse Global would crash when users attempted to open certain history inquiry screens while connected through a Remote Desktop / Terminal Server environment.
The problem has been resolved in a later build (see Resolution / Fixed Build below).

Resolution
Affected Areas
The crash could occur when opening the following screens:
- AR Summary History View

- AP Summary History View

- IN Summary History View

- GL Account Balance View


Symptoms
When navigating to the Summary History View, Traverse closes unexpectedly with the Windows error:

Traverse Global has stopped working – A problem caused the program to stop working correctly. Windows will close the program and notify you if a solution is available.

The entire application terminates immediately.

When It Occurs
The issue occurs specifically when users access Traverse through:
Remote Desktop / Terminal Server / Virtual Machine (RDP session)
The same screen works correctly when:
- Accessed directly on the database server

- Accessed on a local workstation

- Accessed in non-RDP environments


Steps to Reproduce
- Log into Traverse via Remote Desktop (RDS / VM)

- Navigate to Accounts Receivable → Interactive View → Summary History View

- The application crashes immediately


Root Cause
The issue was caused by a rendering incompatibility in Remote Desktop sessions.
Traverse uses chart and graphical rendering components that rely on hardware-accelerated graphics. Remote Desktop environments do not fully support this rendering method, which caused the application to terminate when loading summary history visual components.

Impact
- Users working in terminal server environments cannot access summary history screens

- The entire application closes

- Prevents AR inquiry and reconciliation work


Resolution
The application was updated to prevent the graphics rendering crash when running in Remote Desktop environments.
The User was able to access the AR Summary History View, after disabling the Hardware Acceleration.

Fixed Build
Resolved in Build: 25143 (SP3 Release – May 23)
Customers experiencing this issue should upgrade to this build or newer.

b7817399-8b8f-4333-a3fa-f9f3abe2d4ee.title: Production Order Shows “Quantity must be greater than 0” and Lot Number Cannot Be Entered
b7817399-8b8f-4333-a3fa-f9f3abe2d4ee.content:
Problem
While recording production in Traverse Global, the user receives the error

"Quantity must be greater than 0"

Even after entering a quantity (example: 1), the system does not accept it. The user also cannot enter a lot number in the Record Production Activity screen.

Resolution
Environment
- Product: Traverse Global

- Module: Manufacturing / Production Order

- Screen: Record Production Activity

- Common Scenario: Order marked Completed but not yet posted

- Possible Add-On: Warehouse Management (WM)



The production order appears finished, but:
- Quantity cannot be entered

- Lot number field is unavailable

- The system continues to show the “Quantity must be greater than 0” error

This prevents the produced assembly from being added to inventory.


The Production Order has already reached the Completed status.
Even if it has not been posted yet, Traverse treats the order as locked for production entry. At this stage, the system expects that all production quantities and lot tracking were already recorded earlier.
Because of this:
- The system will not accept new produced quantities

- The lot number cannot be assigned

- The screen behaves as read-only for production values

This protects costing, inventory, and WIP accounting integrity.
Uploading image...

How to Confirm
Open the Record Production Activity screen and check the order status.
If the status shows Completed, the system will no longer allow quantity or lot entry.
Resolution (Recommended Approach)
You should not reopen or modify the completed production order.
Instead, correct the inventory using an adjustment.
This keeps the accounting history accurate and prevents costing issues.


Correcting the Inventory Quantity
For Standard Inventory
- Go to Inventory → Transaction→ Inventory transaction

- Select a batch code

- Choose the correct adjustment type (Increase or Decrease)

- Enter:
- Item ID (finished assembly)

- Location

- Lot number (create if needed)

- Enter the quantity to correct inventory

- Save and Post the adjustment

Print the Journal:
For Warehouse Management (WM) Users
If Warehouse Management is installed, the adjustment must be performed inside WM instead of standard Inventory Adjustment using
The adjustment will:
- Add the produced quantity to on-hand inventory

- Allow lot number assignment

- Keep manufacturing history unchanged

92278aba-db49-44ea-a1ad-975c6cdd4df4.title: Alerts Not Triggering – Creating a Custom “Birthdays Today” Alert in Traverse
92278aba-db49-44ea-a1ad-975c6cdd4df4.content:
Problem
Users have existing Aptean / Traverse Alerts (Actions) configured, but they are not running or sending notifications as expected.
The goal is to set up a working alert that emails a list of employees whose birthday is today.

Resolution
Most alerts fail for one of these reasons:
- The Action is not scheduled

- The SMTP profile is not configured

- The Action output has no data

- The Action service is not running

- The wrong fields or filters were selected

It is recommended to create a simple alert first (like Birthday Today) to confirm the alert system is functioning.

Creating a “Birthdays Today” Alert
Step 1 — Create the Action
- Go to System Manager → Actions → Actions

- Click New

- Name the action: "Birthday Today"


Step 2 — Configure the Output
Open the Output tab and select only the fields needed:
- Employee ID

- Employee Name

- Birth Date

Step 3 — Configure Email Notification
Open the Email tab.
- Add recipients under Send To

- Enable:
- Send Email

- Attach Output File (optional – sends a report attachment)

- Select the correct SMTP ID

- Enter subject and body text

Confirming if the alert works fine by setting up a employee ID with the birth date as of today, the alert seems to be triggering properly now,

You should also verify if you have setup the alert "Birthday Today" in the traverse design studio by navigating to Designers >Actions Designers,
You should be clicking on the "Data Source" tab and set the below query such that this alert works,

b8da5e96-4663-46ea-9e32-2a327295fdb2.title: AR Detail History View – “Qty Ship Sell” Total Not Displaying When Grouped by Invoice
b8da5e96-4663-46ea-9e32-2a327295fdb2.content:
Problem
Users reviewing invoices in AR Detail History View are unable to see the total value of Qty Ship Sell when grouping records by Invoice Number.
Instead of seeing a summed total, they must expand each transaction line individually to view quantities.
This makes reviewing invoice quantities slow and inconvenient, especially during reconciliation.

Resolution
Environment
- Product: Traverse Global

- Build: 24327

- Module: Accounts Receivable → Detail History View


After grouping records by Invoice Number, the expected totals row does not appear.
Users only see individual lines:
No summarized quantity → Must expand each invoice → Manual checking required


- Log into Traverse Global

- Navigate to Accounts Receivable

- Open Detail History View

- Group data by Invoice Number

- Look for the total of Qty Ship Sell

Result
The total is not displayed unless each record is expanded.
The issue is not caused by data, permissions, or a system defect.
The grid layout (view configuration) lost its Totals Bar setting.
Traverse stores grid display preferences inside the user layout. If the layout becomes altered or corrupted, summary totals will stop appearing even though the data is correct.
The totals row is simply hidden in the saved layout.

Reset the grid layout to restore the totals row.

- Open AR Detail History View

- Click the Reset Layout button on the toolbar

- Reopen the screen

The totals will appear again automatically.

2d038774-f6ce-4b21-81d7-10c4c31cd54d.title: Traverse Payment Integration – Unable to connect to the remote server (TRAVERSE.Integration.TPS)
2d038774-f6ce-4b21-81d7-10c4c31cd54d.content:
Problem
When users attempt to process a credit card payment in Traverse using the External Payment option, the payment fails immediately with the message:

Unable to connect to the remote server (TRAVERSE.Integration.TPS)

The credit card device (Ingenico Lane 3000) is connected via USB and is visible to Windows, but Traverse is unable to communicate with it.
Because of this, store staff cannot swipe cards and must manually enter card numbers, slowing down checkout operations.

Resolution
- Product: Traverse Global

- Version: 11.2 (Build 23349)

- Device: Ingenico Lane 3000 (USB EMV/Pin Pad)

- Payment Provider: OEExpress / OEExpress_SCE

- Occurs on: Newly installed workstations


Steps to Reproduce :
- Connect the Ingenico Lane 3000 to the workstation

- Open Traverse

- Go to Sales Order

- Click External Payment

- Attempt to swipe a credit card

- Error appears immediately


Cause
The card reader does not communicate directly with Traverse.
It requires a middleware application called RCM (Remote Client Manager) to act as the communication bridge between:
Traverse → Payment Service → Card Reader
On new machines, the RCM software is typically not installed or not configured. When Traverse attempts to send a payment request, no service is listening — resulting in the remote server connection error.
This is why the device appears functional in Windows but fails inside Traverse.


Please find the resolution steps below,
Install and configure the RCM software on each workstation using a card reader.
Step 1 — Install RCM
Install the OpenEdge RCM application on the workstation:
RCM_Windows_GA.exe
The RCM program has a Device Configure option that will allow you to change the communication port that the device uses if necessary, such as COM4 or COM6.
This is required for all EMV / pin pad devices.

Step 2 — Configure the Device
- Launch RCM

- Open Device Configure

- Select the Ingenico device

- Assign the correct COM port (example: COM4 or COM6)

- Save the configuration



Step 3 — Verify Traverse Settings
Confirm the payment configuration matches the environment:
- Payment Provider = OEExpress_SCE

- SM Defaults configured correctly

- Payment Service Integration setup completed

- AR Payment Methods linked properly

Step 4 — Restart and Test
- Close Traverse

- Restart RCM

- Reopen Traverse

- Retry External Payment

The device should now activate and process the transaction.

b251e1a6-3307-44b1-8841-1354a9f23c4b.title: How to Change GL Account IDs in Traverse
b251e1a6-3307-44b1-8841-1354a9f23c4b.content:
Problem
This article provides instructions on how to modify existing General Ledger (GL) account IDs in Traverse, specifically when a segment of the account number needs to be corrected while retaining associated budgets and activity

Resolution
How to Change a GL Account ID in Traverse
This article explains how to update an existing GL Account ID in Traverse using the Change IDs function.
Overview
The Change IDs function allows you to rename an existing GL Account ID across the system. This update applies to all records, including historical transactions.
⚠️ Important: This process does not merge accounts or move data into an already existing GL Account ID.
Steps to Change a GL Account ID
Step 1: Navigate to Change IDs
Go to: System Manager → Setup and Maintenance → Change IDs
How to Change a GL Account ID in Traverse
This article explains how to update an existing GL Account ID in Traverse using the Change IDs function.
Overview
The Change IDs function allows you to rename an existing GL Account ID across the system. This update applies to all records, including historical transactions.
Steps to Change a GL Account ID
Step 1: Navigate to Change IDs
Go to:
System Manager → Setup and Maintenance → Change IDs
Step 2: Select ID Type
- In the ID Type drop-down, select GL Account ID.

Step 3: Select Existing GL Account ID
- In the From column, select the existing GL Account ID that you want to change.

Step 4: Enter New GL Account ID
- In the To column, enter the new GL Account ID.

- Ensure the new ID does not already exist in the system.

Step 5: Proceed with the Change
- Click OK to continue.

You will see the message:
“All users must be out of the current company before performing this process.”
- Ensure that no users are logged into Traverse.

- Click OK again.

Step 6: Confirm the Action
When prompted with:
“Do you wish to continue?”
- Select Yes.

Step 7: Completion Message
If the process is successful, you will see the message:
“Change ID function completed successfully.”
Important Notes
- This process updates the GL Account ID across all current and historical records.

- This function cannot be used to:
- Merge two existing GL Account IDs

- Transfer data into an already existing GL Account ID

- If the process fails, you may see the message:
“All changes were not successful. Please check the list for failed.”

This usually indicates that:
- The new GL Account ID already exists, or

- One or more users were still logged into Traverse during the process

0bebba71-9603-4512-8621-13b3bfd71863.title: How to Update Traverse Standard Help Content to Online Version
0bebba71-9603-4512-8621-13b3bfd71863.content:
Problem
Customers using Traverse Standard may find that the local help content is outdated. This issue arises because the application is configured to pull help files from a local directory rather than the current online documentation.
Reference screenshot:

Resolution
To ensure Traverse loads the updated online help content, the local Help folder must be renamed so the application no longer references it.
Steps to Resolve
Locate the Traverse installation directory on the system.
Default path: C:\Program Files\Open Systems, Inc\TRAVERSE
Open the TRAVERSE folder and locate the Help folder.
Rename the Help folder by adding a prefix (for example, rename it to zzHelp).
Log out of Traverse Standard.
Log back into Traverse Standard.
Navigate to Help -> Contents within the application.
Result:
Traverse will now bypass the local help files and load the online help URL, displaying the most up-to-date help content.

e5004fbd-aaac-444f-b714-c953d7ee1f8c.title: W-3 Box 15 State and Employer State ID Not Printing – Multi-State W-2 Processing
e5004fbd-aaac-444f-b714-c953d7ee1f8c.content:
Problem
Customers may report that W-2 forms print correctly with state information, but the W-3 Transmittal does not print the State or Employer State ID in Box 15. This is typically not a system issue and is related to IRS reporting rules.

Resolution
- W-2 forms show correct State and State ID

- W-3 Transmittal Box 15 is blank or shows “X”

- Customer expects a specific state (ex: CA) and State ID to print


Per IRS guidelines: If W-2 forms include wage and tax data for more than one state, the W-3 must show an “X” in Box 15 and should not display a single State or Employer State ID.
This is expected behavior when employees have wages reported across multiple states.

- Confirm W-2 data includes more than one state

- Verify State Tax ID exists in Tax Authority setup (for data validation only)

- Confirm customer is processing W-2/W-3 for the correct payroll year

No system fix is required. This is working as designed based on IRS/SSA requirements.

12f336b6-9503-4dce-b5e2-6d06ec6369e8.title: Sales Order Acknowledgement – Logo Not Printing When APS Is Enabled
12f336b6-9503-4dce-b5e2-6d06ec6369e8.content:
Problem
Customers report that the company logo does not print on the Sales Order Acknowledgement. The issue occurs only when APS (Aptean Print Services) is enabled. When APS is disabled, the logo prints correctly.
- Application: Traverse

- Feature: Sales Order Acknowledgement

- Printing Method: APS (Aptean Print Services)

- Logo does not appear on the Sales Order Acknowledgement.

- Re-adding the logo in Design Studio does not resolve the issue.

- Printing works as expected when APS is disabled.

Resolution
When APS is enabled, the issue is related to the image format of the company logo. APS fails to process the logo image due to a color space mismatch.
This error can be found in the APS logs:
Numbers of source Raster bands and source color space components do not matchHow to Verify
- Navigate to the following directory on the server:
ApteanPrintAgent

- Open the log file:
ApteanPrintAgent.out.log

- Search for the error message:
Numbers of source Raster bands and source color space components do not match

- If this error is present, the issue is confirmed to be related to the logo image.


Steps to resolve:
Follow the steps below to resolve the issue:
- Locate the current company logo image.

- Open the image using Microsoft Paint.

- Click File → Save As → JPEG (.jpg).

- Save the image (this reprocesses the image into a compatible format).

- Open System Manager in Traverse.

- Navigate to Company Logo settings.

- Load the newly saved JPEG logo.

- Save the changes.

- Close and reopen Traverse.

- Reprint the Sales Order Acknowledgement.

The logo should now print correctly with APS enabled.

04c4ba79-e350-4ca4-991b-fac29f8c8b0e.title: How to resolve the error 'Current record cannot be deleted' while attempting to delete the 'Batch Code' in 'AP Payment Batch Codes'?
04c4ba79-e350-4ca4-991b-fac29f8c8b0e.content:
Problem
How to resolve the error 'Current record cannot be deleted' while attempting to delete the 'Batch Code' in 'AP Payment Batch Codes'?

Resolution
The reported error occurs when the selected Payment Batch is not available for further actions because it is currently in use. This typically happens when the batch is actively associated with an ongoing process or when one or more payments have already been prepared within the batch but have not yet been posted.
In such scenarios, the system prevents modification or deletion of the batch to ensure data integrity and to avoid interrupting in-progress payment activities.

Verification Steps:
To confirm whether the batch is actively in use, we can perform the following checks:
- Navigate to the Edit Register or Payment Register screen.
- Review the Batch Code drop-down list.
- Verify whether the concerned batch appears in the list.
- If available, preview the batch to review the payments currently prepared under it.



Resolution:
Based on the findings, one of the following actions can be taken:
- If the payments within the batch are valid, proceed with printing the required Checks or Vouchers, and then post the payments to complete the process.
- If the payments were prepared under an incorrect batch, the payments may need to be re-prepared under the correct batch. The existing batch can then be cleared.
- Once the batch no longer contains any prepared or pending payments and is no longer in use, it can be deleted as required.



Delete the empty batch (as needed):
i. Navigate to 'AP Payment Batch Codes':
We can access the Payment Batch Codes under the path: Applications -> Accounts Payable -> Setup and Maintenance -> Payment Batch Codes

ii. Select the now-empty batch and Click Delete:
The user will be able to delete the Batch without any issues now.


NOTE: The Default Batch (######) is system-defined and cannot be deleted, even when it contains no payments.

bfbc8900-7da5-4a5a-b4e7-611e6d000f65.title: How does 'Import' function works in Traverse?
bfbc8900-7da5-4a5a-b4e7-611e6d000f65.content:
Problem
Understanding and Executing Data Import in Traverse



Let us consider the below sample Import file for GL Transactions Import:

Resolution
Introduction:
The Import feature in Traverse allows us to bring data from external systems or files into Traverse efficiently. It is commonly used when:
- Migrating data from another system
- Creating or updating large volumes of records
- Automating repetitive data entry tasks
Traverse imports data using plain-text (ASCII) files and a structured framework that ensures data accuracy, validation, and correct routing into the database.
High-Level Import Flow in Traverse:
Every import in Traverse follows three mandatory stages:
- Create an Import Layout Definition
- Create an Import Map Definition
- Run Import via Import Mapped Data
Each stage builds on the previous one. In order to proceed with the Import process, the User must have a 'Source File' that contains all the required information, corresponding to the function, to which the import is performed.
For example, Traverse supports Import in the following modules:
- AP Transactions
- AR Transactions
- BR Transactions
- BR Cleared Transactions
- CRM Contacts
- GL Transactions
- IN Physical Inventory Counts
- IN Item Prices
- MB Bills of Material
- MFG Production Activity
- PA Transactions
- SO Transactions
- SO Customer Pricing
Pre-requisites: Source File
Supported File Formats:
Traverse supports only ASCII text files, typically created using Excel and saved as .csv or .txt.
Supported formats:
- Comma-delimited
- Comma-quote delimited (used when values contain commas)
- Fixed-length field
- Fixed-length record
Key Guidelines:
- First row may contain column headers
- Each row represents one record
- All values are initially treated as RawText
- If commas exist within data (e.g., descriptions), values must be enclosed in quotes
Step 1: Import Layout Definition:
The Import Layout Definition tells Traverse how to read the source file. This can be accessed under the path: System Manager -> Company Setup -> Import Layout Definition.
Purpose:
- Defines file structure
- Identifies fields
- Applies conversions and translations
- Filters unwanted records
Key Configuration Areas
SettingDescriptionFile TypeDelimited or Fixed WidthSkip RowsUsually 1 to skip headers (If no header is present, we can keep it as '0')Field SeparatorComma, tab, space, etc.Row SeparatorCRLF (most common)Text QualifierUsually quotesGet FieldsAuto-reads column namesData TypeAlways starts as RawTextData Conversion:
Because all imported values start as 'Raw Text':
- Numeric fields → must be converted
- Date fields → must be converted
- Boolean fields → must be converted
Conversion is done using functions (e.g., CONVERT) within the layout definition. The available functions are listed as below:
FunctionSyntaxDescriptionLEN=LEN([FieldId])Returns the numeric length the identified field value.TRIM=TRIM([FieldId])Removes leading and trailing spaces from the identified field value. Returns a text value.SUBSTRING=SUBSTRING([FieldId], start, length)Returns the subset of text characters from the identified field value.CONVERT=CONVERT([FieldId])Converts the identified field value to the field type of the current field.ISNULL=ISNULL([FieldId1],[FieldId2])Replaces a null (or empty string) value with the identified replacement value.NULLIF=NULLIF([FieldId1],[FieldId2])Returns a null when the value of field 1 matches the value of field 2.ROWID=ROWID()Returns the sequential id of the source data.GETDATE=GETDATE()Returns the current session date (workstation date).XLATE=XLATE([FieldId])
Extended: val1;xlate1;val2;xlate2Translates the value of the identified field using a set of key/value pairs provided in the Extended properties of the field definition.PARSE=PARSE([FieldId], "mask")
Evaluates the contents of the identified field using a preset mask to specify positional attributes of the field value.

Translation & Mapping:
If external values don’t match Traverse values:
- Use Extended Info to map equivalents
- Example: Source Bin I8 → Traverse Bin A-03
Filtering:
Layout definitions can filter records:
- Include or exclude specific items
- Limit locations, lots, bins, etc.
Setup:
- Click on 'New' icon at the top to create a new Layout ID
- Layout ID: Enter the Layout ID as preferred. [In this example, it is BR_F]
- Description: Enter the Description for the layout.
- File Type: Select a File Type that describes the plain-text source file. [The most common file type is ‘Delimited’].
- Number of rows: Enter the Number of rows the system should skip before importing the data. [Usually, we will have a title row for the columns, so we would enter ‘1’ to skip the first row].
- Field separator: Select the Field separator used in the source file to separate the fields. A Comma is the most common separator.
- Row separator: Select the Row separator used in the source file. The most common separator is the ‘CRLF' (carriage return line feed)
- Text qualifier: Select the Text qualifier that is used when a field separator occurs within a field. If there are no such entries, enter 'NONE'
- Filename: We can either enter the path and filename where the source file is located or browse to the source file under the 'Filename'. This enables us to use the 'Get Fields' function, which directs the system to read the column names from the source file and fill in the detail grid.
- Get Fields: The Get Fields function will only work if the first row of the source file contains column headings. If we do not have a path and filename selected, enter the column names from the source file into the detail grid with a data Type of ‘RawText’
- All the fields, including numeric or date fields, will be imported as a data type of ‘RawText’, and this needs to be later converted to the desired data type with the help of following functions:


Step 2: Import Map Definition:
The Import Map Definition links source fields to Traverse destination fields. This can be accessed under the path: System Manager -> Company Setup -> Import Map Definition.
Purpose:
- Routes data into the correct Traverse tables
- Uses Traverse assemblies and schemas
Key Components:
ElementDescriptionFunction IDDefault / IN Pricing / SO PricingAssemblyImport engine for the moduleClassHolds schemasSchemaDefines available propertiesPropertyDestination Traverse fieldFieldSource layout field

Note: Not all fields are mandatory. Only mapped fields are imported.
Setup:
- Click on the New icon to create a new Import Map ID
- Function ID: Select a Function ID for the map definition. [Use the ‘Default’ option unless we are importing IN Item Price (IN Pricing) or SO Customer Pricing (Pricing)]
- Description: Enter the Description for the Map ID.
- Assembly: Browse the required assembly
- Class ID: Use the Class ID as needed
- Expand the properties grid of the schema by clicking on the plus sign. Set up the necessary mappings for the corresponding module import.
- Once everything is set up as desired, click on 'Save' at the top to save the Map ID.
Assembly and Class Information:
ModuleFunctionAssemblyClassAPTransactionsTRAVERSE.Import.APTransactionTRAVERSE.Import.AccountsPayable.TransactionImportARTransactionsTRAVERSE.Import.ARTransactionTRAVERSE.Import.AccountsReceivable.TransactionImportBank RecCleared TransactionsTRAVERSE.Business.BankRecTRAVERSE.Business.BankRec.ClearedTransImportBank RecTransactionsTRAVERSE.Business.BankRecTRAVERSE.Business.BankRec.TransactionImportCRMContactsTRAVERSE.Business.CRMTRAVERSE.Business.CRM.ContactImportGeneral LedgerTransactionsTRAVERSE.Business.GeneralLedgerTRAVERSE.Business.GeneralLedger.TransactionImportPhysical InventoryPhysical CountTRAVERSE.Business.PhysicalInventoryTRAVERSE.Business.PhysicalCountImportInventoryItem PricingTRAVERSE.Import.INItemTRAVERSE.Import.INItem.ItemPriceImportMFG BOMAssembly HeaderTRAVERSE.Import.MfgBomTRAVERSE.Import.Manufacturing.AssemblyHeaderImportMFG ProductionActivityTRAVERSE.Import.MfgProductionTRAVERSE.Import.Manufacturing.ProductionActivityImportPayrollTransactionsTRAVERSE.Business.PATransactionTRAVERSE.Business.Payroll.TimeTicketImportSales OrderTransactionsTRAVERSE.Import.SOTransactionTRAVERSE.Import.SOTransaction.SOTransactionImportSales OrderCustomer PricingTRAVERSE.Import.PricingTRAVERSE.Import.Pricing.CustomerPricingImport
Step 3: Import Mapped Data:
Once layout and map are ready, data is imported using Import Mapped Data. This can be accessed under the path: System Manager -> Company Setup -> Import Mapped Data.
- Map ID: Select the Map ID that was set under Import Map Definition. (In this example, BR_F)
- File Name: Choose the CSV file containing the BR Transactions. [It may appear by default, if it was already set up in the SM Import Layout Definition]
- Click on the "Read Data" button to Read the data from the File.
- Click on the "Verify Data" button to validate the data from the File against the requirement of Traverse data fields
Import Actions:
1. Read Data:
- Loads file into preview grid
2. Verify Data:
- Validates business rules
- Flags errors (missing values, invalid references)
3. Fix Errors (If any):
- We can correct directly in grid (small issues)
- Or update source file and reload
4. Import Data
- Writes validated data into Traverse
- Import is cumulative unless otherwise restricted


NOTE: Re-running import adds data again unless prevented by logic. So, it is recommended to ensure if the Import was not performed by 2 users simultaneously for the same records.
Single-Level Import vs Multi-Level Import:
1. Single-Level Import:
Used when data has one logical level, such as:
- GL Transactions
- Physical Inventory Counts
- AR/AP/BR/GL Transactions
In short, each row represents one record

2. Multi-Level Import:
Used when data has parent-child relationships, such as:
- Manufacturing Bills of Material (BOM)
Traverse uses CompoundData schemas where:
- One row can contain header, routing, and component data
- Hierarchy is reconstructed during import
Special Case: Item Price Import:
Item pricing uses a dedicated import process, but still requires:
- Import Layout Definition
- Import Map Definition
- Default map setup in SM Business Rules
Special Options
- Apply pricing to all locations
- Apply pricing to all units of measure
- We can choose: - Create only
- Update only
- Create + Update

Import respects sequence order in the source file.
Modules That Support Import in Traverse:
The following Traverse modules support import functionality:
Financial Modules:
- Accounts Payable Transactions
- Accounts Receivable Transactions
- General Ledger Transactions
- Payroll Transactions
- Bank Reconciliation Transactions
- Bank Reconciliation Cleared Transactions
Inventory & Manufacturing:
- Inventory Physical Inventory Counts
- Inventory Item Prices
- Manufacturing Bills of Material (BOM)
- Manufacturing Production Activity
Sales & CRM:
- Sales Order Transactions
- Sales Order Customer Pricing
- CRM Contacts
Notes:
- Import in Traverse is definition-driven
- Layout controls how data is read
- Map controls where data goes
- Verify step is critical to avoid bad data
- Multi-level imports require careful file design
- Pricing imports have additional rules and options

73aa3e22-b029-46e8-b0c6-ffe130ec39e2.title: Check Number Field Not Displayed in AR Cash Receipts Screen
73aa3e22-b029-46e8-b0c6-ffe130ec39e2.content:
Problem
Users may encounter an issue in the Accounts Receivable → Cash Receipts screen where the Check Number field does not appear for certain customers when entering cash receipt transactions.

Resolution
This issue occurs when the Payment Method used for the cash receipt is not configured with the correct Payment Type.
To resolve the issue, follow the steps below:
- Navigate to the AR Payment Method setup screen: Accounts Receivable → Setup and Maintenance → Payment Methods

- Identify the payment method being used for check payments.

- Verify the Payment Type assigned to the payment method.

- Ensure the Payment Type is set to CHECK.
- If the payment type is set to any value other than CHECK, the Check Number field will not be displayed in the AR Cash Receipts screen.

- Save the changes.

-
Log out of the current session and log back in to ensure the changes take effect.

- Re-open the AR Cash Receipts screen and verify that the Check Number field is now visible.

60a3f8f0-8d27-44ad-8d2a-37d1bc9cc388.content:

===================================

------------------------------
Edition = Global

9edc0e60-72a4-4cce-99ec-26f211fbca26.title: How to perform BR Transactions Import for a specific 'Bank Account ID' from a .csv file?
9edc0e60-72a4-4cce-99ec-26f211fbca26.content:
Problem
How to perform BR Transactions Import for a specific 'Bank Account ID' from a .csv file?



Let us consider the below Import file:

Resolution
In this example, the Transaction Type is set to “-1”, which represents a Disbursement transaction. The system uses predefined enumeration values to identify different transaction types.
Accordingly, the appropriate enumeration value must be used based on the nature of the transaction being imported or processed. The supported transaction type values are as follows:
2Deposit4Adjustment-1Disbursement-3Transfer

It is important to ensure that the correct enumeration value is specified to avoid processing errors and to ensure accurate transaction classification.

It is a 3-step process that comprises of the following:
I. Set up the SM Import Layout Definition:
- Go to the SM Import Layout definition under the path: Applications -> System Manager -> Company Setup -> Import Layout Definition
- Click on 'New' icon at the top to create a new Layout ID
- Layout ID: Enter the Layout ID as preferred. [In this example, it is BR_F]
- Description: Enter the Description for the layout.
- File Type: Select a File Type that describes the plain-text source file. [The most common file type is ‘Delimited’].
- Number of rows: Enter the Number of rows the system should skip before importing the data. [Usually, we will have a title row for the columns, so we would enter ‘1’ to skip the first row].
- Field separator: Select the Field separator used in the source file to separate the fields. A Comma is the most common separator.
- Row separator: Select the Row separator used in the source file. The most common separator is the ‘CRLF' (carriage return line feed)
- Text qualifier: Select the Text qualifier that is used when a field separator occurs within a field. If there are no such entries, enter 'NONE'
- Filename: We can either enter the path and filename where the source file is located or browse to the source file under the 'Filename'. This enables us to use the 'Get Fields' function, which directs the system to read the column names from the source file and fill in the detail grid.
- Get Fields: The Get Fields function will only work if the first row of the source file contains column headings. If we do not have a path and filename selected, enter the column names from the source file into the detail grid with a data Type of ‘RawText’
- All the fields, including numeric or date fields, will be imported as a data type of ‘RawText’, and this needs to be later converted to the desired data type with the help of following functions:
FunctionSyntaxDescriptionLEN=LEN([FieldId])Returns the numeric length the identified field value.TRIM=TRIM([FieldId])Removes leading and trailing spaces from the identified field value. Returns a text value.SUBSTRING=SUBSTRING([FieldId], start, length)Returns the subset of text characters from the identified field value.CONVERT=CONVERT([FieldId])Converts the identified field value to the field type of the current field.ISNULL=ISNULL([FieldId1],[FieldId2])Replaces a null (or empty string) value with the identified replacement value.NULLIF=NULLIF([FieldId1],[FieldId2])Returns a null when the value of field 1 matches the value of field 2.ROWID=ROWID()Returns the sequential id of the source data.GETDATE=GETDATE()Returns the current session date (workstation date).XLATE=XLATE([FieldId])
Extended: val1;xlate1;val2;xlate2Translates the value of the identified field using a set of key/value pairs provided in the Extended properties of the field definition.PARSE=PARSE([FieldId], "mask")
Evaluates the contents of the identified field using a preset mask to specify positional attributes of the field value.

- ​​​​​​​Once everything is set up as desired, click on 'Save' at the top to save the Layout:

NOTE: In the Bank Reconciliation Transaction Import, the Bank ID is currently configured as “MAIN”, since the import is performed for a fixed Bank Account ID 'MAIN'. Please note that this Bank ID must be updated according to the user’s requirement.

II. Set up the SM Import Map Definition:
- Go to the SM Import Map Definition under the path: Applications -> System Manager -> Company Setup -> Import Map Definition
- Click on the New icon to create a new Import Map ID [In this example, we are using the Map ID as BR_F]
- Function ID: Select a Function ID for the map definition. [Use the ‘Default’ option unless we are importing IN Item Price (IN Pricing) or SO Customer Pricing (Pricing)]
- Description: Enter the Description for the Map ID.
- Assembly: Browse the assembly as TRAVERSE.Business.BankRec
- Class ID: Use the Class ID as TRAVERSE.Business.BankRec.TransactionImport for BR Transactions Import
- Expand the properties grid of the schema by clicking on the plus sign. Set up the necessary mappings for the BR import.
- Once everything is set up as desired, click on 'Save' at the top to save the Map ID.


III. Import the data into Traverse through SM Mapped data:
- Go to SM Import Mapped Data under the path: Applications -> System Manager -> Company Setup -> Import Mapped Data
- Map ID: Select the Map ID that was set under Import Map Definition. (In this example, BR_F)
- File Name: Choose the CSV file containing the BR Transactions. [It may appear by default, if it was already set up in the SM Import Layout Definition]
- Click on the "Read Data" button to Read the data from the File.

- Once the data was read successfully, click on 'Verify Data' button to check the data for errors. If the data has errors, those records will be flagged. If there are no errors, it will appear as follows, and then we can import the data into the BR Transactions screen.​​​​​​​
​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

Now we can observe the transactions being imported into the BR Transactions screen under the path: Applications -> Bank Reconciliation -> Transactions -> Transactions:

d6f5ff68-2c50-4fed-b058-8e0a30d5a902.title: Entering Annual Salary for Employees in Traverse Payroll
d6f5ff68-2c50-4fed-b058-8e0a30d5a902.content:
Problem
The customer inquired about the possibility of entering an employee's total annual salary in Traverse and having the system automatically calculate the weekly gross pay

Resolution
Issue / Question
Customers may ask whether Traverse allows entry of an employee’s total annual salary in:
Payroll → Setup → Employee Information
with the expectation that Traverse will automatically divide the annual amount by the number of payrolls in a year (for example, weekly or biweekly) to calculate the gross pay per pay period.
The goal is often to avoid minor rounding differences that can result in the year-end total being off by a few pennies.
Explanation
Traverse Payroll does not currently support entering an employee’s salary as a single annual amount and automatically calculating the gross pay per pay period.
Instead, Traverse is designed to calculate payroll based on the amount entered for each pay period (weekly, biweekly, semi-monthly, etc.). All payroll calculations and year-to-date totals are derived from this per-pay-period amount.
Resolution
- Annual salary entry is not supported in Traverse Payroll.

- Salary must be entered as a per-pay-period amount in:
Payroll → Setup → Employee Information

- Traverse does not automatically divide an annual salary by the number of payrolls in a year.

Recommended Best Practice
To avoid year-end rounding discrepancies:
- Manually calculate the per-pay-period salary based on the annual amount and pay frequency.

- Enter the calculated per-pay-period amount in the employee’s payroll setup.

- If needed, make minor adjustments in the final payroll of the year to ensure totals align with the intended annual salary.

Summary
Traverse Payroll requires salaried employees to be set up using a per-pay-period salary amount. There is currently no option to enter an annual salary and have the system automatically calculate weekly or other periodic gross pay.

3f6ca490-4743-41f2-a71c-01bfe1cb4e56.title: 1099 Processing: Changes in Manage 1099 Invoices Not Reflected
3f6ca490-4743-41f2-a71c-01bfe1cb4e56.content:
Problem
The client is in the process of generating 1099 forms for year-end reporting and observed that certain invoices are not being included in the 1099 totals.



Upon review, it was identified that:

-
The affected invoices were originally processed without being marked as 1099-eligible

-
At a later point, the user attempted to correct this by updating the invoices using the Manage 1099 Invoices screen

-
Although the 1099 checkbox was enabled in the Manage 1099 Invoices screen, the invoices still did not appear in the 1099 Processing screen

This led to confusion, as the user expected the updated invoices to automatically reflect in the 1099 totals.



Let us consider the below example invoice of $160.28 for the Vendor 0001:

Resolution
Why This Happens (System Behavior):

In Traverse, the 1099 Processing screen does not dynamically refresh invoice-level changes made in the Manage 1099 Invoices screen.



Key points:

- The Manage 1099 Invoices screen allows users to manually adjust or correct invoice-level 1099 flags and amounts
- However, changes made here are not immediately reflected in the 1099 Processing totals
- The Generate action in the 1099 Processing screen is required to recalculate and refresh vendor 1099 totals

Until the Generate button is clicked again, the system continues to display previously calculated totals, causing updated invoices to appear as though they are not included.



Root Cause:

The invoices were correctly updated in Manage 1099 Invoices, but the 1099 Processing screen was not regenerated after the changes were made.

When we review the '1099 Processing' screen, the specific Invoice is currently missing in the totals:



Resolution:

i. Navigate to Accounts Payable -> Periodic Processing -> 1099 Processing

ii. Select the appropriate Fiscal Year

iii. Click the Generate button

iv. Traverse would throw a pop-up asking if we want to start over, and we need to click on 'Yes'



This recalculates vendor 1099 totals based on Current data. Any changes made in Manage 1099 Invoices. Review the refreshed vendor totals

[Confirm that the previously missing invoices are now included in the 1099 amounts. Once the Generate process was run, the updated invoices appeared correctly, and the issue was resolved.]



Points to remember:

- Any time changes are made in Manage 1099 Invoices, the Generate option must be run again in 1099 Processing
- The Generate function:
- Recalculates totals
- Refreshes vendor 1099 data
- Ensures manual corrections are reflected correctly

-
This applies whether:

- Invoices were initially excluded from 1099
- Amounts were adjusted
- Form codes were updated

Outcome

After running Generate in the 1099 Processing screen:

- Updated invoices were successfully included/excluded
- Vendor 1099 totals reflected correctly
- The user will be able to proceed with year-end 1099 processing without further issues

e8115653-0c57-4df6-aaa9-362a3be40c53.content:
Problem
A user is logged into Traverse and is unable to log out. The application becomes unresponsive, preventing the user from closing the session normally.

This issue typically occurs when a user session becomes stuck on the Remote Desktop Server (RDS) due to an unexpected system state, such as a temporary system glitch, network interruption, or multiple transaction screens being left open simultaneously.

Problem
Customers needing to submit W-2 files to state authorities (like Kentucky) and the IRS often require these files to be in a .txt format

This article outlines a simple method to rename your existing W-2 magnetic media file to include the .txt extension, making it compatible for submission.

Locate the file: Navigate to the folder where your W-2 magnetic media file is saved.

5e9011fd-111a-4853-b13f-6c0f6cad8685.title: Using Description Items in Traverse for Non-Inventory Sales and Purchase Transactions
5e9011fd-111a-4853-b13f-6c0f6cad8685.content:
Problem
The customer requires an Item ID that can be used in Sales Order and Purchase Order transactions; however, the item should not be tracked in Inventory. Using a standard Inventory Item would incorrectly affect on-hand quantity, inventory valuation, and COGS calculations. The customer needs a way to reference an item in transactions without maintaining stock levels.

Resolution
To meet this requirement, Description Items should be used instead of Inventory Items.

Why Use Description Items?

- Description Items can be selected in Sales Orders and Purchase Orders.
- Inventory quantities are not tracked for Description Items.
- Unit cost and unit price can be modified at the transaction level without affecting the master item setup.
- Fixed approximate cost and price values can be stored for reference.
- Description Items can later be converted to Inventory Items if required using IN-SM Convert Items.

Information Maintained for Description Items

For each Description Item, the following details can be configured:

- Item ID and Description
- Additional Description (optional)
- Tax Class
- Unit of Measure
- Unit Cost and Unit Price
- GL Expense Account
- GL Sales Account
- GL Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) Account
- GL Inventory Account

Steps to Create a Description Item:

i. Navigate to the SM Description Items setup screen under the path: Applications -> System Manager -> Company Setup -> Description Items

ii. Click New to create a new Description Item record.

iii. Enter a unique Item ID.

iv. Enter the Description (and Additional Description if required).

v. Select the appropriate Tax Class.

vi. Enter the Unit of Measure.

vii. Enter the Unit Cost and Unit Price.

viii. Assign the GL Expense, Sales, COGS, and Inventory accounts as applicable.

ix. Click Save to complete the setup.



Notes:

- Description Items do not affect inventory on-hand quantities or inventory valuation.
- These items are suitable for services, freight, fees, or non-stock purchases and sales.
- If inventory tracking is required in the future, Description Items can be converted to Inventory Items using the IN-SM Convert Items utility.





Illustrative Example (Non-Tracked Packaging or Bundle Item)

Scenario: A customer sells a set of multiple products packed together in a box (for example, a promotional kit or bundled items). The box itself is only a packaging or reference item and should not be tracked in inventory, as only the individual items inside the box are inventoried.



Requirement:

- The user wants to add an Item ID such as BOX-SET 1 on the Sales Order or Purchase Order.
- The quantity and stock of the box should not be tracked in Inventory.
- The box should not affect inventory valuation or on-hand quantity.

Recommended Approach: Create BOX-SET 1 as a Description Item.



How It Works:

- The Description Item (BOX-SET 1) can be added to SO or PO lines for reference and pricing.
- Traverse will not track quantity or stock levels for this item.
- The user can assign a fixed price (e.g., packaging or handling charge) without impacting inventory accounts.
- The actual inventory tracking remains on the individual stocked items inside the box.



Example Use Cases:

- Packaging or box charges
- Service or handling fees
- Bundled kit reference lines
- Non-stock miscellaneous charges

This approach ensures accurate inventory tracking for real stock items while allowing flexible reference items in transactional documents.

45260247-03c4-4bbe-a1ff-17dcbecaa04f.title: Avalara Address Validation for International Addresses
45260247-03c4-4bbe-a1ff-17dcbecaa04f.content:
Problem
The error "country code GBR is not a supported country" during address validation occurs.

Resolution
Overview
When working with international customer addresses, users may encounter limitations with Avalara address validation. This article focuses specifically on how Avalara handles address validation for international addresses and what to expect when validation is not supported.
Address Validation Limitation
Avalara address validation is currently supported only for U.S. and Canadian addresses. When attempting to validate an address for any other country, the validation process will fail, and an error message may be displayed indicating that the country is not supported.
For example, validating an address with the country code GBR (United Kingdom / Great Britain) may return a message stating that the country is not supported for address validation.
Expected Behavior for International Addresses
- Address validation will fail for all non-U.S. and non-Canadian addresses.

- This is expected system behavior and not a configuration or data issue.

- The correct country code (such as GBR for the United Kingdom) can still be used even though validation is not available.

Impact on Processing
Address validation is not required for international addresses in order for Avalara to function correctly. Even when validation is skipped:
- Sales orders can be processed without interruption.

- Avalara will continue to calculate tax accurately for international transactions.

Recommended Action
When entering or updating an international address:
- Enter the address using the correct country code.

- Make sure that the country code is correctly configured. For more to learn about country codes setup, refer to KB Article: 000092559

- Make sure that the country code is added to the Valid Countries section of the SM Tax Service Integration screen.

- Bypass or skip the address validation step if validation fails.

- Proceed with normal transaction processing.

Summary Avalara does not support address validation for international addresses at this time. However, this limitation does not affect tax calculation. Users can safely bypass address validation and continue processing transactions for international customers.
Supporting References
To know more about three letter country code: Avalara Country Codes – Ordway Support Portal
To validate the statement that Avalara does not support the International address validation, refer: Can AvaTax validate international addresses?

8079a5b2-4631-4eb7-a0d3-3cedaded1874.title: Payroll withholding
8079a5b2-4631-4eb7-a0d3-3cedaded1874.content:
Problem
Procedure to set up withholdings in Payroll.

Resolution
Payroll Withholdings
When you set up a State for the first time first go to File Maintenance > Payroll Information > Set up State unemployment reports. This determines the Order the information is printed on the Unemployment reports.

If this set up is not done you will get this message when you enter the SUI state in the employee tax information record.

Codes maintenance > Tax Authority Setup
Choose the Tax Authority, Federal, State or local. Chose the Code and Page Down.
State and Federal Records should be setup. Any Local Taxes will need to be created. Check the SUI Table ID to make sure the x is included. This will allow the formula to read a company specific table.

Codes Maintenance > Withholdings
This is where exclusions are setup for Deductions and Earning Codes. When setting or checking exclusions for the Tax Authority > Federal, make sure exceptions for the OAS and EOA match, the MED and EME also need to match each other. These are the Employer and Employee portions of the FICA taxes. If they do not this can cause discrepancies on the 941 Worksheet.

You will need a GL account for the Liability Account. For some codes, employer paid taxes, you will also need an Accrued Taxes Account. The tax ID that is entered here will be used on reports and forms like the W-2. If you have an Earning Code that uses a fixed withholding it will read the fixed percent entered here.
Exclusions from withholding can also be set at the employee level. In File maintenance > Employee > Tax Information > Withholding Setup.

Check here when only one employee is having an issue where they do not have any withholding as compared to all others.

Codes maintenance >Tax Groups
A tax group will be assigned to an employee in File Maintenance > Employee > Tax Information. This will group employees by the State and Local taxes that are to be withheld. Enter the Appropriate State and local taxes to be withheld.

If transactions were entered for an employee the tax group used in calculate checks will be the one entered during transaction entry.
File Maintenance > Tax Tables
These Tables hold the information for calculating withholding. You’ll find the State Withholding tables here, STX. State unemployment, SUT tables. State other taxes, SOT. The Federal withholding tables, FED. The FICA and MEDEM tables for calculating OAS, EOA, MED and EME withholdings.
Note: EOA is the employer portion of the OASDI, OAS is the employees’ portion. These withholding amounts should match. EME is the employer portion of Medicare. MED is the employee portion of the tax, these should also match. There is an exception here and that is for employees making over $200,000.00 there is an additional 0.9% in MED withholding, so in these instances the MED withholding will exceed the EME.


File Maintenance > Formula Maintenance
The Formulas for calculating Withholdings can be setup or maintained here. If you wish to review a formula it may be best to go to Master File Lists > Formula Lists and print the formula out. The formulas use the amounts from the tax table to calculate withholding.
Self-adjusting formulas: A self-adjusting formula checks the YTD tax amount and the YTD earnings if the tax amount is understated then on a single paycheck it will increase the withholding so the YTD tax amount is the correct percent of the YTD earnings amount.  If it is overstated then there will be no withholding. The formulas that are self-adjusting are State SUI, FUTA, EOA, OAS, EME and MED. The amounts are found in Employee History.
File Maintenance > Employee > Tax Information
Once the above setup is completed you can fill out the Tax Information Screen of the Employees’. Here you set the employees Tax Group, withholding status, Exemptions (99 exemptions can be entered and there will be no withholding.) Extra withholding, a fixed withholding amount can be set, Tax Table ID, and SUI State. Some states may have prompts these come from a table in File Maintenance Tax Tables.

This is the information that will be used in Calculating this employees withholding. State and Local Tax Information must be in both the Tax Group and here. This is of Importance for employees that live in one state and work in another or may work in multiple states. The tax group entered during transaction entry is the one used for calculating checks.

13e3d977-d584-45c7-a90f-e76ed755c383.title: How to Create a Zero-Dollar Manual Check in Payroll?
13e3d977-d584-45c7-a90f-e76ed755c383.content:
Problem
Customers may encounter discrepancies between payroll reports and federal tax filings, such as Form 941 and year-end W-2 reporting. In some cases, taxable wages, gross earnings, or withholding amounts may not align correctly due to payroll calculation issues, manual adjustments.

Resolution
Resolution

To correct the taxable wage discrepancy and align payroll and tax reporting, a zero-dollar manual payroll check can be created to adjust taxable and gross earnings without issuing an actual payment.

Steps to Create a Zero-Dollar Manual Check:

A. Access the 'PA Manual Checks' screen:

Navigate to the 'PA Manual Checks' screen under the path: Applications -> Payroll -> Payday Work -> Manual Checks.



B. Create a New Manual Check

- Click New to create a new manual check record.
- Select the Employee ID.
- Enter the Check Date and Pay Code as required.
- Leave the Check Number blank for automatic assignment (if applicable).

C. Set Earnings to Zero

i. In the Earnings tab we need to set the following fields to zero:

- Hours = 0
- Rate = 0
- Amount = 0

This ensures no gross pay is issued to the employee.



D. Calculate Taxes:

i. Click the Calculate Tax option. This action pulls in the Withholding Details for the employee.



E. Adjust Taxable and Gross Earnings

i. Navigate to the Withholdings / Taxable Earnings section.

ii. Manually update:

- Taxable Earnings
- Gross Earnings

Enter the adjustment amount required to correct the discrepancy (for example, $10.00).

This step ensures:

- Federal taxable wages are corrected.
- Year-end W-2 and 941 reporting align with payroll records.



F. Save the Manual Check

- Click Save to finalize the zero-dollar manual check.



This check can now be posted, from the PA Post Checks screen, and the reports





Expected Outcome:

- The manual check posts no net pay to the employee.
- Taxable wages and gross wages are adjusted for reporting accuracy.
- Form 941 and W-2 reports reflect corrected wage values.
- Payroll and tax reports are reconciled without rerunning payroll.

Notes:

- Zero-dollar checks should only be used for payroll reporting corrections.
- Always document the adjustment for audit and compliance purposes.
- Review payroll tax reports after posting the manual check to confirm corrections.
- It is recommended to test this process in a non-production environment, if available.

Summary:

A zero-dollar manual check is a corrective payroll tool used to adjust taxable and gross earnings without issuing additional wages. By setting earnings to zero, calculating taxes, and manually adjusting taxable and gross earnings, payroll discrepancies—such as incorrect Form 941 wages or W-2 reporting differences—can be resolved accurately.

81f8ebd7-3be3-4cc2-9898-dbd8fb79da92.title: Activating a License Key Using Traverse License Server Manager
81f8ebd7-3be3-4cc2-9898-dbd8fb79da92.content:
Problem
Multiple users are unable to access the sandbox, we receive the attached error message. or Need to activate sandbox or production license key

Resolution
KB Article: Activating a License Key Using Traverse License Server Manager
Overview
This Knowledge Base article outlines the steps required to activate a Traverse license key using the Traverse Global License Server Manager. License activation must be completed carefully to ensure uninterrupted application access. Prior to activation, it is important to verify that no users are actively logged in to the customer environment.
Prerequisites
- Access to the customer’s installation survey
- Administrative access to the customer’s RDS server
- Valid license key provided by the Fulfilment team
- Correct Site ID, obtained from the Fulfilment team or installation survey
- Access to Traverse Global License Server Manager
Procedure
Step 1: Verify Active User Sessions
- Obtain the customer’s RDS server details from the installation survey.
- Log in to the customer’s RDS server.
- Open Task Manager.
- Navigate to the Users tab.
- Ensure there are no active or disconnected sessions related to the affected customer.
- If users are logged in, request them to log off before proceeding.
Step 2: Open Traverse License Server Manager
- Launch Traverse Global License Server Manager from the server.
- Locate and select the Customer Profile ID from the list.

Step 3: Activate the License Key
- Navigate to the Product ID tab.
- Enter the license key provided by the Fulfilment team.
- Click Activate Product.
Step 4: Enter Site ID
- Go to the Site ID tab.
- Enter the Site ID.
- This information can be obtained from:- The Fulfilment team, or
- The customer’s installation survey

Step 5: Apply Configuration and Restart Service
- Click Update Configuration to apply the changes.
- Restart the License Service to complete the activation process.

Post-Activation Validation
- Confirm the license status shows as Active.
- Launch Traverse to verify successful login.
- Ask the customer to validate access from their end.
- Update the corresponding support or Salesforce case.
Important Notes
- License activation should always be performed during a controlled change window.
- Ensure accuracy when entering the Product ID and Site ID to avoid activation failures.
- Restarting the license service is mandatory for changes to take effect.

fa1e2994-1a12-41a8-b69a-9a41843e6e16.title: The customer is required to enter a Name Control and Control Code but is unsure where to obtain this information.
fa1e2994-1a12-41a8-b69a-9a41843e6e16.content:
Problem
The user encountered errors while generating the 1099 Magnetic Media file and was prompted to enter a Name Control and Control Code. They are seeking clarification on what these fields are and where to obtain the required information.

Resolution
Understanding Name Control and Transmitter Control Code (TCC) for IRS FIRE Filing
Overview
When generating and submitting electronic information returns (such as 1099 forms) to the IRS, filers must comply with the IRS Filing Information Returns Electronically (FIRE) system requirements. Two critical fields required during this process are:
- Name Control

- Transmitter Control Code (TCC)

This article explains what each field represents, why it is required, and how filers can obtain or verify the necessary information.
What Is Name Control?
Name Control refers to the filer’s legal name as it is registered with the IRS.
How to Enter Name Control
- Enter the business name or filer name exactly as it appears on IRS records.

- This is typically:
- The legal business name associated with the EIN, or

- The filer name used in previous IRS filings.

Important Notes
- The Name Control must match IRS records to avoid file rejection.

- Do not use abbreviations or alternate spellings unless they are officially registered with the IRS.

What Is a Transmitter Control Code (TCC)?
The Transmitter Control Code (TCC) is a 5-digit alphanumeric code issued by the IRS. Eg: CRI25
Purpose of the TCC
- Uniquely identifies the business or entity transmitting electronic information returns.

- Acts as authorization and login credentials for submitting files through the IRS FIRE system.

- Required for all electronic 1099 submissions via FIRE.

How to Obtain a TCC (First-time filing 1099’s)
To receive a TCC, filers must apply directly through the IRS.
Step-by-Step: Applying for a TCC
- Visit the IRS Information Returns (IR) Application for TCC page.

- Submit the online application (this replaced the legacy Form 4419).

- Complete all required business and transmitter details.

- Submit the application for IRS review.

- Once approved, the IRS issues the TCC directly to the filer.

IRS Resource:
Filing Information Returns Electronically (FIRE) | Internal Revenue Service

If You Do Not Have or Cannot Locate Your TCC or Name Comtrol
- The TCC cannot be generated, retrieved, or reset by Aptean support

- For security and compliance reasons:
- Support does not have visibility into your TCC or Name Control

- The filer is solely responsible for retaining this code.

Link:
About Information Returns (IR) Application for Transmitter Control Code (TCC) for Filing Information Returns Electronically (FIRE) | Internal Revenue Service
Recommended Actions
- Contact the IRS directly if:
- Your TCC is lost

- You are unsure whether one was previously issued

- You need to reapply for a new TCC

Key Compliance Notes
- The system strictly follows IRS FIRE electronic filing requirements.

- Both Name Control and TCC must be valid and accurate for successful submission.

- Incorrect or missing information may result in:
- IRS file rejections

- Delays in processing information returns

6feba4fd-deb0-45b0-8c11-e20da94084d0.title: How to resolve the error 'Company ID is required' while accessing the 'Detail' in GL Statement Contents?
6feba4fd-deb0-45b0-8c11-e20da94084d0.content:
Problem
How to resolve the error 'Company ID is required' while accessing the 'Detail' in GL Statement Contents?



This error prevents the user from proceeding with the statement setup, even though a valid Company ID is selected.

Resolution
Root Cause:
This issue typically occurs when the GL Account Mask is not properly populated for the company in the System (SYS) database, specifically in the table: SYS.dbo.tblSmCompInfo
If the column GlAcctMask is NULL for the affected Company ID, the application is unable to validate the company during Statement Content creation, resulting in the above error.
Although the Account Mask is a mandatory configuration, there are scenarios where:
- The Account Mask was not correctly written to the SYS table during initial setup, or
- The setup was partially completed, leaving the GlAcctMask value empty at the database level.

The Account Mask is configured within the application under the following path: General Ledger -> Setup and Maintenance -> Account Mask

As a first step, we recommend verifying whether the Account Mask setup has been completed on the GL Account Mask screen. If the setup is incomplete, completing it should resolve the issue.

If the issue persists despite the Account Mask being configured, further validation at the database level will be required, in which case the following steps should be performed:

Resolution Overview:
To resolve this issue, the GL Account Mask must be validated and, if missing, updated in the SYS database for the affected company.
Once the Account Mask is correctly populated, the system will allow Statement Content to be created without errors.

Resolution Steps:
Step 1: Identify Companies with Missing GL Account Mask:
Run the following query to review the list of companies and verify whether the GlAcctMask value is populated:
SELECT TOP (1000)
[CompId],
[Name],
[GlAcctMask]
FROM [SYS].[dbo].[tblSmCompInfo];
Review the results and identify the new company where the GlAcctMask column is NULL. [In this example, for the Company 'TST', the value is NULL]


Step 2: Update the GL Account Mask for the Affected Company
If the GlAcctMask value is found to be NULL for the new company, update it using the following query (replace the Company ID and mask value as appropriate):
UPDATE [SYS].[dbo].[tblSmCompInfo]
SET GlAcctMask = '0000-00'
WHERE CompID = 'XXX';
Note: The account mask value used in this update must match the format defined for the other working company's Account Mask, and the Company ID should match the required Company ID (For example, KTD).


Post-Update Validation:
After updating the GlAcctMask value:
i. Log back into the application.
ii. Navigate to the Statement Content setup.
iii. Attempt to create the Statement Content again.
The error “Company ID is required” should no longer occur.


Important Notes on Account Mask Configuration:
- The GL Account Mask is a one-time setup. It is configured through the application under the following path: General Ledger -> Setup and Maintenance -> Account Mask
- Once defined, the Account Mask cannot be undone or modified through the UI.
- Even if the Account Mask appears to be configured in the application, a missing or NULL value at the database level (tblSmCompInfo.GlAcctMask) can still cause validation errors such as this one.
- In that instance, we need to make the changes through the SQL tables

f92a7d0b-36a4-416b-9211-871fe02d4b8f.title: FED__FUT percentage is not pulled in correctly
f92a7d0b-36a4-416b-9211-871fe02d4b8f.content:
Problem
During payroll processing for Payroll Year 2026, Federal Unemployment Tax (FUTA) was not being calculated as expected for employees associated with New York. Upon review, it was observed that FUTA wages and tax amounts were either missing or calculated at a zero rate, despite no known change in federal FUTA requirements for the year.

This caused concerns around underpayment of FUTA and potential compliance risk if not corrected in a timely manner.

Resolution
Root cause:
Traverse determines the applicable FUTA rate using the FED__FUT formula table unless a state-specific FUTA override table exists.
In this case, a state-specific formula table for New York FUTA Credit Reduction (FEDNYFUT)  was present and taking precedence over the standard FED__FUT table. This New York–specific entry was configured with a 0% rate, which resulted in FUTA not being calculated.
This type of entry is typically introduced when a state temporarily assumes FUTA liability (as some states did during COVID-related relief periods). However, this entry remained active even though it was no longer applicable for 2026, causing the incorrect calculation.

Resolution
To resolve the issue and restore correct FUTA calculation:
i. The New York FUTA Credit Reduction formula table entry was reviewed and identified as the overriding table being applied instead of FED__FUT.

ii. The entry was updated to align with the standard federal FUTA configuration by setting:
- Rate: 0.6%
- Wage Limit: $7,000

iii. Alternatively, the state-specific FUTA override entry could be removed entirely, allowing Traverse to default back to the FED__FUT table.

iv. In this case, the state specific table FEDNYFUT (with 0.0000) overrode the default FED__FUT one.

v. Once updated, FUTA calculations resumed correctly for subsequent payrolls.

The issue was caused by an outdated New York FUTA Credit Reduction (FEDNYFUT) formula table overriding the standard FED__FUT configuration. Updating or removing the override restored correct FUTA calculation and ensured ongoing compliance for Payroll Year 2026.

72316552-4950-45af-be4b-c48fb3c09914.title: Traverse Global - WMS Mobile Error 500.19
72316552-4950-45af-be4b-c48fb3c09914.content:
Problem
WMS Mobile users are unable to access WMS. When attempting to log in, they receive the message:

Cause
Per design, WMS Mobile adds the necessary handlers via the "Web.config" file. IIS has the same handlers manually set up which creates duplicates of the handlers.
For WMS Mobile, adding the handlers in IIS is not required and is not part of typical implementations.
If duplicated, this causes a conflict running WMS Mobile.

To check for the duplicate entries, verify the name of the handlers in the error, then check if this is set up in IIS already.

Access IIS on the Web server and click on Handler Mappings:

With this error example, we are looking for ASPxUploadProgressHttpHandler and ASPxHttpHandlerModule.

They both exist in IIS' Handler Mappings:

In WMS Mobile's "Web.config" file, we can see this file also adds the handlers which is part of the design:

Resolution
This was resolved by technical IT resources.
The user had these handlers already set up in IIS, and it was determined they needed to maintain that setup.
A modified "Web.config" file was provided that replaces the handlers when WMS is accessed. Once in place, users can access WMS again.

29a45e44-0851-4649-bb9b-5b814aece6ec.title: Traverse Global - MFG Production Scheduling - Work Center Hours
29a45e44-0851-4649-bb9b-5b814aece6ec.content:
Problem
The problem discussed in this article is that Production Orders seem to schedule for times when the work centers are closed.

If we drill into an example order, we can see it is planned to start on the 10th, which is a Saturday on this calendar.

Resolution
To resolve this, let's look at the schedule:

Right away, we can see that instead of setting closed hours, the schedule is actually completely open on Saturday and Sunday.

In order to set a day as closed, it must have a start and finish date of 00:00. Let's make this change for both days and save.

Drill back into the line on the schedule and click Recalculate:

We'll now see the estimated start date pulled to January 7th instead of the 10th.

NOTE: Depending on existing production planning, this could have been moved forward or backwards or stretched out even more depending on timing.

If we save and close this window, we'll also see the calendar reflect the change for that row.

NOTES:

f4c7a8dd-cd1b-472d-b787-3c86cf9a0dc0.title: How to include/exclude Line Item entries with 'Zero' shipped Quantities from appearing on SO Invoice?
f4c7a8dd-cd1b-472d-b787-3c86cf9a0dc0.content:
Problem
How to include/exclude Line Item entries with 'Zero' shipped Quantities from appearing on SO Invoice?

Resolution
Printing Zero Shipped Line Items in Sales Orders (SO):
Prerequisites: This functionality to remove the 'Zero Shipped Line Items' is available only for Users using Build 25199 or later.

Starting from Build 25199, a new Sales Order (SO) Business Rule “Print Zero Shipped Line Item”, and a 'Print Zero Shipped Line Item' option during invoice printing has been introduced.
- When the Business Rule it is set to “No”: Line items with zero shipped quantity will default to not printing on the invoice.
- This rule applies to both:- Printing invoices from current orders (online and batch).
- Printing invoices from history.

- This setting will not have any impact on the Accounts Receivable (AR) Invoice.

Note:
- This rule does not affect quotes — zero shipped items will still appear on quotes.
- If an SO order has no line items to print (and no taxable, non-taxable, tax adjustment, freight, or miscellaneous charges), a “Nothing to process” message will be displayed.
- An invoice should not be posted to open invoices if it does not have any line items to print or any applicable charges.

Navigation Path:
To configure this setting, the User needs to follow the steps below:
- Go to Applications -> System Manager -> Company Setup -> Business Rules.
- Under Applications, select SO – Sales Order.
- In the Miscellaneous section, locate the Print Zero Shipped Line Item setting.

A. Include Zero shipped Items:
i. If the User wants the 'Zero Shipped Line Items' to be selected by default when printing SO Invoices, the User needs to set 'Print Zero Shipped Line Item' setting to 'Yes'.
ii. Once set, hit on 'Apply' and 'OK' to save the changes.

iii. Let's consider the below example of 2 Line Items entries, where one of the Line Items is partially shipped, while the other Line Item is not shipped at all.

iv. The SO Invoice will include the 'Zero shipped Line Item' entry (example below).

B. Exclude Zero shipped Items:
i. If the User does not want the 'Zero Shipped Line Items' to be selected by default when printing SO Invoices, the User needs to set 'Print Zero Shipped Line Item' setting to 'No'.
ii. Once set, hit on 'Apply' and 'OK' to save the changes.

iii. Let's consider the below example of 2 Line Items entries, where one of the Line Items is partially shipped, while the other Line Item is not shipped at all.

iv. The SO Invoice will not include the 'Zero shipped Line Item' entry (example below).

Additional Clarification on Printing Behavior:
While the “Print Zero Shipped Line Item” Business Rule controls the default behavior for whether zero shipped line items are included on Sales Order invoices, this setting is not enforced at the time of printing.

At the time of printing Sales Order invoices:
- Batch printing: When batch printing from SO -> Transaction Journals -> Print Invoices, and
- Online Printing: When printing invoices directly from an SO Orders screen
The User is still provided with the “Print Zero Shipped Line Items” print option and may manually choose to include or exclude zero shipped line items, regardless of how the Business Rule is configured. This allows flexibility for Users to adjust the output on a per-print basis while using the Business Rule as the system default.
