3c976383-7704-4d2b-aa66-534226e09187.title: Microsoft SQL Instance Collations - Traverse Global
3c976383-7704-4d2b-aa66-534226e09187.content:
Problem
A SQL error is encountered indicating a conflict with SQL's collation:

Cause
The data currently loaded comes from a SQL instance of a different collation. Depending on what data is present and what process is occurring in the software, there can be a conflict in a mismatched collation.

Resolution
A new SQL instance with the necessary collation is required. In this example, the expectation is that the instance collation is Latin1_General_CI_AS.
We can create a new SQL instance with this collation, allowing us to process and continue our investigation.

In the install process, the dialogue window will open to SQL Collations by default, and if you look through the list, you might not see what you are looking for.

In the past there was one list of possible choices users would need to navigate. In our example, we want to create the instance as Latin1_General_CI_AS which is not here.
There are now two choices at this screen: Windows Collation and SQL Collation.

If we toggle Windows Collation we are now able to pick what we need:

Once we click through this we can finish the install process, restore our backups and continue our work without error.

97c9e600-115a-48d9-a6d8-072e6a713d29.title: How to Write Off Unpaid Invoices and Finance Charges to Remove Them from AR Open Invoices and Statements?
97c9e600-115a-48d9-a6d8-072e6a713d29.content:
Problem
How to Write Off Unpaid Invoices and Finance Charges to Remove Them from AR Open Invoices?



In certain business scenarios, invoices or finance charges remain unpaid for an extended period and are determined to be uncollectible or no longer valid for recovery. These outstanding amounts continue to appear in Accounts Receivable (AR) Open Invoices, which can impact ageing reports, customer statements, financial accuracy, and customer account clarity.



Users often encounter challenges in determining the correct and compliant method to write off unpaid invoices or finance charges in the system so that they are properly removed from the AR open balance without causing discrepancies in financial reporting. Improper handling may result in inaccurate AR balances, overstated receivables, or audit concerns.



This document outlines the correct process for writing off unpaid invoices and finance charges, ensuring they are appropriately cleared from AR Open Invoices and AR Statements while maintaining accurate General Ledger and financial records.

Resolution
Write Off Using a “Write-Off” Payment Method (Best for Operational Simplicity)
This method marks the finance charge invoice as paid using a write-off payment type.
Step A: Create a Write-Off Payment Method (One-Time Setup)
- Navigate to:- Accounts Receivable → Setup and Maintenance → Payment Method IDs

- Create a new Payment Method ID, for example:- Payment Method ID: BADDEBT
- Description: Bad Debt Write-Off
- Set Payment Type to Write Off.
- Assign the appropriate General Ledger account for bad debt or write-offs.

- Save the Payment Method.


Step B: Apply the Write-Off to Finance Charges
i. Navigate to: Accounts Receivable → Transactions → Cash Receipts
ii. Select the customer.
iii. Choose the Write-Off Payment Method created above.
iv. Apply the payment to the finance charge invoice.

v. Print the Cash Receipts Journal from Accounts Receivable -> Transaction Journals -> Cash Receipts Journal:

vi. In Accounts Receivable -> Transactions Journals -> Post Cash Receipts, Post the 'Cash Receipts':

vii. Review the results:
A. Traverse 11.0: Once the Finance charges were written off, it would be removed in the 'AR Hold/Release Invoices' screen, and only the remaining Invoices will be available:

B. Traverse Global 11.2: Here the remaining steps to continue remain the same. However, in order to remove paid invoices from the AR Hold/Release Invoices screen, it is necessary to run AR Periodic Maintenance.
- Please navigate to the following path to perform this action: Accounts Receivable -> Periodic Processing -> Periodic Maintenance
- Once the general Periodic Maintenance process has been completed successfully, the paid invoice entries should be cleared and will no longer appear in the AR Hold/Release Invoices screen.


Result:
- Finance charge invoice is marked as paid
- Invoice is cleared from Open Invoices
- Amount is posted to the designated write-off GL account

078244ec-43bd-4f66-bf76-21d9c119b3e5.title: Document Archive Enabled but No Documents Visible in 'SM Manage Documents' – Configuration Correction Required
078244ec-43bd-4f66-bf76-21d9c119b3e5.content:
Problem
The customer reported that the Document Archive feature is enabled for both Accounts Payable (AP) and System Manager (SM). However, when navigating to the SM Document Archive screen, no documents are displayed.


Despite confirming that the corresponding Business Rules for AP-Accounts Payable module shows the Use Archive option as enabled, the SM Manage Documents remains empty, and no documents are being saved to the archive.

Upon verification, the “Use Archive” option was set to Yes within the TPS Settings of the System Manager Business Rules.

Resolution
Resolution:
i. Verify that the 'Use Archive' rule within the Archive section was turned on (set to 'Yes') in the Business Rules for the desired Application(s). In this example, it is 'AP-Accounts Payable':

ii. A. Verify that the 'Enable Document Archiving' rule is set to 'Yes" in the Business Rules for the 'SM-System Manager' in the 'Miscellaneous' section. This setting acts as the master switch to turn on Document Archiving functionality system wide. If this option was not enabled, toggle it to 'Yes' and save the change by selecting the 'Apply' button.
[Within the 'TPS Settings' of 'SM-System Manager' Business Rules, the 'Use Archive' is specific for enabling the document archive feature when it comes to archiving TPS Receipts when processing Credit Card charges using the Traverse Payment System.]

ii. B. Alternatively, the 'SM-System Manager' "Enable Document Archiving" rule may also be configured under the 'Configuration Group' section as well within Business Rules. To navigate to these rules, expand the Configuration Group section housed within Business Rules, under the Application section. Next select the 'Archive' option to see the different Archiving options across all available applications:

If it was identified that the "Miscellaneous" 'System Manager' rule is not enabled (set to Yes), it will need to be changed to 'Yes' to enable Document Archiving. After the System Manager rule has been set to 'Yes', individual applications should be able to enabled or disabled within this Configuration Group - Archive section as well. To save the changes select 'Apply' and 'OK'.

Note: Depending on the Build and Version of your Traverse environment, when toggling the SM - System Manager business rule 'Enable Document Archiving', or the Archive Configuration Group, 'Miscellaneous - System Manger' to "No" to disable document archive, Traverse may also automatically revert all the individual Applications 'Use Archive' Business Rule to "No" as well. So if it is determined that Document Archiving needs to be re-enabled after this has taken place, the SM Business Rule for 'Enable Document Archiving' (or the Archive Configuration Group, 'Miscellaneous - System Manger') will need to be set to "Yes", followed by enabling the individual applicable applications 'Use Archive' business rules.

Outcome:
- After enabling Document Archive under Configuration, the system successfully archived newly generated documents. The Document Archive screen now displays the archived documents as expected.
- All documents created going forward will be properly stored and accessible for future reference.

df67bf5d-4131-447c-b47c-47e2517aed8c.title: Why do the 'Cleared Transactions' in the Bank Reconciliation are still appearing as 'Outstanding' in Reconciliation Report?
df67bf5d-4131-447c-b47c-47e2517aed8c.content:
Problem
The Client has encountered an issue in Traverse involving several transactions for a specific bank account.

In the 'BR Cleared Transactions' screen, these transactions are marked as cleared. However, in the tblBrMaster table, they do not have a StatementID assigned.

As a result, these transactions are incorrectly appearing as outstanding in the Reconciliation Report for June 2025, despite being cleared in the UI.

Resolution
Issue Description:
In the Traverse application, when we utilize the ‘Toggle’ icon to select entries for clearing within a Bank Reconciliation (BR) Statement, and then clear those entries, the selected entries appear as cleared in the Traverse user interface. As a result, those entries no longer appear on subsequent BR Statements.

Report Discrepancy Observed:
Despite the entries being cleared in the UI, when generating the BR Reconciliation Report, these same entries are still displayed as ‘Outstanding’. This discrepancy causes the bank reconciliation balance to be inaccurate, as the cleared entries continue to appear in the report.

Root Cause Analysis:
Upon further review of the backend data in the SQL tblBrMaster table, we observed the following behavior:
- The entries in question are marked as not cleared, despite having been assigned a valid Statement ID.
- Although the UI reflected that the entries were cleared, the database record did not update the clearing status correctly.
This mismatch between the UI and the database caused the entries to reappear as outstanding in the report, creating inconsistencies between the application view and the reconciliation report.

SQL tblBrMaster table:
The Column 'ClearedYn' being equal to '0' represents that the entries were not cleared with specific to the SQL tables.

Reconciliation Report generated from Traverse:

Reason for Behavior:
The issue is directly related to the use of the ‘Toggle’ icon for selecting or deselecting entries during the clearing process. When this toggle mechanism is used, the clearing status does not update as expected at the database level, even though the UI shows them as cleared.

Resolution:
This behavior has been identified as a Bug and was addressed under Change Request: DEV-291744.

https://dev.azure.com/TraverseERP/b746159b-5617-4616-8466-ae9d6a61d66f/_workitems/edit/99986

This has been resolved in the Build 25353 (Service Pack 7 of 2025)

Workaround:
As a temporary workaround, we suggest unclearing the entries in Traverse and then re-clearing them in the appropriate statement by manually selecting each entry, rather than using the Toggle option.

fdfa7c81-f453-48cf-baf1-dd8655656777.title: Error "Insufficient disk space in filegroup 'PRIMARY'. Create the necessary space by dropping objects in the filegroup, or setting autogrowth on for existing files in the filegroup."
fdfa7c81-f453-48cf-baf1-dd8655656777.content:
Problem
When trying to Post production Activity, getting error "Insufficient disk space in filegroup 'PRIMARY'. Create the necessary space by dropping objects in the filegroup, or setting autogrowth on for existing files in the filegroup."

Resolution
Check disk free space
- Ensure the drive hosting the SQL data files has sufficient free space
- Minimum recommendation: 10–20% free disk space
In SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS):
- Right-click database TNK → Properties
- Go to Files
- Select the PRIMARY data file (.mdf)
- Ensure:
- Autogrowth = Enabled
- Growth is set to a fixed MB size (e.g., 512 MB or 1 GB)
- Max size is not restricted (or increased appropriately)

3b031cc3-2541-49a7-9b47-7d6205fc2599.title: Unable to delete a Transaction Allocation
3b031cc3-2541-49a7-9b47-7d6205fc2599.content:
Problem
When the User attempted to delete a specific Transaction Allocation ID, Traverse threw an error stating that the record could not be deleted from the system.

The system continued to prevent deletion, throwing the below error:


Detailed Error Message:
===================================

Current record cannot be deleted.

===================================

Current record cannot be deleted. (TRAVERSE.Controls)

------------------------------
Program Location:

at TRAVERSE.Client.PluginControlBase.DeleteRow()
at TRAVERSE.Controls.TravNavigator.OnDelete(TravNavigatorEventArgs e)

This required a detailed review to identify any dependencies preventing the deletion and to ensure that the allocation was not being referenced within other master or transactional records.

Resolution
The Transaction Allocation ID under review continued to be mapped to multiple vendor records within the system. When an Allocation ID is still actively referenced by vendor profiles, the system is designed to prevent its deletion. This safeguard exists to maintain data integrity and to avoid issues such as incorrect allocation-based reporting, disrupted historical transaction references, or inconsistencies within vendor-level configuration.
To successfully delete an Allocation ID, it is essential that we first ensure the allocation is no longer tied to any vendor or dependent record.

Steps to be followed to resolve the issue:
i. Identify All Vendor Records Linked to the Allocation ID:
Before attempting deletion, we must locate every vendor record that is still associated with the Allocation ID. This is a mandatory step, as removing the allocation from all linked records is required before the system will allow deletion.

The Vendor Detail List is the appropriate area to identify these dependencies.
[NOTE: While this list is not interactive like an Interactive View, and therefore does not allow direct filtering on Allocation ID, it still provides all relevant details needed for this task.]

a. For generating the 'Vendor Detail List', navigate to the 'AP Vendor Detail List' under the path: Applications -> Accounts Payable -> Master Lists -> Vendor Detail List.
b. Generate a report without any filters to include all the records

ii. Generate and Review the Vendor Detail List:
To proceed:
- Generate the complete Vendor Detail List from the system. We can use either 'Output' or 'Preview' option here
- Open the generated report using a PDF viewer.
- Use the search function within the PDF viewer to look for the Allocation ID as a keyword.
- The search results will highlight all vendor records that currently reference the Allocation ID in question.
- We need to make note of all the 'Vendor IDs' associated with this 'Transaction Allocation ID'
This method ensures that we obtain a full and accurate list of dependencies.

Output:

Preview:

iii. Remove or Update the Allocation ID in Vendor Records:
Once the associated vendor records have been identified, we must update those records accordingly:
a. Navigate to the AP Vendors screen using the path: Applications → Accounts Payable → Setup and Maintenance → Vendors


b. Locate each vendor record that was found through the Vendor Detail List search.


c. Navigate to the 'Defaults' Tab and remove the Allocation ID that needs to be deleted.
- If required, replace it with a new Allocation ID.


d. Click on Save to apply the changes.


This process must be repeated for every vendor record that is tied to the Allocation ID.



iv. Proceed with Deleting the Allocation ID:
After all associated vendor records have been updated and the Allocation ID is no longer referenced anywhere in the system, deletion can be performed without any restrictions or errors. At this stage, the system will allow the removal of the Allocation ID because all dependencies have been cleared.

This can be done under the 'GL Transaction Allocations' screen under the path: Applications -> General Ledger -> Setup and Maintenance -> Transaction Allocations:

364ed0a4-f046-4b54-a8cb-d787f07e0aba.title: Configuring Email Attachments to Display Invoice Number in Traverse
364ed0a4-f046-4b54-a8cb-d787f07e0aba.content:
Problem
The customer has requested the ability to automatically include the Invoice Number in the file name of PDF attachments generated when emailing invoices through Traverse. At present, when an invoice is sent via the system’s built-in email functionality, Traverse generates a default file name for the attachment, which does not contain any invoice-specific identifiers. This results in file names that are generic and do not provide immediate clarity for either the sender or the recipient.

Resolution
Configuring the Invoice Number in the Email Attachment File Name:

Traverse provides the ability to customize the file name of documents sent through email by allowing the use of both static text and dynamic fields. This configuration can be performed in the SM Document Settings screen.

Navigation Path: Applications -> System Manager -> Document Delivery -> Document Settings





Defining the Document File Name:

Locate the required 'Form ID', for which the 'File Name' of the attachment needs to be updated. In this case, it would be 'SO Invoice'. Within the 'SM Document Settings' screen, users can define how the attached document should be named when it is emailed from Traverse.

In the Document Name field, users may specify the desired file naming format. This field supports:

-
Static text (e.g., “Invoice”)

-
Dynamic fields such as Invoice Number, which automatically populate based on the document being processed

If a custom document name is not defined, Traverse will automatically assign a default system-generated file name.



Adding the Invoice Number:

To include the Invoice Number in the email attachment name, the user can insert the dynamic field directly into the Document Name section. For example:

Invoice [Invoice Number]



When an invoice is emailed, the system will replace the dynamic value with the actual invoice number.
For instance, if the invoice number is 186, the file name will appear as:

Invoice 186.pdf



This ensures clarity and easy identification for both the sender and the recipient.

Additional Notes:

-
The Invoice Number field is a dynamic merge field and can be used not only in the file name, but also in the email Subject, email Body, or Attachment Header, depending on the requirement.

-
This configuration helps simplify document tracking, improves naming consistency, and reduces the need for manual renaming.

d8ffa491-e39f-47b9-ba25-58a8ae1081c4.title: How to resolve the error "Employee ID is not in File" while creating Manual Checks?
d8ffa491-e39f-47b9-ba25-58a8ae1081c4.content:
Problem
How to resolve the error "Employee ID Not in File" while creating Manual Checks?

Resolution
When a User has completed the ‘Calculate Checks’ process and proceeds to review the Edit Register, there may be instances where the User wishes to make modifications to an existing check or add a new check altogether. This could occur if an adjustment needs to be made to a check already listed in the register or if there is a requirement to include a check for an employee who was not part of the original check calculation.



In the current example, we have 10 Checks calculated for 10 employees at the moment:



When the User navigates to the PA Manual Checks screen and attempts to retrieve the Employee ID for an employee who was not included in the initial check register, Traverse will display an error message indicating that the selected employee is not part of the current check run.



To resolve this issue, the User simply needs to click on the ‘New’ icon to create a new record within the existing Pay Check Run. Once we hit on 'New', we can see that the total number of Check records is increased by one.



After confirming the addition, the User may proceed to add the employee’s pay information, complete the necessary check details, and then save the Manual Check.



Once the new record has been created, the User can verify this by reviewing the Edit Register to ensure the new entry is reflected correctly.



Following this, the checks can be printed and subsequently posted as part of the regular payroll process.

8a9692cb-b6d8-4d7b-ac3d-1232a7ae90e6.title: Why does the 'Financial Statement' totals in Excel not aligning with the totals on the Traverse reports?
8a9692cb-b6d8-4d7b-ac3d-1232a7ae90e6.content:
Problem
The customer has reported a discrepancy between the totals displayed on the Traverse Financial Statement report and the totals calculated in Microsoft Excel after exporting the same data.



Specifically, when the customer uses Excel’s AutoSum feature on the exported financial data, the resulting total does not match the total value shown directly within the Traverse report.



While Traverse displays a consistent and expected total based on the underlying financial records, Excel is returning a different total when AutoSum is applied. The customer is seeking clarification on why these two totals do not align and whether this difference is related to how the data is being calculated, formatted, or interpreted in Excel versus Traverse.



Further investigation is required to determine whether the discrepancy is caused by Excel formatting, data type recognition (such as numeric values stored as text), or differences in calculation logic between Traverse and Excel.

Resolution
The discrepancy between the totals displayed in the Traverse Financial Statement report and the totals calculated in Microsoft Excel was reviewed and traced to a data formatting issue within Excel.



Upon analysis, it was identified that certain negative values in the exported Excel file were formatted as text rather than numeric values. Because of this, Excel’s AutoSum function did not recognize those entries as valid numbers and excluded them from the calculation, resulting in totals that did not align with the figures shown in Traverse.



Traverse calculates totals based on the underlying numeric data stored in the system, which is why the totals displayed within the application were accurate. To resolve the discrepancy in Excel, the text-formatted values must first be converted to numeric format (for example, by using Text to Columns or reformatting the cells as General/Number). Once the values are converted to numbers, the AutoSum function works as expected and the totals in Excel align correctly with the Traverse report.



Let us consider the example here, where the expected value is $175007.24, however, Traverse shows $199138.17 (excluding the negative entry considering it as Text)



Steps to Convert Text-Formatted Numbers to Numeric Values in Excel

Method 1: Using Text to Columns (Recommended)

- Open the Excel file containing the exported financial data.
- Select the entire column that contains the values (including the negative numbers).
- Go to the Data tab on the Excel ribbon.
- Click Text to Columns.
- In the wizard, select Delimited, then click Next.
- Click Next again (no delimiter selection required).
- Under Column Data Format, select General.
- Click Finish.

Output:





Method 2: Convert Text to Numbers:

Cells that are formatted as Text can be identified by a small green triangle indicator appearing in the upper-left corner of the cell, as shown below. This indicator signals that Excel is treating the value as text rather than as a numeric value.



To correct this, click on the warning icon that appears next to the selected cell. From the available options, choose Convert to Number.

Once converted, the value will be recognized as a numeric entry, allowing Excel functions such as AutoSum to calculate totals correctly.



If there are additional entries formatted as text, we can sort the list to group those entries together and convert them accordingly.



Once this is done, using the AutoSum function should reflect the calculations accurately, and the arithmetic operations will be performed as expected.

bbd89a3e-70c8-4928-9485-9b9330293e1c.title: Unlocking a Locked Transaction Batch
bbd89a3e-70c8-4928-9485-9b9330293e1c.content:
Problem
When attempting to edit a transaction, print a report, or post transactions a message may appear stating that a transaction is currently in use or that the batch is in use or locked. This KB article describes the steps to unlock the batch.

Transaction lock
If you are trying to edit a transaction, you may receive the following error:


If you are trying to run a report, you will get the following error instead:

Resolution
Traverse uses Batch Codes for record processing. These batches allow multiple users to work in the same module at the same time, without having other users actions affecting others that are using that module. The batches may also be used to “separate” transactions into different “categories” so that you can enter and post at different times. It is possible to have an entire batch locked, or transactions within a batch locked via an Activity Lock.

Clear Transaction Locks View
To see a full list of Transaction locks, users can access the SM Clear Transaction Locks View in System Manager > Administration. This view will contain all real-time activity records. Alternately, activity can be found in the batch's activity, discussed in the next section below.

Apply any desired filtering and then click Apply Filter to see any current transaction locks. If you wish to remove the lock, click the box in the transaction's corresponding Select column and then click Unlock at the top.

NOTE: If a workstation session is terminated or application crash occurs, it is possible transactions are now stuck in a locked status. This view will provide these transactions, but there may also be legitimate transactions users are currently working in. If there is a transaction you wish to access, confirm with the user that they are no longer in it. If the transaction is unlocked and a user is still in the transaction you risk losing any unsaved work.

Alternate Method of Unlocking:
- To Unlock the record, follow the steps below:
- Go into the module (Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, etc.)
- Choose Setup and Maintenance
- Select Transaction Batch Codes program
- Once you access the Batch Codes screen, you will see all batches that have been created each on its own separate row. Find the row with the batch that is locked, or with the batch that contains the transaction that is locked.
- Verify that the columns for Lock Date and Lock By are blank on that row. If they are not, click the Lock button just to the left of these columns to toggle off the lock. This may unlock the batch. If it doesn’t, proceed to the next step.
- select the Activity Button () next to the batch with the locked record.

- This will open the Bath Activity dialog box.

- You will see the record that is locked in this dialog box. To delete the lock, you highlight the record as shown above. You then click the Delete button (). This will delete the lock without affecting the transaction.
- Close the Batch Activity and Batch Codes screen.
- You have successfully unlocked the transaction and are able to continue processing in Traverse.

6bf220c6-af8c-44b4-a8a5-d5ad6c0878f2.title: Freeze Quantities in Physical Inventory
6bf220c6-af8c-44b4-a8a5-d5ad6c0878f2.content:
Problem
How to Use the Freeze Quantities functionality in Physical Inventory?

Resolution
Purpose: The Physical Inventory process ensures your inventory records match the actual stock on hand. A key part of this process is the Freeze Quantities function, which locks the current on-hand quantities before counting. This helps prevent discrepancies and ensures accurate inventory tracking.

What is Freeze Quantities? The Freeze Quantities function allows you to create a batch for a physical inventory count and lock the quantities of items at a specific point in time. This ensures that the numbers you count reflect the actual stock levels.
Important: Make all necessary item adjustments before freezing quantities.
Note: An item cannot be included in multiple batches for the same location. Attempting this will generate a warning/error.

Step-by-Step Guide to Freezing Quantities:
- Filter Items: Use the data filter to select items for the batch. Leaving it blank will include all items.

- Choose a Batch Code: Pick an existing batch or create a new one with a unique code.

- Enter a Description: Provide a name or description for the batch.

- Select Location: Specify a location to include, or leave blank for all locations.

- Set Count Date: Indicate the date for the inventory count.

- Assign User: Optionally, assign a user to perform the count.

- Select Bins: Choose bins for counting. Use Select All for all bins or Unselect All to clear selections.

- Add Notes: Include any relevant information about the batch.



Batch Actions / Command Buttons:
Batch Actions:
- Freeze: Locks current on-hand quantities for all items in the batch. For a new batch, this also saves and prepares it.

- Prepare: Prepares the batch and creates the records needed for counting.

- Assign: Assigns a user to perform the count for this batch.

- View Activity: Displays a log of all actions taken for the batch.


- Reset: Clears all entries and deletes the batch if it has already been saved.



Summary: Using Freeze Quantities ensures accurate physical inventory counts by locking the current stock levels. It helps avoid duplicate items in multiple batches, supports clear assignment of counters, and provides a way to track batch activity. Following this process ensures reliable inventory data and smoother reconciliation.

993b1791-7eab-4124-8833-2b7ee66eba5a.title: How to apply ON ACCOUNT balances to open AR Invoices
993b1791-7eab-4124-8833-2b7ee66eba5a.content:
Problem
Prepayments or Deposits are often entered in Accounts Receivable as Cash Receipts prior to the entry of the invoice they will pay.  The amounts are typically applied to an Invoice Number of ON ACCOUNT, though the actual Invoice Number used can vary depending on how things are set up in the Business Rules.  Later, when the invoice is entered, the payments to ON ACCOUNT need to be moved to the Invoice or Invoices they are meant to pay.

Resolution
To move payment balance from ON ACCOUNT or any other Invoice Number that has a payment balance to offset open Invoice amounts you would use the Splite/Reapply function of the Hold/Release Invoices screen in Accounts Receivable.
- Open Accounts Receivable -> Open Invoices -> Hold/Release Invoices
- When the screen appears, at the top of the screen fill in the Customer ID of the Customer for which you will be reapplying Payment.
- The grid section of the screen will display all open Invoices and Payments.
- In the first column beside the ON ACCOUNT Payment you will be reapplying put a check mark in the box to choose that payment.
- Click the Split/Reapply button at the top of the screen.
- A new AR-Split screen will appear showing the open Invoices, and the Payment that was chosen at the bottom of the list.  The total amount of that payment will initially be displayed on the row of the payment in the Applied Amount column.
- To apply some or all of that payment amount to any of the other open invoices on this screen go to the row of that invoice and fill in the amount you wish to apply to that row's Applied Amount column.  Each time you do this the amount in the Applied Amount column of the payment you chose will decrease by a corresponding amount.
- Repeat this process until either there is no more payment left to apply (the Applied Amount column is zero for the last Payment row) or until you have paid all the Invoices you wish to pay.
- If you wish to automate this process you may press the Auto Apply button at the top of the screen.  This will take the entire payment amount and attempt to apply it to all the open invoices beginning at the top and working its way down until either all invoices are paid or the Payment Amount runs out.
- Change or confirm the Reapply Date, Period, and Fiscal Year on which the reapplication of the Payment will occur.  Then Press to OK button on the top left to reapply the payment.
- A message will appear stating the process is complete once it has finished the reapplication of the payment.  The AR Hold/Release Invoices screen will not show new transactions reapplying the payment to the invoices that were chosen.
- Optionally, to remove any Invoices that were completely paid off and that now have a zero balance you may run the Periodic Maintenance process on the Periodic Processing menu.  When you run Periodic Maintenance, only choose the checkbox to Perform General Periodic Process and nothing else.

0004b3a1-dcb3-4a38-83ec-2209334e77e5.title: Form '<Form ID>' is in use. Warning message received when Printing forms.
0004b3a1-dcb3-4a38-83ec-2209334e77e5.content:
Problem
When a user is attempting to print or output a Form from Traverse, they may receiving a warning message stating: "Form '<Form ID>' is in use." which will not allow the selected form to be printed or outputted.

An example of this warning message is shown below, which is indicates the warning of "Form 'SO PICK' is in use." and the full error detail of this warning message are indicated below.

Warning message Text:
TITLE: Traverse Global
------------------------------

Form 'SO PICK' is in use.

------------------------------
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION:

Form 'SO PICK' is in use. (TRAVERSE.Client.SOPrinting)

------------------------------
BUTTONS:

OK
------------------------------

Technical Details text:
===================================

Form 'SO PICK' is in use.

------------------------------
Edition = Global
Build = 25353
User = user1
LicenseServer = localhost
Culture = English (United States)
DefaultCompID = GLO
SysDb = GLOSYS
SessionID =
MachineName =

===================================

Form 'SO PICK' is in use. (TRAVERSE.Client.SOPrinting)

------------------------------
Program Location:

at TRAVERSE.Report.SalesOrder.PrintPickingSlipsControl.BeforePrint(CancelEventArgs e)

Another variation of this warning message could also be in the form of a red circle with a X in it, shown below. When you hover your mouse pointer over the red X, a message will appear stating: "Form '<Form ID>' is in use by '<User ID>'.".

Cause
The "Form '<Form ID>' is in use" notification message is typically received when another Traverse Global user is in the process of printing or preparing to print the corresponding form. When the Printing function is opened, Traverse Global places a lock on the corresponding Form ID. This is necessary to guarantee proper document number assignment during the printing process.

Another cause of this warning message is if during the printing of the form, the workstation unexpected shut down and didn't properly close Traverse, then the lock on the form may not have been released, causing the need for it to be manually released.

Resolution
Step 1: To navigate to the From ID Lock administration controls go to System Manager -> Company Setup -> Form Numbers:

Step 2: Locate the Form ID that was identified in the "Form is in use." warning message. (For example, see the SO PICK Form ID shown below.)

​​​​​​Step 3:  It is recommended to check with the Traverse Global user listed in the Locked By column to ensure they have completed their printing process for the corresponding form before proceeding with the remaining steps.

Step 4: To manually unlock the Form ID from being in use, uncheck the Locked check box to release the lock for the corresponding Form ID. (For example, see the SO Pick Form ID shown below.)

Step 5: Click the Save button to fully remove the lock.

Note: You can use the same steps to fix all the form in use errors.

56d1bf81-58e2-4135-8502-2e68eeed146e.title: License service restart from License server manager (Traverse - SaaS)

Resolution
KB Article: Resolving “Unable to Connect to Traverse – All Orders Failing” Issue
Overview
This Knowledge Base article outlines the troubleshooting and resolution steps to follow when no users are able to connect to Traverse and all orders are failing, such as in a bookstore environment. This issue is commonly related to Traverse License Server availability rather than server downtime.
Issue Description
The customer reports that:
- No users are able to log in to Traverse
- All order processing has failed
- The server itself is up and running
Initial Verification
Step 1: Check Active User Sessions
- Obtain the customer’s RDS server details from the installation survey.
- Log in to the customer’s RDS server.
- Open Task Manager.
- Navigate to the Users tab.
- Check for any active or disconnected user sessions related to the affected customer.
Observation
- If no active sessions are present for the customer
- And other customers hosted on the same server are able to log in successfully
This confirms the issue is not related to the RDS server or server availability.
Root Cause
When the RDS server is operational and other customers are unaffected, the issue is most likely caused by the Traverse License Server service being unresponsive or stalled for the affected customer.
Resolution Steps
Step 2: Restart Traverse Global License Server
- Open Traverse Global License Server Manager.
- Locate and select the customer’s Profile ID.
- Click the Restart option available in the bottom-left corner of the License Server Manager.
- Allow a few minutes for the license service to restart completely.
Validation
- After restarting the license service, log in to Traverse and verify:
- The application launches successfully
- Orders can be processed normally
- Ask the customer to validate from their end and confirm access is restored.
Customer Communication
- Inform the customer that the issue was related to the Traverse Global License Server.
- Confirm that the license service has been restarted.
- Request them to validate login and order processing.

a723d038-b7c8-4752-b679-3e95108685f0.title: Generating/Previewing a WM Update Perpetual Inventory Journal
a723d038-b7c8-4752-b679-3e95108685f0.content:
Problem
Is there a way to preview or generate a journal that contains all the entries that will take place when the WM Update Perpetual Inventory is performed? In other applications journals are available for review before posting, is there a similar preview or journal option that exists for Physical Inventory updates?

Resolution
Although the Warehouse Management - Physical Inventory module does not have a dedicated journal section like other applications, the ability to preview or generate a journal of the entries before updating perpetual inventory does exist.

Within the Warehouse Management > Physical Inventory > Update Perpetual Inventory screen, there is a Journal function. This Journal functions the same way as journals in other modules by allowing users to review or generate a report of all adjustments and entries that will be posted when the update perpetual inventory performed.

Users can preview or generate this Journal to verify quantities, variances, and adjustments before finalizing the update. This ensures accuracy, provides an audit trail of the entries, and provides visibility into what will be posted.

To review the WM Update Perpetual Inventory Journal perform the following:
Navigate to Warehouse Management > Physical Inventory > Update Perpetual Inventory
- Select the "Do the following, then check the box." checkbox.
- Select the desired batch code(s).
- Select the "Journal" button in the top tool bar options to launch a preview screen of the WM Update Perpetual Inventory Journal.

4e080d5b-c5d2-4f28-8b87-cb2d93101406.title: What is the difference between Open Invoice and Balance Forward Type Account in AR Customers
4e080d5b-c5d2-4f28-8b87-cb2d93101406.content:
Problem
What is the difference between an Open Invoice and a Balance Forward Type Account in Accounts Receivable - Customers?

Resolution
The AR Customers account can be of the following 2 types:
1. Open Invoice Type (most commonly used): the customers have all invoices listed separately on their statement and cash receipts are applied to individual invoices.
2. Balance forward Type: The customers will have all open invoices combined into one open balance invoice when periodic maintenance is run. Cash receipts are applied to a period balance and not individual invoices. Statement balances will be listed as one open invoice balance.

i. This can be changed in the path: Applications -> Accounts Receivable -> Setup and Maintenance -> Customers:


ii. Pull up the required Customer record from the lookups available in the 'Customer ID' field:


iii. Navigate to the Defaults Tab:


iv. There we can find the Field 'Acct Type' corresponding to the account type. We can update the Account Type as needed from the drop-down:
- Open Invoice
- Balance Forward


v. Once it has been updated, click on the 'Save' icon at the top left corner of the screen:



Let's observe how each Balance Type impacts the Customer Statement:
i. Open Invoice:  The customers have all invoices listed separately on their statement and cash receipts are applied to individual invoices.

ii. Balance Forward: The customers will have all open invoices combined into one open balance invoice when periodic maintenance is run. Cash receipts are applied to a period balance and not individual invoices. Statement balances will be listed as one open invoice balance.

37a7c593-8990-4b35-8dd6-aabad96d9759.title: How to unfreeze the quantities frozen in the 'IN Freeze Quantities' screen of Traverse?
37a7c593-8990-4b35-8dd6-aabad96d9759.content:
Problem
How to unfreeze the quantities frozen in the 'IN Freeze Quantities' screen of Traverse?

Resolution
The method to unfreeze quantities differs slightly depending on whether the client is having WM installed or not:
- If WM is installed in Traverse Global Version 11.2, the WM - Physical Inventory - Freeze Quantities provides a Reset option. This feature allows the User to directly revert the freeze applied to a specific Batch without requiring deletion of the Batch. Once the Reset option is used, the frozen quantities are released, and the Batch can be reused as needed.
- However, in Inventory, the Reset functionality is not available. To unfreeze the quantities, the User must delete the existing Batch. Deleting the Batch automatically releases all frozen quantities, making them available for further processing.
To delete a Batch and unfreeze quantities in the Inventory - Physical Inventory feature, the User should perform the following steps:
i. Navigate to the IN Freeze Quantities screen using the following path: Inventory -> Physical Inventory -> Freeze Quantities:


ii. On the screen, select the Batch to be removed and click on the Delete icon located on the top menu bar.


iii. A system prompt will appear requesting confirmation. Click Yes to proceed with the deletion.


Once the Batch is deleted, all frozen quantities are released and become available. The User may then create a new Batch (even with the same name, if preferred) and continue with preparing and freezing the inventory quantities as required.

c98083c2-34d4-432f-86c7-86e6ac57b1eb.title: How to resolve the error 'Current record cannot be deleted' while attempting to delete the 'Batch Code' in 'IN Freeze Quantities'?
c98083c2-34d4-432f-86c7-86e6ac57b1eb.content:
Problem
How to resolve the error 'Current record cannot be deleted' while attempting to delete the 'Batch Code' in 'IN Freeze Quantities'?

Detailed error message:
===================================
Current record cannot be deleted.
===================================
Current record cannot be deleted. (TRAVERSE.Controls)
------------------------------
Program Location:
at TRAVERSE.Client.PluginControlBase.DeleteRow()
at TRAVERSE.Controls.TravNavigator.OnDelete(TravNavigatorEventArgs e)

Resolution
This error generally occurs when the Batch is currently in use by one or more users. For instance, if any user is logged into the IN Physical Counts Entry screen with this Batch active, Traverse identifies the Batch as being in use and prevents its deletion to maintain data integrity.
On the IN Freeze Quantities screen, the Lock Date and Lock By fields indicate the timestamp and the username of the user who currently holds the lock on the Batch.


Resolution:
A. Ensure all users close the relevant screen:
Request the respective User to either log out of the IN Physical Counts Entry screen entirely or navigate away from the specific Batch in question to release the lock.

OR

B. Manual removal of lock (if necessary):
In cases where the lock persists even after the user has logged out, the lock can be manually released using the following steps:
-
-
- Navigate to the IN Freeze Quantities screen using the path:
- Inventory → Physical Inventory → Freeze Quantities
- Locate the Lock icon corresponding to the Batch and click it to release the lock.



Delete the Batch:
Once the lock has been successfully removed, the Batch can be deleted as required without encountering the error.


Note: Always verify that no other users are accessing the Batch before manual intervention to avoid potential data conflicts.

3a80cbd4-ca00-4e15-b8b1-339676585861.title: Disable the prompt - "Copy Kit from History" for SO Transaction Order Entry
3a80cbd4-ca00-4e15-b8b1-339676585861.content:
Problem
The user always uses the current Bill of Materials (BOM) for kit items on sales orders and never copies kit history. However, the system shows a prompt on every order asking whether to copy the kit from history. This adds unnecessary steps and slows down the process. Is there a way to turn off this prompt?

Resolution
To prevent the system from prompting users to copy kit history on each sales order, adjust the following setting in the Bill of Material business rules:
- Navigate to Business Rules and choose the application BM - Bill of Materials/Kitting.
- Locate the setting labeled "Show Kit History Selections in Sales Order Transactions," possibly found under the Miscellaneous section.
- Change the value from Yes to No.
- Select "Apply" to save the changes.
Setting this option to No disables the kit history selection prompt on the Sales Order screen. This ensures that kit components are always sourced directly from the current Bill of Materials (BOM), aligning the system behavior with the user's standard workflow and eliminating unnecessary steps.

3d51dfd2-7d86-4844-8ff3-9e2ad077358c.title: AP Payment History View – Bank Account Number Masking Not aligning with Business Rules Configuration
3d51dfd2-7d86-4844-8ff3-9e2ad077358c.content:
Problem
We identified an inconsistency in the way Bank Account Numbers are displayed within the Accounts Payable module.



n the System Management (SM) module, under Company Setup -> Business Rules, we have configuration options that determine how Bank Account Numbers should be displayed across the application. These settings allow us to choose whether account numbers should appear fully, partially masked, or completely hidden based on organizational policies and data-protection requirements.



Although the masking preference is correctly configured under SM Business Rules, the AP Payment History View does not honor this configuration. In the below example, we can see that the 'Bank Account Display' field is set to 'Partial' [The same criteria work for 'None' as well]



In the AP Payment History View, we can see that the Bank Account Numbers are partially masked:



However, when filters are applied using the Funnel icon, the complete Bank Account Numbers are displayed instead of appearing masked or hidden as defined in the Business Rules.



This behavior is inconsistent with the expected functionality, as the AP Payment History View should adhere to the masking logic defined within Business Rules. The display of full account numbers within a filter interface bypasses the masking settings and results in unintended visibility of sensitive financial data.

Resolution
To address the inconsistency with the Bank Account Number masking behavior in the AP Payment History View, we have submitted the Change Request DEV-302390. This request specifically targets the issue where the system continues to display the full Bank Account Number when filters are applied through the Funnel icon, even though the Business Rule: Bank Account Display is configured to show the number as Partial or None..



The Change Request ensures that the masking logic defined within the Business Rules is consistently enforced across all relevant screens, including the AP Payment History View. Once implemented, this update will align the application behavior with the intended confidentiality controls and prevent unauthorized visibility of sensitive account information.



The issue is observed up until the Build 25304 of Traverse11.2, and the Change request can be found through the below link:

https://dev.azure.com/TraverseERP/b746159b-5617-4616-8466-ae9d6a61d66f/_workitems/edit/101007

8de03ded-0465-457a-b215-af8770fc0233.title: How to restart SQL server in Traverse
8de03ded-0465-457a-b215-af8770fc0233.content:
Problem
How to restart the SQL server from the Server.

Resolution
Method A — SQL Server Configuration Manager (recommended for SQL services)
- Log in to the server with an account that has administrative rights.

- Open SQL Server Configuration Manager:
- Windows 10/Server: Start → type SQL Server Configuration Manager and open it.

- In the left pane choose SQL Server Services.

- In the right pane right-click the service SQL Server (MSSQLSERVER) for the default instance or SQL Server (INSTANCENAME) for a named instance.

- Click Restart.

- Wait until the status shows Running again.

Method B — Services MMC (services.msc)
- Log on to the server as admin.

- Press Win + R, type services.msc, press Enter.

- Find SQL Server (MSSQLSERVER) for the default instance or SQL Server (INSTANCENAME) for named.

- Right-click → Restart (or Stop then Start).

2677f8ef-b8f9-420f-9963-6d7552cd0fb2.title: Time Ticket Journal Missing Required Fields When Project Costing–Payroll Interface Is Turned Off
2677f8ef-b8f9-420f-9963-6d7552cd0fb2.content:
Problem
When using Project Costing without the Payroll Interface enabled, the Time Ticket Journal in the Project Cost module does not display several critical fields needed for validating data entry. The missing fields include:
- Customer ID

- Customer Name

- Project ID

- Task Code

- Rate Code

When the Payroll Interface is enabled, these fields appear correctly. However, with the integration turned off, the printed or previewed Time Ticket Journal does not show this information. This leads to incomplete reporting and makes it difficult for users to verify and track project-related labor costs.
The customer relies on Project Costing without Payroll integration, and therefore cannot view essential project and customer details required for proper validation.

Resolution
This issue has been confirmed as a bug and was logged under:
Bug 100623* CR - Missing Fields in Time Ticket Journal When Payroll Interface is Disabled - 05783130 - DEV-299580
The defect has been fixed in:
Traverse Version 11.2.25304
After updating to this version (or later), all missing fields—Customer ID, Customer Name, Project ID, Task Code, and Rate Code—will display correctly in the Time Ticket Journal even when Payroll Interface integration is turned off.
If the customer is on an earlier version, upgrading is required to resolve the issue.

9ef510c5-ae04-4a77-9dc2-c4642654be32.title: User Unable to Login to Traverse – RDP Port Blocked
9ef510c5-ae04-4a77-9dc2-c4642654be32.content:
Problem
The user was unable to log in and encountered the following error: “Problem connecting to RemoteApp. Error code: 0X3000008.”

Resolution
We've connected with the user, Laura, to review the issue. It appears that her organisational security settings are blocking access to the RDP port, preventing login to Traverse using the downloaded RDP file.

As a workaround, we provided the RDP link to access the web version of the application. This allows her to continue working without interruption. We also informed her that if she wishes to use the RDP file directly, she will need to contact her IT team to allow the RDP port through their security settings.

NOTE: There is no functional difference between the web version and the RDP version of Traverse. However, the RDP version offers some advantages, such as exporting documents locally.

f04793a4-06ac-48ea-8814-d3838512e635.title: How to Determine Group Creation Date?
f04793a4-06ac-48ea-8814-d3838512e635.content:
Problem
The customer wants to determine the creation date of a specific Group in STE Production. Attempts to find this information using the SM Audit Explorer were unsuccessful. The group in question is named “Marketing.” The customer is requesting guidance on whether support can retrieve this information or if there is a process to determine it.

Resolution
We informed the customer that Traverse does not audit group-related activities, and details such as when a group was created, deleted, or modified are not stored on the backend.

However, based on a review of the TSM and STE databases, we observed that GroupId values are assigned sequentially as groups are created. This means:
- A lower GroupId corresponds to an earlier creation.
- For example, GroupId = 1 was the first group created, and subsequent groups follow in order.
This information was shared with the client, allowing them to estimate the approximate creation order and relative age of each group, even though exact timestamps are not available.

9a4ca9d1-98bd-4ba5-8f09-2c94a2b0bf24.title: WMS Login Issue Resolved – License Limit Identified
9a4ca9d1-98bd-4ba5-8f09-2c94a2b0bf24.content:
Problem
The customer reported recurring issues with Warehouse Mobile (WMS) logins, stating they were unable to log in. This was the second occurrence within a week, and they requested a more reliable solution.

Resolution
We reviewed the customer’s account and confirmed that it has 13 user licenses, all of which were in use at the time of the issue. For WMS access, at least one license must be available for the WMS master login, which then allows other Warehouse Mobile users to access the application. When all licenses are occupied, additional login attempts result in the error:

“Login was unsuccessful. Please try again or contact your system administrator.”

What We Did:
- Verified the number of active licenses and confirmed the cause of the login failures.
- Informed the customer that logging out one user would free a license.
- Advised that once a license is available, we can recycle the site to allow a successful WMS login.
What We Recommend:
- To prevent future login issues, increase the number of user licenses.
- The customer’s account manager has been included to assist with licensing options.
Note: The WMS portal consumes only one license for the master login, regardless of the number of Warehouse Mobile users configured.

6a7cf047-e4e0-4e88-a7c8-8f8bc62125eb.title: RDS Server Sporadic Access Error – Active Users Unaffected
6a7cf047-e4e0-4e88-a7c8-8f8bc62125eb.content:
Problem
Some users are experiencing intermittent login failures when trying to access the application. During their login attempts, the system briefly grants access but then immediately logs them out. The issue appears sporadic and may affect multiple users attempting to access the application at the same time.

Resolution
Initially, we need to validate whether the server is accessible internally and confirm that it is up and running.

In this scenario, the server is operational with active users logged in, and not all users are affected. This is not like a full “Agent unavailable” issue where the entire VM goes down and all customers connected to the server are disconnected. Based on our observations, this issue has occurred a few times before, and it does not impact users who are already logged in and working. It only affects new users attempting to access the application when the issue occurs.

Even when attempting to connect internally to the server, the error message shown below is received. This issue occurs sporadically across a few RDS servers at different times of the day. At present, the only known resolution is to restart the server.

If the issue occurs during business hours, we need to assess the number of users impacted. If the impact is significant, leadership approval should be obtained before restarting the VM, as this will disconnect all active users and cause disruption.

If the impact is minimal, the VM restart can be scheduled after business hours, with users informed the next day. This approach resolves the issue while minimizing disruption.

b54e4b02-c06c-406b-b8de-a7324bd5d444.title: Failed to validate certificate the application will not be executed.
b54e4b02-c06c-406b-b8de-a7324bd5d444.content:
Problem
Failed to validate certificate the application will not be executed.

Resolution
If a client is getting "Failed to validate certificate the application will not be executed" then please follow the below steps:

- Add a URL exception in the Java Control Panel, follow these steps:
- Open the Java Control Panel:
- On Windows: Open the Start menu and search for "Control Panel".
- Within the Control Panel, search for "Java" and click on the icon to open the Java Control Panel.
- On Mac: Open "System Preferences". Search for and click on the "Java" icon to open the Java Control Panel.
- Access the Security settings: In the Java Control Panel, select the "Security" tab. Open the Exception Site List: Within the Security tab, click on the "Edit Site List" button. Add a URL to the Exception Site List:
- In the window that opens, click "Add". Enter the URL you want to add as an exception. Make sure to include the correct prefix e.g. (http://tnsrvr:8888). Click "OK" to confirm the URL. Save the changes:
- Once you have added all the URLs you need, click "OK" to close the Exception Site List window.
- Click "OK" again in the Java Control Panel to save all changes.
- Close and restart: Close the Java Control Panel.
- You might need to restart your browser or application for the changes to take effect.
Note: Ensure that the URLs you add as exceptions are trustworthy, as allowing access to non-secure content can pose a risk to your system's security.

If still the issue persists, please follow the below step:(it might be due to the Mismatch in JAVA in the workstation and the server).
- Look the java version in server and the workstation.
- For example, if the Server version was Java 8_171, Workstation JAVA was 8_031, uninstalled the older version of Java in control panel.
- Downloaded the version of java 8_20 for 64 bit in workstation as in server from oracle.com - Java archive.
- After installing java did cross check the java installed
- Open the command prompt or terminal and run the command: java -version - Output JAVA version
- Then try to launch OSAS.

38b6f97c-4213-4dd6-8c9b-9f35662caa97.title: Adding new user in OSAS
38b6f97c-4213-4dd6-8c9b-9f35662caa97.content:
Problem
Customer facing issue to add new user in OSAS

Resolution
Resource manager> Installation & configuration > User > Append

User ID – What is entered here is what the user will need to enter at Login Name - This is label or Identifier
BBj User ID - this is the user ID that will be populated in the EM it is required for BBj validation.
Password – This can be entered when the user is first set up, the user will need to enter this at log in. Once this is done it cannot be changed in this screen. The user will be able to change it at log in. The Administrator can only change this in the EM after the initial creation of the user.
Terminal ID - assign a unique terminal ID for the user make sure you say yes to updating the config.bbx file. The MDI menu requires an entry in the config.bbx.
Archive Control – Archiving can be controled at the user level or the Report level. To set it at the user level enter Always, Prompt or Never. Archive Directories must be set up first.
Archive Path and Archive Share path. - If you wish the archive directories to be unique for this user then enter those paths here.
E-mail Login ID and E-Mail Password – This would only be used if the security on the smtp server, based on the email from address, required that user to have their own email login and password.
Lastly Assign the user a role for each company that you wish them to work in. when finished Choose Done. If this is a new user and the Terminal ID assigned does not exist in the config.bbx file you will get the following verification, choose Yes.

A new user is always assigned the MDI menu There are three options for a solution. Delete the user and start over and make sure to update the config.bbx, Use a text editor and add the alias for the terminal ID to the config.bbx, \osas8\progRM\config.bbx or you can log in as a different user go to preferences enter the terminal ID of the new user and change the menu style.
Roles – This information is held in the OSCODE file, \osas8\data. The Role assigned to a user provides them or denies them access to menu Items. The ADMIN role is created during install. It is assigned to the initial user entered during installation that user also gets assigned the T000 terminal ID. There must always be one user with the ADMIN role. Additional roles can be created and assigned. The set up follows the menu structure. Enter thru the Application ID to get to the main Menu. In the Application ID enter OS to get to the User Functions menu and the Other Commands.

Devices – The file that holds the information for the Devices function is the config.bbx file, \osas8\progRM.  It is a text file and can be edited with a text editor such as notepad or Notepad++.  If the file is changed you must exit OSAS to reread the file. In Devices you can add Printers, Terminal ID’s you can also edit existing ones.  See the User’s Guide RMDOC.
Directories and System Info – Before you exit this function make sure you write your changes. After writing the changes it will close OSAS and you will need to log back in. The Information in this function is held in the OSINFO file \osas8\sysfil. The Paths to data and the programs use relative pathing.  The Utilities and [Other Paths] Use physical drive pathing these must be correct or The File rebuild, Change File size and Maintenance updates will fail.

b3118815-dcd9-479d-9874-0da2a440e22a.title: Upgrade OSAS to the latest build
b3118815-dcd9-479d-9874-0da2a440e22a.content:
Problem
Upgrade OSAS to the latest build

Resolution
RM Install maintenance Updates:
Install Maintenance Updates - Open Systems provides periodic updates to OSAS that contain enhancements and other updates to the software.
Use the Install Maintenance Updates function to install or reinstall these periodic OSAS maintenance updates, which keeps OSAS applications up to date.

Installing updates:
To install updates, you must have access to the Internet, and you must be current on your Software Maintenance subscription with Open Systems. Contact your software provider for more information.
If you have a multiuser system, make sure no one else is logged onto the system.

To install maintenance updates, follow these steps:
1. Select Install Maintenance Updates from the Installation and Configuration menu.
2. After the Install Update Media screen opens up, a Product ID dialog box appears with the product ID used during initial installation in the Product ID field.
Verify the ID and click OK / press Enter to continue.

3. If an update is available, the screen displays a description of the update and the updates build number. Update builds are numbered incrementally, which means newer builds have higher numbers. The Install Update Media screen displays the number of the last update you installed and the date on which it was installed, or “N/A” if you have never installed an update.

Choose Continue if you are in the Text menu, Page Down till the last and then Press continue (C).

4. If the new update build is more recent than the current build on your system.
Install? Will be checked by default (or set to Yes in text mode) and you cannot change it.

If the update is already installed on your system, Install? Will be unchecked (or set to No in text mode). You can toggle Install? If you want to reinstall the update (note that the update function will not reinstall programs and files if they are unchanged).

5. To begin the update process, press Install Updates (I). During the update, the installer will check the application modification folder for programs or files that may conflict with the update. If a conflict exists, a notification box will appear with the path to the log file. You can continue with the update, view the log file, or exit the update process.

6. Once OSAS completes the update installation, it will close and restart at the login screen.

Support Issues

Build mods conflict messages

When this warning screen pops up, Just exit the screen.
A text file is created in the sysfil directory buildxxxxxmodconflicts.txt \osas8\sysfil.

Capture it to send to advanced support, open it to find the mods that are affected. It will also provide the path to the mods.

Compress the modifications directory and capture them for advanced support. Send the mods and the buildmodsconflict.txt to advanced support to have the mods brought up to date.
Once advanced support returns the re-worked mods put them in place and install the maintenance update.  You will still get the message but move past it to install.

Java settings classpath update.jar.  Can’t find the update.jar  In the EM check the BBjServices > Java Settings > Classpath > bbj_default.  If the update.jar classpath entry is missing add it back in.

In the OSAS directory go to the progRM folder of the install and choose the update.jar file.
Then, Click FILE > Save .  Lastly stop and start BBJ services.

There are additional messages that you may encounter when applying updates.  These can have to do with a Product ID and a license serial number not belonging to the same site ID.  The site not being on maintenance or the information not being correct on the update server.  Check the account and make sure both keys are assigned to the customer account and that the account is on maintenance.  The license being checked will be the license being listed in the blmlog.txt.

Invalid user count - The user count in the license is greater than what we have on record.  This is the user count on the OSI feature.  The issue is usually on our end the count is recorded incorrectly.

Note:
Just tagging the setting Install? Back to Yes, will not necessarily give a reinstall of the maintenance.
Hence, It is suggested to clear the maintenance files then Go through the install maintenance updates again.

4f20db34-4134-473a-a0a2-43f78f2ce0a6.title: Managing Print Agents in the Agents Page
4f20db34-4134-473a-a0a2-43f78f2ce0a6.content:
Problem
Purpose: To help users view, search, filter, and manage print agents through the Agents Page.
Overview: The Agents Page lists all connected and disconnected print agents, displaying their operational status, version, and connection metrics.

Resolution
Sections and Functions:
- Connected Agents: Show agents currently online and communicating with the Print Service.

- Disconnected Agents: Display agents that are offline or unresponsive, along with their last connection time.

Visual of a Connected Print Agent
Agent Cards:
- Include Agent Name, Status, Version, and Reconnect count.

- Connected agents with the latest version are selectable for configuration.


Key Elements:
- Radio Button: Selects cards to display only connected agents running the latest version.

- Agent Name: Unique identifier for each agent for easy distinction.

- Status: Shows current operational state:
- Connected: Agent is online and actively communicating with the Aptean Print Service.

- Version: Displays the current print agent version on the machine.

- Reconnects: Number of retry attempts made by the agent.

- Selectable Card: Only connected agents with the latest version can be configured.


Visual of a Disconnected Print Agent

- Print Agent Status: Displays agents that are currently disconnected, along with the time they were disconnected.

- Non-selectable Card: Disconnected agents cannot be selected for configuration, as they are not actively connected to the Aptean Print Service.


Operations
The following operations can be performed on the agent’s information.
Search agents - Agents can be searched easily by typing their names in the search bar. This feature filters and displays matching agents dynamically.
Filter by status - Agents can be filtered by their current operational status connected, disconnected, or all. This helps quickly view agents based on their activity state.
Filter by version - Agents can be filtered based on their running version, including options like all, unsupported versions, 2.00, 1.4.1, 1.4.0, 1.3.0, 1.2.0, 1.1.0, 1.0.1, and 1.0.0. This enables tracking agents by specific agent versions.
Download Latest Installer - Initiates the process to download and install the latest agent version. This ensures all agents stay updated with the newest features
Toggle view - Agents can be toggled between Card View and Table View for flexible display options. This allows users to choose their preferred layout for viewing agent details.

Pagination View: Allows users to move between pages of agent cards, facilitating navigation when many agents are listed.
Dropdown Menu: Enables selection of the number of cards displayed per page, allowing users to customize their view according to preference.
Config Button - Navigates to the configuration page, where users can configure agent settings.

243b5f94-6ded-4e07-8523-0abcc5c14718.title: Job Failed – Unable to Print from Physical Printer
243b5f94-6ded-4e07-8523-0abcc5c14718.content:
Problem
When attempting to print from a physical printer, the queued job fails and displays one or both of the following error messages:
- No print service found.

- Invalid name of PrintService.

Cause
This usually indicates that the system is unable to detect or communicate with the printer service.

Resolution
This issue occurs when the printer network is temporarily unavailable. When the printer network is down, the agent is unable to establish a connection with the printer service. Because of this:
- The agent cannot detect the available printers.

- The agent cannot queue or forward print jobs.

- Any existing jobs remain in a failed or pending state until the network connection is restored.

The failure is not caused by incorrect printer configuration or user error, but by the printer network being inaccessible at the time of the job attempt.
Once the printer network is restored:
- The agent will automatically reconnect to the printer service.

- Previously queued jobs will resume processing.

- The printer will begin receiving print jobs without any additional user action.

No manual reconfiguration is required; the system will recover and resume normal operation once network connectivity to the printer service is re-established.

ad80ca84-529d-48e9-88d5-b2845fb3a2fd.title: How to make GL Manual Entries?
ad80ca84-529d-48e9-88d5-b2845fb3a2fd.content:
Problem
How to make GL Manual Entries?

Resolution
Procedure for Entering Journal Entries in Traverse:

To record manual Journal Entries in the General Ledger (GL), please follow the detailed steps outlined below.

i. Verify the Correct GL Fiscal Year

Before creating any journal entries, confirm that the system is set to the appropriate GL Fiscal Year.

-
If the CPA or accountant is posting entries for prior fiscal years, ensure they switch to the corresponding year before proceeding.

-
If the entry pertains to the current fiscal year, no change is required—the current year can remain as is.

This step is essential to ensure that the transactions are recorded against the correct fiscal period. This can be done under the path: General Ledger -> Periodic Processing -> Change Fiscal Year:



ii. Access the 'GL Transactions' Screen:

Navigate to: General Ledger -> Transactions -> Transactions

This is the primary screen used for entering manual journal entries.



iii. Create a New Journal Entry:

-
Click New on the toolbar to begin entering a new transaction.

-
Batch Code

-
If your system is configured to use transaction batching (via business rules), select an existing batch code or create a new one.

-
Account ID

-
Select or type the GL Account ID to which the transaction will be posted.

-
Description

-
Enter a meaningful description (e.g., “Training Expense Adjustment”).

-
This will print in the Description field on the GL Journal Report.

-
Debit Amount

-
For debit entries, enter the amount in Debit Amt Fgn.

-
Skip this field for credit entries.

-
Credit Amount

-
For credit entries, enter the amount in Credit Amt Fgn.

-
Skip this field for debit entries.

-
Date

-
The system will default to today’s date. Update it if the transaction should be posted to a different date.

-
Period

-
The fiscal period corresponding to the selected date will auto-populate.

-
Adjust the period only if the entry needs to be posted to a different accounting period.

-
Source Code

-
Accept the default M1 for manual entries.

-
For automatically reversing accrual entries, use R1.

-
The source code must begin with M for manual entries.

-
Reference

-
Enter a reference number or identifier. Or we can leave this as blank.

-
This will print in the Reference field on the GL Journal Report.

-
Allocation Option (A)

-
Select this checkbox if the transaction should use account allocation rules defined for the selected GL account.

-
If no allocation record exists, the system will display a warning.

-
Cash Flow Option (C)

-
Select this box if the transaction affects the Cash Flow Statement.

-
Clear it for non–cash flow transactions (e.g., internal corrections).

-
Ensure accuracy—incorrect selection can impact the Cash Flow Statement.

-
Comment

-
Enter a comment describing the purpose or nature of this group of entries.

-
This appears in SM System Audit → Activity, providing traceability.

-
If your business rule requires comments, entries cannot be written until this field is completed.



iv. Completing the Journal Entry:

Continue entering all necessary debit and credit lines until the balance at the bottom of the screen equals zero.

- For entries requiring offsets across multiple accounts, add additional lines as needed.
- The journal cannot be posted until the entry is fully balanced.
- Once everything was added, hit on 'Save' to save the changes.
- If we are ready to write them to journal, hit on the 'Write' icon

Problem
What is the use of 'Group By' field in TRAVERSE Actions?

Resolution
The Group By option allows users to organize and consolidate alert results into a structured set of emails or output files based on a selected field. Instead of sending or generating one large collection of all records, the system intelligently groups related records according to the chosen criterion, ensuring that each recipient receives a clear, concise, and well-organized summary.

For instance, when alerts are grouped by Vendor Class, the system generates one consolidated email or output file per vendor class. Suppose there are three vendor classes—A, B, and C—the recipient will receive or the system will create three separate emails or files, one for each class. Each will include all vendor records belonging to that specific class, providing a complete summary of data within that group. However, if the Group By field is set to Vendor, the system will send or generate individual emails or files for each vendor, as each represents a distinct grouping.

Let us consider the below example, with the 'Group By' field set as the 'Vendor Class', with three Vendor classes namely MFG, HVAC, UTL:

If the output type is configured to send emails, the system generates separate emails based on the selected Group By field. Conversely, if the output is configured to generate output files, the same grouping logic applies—creating either a single consolidated file or multiple individual files, depending on the selected Group By field.

In this example, we have both set up as shown below:

In this case, we have 3 different Vendor Classes, making 3 Output Files and 3 Emails getting sent. And the 'Vendor Class' name will be appended at the end of the file Name that is getting outputted.:

Similarly, when grouping is configured by Sales Rep ID, all customers associated with a particular sales representative are included in a single email or output file. This prevents multiple, repetitive notifications and instead delivers a consolidated summary for each representative, promoting clarity, efficiency, and easier tracking of related records.

5aaab63e-3f9c-41cf-a795-447782749b12.title: Significance of SO Order Acknowledgement
5aaab63e-3f9c-41cf-a795-447782749b12.content:
Problem
What is the significance of SO Order Acknowledgement?

Resolution
A Sales Order (SO) Order Acknowledgement is a formal confirmation sent by the seller to the customer immediately after a sales order is created. It serves as an official communication that the order has been received, reviewed, and accepted for processing. This document plays a crucial role in ensuring transparency, accuracy, and alignment between the seller and the customer before any picking, packing, or shipping activities begin.

Order Acknowledgements are typically generated before any order fulfillment activities. They are printed or sent:
- After the Sales Order is created.
- Before the Sales Order is picked, verified, or invoiced.

The primary purpose of an Order Acknowledgement is to:
- Confirm receipt of the customer’s order.
- Provide detailed visibility into the items ordered.
- Ensure both parties agree on the order’s terms before fulfillment.
- Prevent miscommunication related to product quantities, pricing, delivery dates, and other key details.
By sharing this confirmation early in the order lifecycle, the seller helps avoid downstream issues that could impact fulfillment accuracy.

System Behavior & Constraints:
In Traverse:
- Order Acknowledgements are designed to print only for orders in NEW status.
- Once the Sales Order moves into picked, verified, or invoiced status, the acknowledgment is no longer applicable.
- As a result, certain fields, such as Qty Shipped, are not included, because no shipping activity has occurred yet.
-
- The intention of the Order Acknowledgement is to confirm the original ordered quantities, not the shipped or fulfilled quantities.- Shipped quantities are available only after fulfillment.
- Including shipping-related fields would contradict the acknowledgement’s purpose and workflow sequence.

This design ensures that Order Acknowledgements remain accurate and relevant to their purpose.

- Add Required Ship Date to the PO grid.
