437b5ef7-4ca0-4e14-a75e-d5a3a4b181c5.title: Understanding the “Replace” Checkbox in 'PA Earning Types'
437b5ef7-4ca0-4e14-a75e-d5a3a4b181c5.content:
Problem
What is the use of the “Replace” Checkbox in 'PA Earning Types'?

Resolution
The “Replace” checkbox in the Earning Code setup determines whether the pay associated with that earning code should add to or replace the employee’s regular pay for the period.



Functionality Overview:

-
If the “Replace” checkbox is cleared:
The earning code’s pay will add to the employee’s regular pay. This is typically used for additional payments such as bonuses, incentives, or overtime, where the employee receives the amount in addition to their regular salary.

-
If the “Replace” checkbox is selected:
The earning code’s pay will replace the employee’s regular pay. This is used in cases such as Paid Time Off (PTO), Sick Leave, or Leave without Pay, where the earning replaces the standard working hours for that period rather than adding to them.



Example Scenario:

Let us consider an employee who is scheduled to work 40 hours per week:

i. Bonus Scenario (Additive Pay):

- The employee receives a bonus in addition to their regular salary.
- In this case, the Replace checkbox should be unchecked.
- The bonus amount will be added on top of the employee’s regular weekly pay.
- For example:

-
-
-
Regular Pay: 40 hours × ₹500 = ₹20,000

-
Bonus: ₹5,000

-
Total Pay = ₹25,000



ii. Leave Scenario (Replacement Pay):

- The employee takes 20 hours of Paid Leave (PTO) in a week.
- Since leave hours are meant to replace the regular work hours, the Replace checkbox should be checked.
- This ensures the system substitutes leave hours for regular hours instead of adding them.
- If you attempt to enter both 30 hours of regular work and 20 hours of leave (totaling 50 hours), Traverse will not allow the entry, since the employee’s standard workweek is set to 40 hours. [This setting can be found the SM Business Rules]
- The leave pay effectively replaces the working hours, keeping the total within the allowed limit.

Summary:



Use the Replace checkbox to control whether the earning code supplements or substitutes the employee’s regular pay.

-
Leave the box unchecked for additions like bonuses or extra pay.

-
Check it for replacements such as leave or non-working pay.



These Earning Types will, in turn, be assigned to the PA Earning Codes, which define the corresponding pay for employees.

689c59d2-c0a4-4702-9f76-42f0c308176b.title: Handling Prepayments in Positive Pay: Why a Check May Not Appear in Traverse?
689c59d2-c0a4-4702-9f76-42f0c308176b.content:
Problem
Handling Prepayments in Positive Pay: Why a Check May Not Appear in Traverse?



This document outlines a scenario where a client recorded a Prepayment and expected it to be included in the Positive Pay file within Traverse. However, the check record did not appear in the Create Positive Pay File screen.

Resolution
This document explains the root cause and how the issue was resolved by addressing a duplicate check number.

Scenario Summary:
- The client had already entered a Prepayment in the system with the Payment number of "123"
- They intended for this Prepayment to be included in the Positive Pay file to be submitted to the bank.
- After completing the 'Prepare Payments' step and upon navigating to the Create Positive Pay File screen in Traverse, the expected check record was not displayed, causing confusion.


Clarifications and Observations:
- Positive Pay files in Traverse can include Prepayments, even if the check is not printed.
- Traverse pulls in any eligible check record with a valid, unique check number for Positive Pay processing.
- If a check does not appear in the Positive Pay screen, it often means the check number has already been used in a previous Positive Pay file or is considered already processed by the system.

Root Cause:
- The check number assigned to the Prepayment had already been used previously in another Payment.
- To prevent duplication and ensure check fraud protection, Traverse excludes such previously processed check numbers from being re-listed in new Positive Pay file creation. That is, the old record would already sit under the 'Sent' category, and the expected Payment will not appear under the 'New' category.
- As a result, the Prepayment record will be excluded from the Positive Pay file creation screen.

Caution Before Proceeding with Any Changes:
While it may seem straightforward to update the check number (e.g., change it to "123_1"), this can pose a risk if the original number has already been communicated to the bank.

Positive Pay files are designed to prevent fraud by ensuring only the authorized check numbers and amounts are cleared by the bank. Any mismatch between the payment issued to the vendor and the file sent to the bank could cause:
- The bank to reject the check.
- Delays or disputes in payment processing.
- Increased risk of fraud, if old check numbers are reused without coordination.
Hence, before modifying the check number:
- Validate whether "123" was indeed reused and already cleared through a previous Positive Pay submission.
- Contact the vendor (if needed) to confirm whether the original check was already received, deposited, or can be voided/shredded.
- Only proceed with assigning a new unique check number once confirmation is received that the original check will not be presented again.


Resolution:
If it is safe to proceed with a new check number (after completing the above validations), kindly follow these steps:

i. Navigate to the ‘AP Create Positive Pay File’ screen under the path: Applications -> Accounts Payable -> Pay Invoices -> Create Positive Pay File:


ii. Check if any existing records use the same Payment Number (Check Number):
- In the Show drop-down, first check under ‘New’.
- Then switch to ‘Sent’ and review again.

NOTE: If any records already exist with the same Payment/Check Number, the current Prepayment record must be updated with a new, unused check number.

iii. Open the ‘AP Prepare Payments’ screen under the path: Applications -> Accounts Payable -> Pay Invoices -> Prepare Payments:
- Pull up the same Batch Code, in which this 'Payment' record was prepared
- When prompted, click ‘Yes’ to unprepare the payments.


iv. Next, go to the ‘AP Hold/Release Invoices’ screen.
- Pull the Vendor ID from the drop-down
- Select the appropriate Invoice. [It would have already been marked as 'Paid' with the Payment Number]
- Click the ‘Prepay’ icon again to re-enter the payment information.
- Important: Ensure a new, unique check number is used during this step.


v. Once the new check number is entered, return to the ‘AP Prepare Payments’ screen and reprepare the payments as usual.


vi. Finally, revisit the ‘AP Create Positive Pay File’ screen. We should now be able to see the updated check record available for inclusion in the Positive Pay file.


vii. The user can now generate the Positive Pay File from the 'AP Create Positive Pay File' screen by selecting the necessary payment entries, specifying the desired file path, and then clicking on 'Create':


Key Takeaways:
- Traverse does support including Prepayments in Positive Pay files—even if the checks are not physically printed.
- Check records will not show up in the Positive Pay creation screen if the check number has already been used and processed.
- Always coordinate with the vendor and bank before altering check details already processed.
- Maintain a unique and consistent check numbering system for Positive Pay accuracy and compliance.

Problem
While processing transactions within Traverse a Lot Number recorded did not properly get created for a corresponding Item ID/Location ID in Inventory - Setup and Maintenance - Lot Numbers. Now whenever users are trying to do anything with that Item/Loc/Lot they are receiving an error that says: "Invalid Lot Number" and cannot proceed with the Transaction Entry.

Resolution
This indicates that for some reason the Item/Location ID/Lot Number didn't properly get added to the Lot Number Master (Inventory - Setup and Maintenance - Lot Numbers) and may need to be manually added to the IN Lot Numbers. This is done by following these steps:

1. To add a lot number to an item, click the New button on the toolbar.

2. Select the Item ID from the drop-down list. Only lotted type items will appear in the list.

3. Select the Location ID where the lot number is located, or where you want to add the lot number.
4. Enter the new Lot Number, or for existing lots, the Lot Number is displayed

5. Change the Status of the lot, as necessary.
6. Enter or edit the Initial Date, Vendor ID, Comment, and Expires fields as necessary.

7. Click the Save button, on the toolbar, to save any changes made to the lot numbers.

7e421cf9-809e-4ff3-a133-15ad66532340.title: Traverse Global - Auditing WMS Picking
7e421cf9-809e-4ff3-a133-15ad66532340.content:
Problem
A user may pick an order in the WMS Backoffice or WMS Mobile application and an issue arises.
Auditing WMS Picking and Packing can be a challenge as there is not currently an SM Audit feature for WMS activity. The data can provide some information, however once the packing process is completed the direct data is no longer stored in the tables to refer to.
This KB will discuss strategies to review the issue.

Resolution
We have some resources available to audit the actions that may have occurred in WM. We'll use WM Picking for our examples but know you can use this information for other WMS activity you are trying to investigate. The Warehouse Management (WM) Activity View, System Manager (SM) Activity Logs, and the Inventory (IN) Detail History View all have information that can help. If all else fails, querying the data can help, but most everything is here already.

WM Activity View
The WM Activity View contains some helpful information centered around what has occurred when WMS is used. It will not provide you information for inventory-related transactions that occur outside of WMS. You will need the IN Detail History View for that.

For auditing, let's reference the example above. Some of the columns you see are not the defaults, but are helpful. Such as Entry Date, UserID, Host ID, Reference ID, Transaction ID, and the deleted flag and Delete date. These will tell us who did what, on what workstation, and sequence of events which can help serve as possible steps to reproduce an issue.
We are filtering for a specific item as seen at the filter in the top, and we are also filtering by the Entry Date value for anything from the year 2025.

For scenarios where a user picks goods/rew materials, you will see the pick's progression in this view.
The goods are moved out (picked) from one bin into the working bin. In the example below, from bin A-01 to the working bin ALW.

If the pick is confirmed and packed they move to a packing bin, you will see the goods move from the working bin to the packing bin similar to the shot below.

Once the pack is confirmed you will receive a record noting the move out of the packing bin to complete the process.
Note, there is a reference to the related order this was picked for in the final record as well.

Maybe you are hunting down a different issue. Perhaps the customer picked raw materials for production but they may have actually backflushed from the Record Production Activity function. The WM Activity view can help clear up what may have been picked in WMS vs. the MP Backflush process. You may still need to review the Backflush activity log if it was not picked in WMS.

With our example above, we are still only getting a picture of things. It might be enough information to explain something, or gather steps to test out the issue and replicate it. Or its simply part of a whole and more information is needed. Let's move on to the SM Activity Logs.

SM Activity Logs

The SM Activity Logs function contains all the recorded activity logs. If you confirmed a pick in WMS, the log will display there. While it does display in the activity of the confirm function, you may want to consider looking in SM instead because all activity will show there. Perhaps the customer provided information that didn't occur or they mis-remembered, you can filter on all the activity logs for that user or workstation in SM Activity. The downside is that it can take time to pull all the logs in and then you need to filter through that in the columns. But again, you get the full picture if you use SM Activity.

How can we use this to audit? In the example above, perhaps we are investigating a picking issue still, so lets filter on all the "Admin" user activity for the last two weeks. NOTE: the workstation date is the local time on the machine used, the server time is recorded in UTC.

In our example the customer reported a picking issue. Let's review the October 23rd records.

We can see the "WM Pick" record does not have a comment of "Confirmation log" and if you click on the "ViewLog" button get a message "Print Log does not exist for this activity." This type of record occurs when you are using the pick function and confirm a pick but do not pack it at the same time.

If the pick record that has "Confirmation Log" in the comments we know they picked and packed this at the same time. There will also be a log if you click on the "ViewLog" button.

If they had only used the Packing function (order already picked, packing activity is later after picking,) you'll see an entry of this style:

Note the "Description" value is "WM Pack Orders" instead of "WM Pick" in this scenario. There will also be a log if you click on the "ViewLog" button.

Lastly, let's talk about why the logs matter here anyway. It is true you can look at the WM Activity View and should be able to determine the same information there. It can be difficult to look through, though far from impossible.
Another reason the activity logs can help, let's say you're trying to replicate a suspected bug and you know the customer picked an item in WMS. The context around the pick matters. Perhaps the issue only occurs when you have a mix of lotted and non-lotted items getting picked. Perhaps the issue occurs when you pick more than 3 items. Maybe its a customer specific issue and you need to test picking the exact items, quantities, lots, and bins the customer picked.

All of this information can be found in the logs, or using both the logs and the WM Activity View. Ideally, you can then place this data together sequentially and produce proposed steps to reproduce that you can test through.

IN Detail History View
The IN Detail History View gets an honorable mention in this document, only it has no detailed information about WMS Picking. You will see the end result of picking in this view. So in our example above in the WM Activity View, we will see the end result of a qty of 100 for item Comp#1 used for a production order.

The IN Detail History View is a great view to audit inventory-related issues. This is thanks to the History Sequence number values and the Entry Date values. Both of these help establish sequence, which is critical in replicating issues, and in explaining issues. This view is a direct representation of the inventory data stored in tblInHistDetail, which is where all inventory records go at one point or another in the software's various processes. This table also retains a timestamp for the records to further enhance your understanding of sequence.

Often times customers report issues from days, weeks, or months prior. So Establishing sequence is critical to understanding what someone did after the fact, in a time when related orders have long been processed. As time goes on, the picture of what occurred in an issue can become clouded and buried by many other activities and actions.

Last point, while it does not give us picking detail, it does tell us what else has occurred with this item. Perhaps the customer usually picks raw materials in WMS, but this time they backflushed in production. The view can point you in the next direction to go and verify the facts. It also helps you understand what else might be going on at the same time as an issue. Perhaps another users was shipping the same item at the same time as your pick and when that happens there is a bug. You may not catch that without investigating what is in this view.

91798924-72db-443b-bde2-51542680419e.title: Mapping Network Drive
91798924-72db-443b-bde2-51542680419e.content:
Problem
Getting the error “Update folder does not exist or is invalid” when trying to apply build update in individual Workstation

Resolution
Had problem with accessing the network drive.

To Map a Network Folder in Windows
- Open File Explorer (you can press Windows + E).
- On the left panel, click “This PC.”
- At the top, click the “Computer” tab (or “See more” → “Map network drive” on Windows 11).
- Click “Map network drive.”
- Choose a Drive letter (e.g., Z:).
- In the Folder box, type the network path
- (Optional) Check “Reconnect at sign-in” if you want it to stay mapped after restart.
- If prompted, enter your network username and password.
- Click Finish.
You should now see the network folder under This PC as a new drive (e.g., “Z:\Share
\\ServerName\SharedFolder

or Open Traverse> Help> Check for Updates
Click on the 3 dots to access the Network Path

Right Click Network> Map Network Drive

Enter the shared Network Path and hit Finish.

You will get a pop up like below and need to enter Admin username and password and hit Ok.

93fd8904-9552-4ba0-a1be-0adb9ea92e10.title: Traverse Global How to Navigate Avalara Admin Console for Company Sandbox
93fd8904-9552-4ba0-a1be-0adb9ea92e10.content:
Problem
Traverse Global and ProcessPro Global interface with Avalara via the Tax Integration. Times may arise when you need to access and view Avalara's Admin Console for your tasks. This includes creating a company, making changes to that company, viewing transactions sent from our software to Avalara, and setting up exemptions. There are other functions, less common that we may need to use, but will note in summary below.

This internal document is meant to be a high-level overview of the features we may use in support. It is not intended for customer use.
Customers may need to work with Avalara's support at times.

Resolution
THIS IS INTERNAL ONLY! DO NOT DISTRIBUTE TO ANY OUTSIDE RESOURCESSandbox credentials are shared in Secret Server in both the Traverse Global and ProcessPro Global directories. Look for "Avalara Admin Console Sandbox and ProcessPro Global Credentials" or "Avalara Admin Console Sandbox and Traverse Global Credentials."

Home Screen
Consider this more of a landing page. In our example below, it's a bit like a dashboard.

What you see in the Admin Console is largely company specific. So if the company you are testing with is the AVA company, most of the options on the menus you see are related only to that company. In the top left, you have the current company you are referencing. There are many companies in the sandbox. It is used by support, development, and services.

If you are testing in a Traverse Global or ProcessPro Global vanilla environment its pointing here, you will need to toggle through the companies and change to the one you are looking at in order to access the transactions you are testing with. The same thing is true for testing with customer data.
An important note here, if you are testing with customer data you may need to set a company up in the admin console. If I restore company ABC, ABC needs to be set up as a company in the Admin Console. There is a separate KB available on this topic.

Below that you have the Admin Console menu with access to the other functions offered.

On the right, you'll see a support chat option, help, which includes Avalara-related documentation, and the Account information.
Account information offers the ability to add users and admins to our account, so you could have your own login to the sandbox if you'd like. You can also access the companies here, similar to how you did on the left side of the screen.

Registrations
The Registrations feature is something our customers would use to get registered for their potentially many tax jurisdictions where they need to remit sales tax to. This helps handle the preparation of government forms and filing with the appropriate tax authorities, and payment of state registration fees. There may be other fees and items our customers need to handle aside from this.

This information is ore for awareness, but if customers have questions they need to work with Avalara support.

Transactions
Transactions is a place where you can add or view transactions. Data will flow here from our software once invoiced and posted. If a user needs to add or change a transaction, they can do that here as well. There is also an import function and tax calculator.

The tax calculator is handy for customer cases, when they feel a calculation was incorrect. It can also serve as an address validation tool for you in scenarios where that may be an issue in the software.

Payables
The Payables section is not something we have access to in our sandbox, its just not a feature we'd need to use. For customers, it is a place where they can manage use tax on vendor invoices.

Exemptions

The Exemptions feature is where you go to enter customer exemptions to taxes. If the customer has a certificate for their exemption that can be entered in the Customer Certificates feature.

A quick note related to exemptions and support, items can be exempted depending on the tax code associated with them. Avalara has a library of codes that can be used with items, to detect the type of item, related tax jurisdictions, and help with that process. If there is ever a question on what occurred, the transaction can be reviewed in the admin console to verify the codes used and amounts in play for the transaction and taxes. The reports can also help determine what was done and why.

Returns
The returns section is not quite something we would use in our sandbox but is something good to be aware of. This feature allows our customers to manage their returns. They can use this to file returns, prepayments, and remit sales tax with one payment.

Reports

The Reports section is used to provide information to our customers. There are many reports available providing information like:
- Invoice details and sales
- Transactions summarized by tax jurisdictions within a state
- Exemption reporting
- Sales and sellers use tax reporting
- Tax liability by region or country
- Transactional tax details broken down by county/city

Integrations
Not something that comes up for use by support resources. There may be information in here about the software integrations with Avalara (AvaTax.)

Settings
The Settings section is where you will have the most interaction. Below is a breakdown of each section within Settings.

Where you report tax
This section is where you alter the tax jurisdictions you are registered to sell in. You can pick the countries, states/provinces, and local jurisdictions in this function.

What you sell and buy
This is a way to tell Avalara the items you sell and how you categorize them, what code it should use. Our software allows you to associate codes with SM Tax Classes however you may want a more granular coding of things. A benefit to using this feature in the Admin Console is that Avalara will pass the correct amounts to our software when those codes are used. For example, in Minnesota clothing is not taxed. You may want to associate your clothing items with Avalara's code that would calculate no sales tax if it was clothing and in Minnesota. If sold from California it would detect that and tax accordingly. It can be more complex than just this example but its a good start. This information can be entered manually or imported and codes assigned.

Company locations
For jurisdictions that require customers to report taxes by location. You can set these up in the Company locations feature. There is a link to Marketplaces here, which is the same thing as the Marketplaces listed below.

Marketplaces
If the customer does business through an online marketplace like Amazon or Etsy, for examples, they might have the Marketplace setup to import transactions into that Admin Console. This may bypass our software and is something to be aware of. Transactions would either need to be imported into our products after, or imported before and then committed to Avalara.

As support reps, this is likely something handled when the Tax Integration is implemented, though it could arise in general support work as questions. Again, it is more something to just be aware of.

License and API keys
This is not something we will see in the sandbox currently.

All settings
This is an area that brings everything above together, simply another way to get at everything.

238071c9-d75d-4208-bb29-83fa981559be.title: Traverse Global Tax Integration - How to Test Tax Integration with Customer Data
238071c9-d75d-4208-bb29-83fa981559be.content:
Problem
A time may arise where you need to test the Tax Integration with customer data loaded. The Resolution section below will outline how to update the environment to point to our sandbox account.

Resolution
THIS IS INTERNAL ONLY! DO NOT DISTRIBUTE TO ANY OUTSIDE RESOURCES
Sandbox credentials are shared in Secret Server in both the Traverse Global and ProcessPro Global directories. Look for "Avalara Admin Console Sandbox and ProcessPro Global Credentials" or "Avalara Admin Console Sandbox and Traverse Global Credentials."

The steps below will help outline what you need to do in order to test.

Once you have the company, SYS, and client folder in place, make sure you clear things like document delivery, credit card processing, etc.
It is recommended that you create a new customer and test with that, but if you must test with a customer from their data be sure the above things are cleared.

The next thing to consider is the database name. Let's pick on a customer using the Tax Integration with a database name of "FSC."
In order to use the integration with customer data in our sandbox, we need to be sure the company is set up in the Avalara Admin Console.

NOTES:
- It is possible another user in the company has already tested this customer at some point, and you may not need to set this up.
- It is also possible the company you want to set up exists for a different customer. You can restore your company database as a different name and set that up in the Admin Console or attempt to use the existing company in the Admin Console, paying attention to the jurisdictions that are set up and adjusting as needed.

Let's look in the Admin Console:

Once logged in, click on "Account" in the top right and then "Companies"

There will be a large list on the screen, you can try searching for the company or scroll and navigate the pages that way.
In our scenario, FSC does exist and it is for the customer I intend to use. It is great news that FSC exists and also that it is for the customer I am using, here is why.

When a company is setup in the Admin Console you must select the tax jurisdictions to use, so the company cannot simply exist but you must also tell it what jurisdictions you are using. Jurisdictions are the various tiers where there are taxes for example there may be one level of tax for Minnesota, another for the county of the sale, maybe there is also a local tax for the city. Since it is already set up, it is likely the jurisdictions that we need are set up too.

For example testing with FSC, I need to think about the AR customers I am testing with. I have a weird SO Order issue that might be due to the customer we are shipping to. For my testing, I want to carefully use that customer, or create a new customer as a copy of the real one, so that taxes are calculating the same as what the customer is reporting to us in support.
Again, you can use the actual AR customer while testing but take care to ensure you are not accidentally emailing them from document delivery, or charging their stored credit cards, or anything else that sends data some place we don't want it to.

If you need to set up the company in the Admin Console, please review the KB "Tax Integration - How to set up a company" for assistance.

While we are talking about testing, perhaps you also want to test this in a vanilla environment? If you do, you also want to be sure the jurisdictions are selected so that you can see how it behaves for you. So maybe you are shipping 100 dollars of taxable goods to Denver, Colorado you are testing that in the FSC company and then in your own vanilla environment you need to do the same thing. You just need to make sure that you have that jurisdiction set up so when you calculate tax in the software, it can do that.

If you don't have the jurisdiction added in the Admin Console, you will not get a value for your tax calculation. There is a KB titled "Tax Integration - How to add jurisdictions to a company" that can assist with the process or adding jurisdictions.

At this point in the process, the Admin Console should have the company, whether it was already there or we just added it. Let's proceed with the FSC example. FSC is now in the Admin Console, it has the jurisdictions added that I need in order to test the customer issue I need to review.

My next step is to access our software and navigate to SM > Setup and Maintenance > Tax Integration.
NOTE: in older builds its possible this menu exists in SM > Tax Setup > Tax Service Configuration.

Proceed to swap out the customer's setup with our sandbox credentials:


Click "Test Connection" and then "Update."

Lastly, double check the Business Rules for SM > Tax Integration > Tax Service, for our example using FSC, this should say FSC:


Again, this value is going to be whatever database you are using. A vanilla environment named GLB would have GLB here, because the Tax Service Integration was setup that way for that particular company.

At this point, you can proceed with testing. As a reminder, be sure to take care of document delivery, credit card processing settings, and any other setup that enables transfer and communication from the software to other parties.

dabe8b4a-cf4f-49bd-82b4-901dddc19e7b.title: Traverse Global Tax Integration - How to set up a company
dabe8b4a-cf4f-49bd-82b4-901dddc19e7b.content:
Problem
You may need to test a customer environment in our Avalara sandbox environment. While the setup is simple, something often overlooked is that the company must be set up in Avalara's Admin Console so that you can actually test. This document will discuss how to set this up.

Resolution
THIS IS INTERNAL ONLY! DO NOT DISTRIBUTE TO ANY OUTSIDE RESOURCES
Sandbox credentials are shared in Secret Server in both the Traverse Global and ProcessPro Global directories. Look for "Avalara Admin Console Sandbox and ProcessPro Global Credentials" or "Avalara Admin Console Sandbox and Traverse Global Credentials."

Setting up a CompanyLet's say the company does not exist, or we need to add jurisdictions. We'll approach adding a company and jurisdictions so you know how to do both if needed.

First, access the Avalara Admin Console and login.
Next, access "Companies" and click "Add a company"

In this example, we need to use the MNT company, so we will set that up here:
We'll keep this as a standalone company and click "Next" at the bottom.
You can use any valid address for the company address, I typically use the old Minnesota office's location: Validate the address and then click "Next."You will get a prompt asking if you want to collect sales tax in other regions. Avalara covers mostly the US, but it might be possible to use it with other countries like Canada. Use the dialogues accordingly to set these up, we'll say yes and add more regions.
Remember, if you need to test taxes in different states, you need to add those jurisdictions. If working with customer data, look at some of the places their orders are getting shipped to to see what jurisdictions you may need to add and test with.In this example, the company is a Minnesota company but let's say we also do business in Wisconsin. We'll proceed to add that now by clicking "Yes, add more US regions." It's a preference thing here, but I will choose "Select from a list" Scroll down to Wisconsin and check it.NOTE: Some states may require you to click more boxes if there are jurisdictions inside the state that you need to opt to do business in. Potentially counties and local areas.Click "Add selected regions" and "Next"You will have an option to look at and add other countries if they are available from Avalara for use.We'll click "No, where I collect tax is complete."You can always come back here to make changes and add more jurisdictions. As a customer, they may find they are doing more and more business that requires them to come back in here and do the same.Depending on the jurisdiction, you may have other things you can change, so the next screen may have differing options. We'll click "Done with tax jurisdictions" which makes way to activate the company When ready, click "Activate company" so that it can be used with our software.

At this point the new company is setup in the Admin Console and you can proceed with your remaining setup work in Traverse Global and ProcessPro Global.

3a34aaae-aac3-4e18-9e48-eafab36662ab.title: Traverse Global Tax Integration - How to add jurisdictions to a company
3a34aaae-aac3-4e18-9e48-eafab36662ab.content:
Problem
Editing Jurisdictions
A time may arise when you need to edit jurisdictions for your Avalara company. Maybe you're just testing and need to try a few different states to mimic exactly what the customer is doing. 6b543dc7-3d06-4ccc-9f29-b223b8d6c94f.title: Traverse Global - Identifying Custom Python Files
6b543dc7-3d06-4ccc-9f29-b223b8d6c94f.content:
Problem
Times may arise when you are troubleshooting an issue and a python customization is present. You are investigating in a customer's environment, or perhaps restored backups of theirs. You may have reviewed the menu overrides, Design Studio changes, but something is still off if you compare the environment to a vanilla one. This document will discuss how to identify if the file is in use and what you may want to consider when troubleshooting.

Resolution
The first step is to look at the function in question.

In this example, let's say the customer reports an odd message when opening the AP Create ACH File function. So we obtain their client folder, company and SYS databases and load that up.

We access the AP Create ACH File function, and observe the error. They have not custom overrides in SM > Setup and Maintenance > Application Menus, or if looking in Design Studio, nothing in System Data > Custom Menu.

What next? Let's observe the screen:

In the bottom right corner, we see "Scripting Enabled."

Next, let's look at the client folder, and within it, we'll find a Python file, this will have a ".py" extension.

In this scenario there is only one file present, so it is easier to imagine this is a factor in the issue we're investigating. There could be multiple files listed if the customer has many Python-related customizations. We just need to read through these and look at what may be in play.

It should be noted, since we're discussing customizations, there is a lot of room for ambiguity, interesting file names, and some of these files may not be prepared by our company as a modification. Just something to think about when you are determining if an escalation is required.

What does this mean for us? Well, next we can rename this file or change the file extension to something else like .TST or .OLD, or move it out of the client folder.
Let's do that and then close the software. Go back to the AP Create ACH File function and observe. Since the python file is not in use this time, as confirmed by a lack of seeing "Scripting Enabled" in the bottom right corner, we can see how this behaves without that file present.

If the issue does not occur, we should treat this as a customization issue and route it accordingly.

If there are multiple python files, its best to choose the file that is logically close in name to whatever the function is. The customer could have python customizations in multiple functions. If unsure you could seek out SOW/CBR documentation or other modified documentation. We can also escalate this as an REA to determine what custom files there are and possibly gain more insight. Overall, we know Python files are not part of the vanilla solution, and we are dealing with a customization.

As a final comment, be sure to investigate this with the mindset of layers. Customers can have many customizations, sometimes multiple in the same area. Consider menu overrides, design studio changes, and python changes when applicable.

74e99185-cbba-4d04-8fb3-a91ae31a3e48.title: How to recalculate the Depreciation for a specific period that was not posted?
74e99185-cbba-4d04-8fb3-a91ae31a3e48.content:
Problem
How to recalculate the Depreciation for a specific period that was not posted?

Resolution
To perform this action, the user should follow the steps below:

i. Navigate to the Compute Period Depreciation Screen:
Go to the following path in Traverse: Applications -> Fixed Assets -> Period Work -> Compute Period Depreciation



ii. Uncheck the Depreciation Type:
In the lower section of the screen, deselect the Depreciation Type 'Book' checkbox.



iii. Recalculate Depreciation:
Click the Calculate icon again.



iv. Confirm the action:
A confirmation pop-up will appear asking whether we wish to clear the calculated depreciation. Select Yes to confirm.

This step will reset the previously calculated depreciation values.



v. Recompute as Needed:
Once the reset is complete, the user can proceed with recalculating the depreciation as required.

e1d34ea4-dda5-406c-bc91-6dba76f52edc.title: Removing Zero Balance Accounts from GL Financial statement
e1d34ea4-dda5-406c-bc91-6dba76f52edc.content:
Problem
The customer reported that zero-balance bank accounts continue to appear on financial reports, even after inactivating the account numbers and confirming there was no activity for the current year.

Resolution
The first thing to check would be whether the "Accounts with Zero Balances" is left unchecked before running the report.

a1c774df-7616-42b4-9c1f-268ff637eef8.title: How Allocations work in OSAS
a1c774df-7616-42b4-9c1f-268ff637eef8.content:
Problem
Customer basically wants to know, how do Allocations work in the GL and how to set them up

Cause
Customer basically wants to know, how do Allocations work in the GL and how to set them up.

Resolution
HOW ALLOCATIONS WORK.

You cannot access this function if you did not elect to use allocations in the Resource Manager Options and Interfaces.

With this function, you enter the major account number, each account to which to distribute transactions, and the percentage of the amount each account receives.

When you enter a transaction for an account set up in the GLALxxx (Allocations) file, you indicate that the transactions should be allocated;
when you post, the system creates journal entries to the accounts specified in the allocation record.

1. Enter the number of the major account whose journal entries you want to allocate to other accounts.
The description of the account appears for verification.
Note : if the account has been marked inactive, you will receive the message.

2. Enter a description of the allocation. It prints in the Allocations List.

3. Enter the number of each account to which to allocate entries made to the major account.
Because the system cannot split a penny, the first account in the record receives all the rounding adjustments.

4. Enter the percentage to be allocated to each account.

NOTE:
If you enter transactions against one major account and then distribute them to several other accounts.
We can use the Allocations function to set up an allocation record for the major account.
We can specify each account to which transactions are allocated (up to 45) and the percentage that each account receives.
The sum of the percentages must equal 100 percent

3a313c04-82c4-4476-8361-45fd9f9f546b.title: PO Reorder Processing and Unexpected Calculations
3a313c04-82c4-4476-8361-45fd9f9f546b.content:
Problem
PO Reorder Processing does not calculate the expected quantity to reorder, or calculates no quantity.

We'll use this example below, where a the "Order Qty Min/Max" of 39 is unexpected, it should be a quantity of 61:

The Order Quantities fields for the item, located in Inventory > Setup and Maintenance > Items: Location tab are set up properly.

Cause
In process transactions that are not yet posted.
Old transactions that either need to be completed/posted or removed.

Resolution
There are some key areas in the software that can contribute to the calculation. Verify if there are any open PO Orders, PO Order Requests, Requisitions, and Sales Returns. It may be possible that there is a forgotten request or transaction for the item in question.

Purchase Orders Influence
Review the PO Order View for the item in question.
This provides information about any PO Transactions, Requisitions, or Order Requests. Review these types of transactions as they can have an impact on the calculation.

We can see that there is an old PO Order Request for a quantity of 22. In this scenario, this request is out dated and we will remove it. If we do, and re-run the PO Reorder Processing calculation, we'll get the expected quantity of 61.

Sales Orders Influence
Review the SO Open Order Detail View for the item in question.

This provides information about any SO Returns/Credit Memos with a Qty Shipped value. If looking at the SO Order function for RMAs/Credit Memos, it will have a Qty Returned value. Review these types of transactions as they can have an impact on the calculation.

If the business rules are set not to return goods direct to stock, verify any entries for in the Sales Order >Transactions > Returned Items function. Any Approved/unposted returns' items will reflect in inventory and impact PO Reorder Processing.

Overall, you may find that the calculation is correct even though it is unexpected. Perhaps there are some old or forgotten orders for the item that need to finish processing or simply be removed. If this does not explain any irregularities, please contact support for further assistance.

08108ab2-0697-4819-9b8e-59f3c61b25e2.title: Missing Payment Number Issue
08108ab2-0697-4819-9b8e-59f3c61b25e2.content:
Problem
The case involves a high priority issue where a user is unable to prepare prepaid payments due to an error stating "All prepaid payments must have a payment number." The user is unsure how to identify the prepaid payment missing a payment number.

Resolution
This error typically occurs when one or more payments in the batch do not have a valid Payment Number assigned. Such cases usually arise if the user has not printed the AP Checks for those payments.

To verify this, we can review the AP Payment Register and check whether any entries are missing a Payment Number.
- If any such entries are found, they can be removed from the current payment posting using the Select Payables option. These entries can be processed separately once the issue is corrected.
- If all checks have already been printed and no entries are missing a Payment Number, we can temporarily update the Business Rule to 'Yes' that restricts the posting. This rule can be reverted to “No” after the posting is completed.

Alternatively, if the user is comfortable re-preparing the payment batch, the following steps can be performed:
i. Restart Payment Preparation
- Navigate to the AP Prepare Payments screen.
- Select the batch that has the issue.
- When prompted with “Payments already on file for batch. Do you wish to start over?”, click Yes.
ii. Re-prepare and Print Checks
- Re-prepare the payments for the same batch.
- Print the checks and review the Payment Register to confirm that all payments have valid numbers assigned.
iii. Post Payments
- Proceed to post the payments again after verification.

93f85dfc-2b13-4268-9aa4-6fda9df41e81.title: What is the Component Where-Used Report and what are its uses?
93f85dfc-2b13-4268-9aa4-6fda9df41e81.content:
Problem
What is the Component Where-Used Report and what are its uses?

Resolution
The Component Where-Used report provides visibility into which Bills of Material (BOMs) include specific components. This report is particularly useful when a component is being discontinued or has experienced a significant price change. By analyzing this report, management can determine which finished goods will be impacted and make informed decisions regarding potential replacements.

The report can be viewed in two formats:

-
Single Indentation: This option displays the component and the BOMs in which it is used in a simple, flat list. It allows us to see the component and the immediate bills it is part of. The structure of this report resembles an upside-down BOM because we are looking from the component upward to all BOMs where it is used.

-
Fully Indented: This option provides a hierarchical view, showing not only the BOMs in which the component is used, but also whether those BOMs themselves serve as components in other higher-level BOMs. This hierarchical view is especially helpful for understanding the broader impact of changes to a component, as it allows us to trace the effect of a low-level component up through the levels of finished goods.

How to generate Component Where-Used Report?

We can refine the data using the Data Filter, which allows us to select specific criteria or leave the filter blank to include all available data. We can filter based on the 'Component ID' and the 'Location ID'.

This can be accessed under the path: Applications -> MFG-Bills of Material -> Reports -> Component Where_Used



Other report options include:

-
'View' Section: The format of the report can be chosen from the View section.

- Single Indentation: By selecting the Single Indentation option, we can generate a straightforward list showing each BOM containing the component.
- Fully Indented: By selecting the Fully Indented option, we can view a detailed hierarchy that illustrates how changes in a low-level component may affect multiple assemblies at higher levels.

-
'Report Layout' section:

-
Page Break after Component: If selected, this option inserts page breaks after each component to improve readability. The default setting for this option can be defined through the System Manager Print Preferences, and it can be overridden when printing.

-
Banded Rows: This option highlights alternating lines in the report, making it easier to read.

-
'Include' section:

- Quantities: Provides the Quantity information
- Scrap Quantities: When available, selecting this option includes scrap quantities in the report.
- Yield Adjustments: When available, selecting this option includes any yield adjustments in the report.



The User can either use 'Preview', 'Print', or 'Output' option to export the report as needed. The sample report can be found below:

9ee9d637-2dd3-4db5-8553-d3956b7b8d63.title: Why is the User not able to delete the 'Assembly ID' in MB-Bills of Material?
9ee9d637-2dd3-4db5-8553-d3956b7b8d63.content:
Problem
Why is the User not able to delete the 'Assembly ID' in MB-Bills of Material?



When the User attempts to delete an 'Assembly ID', he/she is getting the below error message:

===================================

Current record is in use and cannot be deleted.

===================================

Current record is in use and cannot be deleted. (TRAVERSE.Client.MfgBom)

------------------------------
Program Location:

at TRAVERSE.Client.Manufacturing.AssemblyHeaderControl.OnAssemblyHeaderControlDeletingRow(CancelEventArgs e)
at TRAVERSE.Client.Manufacturing.AssemblyHeaderControl.AssemblyHeaderControl_DeletingRow(Object sender, CancelEventArgs e)

This error typically occurs when the Assembly that a user is attempting to delete is referenced as a sub-assembly in one or more other Assembly IDs within the Bill of Materials (BOM). Since the system prevents the deletion of assemblies that are still in use, the user encounters this error.



To verify whether the assembly is being used elsewhere, the user can run the Component Where-Used report. This report provides a detailed list of all assemblies in which the target assembly is referenced, allowing the user to identify any dependencies that must be addressed prior to deletion.

Kindly refer to the article for reference: What-is-the-Component-Where-Used-Report-and-what-are-its-uses

In each assembly, the target assembly (for example, JK_Test) should be removed from the Component section.



We need to navigate to the respective Assembly ID and delete the corresponding sub-assembly alone and save the record:



After all references to the target assembly have been cleared, the system will allow the assembly to be deleted successfully.

This process ensures that the deletion is performed safely without leaving broken references in other assemblies, maintaining the integrity of the BOM structure.

79fc908c-60fc-4f5b-94b3-6356f9cea67f.title: How to replace the Client Folder on a workstation?
79fc908c-60fc-4f5b-94b3-6356f9cea67f.content:
Problem
How to replace the Client Folder on a workstation?

Resolution
In certain scenarios, the Client folder on the end user’s workstation may become corrupted or may be missing essential files after a fresh installation. This can result in errors during application launch, unexpected behavior while running modules, or failed connectivity between the client and server components.
Why Do We Replace the Client Folder?
Replacing the Client folder is required when:
- Some files in the installation process are skipped or corrupted due to network interruptions, antivirus restrictions, or permission issues.
- The installation package may not have deployed all required files correctly.
- Users may have inadvertently deleted or modified critical files within the Client folder.
- The Client folder is out of sync with the version deployed on other workstations or the server.
- Application crashes, missing DLL errors, or module access failures point to incomplete or damaged Client folder contents.
By copying the Client folder from a verified working workstation, we ensure that the new machine has all the required files and a consistent version, resolving corruption-related issues.
Resolution Steps:
On the Old (Working) Workstation:
- Navigate to the installation path: C:\Program Files\Open Systems, Inc\TRAVERSE [TRAVERSE Global for 11.2]
- Right-click on the Traverse / Traverse Global folder.
- Compress the folder into a .zip file.
- Upload the zipped folder to the designated FTP link or into the shared network path.


On the New (Problematic) Workstation:
- Navigate to the same installation path: C:\Program Files\Open Systems, Inc\TRAVERSE [TRAVERSE Global for 11.2]
- Delete the existing Client folder. [Optional: Take a backup by compressing the folder into a .zip file and saving it elsewhere.]
- Download the working Client folder zip from the FTP location/ or from the shared Network path.
- Extract the contents.
- Place the extracted folder contents into the path: C:\Program Files\Open Systems, Inc\TRAVERSE [TRAVERSE Global for 11.2]


By following the above steps, any corruption or missing content within the Client folder can be resolved effectively. This ensures Traverse functions as expected on the affected workstation and avoids unnecessary disruptions to business operations.

a81bd91d-551a-460f-969f-036175e60001.title: How to edit an entry after performing 'Read Data' in the SM Import Mapped Data screen?
a81bd91d-551a-460f-969f-036175e60001.content:
Problem
How to edit an entry after performing 'Read Data' in the SM Import Mapped Data screen?

Resolution
The SM Import Mapped Data screen in Traverse is designed to help us review, verify, and import data from ASCII files into various modules. This utility ensures that the imported data is mapped correctly and validated before it is posted into the system.

We can use this functionality to import data into the following modules:

-
GL/AR/AP/SO Transactions

-
CRM Contacts

-
BR Transactions and Cleared Transactions

-
IN Physical Counts Entry

-
IN Item Prices

-
SO Customer Pricing

-
PA Payroll Transactions

By utilizing this process, we ensure accuracy and consistency while bringing external data into Traverse.

The User can navigate to the 'SM Import Mapped Data' screen under the path: Applications -> System Manager -> Company Setup -> Import Mapped Data:



Purpose of the ‘Read Data’ Function:

The Read Data function is intended to display the mapped data from the ASCII file (commonly a .csv file) for review before the import. In certain situations, we may need to make corrections or adjustments to the data at this stage. The system provides editing functionality to facilitate these updates.



Editing Data After ‘Read Data’:

-
When we select Read Data, the mapped data from the ASCII file is displayed in the top section of the screen.

-
At this stage, the data remains editable. Any necessary corrections or adjustments can be made directly in the top section.

-
Once we complete the edits, we should select Verify Data to check for compatibility and confirm that the data types align with Traverse field requirements.





Editing Data After ‘Verify Data’:

-
Even after we select Verify Data, the entries in the top section (Read Data section) remain editable.

-
The Verify Data function transfers the information into the bottom section (Verify Data section) for further validation and confirmation.

-
The system cross-checks the mapped fields with the intended source fields, ensuring that layouts, field types, and required mappings are accurate.

-
If issues are detected, such as missing fields or mismatched data, the system displays a prompt directing us to review and correct the errors.

-
Corrections can still be made in the top section. Once updated, we should select Verify Data again to ensure the corrected entries are reflected accurately in the bottom section without errors.



Important Note:

If errors are detected during the Verify Data stage, it is recommended to make the corrections in the top (Read Data) section and then run Verify Data again. This ensures that the updated entries are revalidated and transferred correctly into the bottom section.

However, if we are confident about the change to be made, we are allowed to make the changes directly in the bottom section, followed by importing the Data directly into the system.





Summary:

-
The Read Data stage displays the mapped data and allows us to perform initial edits.

-
The Verify Data stage validates the mapped fields, identifies potential issues, and displays the verified results in the bottom section.

-
Errors should be corrected in the top section and reverified to ensure accuracy before proceeding.

-
Once the data is verified successfully, we can continue with the Import Data function to complete the process.

81bde2b9-2073-425e-8a3a-003d42b8163d.title: Understanding the Impact of Purging Statements in Bank Reconciliation
81bde2b9-2073-425e-8a3a-003d42b8163d.content:
Problem
This documentation is intended to provide a clear understanding of the Purge Bank Reconciliation (BR) Statement feature, outlining its impact and the circumstances under which it may be recommended. While the option to purge exists in Traverse, it is not typically required for day-to-day operations and should be used with caution. The content here explains the risks and considerations associated with purging statements, including the permanent removal of both the statement and its cleared transaction records. It also highlights the impact of purging statements on financial data and provides guidance on scenarios where its use may be appropriate.

Resolution
The 'BR Purge Cleared Transactions' feature in Traverse is not a function that is generally required to be performed during regular operations. In fact, it is typically recommended not to run this feature unless there is a specific and well-justified need.

This feature is designed to permanently remove previously created bank reconciliation statements from the system. Once executed, the following occurs:
- The statement itself is deleted.
- All associated transaction records that were cleared on the purged statement are permanently removed from the system.
- Unless we review the 'Activity' of the Purge Cleared Transactions there will be no trace of the purged entries.
It is important to note that once a statement is purged, it cannot be retrieved or restored. Both the statement and its linked cleared transaction records are lost irreversibly.
When to Use This Feature?
Although the purge functionality is rarely required, there may be certain scenarios where its use is appropriate. Examples include:
- Removing Unnecessary Data:
If old statements are no longer required for business or auditing purposes, and the organization has determined that they should not be retained, this feature may be used to permanently clear them from the system.

- Correcting Errors:
If a statement was created with an incorrect date, the purge option may be used to remove the invalid statement so that a correct one can be generated.
Important Considerations:
- The purge process is permanent and cannot be undone.
- This action should only be executed after careful review and explicit approval, ideally in consultation with the Accounting or Audit teams.
- Organizations must confirm that the targeted statements are not required for financial audits, compliance reviews, or reconciliations before purging.

Recommendation:
Unless absolutely necessary, avoid running the Purge Cleared Transactions feature. If it must be performed, ensure:
- A proper review process is in place.
- Approval is obtained from the responsible team/authority.
- The correct filters are applied to prevent accidental removal of unintended data.

Steps to purge a BR Statement:
Step 1: Update Statement Status to Reconciled:
- Before purging, confirm that the BR statement status is set to Reconciled.
A. Historical Statement:
- For older statements, typically reconciled in the past (e.g., from prior years), no additional action is needed since they are generally already in Reconciled status.

B. Incorrect Statement:
- If the statement was created in error and needs to be deleted, first update its status to Reconciled.
- Ensure that no entries are cleared within the statement before proceeding with the purge.
- To update the status, navigate to: Bank Reconciliation → Reconciliation → Cleared Transactions
- Pull up the required 'Bank Account ID' and the 'Statement Date'
- Set the statement status to 'Reconciled' using the 'Change Status' icon.



Step 2: Purge Cleared Transactions:
- To perform the purge, we need to navigate to: Bank Reconciliation → Reconciliation → Purge Cleared Transactions
Once on the screen, it is critical to apply the correct filters to ensure that only the intended statement(s) are purged. Selecting the wrong filters may lead to accidental removal of valid records.
- Historical Statements:- When purging older statements (for example, those reconciled years ago and no longer needed), apply the filter using only the Statement Date (e.g., equals or less than).
- This method allows you to clear multiple outdated statements across all Bank Account IDs in one action.

- Incorrect Statement:- When targeting a specific incorrect statement that was created in error, apply both Bank Account ID and Statement Date filters.
- This ensures that only the intended statement is removed, while all other statements remain intact.

Note: The use of precise filters is mandatory to prevent unintentional data loss. Always double-check the filters before confirming the purge.

After applying the filters:
- Select the confirmation checkbox (“Do the following, then check the box”).
- Click OK to execute the purge.

Once completed, the selected statement will be permanently removed from the BR Cleared Transactions screen. This process can be used either to clean up long-standing historical data that is no longer required or to delete an incorrectly created statement.

6738de7f-dae2-4545-81ea-0f1e17cc2f45.title: What is the use of 'Split By' field in the Direct Deposit Tab of 'PA Employee Information' screen?
6738de7f-dae2-4545-81ea-0f1e17cc2f45.content:
Problem
What is the use of 'Split By' field in the Direct Deposit Tab of 'PA Employee Information' screen?

Resolution
The Direct Deposit tab in the PA Employee Information screen is used to record and maintain an employee’s direct deposit details. This tab is available only if the Banking module is installed.

Within this tab, we can configure up to six distributions per employee, allowing payroll to be split across multiple bank accounts if required.

The ‘Split By’ field determines how the employee’s net pay is divided for direct deposit purposes. It provides three options:
i. None:
-
- The employee will not receive direct deposit. The below section will be greyed out meaning no direct deposit will be created.
- Their full wages are issued as a paper paycheck.


ii. Amount:
-
- A fixed amount of the employee’s net pay is deposited into the specified account(s).
- Any remaining balance that is not allocated through direct deposit is automatically issued as a paper check.

Example: If $100 is specified for direct deposit and the employee earns $1,000, $900 will be issued as a paycheck.


iii. Percent:
- A percentage of the employee’s net pay is deposited into each of the designated accounts.
- The total percentage must equal 100%. If not, a warning message will appear, and the tab cannot be closed until corrected.

- Example: If 60% is deposited into a checking account and 40% into a savings account, the full pay will be distributed without generating a paper check.

The Total field at the bottom of the tab displays the overall distribution when using the Percent option.


NOTE:
Once the setup is complete, we must generate and send a prenotification file to the bank. This step is mandatory before processing direct deposit transactions or printing employee vouchers, whenever any change is made to the 'Direct Deposit' Tab.
[Kindly refer to the below article on steps to create a 'Prenotification' file: https://connect.aptean.com/s/article/How-to-create-a-Prenotification-File-for-Direct-Deposit-in-Payroll ]

531fbe26-2d3c-426f-8a33-e84e0cb94b86.title: Why Does Traverse Generate a part of the Employee's Pay is generated as Paper Check instead of a Direct Deposit in Payroll?
531fbe26-2d3c-426f-8a33-e84e0cb94b86.content:
Problem
Why Does Traverse Generate a Portion of the Employee’s Pay as a Paper Check Instead of Processing the Entire Amount Through Direct Deposit in Payroll?
Under normal circumstances, employees set up for Direct Deposit in Traverse Payroll receive their entire pay via electronic transfer. However, during a particular pay run, the system generates only a portion of the wages (for example, $100) as a Direct Deposit, while the remaining balance is issued as a Paper Check.

Resolution
This issue typically occurs due to the configuration in the “PA Employee Information” screen, specifically within the ‘Split By’ field settings for the employee.
For example, in the case of Employee AEB, the system is configured to split payments by Amount. With this setup, whenever the employee’s pay exceeds $100, the system issues the excess amount as a Paper Check rather than processing the full payment through Direct Deposit.


If the intention is to ensure that the entire payroll amount is paid through Direct Deposit without generating a paper check, the following adjustment should be made:
- Navigate to the “PA Employee Information” screen.
- Locate the ‘Split By’ field and update its value to Percent.
- In the Amount/Percent field, enter 100%.
- And then hit on 'Save' to record the changes
- Then ensure to send the prenotification [as mentioned in the below pop-up]

By configuring the employee’s record in this manner, the system will direct 100% of the employee’s pay through Direct Deposit, eliminating the generation of paper checks.


Kindly refer to the below article on steps to create a 'Prenotification' file: https://connect.aptean.com/s/article/How-to-create-a-Prenotification-File-for-Direct-Deposit-in-Payroll

f98f2069-f756-4148-90cb-1a8d5c485e44.title: Tax is not calculated for the Sales order on a new machine.
f98f2069-f756-4148-90cb-1a8d5c485e44.content:
Problem
Tax is not being calculated for a sales order on a new machine. When attempting to run Tax Calculation on a new Traverse workstation, the customer encounters the following error: "The underlying connection was closed: An unexpected error occurred on a send."

Resolution
This usually occurs because the workstation does not support or is not using the correct TLS version.
Older Windows systems or .NET Framework configurations may not default to TLS 1.2, causing the connection to be rejected by the remote server.
To fix this, we would need to run the attached file on the Registry editor on the user’s PC.
The file contains both 32 bit and 64 bit, we have to verify that the PC is either 32 or 64 , for that thee are multiple ways.
Method 1: Using System Information Tool
- Press Windows + R to open the Run dialog.

- Type msinfo32 and press Enter.

- In the System Information window, look for System Type:
- If it says x64-based PC, you have a 64-bit system.

- If it says x86-based PC, you have a 32-bit system.

Method 2: Using Command Prompt
1.     Press Windows + R, type cmd, and press Enter.
2.     In the Command Prompt window, type the following command:
echo %PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE%
- Press Enter.
- If it returns AMD64, your system is 64-bit.

- If it returns x86, your system is 32-bit.

Once the system type is confirmed, proceed with the appropriate registry update.

Open the registry editor and run it as an administrator.



Next, click File → Import and select the appropriate 32-bit or 64-bit registry file you downloaded.
Once the import is successful, a popup will appear stating: “…successfully added to the registry.”

After completing this step, try running the tax calculation again. It should now complete successfully.

29b4adec-12ee-4fc2-90b8-069ca49fda18.title: Remove incorrect statement in Bank Rec Clear transaction

Add the filter with Statement date of 12/31/2025, along with the 'Bank Account ID' as needed. Then check the checkbox "Do the following, then check the box" and click OK.

This ensures that the specific statement belonging to only the intent Bank gets purged, without disturbing any of the other Statements with the same Date.

This will remove the statement from the Bank Rec cleared transaction screen, which was created in error.

8f7fefc8-232e-433f-b101-b9cd750e245b.title: Understanding Bank Reconciliation – Cleared Transactions
8f7fefc8-232e-433f-b101-b9cd750e245b.content:
Problem
The Bank Reconciliation functionality allows users to capture, store, and utilize bank statement information for identifying, matching, and referencing cleared transactions.
Within the Reconciliation menu, two reports are available:
- Obsolete Report: Retained only for backward compatibility. Hidden from the menu by default.

- Active Report: Contains extended and updated reconciliation features.

This article explains how to process Cleared Transactions using the Bank Reconciliation module.

Cause
General Overview of Functions in the Bank Reconciliation Cleared Transactions Screen

Resolution
Step 1: Access Cleared Transactions
- Navigate to: Bank Reconciliation → Reconciliation → Cleared Transactions.
- On the Cleared Transactions screen:- Select a Bank Account ID from the header.
- On the Statement tab, enter details from your bank statement.
- The Fiscal Period/Year defaults from the Ending Date but can be changed to any valid period/year.
- Multiple statements can share the same period/year for a given account.
-

- The following fields auto-update at the bottom of the screen:
- Currency ID – Currency linked to the bank account.
- Current GL Balance – Transactions posted to GL (excluding those outside the fiscal year/period).
- Outstanding – Total uncleared transactions (Deposits, Disbursements, Adjustments, Transfers).
- Adjusted – Total cleared transactions (same tabs).
- Statement – Ending Balance entered on the Statement tab.
Step 2: Clear Transactions in Bulk
Use Select All on Deposits, Disbursements, Adjustments, or Transfers tabs to mark all transactions as cleared.
Step 3: Process Cleared Transactions
Click the OK button on the toolbar to process the cleared transactions.
This action links the cleared entries to the statement, ensuring they no longer appear when reconciling future statements.
Step 4: Toggle Cleared Status
Use the Toggle button to switch the “Cleared” status of all the cleared transactions to uncleared and vice versa.
Step 5: Unselect Transactions
Use the Unselect All button to mark all transactions in the list as not cleared.
Step 6: Apply Filters
Use the Filter icon on column headings to refine the transaction list.
After filtering, apply Select All or Unselect All to update only the displayed transactions.
Step 7: Mark Statement as Reconciled
Click the Change Status button on the toolbar to set the statement to Reconciled.
This is optional but prevents further updates.
The status can be changed back to Open if modifications are required.

1df8a2e7-1094-48f2-b1f4-796ebdb7a3f2.title: How to Set up Terminals in Traverse
1df8a2e7-1094-48f2-b1f4-796ebdb7a3f2.content:
Problem
How to Set up Terminal

Resolution
To set up Terminals, follow these steps:
1. Select Terminals from the Setup and Maintenance menu

2. The Terminals screen appears.

3. Select the New Record button on the toolbar to open a blank Terminal record.
4. Enter a Terminal ID in the Terminal ID field. This is a reference for the terminal
configuration you will set up.
5. If applicable, select a Terminal ID from which to copy settings in the Copy From field. All the
information from the Terminal ID selected to Copy From, will be copied into the new
Terminal ID.
6. Enter or edit a Description in the Description field. This would be a more descriptive term
for this Terminal ID.
7. If applicable, enter or select a Location ID in the Store ID field. The Store ID lookup box
refers to your inventory warehouse Locations.
8. Enter a transaction prefix in the Prefix field. The transaction Prefix is added to the
Transaction Number to generate unique Transaction IDs for each Terminal ID.
9. Enter a message to appear on the Terminal menu in the Message field. The text may contain one or more menu message tokens. You can drag and drop message tokens from the Message Token list into the Message field.

Tokens
Tokens are a type of variable that represents a context-sensitive value that can be included in
an output. They are placeholders that show a real-time value when the software runs.
Example: A Receipt Header could be established to include the Current Date,
Terminal ID, and User ID using the following combination of text and token
values:

10. If you want a default Sales Rep for the Terminal, enter or select a Sales Rep in the Sales
Rep field.
11. Enter or select a default Payment Method for the Terminal in the Payment Method field.
12. Enter or select a Tax Group in the Tax Group field. This will determine if sales tax is
calculated for the transactions entered through the Terminal.
13. Enter or select a Distribution Code in the Dist Code field.
14. If applicable, enter a Maximum Discount percentage allowed in the Max Discount (%)
field. A value of 0 means there is no Maximum Discount percentage.
15. If applicable, enter the number of days before a Layaway is due to be paid in full in the
Layaway Days field. A value of 0 means there is no default due date.
16. Select the Printer Option you want to use for this terminal: Receipt, Invoice, Both or
Prompt.
17. Select the Printer Configuration button to set up the Form Printers for this Terminal for
Receipts and Invoices.
18. Enter a text value to include on the header and/or footer of the receipt in the Receipt
Header and/or the Receipt Footer fields. Text may contain one or more receipt tokens. You
can drag and drop message tokens from the Receipt Tokens list into the Receipt Header
and/or the Receipt Footer fields



19. Click the Save button to save the terminal setup, or any changes made to the terminal.

f229b9db-82b5-4417-8b57-c4e8bd159695.title: Assign a TRAVERSE Terminal User to a Terminal
f229b9db-82b5-4417-8b57-c4e8bd159695.content:
Problem
How to Assign a TRAVERSE Terminal User to a Terminal

Resolution
Now that you have created a user and a terminal, you need to tie the TRAVERSE user to the terminal through the TRAVERSE.POS.exe.config file. This file is used by the POS executable on the terminal to identify the TRAVERSE servers, license port, default company, logout delay, and the user with which to connect to TRAVERSE.

NOTE: You may use the same configuration file on multiple terminals if the company ID, system database, license server, and license port configuration information is the same for all terminals.

1. Click on the Config Generator button on the toolbar to open the configuration generator popup window

2. The Config Generator screen appears.
3. Enter a default company for the terminal in the Company ID field.
The current TRAVERSE company populates the Company ID field by default.
This would be your 3 digit company ID used when selecting a company on the File,
Change Company selection.
4. Enter the TRAVERSE system database in the System Database field.
The current TRAVERSE system database populates this field by default.
This usually has SYS as the database name for the system database.
You can get this information by opening the License Server Manager on your SQL
server.
• Enter the TRAVERSE License Server IP address or name in the License Server field.
• This field automatically populates with the current TRAVERSE system license server
information.
• The name of the server that has SQL installed on it is typically the license server. An
example of a license server name might be SQLSERVER. This is not the server and
SQL instance name, just the server computer name.
• You can get this information by opening the License Server Manager on your SQL
server.
5. Enter the TRAVERSE License Server port number in the License Port field.
• This field automatically populates with the current TRAVERSE system License Server
information.
• By default this port number is 2113.
• You can get this information by opening the License Server Manager on your SQL
server.
6. Select the check box to set up the terminal in Disconnected Mode.
The Point of Sale terminal application can be configured in one of two ways:
• Connected - The POS application has a full-time connection to the main TRAVERSE
database. Transactions are recorded directly to the POS tables in the TRAVERSE
database. The Active Order Processing function in TRAVERSE synchronizes the
Inventory quantity, history, and transactional cost retrieval between the POS tables
and the main TRAVERSE database.
• Disconnected - The POS application uses a local database on each sales terminal to
retain transactional data. The local terminal databases are synchronized with the
POS tables in the TRAVERSE database via a Synchronize function on the terminal.
The data in the POS tables is then updated in the main TRAVERSE database
automatically via the Active Order Processing function.
7. Accept or enter the Data Provider folder value.
This should not need to be changed. This is the path to the Data Provider folder, which
stores the data provider files TRAVERSE uses to process data.
8. Enter or select the logout delay in minutes into the Logout Delay field. A value of 0 means
there is no logout delay for the terminal.
9. Enter the login name of the User you created for the Terminal to access TRAVERSE into the
Login Name field.
This is a TRAVERSE User ID, not the POS User ID set up in the prior section of this
manual. You can set up a User for this purpose in the SM Administration, User setup
function.
10. Enter the login Password for the User you created for the Terminal to access TRAVERSE,
into the Login Password field.
This is a TRAVERSE User password, not the POS User set up in the prior section of this
manual. You can set up a User for this purpose in the SM Administration, User setup
function.
11. Select the Print Mode for this terminal. The available selections are:
• Print - will automatically print the receipts and invoices generated from the POS
Terminal transaction entry. The printer used will be the printers set up in the Invoice
Printer and Receipt Printer fields in the Terminal setup screen.
• Demo - will preview a copy of the receipts and invoices generated from the POS
Terminal transaction entry.
12. Select the UI Culture to be used for this terminal. The default is en-US.
13. In the Payment Service section:
• Enter the Terminal ID, User ID, Merchant Key, and Password the terminal(s) should
use to send payment data to your Payment Service Provider.
• If the Payment Device Type and Standard Entry Class fields are populated, check
the values and edit only if necessary.
14. Click the Generate button. This creates the TRAVERSE.POS.exe.config file for the
Terminal. A dialog box will open to allow you to choose where to save the configuration file.
Select the folder within which to save the file, then click OK.
15. A notification popup window will display to let you know the file has been generated. Click
OK to close the popup window.
16. Close the Config Generator popup window by clicking on the red “X” in the upper right
corner of the window.
17. When you set up the terminal, copy the TRAVERSE.POS.exe.config file you just created to
the same location as the TRAVERSE.POS.exe file on the terminal.
