4bb953b7-8355-4e87-8440-7750076fb4a9.title: Why Fiscal Period/Year Entries Differ Between 'AP Open Invoice View' and 'Transaction History View'
4bb953b7-8355-4e87-8440-7750076fb4a9.content:
Problem
There is a discrepancy between the Fiscal period/year displayed in the AP Open Invoice View and the actual Fiscal period/year of the transaction as reflected in the Transaction History View.

Specifically, within the AP Open Invoice View, the fiscal period/year may appear as a different period than the one recorded for the same transaction in the Transaction History View. Upon reviewing the Transaction History, it becomes evident that the fiscal period associated with the transaction does not align with what is shown in the AP Open Invoice View.

What causes the fiscal period/year entries in the AP Open Invoice View to differ from those in the Transaction History View?

Resolution
The Fiscal Year and Fiscal Period values displayed in the AP Open Invoice View are derived from the AP Transaction Table at the time the transaction is posted. Under normal circumstances, these values remain consistent with the corresponding records in the Transaction History View.  [The transaction History View can be accessed by double-clicking the 'Transaction ID' field]

However, when a payment is voided, the behavior changes. In such scenarios, the Fiscal Period recorded in the AP Open Invoice View does not reference the original transaction history. Instead, it reflects the Fiscal Period/Year of the void transaction. This is the primary reason why discrepancies may be observed between the AP Open Invoice View and the Transaction History View.

To validate this behavior, we can:

-
Navigate to the Column Chooser within the AP Open Invoice View.

-
Add the “Void Created Date” column.

-
Compare the Void Created Date with the Fiscal Period field.

This comparison helps confirm whether the Fiscal Period displayed corresponds to the period in which the void action occurred, rather than the original posting period.

1f37a214-9fff-4471-a265-1388561d342a.title: Creating a Bank Transfer Entry in the Bank Reconciliation Module
1f37a214-9fff-4471-a265-1388561d342a.content:
Problem
Users need to create a bank transfer entry within the Bank Reconciliation module to record the movement of funds between two bank accounts.

Resolution
- The transaction number is generated by the system and displayed in the Trans No field.
- Enter the transaction date in the Trans Date field.
- Enter the Fiscal Period and Fiscal Year for the transfer, or accept the default values provided by the system.
- Enter the Reference for the transfer, or use the default transfer reference. References post to the General Ledger (GL) journal and provide an additional method for locating transactions in the GL.
Note: You can change the default transfer reference using the Business Rules function.

- Enter a Description for the transfer, or use the default description.
Note: You can change the default transfer description using the Business Rules function.

- The Currency ID field is view-only if multicurrency is enabled. Any active Currency ID may be selected for new transaction entries. The transaction entry is not restricted to the bank currency.
- Enter the Amount of the transfer.
- Select the Bank Account ID to which the money is being transferred in the To Bank field.
- Enter the Reference for the transfer or use the previously entered transfer reference. The BR transfer-to reference is configured in the Business Rules function.
Note: References post to the GL journal and can be used for transaction searches in the General Ledger.

327d4adc-a01f-4825-b65d-779b61c9a476.content:
Problem
How to void Payroll Checks

Resolution
Steps to void a Payroll Check

How to void payroll checks:
- We can choose the Data Filter to select the range of filtering options or leave the filter blank to include all available data.

- Void date field: used to select a date for which to void the selected checks.

- Fiscal Period/Year fields: used to select the fiscal period and year for which to void the selected checks.

- We will have to make sure that the check being voided contains the same fiscal period and year for which the original check was made.

Checkboxes:
- Select the Create transactions from history checkbox, if applicable, to re-create the transaction in the transaction history file to calculate a corrected check.

Note: Time ticket transaction records are deleted from transaction history when you void a check.
In short, it takes all the time made on the check and puts it back to the daily work.


- Select the Create checks for voided manual checks checkbox, if applicable, to re-create a corrected manual check using the Manual Checks function.

Note: Only select this checkbox if you select a manual check to void and you want to prepare a corrected check.


- This one is if I do a manual check - take that manual check and put it back out into the manual check. If the entire check was wrong and it is not easier, and you want to start all over, then uncheck both of these. If you do want to go back out and make some changes, then you can leave the checkboxes checked. This applies to the manual check as well.

- The comments field is not mandatory.

Then, we can click on the Apply button on the toolbar to display the posted checks matching the selected criteria.
- Select the checks to void by selecting the Void checkbox adjacent to the check number.

- We can also use the Select All command button to select all of the displayed posted checks, or use the Unselect All command button to deselect the selected posted checks. Once done, we can "Write" the check



Simple Clarifications:
When you void a payroll check, the system automatically creates entries to reverse the original payroll. These entries affect different accounts, and here’s where the system gets the information from:
CR means Credit and DB means Debit
Bank (Cash) Account
It uses the bank account setup to know which cash account to update.
Taxes Withheld and Employer Tax Liabilities
These come from the Tax Authority settings.
Employee Deductions and Employer Contributions
These accounts are pulled from the Deductions and Employer Costs setup (like insurance or retirement plans).
Wages and Employer Expenses
These come from the Department setup linked to the employee.
So, when a check is voided, the system looks at your payroll setup to post the correct reversals - canceling out the original amounts from the paycheck.

6791be8b-1dd0-416d-b77c-3ceb6c91f3cd.title: Troubleshooting RDP Cache Issues Causing Traverse Login Failures
6791be8b-1dd0-416d-b77c-3ceb6c91f3cd.content:
Problem
A user reported difficulties accessing Cloud Traverse through their existing Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) file. Despite having valid credentials and confirmed network connectivity, the login attempts were unsuccessful.

The issue specifically occurs during the first login attempt each morning. When the user tries to launch Traverse via the RDP file, the application screen continues to spin without progressing. The expected “Show Details” option does not appear, leaving the session unresponsive.

To proceed, the user is forced to manually terminate the stalled RDP session through the Task Manager. Even after ending the session, they must reattempt the login process multiple times—often two or more attempts—before finally being able to connect successfully to Traverse.

This recurring behavior causes inconvenience and delays at the start of the user’s workday, highlighting the need for a resolution.

Cause
The cache will be stored in the following path:

C:\Users\<Username>\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Terminal Server Client\Cache

This Cache is used by the Remote Desktop Client to save connection details, and session data to improve the performance of future connections.

However, over time these cached files may become outdated or corrupted, especially if:

- A new RDP configuration is generated,
- Cloud server settings (IP, certificates, or credentials) are updated, or
- The existing RDP file no longer matches the current environment.

In such cases, the old cache interferes with new connection attempts, causing login issues.

Resolution
In order to resolve this issue, the User needs to follow the steps below:

i. Remove the Old RDP File:

Delete the previously downloaded RDP file from the client’s system to prevent reuse of outdated settings.



ii. Find the Windows Login Name:

-
Open the Command Prompt and type the following command: whoami

-
The output will display the currently logged-in Windows username.

-
This username will help in identifying the correct user profile folder under C:\Users.

-
In cases where multiple usernames appear under C:\Users, ensure that you use the profile corresponding to the logged-in user.



iii. Clear the Remote Desktop Cache:

- Navigate to the following path: C:\Users\<Username>\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Terminal Server Client\Cache


- Delete all files inside the Cache folder.





- This action clears outdated or corrupted Remote Desktop cache data and forces the RDP client to rebuild a fresh cache during the next login.



Note: This step is safe and does not affect other system operations.



iv. Download and Use a New RDP File:

-
Download a new RDP file generated from the Cloud Traverse environment. Please follow the steps illustrated in the Document for downloading the new RDP File: https://connect.aptean.com/s/article/How-to-Download-RDP-file-for-Cloud-SaaS-Users

-
Add a shortcut or copy it over to the Desktop as needed.

-
Launch the new RDP file and proceed with login.

The login issue was caused by outdated cached files conflicting with the old RDP configuration. Deleting the old RDP file, clearing the cache, and downloading a new RDP file will resolve the issue, restoring normal login functionality.

dac31927-0ddc-40b1-9ddc-65da777a8ce9.title: Payroll Update Sync Issue
dac31927-0ddc-40b1-9ddc-65da777a8ce9.content:
Problem
During the IPM to Payroll update, the system incorrectly indicated that there were no changes despite the addition of two new employees in IPM who did not appear in Payroll. Additionally, the system failed to remove the termination dates for two re-hired employees entered into the IPM system, causing payroll processing delays.

Cause
The date entered in the IPM to Payroll screen is set earlier than the date the new employees or updates were entered in IPM. As a result, those updates are excluded from the transfer.

Resolution
The IPM to Payroll process transfers employee information and changes made in IPM into Payroll. The date entered on this screen acts as a cutoff. Any changes made in IPM on or before this date are included in the transfer; changes made after this date are not.

- Go to Payroll → Periodic Processing → Setup and Maintenance → IPM to Payroll.

-
Check the date entered in the IPM to Payroll screen.

- Confirm whether the changes or new employees were added to IPM after this date.

- If necessary, adjust the date so that it covers the time period of the new or updated employee data.

- Rerun the IPM to Payroll process to transfer the updates into Payroll.

Recommendation
Always ensure the date entered in the IPM to Payroll screen is current enough to capture any new employee data or changes made in IPM.
Additional Information
If updates are still missing after adjusting the date, verify that the IPM changes were properly saved and approved before running the IPM to Payroll process.

0f36c648-41c0-4251-9fb6-a5d7ff79414d.title: How to Compute Period Depreciation
0f36c648-41c0-4251-9fb6-a5d7ff79414d.content:
Problem
How to use the Period Depreciation function to calculate the depreciation of active assets

Resolution
Compute Period Depreciation
The Compute Period Depreciation function allows you to:
- Calculate depreciation of active assets

- Generate the Period Depreciation Report

- Post period depreciation

Note: Before you can calculate or post depreciation, ensure that the permissions for Fixed Assets Compute Period Depreciation are updated.
Steps to Compute Depreciation
- Select Depreciation Types
- Check the Calculate box next to the types of depreciation you want to process for this period.

- BOOK depreciation is the only type that affects the General Ledger.

- FEDTAX depreciation is used for preparing the Depreciation Tax Report at year-end.

-
Set Period Values
Use the default values in the Beginning Period, Ending Period, and GL Period fields, or adjust them as needed:
- Beginning Period – The first period you want to compute depreciation for. (This will update to the next period after posting.)

- Ending Period – The last period you want to compute depreciation for. (This will also update after posting.)

- Fiscal Period – Displays the current fiscal period. You may change it to the period where depreciation should post.

Example: To calculate depreciation for the entire year at once:
- Beginning Period = 1

- Ending Period = 12

- Fiscal Period = 12 (depreciation will post entirely to period 12).

- Run the Calculation
- Depreciation will be calculated based on the methods you use and the number of periods in your fiscal year.

- This determines whether depreciation should be calculated and posted at the end of each accounting period.

07ed6737-9134-4341-8ad5-1d58c4c47c5b.title: User Defined Data Type Issue - Cannot find data type
07ed6737-9134-4341-8ad5-1d58c4c47c5b.content:
Problem
When moving from an old SQL instance to a new SQL Instance, a user may receive an error using the software such as "Column, parameter, or variable #10: Cannot find data type pDecimal. " This is due to missing User-Defined Data Types (UDDTs) in SQL's model and tempdb system databases. Traverse requires these UDDTs for SQL processes throughout the software. Other examples of UDDTs are: pItemId, pCustId, pCurrency, pTransId and many more.

When a new Traverse database is created, the UDDTs are added to the model and tempdb databases. If a new SQL Instance is created, such as with a server move, the new instance will not have the UDDTs needed for Traverse's SQL processes.

Important Note
If the above error is encountered and the user is on the same SQL instance they have been on, the UDDTs may not be an issue. Its possible that there is a programming issue at hand in that circumstance.
See the Additional Info section below on how to verify this.

Cause
Missing User-Defined Data Types in SQL's model and tempdb databases.

Resolution
- Connect to the SQL Instance where Traverse's databases currently reside

- In the Object Browser, right-click on a Traverse company database, then Tasks > Generate Scripts

- Follow the prompts in the wizard
- Click "Next"


- Click the radio button for "Select specific database objects"


- Click "User-Defined Data Types" and then "Next"


- Click "Open in new query window" and then "Next"


- Click "Next" after reviewing your selections

- Click "Finish"


- Edit the script to remove the USE [DBNAME HERE] and GO portion. We will toggle the database we want the script executed against in the next step.


- Toggle the model database and execute the script

- Toggle the tempdb database and execute the script

- Grant permission to the public group for model and tempdb. This ensures the new UDDTs can be used in software processes.
- Paste this script into a new query window.
SELECT 'GRANT REFERENCES ON TYPE ::DBO.' + name + ' TO public' + CHAR(13) + CHAR(10) + 'GO' + CHAR(13) + CHAR(10) FROM sys.types WHERE name like 'p%'

- From the menu, navigate to "Query" > "Results To", click "Results to Text."


- Click "Execute" to create a script for us granting permission for all the UDDTs to the public group

- Copy the entire results section and paste into a new query window


- Toggle the model database and execute the script


- Toggle the tempdb database and execute the script


- The task is complete. The UDDTs have now been created and are available for the software's processes.

91f7afb3-381e-434b-acf9-513c517b8e95.title: Is printing from Info-Alert possible?
91f7afb3-381e-434b-acf9-513c517b8e95.content:
Problem
Is printing from Info-Alert possible?

Resolution
Info-Alert supports printing Alert and Action outputs to printers configured within the Windows Printers folder. These printers must be assigned to Info-Alert using the Printer Output Groups screen available under the Configuration Options menu.
Navigation: Configuration > Configuration Options > Printer Output Groups.
By default, there are three pre-defined Output IDs (Report IDs) assigned to the Windows default printer. These typically cover the standard report output needs in most Info-Alert environments. However, administrators can add additional Output ID records as needed to meet specific reporting requirements.
To configure printer output:
Printer Output Configuration in Info-Alert
1. Add a New Output ID
- Use the New Record button at the bottom of the screen to add a new Output ID.

- Enter a Description/Heading, select a frequency for outputting alert results to a printer, and choose a Printer.

2. Assign or Change a Printer
- You can change the printer assigned to an Output ID by selecting from the Printer drop-down list.

- If the required printer is not listed, you must add it through the Windows Printers folder.
- Once the printer is available in Windows, it will become selectable in Info-Alert.

- For best results, avoid using ‘(Default)’ and select a named printer instead.

- Important:
On the IA Server, the selected Windows printer must be a physical printer.
Logical devices such as ‘Send to OneNote’ or ‘Microsoft XPS Document Writer’ are not supported.

3. Set Print Frequency
- In the Freq column, select how often Info-Alert should send configured report results to the printer.

- Frequency options include: Always (A), Hourly (H), Daily, Weekly, or Monthly.
- Example: An alert may send emails daily, but you might want to print reports only once a week.

- If Info-Alert runs multiple times per day, Hourly (H) or Always (A) can help prevent missing reports.

4. Review Print Activity
- Click the Details button at the end of each record to view the date and time of the most recent print activity for that Output ID.

Note: Printer Output Groups can only be configured from the full installation of Info-Alert Manager. Remote clients (Manager-only installs) do not have access to maintain this configuration.

f7bc52d1-26c8-4eda-82da-3f530eba3390.title: How to add the Column 'Customer Name' in the SO Open Order Detail View of Traverse 11.2?
f7bc52d1-26c8-4eda-82da-3f530eba3390.content:
Problem
How to add the Column 'Customer Name' in the SO Open Order Detail View?

Resolution
The base query retrieves data primarily from the Sales Order Transaction Detail view (trav_tblSoTransDetail_view) and enriches it with information from:

-
Sales Order Header (tblSoTransHeader) → provides header-level fields such as transaction type, customer ID, shipping, invoice, and charges.

-
Freight Terms (tblSmFreightTerm) → adds the freight term description.

However, the Customer Name is not directly available in either the Sales Order Detail or Header transaction tables/views.

Note: Since the Customer Name is not stored in any Sales Order transaction tables or views, we extend the query to join with the Customer Master table/view to include it.

To achieve this:

-
Use the Customer ID (CustId) from the Sales Order Header (tblSoTransHeader).

-
Join it with the Customer Master view (trav_tblArCust_View), which contains the CustName.

-
Alias this column as CustomerName for consistency in the output.

This ensures that the output includes all the necessary Sales Order transaction detail fields, enriched with the actual Customer Name from the Customer master data.



Key Tables / Views Involved:

-
trav_tblSoTransDetail_view (Alias: d)

-
Stores Sales Order line-level transaction details.

-
Includes item, quantity, pricing, cost, and shipment information.

-
tblSoTransHeader (Alias: h)

-
Stores Sales Order header-level information.

-
Provides fields such as CustId, ShipToId, transaction type, dates, and totals.

-
tblSmFreightTerm (Alias: f)

-
Provides descriptive information about the Freight Terms.

-
trav_tblArCust_View (Alias: c)

-
Customer Master view.

-
Stores the Customer Name (CustName) and other customer-related details.



i. Access Design Studio and access the 'Views Table' under the 'System Data' section
ii. Scroll down to find the ID of SoOrder
iii. Click on Customize on the toolbar

iv. Once the 'Customize' icon is chosen, it opens the Custom View Editor screen as shown below. Then click on the ellipsis (...) next to Data Source:

v. Update the query with the logic as required:

SELECT *
FROM (
SELECT d.TransID, d.EntryNum, d.LocId, d.ItemId, d.ItemType, d.Descr, d.CatId
, d.GLAcctSales, d.GLAcctCOGS, d.GLAcctInv
, SIGN(h.TransType) * d.QtyOrdSell AS QtyOrdSell
, d.UnitsSell, d.UnitsBase
, SIGN(h.TransType) * d.QtyShipSell AS QtyShipSell
, SIGN(h.TransType) * d.QtyShipBase AS QtyShipBase
, SIGN(h.TransType) * d.QtyBackordSell AS QtyBackordSell
, d.PriceID
, CASE WHEN GrpId IS NULL THEN d.UnitPriceSell ELSE 0 END AS UnitPriceSell
, CASE WHEN GrpId IS NULL THEN d.UnitPriceSellFgn ELSE 0 END AS UnitPriceSellFgn
, d.UnitCostSell, d.UnitCostSellFgn
, CASE WHEN GrpId IS NULL THEN SIGN(h.TransType) * d.PriceExt ELSE 0 END AS PriceExt
, CASE WHEN GrpId IS NULL THEN SIGN(h.TransType) * d.PriceExtFgn ELSE 0 END AS PriceExtFgn
, SIGN(h.TransType) * d.CostExtFgn AS CostExtFgn
, SIGN(h.TransType) * d.CostExt AS CostExt
, ISNULL(d.ReqShipDate, h.ReqShipDate) AS ReqShipDate
, CASE WHEN d.QtyShipSell > 0 THEN ISNULL(d.ActShipDate, h.ActShipDate) ELSE NULL END AS ActShipDate
, SIGN(h.TransType) * d.OrigOrderQty AS OrigOrderQty
, d.BinNum, d.ConversionFactor, d.LottedYN, d.InItemYN, ISNULL(d.Rep1Id, h.Rep1Id) AS Rep1Id
, ISNULL(d.Rep1Pct, h.Rep1Pct) AS Rep1Pct, ISNULL(d.Rep2Id, h.Rep2Id) AS Rep2Id, ISNULL(d.Rep2Pct, h.Rep2Pct) AS Rep2Pct
, d.[Status], SIGN(h.TransType) * d.TotQtyOrdSell AS TotQtyOrdSell
, SIGN(h.TransType) * d.TotQtyShipSell AS TotQtyShipSell
, d.ResCode, d.UnitPriceSellBasis, d.UnitPriceSellBasisFgn
, CAST(CASE WHEN GrpId IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS bit) AS ComponentYn
, h.TransType, h.CustId, h.SoldToId, h.ShipToId, h.ShipToName, h.CustPONum, h.ShipVia, h.TransDate, h.BatchId, h.InvcDate
, h.PrintAcknowStatus, h.PrintPackStatus, h.PrintInvcStatus, h.PrintPickStatus
, d.CustomerPartNumber
, f.[Description] AS FreightTerm, h.FreightAccountNumber, h.ResidentialYN, h.DeliverySurcharge
, h.GlobalLocationNumber, h.TotalCharges, h.TotalCharges * h.ExchRate AS TotalChargesFgn
, h.ActualWeight, h.ReqDeliveryDate
, h.CurrencyID, h.Hold, h.ValidAddress

-- ✅ ADD-ON COLUMN
, c.CustName AS CustomerName

FROM [{COMP}].dbo.trav_tblSoTransDetail_view d
INNER JOIN [{COMP}].dbo.tblSoTransHeader h
ON d.TransId = h.TransId
LEFT JOIN [{COMP}].dbo.tblSmFreightTerm f
ON h.FreightTermID = f.ID
-- ✅ ADD-ON JOIN
LEFT JOIN [{COMP}].dbo.trav_tblArCust_View c
ON h.CustId = c.CustId

WHERE h.VoidYn = 0
) ds

v. Use 'Preview Results' and if the results meet the requirement:

vi. Click on 'Execute $ Accept Query' to update the Data source:



vii. Add the newly added Column in the 'Available' section and hit on 'OK':

viii. Open Traverse. [If it was already open, Close and reopen Traverse]. Open the 'SO Open Order Detail View' and we can observe the Column 'Customer Name' from the Column Chooser:

2c8a1a74-48a8-4645-b5e0-96b40ce5c8d9.title: How to correct the Payroll Transaction, where the Deductions were not taken out properly for an Employee?
2c8a1a74-48a8-4645-b5e0-96b40ce5c8d9.content:
Problem
How to correct the Payroll Transaction, where the Deductions were no taken out properly for an Employee?

In some cases, a payroll transaction may be processed without applying the necessary employee deductions such as tax withholdings, health insurance contributions, retirement savings, or other mandatory deductions. This can occur due to setup issues, incorrect deduction codes, or manual oversight during payroll processing. [This typically occurs for a newly set up employee whose Deductions were not properly configured, or the Employee's Deductions were recently updated.]

Example Scenario:
Let us consider an example:
An employee’s paycheck should have included deductions for health insurance ($X) or a retirement contribution ($Y). However, after payroll was processed, the system only applied the 401(k) deduction, and the other deductions were skipped. [The issue was caught before posting of Checks, however, the 'Calculate Checks' was already done]
As a result:
- The employee’s net pay was overstated, leading to overpayment.
- The company’s payroll and financial records became inaccurate, potentially affecting compliance and statutory reporting.

In such situations, it becomes necessary to correct the payroll transaction to ensure both the employee’s pay and the company’s financial/statutory reporting remain accurate. This article explains the steps required to make such corrections.

In the below example, we could see that only the 401K Deduction was taken out of the Check:

NOTE:
This issue may arise due to:
- Incorrect or incomplete setup of deduction codes for a newly onboarded employee
- Recent updates to an employee’s deduction details not being reflected in the payroll system
- Manual oversight during the payroll processing stage

Resolution
When deductions are not properly calculated during the Payroll Check Calculation process, the recommended approach is to manually correct the issue by creating a separate check specifically for the missing deduction amounts.

This ensures that the employee’s payroll record reflects the accurate deduction amounts without requiring adjustments to the original paycheck that has already been processed. By issuing a manual check for the deduction value, both the company’s payroll records and the employee’s year-to-date balances will remain accurate.

Steps to Correct Missing Deductions:

i. The user is advised to enter a new Payroll Manual Check for the affected employee in the PA Manual Checks screen under the path: Applications -> Payroll -> Payday Work -> Manual Checks:

ii. In the pop-up window, enter the same payroll details as the current pay run. Then click OK to proceed.

iii. Pull up the required Employee record, and go to the 'Deductions' Tab to review the deductions that were already applied in the payroll run.

iv. Click on the '+' icon and add the 'Deductions' as required and enter the amount to be added.  [NOTE: This amount needs to be calculated manually]

Then hit on 'Save' at the top to save the changes:

v. Now, if we review the 'Edit Register', we will be able to observe the right 'Deductions' being added:

9be99a43-e08c-4a61-a2c6-3f616108d3df.title: How to take backups of the IA (InfoAlert) server data.
9be99a43-e08c-4a61-a2c6-3f616108d3df.content:
Problem
How to take backups of the IA (InfoAlert) server data.

Resolution Steps:
- Access Administrative Information:
Navigate to Configuration -> Configuration Options -> Administrative Information in the IA server interface.

- Open the Misc Tab:
Click on the Misc tab, which is the fifth header tab on the Administrative Information screen.

- Initiate Manual Backup:
Click the Backup button on the Misc tab. This will start a manual backup of the IA database and create a file named IAData.bak in the IABackup folder located within the InfoAlert root directory.

- Understand Automatic Backup:
The IA Server automatically performs a daily backup of the IA database, saving the IAData.bak file to the same IABackup folder.

- Integrate Backup into Nightly Routine:
Ensure that the IAData.bak file in the IABackup folder is included as part of your existing nightly backup solution.

- Backup via SSMS (Optional):
You can also back up the IA database through SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS). Log in to the InfoAlert SQL instance using admin credentials and follow the standard SQL Server backup procedures as described in the knowledge base article for data backups. KB Number #000079509

d2aa9588-3223-4c88-845f-c32118add651.title: Processing Refunds - Accounts Receivable
d2aa9588-3223-4c88-845f-c32118add651.content:
Problem
This article outlines the proper steps for processing customer refunds due to overpayments in the Accounts Receivable (AR) system. The process uses a pass-through liability account ("Refunds Payable") and involves transactions across AR, AP, and the General Ledger.

Note: Sample General Ledger (GL) accounts are used in the examples. Replace these with your organization’s actual GL account numbers.

Resolution
Step 1: Setup Requirements
A. Create “Refunds Payable” GL Account
- Set up a Refunds Payable account (e.g., 205101) on the Balance Sheet, typically placed after the Accounts Payable accounts.
- This account will act as a liability pass-through during refund processing.

B. Configure 'Refund' Payment Method
- In Accounts Receivable > Setup and Maintenance > Payment Methods, create a new ‘Other’ Payment Method.
- Assign the Credit GL Account as 205101 (Refunds Payable).


Step 2: Process Customer Refund
Scenario: Customer has a $100 Overpayment to be Refunded
1. Enter a Negative Cash Receipt in AR
- Apply the receipt either to the overpaid invoice or an “On Account” balance.
- Select the newly created Refund Payment Method.


2. Enter Invoice in Accounts Payable (AP)
- Create a vendor invoice payable to the customer.
- Use 205101 – Refunds Payable as the expense account on the invoice line.
- Prepare, print, and post the refund check to the customer/vendor.

99d097e3-8479-4af4-8e95-930d9c2eb2d6.title: How to retrieve the information in the 'IN Transactions' screen using SQL Query?
99d097e3-8479-4af4-8e95-930d9c2eb2d6.content:
Problem
How to retrieve the information in the 'IN Transactions' screen using SQL Query?



The User would like to retrieve the information as same as in the 'IN Transactions' screen, but from through SQL.

Resolution
The following SQL query can be used to extract data that mirrors the details available in the IN Transactions screen within Traverse. This query provides information such as item details, transaction type, location, cost adjustments, quantity, and comments:



SELECT
CASE TransType
WHEN 31 THEN 'Increase'
WHEN 32 THEN 'Decrease'
END AS [Type],
i.ItemId AS [Item ID],
i.Descr AS [Item Description],
t.LocId AS [Location ID],
c.Descr AS [Location Description],
t.GLAcctOffset AS [COGS Adj],
t.TransDate AS [Date],
t.SumYear AS [Year],
t.GLPeriod AS [Fiscal Period],
t.Uom AS [Unit],
t.Qty AS [Adj Qty],
t.CostUnitTrans AS [Unit Cost],
t.Qty * t.CostUnitTrans AS [Ext Cost],
t.Cmnt AS [Comments]
FROM dbo.tblInTrans t
INNER JOIN dbo.tblInItem i ON t.ItemId = i.ItemId
INNER JOIN dbo.tblInLoc c ON t.LocId = c.LocId;

Explanation of the Query:

-
Transaction Type (Increase/Decrease):
The CASE statement translates the transaction type codes (31 = Increase, 32 = Decrease) into readable text for clarity.

-
Item Information:
Retrieves the Item ID and Item Description from the Item Master (tblInItem).

-
Location Details:
Includes both the Location ID and Location Description by joining with the Location Master (tblInLoc).

-
Accounting Information:
Pulls the COGS Adjustment Account (GLAcctOffset) tied to the transaction.

-
Date and Periods:
Displays the Transaction Date, Fiscal Year (SumYear), and Fiscal Period (GLPeriod) to align with accounting records.

-
Units and Quantities:
Shows the Unit of Measure (UOM), the Adjusted Quantity (Adj Qty), and the Unit Cost.

-
Extended Cost:
Calculates the extended cost as Quantity × Unit Cost.

-
Comments:
Retrieves any notes entered with the transaction for additional context.



NOTE: This query will not return any posted IN Transactions. It only retrieves real-time entries currently sitting in the IN Transactions screen, i.e., those that have not yet been posted.

7f7c6434-27ee-494e-83bc-ed90f0085c66.title: How to reverse a Bank Reconciliation Transaction that was posted to an incorrect Period?
7f7c6434-27ee-494e-83bc-ed90f0085c66.content:
Problem
How to reverse a Bank Reconciliation Transaction that was posted to an incorrect Period?

In the example below, a 'Deposit' of $100 was made to Fiscal Period '8' of '2025.' However, it was intended for Period '9' of 2025. Now, the User prefers to reverse the incorrect entry posted to Fiscal Period '8':

Resolution
If a Bank Reconciliation Transaction has been posted to the wrong period, the recommended best practice is to handle the correction by entering offsetting entries of the same type [For example, reversing a Deposit through a negative Deposit].

This approach ensures proper audit tracking and provides clear visibility of both the error and its correction.

Steps to Correct the Error:
i. ﻿Access BR Transactions screen:
- Navigate to the 'BR Transactions' screen under the path: Applications -> Bank Reconciliation -> Transactions -> Transactions:

ii. Enter Reversing/Offsetting Transactions:
- Record the reversing entry as a negative deposit in the incorrect Period [In this example, we would be entering the Amount as -100.00 for the Period '8']
- Once entered, 'Save' the Transaction entry
- This will offset the original transaction and effectively clear out the incorrect entry.

ii. Review Journal and Post the Transactions:
- Now the User can proceed with printing the Transaction Journal in the 'BR transaction Journal' screen:

- Then, the User can post the same from the 'BR Post Transactions' screen:


iii. Visibility of Corrections:
- In the BR Clear Transactions screen, both the original incorrect deposit (positive) and the reversing entry (negative) will be visible.
- This side-by-side visibility of positive and negative entries makes it easier to identify that a correction was performed.
- The correct deposit in the appropriate Period will then reflect the proper transaction history.


Once the reversal was done, we can proceed with creating the entry in the intended Period again, as per the requirement.

NOTE:
- One possible approach would be to issue Positive BR Disbursements in the incorrect Fiscal Period/Year to offset the original, incorrectly entered BR Deposits.
- From a General Ledger perspective, the overall entries and the resulting ending BR balance would remain the same, ensuring the financial impact is neutralized.
- However, it is important to note the difference in how this appears within BR Cleared Transactions.
- Instead of the incorrect entries simply “washing out” against each other under Deposits, the system would show a balance in Deposits as well as a separate balance in Disbursements for the same error.
- This distinction makes the error more visible in reporting, since both sides of the adjustment are reflected rather than being offset in a single category.

f6736267-5860-4b5f-8343-9f101bb57300.content:
Problem
Why does the 'FA Retire Assets' screen shows only zero values for an 'Active Asset'?

Resolution
In order to proceed further, we would need to ensure that the specific Asset was not retired accidentally in the past. To confirm this, the User can filter out the specific Asset ID in the 'FA Retired Assets' view and observe if there were any history of retirement for that asset.



Verify if the Asset Was Previously Retired:

-
Navigate to the FA Retired Assets View under the path: Applications -> Fixed Assets -> Interactive Views -> FA Retired Assets View

-
Optional: Filter by the specific Asset ID in question.

-
Review the results to determine whether there is any history of retirement for the asset: If there is a record in the 'Retirement Date', it was already retired. If not, it is an actual 'Active Asset':



Outcome:

-
If a retirement history exists: This needs to be resolved via scripting, as the asset may have been retired in error previously.

-
If no retirement history exists: Proceed with the corrective steps below:



i. Access the FA Fixed Assets screen:

676fdd54-a552-4248-8175-bca4bc4a240e.title: What prevents the User from updating the GL Account Status and Description?
676fdd54-a552-4248-8175-bca4bc4a240e.content:
Problem
What prevents the User from updating the GL Account Status and Description?



When the User is attempting to update the 'Status' and 'Description' of a GL Account. But Traverse is throwing the below error stating, that the 'Account Type' cannot be changed for existing Accounts. While we are not making any changes to the 'Account Type':

Resolution
This situation is generally unlikely to occur under normal circumstances. It would only arise if an account was initially created correctly, but later the underlying SQL data table was directly modified and the Balance Type (Debit or Credit) was manually swapped to the opposite value.
As long as the 'GL Account Setup' is not altered directly in the Traverse UI, the account will function as expected. However, if a user subsequently attempts to make changes to this account within Traverse and then saves, the system will automatically validate all the account details. During this validation, Traverse will detect that the Balance Type does not align with the account configuration, and as a result, an error will be generated.

To address this situation, the following approaches can be taken depending on whether the account has historical transactions:
i. Accounts without history:
- If the account has no historical transactions, the recommended approach is to simply delete the account and then recreate it with the correct configuration.

ii. Accounts with history
- If the account has existing historical transactions, it cannot be deleted. In this case, the only way to proceed is to ensure that the Account Type correctly matches the Balance Type.
- The user will need to change the Account Type to one that is consistent with the Balance Type defined for the account.
- To update the 'Account Type', we need to click on to the drop-down, and choose the 'Account Type' aligning with the Balance Type:

- Once updated, update the 'Description' or 'Status' as needed and hit on 'Save' icon at the top to save the changes:

This error indicates that the necessary details have not been configured in the SM User Defaults screen. - In the 'Aptean Cloud Printing' section of the SM User Defaults screen, ensure the following details are completed:
- Account ID
- API Key
- Default Printer
- Enable Cloud Print: Yes
- Printing mode: Production
- Workstation Name: [Hostname/Workstation]

17ae3b94-4051-4dbe-8042-ab690f9a705b.title: How to export numerical values out of the Interactive Views for mathematical processes in Excel?
17ae3b94-4051-4dbe-8042-ab690f9a705b.content:
Problem
How to export numerical values out of the Interactive Views for mathematical processes in Excel?



Let us consider the below example of the 'PO Order View' screen:



When exported as an Excel, we can observe that the applied formula for a set of numerical values is formatted as 'Text' returning the result as '0':

Resolution
When exporting data from Interactive Views to an Excel file, the numerical values are often formatted as 'Text' instead of actual numerical data. This requires the client to manually update the format each time they generate an export, which can be time-consuming and prone to errors.

To ensure that numerical values are correctly exported as numbers rather than text, users can modify their User Preferences settings within the application. By configuring these preferences appropriately, the exported data will retain its intended numerical format, eliminating the need for manual adjustments and ensuring compatibility with calculations or further processing in Excel.



Steps to update 'Preferences':

i. In order to get this done, the User needs to navigate to the 'Preferences' under the path: View -> Preferences:



ii. Locate the setting 'Export Cells as Displayed'.

iii. And then switch the setting 'Export Cells as Displayed' to 'False'.

iv. Click on 'Save' icon at the top to save the changes and then close the 'Preferences' screen:



This update provides a seamless export experience, meeting the client’s requirements while improving efficiency. Now, when the User exports the 'PO Order View' this will assist us with the mathematical operations as required:



Benefits of This Configuration:

-
Ensures numerical values are correctly formatted as numbers.

-
Eliminates the need for manual formatting adjustments in Excel.

-
Enhances data accuracy and compatibility with mathematical operations.

-
Improves efficiency in handling exported reports.

Considerations and Limitations:

While this setting ensures numerical fields are exported in the correct format, it also affects fields that are encoded as numbers within the SQL database. Certain fields which are stored as numerical codes, will also be exported as numerical values. This may lead to interpretation challenges when reviewing the exported data.

In the given example, we can observe that the Column 'Transaction Type' is coded as numerical values, with the numerical codes correspond to the following values:

- 0  = Request
- 1  = Goods Received
- 2  = Invoice Received
- 9  = New Order
- -1 = New Return
- -2 = Debit Memo



NOTE:

Users are advised to enable this setting only when prioritizing numerical accuracy for fields such as Quantity and Item details. If categorical fields encoded as numbers require interpretation, the User can export the Excel as such.

By following this approach, users can optimize their data export process while maintaining the integrity and usability of the extracted information.

71ce8fc9-7317-44a6-a69b-a884ec0a6144.title: How to whitelist emails being sent from Traverse on the Mail Server?
71ce8fc9-7317-44a6-a69b-a884ec0a6144.content:
Problem
How to whitelist emails being sent from Traverse on the Mail Server?

Resolution
1. Whitelisting Emails in Microsoft Exchange Server

Step 1: Add Traverse Application to IP Allow List

-
Open the Exchange Admin Center (EAC).

-
Navigate to Protection > Connection Filter.

-
Click on Edit under the IP Allow List.

-
Enter the IP Address or Domain Name used by the Traverse application to send emails.

-
Click Save to apply changes.

Step 2: Create a Transport Rule for Additional Assurance

-
Go to Mail Flow > Rules.

-
Click New Rule > Create a new rule.

-
Enter a descriptive name, e.g., "Whitelist Traverse Emails".

-
Under Apply this rule if..., choose The sender’s domain is and enter the Traverse email domain.

-
Under Do the following, select Modify the message properties > Set the spam confidence level (SCL) to ‘-1’ (to bypass spam filtering).

-
Click Save.



2. Whitelisting Emails in Microsoft 365 (Office 365)

Step 1: Allow Traverse Email Domain in Microsoft Defender

-
Sign into Microsoft 365 Defender Portal at https://security.microsoft.com.

-
Navigate to Email & Collaboration > Policies & Rules > Threat Policies.

-
Under Anti-spam policies, select Allowed and Blocked Senders and Domains.

-
Add the Traverse email domain (e.g., @traverseapp.com) to the Allow list.

-
Click Save.

Step 2: Modify Mail Flow Rules (Transport Rule for Extra Assurance)

-
Open Exchange Admin Center.

-
Navigate to Mail Flow > Rules.

-
Click New Rule.

-
Follow the steps mentioned in the Exchange section to add a rule ensuring that emails from Traverse are not flagged as spam.





3. Whitelisting Emails in Google Workspace (Gmail)

Step 1: Allow Traverse Email Domain in Google Admin Console

-
Log into Google Admin Console at https://admin.google.com.

-
Navigate to Apps > Google Workspace > Gmail > Spam, Phishing, and Malware.

-
Click Add Setting under Email Allow List.

-
Enter the IP Address or Email Domain used by Traverse.

-
Click Save.

Step 2: Create a Compliance Rule to Bypass Filters

-
Navigate to Rules in Google Admin Console.

-
Click Create a new rule.

-
Set conditions:

-
If the sender domain matches: @traverseapp.com

-
Then deliver the email without spam filtering.

-
Click Save.

9bc1ef80-733e-4a50-98d1-73f92d2f018c.title: How does Average Costing work in Inventory?
9bc1ef80-733e-4a50-98d1-73f92d2f018c.content:
Problem
How does Average Costing work in Inventory?

Resolution
Average Costing:

Average Costing is a widely used inventory valuation method that calculates the cost of inventory by determining the weighted average cost of all inventory items available. This method ensures that price fluctuations over time are smoothed out, resulting in a consistent and stable cost metric for inventory valuation and cost of goods sold (COGS).

How Average Costing Works:

Whenever a new purchase of inventory is made, the total cost of the inventory on hand is recalculated to include the cost of the new purchase. The average cost per unit is then derived by dividing the updated total cost of the inventory by the updated total quantity of inventory. This recalculated average cost is subsequently used to determine the value of inventory sold and the remaining inventory balance.



Formula:

Average Cost per Unit=Total Cost of Inventory / Total Quantity of Inventory​

Example of Average Cost Calculation

-
Initial Purchase:

- Purchase 1: 100 units @ $10 = $1,000

-
Second Purchase:

- Purchase 2: 50 units @ $9 = $450



-
- New Total Quantity: 100 + 50 = 150 units
- New Total Cost: $1,000 + $450 = $1,450
- New Average Cost per Unit: 1,450/150=9.67 (rounded to 2 decimal points)



-
Sale:

- Sale of 25 units at the current average cost ($9.67 per unit)
- COGS: 25 × $9.67 = $241.75



-
- Remaining Quantity: 150 - 25 = 125 units
- Remaining Inventory Value: $1,450 - $241.75 = $1,208.25



-
New Purchase:

- Purchase 3: 100 units @ $10.50 = $1,050



-
- New Total Quantity: 125 + 100 = 225 units
- New Total Cost: $1,208.25 + $1,050 = $2,258.25
- Updated Average Cost per Unit: 2,258.25/225=10.04



Key Benefits of Average Costing

- Stability: Reduces the impact of price fluctuations by averaging costs over time.
- Simplicity: Easy to calculate and implement in inventory systems.
- Consistency: Provides a more uniform measure of inventory cost for financial reporting.

Resolution
The above-mentioned error will usually occur only if the 'GL Account Mask' is differing between the 'Companies'. In order to resolve this, the User can follow either of the below steps:

i. Review the Account Masks manually across all the Companies:

- Log into one of the existing Companies Company
- Navigate to the GL Account Mask screen under the path: Applications -> General Ledger > Setup & Maintenance > Account Mask

- Make note of the 'GL Account Mask' setup of the older Company:

- Toggle to the new Company as well and review the same:

- Verify that the GL Account Mask has identical settings for the 'Case' and 'Fill' fields across all companies. Inconsistencies in these settings can trigger the error.
In case any discrepancies are observed, the User need to manually update the Mask to match with the regular settings [In this example, the 'Fill' was differing]

ii. Review the "Account Mask" setup in the SSMS:
Examine the SYS table SMCompInfo to confirm the GL account mask being used by each company. If discrepancies are found, update the incorrect account mask to match the correct one.

Query [Needs to be executed against SYS Database]:

SELECT TOP (10) [CompId]
,[Name]
,[GlAcctMask]
FROM [SYS].[dbo].[tblSmCompInfo]

Once the discrepancy was observed, it can be rectified accordingly in the Traverse User Interface, as required.

1bbb6439-b60d-486d-851d-d89e3149b0d3.title: How to delete an incorrect PO without the Receipts & Invoices posted?
1bbb6439-b60d-486d-851d-d89e3149b0d3.content:
Problem
A user needs to delete an incorrect Purchase Order (PO) in Traverse. In this particular case, the goods have already been received, and the PO has also been invoiced, which means that the status of the PO is set to “Invoice Received.”

Although the receipts and invoices have been entered, they have not yet been posted to the system. Despite this, when attempting to delete the PO, Traverse displays the following error message:

===================================

Current record cannot be deleted.

===================================

Current record cannot be deleted. (TRAVERSE.Controls)

------------------------------
Program Location:

at TRAVERSE.Client.PluginControlBase.DeleteRow()
at TRAVERSE.Controls.TravNavigator.OnDelete(TravNavigatorEventArgs e)

Resolution
The reason this error occurs is because the record is currently locked, as there are one or more Invoices and Receipts associated with the transaction. Traverse does not allow the direct deletion of a transaction in such cases, in order to preserve system integrity.

To successfully delete the transaction, the user must carefully follow the steps below:

i. Delete the Invoices

- Click on the Receipts/Invoices icon to find the Invoices and Receipts that are linked to the transaction.

- Go to the Invoice section by clicking on the below icon:

- In this case, it will be the below Invoice. There is no direct deletion option to delete the Invoice. The User needs to remove the Line Item(s) and then hit on 'Save'. This action will delete the 'Invoice'

- Once saved, the 'Invoices' section will be appearing as below:



ii. Delete the Receipts

- Once the invoices have been removed, proceed to delete the associated receipts, by clicking on the 'Receipts' button:

- In this case, it will be the below Receipt.

- There is no direct deletion option to delete the Receipt as well. The User needs to remove the Line Item(s) and then hit on 'Save'. This action will delete the 'Receipt'

- Once saved, the 'Receipts' section will be appearing as below:

Note: Even after deleting both the invoices and the receipts, the transaction will continue to reflect the status “Invoice Received.” This is expected system behavior.



iii. Delete the Transaction

- After the invoices and receipts are removed, the user can proceed with deleting the transaction itself.

- We can observe that the Transaction #0001047 is no longer appearing in the 'PO Transactions' lookup:



NOTE: This method works only if no Receipt or Invoices were posted in this Transaction.

4e82fc39-e5d8-4b7c-adf4-274862dcca19.title: Doc unity scanner issue
4e82fc39-e5d8-4b7c-adf4-274862dcca19.content:
Problem
User is unable to save the scanned document. Getting the error.
User scans the document, enters the Vend#, Vendor name, Doc Date manually.

Cause
In the given example (Vendor Contract), the capture profile was not configured properly:
- Vendor ID → Set to Manual Entry
- Vendor Name → Set to Lookup (auto-populates based on Vendor ID)
- Expiration Date → Set to Manual Entry
- Document Date (Doc Date) → Set to Zone, but no zone was defined in the capture profile.
Since no zone was configured, the system expected manual entry, but the setting was still pointing to Zone.

Resolution
Step 1: Review Capture Profile
- Open the Capture Profile for the document type (Vendor Contract in this case).

2.Review each field’s configuration:
- Vendor ID → Manual Entry
- Vendor Name → Lookup (auto-fills from Vendor ID)

- Expiration Date → Manual Entry
- Doc Date → Zone (requires a defined zone on the document)

Step 2: Correct the Configuration
- Since no zone is defined for Doc Date, change its Populate Action to Manual Entry.
- Click Apply to save changes.

Step 3: Reprocess the Document
- Return to Document Capture.
- Select the affected document.
- Enter the Vendor ID manually.
- Click the Capture Keyword button:
- This will auto-populate the Vendor Name and other lookup fields.
- Adjust the Doc Date manually if required.
- Save the document successfully.

adccc9b0-9915-4a2f-b2b1-ca8337877ba0.title: Difference between RDP web client and RDP Session via VPN Tunnel
adccc9b0-9915-4a2f-b2b1-ca8337877ba0.content:
Problem
When the client wants to add new user to Traverse, make sure whether they access Traverse via RDP web client or through RDP Sessions via VPN Tunnel. What is the difference between these two?

Resolution
The difference between using an RDP (Remote Desktop Protocol) web client and an RDP session via a VPN (Virtual Private Network) tunnel mainly revolves around how the connection is established and the level of access and security provided. Here’s a breakdown of the key differences:

RDP Web Client

-
Connection Method:

- Web-Based Access: The RDP web client is typically accessed through a web browser. Users connect to the remote desktop environment via a web-based interface provided by services such as Remote Desktop Web Access (RD Web Access) or third-party web clients.
- No VPN Required: You don’t necessarily need a VPN to use the RDP web client; it uses HTTPS (port 443) to securely communicate over the web.


-
Accessibility:

- Convenience: It’s generally more convenient for users as it allows access from any device with a web browser and an internet connection without requiring additional software or VPN setup.
- Limited Functionality: May offer limited functionality compared to a full RDP session, depending on the web client’s capabilities.


-
Security:

- Encrypted Connection: Typically uses HTTPS to encrypt the connection between the web client and the RDP server, providing a secure channel for remote access.
- Authentication: Often uses standard web authentication methods which may include multi-factor authentication (MFA) depending on configuration.


-
User Experience:

- Varies by Client: The performance and user experience can vary based on the web client used and its compatibility with different browsers.



RDP Session via VPN Tunnel

-
Connection Method:

- VPN Required: An RDP session via VPN requires a VPN client to create a secure tunnel between the user’s device and the remote network. The RDP session is then established within this secure tunnel.
- Direct RDP Access: After establishing the VPN connection, users can directly access the remote desktop using the RDP client (e.g., Microsoft Remote Desktop).


-
Accessibility:

- Controlled Access: Typically used in environments where access needs to be controlled and restricted to specific users. It may require additional configuration for access through the VPN.
- Requires VPN Setup: Users need to have VPN software installed and configured, which can be more complex than using a web-based client.



Summary

- RDP Web Client offers convenience and ease of access through a web browser without requiring a VPN, but may have limited functionality and relies on web-based security.
- RDP via VPN Tunnel provides a higher level of security with encrypted access to the entire network and full RDP features but requires VPN setup and configuration.

The choice between these methods depends on factors like security requirements, user convenience, and the need for accessing additional network resources.

RDP session via VPN Tunnel Icon would look like



Login to RDP web client would look like

86bdb209-a489-4a73-81f0-47ddc836f2a5.title: Avoid Outlook POP up while using send Feature in Traverse
86bdb209-a489-4a73-81f0-47ddc836f2a5.content:
Problem
When customer clicks to send PO through document delivery, a separate outlook screen is opened with the attachment of the PO in it. Customer wants this feature to be removed so that as soon as they click send, the email is sent without any outlook pop up

Resolution
Steps to Configure SMTP for Document Delivery in Traverse
- Log into Traverse with Admin rights.
- Go to:
-  System Manager → Company Setup → Business Rule → Document Delivery tab
- In the Mail Method section:

- Change from Use MAPI to No.
Enter the SMTP Settings:
- SMTP Server: (e.g., smtp.office365.com or your mail server hostname)
- Port:- 587 for TLS (recommended)
- 465 for SSL (if required by your mail host)

- Requires Authentication: (check this if using Office 365, Gmail, or any authenticated SMTP)
- Username: The email account that will send POs (e.g., ap@company.com)
- Password: The email password (or app password if MFA is enabled).
- From Email Address: The default sender email.
(Optional) If using Office 365 / Gmail / Secure mail providers:
- Make sure SMTP is enabled for the account.
- If MFA is enabled → use an App Password instead of the regular password.
- For Office 365 → sometimes "SMTP Authenticated Submission" must be enabled by the admin.
Test the connection using the “Test Email” button (available in newer Traverse versions).
- If successful → you’ll see a confirmation.
- If it fails → check firewall, credentials, and mail provider’s SMTP settings.
Save changes.

When we try to use the Send feature after this, it won't open any outlook screen, instead you will get a Traverse pop up, where the PO will be attached. Where we enter the receiver email and send the email.

013da693-e509-4757-93c2-e37ddcb06d68.title: Configuring Punch Overrides in On Time Web
013da693-e509-4757-93c2-e37ddcb06d68.content:
Problem
Punch Overrides are rules used to automatically replace recorded punch times with predefined override times. This feature is helpful for standardizing time entries or correcting common variances in employee punches.

Resolution
Punch Overrides can be configured at three levels:

-
Global – Applies to all employees

-
Employee Specific – Applies only to selected individuals

-
Supervisor Group – Applies to all employees under a specific supervisor group

The system reviews the time range defined in the policy and replaces the matching punch type time with the specified override time.

How to Access

Navigate to:
Company Settings > Punch Overrides

Available Configuration Options

When creating or editing a Punch Override, the following fields are available:

-
Start Time – Beginning of the range when the override is active

-
End Time – End of the range for applying the override

-
Override Time – The time that will replace the actual punch within the defined range

-
Punch Type – The type of punch this override applies to:

-
IN

-
OUT

-
GO LUNCH

-
RETURN LUNCH

Use Case Example

If an employee typically punches in between 7:50 AM and 8:10 AM, you can set:

-
Start Time: 7:50 AM

-
End Time: 8:10 AM

-
Override Time: 8:00 AM

-
Punch Type: IN

This ensures all punches within that window are automatically recorded as 8:00 AM.

acff9ab3-6a45-47cd-9c4d-3c7d357427ef.title: IN Copy Items to Locations
acff9ab3-6a45-47cd-9c4d-3c7d357427ef.content:
Problem
A new location has been added under IN Location, and there is a need to copy all existing Item IDs to this newly added location. Guidance or support is required to perform this action efficiently.

CA001 was the new location that was added.

Resolution
The possible solution would be to copy items to this location using the Copy Items to Location function.

The Copy Items to Locations function allows us to copy a full list or a filtered set of item records from one location to one or more other locations within the system. This includes the option to copy specific data such as pricing, vendor, or bin information.
Purpose
Use this feature to replicate item information across multiple inventory locations efficiently, with flexibility to include or exclude specific data.

Steps to Copy Items to Locations
1. Open the Copy Items to Locations screen.
Navigation: Applications > Inventory > Setup and Maintenance > Copy Items to locations.

2. Use the Data Filter (optional):
- Select a range of Item IDs and/or Product Lines to filter the data.
- Leave the filter blank to include all available items.

3. Select the Copy from Location ID, which is the source location containing the items you want to copy.
- Select the Account Code you want to assign to the items in the selected destination locations.
- Enter comments about the copy in the Comments field (optional).
- Choose what to include by selecting or clearing the checkboxes for:
4. Location Information
- Price Information
- Cost Information
- Vendor Information
- Bin Information
5. In the Select Location To area, check the boxes for the locations you want to copy the items to.

6. Select the Account Code for each chosen location, if needed.

7. Click OK to begin copying the items. A confirmation message will appear once the process is successful.

Activity Log:
Use the Activity Log to view all post-copy activity for administrative purposes.

ceea4e38-a33b-4803-a8dd-dded3e0a99d7.title: How to Download and Install Remote Desktop (RDP) Application on Windows?
ceea4e38-a33b-4803-a8dd-dded3e0a99d7.content:
Problem
How to Download and Install Remote Desktop (RDP) Application on Windows?



The Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) application is necessary to allow the user to remotely access the server and launch Traverse directly from the server, eliminating the need for a local installation. 19a7e22d-83ad-464c-88cc-09ca014366d9.title: Why the 'Transaction CutOff Date' Cannot Be Updated in PA Calculate Checks?
19a7e22d-83ad-464c-88cc-09ca014366d9.content:
Problem
When attempting to calculate Checks, the users encountered a situation where the fields "Transaction Cutoff Date," "Period End" Date, and "Date on Checks" within the PA Calculate Checks screen appear greyed out (disabled). As a result, users are unable to modify or enter values in these fields.

This behavior prevents updating the dates as required during the check calculation process and needs to be addressed to proceed further.

Resolution
This issue typically occurs when Payroll checks have already been prepared, either by the same user or by another user within the system. As a result, certain date fields such as Transaction Cutoff Date, Period End Date, and Date on Checks appear greyed out and cannot be modified.

Steps to Confirm the Issue:
A. Reviewing the 'PA Edit Register':
- Navigate to the following path: Applications -> Payroll -> Payday Work -> Edit Register
- Review the PA Edit Register to verify if payroll checks have already been prepared.

- If the 'Calculate Checks' process was not prepared, the 'Preview' result will be as follows:

B. Review the 'Calculate Checks' Activity:
Review the Last run 'Workstation date' and see if it belongs to the current Pay Period.

Steps to Resolve the Issue:
i. On the PA Calculate Checks screen, locate and click on the Reset icon.
- This action will restore the fields to their default values.
- Any checks that were previously calculated will also be reset.
NOTE: Using the Reset option does not delete payroll data; it simply resets the calculation process so that dates can be updated.

ii. Once the reset is complete, the greyed-out fields will become editable.
- Enter the required dates (e.g., Transaction Cutoff Date, Period End Date, Date on Checks).
- Click OK to proceed with the payroll calculation.

48660d51-1b6f-408f-9756-8bc185e8333c.title: Managing Credit Card Authorization for Cash Receipts and AR Transactions
48660d51-1b6f-408f-9756-8bc185e8333c.content:
Problem
How to manage Credit Card Authorization for Cash Receipts and AR Transactions?

While processing the Cash Receipts through a Credit Card, when the 'Authorization Code' was not entered, the User will be getting the below error when he/she is attempting to post the 'AR Cash Receipts':

Detailed Error message:

===================================

CC authorization is required for one or more transactions.

------------------------------
Edition = Global
Build = 25199
User = 14
LicenseServer = localhost
Culture = English (United States)
DefaultCompID = CPU
SysDb = SYS
SessionID = XXXX-XXXX
MachineName = XXXX-XXXX

===================================

CC authorization is required for one or more transactions. (TRAVERSE.Client.ReportViewer)

------------------------------
Program Location:

at TRAVERSE.Client.ProcessControlBase.OnProcessCompleted()
at TRAVERSE.Client.AccountsReceivable.CashRcptPostControl.OnProcessCompleted()

Resolution
When payments are made using credit cards and the transaction amount exceeds the threshold defined in the AR Business Rules under "CC Authorization Required for Amounts Exceeding", an authorization number becomes mandatory.

Without a valid authorization number, such transactions will be blocked from posting during the posting process, as mentioned above.

Important Note:
Transactions processed via the Traverse Payment System (TPS) are automatically managed and do not appear in this function. This feature is specifically intended for manually entered credit card transactions that require post-entry authorization.

Procedure: Entering or Editing Authorization Numbers
To ensure smooth posting and compliance with business rules, the User needs to follow the steps below to manage authorization numbers for applicable transactions:

i. Access the Credit Card Authorization Function: Navigate to the AB Credit Card Authorization screen under the path: Applications -> Accounts Receivable -> Transactions -> Credit Card Authorization:

ii. Locate the Transaction:
From the displayed table, select the cash receipt or AR transaction for which the credit card authorization needs to be added or updated.
- If we are unable to find a particular transaction, check the "Show All" box. This option displays all cash receipt records, including those that do not currently require an authorization number or already have one assigned. After selecting "Show All,"  we need to click the Refresh icon on the toolbar to update the table view accordingly.

iii. Enter Authorization Number:
In the Authorization field, the User needs to input the appropriate credit card authorization number for each transaction that lacks one.

iv. Save the Changes:
Once all necessary entries have been made, click the Save icon on the toolbar to confirm and store the authorization data.

This process ensures that all required credit card payments are properly authorized and eligible for posting,

0d55deea-da3a-4ec6-8367-f2cc5f920577.title: How to create 'Cash Deposits' in Accounts Receivable?
0d55deea-da3a-4ec6-8367-f2cc5f920577.content:
Problem
How to create 'Cash Deposits' in Accounts Receivable?

Resolution
Under normal circumstances, when creating a Cash Receipt in Accounts Receivable, we select an existing Customer record. The receipt is then applied either:
- Directly against an 'Outstanding Invoice' for that customer, (or)
- As an 'On Account' payment linked to that specific customer’s profile for future allocation.

However, there are scenarios, such as when receiving donations, where an active customer record does not exist in Accounts Receivable.

Since donations are typically one-time contributions and not linked to sales transactions or invoices, there is no customer profile or invoice to associate the payment with.
In such cases:
- The amount received must still be recorded in Traverse as a Cash Receipt.
- This ensures the funds are reflected in the Bank account in the General Ledger.
- The receipt will not be tied to any specific customer or invoice but will still maintain a proper accounting trail.

This approach ensures that:
- The bank account reflects the inflow of funds from the donation.
- The transaction is properly documented for audit and reporting purposes.
- There is a clear distinction between customer-related receipts and non-customer receipts such as donations.

In order to create 'Cash Deposit' record in Traverse, the User needs to follow the below steps:
i. Navigate to the 'AR Cash Receipts' screen under the path: Applications -> Accounts Receivable -> Transactions -> Cash Receipts

ii. Click on the 'New' icon to create a new Cash Receipt:

iii. For creating the 'Cash Deposit', we need not choose any 'Customer ID'. We can proceed with entering the 'Payment Method ID', 'Payment Amount' and the 'Credit GL Account'. Then add a Line entry in the grid section and apply the Amount against that Invoice. And hit on 'Save' once done.

The 'Credit GL Account' can be any Revenue Account, as the money is getting increased.

iv. After printing the 'Cash Receipts' Journal, post the 'Cash Receipt' Batch

v. We can observe its impact hitting the Bank Reconciliation as a 'Bank Deposit':

d41b375e-df58-42ba-a5d9-aa87301164f0.content:

L1 = f.GetNumericVariable("FC1")
L2 = min(L1, 1)

L4 = max(0, L3 - 1)
L7 = f.GetNumericVariable("GRANDTOTGROSS")
L8 = (L7 * L2 * .01) +(L7 * .5 * L4 * .01)
f.SetNumericVariable("CALCVALUE",L8)




Under PA Employee Information> Employer Costs> create line entry for 401 code and set to

6e97abe1-4d32-4dc5-8866-2350f0f94f95.title: Incorrect Federal Withholding Calculation on Bonus Payment with Fixed Withholding Setup
6e97abe1-4d32-4dc5-8866-2350f0f94f95.content:
Problem
Incorrect Federal Withholding Calculation on Bonus Payment with Fixed Withholding Setup:

The client is adding a $100 bonus to a salaried employee’s paycheck using a Bonus Earning Code configured as Fixed Withholding, with a fixed withholding rate set at 22%. However, after adding the bonus, the employee’s Federal Withholding amount increases significantly higher than expected. The client wants to know if this is known behavior or if it indicates an issue with the withholding calculation.

Resolution
The client reported an issue involving a $100 bonus applied to a salaried employee’s paycheck using a Bonus Earning Code set to Fixed Withholding at 22%.

After applying the bonus, the Federal Withholding amount increases more than expected, beyond what would result from a straightforward 22% withholding.

This behavior was reviewed and confirmed by the development team as a product defect.

A Change Request (CR) has been submitted to address the issue: CR DEV-287519.
https://dev.azure.com/TraverseERP/b746159b-5617-4616-8466-ae9d6a61d66f/_workitems/edit/99021

CR - Incorrect Federal Withholding Calculation on Bonus Payment with Fixed Withholding Setup - 04520447 - DEV-287519

The issue has been resolved in build SP-5 (Build 25262), which includes a fix to ensure correct withholding calculations for bonuses with fixed tax rates.

Clients experiencing this issue are encouraged to update to build SP-5 25262 to apply the fix.

6f37b73c-734f-4a52-84fd-ae77a5f64330.title: ON TIME WEB time zones issue
6f37b73c-734f-4a52-84fd-ae77a5f64330.content:
Problem
When some employees work in CST zone and others in EST zone. Customers might get issue with the time in the timesheets entered by their employees, since the server might have set to a different time zone.

Resolution
To prevent these time discrepancies, it is important to assign a specific time zone to each employee based on their physical location. This ensures that all time entries reflect the correct local time for the employee, regardless of the server’s default time zone. Here’s how to do it in OTW:

- Log in to OTW – Start by accessing the OTW system with your credentials.
- Navigate to Company Settings – From the main menu, go to Company Settings and then select Employees. This will bring up the list of all employees in your organization.

- Access the Employee Mobile Tab – Click on the individual employee you want to update. Go to the Mobile tab in the employee information screen. This section manages mobile access settings and time zone configurations.
- Enable Mobile Access – Make sure that Mobile Access is enabled for the employee so that their device can sync with the system.
- Set Employee Time Zone – In the Mobile Time Zone field, select the employee’s local time zone. This setting will override the time zone of the employee’s mobile device and ensure that all times they log are recorded correctly in the system.

- Optional: Leave Blank for Company Time Zone – If you leave the mobile time zone field blank, the system will default to the company’s standard time zone. This is useful for employees who work in the same location as the company’s main office.

13f68a32-b169-4a1b-a727-e2a961c0095c.title: Setup employee rates in Project Costing
13f68a32-b169-4a1b-a727-e2a961c0095c.content:
Problem
How to set up employee rates in Project Costing?

Resolution
Setting Up Employee Billing and Cost Rates in Project Costing

To manage billing and cost rates for your employees, use the Employee Rates function. This allows us to define rates for each employee, which will be applied when entering time tickets to calculate income and costs. We can assign multiple rates to an individual employee based on different roles or projects.



Side notes:

If the Project Costing system module is integrated with Payroll, employee and earning code details will be pulled from the Payroll Employees file. If there is no Payroll integration (or if Payroll is not installed), the system will retrieve employee data from the System Manager Employee file. Before using the Employee Rates function, ensure that we’ve entered employee information in either the Payroll Employee Information function or the System Manager Employees function.



Creating an Employee Rate

Navigation: Applications -> Project Costing -> Setup and Maintenance -> Employee Rates

- Click the New button on the toolbar to start adding billing and cost rates for an employee. This will open a new section for us to fill in the required details, as shown below.

- Choose the employee’s ID from the Employee ID field.
- Select the appropriate rate code for the employee from the Rate Code field.
- Enter the rate you charge for the employee’s time in the Employee Rate field.
- Enter the rate you pay the employee in the Cost field.
- Select a Payroll Earning Code that will apply to the employee’s rate from the Earning Code field.
- If you want this rate to be the default when entering time tickets, check the Default Rate box.
- Note: If you leave the box unchecked, the system will use the rate set in the Project’s General tab instead of the employee’s rate when entering time tickets.

- Click the Save button on the toolbar to save the new employee rate.

Editing an Employee Rate

- Select the employee ID you want to edit from the Employee ID field.
- Make any necessary changes to the fields.
- Click the Save button on the toolbar to save the updates.

E.g., I have made changes to the cost from 40.00 to 50.00 for employee id ADMIN. The changes are reflected as shown below.

Deleting an Employee Rate

- Choose the employee rate you want to delete from the Employee ID field.
- Click the Delete button on the toolbar to remove the selected rate.
- It would prompt the following "Are you sure you want to delete selected record(s)?" Hit, OK. The chosen record would automatically be deleted from the system.

E.g., Here the ADMIN employee id has been deleted from the system.

ccf88eb2-9405-4e91-8e29-c84cc446cd50.title: How to Add Freight Charges as a Line Item in a Purchase Order
ccf88eb2-9405-4e91-8e29-c84cc446cd50.content:
Problem
Vendors may include freight charges on the same invoice as the items purchased, but bill them separately. To ensure accurate accounting and visibility, these freight charges need to be itemized on the Purchase Order (PO).

Resolution
To handle freight billing correctly, freight charges should be added to the PO as a separate, non-inventory line item (e.g., using a freight item code or a descriptive entry).

Steps to Add Freight Charges as a Line Item in a PO:

To add freight charges to a PO, go to the Purchase Order module and click the plus icon to create a new transaction. Select the appropriate Vendor ID from the dropdown list.

Enter the first line item by selecting the Item ID for the product or service being ordered.

To include freight charges, use the second line item. Do not select an Item ID—simply type "Freight Charges" in the Description field and enter the appropriate amount.

Click Save. Then, click “All” to receive all items and invoice them by providing a Receipt Number and Invoice Number. Click OK to complete the process.

A sample invoice is attached for reference, showing where the freight charges have been added as a line item. You can see the freight charges being added to the total amount.

3ebe47bb-3655-486b-ad05-9b7834613559.title: Unable to Login to RDP version of Traverse
3ebe47bb-3655-486b-ad05-9b7834613559.content:
Problem
When attempting to sign into remote desktop and enter my credentials, I receive an error. See below:

Resolution
The server was unable to contact the domain controller, which is required for Network Level Authentication (NLA) to verify user credentials. This issue can occur due to several factors, such as:

- Network interface issues
- DNS resolution failures
- Stale or failed domain sessions
- Routing or firewall restrictions
- Critical system services not running properly
In this case, it appears to have been a temporary connectivity issue with the domain controller. Rebooting the server restored the connection and successfully resolved the error.

iv. Now, uncheck the 'Checkbox' corresponding to that 'Payment Number' and then hit on 'OK' to unclear the same.

After this, the User can go back to the 'AP Void Payments' screen under the path: Applications -> Accounts Payable -> Pay Invoices -> Void Payments, to proceed with voiding the Payment [In this example, the Payment corresponding to the Payment Number '237']

The reinstated Invoices will now be returned to the 'AP Hold/Release Invoices' screen:
