19f5ddbc-4d94-48db-8ba3-48f88fe106ec.title: Traverse - How Receipts Post When PO Is Still Open?
19f5ddbc-4d94-48db-8ba3-48f88fe106ec.content:
Problem
How do receipts get posted if the PO itself is never posted or is still open?

Resolution
Solution:
Receipts are processed as separate transactions from the Purchase Order. When a receipt is created for a PO:
- The system updates the PO status to Goods Received, and there will be no invoice yet.
- Posting the receipt updates inventory and financial records independently of the PO posting.
- This design allows partial receipts and supports real-world scenarios where goods arrive before invoicing.
If invoicing is still pending, the PO remains open and visible in the PO Transactions screen. Once all related invoices are created and posted, the system will fully close the PO.

Steps:
Go to Purchase Order → Transactions → Transactions.
Click New Record and select the Vendor ID. Enter the Item IDs and their respective quantities to be received,
Click All and check the boxes next to Receive All . Enter the Receipt Number and adjust the receipt if needed.
Then, click OK to update the transaction type to Goods Received.

Then the User can proceed with posting the 'PO Transactions' ad that will mark the 'Receipts' as posted as well. [NOTE: Once posted, the Receipts cannot be deleted.]

As the invoicing is still pending, the PO remains open and visible in the PO Transactions screen. Once all the items were received and the related invoices are created and posted, the system will fully close the PO.

dbc7dd18-8f37-4e2a-a9bc-669ebae3e155.title: How to add/remove Users from the 'Contact Name' drop-down while creating cases from 'AppCentral'?
dbc7dd18-8f37-4e2a-a9bc-669ebae3e155.content:
Problem
How to add/remove Users from the 'Contact Name' drop-down while creating cases from 'AppCentral'?

NOTE: This privilege to choose the 'Contact Name' from the drop-down, while creating support tickets will be available only to the 'Admin' Users

Resolution
We can manage which users appear in the 'Contact Name' drop-down when creating cases through AppCentral by adjusting the user’s contact profile in Salesforce. In the 'Support Information' section of the contact record, there is an option labeled 'Prohibit Creating Cases'.

If this checkbox is enabled, the user will no longer be allowed to submit support cases via AppCentral, and their name will not be visible in the drop-down list. If we want to allow the user to log cases, we should ensure this checkbox is unchecked.

This approach helps us streamline case submissions and ensure that only the appropriate users have access to create tickets via AppCentral.

84c1da61-4ce9-40fc-a4de-8eeaac92fbc3.title: Missing ASN, re-send ASN
84c1da61-4ce9-40fc-a4de-8eeaac92fbc3.content:

55022ecd-0b80-4a1d-8d4d-c2dea8d08f35.title: Workaround to Automatically Open Embedded Files Without Prompting to Save
55022ecd-0b80-4a1d-8d4d-c2dea8d08f35.content:
Problem
When attempting to open an embedded file associated with a Sales Order (SO) transaction, the system prompts the user to save the file before opening it.

Resolution
The system lacks a predefined default document folder. Without this setting, it cannot preview files directly and instead prompts users to save them. As embedded files are directly saved in SQL.

To do this, go to:
System Manager > Company Setup > User Defaults
Then click on System Manager again under the Modules section.

Set up a Default Document Folder by specifying a valid path where temporary files can be stored. For example: C:\TempDocs\ or a network location accessible to the user.

Once this is set, the system will automatically open embedded documents from the specified location, allowing for seamless previews without the need to save each file manually.

You should now be able to open and view embedded files directly.

45dabcf6-acd6-4ab3-9ff9-f304383f9c5c.title: Setting Up a Declining Balance by Percentage Deduction for 401(k)
45dabcf6-acd6-4ab3-9ff9-f304383f9c5c.content:
Problem
An employee needs to contribute to a 401(k) plan using a declining balance by percentage method. The goal is to have the system automatically reduce the deduction amount each payroll run until the set balance is exhausted, at which point deductions will stop.

Resolution
To set up a declining balance by percentage for a 401(k) deduction, go to Payroll > Setup and Maintenance > Employee Information > Deductions Tab.

Select the employee’s record and locate the 401(k) deduction. Change the deduction type from Standard Percentage to Declining Balance by Percentage.

In the balance field, enter the total amount to be deducted. The system will use this as the maximum limit and deduct based on the percentage set. Choose E to represent declining balance by percentage, then enter the percentage to be deducted each payroll period.

The system will automatically reduce the balance each payroll run. When the balance reaches zero, the system will stop the deduction.

9b707dd1-f2fd-4b4d-87ee-fed54b96c363.title: Project Costing Adjustments
9b707dd1-f2fd-4b4d-87ee-fed54b96c363.content:
Problem
When setting up the Project Cost module for the first time, your organization has several ongoing projects with previously incurred costs such as time, materials, expenses, and deposits that were not recorded in the system. You need a way to accurately reflect these existing costs in the new system without re-entering them through detailed time tickets or transactions.

Resolution
Use the Adjustments function to directly enter these historical project details—such as time, material, expense, deposits, fixed fee billing, and more into the system. This allows you to bring your in-progress projects up to date without recreating every transaction. Additionally, you can use this function to move deposits between tasks within a project as needed.

- In the Increase/Decrease column:- Select 'Decrease' to delete a transaction amount from a Project/Task.
- Select 'Increase' to add a transaction amount to a Project/Task.

- Select the Type of transaction to increase or decrease.
- Choose the Fiscal Period and Fiscal Year for each transaction.
- Enter the Quantity, Extended Cost, and/or Extended Income amount to increase or decrease on each transaction.
- Use Description/Additional Description to explain the purpose for the adjustment.
- All adjustment transactions will be written to the activity history for the selected project.
Post Adjustments
- Deposit and Deposit Applied adjustments do not create GL entries
- Deposit adjustments will not post to Accounts Receivable Aging
- Fixed Fee Billing adjustments do not create GL entries
- Fixed Fee Billing adjustment only updates Fixed Fee Available
- Update the Fixed Fee amount in project maintenance
- Adjustments with status of 'Billed' for Time & Material and Fixed Fee projects or tasks will not create GL entries
Deposit, Deposit Applied, and Fixed Fee Billing Adjustments for Fixed Fee and Time & Material

Post Deposit, Deposit Applied and Fixed Fee Billing Adjustments - No GL Entries


Time, Material, Expense and Other Adjustments for Fixed Fee

- Income adjustments for Fixed Fee projects or tasks do not create GL entries
- Time cost posted adjustments for Fixed Fee projects or tasks will post to Cost (502000) and Payroll Clearing (600000) accounts
- Material cost posted adjustments for Fixed Fee projects or tasks will post to Cost (502000) and Adjustments (420000) accounts
- Expense cost posted adjustments for Fixed Fee projects or tasks will post to Cost (502000) and Adjustments (420000)accounts
- Other cost posted adjustments for Fixed Fee projects or tasks will post to Cost (502000) and Adjustments (420000) accounts
Post Time, Material, Expense and Other Adjustments for Fixed Fee – GL entries for cost only


Time, Material, Expense, Other Adjustments for Time & Material

Post Time, Material, Expense and Other Adjustments for Time & Material – GL entries for income & cost

- Adjustments with status of 'Posted' for Time & Material projects or tasks will create GL entries for Income and Cost
- Time income posted adjustments for Time & Material projects or tasks will post to WIP (123500) and Accrued Income (402500) accounts
- Time cost posted adjustments for Time & Material projects or tasks will post to Cost (502000) and Payroll Clearing (600000) accounts
- Material income posted adjustments for Time & Material projects or tasks will post to WIP (123500) and Accrued Income (402500) accounts
- Material cost posted adjustments for Time & Material projects or tasks will post to Cost (502000) and Adjustments (420000) accounts
- Expense income posted adjustments for Time & Material projects or tasks will post to WIP (123500) and Accrued Income (402500) accounts
- Expense cost posted adjustments for Time & Material projects or tasks will post to Cost (502000) and Adjustments (420000) accounts
- Other income posted adjustments for Time & Material projects or tasks will post to WIP (123500) and Accrued Income (402500) accounts
- Other cost posted adjustments for Time & Material projects or tasks will post to Cost (502000) and Adjustments (420000) accounts

25bd85e4-da44-439a-a43d-3d1b40785fda.title: How to add a new 'Earning Code' so that it can be imported into Traverse through the Payroll Import?
25bd85e4-da44-439a-a43d-3d1b40785fda.content:
Problem
How to add a new 'Earning Code' so that it can be imported into Traverse through the Payroll Import?



In some cases, a new Earning Code may have been added successfully in Traverse through the PA Earning Codes screen. However, during data import, Traverse does not rely solely on the earning codes maintained in this screen. Instead, it reads the raw values from the import file and applies the corresponding mappings using the Translation/Conversion functions defined in the SM Export Layout Definition.



If such a Translation was missing, Traverse would cause issues at the time of Data Import.

Resolution
Consider the following example where specific Earning Code values are already configured for import translation:
- ‘01’ translates to ‘REG’ (Regular Pay)
- ‘02’ translates to ‘HOL’ (Holiday Pay)
- ‘03’ translates to ‘PTO’ (Paid Time Off)
Now, if the user attempts to import data with a new value such as ‘04’, intended to represent ‘VAC’ (Vacation Pay), but this value hasn’t been added to the Translation/Conversion setup within the Import Layout Definition, Traverse will encounter issues during the import process. This is because it will not recognize or properly map the new value, leading to import errors or incomplete data processing.

To prevent such issues, the user must manually update the Import Layout to include the new translation entry. The steps are as follows:
i. Navigate to: Applications → System Manager → Company Setup → Import Layout Definition


ii. Locate and select the appropriate Import Layout used for the payroll import process.

iii. Within the layout, identify the line that contains the Translation/Conversion function applied to the Earning Codes field.


iv. Click on the Ellipsis (‘…’) button associated with the Extended Info column for that line.


v. In the Extended Info section, add the new translation entry: Enter the import value (e.g., ‘04’) and its corresponding translation value (e.g., ‘VAC’), and hit on 'OK'

vi. Save the changes.


Once this update is completed and saved, the user should be able to import the file successfully, and Traverse will correctly map the Earning Codes, including the newly added code, during the import process.

[In case the 'SM Import Mapped Data' screen is already, please have it closed and re-opened, after the changes made to the SM Import Layout Definition, to ensure the changes are getting reflected.]

0e6fdb54-80d2-47a4-9cdf-52bc9b7ef863.title: Why is the Payment Information duplicates in the 'AP Payment History View' of Traverse 11.0?
0e6fdb54-80d2-47a4-9cdf-52bc9b7ef863.content:
Problem
Why is the Payment Information duplicates in the 'AP Payment History View' of Traverse 11.0?

Resolution
The 'AP Payment History View' screen is designed to display all recorded payments. It functions by pulling in every entry associated with payments from the system, based on the uniqueness of the payment number.

How the System Interprets Duplicate Payment Numbers?
When users record separate payment transactions using the same payment number, whether intentionally or inadvertently, the 'AP Payment History View' treats each transaction as a distinct entry. This is evident in the summary or header view, where each transaction will appear as a separate line item, despite sharing the same payment number.

This design is based on the fact that each transaction record is differentiated not solely by the payment number, but by its underlying transactional metadata, such as posting date, amount, vendor, and type (e.g., regular payment, prepayment).

Behavior of the Detail View with Duplicate Payment Numbers:
When a user selects any of the listed entries for a shared payment number, the detail section of the screen consolidates and displays all invoices linked to that specific payment number, regardless of which transaction instance was selected. This collective display helps ensure that users are presented with a comprehensive view of all invoice activity associated with the payment number across time.
This behavior may initially seem counterintuitive, especially when the same payment number has been reused across unrelated transactions. However, it is an intentional design choice meant to provide visibility into all financial activity linked to a given payment number within the system.

Illustrative Example:
Let us consider the following scenario:
- A payment with Payment Number '1500' was made to Vendor ID 'Ace001' several years ago, with a payment amount of $20,667.79.
- Later, another transaction was created, either intentionally or accidentally, where Payment Number '1500' was reused for a Prepayment of $11,148.97, also for Vendor 'Ace001'.
- Both the Transaction and the Payment were successfully posted in the system.
Now, when reviewing the 'AP Payment History View', users will observe:
- Two separate entries under Payment Number '1500' in the header section:- One representing the original payment of $20,667.79
- Another for the more recent prepayment of $11,148.97

- However, upon selecting the detail section of the older entry, pointing to the Payment amount of $20,667.79 will reflect a combined list of invoices associated with both transactions, displaying a total of $31,816.76 (i.e., $20,667.79 + $11,148.97).
- And there will be a separate entry associated with the current Payment of $11,148.97 comprising of the present Invoice processed

6e152fb1-13f0-48ed-9413-e3374a0031c8.title: Duplicate data appear in the alert - InfoAlert
6e152fb1-13f0-48ed-9413-e3374a0031c8.content:
Problem
An alert’s output data source has suddenly started producing duplicate (doubled) data. This unexpected behavior needs to be investigated and corrected.

Example attached.

Alert ID I00055:

You’ll notice that the item ending in 907 appears twice in the list, along with other items that are also duplicated.

Resolution
-
Understand the Change

It’s always best to identify what changes were made that might have caused the issue.

Once we analyze the change, resolving the issue becomes much easier.


-
Area to Investigate

In this case, the problem is related to the Manage Notification setup, which is responsible for triggering alerts.

This setup is crucial and must be reviewed carefully.


-
Duplicate Alerts Observed

Upon reviewing and comparing with other working alert setups, it was found that there were duplicate entries with the same sequence number (1) for the same email address.

-
How the System Interprets This

The system interprets multiple entries with the same sequence number as separate triggers.

As a result, it generates and sends the alert twice (or as many times as the duplicate entries exist).


Setup Limitation and Deletion Challenge

-
Complexity of the Setup

In Microsoft Access (since Infoalert is built on this platform), the Manage Notification setup allows adding multiple entries, but editing or deleting existing entries is not straightforward.

-
Deletion Method (Not Recommended for Regular Use)

Direct deletion is not supported through the standard UI.

However, using Shift + Delete on a selected record does delete the entry, though this method is not generally recommended.

This approach was only used because the duplicate entry with the same Seq number was the only change that was made. (Read Step 1)



-
How to Delete a Record (If Absolutely Needed)

Click on the leftmost column (record selector) of the record you wish to delete.

If a small triangle icon appears, that record is selected.



Press Shift + Delete on your keyboard.

The deletion is auto-saved, so no need to save manually.



Final Outcome

-
Result After Fixing

-
After removing the duplicate record, the alert's output source functioned as expected, with no duplicate entries generated.

a73e5138-ae7d-4282-abb0-bd5bfe19b8b6.title: Activity Report and Error Report in Info Alert
a73e5138-ae7d-4282-abb0-bd5bfe19b8b6.content:
Problem
How are the Activity Report and Error Report used within the Info Alert?

Resolution
Info-Alert is designed to run automatically and unattended, IA ‘logs’ all the server runs in an Activity Report and ‘logs’ any error messages in the Error Report.

Activity Report:

Navigation:

Reports -> History and Activity ->Activity Report

The Activity Report includes the IA Server activity that occurs during an IA Server run.

Enter criteria as necessary:

- Activity date range
- Tracking level range

Select the check box to Show colors on the report.

-  Reset clears the criteria you entered.
-  Preview displays a print preview of the report.
-  Print sends the report to a printer to create a hard copy.
-  File creates a PDF of the report and saves it in the Reports folder in the Info-Alert installation directory.

TIP: Using the Activity Report: If we saw alerts flagged but 0 records reported, then we may have a problem with the DNR (Do not re-notify) setting in the Alert Schedule tab, or the actual alert code. If we saw no alerts flagged, even though we know there are alerts selected in the alert list, then the Alert schedule settings for this alert would be suspect.

In Short: The Activity Report can be viewed by date range or tracking level, or again, simply choose Preview to show the entire Activity Log. Use the page selector at the bottom of the screen to easily move through the pages.

_____________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________

Error Report:

Navigation:

Reports -> History and Activity ->Error Report

Enter error date range criteria as necessary.

Use the appropriate button:

- Reset clears the criteria you entered.
- Preview displays a print preview of the report.
- Print sends the report to a printer to create a hard copy.
- File creates a PDF of the report and saves it in the Reports folder in the Info-Alert installation directory.

acbf9c8d-cf08-4c28-8aef-b96cec3a94c3.title: Sales Order cannot be updated
acbf9c8d-cf08-4c28-8aef-b96cec3a94c3.content:
Problem
When attempting to change or Verify a Sales Order, a message will appear stating "Unable to Update" and the order cannot be saved.  Often the case notes will reference problems with Serial Numbers.

Resolution
This Knowledgebase Article is specific to Rudco Products.  It should not be used to diagnose problems with any other client, and should never be attached to a Salesforce case, including Rudco's.  It is for internal use only.

Rudco Products has some customizations over in the TRAVERSE 11.0 version of Warehouse Management that related to Bills of Lading.  The process of picking Sales Orders is not the standard practice normally performed by TRAVERSE.  What often happens is that the Serial Numbers from the serialized Inventory Items gets messaged up such that there are duplicates, the Serial Numbers in WM don't match the ones in Sales Order, or some other inaccuracy or mismatch.

To resolve the issue, it is usually required that a connection needs to be made to Rudco's SQL Server to change the Serial Number entries in the table.  Here is the process.

- Log on to Rudco's Server.  This can be done using Remote Desktop Connection.  Instructions for this is in Secret Server.
- From the logon server, log on to RUDCO-FS1.  It uses the same username and password as above.
- Load SSMS
- Query the tblSoTransser and the tblWmPick tables.  Select all records where TransId equals the Order number of the problem order.
- In order for everything to work correctly, the serial numbers listed in each table need to match, have no duplicates, and the serial numbers all need to be valid and available an in the location listed.
- If there is a problem with a serial number, delete it from one or both tables.
- If nothing seems to work, delete all the records in both tables for the order number and the item ID that is a problem.

a5b1a2ed-080a-4277-9884-07a618fa49ef.title: Traverse - Is it possible to Merge Duplicate Vendors?
a5b1a2ed-080a-4277-9884-07a618fa49ef.content:
Problem
Is it possible to merge duplicate A/P vendors into one Vendor ID in Traverse?

Resolution
Traverse does not provide a direct feature to merge duplicate vendors under a single Vendor ID.

However, here are the available options:

Option 1: Manual Workaround (for internal use only)

If merging transaction history is not required, you can:

-
Choose one Vendor ID to retain as Active.

-
Set the remaining duplicate Vendor IDs to Inactive.

-
Moving forward, use only the active Vendor ID for new transactions.

Steps to Inactivate a Vendor in Traverse :

-
Navigate to:
Accounts Payable → Setup and Maintenance → Vendors

-
In the Vendor ID field, select the vendor you wish to inactivate.

-
At the top-right corner, locate the Status field.

-
Change the status from Active to Inactive, as needed.

-
Click Save to apply the changes.

This allows users to consolidate operations without data loss, but historical transactions will remain under their original Vendor IDs.

Option 2: Merge with History (requires Professional Services)

If the customer wants to merge history and all related data under a single Vendor ID, this task requires database-level work and must be handled by the Aptean Professional Services Team.

d3847a7a-5ba3-4321-af9e-470430ee645d.title: Audit Explorer - System Audit
d3847a7a-5ba3-4321-af9e-470430ee645d.content:
Problem
What is the purpose of an Audit Explorer, and what is the significance of this function?

Resolution
The Audit Explorer function serves as a crucial tool within the system for managing and reviewing audit data. Its primary purpose is to allow users to retrieve and sort audit data across various key business entities.

Specifically, you can use the Audit Explorer to view audit information for:

- Sales Orders
- Work Orders
- Production Orders
- Purchase Orders
- Vendors
- Customers
- Items
- Projects

To view audit data you must say 'Yes' to the Audit Orders, Customers, Vendors, Items, etc. options in the Business Rules function in the applications that have the Auditing option.

For Vendor (System Manger -> Company Setup -> Business Rules -> Accounts Payable)

For Customer (System Manger -> Company Setup -> Business Rules -> Accounts Receivable)

Audit Orders: Select Yes to keep a log of changes to order transactions; otherwise, select No. This will track any user-made changes to your transactions. The changes to the order transactions can be viewed using the Audit Explorer on the System Manager, System Audit menu.

For tracking Bank Rec transactions (System Manger -> Company Setup -> Business Rules -> Bank Reconciliation)

Audit Transactions: Select Yes to audit bank reconciliation transactions; otherwise, select No. The transactions can be viewed using the Audit Explorer on the System Manager, System Audit menu.

For IN Items (System Manger -> Company Setup -> Business Rules -> Inventory)



For auditing Production Orders (System Manger -> Company Setup -> Business Rules -> MFG Production)

For auditing Payroll employees (System Manger -> Company Setup -> Business Rules -> Audit employee)

For auditing Purchase orders (System Manger -> Company Setup -> Business Rules -> Purchase Order)

For auditing SD orders (System Manger -> Company Setup -> Business Rules ->Service Director)

For auditing Sales orders (System Manger -> Company Setup -> Business Rules -> Sales Order)

Furthermore, if the 'Maintain User Log' option is enabled in the Business Rules function, the Audit Explorer will also track user activity, providing insights into who performed what actions within the system.

Each entry in the Audit Explorer includes an Audit Type that indicates the action taken—such as record insertion, update, or deletion. If user logging is enabled, the Audit Type will also reflect user activities such as login, logout, and which session/ screen is open/close.

Note: Navigation: Applications -> System Manager ->System Audit -> Audit Explorer.

The Function column lists the function being audited.

The Object column lists the Traverse table name in which the audit entry can be found.

The Key Value column lists the entered value of the audit entry.

The User column displays the user ID responsible for the transaction activity.

The Session column displays the session ID during which the activity was performed.

The Date column displays the specific date and time that the activity occurred.

After arranging and sorting the columns how you want to view the audit information:

- Use the Preview Report button to view a preview of the information as a report. To print the report, click the Print button or to export the report to a PDF, HTML, Text, or XML File, click the Export Document button.

- Use the Export Data button to export and save the data as an HTML, plain text, or Microsoft Excel document.

Note: Depending on the output type selected, the information may export exactly as it appears on the screen, including column widths and expanded or collapsed grouped entries.
- Use the Views button to save the current parameters set for the information for viewing at a later time. You can also use the button to select, edit, or delete from the multiple saved views.

- Use the Reset Layout button to reset the column headings and any sorting changes made to the information table.

- Use the Purge button to purge audit records for a company.

- Use the Cancel button to cancel the data retrieve.

Beyond just viewing, the function also provides the capability to purge audit history, which helps in removing unnecessary entries and maintaining a streamlined audit log.

000078170 -https://connect.aptean.com/s/article/5003i00000MBEjHAAX1660947874526  Refer this article for Purging information.

Note: The Audit Explorer also audits Business Rule changes

In Short:

The significance of the Audit Explorer lies in its ability to provide a centralized and detailed view of changes and activities related to critical business data. This is essential for maintaining data integrity, ensuring compliance, and providing a historical record of transactions and user interactions.

98276f06-82b5-476b-9f69-63862cd07031.title: How to resolve the error "Error writing to file: C:\Program Files\Open Systems, Inc\TRAVERSE\TRAVERSE.exe. Verify that you have access to that directory." when accessing Traverse from the Desktop shortcut?
98276f06-82b5-476b-9f69-63862cd07031.content:
Problem
How to resolve the error "Error writing to file: C:\Program Files\Open Systems, Inc\TRAVERSE\TRAVERSE.exe. Verify that you have access to that directory." when accessing Traverse from the Desktop shortcut?

Resolution
This issue typically arises when the original source of a shortcut is no longer available. This can occur if the associated application was removed or uninstalled, or if the end user’s access to the specified installation folder has been revoked or restricted. As a result, the shortcut cannot locate or launch the intended executable file.

To resolve this, follow the steps below depending on whether the problem is related to application access permissions or to the application installation itself.

A. Updating Application Access:
i. Verify that no Traverse processes are running:
- Press Ctrl + Shift + Esc to open Task Manager.
- Review the running processes and ensure that no TRAVERSE.exe instances are active.
- If any processes are found, end them. This step is necessary because an active Traverse process may lock files, preventing the installer or update from writing to the directory.

ii. Run the installer with administrative privileges:
- Once we have closed all active Traverse applications, locate the Traverse installer or update executable file in the path: C:\Program Files\Open Systems, Inc\TRAVERSE\
- Right‑click the TRAVERSE.exe' file and select Run as administrator.
- This ensures that the setup program has sufficient privileges to write to protected directories, such as Program Files. If the permissions are blocked, we might need to check with the 'Administrator'

iii. Verify and update folder permissions:
- Then, navigate to: C:\Program Files\Open Systems, Inc\TRAVERSE\.
- Right‑click the folder → Properties → Security tab.
- Confirm that the Windows user account (or the account performing the installation) has Full Control permissions.
- If permissions are insufficient, log in as an administrator or request elevated access to update the folder security settings.

Once these access permissions are properly configured, the user should be able to run Traverse and perform the designated tasks without further interruption.

B. Verifying and Restoring Application Installation:
i. Navigate to the Traverse installation directory:
- Go to: C:\Program Files\Open Systems, Inc\TRAVERSE\.

ii. Check for the Traverse executable file:
- Verify whether the TRAVERSE.exe file is present in this directory.

iii. Reinstall or replace missing files if required:
- If the executable file is missing, the user may need to reinstall Traverse completely.
- Alternatively, copy the Client folder from another workstation where Traverse is installed and functioning correctly, then replace the missing files in the affected machine.

By ensuring proper access rights and verifying the integrity of the Traverse installation files, the issue can be resolved efficiently.

1f84e562-3eab-4ef3-9b47-494d4408bcfe.title: How to Set Up a Service Contract in Service Director
1f84e562-3eab-4ef3-9b47-494d4408bcfe.content:
Problem
How to Set Up a Service Contract in Service Director

Resolution
Prerequisites:
- Customer must be set up in Accounts Receivable
- Equipment to be serviced must be entered under Site Equipment
- Access to Service Director’s Setup and Maintenance menu
Step 1: Access the Service Contracts Screen
- Navigate to:
- Applications > Service Director > Setup and Maintenance > Service Contracts

- Click New or Add (depending on your system version).
- Fill in the General Information:
- Contract Number (can be auto-assigned or manually entered)

- Status (Active, Inactive, etc.)
Step 3: Define Contract Dates
- Effective Date: When the contract starts

Step 4: Select Covered Equipment

- Click Add Equipment or navigate to the Equipment tab.
- Choose equipment previously entered under Site Equipment.
- Define:
- Service frequency
- Parts/labor coverage
- Any specific technician or schedule
Step 5: Configure Billing (If Applicable)

- Navigate to the Billing section.
- Enter:
- Billing Cycle (Monthly, Quarterly, Annually)
- Billing Amount
- GL account codes if integrated with financials
Link to Accounts Receivable for automated invoicing (optional)
Step 6: Add Notes or Special Instructions
- Use the Notes or Comments field to include:- Customer preferences
- Exclusions
- SLA terms

Step 7: Save the Contract
- Once all required fields are completed, click Save or Submit.

ac407d01-8127-4e0a-be94-188b065c9ea7.title: How to Create a Service in Service Director & Add Elements (Manual vs Auto-Discovery)
ac407d01-8127-4e0a-be94-188b065c9ea7.content:
Problem
How to Create a Service in Service Director & Add Elements (Manual vs Auto-Discovery)

Resolution
Step 1: Access Service Director
- Log in to the Traverse Web UI.
- Go to Applications > Service Director.
- The Service Director dashboard will display existing services and their health status.
Step 2: Create a New Service Container
- Click on the “+ Add Service” or “Create Service Container” button.
- Enter the following:
- Service Name (e.g., CRM Application)
- Description (optional but helpful)
- Owner / Group (assign team or responsible person)
- Click Save to create the container.
Tip: Use a consistent naming format like App_Name - Location for clarity.
Step 3: Add Elements to the Service Container
You now need to associate infrastructure components (devices, monitors, policies) that make up this service.
Traverse provides two methods to add elements:
Option 1: Manual Addition
Use this method when you want full control over which elements are included.
- Open the newly created Service Container.
- Click Add Element > Manual.
- Choose from:
- Devices
- Monitors
- Device groups
- Performance policies
- Select the items and click Add.
Use manual mode when the service components are known and stable.
Option 2: Auto-Discovery
Use this for dynamic or complex services where components might change over time.
- Open the Service Container.
- Click Add Element > Auto-Discovery.
- Define rules for dynamic inclusion:
- By IP range
- By device group
- By monitor type (e.g., HTTP, Disk, SNMP)
- By naming pattern
- Set thresholds or availability logic if required.
- Save the rule.
Auto-discovery will automatically update the service as matching components are added or removed from Traverse monitoring.
Step 4: Confirm & Save
- Review the added elements.
- Use the Preview or Dependency View to visualize the hierarchy.
- Click Save or Apply to finalize the service setup.
Best Practices:
- Use manual mode for core services with known infrastructure.
- Use auto-discovery for branch sites, cloud components, or dynamic workloads.

edbdb27a-58c9-48b5-9156-fe95d283d416.title: Error "Utility.Exceptions.MapperValidationException" in EDI Purchase Order Validation View
edbdb27a-58c9-48b5-9156-fe95d283d416.content:
Problem
Customer did receive the order from the Trading Partner, but it wasn't unique for the part. So they manually edited the Order that they had received from the trading partner. They edited the PO number and Part number. Received the below error when submitting the ASN's.

Utility.Exceptions.MapperValidationException: Mapper has encountered 2 Validation Errors: Error in Transaction No. 1; ; Line 30 -- The 'LIN0301' attribute is invalid - The value '' is invalid according to its datatype 'http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema:int' - The string '' is not a valid Int32 value. Error in Transaction No. 2; ; Line 30 -- The 'LIN0301' attribute is invalid - The value '' is invalid according to its datatype 'http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema:int' - The string '' is not a valid Int32 value.

Cause
EDI

Resolution
The validation failed because the EDI Ship-To code sent isn't linked to a ship-to in Traverse and the PO file didn't contain a full ship-to address.

Under Accounts Receivable> Setup and Maintenance> Customers
Pull up the customer in question, navigate to Ship To Tab
Create new ship to location and enter new EDI Ship-To Code "18016-CC45" and Save
Navigate to EDI Connector> Purchase Orders -850 > Process Purchase Orders
Select the check box for the specific order and hit Validate at the top.

It will pass validation after that.

96ec54ce-fbea-4271-8b50-bcdfcf5fa2e8.title: How to resolve the error 'Total X' is invalid in the GL Statement Contents screen?
96ec54ce-fbea-4271-8b50-bcdfcf5fa2e8.content:
Problem
How to resolve the error 'Total X' is invalid in the GL Statement Contents screen?

This error is occurring on a newly set up 'GL Statement Content' and is stopping the User from saving the 'Statement Content'

[There can be any numbers starting from 1 to 9, in the place of 'X' for the error message. Please find the below example]

Resolution
This particular error is typically triggered when invalid or unsupported characters are present in the 'Totals' field of a GL Statement Content setup.

The system expects this field to contain only specific, predefined characters that determine how account totals are calculated and displayed within the report. If the field contains any characters other than the supported values ‘+’, ‘-’, or ‘0’, it leads to the above error.

To resolve this issue, the user should follow the steps below:
i. Navigate to the 'GL Statement Contents' screen under the path: Applications > General Ledger > Management Reports Setup > Statement Contents.

ii. In the specific Statement Content ID where the issue is reported, locate the 'Sequence No' or the 'Line entry' that is causing the issue

iii. Click on the ellipsis (...) icon to expand the Detail section for the Sequence

iv. In the ‘Totals’ field of that line, kindly review the value entered.

v. Ensure that only the allowed characters ('+', '-', or '0') are used. If any invalid characters are found, remove or correct them accordingly.

vi. Now, the User can proceed with saving the changes without any issues:

8a26fdb6-98f1-4f91-90ed-2bdcb0cccbac.title: How to setup Cost Break
8a26fdb6-98f1-4f91-90ed-2bdcb0cccbac.content:
Problem
Does the Cost Break in calculate on the quantity ordered or the quantity received in Purchase Order?

Resolution
You can use the Cost Breaks feature to set up tiered discounts for vendor purchases based on quantity.
For example, you might create a cost break ID that applies:
- 1% discount for purchases of 10 items
- 2% discount for purchases of 20 items
- 3% discount for purchases of 30 or more items

Note: Cost break is calculated on the quantity ordered in purchase order. And it does not matter on the quantity received.

Creating a Cost Break

Go to Inventory > Setup and Maintenance > Cost breaks
- Click the New button on the toolbar to create a new cost break record.
- In the Cost Break ID field, enter a unique ID for the cost break.
- In the Description field, provide a brief description of the cost break.
- In the Break Quantity field, enter the minimum quantity required to qualify for the discount.
- In the Adjustment field, enter the discount or markup value that applies after the break quantity is reached.
- Use a minus sign (-) for a markdown (discount).
- Use a plus sign (+) for a markup (increase).
- In the Adjustment Type field, choose whether the adjustment is a Percent or a Fixed Amount.
- Click the Save button on the toolbar to store the new cost break.

58f1e532-fafb-4447-9b1b-ca57ecc583fd.title: Implementation of Pre-defined List in Base UOM

d3be2931-00fb-4a02-854d-ff94e554b7fa.title: Underpaid employee needs to be paid correctly
d3be2931-00fb-4a02-854d-ff94e554b7fa.content:
Problem
The user has processed and posted a payroll transaction for an employee. After posting, they realized that the employee was underpaid, and an additional amount needs to be included. What is the recommended way to correct this underpayment?

Resolution
To resolve the underpayment, you can create a new payroll transaction for the same employee with 0 hours and enter the difference in the amount that needs to be paid. This will allow you to correct the pay without affecting the employee's worked hours. Once entered, review the transaction for accuracy and proceed with posting as usual. This method ensures the employee receives the remaining balance while maintaining the integrity of the original payroll data.
Resolution Steps to Correct Underpayment in Payroll:
To correct an underpayment for an employee, follow these steps to add the missing amount without affecting recorded work hours:
Example Scenario:
An employee named CMV was already paid for 10 hours, totaling $150, and the transaction has been posted.

You now need to add an additional $100 to the employee's pay.

Steps:
Navigate to Payroll Transaction Entry:
Go to Payroll > Daily Work > Payroll Transactions.

Create a New Transaction:
Enter the employee ID (e.g., CMV).
On the Earnings tab:
- Set Hours to 0.
- Enter the Amount as 100.
- Leave the Rate field blank.
- Save the transaction.

Preview the Time Ticket Journal:
- Go to Print/Preview PA Time Ticket Journal.
- Review the journal to confirm the $100 addition is accurate.

Post the Transaction:
- Navigate to Payroll > Daily Work > Post Transactions.
- Select the batch and post the transaction.

Calculate Checks:
- Go to Payroll > Payday Work > Calculate Checks.
- Enter the required details (such as Group Code and Start Date).
- Click OK to generate the preview report.
- Verify that the additional $100 has been included alongside the previously posted $150.


This process ensures the employee is paid the correct total amount while preserving the accuracy of the original work hours.

dec11208-60a8-4e90-a518-8c3b66d7242a.content:

An attempt was made to either remove the part from Edit Released orders screen (MFG Production) but the system does not allow the update. When trying to save the changes, the following error message is displayed: "Unable to update data."



Detailed error code:

------------------------

at TRAVERSE.Business.Manufacturing.RequirementsProvider.Update(OrderReleases header)
at TRAVERSE.Business.Manufacturing.OrderReleasesProvider.UpdateHeader(OrderReleases header)
at TRAVERSE.Business.Manufacturing.OrderReleasesProvider.Update(OrderReleases entity, Boolean throwException)

===================================
Program Location:
at TRAVERSE.Business.Inventory.QuantityProvider.UpdateQuantity(String compId, ITransaction transaction, QuantityStatus status, Item item)

Resolution
The error trace indicates that the failure occurred within the QuantityProvider.UpdateQuantity() method in the Inventory module. This suggests that the part in question does not have a valid Unit of Measure (UOM) assigned in the inventory.

Without a valid unit, Traverse is unable to perform quantity-related calculations or updates, resulting in a blocked transaction during the save operation.

IMAGE 1

The component was listed with a unit of measure (UOM) “EA” on the work orders, but this UOM does not exist for the item in Inventory setup—the only valid UOM for the item is “LF.”

IMAGE 2: Component has EA as UOM

After adding “EA” as a valid UOM for the item, we will be able to successfully delete the component from both work orders.

First, a confirmation message will appear asking if you're sure you want to delete the component. Upon clicking 'Yes', you must then save the changes, which will prompt a message to recalculate the requirements. After clicking 'OK', the component will be successfully and permanently removed from the work order.

a1635967-8715-480a-b5fe-b1a2b3d54496.title: How to Adjust the 'Invoice Due Date' Automatically Populated for a Specific Vendor?
a1635967-8715-480a-b5fe-b1a2b3d54496.content:
Problem
When an User enters an AP Transaction for a Vendor, the system automatically calculates and populates the Invoice Due Date, Discount Due Date, and applicable Discount Percentage.



The Users would like to have the ability to customize these based on the vendor’s agreed payment terms.

Resolution
We can configure the Net Due Date, Discount Due Date, and Discount % for a specific vendor by setting up a custom Terms Code in the Accounts Payable module.



Terms Codes define how the system determines payment timelines and early payment discounts. Once a Terms Code is configured and assigned to a vendor, the system will automatically apply the correct Net Due Date, Discount Due Date, and Discount Percentage during invoice entry.



I. Steps to Create a Terms Code:

i. Access the 'AP Terms Codes' Screen:

-
Navigate to the AP Terms Codes function under the path: Applications -> Accounts Payable -> Setup and Maintenance -> Term Codes



ii. Add the 'New' Terms Code as needed:

Let’s consider a vendor agreement where we offer the following payment conditions:

-
A 25% discount is available if the invoice is paid within the first 5 days from the invoice date.

-
The full invoice amount is due within 15 days from the invoice date, with no discount applicable after day 5.

To configure this in the Terms Code screen:

- Terms Code: Assign a unique identifier (For example: 25DN15)
- Description: Provide a brief explanation of the payment terms. (For example: 25%Dis-Net15)
- Discount %: Enter the discount percentage available for early payment. (For example: 25)
- Discount Days: Define how many days from the invoice date the discount is applicable. (For example: 5)
- Net Due Days: Specify the number of days within which the invoice must be paid in full. (For example: 15)
- Day of the Month: Enable this checkbox if due dates should align with specific calendar dates instead of a day-count from the invoice date. (Here, we leave this checkbox Unchecked, since we are basing this on day count, not a specific calendar date
- (Optional) Use 'Minimum Days' with Prox Terms: When the Day of the Month checkbox is selected, the Minimum Days field becomes available. This field determines whether the invoice due date should roll into the following month based on when the invoice is entered. [For Example: If we set Minimum Days to 10, Net Due Date to 30, and the invoice date is the 25th, the due date will be adjusted to the 30th of the next month. This configuration ensures that invoices posted late in a month are not due in the same month, providing vendors with adequate lead time.]



iii. Save the Terms Code:

-
Select Save to store the new terms code.

II. Assigning the Terms Code to a Vendor

To apply the configured terms:

-
Open the AP Vendors screen under the path: Applications -> Accounts Payable -> Setup and Maintenance -> Vendors.

-
Pull up the required Vendor ID from the lookups

-
Navigate to the 'Defaults' Tab and locate the Terms Code

-
Update 'Terms Code' field, and save the vendor record.



Once saved and assigned to the vendor, the system will:

-
Automatically calculate a 25% discount if the payment is made within 5 days.

-
Set the due date for the invoice at 15 days from the invoice date.



III. Result:

i. Open the AP Transactions screen under the path: Applications -> Accounts Payable -> Transactions -> Transactions.

ii. Create a new 'Transaction' and add the 'Vendor ID' for whom the 'Terms Code' was updated and post the same

Notes:

-
Any changes to Terms Codes will only affect newly entered transactions.

-
It is important that we confirm vendor agreements before creating or assigning new terms codes.

5c9a88f9-a49a-44ec-8403-c031f1e1b3ef.title: Customer Payment Terms
5c9a88f9-a49a-44ec-8403-c031f1e1b3ef.content:
Problem
How do I create a customer payment term.

Resolution
To setup term codes, first go to Accounts Receivable > Setup and maintenance > Term codes

- Use the Terms Codes function to create, modify, or delete codes that define customer payment terms. These codes act as shorthand for specifying business conditions with customers. For instance, one customer might be assigned a terms code allowing a 10-day discount period, while another might have a 30-day discount period.
- Once you've set up the terms codes, you can assign them to customer records. These terms will then be automatically applied during transaction entry, though they can still be adjusted for individual transactions as needed.
- You can also set a default terms code for each customer using the Customers function, which can later be overridden during transaction processing.

- Click the New button on the toolbar to open a blank terms code entry screen.
- In the Terms Code field, enter a unique code for the new payment terms.
- In the Description field, enter a brief description of the terms. This description will appear on invoices and credit memos.
- In the Disc % field, enter the discount percentage (between 0 and 100) that will be applied if the customer pays within the discount period.
- In the Net Due Days field, enter the number of days the customer has to pay the invoice in full.
Note:

If you check the Day Of Month box, the Net Due Days field will instead accept a specific day of the month (this is known as Prox Terms).
Enabling Day Of Month will also activate the Minimum Days field, where you can specify the minimum number of days a customer has to pay and still qualify for the discount.

Example:
If Minimum Days is set to 10, Net Due Date is set to 30, and Discount is 10%, and a customer places an order on the 21st, the invoice will not be due on the 30th of the same month. Instead, it will be due on the 30th of the following month. When this option is enabled, the system always selects the first occurrence of the due date in the month after the invoice date.

In the Discount Days field, enter the number of days the customer has to pay the invoice in order to receive the discount.

Click the Save button on the toolbar to save the new terms code.

c79da65b-3254-4240-b110-ae857711287b.title: Closing fiscal period
c79da65b-3254-4240-b110-ae857711287b.content:
Problem
Looking for a way to automatically close or restrict a specific sales account at the end of each fiscal period to prevent further postings.

Resolution
While the system doesn't explicitly refer to closing a "specific sales account" in isolation, you can close accounting periods for individual applications, which would encompass your sales-related data. This process effectively prevents further transactions from being posted to those periods.

To close an accounting period for a specific application, you would follow these steps:

- Change to the Company ID whose period you wish to close.
- Select the Fiscal Year you intend to work with.
- Select the checkbox next to the specific Application and Period you want to close. You can also click the Plus (+) sign next to a period to display the Application IDs you have installed and then select the checkbox for each App ID you want to close for that period.

It's important to note that if you close a General Ledger (GL) period, you will not be able to post any transactions from any application to the General Ledger for that specific period. This means that once a GL period is closed, no further sales invoices, payments, or cash receipts can be posted to the GL for that period.

This method allows you to manage and finalize periods for applications that handle your sales data, ensuring that transactions are recorded within the correct fiscal periods.

4a76bb28-9523-4efa-9a3e-67c42c0a5a29.title: Creating Zones in Warehouse Management WM

0419e8ca-6eff-4026-8196-6b8cc8ca5ece.title: Explaining PO Returns: Purpose and Step-by-Step Creation
0419e8ca-6eff-4026-8196-6b8cc8ca5ece.content:
Problem
Understanding the Need for a PO Return and How to Create them?

Resolution
A PO Return is required only when an invoice has already been posted, or when the transaction is in the "Invoice Received" status. In such cases, direct reversal of the receipt is not allowed, and a PO Return must be created to properly adjust the order.
If only the receipt has been posted and the invoice has not yet been recorded—or if the order is still visible in the transaction screen with the status "Invoice Received"—the transaction can generally be reversed using the Reverse option. For detailed guidance on this process, please refer to Knowledge Base article KB 000092225.


Valid reasons for creating a PO Return include:
- Incorrect quantity or price was invoiced and already posted.
- Invoice was matched to the wrong item or PO.
- Goods were received and invoiced, but the project or requirement was later canceled.
- A pricing or tax discrepancy was identified after invoice posting.
- Duplicate invoice or receipt was posted and cannot be directly reversed.
Using a PO Return in these cases ensures proper adjustment of both inventory and financial records, and helps maintain clean, auditable data.
Step-by-Step Instructions to Create a PO Return
For example, if you have an original purchase order that has already been invoiced and posted, and now you need to return the order, follow these steps:
Start a New PO Return
Ensure the Transaction Type is set to "New Return".
Click the "+" (Add) icon to create a new PO return entry.
Enter Return Details
Fill in the necessary fields.
Make sure the Sold-To ID, line items, and other details exactly match the original PO.
This ensures the return is correctly linked to the original transaction.

ORIGINAL PO:

PO RETURN:

Create Return Receipts and Invoices
Create the receipts and invoices as a mirror of the original transactions.

Save each entry as you go.

Observe Status Changes
Once the receipt is created, the transaction status will change to "Return Authorization".
After the invoice is processed, the status will update to "PO Debit Memo".

Preview and Post the Journal
Preview the Miscellaneous Debits Journal to verify the return entries.

Navigate to Transaction Journals > Post Transactions and post the journal.

Summary
When your Transaction Type is set to "New Return", it updates to "Return Authorization" once goods are sent back to the vendor. After the returned goods are invoiced (debited), it changes to "PO Debit Memo". This process ensures the return is properly recorded and reconciled.

e8d1bbda-9951-46e1-973b-bf8d6a394372.title: Batch Codes Created via API Inserted into Incorrect Company Database in TraveSE
e8d1bbda-9951-46e1-973b-bf8d6a394372.content:

-
Monitor backend SQL activity using SQL Profiler.

-
Notice that the batch code is inserted into a different database, such as "YY".

This issue has been identified as a production bug (internal ID REA DEV-283899 / TFS ID 98434).

The problem will be fixed in Traverse build CXT-2025-SP4-25199. In this build, the database context routing for API batch creation requests has been corrected, ensuring batch codes are inserted into the intended company database.

Bug 98460: CR - API Issue - Base issue - 04351510 - DEV-284132

4c7fcc51-6df3-4110-8fbb-bca3f7415c73.title: Server time zone and Workstation date and time
4c7fcc51-6df3-4110-8fbb-bca3f7415c73.content:
Problem
Where does the server retrieve its date and time from, and where is the workstation's date and time sourced? Additionally, is it possible to change the time zone settings on both the server and the workstation?

Resolution
The Run Time (Server) displayed in areas such as Posting Activity is generated using GMT/UTC, which is the system’s default behavior. These timestamps are captured at the programming level. Meanwhile, the timestamp shown at the end of reports is sourced directly from the server’s local system time.

(Please refer to the attached screenshots of a report and posting activity as examples.)

The workstation date/time, on the other hand, is taken from the local system clock of the workstation. For example, if the workstation time shows 5:25 PM, the timestamp recorded for actions performed from that workstation will reflect 5.25 PM, accordingly, including the date.

This distinction explains the difference in timestamps depending on where and how an action is initiated, either from the server or the user's local machine.

1. Report Time:
- Pulled From: The operating system's system clock of the server machine.
- Time Zone Control: Controlled by the server's time zone settings in the OS (e.g., Windows Server).
2. Workstation Time:
- Pulled From: The local system clock of the user's computer (workstation).
- Time Zone Control: Controlled by the local operating system's time zone settings (e.g., Windows).
3. Posting Activity Runtime (Server)

- Pulled From: Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), which is the system’s default behavior for capturing posting timestamps.
- Used For: Recording the exact time of posting actions within the system, primarily for consistency across global environments.
How to change the Time Zone on the Server:

- Windows Server:
Go to Control Panel > Clock and Region > Date and Time
Click Change time zone
Select the desired time zone and apply changes. (Note: To make these changes on the server, you will need to have administrator permissions.)

Alternatively, we can run a prompt in Command Prompt.
To verify or adjust the time zone on each user’s workstation, please follow these steps in Command Prompt:
(Note: the same procedure can be followed if the server time needs to be changed as well)
To check the current time zone:

tzutil /g

To set the time zone to Pacific Standard Time, for example:

tzutil /s "Pacific Standard Time"

Important Note: Changing the server time zone may affect scheduled tasks, logging, or app behavior, so it should be done with caution.

02d7c0b5-e9b2-46a3-b8ba-3f5cff280329.title: How to Remove a Corrupted or Shredded Check from a Payment Run Before Posting?
02d7c0b5-e9b2-46a3-b8ba-3f5cff280329.content:
Problem
During a check run involving a large number of checks (for example, 100 checks), the sequence was set to begin from Check No. 1 and continued accurately up to Check No. 49. However, Check No. 50 was corrupted due to the Printer fault (Ink discharge) and subsequently shredded.

The remaining checks were intended to be printed starting from Check No. 51 through 101. The expectation is for the Traverse system to skip Check No. 50 and reflect a continuous sequence from 1 to 49, then 51 to 101—excluding the shredded check.

However, Traverse assigned check numbers sequentially from 1 to 100 in the Payment Register, including the invalid Check No. 50. This results in a mismatch between the physical check stock and the system records, for the last 51 Checks.

Assistance is required to remove the entry for the shredded Check No. 50 and correct the check sequence before the batch is posted, ensuring that the Payment Register reflects only the valid and actually printed checks.

Resolution
In scenarios where a check within a payment run has been corrupted or shredded (for example, Check No. 50), and needs to be excluded from the system records without disrupting the overall check sequence, the following steps can be followed using the AP Print Checks screen in Traverse:

A. Review the AP Payment Register
i. Before making any changes, we need to review the AP Payment Register under the path: Applications -> Accounts Payable -> Pay Invoices -> Payment Register
ii. Carefully review the listed checks and identify the last correctly printed check number that matches the physical paper copy.
For this scenario, the check sequence was correct up to Check No. 49, and Check No. 50 was the corrupted one.

B. Update Check Printing Parameters in AP Print Checks Screen
i. Navigate to the AP Print Checks screen under the path: Applications -> Accounts Payable -> Pay Invoices -> Print Checks
ii. To skip the voided or corrupted Check No. 50, we need to set the below numbers:
- Set the Starting Check Number to 51.
- Set the Last Good Number to 49.
This approach ensures that Traverse resumes check numbering from 51 onward, explicitly omitting Check 50 from the internal sequence. The check numbers already assigned up to Check 49 remain unchanged in the check run, while the subsequent checks—originally following Check 49—are renumbered starting from 51.

Note: If the checks have already been printed and we only want to update the system records (without reprinting), we can use the ‘Output’ option instead of the 'Print' button. This will reflect the updated check sequence in Traverse without triggering another print job.

C. Validate the Adjusted Check Sequence
i. Once the process is complete, we need to review the AP Payment Register again under the path: Applications -> Accounts Payable -> Pay Invoices -> Payment Register.
ii. We can observe the sequence corrected as expected as shown below:

741ae958-9e37-4a70-a3ed-6662f8f6c0a6.title: When outputting ACH file>the "EffectiveEntryDate" is pulling the workstation date of when the ACH file is created.
741ae958-9e37-4a70-a3ed-6662f8f6c0a6.content:
Problem
While trying to set up an export layout for ACH, the "date" field options are returning the current date. We were trying to use one that pulls the "payment date" from the Create ACH File screen. In Global (11.2), the EffectiveEntryDate field works as expected, but in Standard (11.0), it pulls the workstation date.

The AP Transaction has an Invoiced date of 9/19/24



Prepared Payments on 11/19/24, with a payment date of 9/19/24

Prepared voucher

Created ACH File

b8678fc9-3c29-424a-8f98-1f26afaafa60.title: SQL Profiler Troubleshooting - Basic Example of Use
b8678fc9-3c29-424a-8f98-1f26afaafa60.content:
Problem
Building on the KB document, "SQL Profiler for Support - General," let's look at a more basic example of how you would use this.

We'll pick on the WMS Picking Slip function as it serves a great example. Let's say the scenario is that it prints but nothing is on it.
We can run a trace and see how the process is building things and determine what is really getting pulled on to the Picking Slip. In reality, we're using profiler to see what was running as step one. Step two is taking that information and building it out in SQL to run manually and investigate the issue further.

To effectively use this information, you need to have some familiarity with the software's tables and familiarity with T-SQL. None of this information is to be shared with customers, this is absolutely internal. A customer could misuse this and do great harm.

Resolution
SQL Profiler
To start things off we need to be ready to run the Picking Slip process and then we'll set the trace up.


Let's do a regular TSQL trace:


And we'll remove the login audits and the existing connection:
Click run and go back to Traverse and print or output the Picking Slip.

Stop the trace after the report has printed or output.

First we see a temporary table, likely to serve as a filter for the process or to use the data it contains later in the proc.

Next, it inserts a value into that temporary table. Since I chose to print just one picking slip, it is creating a record for the order I want to print, and putting it in the temporary table.

Next, we are notified that a proc was run. This is good to know, because we will want to go get this in SQL next so we can run it manually and see what is going on.

Lastly, we get the proc again, but with the parameters in which it is run by.

In this example, there are only a few parameters but this really shines when you are using it to find something that has many parameters. Now you know exactly how the software was running this proc to the point of an issue. Or to the point where it prints weird information. Etc.

Here is a commentary on the other profiler hits that may occur above and below the screenshots I included. Those represent adhoc hits, where the software's code is doing something and using SQL. You can click through those records and get an idea what the software is doing but information is minimal. We are going to focus on the Picking Slip process that got trapped because the software design is relying on this to generate everything the Picking Slip Report will print for us. So in essence, this is going to explain what the oddity is that the customer is reporting.

SQL Server Management Studio
Now that we have some information let's put this together and look at the reported issue.
First, lets open SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) and login to the instance.

Next, lets open a new query window and we'll start building our statement to investigate this.

Copy in the statements from profiler to build the temporary tables and insert data, we'll also copy the proc execution to keep this information but we'll comment it out. You'll see why further below:

Next, let's go get the proc and paste that in here. We can expand the database we ran this in, GLB for this example.

Expand Programmability then expand Stored Procedures


Navigate to trav_WMPickingListDtl_proc, right-click on that and Modify:


NOTE: Do not do this in production for a customer, you should be doing this with restored data in your secure server. Using the Modify function, or scripting the procedure as an Alter, Create, Drop and ____, are all risky options in production because you can accidentally change a customer's procedure. That can potentially take them down or cause data issues and require re-running various server updates. It should simply be avoided.

Copy the entire procedure and paste that into your other window, below the commented execute statement.
This shot doesn't display the whole proc but it is all highlighted for this part.


Next, you need to remove the use statement, I'd also get rid of the comment:

Remove these SETs:

And change the ALTER PROCEDURE section to DECLARE:


Remove the AS since we are not using the ALTER statement and remove the beginning of the try catch:

Also remove the ending of the try catch, this section is at the bottom:

See example further below for clarifications.

I also added a commented out section to drop the other two temporary tables that the proc creates. I do this in case I want to re-run this proc wide open, so I pre-emptively create this before doing any work.
Alternately, you could check to see if the object exists and drop and recreate it similar to what it is doing for the temp table #PickIDs.

The parameters we got from Profiler have been entered in to the parameters under the DECLARE, so that is ready to go.

Lastly, I like to just read through the whole process and see what it is doing. I'll exclude a screenshot because its a lot to scroll through. With more complex procedures reading through the proc first might help you quite a bit if you have an understanding of what is going on before you start stepping through it.

At this point we could run this wide open, just execute it since everything is in place now, and our results yield nothing. So our SQL results are just like what was reported, blank.

If there was data here, but not when running this in the software, it would be best to pursue a client-side issue since the server side appears to be getting data fine.

Naturally, this takes us to the next phase of investigation: why is this occurring?
We'll approach stepping through this bottom to top, to look at what the results were and what lead to that result.

We know this statement yields nothing so we must look at where this all comes from. In this example, we may want to focus on the filter (WHERE clause of the SQL statement.)

Perhaps there is no result because the Qty value from the temporary table #qtyOnHand is not greater than 0.
We know the variable @PrintBinQty is 1 (verify this in the DECLARE section if unsure.)
We may also want to check on the other two temporary tables involved to see what they hold. You may want to look at the last few tables in the section I did not mention, however you may have the most luck with the first ones.

What should you look for? Anything, for the temp tables, what is in there? Is there anything? For the other tables they join to, they look at bins and container names, and UOMs for the items. Overall, maybe something is missing or incorrect, or causing the information to become excluded. There is not always a straight answer as to what you should expect.

In all, the next step is to step through the procedure how you see fit to. Maybe its running the statements as SELECT statements instead of INSERT statements, to see what it is getting and moving around. We'll look at this more in our example now.

Let's look at both temp tables wide open:

Let's read further up to see what populates these tables. We'll look for the initial INSERT statement and pay attention to updates and possible DELETE statements. Anything that explains what comes and goes from these tables.

I'll jump right to the first INSERT statement for #PicksInfo, I have copied my DECLARE section from further above down to right in-between the INSERT and SELECT, so that I can highlight the DECLARE and SELECT, allowing me to see what it wants to put in this table.
No results. But we know that there is a value in #PickIDs.
Let's run this without the filter (SQL's WHERE clause) and see what we get:

Looking at the filter logic, the sum of QtyReq - QtyPacked must be greater than 0. If we add QtyPacked to the SELECT we can see that 10 has already been packed, thus there is nothing to print for the picking slip:

Okay, this may now have become a silly example, we could have seen that this was already packed if we looked in other areas such as the WMS Release Items function. But sometimes cases are presented to us in a way, the answer may be obvious, but only once you reach the end of your investigation.

Hopefully this has helped as a more basic demonstration on how to use this feature. Look for a more complex example KB in the future.

7729c340-3bb4-452d-9568-fc6ca71db451.title: General Install Package Information
7729c340-3bb4-452d-9568-fc6ca71db451.content:
Problem
This is an internal only document.

The purpose of this document is to bring awareness to the components of install packages. As support resources, we may need to test an install package and/or deploy it. It's best to have an understanding of what the package contains and how it needs to be delivered for a successful implementation. We will discuss what an install package is and what the components can be further below.

Resolution
Traverse Layers
First let's talk about layering. Traverse can have layers of programs, the client layer, business layer, and data layer. Customizations also respect  those layers and sit on top of and enhance the vanilla layers below. ProcessPro Global is an excellent example of layering, really it is Traverse Global with a modified layer on top of it that make it ProcessPro Global. Customers then have additional; modifications that sit on top of the layers as needed. In some cases of multiple customizations, you may have 3 or more layers, all depending on the kinds of modifications in play.

Why make Traverse sound like an onion? In order to deliver the layers the right way, install packages were developed as we know them to make it easy to deliver files to a customer. The regular build updates process delivers the vanilla level of files for Traverse Global or ProcessPro Global while install packages deliver the rest. In the case of ProcessPro Global, the updates process delivers the ProcessPro Global files and the Traverse Global files all as one package.

What is an Install Package

An install package is a group of files packaged as a deliverable for the customer, for support that mainly means customizations. Physically, it comes as a self-extracting executable, sometimes you are provided with this already extracted. In the end, the contents get copied into the updates folder and the updates get applied based on the type of update: Client-only, server-only, or both.
It uses a special assembly list, AssemblylistCustom.xml, that lists out all the custom files the client folder needs to have. This allows us to use the updates process when applying the updates client-side. Server-side updates can be completed after the files are copied into the updates folder at the beginning of the process, covered in a different KB.

Longstanding, the process has been to provide every custom file that the customer needs present in their environment, so the install package includes everything the customer needs in order to run their customizations. This is usually true even if only one thing is new or different for the new install package the client receives. Double-check what you do receive for the package, as it also possible you are only be given the updated files, and potentially an updated assembly list to reflect the new/updated file(s).

Since an install is delivering custom components, it could really be delivering anything. As someone testing or deploying this, we need to be aware of what is in the package so we know what to test or deploy. If you are testing, be sure to get information about the changes that warrant a new package. If you are deploying, make sure to get information as to the kind of update. Is it client only? Server only? Both? Are there any special updates involved, like WMS mobile or Portals? Other applications or executables?

Components of an Install Package

Overall, we have a potential client side portion of the install package, a server side to the install package, and then there's a mixed bag of other things. So first, get acquainted with what you have if you have a related task. Here are categories of what may be in here:

- Install Steps
- Client side files
- Server side files
- WMS mobile files
- Portals files
- Design Studio files
- Other

Install Steps
There should be a note included in the install package that provides the install steps to take. It will specify the order in which things should be applied and what should be applied. For example, perhaps there are 3 custom server update files to run. This document will list the names of the files to run, and in what order so that things are layered properly. If you have a self-extracting install package, the steps file will generate in the process. If there is no note, be sure to double check with whoever provided the install package. It is better to prepare than to miss something.

If you are not deploying the install package and someone else is, make sure they also get the steps so there is no question how deployment should go. That is case per case, since customizations can be all kinds of things, they may not be the same steps to deploy as the last time.

Client Component
You may have dlls, configuration files, forms, reports, FRM's, REPX's, XSD's . This depends on the version in play. For example, frms and repx files are Design Studio files that get placed in the client folder for Traverse 11.0. In Traverse Global or ProcessPro Global, you would have changes saved to the database so physical files do not need to be present in the client folders. You may find these file types for the global platform as part of the install package, as a means to save to the database for the customer.



There could be other special files in here. Since we are talking about customizations, the customer may have requested anything and we devised a way to accomplish that. This is another reason its good to be aware of what is in the install package so you know what to do.

Server Component
There will be a server folder if there is a server side component to the install package. If they exist in the install package, there will be a TSMX file as part of the package. File naming conventions may vary, but you will notice it is very different from 'ServerUpdate_25143.' Depending on the customizations in play, there could be multiple files. The install steps noted above will help you understand what you need to run for the update. If there is any question to that, or something seems incorrect or out of place, ask whoever provided the package to you to clarify.

WMS Mobile
It may be possible a customer has a WMS Mobile customization, or potentially a hotfix. In this case the install package will likely have a 'Portal' or 'WMS' directory in the install package with the files you need. Typically arranged in a way similar to the directory in wwwroot such that you only need to copy the files in and they will merge with the appropriate directories.

For clarity, WMS backoffice is part of the Traverse Global or ProcessPro Global client and those custom files would be deployed with the rest of the install package to the Traverse Global or ProcessPro Global client and/or part of the custom server update. WMS Mobile would live in the appropriate Inetpub > wwwroot directory where the WMS mobile files are at for the customer.

Portals
Like WMS Mobile, a customer may have Portals customizations that could reach to the Traverse Global or ProcessPro Global client and/or the Portals pieces within Inetpub > wwwroot where the internal and external portals files live. If there are mods for the mobile component, it is likely you will have a 'Portal' directory in the install package with the files you need. Typically arranged in a way similar to the directory in wwwroot such that you only need to copy the files in and they will merge with the appropriate directories.

Design Studio
There was a note above in the client section as its possible there are FRM or REPX files in the client section of the install package. It simply depends on the version the customer is on and types of changes. Some customers have FRM and REPX directories in the install package because the customer has many of these changes. It is best to take note of what files are in there so you know if you need to test or deploy anything new.

Other
This is am interesting category, back to the nature of customizations, the customer has a need that we try to accommodate with customizations to the software. This opens doors too all kinds of files and supporting items sometimes. So this last category is meant to bring awareness that anything can be in an install package and it is best to inspect this so you know what is in play. Users may have supporting python files, custom executables or utilities that are included with the packages. For more information, we likely have supporting files like SOW and CBR documentation but not everything is always documented, even when it should be.

Lastly, consider that customers may also use Design Studio. If you happen across any files or changes, they do not always mean we have produced them. Sometimes customers modify things already modified for them as part of an install package. It is always a great practice if deploying an install package to backup all databases, client folder, update folder, and then if WMS or Portals updates are delivered, those directories in Inetpub > wwwroot should also get backed up respectively.
