5501bba3-1d64-4413-b0b6-daaa62e320fd.title: How to setup postal code format
5501bba3-1d64-4413-b0b6-daaa62e320fd.content:
Problem
In vendor setup, after changing Country code to CAN (Canadian company), the Postal Code field does not update to a Canadian format. No alpha characters are permitted, only numeric, and the format remains the U.S. 5 digit-4 digit, rather than changing to two 3-digit fields.

Resolution
Go to System Manager > Setup and Maintenance > Country Codes

Review the postal code mask for the country code CAN.

We can see that the format is in #####-####. This accepts only the numbers in the format 5 digit- 4 digit.

Input masks specify how data is entered and displayed in text fields.

EnterFor#Using a digit or space (optional)0Using digits 0-99Using digits 0-9 (optional)LUsing letters A-ZAUsing digits 0-9 and letters A-ZaUsing digits 0-9 and letters A-Z (optional)CUsing any characters except spaces<Causes all following characters to be converted to lowercase>Causes all following characters to be converted to uppercaseNote: If your mask consists of four characters and you want all to be numbers, enter 0000. If you want the first and third characters to be letters, the second character to be a number, and the fourth character to be a letter or a number, enter L0LA.

Change that Postal code mask to AAA-AAA so that it accepts both numbers and alphabets.



Click SAVE and the format will be changed to the Canadian format.

54ef506f-cd88-4927-b9d3-01047c24fc74.title: How to Issue a Single Check for a Vendor when an Invoice and Debit Memo need to be processed together?
54ef506f-cd88-4927-b9d3-01047c24fc74.content:
Problem
How to Issue a Single Check for a Vendor when an Invoice and Debit Memo need to be processed together?



Let us consider an example where a vendor has both an outstanding invoice and a debit memo in the system at the time of payment processing. For example, if a vendor has an invoice for $100 and an associated debit memo for $20, and the user expects the system to net these amounts and generate a single check for $80. However, during the Accounts Payable check run, the system issues a Check for $100, ignoring the credit balance from the debit memo. As a result, the 'Debit Memo' is sitting within the 'AP Hold/Release Invoices' screen. How to fix this?



Once the 'Prepare Payments' step was done, the below log shows up.



The 'Edit Register' looks as below showing a 'Check' worth of $100 will be issued.



After the Payment was posted, the 'Debit Memo' is sitting in the 'AP Hold/Release Invoices' screen, even though the status was 'Released' at the time of preparing the Payments:

Resolution
In the AP Vendors screen, there is a setting called 'Check Option' in the 'Defaults' Tab that decides how the system processes check payments for vendor invoices. There are two available options:

-
Consolidated:

-
When selected, all approved invoices for the vendor will be combined into a single check during the payment process.

-
This is especially useful for vendors who prefer receiving one consolidated payment instead of multiple checks.

-
It simplifies reconciliation for both parties and reduces the number of checks issued.

-
Individual:

-
When selected, the system will generate a separate check for each individual invoice.

-
This might be required in cases where vendors request one payment per invoice, or when each invoice must be matched and tracked independently.



Note:

If a debit memo has been entered into Accounts Payable for a vendor, and we are using the Individual setting, the system will not be able to apply the debit memo correctly during the check run. And Traverse would retain the 'Debit memo' and will issue the 'Individual Checks' for the Invoices.


In such cases, we must temporarily switch the vendor’s Check Option to “Consolidated” to allow the system to net the debit memo and the invoice together and issue a proper payment.

Once the check run is completed, we can switch the vendor’s setting back to “Individual” if needed.



To update this setting the User needs to follow the below steps:

i. Navigate to the AP Vendors screen under the path: Applications -> Accounts Payable -> Setup and Maintenance -> Vendors.

ii. Pull up the required 'Vendor ID' and then navigate to the 'Defaults' Tab

iii. Update the 'Check Option' setting to 'Consolidated'

iv. Hit on 'Save' to update the changes.



Once this was completed, the User can process the Payments, and the Payment cycle looks as below:

Once the 'Prepare Payments' step was done, the below log shows up.



The 'Edit Register' looks as below showing a 'Consolidated Check' worth of $80 will be issued.

With this, the 'Debit Memo' will be washed off from the 'AP Hold/Release Invoices' screen

Note:  This process works differently in TRAVERSE 11.0

8187926b-43c7-461f-a6ad-bb36cfe0f189.title: How to Clear Stored Update Path in Traverse to Prevent Update Prompts
8187926b-43c7-461f-a6ad-bb36cfe0f189.content:
Problem
Users are repeatedly getting "Updates are available" pop-up prompts when launching Traverse, even though no new updates are available.

Resolution
Here are the steps to remove the stored update path in the UpdateSettings.config file to prevent unnecessary update pop-ups when launching Traverse.

Steps:

-
Navigate to User Folder

-
Open This PC > Local Disk (C:) > Users > Open the folder named after the current user (e.g., CChapa).

-
Note: The username folder will differ for each user login.

-
Access AppData Folder

-
In the address bar, type Appdata at the end of the above address to access the hidden Appdata folder.

(Example: C:\Users\CChapa\AppData) — Refer to Screenshot 1.

-
Locate the Configuration File

-
From there, navigate to:

Local > Traverse > UpdateSettings.config

-
Edit the Configuration File

-
Open UpdateSettings.config using Notepad or any text editor.

-
You’ll see content similar to the following:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?> <configuration> <updateSettings> <ClientUpdateFolder>\\bt-serv-trvrs\TRAV-UPDATES</ClientUpdateFolder> </updateSettings> </configuration>
-
Delete the path inside <ClientUpdateFolder> so it appears as:

xml
CopyEdit
<ClientUpdateFolder></ClientUpdateFolder>
(Refer to Screenshot 2.)

-
Save the File

-
Save the changes and close the file.

-
Verify

-
Open Traverse.

-
Go to Help > Check for Updates.

-
Ensure the Update Server Folder Path is now blank.

3ae75d9e-9369-4422-b4f2-df86364a88d3.content:
Problem
We are getting an error when the Automation tries to run. I’m not sure if this is something that is related to us trying to use a custom dll

Resolution
Title: Traverse Automation Error – Missing DLLs in Action Services Folder

Description:
Customer encountered an error while trying to create a new service in Traverse. The issue appeared during the automation process, possibly linked to a custom DLL.

Issue:
Customer reported:

“I am trying to create the service now and am getting the following error.

We are getting an error when the Automation tries to run. I’m not sure if this is something that is related to us trying to use a custom dll.”

Resolution:
Placing the necessary DLLs in the Traverse Action Services directory resolved the issue.

Ensure all required DLLs, especially custom ones, are present in the Traverse Action Services folder before initiating or testing automation services.

085a240a-0807-4454-a73b-9a6c05924331.title: Service Item are not valid for this function
085a240a-0807-4454-a73b-9a6c05924331.content:
Problem
While trying to create an AP Transaction or a PO Transaction, users are attempting to add an Item ID that is a 'Service' Item Type as a line item entry in the Transaction; however, upon selecting the item, they get a warning message, 'Service Items are not valid for this function'.

Resolution
This warning message indicates that the company is currently not configured to allow purchases of Item IDs that are 'Service' Item types. This configuration is controlled by the "Allow Service Items In Purchases" Inventory Business Rule.

- To review the current Business Rule configuration, please navigate to System Manager → Company Setup → Business Rules → IN-Inventory, and in the Miscellaneous section, the  "Allow Service Items in Purchases" will be present.





- If this Business Rule is set to 'No', users will not be allowed to enter Item IDs that are Service Item Types to AP and/or PO Transactions, and users will receive the warning message that is listed in the Problem section of the article. If this Business Rule is set to 'Yes', users will be allowed to enter Item IDs that are Service Item Types to AP and/or PO Transactions.
- To change this setting, select the desired functionality (Yes/No), and then select the Apply and then the OK button on the bottom left of the SM Business Rules screen.

9efc07c9-0d35-42a7-adb0-b31765104728.title: PO Deposits with discounts
9efc07c9-0d35-42a7-adb0-b31765104728.content:
Problem
How to process a PO deposits with Discounts

Resolution
- Purchase Order is created in the Purchase Order -> Transactions -> Transactions screen.  Fill out all necessary line items.
- When it is all the way entered and saved a prompt may appear asking if you wish to accept the calculated discount.  Choose “Yes”.
- Before leaving the Purchase Order you may wish to look at the Totals tab.  Confirm the Discount Amount and the Terms Code.

- When complete, save the Purchase Order
- If you wish to enter a Deposit, follow these steps.
- Call up the Purchase Order and click the “Update” Button.
- Click the “Deposit” button at the top of the screen.
- Enter the Deposit date and amount.  (When entering the deposit amount, two strategies can be used.  The simplest is to just manually calculate any discount and only enter that discounted amount.  The second strategy would be to enter the full amount and then manually adjust the discount in AP.  For the rest of this explanation, I will be assuming the first strategy.)

- Close the deposit screen and save the Purchase Order.
- Go through all the normal steps to run reports and Post Transactions in Purchase Order.
- In Accounts Payable, there will not be an open AP Invoice with an Invoice Number of “DepositXXXX” where XXXX is the Transaction ID of the Purchase Order.
- Prepare Payments and create a check for this Invoice as normal, and post.

- Note that at this point in the processing, there will be a Debit Memo showing on the Open Invoice View and Open Invoice report for this Vendor that mirrors the Deposit Invoice that was just paid.  The Debit Memo will be on Hold, and it will not appear on the Hold/Release Invoices screen, and will not be (yet) available to be included on a check.  This record is there to make the AP Aging look correct.  Don’t get confused by this.
- When it is time to Receive and Invoice the lines, this can be done by clicking the All button at the top of the screen to receive and invoice all open items at once, or the line items can be received and invoiced one at a time using the Receipts/Invoices button.  I will be describing the second method.
- Click Update on the Purchase Order.  Click the Receipts/Invoices button.  A new window appears.  It will initially be displaying the Receipt Entry.
- Enter a receipt or receipts for all items that are being received.

- Next click the Invoices button at the top to toggle the window over to the Invoice Entry.
- Enter Invoice amounts for the line items received.

- Note the Invoice Date that is entered, which will carry over to AP.  Also note that the full amount of the cost should be entered, and not the calculated discount.  Discount amounts are handled elsewhere.
- Save and close this screen.
- To double-check the date, amount, and discount numbers, go to the Totals tab, and press the button for Invoice Totals on the right.
- A window appears with all Invoices in it.  Click on the line of an Invoice that was just entered, and click the >> button on the top right to see the details.
- Note the totals on the Totals tab, which should be for the full amount of the Invoice.  Click the Payment tab.
- Confirm that the correct amount of the Discount is in the Discount box.  If it is not, calculate it and add it.  The amount of the cost minus the discount, ie the final check amount, should be displaying in the Payment 1 Box.
- Save and Close the Invoice Totals popup.  Save and Close the Purchase Order.
- Go through all the normal steps to run reports and Post Transactions in Purchase Order.
- At this point there should now be an Open Invoice in AP for the full amount of the cost that has a discount available to be applied.  There should also be an open Debit Memo for the amount of any previously entered and posted deposits.  (This is the item from #6 above, now available to be included on a check.)

- If for whatever reason a discount is desired but the discount amount is either incorrect or missing, it can be added at this time on the Hold/Release Invoices screen by choosing the invoice row and clicking the Edit button at the top.
- Payments can now be prepared to include both the new Invoice for the full amount along with the discount, and the Debit Memo representing the amount paid previously as part of a deposit.
- When preparing payments, be care of the Invoice Date chosen to make sure it is on or later than the Invoice Due Date of any invoices or debit memos you wish to include, and that the Discount Due Date is on or later than the Discount Date of any discount you wish to include.

f72f7fdc-67e4-43db-9c3b-0be8386b41dd.title: Cloud Down Option Not Visible in AppCentral
f72f7fdc-67e4-43db-9c3b-0be8386b41dd.content:
Problem
The customer is unable to find the "Cloud Down" option under the Case Type dropdown while creating a case through AppCentral.

Resolution
The issue occurred because the App URL was not populated in the AppCentral Admin Control, which prevented the "Cloud Down" option from appearing in the Case Type dropdown.

To resolve this, we coordinated with the Technical team to obtain the correct SaaS App URL for the customer. Once received, we shared the URL with the AppCentral team, who then updated the configuration accordingly.

27b06d09-49a6-4723-a62e-4ef6440f6c81.title: Labor Codes - Service Director
27b06d09-49a6-4723-a62e-4ef6440f6c81.content:
Problem
What are Labor Codes and how to set them up?

Resolution
Labor Codes are used to define the types of work that technicians are qualified to perform. When assigned to a technician, the Labor Code specifies the tasks they are capable of completing. When linked to a "Work To Do" description, it helps match the most suitable technician to the job.

How to Set Up Labor Codes:

-
Navigate to the Labor Codes screen:
Application > Service Director > Setup and Maintenance > Labor Codes

-
The Labor Codes screen will appear.

-
Click the New Record button on the toolbar to open a blank Labor Code record.

-
In the Labor Code field, enter a unique code (maximum 6 characters).

-
In the Description field, enter a brief description (maximum 35 characters). Additional details can be entered in the Additional Description field.

-
Select the appropriate Tax Class from the Tax Class drop-down list. This determines the applicable sales tax rate based on the Tax Location Group from the Work Order.

-
Enter the Unit of Measure in the Unit field (typically HR for hours or MIN for minutes).

-
Enter the Labor Cost per Unit in the Labor Cost field. This is the internal cost of having an employee with the Labor Code perform work.

-
Enter the Billing Rate per Unit in the Billing Rate field. This is the amount that will be billed to the customer.

-
Select a Calendar Color to represent this Labor Code in the calendar.

-
Select the GL Sales Account from the Sales Account drop-down list. This account will be credited for the billing amount for the time recorded for Employees using this Labor Code.

-
Select the GL Cost of Revenue Account from the Cost of Revenue Account drop-down list. This account will be debited for the cost of the labor recorded for time recorded for Employees using the Labor Code.

-
Select the GL Payroll Expense Account from the Payroll Expense Account drop-down list. This account will be credited for the cost of the labor recorded for time recorded for Employees using this Labor Code.

-
Click the Save button to save your work.

Producing a Labor Code List:

-
Click the Print Preview button to preview the Labor Code report for the code currently displayed on the screen.

-
The Preview Report screen will appear.

-
Click the Print button in the toolbar to print the report.

Note: To print a full list of Labor Codes, you must preview and print each one individually.

4bcfeb41-9b9a-4f67-b993-9bb8725e55fa.title: Form Code OSAS
4bcfeb41-9b9a-4f67-b993-9bb8725e55fa.content:
Problem
The client wants to set up the Form Codes

Setting Up Form Codes

Form codes assign copy names to laser forms that require multiple prints (e.g., file copy, customer copy, accounting copy). Follow these steps to set up or modify form codes:

-
Access Form Codes:
Select Form Codes from the Company Setup menu. The Form Codes screen appears.

Select Form Type:

2aa942fc-fd28-4cb1-9754-c06e9827c4fb.title: Migration from 11.0 to 11.2 - tblApHistDetail  - error "The given value of type String from the data source cannot be converted to type nvarchar of the specified target column"
2aa942fc-fd28-4cb1-9754-c06e9827c4fb.content:
Problem
During the migration of Traverse from version 11.0 to 11.2 for one of their customers, they encountered an error related to the table tblApHistDetail. The error message states:

"The given value of type String from the data source cannot be converted to type nvarchar of the specified target column."

Open Traverse Global Migration Tool
Select the Source and Destination SQL Server Instance, User ID and Password.
Fill in the Migration Type> Traverse 11.0 (Standard), SYS Database
Select the company ID and Hit Execute
Enter Master Username and Master Password and hit Continue

Resolution
Issue 1:  The update process is trying to re-insert records into tblSmPeriodConversionDetail.  Run this script in the v11 company database prior to running the migration to fix this error "Cannot insert duplicate key row in object 'dbo.tblSmPeriodConversionDetail' with unique index 'UX_tblSmPeriodConversionDetail'. The duplicate key value is (13, AP)"



DELETE FROM tblSmPeriodConversionDetail



Issue 2: The main issue is there must be a customization on tblApHistDetail.  Three columns in the v11 company database have column lengths longer than what base Global allows.  Run this script in the target Global company database before the migration to this this error "The given value of type String from the data source cannot be converted to type nvarchar of the specified target column."



ALTER TABLE tblApHistDetail ALTER COLUMN JobId NVARCHAR(20);
ALTER TABLE tblApHistDetail ALTER COLUMN PhaseId NVARCHAR(20);

ALTER TABLE tblApHistDetail ALTER COLUMN TaskId NVARCHAR(20);



Issue 3:  This is optional as it would relate to the SYS database migration, but would address this issue "Cannot insert duplicate key row in object 'dbo.tblSmUserDefault' with unique index 'UX_tblSmUserDefault_AppIdValueId'. The duplicate key value is (TPS10005, duplicate_check)."



Run this is both v11 and Global SYS databases prior to the migration



DROP INDEX [UX_tblSmUserDefault_AppIdValueId] ON [dbo].[tblSmUserDefault] WITH ( ONLINE = OFF )



After the migration, find the duplicate values that migrated.



select * from  tblSmUserDefault where AppId = 'TPS10005'



This should find a duplicate ValueId for both duplicate_check and partial_approval_flag.  Delete the duplciates



delete from tblSmUserDefault where id = 'CEA54474-2BA8-4E38-B68E-03863894750F'
delete from tblSmUserDefault where id = '5231D902-D424-4D19-9367-A407AAAE0B50'



Finally, run this script to recreate the index



CREATE UNIQUE CLUSTERED INDEX [UX_tblSmUserDefault_AppIdValueId] ON [dbo].[tblSmUserDefault]
(

[AppId] ASC,

[ValueId] ASC

)WITH (PAD_INDEX = OFF, STATISTICS_NORECOMPUTE = OFF, SORT_IN_TEMPDB = OFF, IGNORE_DUP_KEY = OFF, DROP_EXISTING = OFF, ONLINE = OFF, ALLOW_ROW_LOCKS = ON, ALLOW_PAGE_LOCKS = ON, OPTIMIZE_FOR_SEQUENTIAL_KEY = OFF) ON [PRIMARY]

800d87b0-bc14-4ee4-b164-038e67b7d18e.title: Updating Local Network Gateway IP Address in Azure
800d87b0-bc14-4ee4-b164-038e67b7d18e.content:
Problem
Louisville, KY location has a new public IP.

Change from:
40.136.45.152
to:
12.206.154.26

Resolution
KB Article: Updating Local Network Gateway IP Address in Azure

This article outlines the step-by-step procedure to update the Local Network Gateway IP address for a customer in Azure.

Prerequisites:

- Ensure Privileged Identity Management (PIM) role is activated before performing these changes. Without activating PIM, you will not have permissions to update the IP address.

Steps:

- Log in to Azure Portal:
- Use your Aptean Cloud account and activate the required PIM role by entering the case number and reason for access.
- Locate the Resource Group:
- Navigate to the server of the particular customer within Azure Portal.
- Click on the server to view its details.
- Identify and click on the associated Resource Group.
- Find the Site-to-Site Connection:
- Within the resource group, search for the Site-to-Site connection that requires the IP address update.
- Click on the connection to open its properties.
- Access Local Network Gateway:
- In the connection details, click on the linked Local Network Gateway.
- Validate that the existing IP address is correct by confirming with customer-provided information.
- Update IP Address:
- On the left navigation pane, click Configuration.
- Under the IP Address section, replace the existing IP address with the new IP address.
- Click Save to apply the changes.
- Download Configuration File for Validation:
- Go back to the connection overview page.
- At the top menu, click on Download Configuration.
- In the download window:
- Set Device Vendor to Generic Samples.
- Set Device Family to Device Parameters.
- Set Firmware Version to Generic-Samples-Device-Parameters.
- Click Download to obtain the configuration file.
- Share with Customer:
- Provide the downloaded configuration file to the customer.
- Ask them to cross-verify and ensure the VPN connection settings are configured correctly from their end.

Note: Always validate changes with the customer’s network team to prevent VPN connectivity disruptions.

Problem
FA Compute Period Depreciation was run for period 1 thru 1 but was posted as from 1 thru 12.

Below the Period Depreciation Report,

Below is the Post Log of Period Depreciation

Resolution
The book has already been calculated and posted for all 12 periods, and this action cannot be undone.

However, if only a single period was posted and the issue is that TRAVERSE incorrectly reflects all 12 as posted, we can adjust it by setting the period back to 1 in the Period Depreciation Setup screen.

To edit the period back to 1 from the Period Depreciation Setup screen, navigate to,

Fixed Asset> Setup and Maintenance> Period Depreciation Setup screen

Once this is calculated, the calculated depreciation can be posted for the correct period.

Problem
When making any change to an existing General Ledger account on the Chart of Accounts screen in General Ledger and then attempting to save a message will appear stating "Fiscal year is not setup in the Period Conversion function. "

Cause
This issue is due period amounts for some account existing for a fiscal year that hasn't been set up in the Period Conversion screen.

Resolution
This issue is due period amounts for some account existing for a fiscal year that hasn't been set up in the Period Conversion screen.  If access to SQL Server in available a query can be run on the tblGlAcctDtl table to find the years in question.

select  Year from tblGlAcctDtl group by year

This will show the list of years that are currently set up in the table.  Navigate to the System Manager -> Company Setup -> Period Conversion screen and set up any Fiscal Years that are included in the list but are not currently set up.

If SQL Server in not available, navigate to the Period Conversion screen and find the earliest year that is set up.  Create new Fiscal Years starting a year earlier than the earliest year and keep creating older years until the message no longer occurs in General Ledger.

b2adae75-c2e9-4f9f-9169-c8cd5dcbb4b5.title: Unable to Access AppCentral Connect Tab or Create New Cases
b2adae75-c2e9-4f9f-9169-c8cd5dcbb4b5.content:
Problem
Some users have reported that the AppCentral Connect tab disappears within a few seconds (typically around 3 seconds) after opening it. This issue prevents affected users from interacting with the tab, specifically blocking their ability to create new support cases through AppCentral.

The behavior is inconsistent and appears to affect only certain users or environments. It does not display any error message before the tab closes, making it difficult for users to proceed with submitting a case or accessing features within the Connect tab.

Resolution
If the AppCentral Connect tab disappears shortly after opening—preventing access to features like creating new cases—please follow the steps below to troubleshoot and resolve the issue:

-
Clear Browser Cache and Cookies
Begin by clearing the cache and cookies in the browser you're using. Accumulated or outdated cached data can interfere with how AppCentral loads and functions, especially after updates.

-
Log Out and Log Back In
If the issue persists after clearing the cache, log out of AppCentral completely. Close the browser, reopen it, and log in again to see if the issue is resolved.

- Update Your Browser
Ensure your browser is up to date. Running an outdated version may lead to compatibility issues with AppCentral. Visit your browser’s official website or settings menu to check for and install the latest updates.
-
Try a Different Browser
If the problem continues, access AppCentral using a different supported browser. We recommend:

-
Microsoft Edge

-
Google Chrome

-
Mozilla Firefox

This can help determine whether the issue is browser-specific.

These steps typically resolve the issue for most users. If the problem still occurs after performing all of the above, please contact support and provide details such as your browser version, user ID, and any relevant screenshots for further assistance.

a7f19fa6-2cf9-4132-bb6e-773b420701e2.title: Setting Up Notifications for an Alert in InfoAlert
a7f19fa6-2cf9-4132-bb6e-773b420701e2.content:
Problem
How can we ensure that alert notifications are correctly configured across all necessary screens so that all relevant users receive timely and accurate alert outputs?

Resolution
To ensure that alert outputs are delivered reliably to the intended users, notification settings must be accurately configured in key areas of the system -- specifically within the Manage Notifications screen and the Select Alerts configuration. Missing or incorrect setup in these areas can lead to alerts not being sent, causing delays or missed actions.

Notifications are important because they ensure the right users are informed of the output or results of alerts.

There are two key areas where notification settings must be properly configured to ensure that results are generated without any issues.

- Manage Notifications screen

Navigate to: Alerts > Alerts > Manage Notifications

The Manage Notifications screen is used to view and manage all alerts currently set up in the Select Alert list. You can use the filters at the top of the screen to narrow down the view by Map ID, Alert ID, or Notification ID—or leave the filters blank to display all configured alerts.

This screen displays key attributes of each alert configuration, including alert sequences, active alerts, notification IDs, and the status of notification actions.

If the alert type is set to email, ensure that the appropriate notification email addresses are correctly configured under the Notification ID tab.

Another place to review notifications is via the Notification button on the Criteria/Notify tab.

-
Navigate to: Alerts > Alerts > Select Alerts, and then select the desired Alert ID (e.g., S00001 as a sample).

Go to the Criteria/Notify tab and click on the Notification button to open the Notification screen.



On this screen, ensure that the email addresses of all users who should receive the alert are properly configured. These IDs will be notified of this alert by email. Mark the associated Alert check box.

Here in this example, the email that needs to be configured is sample@sample.com

- On this screen you can:

- Enter an Email ID, or multiple addresses of those you want notified of this alert by email.
(Info-Alert Email Setup must be properly configured to allow for email output.)
- Enter a Report ID from the drop down list that was previously setup in the Configuration
Options-Define Reports to point to a particular printer for a printed output of the alert.
(There must be at least one valid printer defined in the Windows print applet of this machine
to allow for successful IA Report output).
- Choose a Max Records amount to limit the number of records that show up on your output.
This entry will prevent the potential for a "run-away" notification in the event of non-specific
alert criteria.
- Alert box is checked by default and will provide the specified recipient with the basic Alert
Text output defined within each specific alert.
- Attach box is un-checked by default and works in conjunction with an Action that may be
configured for this alert. The Attach feature allows for a properly configured Action to send a
specific file to the Notification email recipient indicated.
- Action box is un-checked by default and works in conjunction with an Action that may be
configured for this alert. The Action feature allows for a properly configured Action to send
the configured Action email or fax output to the Notification email recipient indicated.
- Event ID is for advanced users and is explained in the Notification Events section of the Info Alert Administrator
manual.

Close the Notification form to return to the Criteria screen for this alert.

d917f223-c2ce-41c7-9ef2-4f49f17d88ff.title: Unrestrict_useraccount_SaaS
d917f223-c2ce-41c7-9ef2-4f49f17d88ff.content:
Problem
Many user accounts from Noble Company were in a restricted state.  Unrestrict all those user accounts and let me know.

Resolution
KB Article: Unrestricting a User Account (SaaS)

This article outlines the procedure to follow when a user account becomes restricted. It includes steps to raise a service request and important user communication requirements.

Steps:

- Log in to the Bastion Server:
- Access the prod001-Bas05 bastion server using your administrative credentials.
- Locate the Organizational Unit (OU) and the username of the restricted user account.
- If you need to unrestrict all restricted users within an OU, note down the OU name.
- Create a Service Desk Case:
- Log in to the Service Desk portal.
- Click on Create New Case.
- Select Aptean Tech Hub Service Request as the case type.

- Enter Case Details:
- Provide a clear description indicating the issue, such as “User account restricted – requires unrestriction.”
- Include the following mandatory information:
- Username
- OU Name
- Domain Name: prod001
- Product Name (if applicable)
- Choose Aptean Tech Hub as the assigned group.
- Submit the Case:
- Review all entered details and submit the service request.

- Post-Submission Process:
- The Tech Hub team or Reliability Tech Hub team will pick up the case and proceed with unrestricting the user account(s).
- Notify the End User:
- Once the account is unrestricted, inform the user accordingly.
- Advise them to log in to the ADSelfService Portal within 7 days to reset their password or complete enrollment.
- Failure to do so will result in the account becoming restricted again.

Note: Always include complete user and OU details in the service request to avoid processing delays.

58098119-e01d-4366-87d7-09690fe62780.title: Creating a New Payroll Department
58098119-e01d-4366-87d7-09690fe62780.content:
Problem
Creating a new department

Resolution
Go to Payroll -> Setup and Maintenance -> Departments

Step 1: Click the New button, on the toolbar, to open a blank department record.

Step 2: Enter a new department ID in the Department ID field.

Step 3: Enter a name for the department in the Name field.

Step 4: Select a similar department to copy from, if applicable. This field is available only when adding a new department.

Step 5: All earning codes, employer taxes, and employer costs set up in the corresponding functions on the Codes Maintenance menu are displayed.

For each earning code, select the general ledger accounts to debit from the adjacent GL Account fields. The accounts are debited when you run the Post Checks function for each earning code, deduction, and cost. This account should be an expense account. Select the Accrued Wages account, if you selected Accrual in the business rules for your accounting basis.

The Accrued Wages account will be credited for the amount of the expenses when Daily Work Transactions are posted.

Step 6: The quarterly and year-to-date expense totals for the department appear in the right-hand pane. These update when you run the Post Transactions and Post Checks functions.

The Total Amount of expenses posted for the expense selected is displayed for each month. This field should not be edited after you have made set-up entries.

Step 7: Click the Save button, on the toolbar, to save the new department record.

4bc8f0cc-3097-49a4-9d59-d33284d774b7.title: Unable to Print Multiple Labels
4bc8f0cc-3097-49a4-9d59-d33284d774b7.content:
Problem
When we print either item labels or receiving labels from Mobile, it prints one label regardless of the number of labels requested.

Resolution
Go to Applications > Inventory > Master Lists > Item Labels
Pull the label style, click on Label Design.

Click on the detail arrow.

Change the multi column layout fields to select the appropriate settings.

The Multi Column Mode should not be set to "None"

- Select "Use Column Count" to create as many columns as are specified in the Column Count number.
- Select "Use Column Width" to create as many columns as will fit with the given width

These select the Multi-Column Layout,  ex. "First Down, then Across", or "

Set your Column Count for the number of columns to print across - ex. 2, 3, etc.

Set your Column Width for the width each column should have.

Set your Column Spacing for the space between each column.



This will enable your labels to print in more than one column.

Click the disk icon to save.

Click the "Preview" button to see a preview of the label layout to verify.

0d4059c9-2ebc-4882-8e37-15a6d5ee3c19.title: OSAS_ Setting up local tax withholding
0d4059c9-2ebc-4882-8e37-15a6d5ee3c19.content:
Problem
Setting up local tax withholding

Resolution
How to create a Local Tax Withholding
- Codes Maintenance – Tax Authority

First step in creating a local tax withholding is to start at the Payroll main menu. Select Codes Maintenance, Tax Authority. Select Local for the Tax Authority then select or enter the correct State Code, MI. Press F2 or click the inquiry icon to select your state from the list of states in the window. Enter 01 for the Local Code. You will be prompted for the Copy From State, MN and Locality, 01. It is very easy to copy the information from an existing location and then edit the information accordingly.

Enter the Description you would like for the new local tax authority. (In this example Michigan – Detroit was used for easy identification)

The new local tax authority for Michigan – Detroit has been created. We will return to edit the values for the Formula and Table ID to reflect the correct values for the state of Michigan and the locality of Detroit. . [Page Down] or F7 to exit.

- File Maintenance – Tax Tables

We need to create a new local tax table for LTXMI01. You must determine if the new local tax withholding is dependent upon a percentage or a percentage and a limit. This new table will contain the information required in the formula PMI01LWH.RTN. When finished creating the new table we will edit the tax authority to correct the Table ID information.
From the Payroll main menu, select File Maintenance, Tax Tables. Enter LTXMI01 and press enter. In the Copy From field enter LTXMN01, if the withholding is based on a percentage or LTXMN01S if a percentage and limit are required, see the examples below. This generates a copy of the appropriate MN local tax table. The recommended naming convention uses the format [LTX]+[STATE]+[CODE]  i.e. LTXMN01.

Change the Description from Minneapolis Local Tax to describe your new local tax. You can edit the Percentage and/or Limit values in the table so they contain the correct value for your Locality. [Page Down] or F7 to exit.


- Formula Maintenance

From the payroll main menu, select File Maintenance, Formula Maintenance to create the new formula PMI01LWH.RTN. Enter PMI01LWH.RTN for the Formula Id and press enter. We want to Copy From PMN01LWH.RTN. The recommended naming convention uses the format P+[STATE]+[CODE]+[LWH]  i.e. PMN01LWH.RTN.

Change the Description for easy identification. [Page Down] and select Create Program at the bottom of the page.  [Page Down] or F7 to exit.

- Codes Maintenance – Tax Authority

Return to Codes Maintenance, Tax Authority and edit the Formula and Table Id information to reflect the new formula and tax tables created in steps 2 and 3 above.

When edits are completed, [Page Down] or F7 to exit.

- Withholdings

From Codes Maintenance open Withholdings. Select Tax Authority Local, State Code MI, Local Code 01 and enter LWH for the Withholding Code. Enter your Description, Liability Acct and Tax Id.  Setup all exclusions you have for deductions and earning codes.

[Page Down] or F7 to exit.

- Setup Tax Groups

To setup the Tax Group, go to Codes Maintenance, Tax Groups to create the new Tax Group.
If the Tax Group exists, enter the Tax Group to edit. If the Tax Group does not exist, enter MI01 for the new Tax Group and Michigan – Detroit for the Description.

Next using Append enter the Withholding information for this Tax Group. Enter the State Withholding information before entering the Local information to the new Tax Group.

When finished with your entries, [Page Down] or F7 to exit.

- State Unemployment Report

Verify that the State Unemployment Report has been setup for this state. From the main Payroll menu, select File Maintenance, Payroll Information. Select Set Up State Unemployment Reports.

Edit the information for your state. When finished, [Page Down] or F7 to exit.

- Edit Employee Withholdings

To test the new Local Withholding setup, edit the Withholding information for an employee and add the new Local Tax Information. Create a manual check and verify that the local tax is calculating for this employee.

Notice the Local tax amount calculated for this employee.

- Repeat steps 1 – 8 to create additional Local Tax Withholdings for this State.



- Variations



- I require a Local Tax Withholding for an employee with a Locality in a second State.

Follow steps 1 – 8 above to create the Local Tax Withholding. Repeat step 6 to create a new Tax Group for both States and the Locality.

Test the new Local Withholdings. Edit the Withholding Information for an employee. Enter the new Tax Group you created above (MNMI) and add the new Local Tax Information. Create a manual check and verify that the local tax is calculating for this employee. Refer to the example below.

8c640b40-132b-4a28-8c71-ebcd83b34311.title: Discrepancy Between Sales Order Task Pane and Item Availability View for an Item
8c640b40-132b-4a28-8c71-ebcd83b34311.content:
Problem
The client has reported a discrepancy between the "Qty Available" displayed in the Sales Order (SO) Task Pane and the quantity shown in the Inventory Item Availability View for a particular item.

The "Qty Available" in the SO Task Pane is expected to be calculated as:
Qty Available = Qty On Hand - Qty Committed - Qty On Hold

Ideally, this value should align with the quantity shown in the Inventory Item Availability View screen. However, in this case, it does not.

Upon further investigation, it appears that the "Qty Available" in the SO Task Pane is being calculated using data from the WM Item Quantity View, specifically by subtracting the committed quantity from the on-hand quantity displayed there. The issue seems to stem from a mismatch in the Qty On Hand values between the IN Item Availability View and the WM Item Quantity View, leading to the observed discrepancy.

This inconsistency is causing confusion for the client when reviewing inventory availability during sales order processing.



Example to Illustrate the Issue:

-
Sales Order: S1

-
Item ID: A

On the Task Pane of the Sales Order screen, the following values are displayed:

-
Qty On Hand: 100

-
Qty Committed: 20

-
Qty Available: 65

Expected Calculation:

Based on the standard formula:

Qty Available = Qty On Hand - Qty Committed - Qty On Hold

Assuming Qty On Hold = 0, the expected available quantity should be:

100 - 20 - 0 = 80

But the system is showing 65, which is 15 units less than expected.

Further Analysis:

When reviewing the WM Item Quantity View for Item A, the Qty On Hand appears as 85 instead of 100.

If we calculate using this value:

85 (On Hand from WM) - 20 (Committed) = 65

This matches what is shown in the Task Pane, indicating that the Sales Order Task Pane is likely using the WM Item Quantity View’s On Hand quantity, not the one from the standard Inventory Item Availability screen.

Cause
Traverse v11.2

Resolution
The root cause of the issue was a mismatch between the Warehouse Management (WM) module and the Inventory module, specifically related to unsynchronized Qty On Hand values.

This has been identified as a known bug, which has been resolved in system builds 23349 and later. Therefore, any customer experiencing this issue should ensure they are operating on build 23349 or newer. Upgrading to a supported build provides a permanent fix for the problem.

While the WmSynchQtyToInventory TSMX utility can be run as a temporary workaround to resynchronize the quantities, it is not considered a long-term solution. For permanent resolution, it is strongly recommended to upgrade to the corrected build after consulting with the development team.

For reference, the associated development request is attached, and it includes the TSMX file used in the interim solution.

Incident 97840 REA - Inventory discrepancy - 04310719 - DEV-278709

Incident 94947 REA - Discrepancy in "Qty Available" Calculation on SO Screen - 04144422 - DEV-263705

Below is the CR request.

CR - On Hand Base issue - 02732757 - DEV-172177

Incident 97840 REA - Inventory discrepancy - 04310719 - DEV-278709

0e1ddc76-226b-4a36-af86-caa91fc2575f.title: OSAS_ODBC
0e1ddc76-226b-4a36-af86-caa91fc2575f.content:
Problem
Client needs assistance in setting up ODBC driver

Resolution
ODBC and Productivity Reports
Setting up a DSN.
There are two things you will need to know.
The name of the server
The name of the Data Base. The database will have been created during the installation of OSAS8 the default name is OSAS Data.
Go to Control Panel > Administrative Tools > ODBC Data Source Administrator (32-bit)
Select File DSN then Add

A file DSN is necessary to get the Productivity reports to function properly
Select the ODBC Driver.  This will have to be the BBj ODBC Driver.  If you are on a client and it is already installed scroll to the right and check the version.  It needs match the interpreter version.

If the Driver isn’t there or it is an older version then a driver needs to be installed.  If the interpreter is 19.23 or less use the remote installer available in the EM.  If it is 20.3 or greater you’ll need the installation media local on the workstation.  For the 20.3 make sure java is installed.
Name the DSN.  What you name it isn’t critical.  Just pick a name like osas8
Configuration

Provide a Description - use the same as the name of the DSN, osas8
Enter the Server name and the Database name
The User Config: Field can be left blank.  This field is useful for pulling data from other companies and prior year in GL and PA.
Choose OK.
Log in using the EM admin user and Password.
If everything is correct the .dsn will be saved to the Documents directory of the user.
If not you will get this message.  So either the server name or the data base name is incorrect or both

Once the DSN is saved choose OK to exit the ODBC Administrator.
Next test the DSN by pulling data into an Excel spread sheet.
This will vary based on the version of Excel
So Find and Choose - Data > From Other Sources > From Microsoft Query.

This will take you to Choose Data Source

Choose Browse.  The File data source will be in the Documents directory

Choose Open.  The data source will be added to the Data Source screen, select it and choose OK.
The ODBC Driver Configuration Window will open Choose OK.
Log in using the EM user and password.
When the Query Wizard opens Find the APVE table and select it and choose Next.

Choose Next in the Filter Data and Sort Order Screens then Finish.  Accept the defaults
Accept the Defaults in the Import Data screen and choose OK.  You should be in Column A row 1
This is the Vendor File so you would see Vendor ID, names and addresses.
Now you know it works.
Finding the Sever and Database Names
Both can be found by logging into the EM
You can find the database name in RM > installation and Configuration > Directories
Possibly the server name
Productivity Reports – Excel spreadsheets
The Productivity Reports are found in the Document directory \OSAS80\Document
To access these from a client the directory needs to be shared (share with everyone to start) and in RM > Installation and Configuration > Directories the Document share path needs to be set.

You should now be able to launch a productivity report from the menu.
The productivity reports shipped with the software are by default set up with sample data. To get your current company information into the report you must refresh the report and tie it to a DSN looking at your company data.
Refresh the report

Click on the Refresh All Button off the Data Menu or Right click on an active field and select Refresh to bring in the current information.

Since the DSN this report was originally created with is not set up on this machine, this message is displayed.
Choose OK and in the screen select your data source

Choose OK and choose OK again at the ODBC configuration screen.
Now log in using the EM user and password.
The data will refresh.
Do not save the report or it will become specific to that company.
User Config: field in the ODBC Configuration screen.
You can use this to pull in data for companies other than the one set up in the OSAS Data database it can also be used to pull in prior year data for General Ledger and Payroll.
For pulling data for another company in the User Config field enter CID=2 where the company is company 2.  For General ledger prior years Example would be for GL year 2020 enter GLY=.Y20. Payroll PLY=.Y20.
This is useful when the database is set up for current year and Company H.
F1 help and Shift+F1 to reach the user guides RM user preferences path to the pdf reader Adobe permission issues.

ec776e41-1aa3-489f-a606-b39f9893da91.title: OSAS_Setting up Direct Printer
ec776e41-1aa3-489f-a606-b39f9893da91.content:
Problem
The alignment on the A/P checks needs to be adjusted. The upper portion of the check needs to be moved up one line. The stub is printing correctly.

Resolution
Direct Printing

To set up a direct printer in OSAS the first step is to share the printer.  This can be done on any workstation where the printer is found in Control Panel > Devices and Printers

Right Click on the printer and go to Printer Properties.  Next go to the sharing Tab.
Check the share this printer box
You can change the share name.  Remove any spaces from the name and shorten the name so it is simple to remember and type.
Also check the boxes Render print jobs on client computers and list in the directory.
Choose Apply then OK


Now we need to know the name of the computer use a cmd prompt to do this.
At the prompt type in ipconfig /all

Hit enter then scroll up to find the Host Name


Scroll back down to the prompt and type in:
DIR>\\<HOST NAME> \<PRINTER SHARE NAME>
If you do this from the Users directory you will get a single page.  If you do this as admin and are in the system32 directory you will get dozens of pages.

This should print out the users directory on the printer.  If we cannot print from a command prompt we will not be able to print from OSAS.  This should be tested on the workstation you intend to print from.
The printer must be able to render the print job it cannot be a host based or GDI printer.  This link can be helpful.  https://www.ibm.com/support/pages/information-printers-various-manufacturers

Once this is successful In OSAS go to Resource Manager > Installation and Configuration > Devices
Choose Append then Choose Printer
Give it Device Name P1 is commonly used. (only P or L are allowed)
In the System Device Name use this format for OSAS version 8 BBj and 7.61 BBj
\\\\<host name>\\<printer share name>
(For 7.61 vpro 5 see below)
Use the F2 look up for a device type for any laser printer “HP Laser Jet” is commonly used.  Make a choice that is appropriate for you printer type.
Page Down into the body of the screen and choose done.  Next Write the changes and restart OSAS so the changes take effect.

Now test by printing from OSAS.  If you get a message Cannot open print device try adding the mode CLIENT to the alias line options.
alias P1 \\\\Brian-Savage\\Dell5350 "HP Laser Jet" CR,CLIENT,SP=1B451B266C3632461B266C304F1B2873313048,SPCOLS=80,CP=1B451B266C3632461B266C304F1B287331362E3648,CPCOLS=177

For vpro5 use the following //<host name>/<share name>
When you have finished before you can print in OSAS you will need to make an edit to the config.bbx
Browse to the config.bbx \osas\progRM and open with a text editor find the printer and add the mode O_CREATE
alias P1 //Brian-Savage/Dell5350dn "HP Laser Jet" CR,O_CREATE,SP=1B451B266C3632461B266C304F1B2873313048,SPCOLS=80,CP=1B451B266C3632461B266C304F1B287331362E3648,CPCOLS=132

a0a1e4f1-3fd7-4d9e-92f3-1b4998c62a18.title: OSAS_Customer receiving error while printing reports

aacd23fa-8ec8-4338-97c4-57c751875684.title: OSAS_Payroll Withholdings
aacd23fa-8ec8-4338-97c4-57c751875684.content:
Problem
Customers needs assistance in setting up State withholding Tax

Resolution
When you set up a State for the first time first go to File Maintenance > Payroll Information > Set up State unemployment reports.  This determines the Order the information is printed on the Unemployment reports.

If this set up is not done you will get this message when you enter the SUI state in the employee tax information record.

Codes maintenance > Tax Authority Setup
Choose the Tax Authority, Federal, State or local.  Chose the Code and Page Down.
State and Federal Records should be setup.  Any Local Taxes will need to be created.  Check the SUI Table ID to make sure the x is included.  This will allow the formula to read a company specific table.

Codes Maintenance > Withholdings
This is where exclusions are setup for Deductions and Earning Codes.  When setting or checking exclusions for the Tax Authority > Federal, make sure exceptions for the OAS and EOA match, the MED and EME also need to match each other.  These are the Employer and Employee portions of the FICA taxes.  If they do not this can cause discrepancies on the 941 Worksheet.

You will need a GL account for the Liability Account.  For some codes, employer paid taxes, you will also need an Accrued Taxes Account.  The tax ID that is entered here will be used on reports and forms like the W-2.  If you have an Earning Code that uses a fixed withholding it will read the fixed percent entered here.
Exclusions from withholding can also be set at the employee level.  In File maintenance > Employee > Tax Information > Withholding Setup.

Check here when only one employee is having an issue where they do not have any withholding as compared to all others.

Codes maintenance >Tax Groups
A tax group will be assigned to an employee in File Maintenance > Employee > Tax Information.  This will group employees by the State and Local taxes that are to be withheld.  Enter the Appropriate State and local taxes to be withheld.

If transactions were entered for an employee the tax group used in calculate checks will be the one entered during transaction entry.
File Maintenance > Tax Tables
These Tables hold the information for calculating withholding.  You’ll find the State Withholding tables here, STX. State unemployment, SUT tables.  State other taxes, SOT.  The Federal withholding tables, FED. The FICA and MEDEM tables for calculating OAS, EOA, MED and EME withholdings.
Note:  EOA is the employer portion of the OASDI, OAS is the employees’ portion.  These withholding amounts should match.  EME is the employer portion of Medicare.  MED is the employee portion of the tax, these should also match.  There is an exception here and that is for employees making over $200,000.00 there is an additional 0.9% in MED withholding, so in these instances the MED withholding will exceed the EME.

File Maintenance > Formula Maintenance
The Formulas for calculating Withholdings can be setup or maintained here.  If you wish to review a formula it may be best to go to Master File Lists > Formula Lists and print the formula out.  The formulas use the amounts from the tax table to calculate withholding.
Self-adjusting formulas:  A self-adjusting formula checks the YTD tax amount and the YTD earnings if the tax amount is understated then on a single paycheck it will increase the withholding so the YTD tax amount is the correct percent of the YTD earnings amount.   If it is overstated then there will be no withholding.  The formulas that are self-adjusting are State SUI, FUTA, EOA, OAS, EME and MED.  The amounts are found in Employee History.
File Maintenance > Employee > Tax Information
Once the above setup is completed you can fill out the Tax Information Screen of the Employees’.  Here you set the employees Tax Group, withholding status, Exemptions (99 exemptions can be entered and there will be no withholding.) Extra withholding, a fixed withholding amount can be set, Tax Table ID, and SUI State.  Some states may have prompts these come from a table in File Maintenance Tax Tables.

This is the information that will be used in Calculating this employees withholding.  State and Local Tax Information must be in both the Tax Group and here.  This is of Importance for employees that live in one state and work in another or may work in multiple states.  The tax group entered during transaction entry is the one used for calculating checks.

a1503fea-e6b1-4bd7-b3f9-a856bdf0f05c.title: Tax Service Integration Validate address error "The Country Code PRI is not a supported country. Address validation was cancelled".
a1503fea-e6b1-4bd7-b3f9-a856bdf0f05c.content:
Problem
User is receiving a "The country code PRI is not a support country. Address validation was canceled." return message when trying to calculate tax and validate an address located in Puerto Rico using the Avalara Tax Service Integration.

Puerto Rico is a US Territory and not considered its own country. This is an expected error when "PRI" is used as a country.

- Go to Sales Order> Transactions> Orders> Click Update
-
Recommended using the following format for the Ship To address:

Line 1: 364 Calle Caoba

Line 2: optional

City: Humacao

State: Puerto Rico or PR

Zip: 00791

- Click on Tax Integration> Validate Address, This should allow the Address to validate properly.

a1444b21-04aa-4833-becd-113f9d4a75d4.title: How to find a missing Transaction (Disbursement, Deposit, Adjustment) in Bank Rec
a1444b21-04aa-4833-becd-113f9d4a75d4.content:
Problem
The issue with checks being processed but not showing up properly in Traverse. We have several checks that we believe have been processed and posted correctly but when we go to do a bank reconciliation, they do not appear in Traverse. How to find a missing Transaction (Disbursement, Deposit, or Adjustment) in Bank Rec?

Resolution
Procedure for Finding a Missing Transaction (Disbursement, Deposit, Adjustment) in Bank Rec,
- Use the Bank Account Register or Register view to find the transactions. If you are using the View, make sure to add the column for "Cleared". If using the Register, check the box to include Cleared Transactions.
- Confirm that the transactions exist. If they have a Status of "Cleared", then continue with these instructions.
- Go to the Clear Transaction screen.
- Call up the Bank Account
- Click the Load Button ([...] and load the most recent statement.

- Look on that statement to see if the transaction appears there and is cleared.
- If it isn't there, keep loading the next most recent statement and looking until you find it.
- If the transaction should not have been cleared, uncheck the box to unclear the transaction if possible. (If the statement has been reconciled, you would need to click the "Change Status" button to open the statement again to be able to do this.)
- Once you unclear the transaction, then you can load the statement you want to see it on and it should be there now so you can clear it or not as needed.

* If the previous statements were reconciled and then purged, then the cleared transactions on it would have been purged and would no longer be viewable. You can check to see what statements were purged by going to the "Purge Cleared Transactions" screen and clicking on the Activity button. In this instance, you can look through your saved Reconciliation Reports for your previous statements that were purged to see if the transaction was listed there.

1e97c005-aa9c-4fef-89e5-175129b4ac60.title: Behavior of the Delete Function on Customer Payment Screen
1e97c005-aa9c-4fef-89e5-175129b4ac60.content:
Problem
Can you confirm what happens when using the Delete function on the payment screen within the customer record?



-
Does it delete the record in the tblArCustPmtMethod table?

-
Does it update the Status field to 2 in the tblSmExternalPaymentMethod table?

Resolution
The outcome depends on the Payment Service Integration configured in your system. You can verify this under:
System Manager > Setup and Maintenance > Payment Service Integration.

Example – OEHostPay Integration:

If the payment integration is set to OEHostPay, then:

-
When the Delete function is used:

-
The system attempts to connect to the OEHostPay portal and request deletion of the stored payment method (e.g., credit card).

-
If the request is successful:

-
The system removes the corresponding record from tblArCustPmtMethod.

-
The Status field in tblSmExternalPaymentMethod is updated to 2 (indicating deletion/inactive).

-
If the request fails:

-
No changes are made to the local records to maintain consistency between systems.

Additional Notes

-
This process ensures data integrity between your ERP and the external payment processor.

-
Status values may vary by implementation, but Status = 2 typically represents a deleted or inactive state.

-
If no payment integration is in use, the system performs only local deletions.

9c8df3df-301b-42bb-828e-2ae023b287ea.title: Local WH not showing up on W2 when state WH and local WH are different.
9c8df3df-301b-42bb-828e-2ae023b287ea.content:
Problem
A customer has an employee who works and goes to college in Richmond, KY but her home address is in Ohio . Per their phone calls with all applicable tax agencies, they were told to withhold Ohio State Tax and not Kentucky State Tax.

The problem is, her W-2 shows her Ohio wages and withholdings, but it does not show local KY04-LWH which is Richmond local tax. they tried adding Kentucky as a withholding state (keeping Ohio the default) under State Taxes in Employee Information and re-generating the W-2's but Richmond still does not show up for her.

Resolution
W2's are actually printed by State.  In most normal circumstances an employee will have state taxes and local taxes both paid to the same state.  But local taxes will only print on a W2 for the state in which the local taxes are set up in.  So, it will not show KY local taxes on an OH W2, and vice versa.

Further, a W2 will not print for a state unless there is some earnings coded to that state.  So the problem with this setup is that they have all the state taxes being recorded in OH, which means they will get only an OH W2, which will not show any KY local taxes.
If they want a second W2 to print for KY which will show only the KY local tax, you need to trick the system into doing that, but you have to do some funny stuff in the History Adjustment screen.

Applications > Payroll > Periodic processing > History Adjustments.

Edit in some State taxable earnings and tax amount, save and close. In the below screenshot we have changed the value from 0 to 10 for the November month.

Go right back in and reverse those entries with negative entries, save and close.

After doing so they should be able to get two W2’s out of the system, one for each state.  First W2 will show all the state wages, but no local taxes.  Second one will be for the other state showing no state wages or taxes, and all the local taxes.

d8dc9e6d-f1f5-4c81-8e8d-3c6ec147bf35.title: Setting Up and Using Divisions in On-Time Web.
d8dc9e6d-f1f5-4c81-8e8d-3c6ec147bf35.content:
Problem
We have different locations across the country, and they do their hiring and payroll independently.  Can we use a single On-Time Web subscription for all our locations?

Resolution
Setting Up and Using Divisions in On-Time Web.



Question: We have different locations across the country, and they do their hiring and payroll independently.  Can we use a single On-Time Web subscription for all our locations?



Various locations can be set up as Divisions in On-Time Web. Follow the instructions below to create a Division in On-Time Web.



- Navigate to Company Settings>Divisions and click NEW button.
- Enter the following information…
- Division ID – Unique identification of each division.  May be alpha, numeric, or a combination of both.
- Description – The title and/or description that helps identify the division.
- Street Address – The physical address of the division location.
- Street Address 2 – Additional line for the address if needed.
- City – The city location of the division.
- State/Province/Territory – The state/province/territory in which the division is located.
- Postal Code – The postal code for the division location.
- Country – Select the country in which the division is located.
- Time zone – Select the time zone for the division.

- Save the New Division Information

- Select Division Admin(s) for the new Division – These Division Administrators will be the person(s) who will be able to set up new employees for the Division. If they have not been set up as an Employee, enter them in the Employee section. If they are already in the system, then do the following
- Navigate to Company Settings>Employees>Settings Tab
- Select the Access Level drop-down and choose Division Supervisor for the employee(s) that have been selected to be Division Supervisor(s)
- Save

- Validate the Division Supervisor(s)
- Navigate to Company Settings>Divisions>Validation Tab
- Select the Employee that will be the Division Administrator and Save.

- Update Employees who belong to the New Division
- Navigate to Company Settings>Employees and search for the employees that are assigned to the new Division.
- Find the Employee(s) who belongs to the New Division
- Select the Default tab
- Click the Division drop-down and select the Division that you want the employee to be assigned to the new Division
- Save

(Repeat this for everyone who belongs to the new Division)

Summary

You have created the new Division

You have assigned Division Administrator(s)

You have assigned employees who belong to the new Division

da31c384-237c-42f2-afc7-fbdbd5edd57d.title: How to add/edit/delete users for a customer under Customer Portal
da31c384-237c-42f2-afc7-fbdbd5edd57d.content:
Problem
How to add users for a customer under Customer Portal. Also how to edit and delete?

Resolution
To work with the Users function, follow these steps:

Select Users from the Customer Portal Manager menu.



Select the company you wish to work with in the Company ID field.

A list of all customer portal users from all customers associated with that company displays. To filter the list, use the filter fields in the Name, Customer ID, Email, Login ID, Status, or Admin columns. Enter your criteria, then use the Filter icon to set how to filter the list. The list will automatically filter.

By default each customer will have an admin user added. The default administrator's login ID will be: “[CompanyID][CustomerID]Admin”. For example, if your company ID is “CPU” and your customer's ID is “Alt008”, the default administrator login ID for that customer would be: CPUAlt008Admin

To add users for a customer:

1. Use the New icon to open the Users screen.

2. Select a customer from the Customer ID drop-down list.
3. Enter a login ID for the user you are creating in the Login ID field.
4. Enter a name for your user in the Name field.
5. Enter an email address for the user in the Email field.
6. The Active check box is only available for users who are not new. If you are adding a new
user, the Active check box is unavailable to mark.
7. Mark the Admin check box if the user will have administrator permissions on the portal for
that customer.
8. Mark the Groups in which the user should be a member.
Select All to mark the user in all groups for which the customer is a member. Select
None to unmark all the groups for which the customer is a member.
Groups will be available when the customer has been added to a group.
9. Select the Default location for the User.

Click the Save Changes icon to save the new user.

To edit a user:
1. Use the Action icon  and select Edit from the menu  for the user you
want to edit.

2. Make any changes to the user information. The LoginID cannot be edited.
3. Mark the Active check box if the user is an active user. Clear the check box if the user is not an active user.
The user will receive an activation email when the Admin for the customer’s account, selects the user and saves changes from the Customer Portal.
4. Mark the Admin check box if the user is an administrative user. Otherwise, clear the check box.
5. Mark the groups in which the user should be a member.
Select All to mark the user in all groups for which the customer is a member. Select None to unmark all the groups for which the customer is a member.



To delete a user:

I. Use the Action icon  and select Delete from the menu for the user you want to delete.
A user may be deleted from the Edit User screen by selecting the Delete icon .
2. When the confirmation dialog "Are you sure you want to delete this record?" appears, press the 0K button. Press the Cancel button to close the dialog box without deleting the record.
3. Users that have been deleted are indicated with an Edit icon in place of the Action icon  and have a Status of "Deleted" (see User List screenshot)
• To restore the user, click on the Edit icon
• A message will appear asking "Do you really want to restore this record?". Click 0K
to restore.

27f4df33-6ab9-4509-828c-83f355f5573d.title: How to Create an Import Map in On-Time Web

This article explains how to set up import mappings in On-Time Web, allowing administrators to define custom layouts for importing Employees, Departments, and Divisions.
