5190cbb8-d8f5-4ac6-8107-fd1d2a8580d7.title: How to setup Vantiv Payment Method
5190cbb8-d8f5-4ac6-8107-fd1d2a8580d7.content:
Problem
Need to setup Vantiv payment method so that we can process credit card payments

Resolution
Go to System Manager > Setup and Maintenance > Payment Service Integration

1) Click on the drop-down menu and select Vantiv

2) Fill in all the details.

- In the Name field, select/enter 'Vantiv' for the Vantiv/Worldpay setup.
- Enter your company's account ID as provided by the payment processor into the Account ID field.
- Enter your company's account token in the Account Token field. Click the square button on the right side of the field to show the account token value.
- Enter 5328 in the Application ID field.
- Enter the acceptor ID in the Acceptor ID field.
- If applicable, enter the terminal ID for the current terminal into the Terminal ID field.
- If applicable, enter the lane ID for the current terminal into the Lane ID field. Lanes are used to link EMV devices to the port or computer the EMV is connected to. Use the Lane function, via the "Lane Manager" button on the toolbar, to add lanes (EMV devices) to the system.
- Enter the transaction URL for your settlement provider into the Transaction URL field.
- Enter the report URL for your settlement provider into the Report URL field.
- Enter the services URL for the payment processing service in the Services URL field.
- The Hosted URL should be set as needed for your gateway. Edit these values only if necessary.
- Select a Market Code from the drop-down list that most accurately describes the service.
- Select the check box to Allow Partial Approvals to approve a portion of the payment prior to processing the Traverse transaction.
- Select the check box to Check for Duplicate Transactions when entering payments into transactions. The process will check for duplicate Customer ID, Amount, and Credit Card Number.
- Enter the TriPOS server URL for the payment processing service in the TriPOS Server URL field.
- Enter the TriPOS cloud URL for the payment processing service in the TriPOS Cloud URL field.
- Enter the developer key your payment processor supplied into the Developer Key field.
- Enter the developer secret into the Developer Secret field.
- If using an EMV or pin pad device (card reader) connected directly to the network, which is the normal configuration when Traverse runs in the cloud or users access Traverse via Remote Desktop, mark the Use Cloud check box; otherwise, if the EMV/pin pad is connected directly to client computers, leave the check box blank.
- The Test Mode field setting allows for testing the configuration. Mark the Test Mode check box to test payment processing. Clear the check box to enable payment processing for customers.
- Select the check box to Allow Debit cards to be used along with credit cards. Otherwise, clear the check box to allow credit cards only.
- Select the check box to Allow Manual Entry of the credit card number on the EMV/pin pad if a card can’t be swiped. Otherwise, clear the check box to use the EMV/pin pad device exclusively to capture the credit card information.
- To disallow pre-authorizations, select the Disallow Pre-Authorizations check box. For more information, click here.
- Select how you want to use signature capture functionality for your payment services from the Prompt for Signature drop-down list.
- If you choose to require a signature above a dollar amount, enter that dollar amount into the Threshold Amount field. If you are not using the threshold, or do not have a threshold amount, enter 0 into the field.



3) Go to Accounts Recievable > Setup and Maintenance > Payment Method to set up the Vantiv/World Pay payment method:

Enter the:

Payment Method ID (ex. CCVantiv) and its Description (ex. Vantiv/World Pay Credit Card).  Status - Keep as Active

Payment Type - select from the drop down:  'External' (You must use this type)

Bank Account ID, CC Company ID, & GL Acct Debit  - see below

Distribution Code (Dist Code) - Select a Distribution Code you would like to link to this Payment Method.

Payment Service - Vantiv

If you use multicurrency, it's important to remember that the currency associated with the GL account (or bank account) you specify in the payment method determines the payment method's currency. In other words, the currency of the GL or bank account in the payment method you assign to a payment determines how the payment is credited. Traverse calculates any conversion needed using the appropriate exchange rate automatically.

-
There are two methods to setting up payment methods for credit cards. You can either select a Bank Account ID to have payments applied as Bank Reconciliation Deposit entries using your Bank's GL account, or you can set up a customer in AR Customers to act as a credit card company ID and select this in the CC Company ID field. This customer will be set up with the "CC Company" box checked on the Defaults tab in AR Customers, and must have a payment method with the type of 'Cash' or 'Check' for the customer setup. See below for more information regarding these two options:

Credit Card Payment Method with CC Company selected

- The GL Account to Debit should be an AR Holding account, NOT a Cash Account.
- Create an AR holding account, and set up a distribution code with the new AR holding account as the AR account.
- Then, when you have a Credit Card Customer (ex. VISA), pick the distribution code you set up with the AR holding account. You must have a payment method for this customer as either Cash or Check.
- When you enter a cash receipt with the credit card payment method and post it, it will make an open invoice to the Credit Card Customer (VISA) for the amount of the cash receipt. The GL accounts posted to will be a debit to the AR holding account from the payment method for the credit card and the credit will be to the AR account set up in the distribution code for the customer for which the cash receipt was entered.
- You will need to make another cash receipt to the Credit Card Customer (VISA) for the amount of the invoice you applied the cash receipt to for your regular customer.
- When you post these cash receipts, the entries to GL will be a debit to the cash account you set up in the bank account associated with your cash or check payment method, and the credit will be to your AR holding account from the distribution code in your Credit Card Customer (VISA). This is where you will see it hit your cash account in GL.



Credit Card and External Payment Method with Payment Type of 'External' with Bank Account ID selected

When you select a bank account ID with an external payment type, you link the payment method to a bank account to utilize the bank account's GL cash account to do the posting. This also applies the payment receipts as BR deposit entries when interfaced with Bank Reconciliation.

-
In General Ledger > Setup and Maintenance > Chart of Accounts set up an account to debit when applying payments to invoices using the credit card payment methods being set up with the type of 'external'. This account should be a cash holding account.

-
In System Manager > Company Setup > Bank Accounts set up a bank account for each credit card payment method to which you want to apply your credit card cash receipts. The GL account selected for the bank accounts needs to be the account you set up in step 1 above.

-
In Accounts Receivable > Setup and Maintenance > Payment Methods set up payment methods for each credit card accepted for payment, selecting 'credit card' or 'external' as the payment type. Select a Bank Account ID of a bank you set up in step 2.

-
When applying cash receipts, using the AR Transactions > Cash Receipts function, enter the credit card information supplied by the customer. For external (TPS) receipts, use the External Payments function for posted invoices, or the Payments button in the Transactions screen to process the cash receipts.

-
When the cash receipts are posted, the GL accounts in the bank accounts set up in step 2 will be debited for the payment amounts. If you have Bank Reconciliation, the deposits will be added to the bank balance and to the reconciliation reports.

-
If you do not use Bank Reconciliation, enter GL journal transactions to transfer the cash balance paid to you by the credit card company from the holding account to your cash account. The credit card fee amount will remain in this account and must be reconciled by your accountant.

-
If you use Bank Reconciliation, enter an account transfer to transfer the amount paid to you by the credit card company from the credit card bank account to your cash bank account. The credit card fee amount will remain in this account and must be reconciled by your accountant.

*If you would like help with this setup, please contact the Aptean team for further assistance.

4) Then to System manager > Company Setup > Business rules.
Select System manager, under TPS settings, choose the Vantiv payment method name you just set up in AR Payment Method (Vantiv) field.

c4153196-2176-4f55-9381-7587f0d73895.title: Preview Alerts in InfoAlert setup
c4153196-2176-4f55-9381-7587f0d73895.content:
Problem
What is the purpose of the "Preview Alerts" button on the Alerts screen for Info Alert?

Resolution
The “Preview Alert” button allows users to manually test alerts without affecting history, outputs, or notifications. It's a safe way to validate logic, filters, and data access before scheduling the alert to run automatically.

Steps to Access and Use Preview Alerts

-
Log in to the environment.

-
Navigate to:
Alerts > Alerts > Select Alerts

-
In the Select Alerts screen:

-
Choose the appropriate Map ID from the drop-down.

-
Check the "Active Only" box to view only alerts marked to run.

-
Select an alert by clicking the far-left column (a black arrow will appear on the selected row ------ )

-
Click the “Preview Alert” button at the bottom of the screen to launch the wizard.

Using the Alert Preview Wizard

- Enter required filters and parameters (From/Thru dates, logic prompt, etc.)

-
These vary by alert and were defined by the alert developer.

-
Check the “Display SQL Command” box to view the SQL logic behind the alert (optional).

-
Choose an Action ID if actions are set up for this alert (optional).

-
Click “Run Alert” to generate test data and wait for the 'Data Generated' message.

-
Click “Show Records” to review the results.

-
Use the “Reset” button to clear inputs and test again with different criteria.

-
Use “Queue” to view any outputs if an Action ID was selected.

Important Notes

-
Previewing an alert does not impact live history or trigger notifications—it's purely for testing.

-
If errors occur, they may be due to alert logic, action setup, or data source issues.

-
This tool is especially useful for confirming filter results and fine-tuning alerts before live execution.

16821e56-7e48-48eb-9ea6-934acd797d5b.title: InfoAlert - Usage of several tabs and how it is configured.
16821e56-7e48-48eb-9ea6-934acd797d5b.content:
Problem
There is a need to understand the purpose and functionality of the Alert, Description, Schedule, Criteria/Notify, Actions, and Snapshot tabs. A detailed explanation is required to clarify how each of these tabs is used and what role they play within the system or process.

Resolution
To access and manage alerts in IA Manager, here’s the step-by-step process along with explanations for each part of the screen:

1. Accessing the Alerts Screen:

- First, log in to the IA Manager application.
- Navigate to Alerts > Alerts > Select Alerts.
- From here, select the appropriate Map ID from the drop-down list.
- You can also check the “Active Only” box if you want to filter and view only active alerts.

2. Using the Alerts Tab:

- This is where all the alerts are listed.
- Use the “Sel” (Select) checkbox to tell the IA server which alert to process during its next scheduled run.
- If this checkbox is left unchecked, the alert is saved in the system with your configurations but won’t be processed — it’s in a preview state.

- You can click the Sel column header to sort by selected alerts.
- One alert can be set up with multiple sequences, meaning you can define different rules, outputs, or notifications within the same alert.

To view these multiple sequences, go to Manage Notifications under the Alerts menu.

3. Description Tab:

- This tab provides the full description of what each alert does.
- You can also see the last run time and date here.
- There’s a Reset button on this screen, which is useful for debugging.
- You can reset the alert’s schedule, history, or snapshot values — especially helpful if the alert isn’t triggering as expected.
- Check Reset All to clear all alert schedule, history and snapshot values for this alert.
Check Reset Alert Schedule and enter a target date and time to reset the alert's last run time to
the indicated date.
Check Reset Alert History and enter a target date and time to clear the alert history records for
this alert to the indicated date. This setting can be used in conjunction with the Reset Alert
Schedule to allow an alert to notify on records that it has already processed.
Check Reset Snapshot Values to reset any snapshot values that may be stored for a specific snapshot alert.

4. Criteria/Notify Tab:

- This is the core setup for how the alert filters data and who it notifies.
- You can define specific parameters like date ranges or field values the alert should monitor.
- If you want to add more conditions, use the New Record button to add multiple sets of criteria.
- There's a Select All option to include everything in your filter (no From/Thru filtering), or you can manually define a range by entering in values into the From/Thru or Individual ID's section to filter accordingly.
- You can also change the criteria fields by using the Alert Field Selections under the Configure Options in the Main menu.

Key fields to fill:

- Number of Days Past Invoice Date – filters records by aging. - Note: This is part of the alert setup criteria shown in the sample configuration. While it is required in this particular example, it may not be applicable or mandatory for all alerts. In this case, it’s just a required field for the sample setup.
- Group Heading – optional, helps organize alerts if you're grouping them.
- Data Source – pick the tested source of data for this alert.
- Action ID – if Actions have been previously created for this alert, to
provide additional result output to files or external email and fax output.
- Note: Both the Number of Days Past Invoice Date and Data Source are required to complete the alert setup in this example.

5. Notification Setup:

- From the Criteria/Notify tab, click the Notification button to configure who receives the alert and how.
- Add one or more email addresses for notifications.
- If you want a printed report, enter an Output ID from the drop down list that was previously setup in the Configuration Options - Define Reports to point to a particular printer for a printed output of the alert.
- You can also define:
- Max Records – to limit the number of records per alert (prevents large or endless emails).
- Alert check box – sends the basic alert text.
- Attach check box – allows a file (from an associated action) to be sent along with the alert.
- Action check box – executes a configured action (e.g., email or fax) when the alert is triggered.
- Output IDs – if printing is involved, choose from the list of printers set up in IA.
- Event ID – for advanced configurations, links the alert to specific notification events.

6. Actions Tab:

- This tab shows what actions are tied to the alert (like sending an email, printing a report, etc.).
- You can see the Action ID and checkboxes showing email/fax settings.
- Use the Interactive checkbox if needed to toggle between manual or automatic behavior.
- The Submit Actions screen works in conjunction with this Interactive check box and provides for the „queuing‟ of email and/or fax output prior to sending. This allows you to view the list of outgoing actions and control which ones will be set for output, adjusted, or deleted and not sent. Checking the Submit column will flag those action outputs to be processed at the next Info-Alert Server run.

- For changes, refer to the Configure Actions section.

7. Alert Sequences:

- You can set up multiple criteria groups for the same alert (called sequences).
- This allows different triggers or recipients under one alert.
- Use the record selector (arrows that toggle between Record 1 of 2, 2 of 2, etc.) at the bottom of the Criteria/Notify tab to switch between sequences.

8. Schedule Tab:

- This controls when and how often the alert runs.
- Options include Daily, Weekly, or Monthly scheduling:
- Daily: Choose every day or just weekdays.
- this setting dictates how often you need to schedule the IA
Server run using the "Windows Task Scheduler‟.

- Weekly: Select specific days.
- Monthly: Run alerts on a specific date, first or last day of the month.

Then define the Daily Frequency:

- Occurs once after – runs alert at a set time once per day.
- Occurs every – runs the alert multiple times per day within a set window.

You can also set up Re-notify Rules:

- This prevents the alert from re-notifying on the same data repeatedly.
- For example, if the rule is “do not re-notify in less than 1 week,” even if the same data triggers the alert daily, the user won’t be alerted again until 7 days have passed.
- Note: The Do Not Re-notify (DNR) rule relies on IA’s saved alert history (default is 90 days). If you need longer DNR periods, either change the alert logic or increase the alert history retention setting.

Tip for Testing:

If you are testing, you can:

- Set Schedule Frequency to Always.
- Set Do Not Re-notify to 0 days.
This will let the alert run and notify every time the server processes — ideal for testing but not recommended in production.

fac26e96-13ed-4e38-9e6a-c37e8a0dd516.title: Re-naming Select Fields
fac26e96-13ed-4e38-9e6a-c37e8a0dd516.content:
Problem
Is there a way to change the system to track time on things other than Jobs/Phases/Tasks?

Resolution
Changing the Labels of Select Fields in On-Time Web



Question:  We don’t have Jobs/Phases/Tasks in our company. Can we use that section to track the time our employees work at our clients' locations and specific things they do at the locations?



There is a lot of flexibility with the Job/Phase/Task section of On-Time Web. We use a 3-tier system that will allow you to track unlimited Jobs with unlimited Phases of the Job and unlimited tasks on Phases. For example, if I have five Jobs that each Job has four phases, and each phase has three tasks.  I can track time on every section of all the jobs.

But if you have Jobs with just tasks or just want to track Jobs, you can do that as well. The system is based on a Parent-Child relationship.

You can also change the naming of the Job/Phase/Task. The example of Clients with different locations and services at those locations.  You can rename the Jobs/Phases/Tasks to Client/Location/Service.

Renaming Select Fields

- Navigate to Company Settings>Settings & Defaults>Custom Labels tab
- Change the label names for the Job/Phase/Task
- Save and Refresh your screen (F5). This allows the system to change the Label Names in the system to the new names.

Now you will be able to see and use the correct labels that your employees recognize, that is related to what you do.

6cb04786-9ffb-442d-af79-82f69313dadd.title: Edit Groups and Permissions of Customer Portal
6cb04786-9ffb-442d-af79-82f69313dadd.content:
Problem
How to add, edit, or delete groups associated with customers in Customer Portals. How to manage permissions for the created groups.

Resolution
Use the Groups function to add, edit, or delete groups associated with all customers. Groups allow you to control the customer portal menu options available to the members of each group.

To work with the Groups function, follow these steps:
1. Select Groups from the Customer Portal Manager menu.

2. The Groups screen appears

3. Select the company you wish to work with in the Company ID field

4. A list of all user groups associated with that company appears. To filter the list, use the filter fields in the Group Name, Group Description, or Customer ID columns. Enter your criteria, then use the Filter icon to set how to filter the list. The list will automatically filter.

To add user groups for a customer:

1. Use the New icon  in the header to open the Groups screen.

2. Enter a group name for the group you are creating in the Group Name field.

3. Enter a description for the group in the Description field.

4. Select a customer from the Customer ID drop-down list. Once you select a customer, the customer's user(s) will appear in the Group Users section.

5. Mark the user check box in the Group Users section to add a user to the new group. Use the All or None button to mark or unmark all the users at once.

6.  Select the Save icon  to save the new group.

To add or remove users to the selected group:

1. In the Groups screen, Use the Action icon and select User from the menu to open the Group User Info screen.

2. Check or clear the Group Users check boxes as required. Use the All or None button to mark or unmark all the users at once.

3. Select the Save icon  to save any changes made to the group users.

To edit a group's menu permissions:

1. Use the Action icon  and select Menu from the menu  to open the Menu Security dialog box, which allows you to select the menu options that are visible to each group's members.



2. Mark the check box next to the Customer Portal menus for the items you want to give this group access to.

The menu permissions granted will cascade down from Home to menu group to menu. For example: if you mark the Home check box at the time, all the boxes will be checked, and access will be granted to all menus below Home. If you mark Order, with Home cleared, access will be granted to all menus in the Order group. You may also mark each menu individually

3. Use the Collapse icon  to collapse the menu groups.

4. Use the Expand icon to expand the collapsed menu groups.

5. Select the Save icon to save any changes made to the menu security.

6. Select the Reset icon  to set the menu permissions back to the original settings.

9ff98eba-af7c-41af-a8a6-3da18eb17278.title: Why does the Layout of reprinted Invoice differs from the originally printed Invoice?
9ff98eba-af7c-41af-a8a6-3da18eb17278.content:
Problem
Why dos the Layout of reprinted Invoice differs from the originally printed Invoice?

Resolution
In order to understand the steps for reprinting a document (such as an Invoice, Check, Order, Receipt, or Voucher) using the Document Archive feature in Traverse, please refer to the following knowledge base article: : https://connect.aptean.com/s/article/How-to-reprint-Invoice-Check-Order-Receipt-Voucher-using-Document-Archive



When Document Archiving is enabled for a customer, users may unintentionally skip selecting the archived document during the reprint process from Interactive Views. This can lead to confusion or result in printing a newer version of the document layout rather than the originally archived version.



During the reprint process:

-
If Document Archive is enabled, the system will display a pop-up window prompting the user to select from previously archived versions of the document.

-
It is important that the user selects the appropriate archived document from this pop-up to retrieve the version exactly as it was printed originally.

-
If the user clicks Continue without selecting a previously archived document, the system will default to printing the document using the current layout defined in Design Studio (current repx in Client Folder for 11.0 or the currently saved Form layout in Design Studio for 11.2. ), which may differ from the original version.



If the 'Design Studio' Layout or the REPX file in the Client Folder was changed in the meantime, after the original document was printed, the Users might find difference in the 'Output'.



In order to avoid any discrepancy, it is recommended to select the 'Archived Document' from the List and proceed with reprinting.

f642c24b-e5b9-4f0c-8ca4-9f0dc00d5ca5.title: How to unpack an Advance Ship Notice (ASN/856) that was confirmed by mistake?
f642c24b-e5b9-4f0c-8ca4-9f0dc00d5ca5.content:
Problem
An Advance Ship Notice(ASN/856) was inadvertently packed and confirmed, and now the User needs to make adjustments before the Advance Ship Notice is exported. Users need a way to reverse the packing confirmation for an order that was accidentally packed and marked as confirmed. Once a transaction is confirmed, edits and modifications can no longer be made to the ASN/Packing information.

Resolution
Issue: Once an EDI Transaction record is confirmed as packed in EDI Connector - Advance Ship Notice-856, the record gets locked, preventing further modifications or repacking.



Resolution Steps:

-
-
The user needs to navigate to the EDI Connector -> Advance Ship Notice-856 -> Process Advance Ship Notice screen.

-
In the 'Process Advance Shipment Notice' screen, the User can locate and delete the ASN associated with the affected order.

-
Once the ASN is deleted, the system automatically moved the order from "Confirmed" to the "New" status.  Once the Order is back in a New status the needed edits may take place.

-
After the edits and modifications take place the User may confirm the edits and export the ASN as normal.

2ebd2156-87e3-479b-9bb3-ddee44d9a28c.title: Why is the 'Change Password' option greyed out for SaaS users
2ebd2156-87e3-479b-9bb3-ddee44d9a28c.content:
Problem
Why do Cloud Users not have the option to reset their Password under the 'Change Password' option available:

Resolution
The following feature called 'Change Password' is present to reset/change the Password within the Traverse User Interface under 'File' menu. This is available only for Traverse users who are setup with a username and password to login to the Traverse UI directly rather than the "use trusted" login, as set up in the Traverse System Manager. (This option will be turned off for whoever logs in using the "Is Trusted" checkbox.) Because cloud users log in to Traverse with the "use trusted" checkbox, this feature is disabled for all Cloud (SaaS) users.



Reason for Feature Unavailability for Cloud Users:

Cloud (SaaS) users utilize the 'Use Trusted Connection' feature for logging into the application, which is designed to simplify access.

The 'Use Trusted Connection' feature automatically mirrors the user's credentials that were used to establish the Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) connection. This eliminates the need to enter a username and password within the Traverse UI. This is because the user has already provided their credentials to establish the RDP connection, followed by entering a 6-digit verification code for Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA).



Process Flow:

- Initial Authorization: Upon establishing the RDP connection and entering the credentials, the user's identity is confirmed.
- Credential Mirroring: Since MFA has authenticated the user, the credentials are automatically mirrored into the Traverse UI, eliminating the need to manually enter them again.
- No Need for Password Change in Traverse: As a result, the 'Change Password' feature is unnecessary for SaaS users because their Traverse credentials are indirectly managed through the initial RDP and MFA login process.

This change does not remove the user's ability to reset their password. The only difference is that, instead of resetting the password directly within the Traverse UI, Cloud users will need to reset it through the provided web link.

If the Cloud user wishes to reset their password, they would need to get that done through the following link: Aptean - Passreset (apteancloud.com)

The user manual regarding the same can be found here: Aptean SaaS - Create or Reset Domain Password.pdf (apteanuserguides.blob.core.windows.net)

0132ba44-2710-48f8-81ce-d63b4127a3f7.title: Creating a Disbursement Entry in Bank Reconciliation Transactions
0132ba44-2710-48f8-81ce-d63b4127a3f7.content:
Problem
How do you create a Disbursement transaction in the Bank Reconciliation module?

Resolution
Step 1: Navigate to Bank Reconciliation -> Transaction -> Transaction.

Step 2: Select the Bank Account ID.

Step 3: Choose the appropriate transaction type you want to create. For example, if you are entering disbursements, select the Disbursement transaction type tab.

Step 4: Click the New Record button from the Transaction function to start entering your transaction details.



Step 5: Enter the required transaction details, including the amount and relevant descriptions, and select the appropriate GL Offset Account corresponding to the transaction.

This account will be used to offset the Disbursement credit to the Bank Account/cash account in the General Ledger.

Step 6:  Navigate Bank Reconciliation → Transaction → Transaction Journals, select the bank account, and click Print or Output.

Step 7: Bank Reconciliation → Transaction → Post Transactions, select the bank account, and check the box next to "Do the following, then check the box". Click OK.

Once everything is confirmed, proceed to post the transaction. This action will transfer the transactions from the BR Transaction Journal to the General Ledger accounts to be reviewed and posted there.

(Side note - manual entries made to the General Ledger cash account will not automatically show up in the Bank Reconciliation module, so it is recommended to make your entries in the Bank Reconciliation transaction screen than directly in the General Ledger, as this will ensure that the two remain in balance.)

72ec6c72-b9cf-42a0-b369-17448220f275.title: How to Ensure Invoices Appear in the Open Invoice Report Using “As Of” Filters
72ec6c72-b9cf-42a0-b369-17448220f275.content:
Problem
The report is not capturing all invoices that were expected, despite the date range being set to include all relevant entries. Some transactions are missing from the report (for example, Invoice # 123 as seen below)

Resolution
Since the AP Open Invoice report uses an “As of” filter for both Invoice Due Date and Discount Due Date, it includes all invoices with dates on or before the specified date. Ensure that you are taking into account both the Invoice Due Date and the Discount Due Date when selecting your date ranges for the report.

For example, if the invoice in question has: Invoice Due Date: 3/16/2025 Discount Due Date: 2/14/2025 To ensure this invoice is included in the report, please set the filters as follows:

-
Invoice Due Date As Of: 3/16/2025 (or later)

-
Discount Due Date As Of: 2/14/2025 (or later)



Invoice #123 now appears in the report:

If the Discount Due Date or Invoice Date filter is set to an earlier date, the invoice will not appear in the report.

ec6a945a-c2e0-4bf4-9552-07befb2299fc.title: Resetting SaaS User Password from Server End (Single user and Multiple users)
ec6a945a-c2e0-4bf4-9552-07befb2299fc.content:
Problem
Need password reset for SaaS user account. Username: prod001\JM

Resolution
KB Article: Resetting SaaS User Password from Server End

This knowledge base article explains how to reset the password for a SaaS user from the server end. It outlines both the automated script-based method and the manual method using Active Directory Users and Computers.

Method 1: Using Bulk Password Reset Script

1. Log in to the **bastion server**: `prod001-Bas05`.
2. Open **Active Directory Users and Computers** under the domain: `prod001.apteancloud.local`.

3. Locate the user by searching their name or navigating directly to the appropriate **Organizational Unit (OU)**.

4. Right-click the user account, open **Properties**, and copy the **username**.
5. Navigate to the following path:
`M:\_Scripts\UserManagement\Traverse Global`
6. Create a `.csv` file and enter the username(s). Each username should be placed on a new line.

7. Run the `bulk_password_reset` script in **PowerShell** from the same directory.

8. Enter the path to the CSV file when prompted.
9. The script will automatically send a password reset email with an **ADSelfService portal link** to the user’s registered email address.

Method 2: Manual Reset via Active Directory

1. In **Active Directory Users and Computers**, right-click the user account and select **Reset Password**.

2. Enter a new password that complies with the password policy.
3. Click **OK** to complete the reset.

4. You must manually share the new credentials and password reset link with the user.

a04170b1-54b2-4a30-bc49-501de1ee9827.title: Unable to Print or Save Purchase Orders – Troubleshooting Steps
a04170b1-54b2-4a30-bc49-501de1ee9827.content:
Problem
Users are encountering an error message when attempting to print Purchase Orders, either for sending to vendors or for saving internally.

Resolution
To resolve the issue, users can try the following steps:

-
Log off and log back in to the system.

-
Alternatively, open Task Manager, navigate to the Users tab, and end the session for the affected user.

Note:
Ending the session under the Users tab will:

-
Force log off the selected user from the computer or server.

-
Terminate all running processes and applications in that session.

-
Result in the loss of any unsaved work.

-
Require the user to log in again to start a new session.

This method helps free up system resources or resolve issues caused by stuck or idle user sessions. Please use this action carefully, especially in multi-user environments, to avoid data loss or disruption.

If these steps do not resolve the issue, restarting the server may be necessary. Ensure that all users are logged out before doing so to prevent data loss or interruption.



Workaround:
As a temporary solution, creating the missing directory in the local folder (as specified in the error path) may resolve the issue.

653cc3b0-a649-40fc-8c46-d175d7811199.title: Report to combine AP Vendor info and AP Payment history info
653cc3b0-a649-40fc-8c46-d175d7811199.content:
Problem
Users need a consolidated view or report that includes Vendor information (such as address details) and Payment information (like yearly dollars spent). However, Traverse does not provide a built-in view that combines both datasets.

Resolution
Since no single view in Traverse contains both Vendor address and Payment summary, the solution involves creating two separate exports and merging them externally using Excel via a VLOOKUP formula.

-
Create Vendor Info Export

-
From Traverse, export the Accounts Payable> Interactive View> Vendor view.

-
Ensure it includes column:

-
Vendor ID

-
Name

-
Address details (Address, City, State, ZIP, etc.)

-
Create Payment Summary Export

-
Use the Accounts Payable> Interactive View> AP Summary History view.

-
Include:

-
Vendor ID

-
Yearly payment totals

-
Merge in Excel Using VLOOKUP

-
Open both exported files in Excel.

-
In the AP Summary file, create a new column next to the Vendor ID.

-
Use VLOOKUP to bring in address info from the Vendor Info file.

Formula:

=VLOOKUP(A2,Sheet2!$A$2:$G$3361,2,FALSE)

-
Here, A2 is the Vendor ID in your AP Summary file, and Sheet2 contains your Vendor address data.

-
Adjust the column index (2 in this case) to point to the correct field (e.g., Name, Address, etc.)

-
Finalize Report

-
Copy the formula across multiple columns to retrieve Name, Address, City, etc.

-
Format the data as needed and save the final report.

9fcf4305-fe13-4210-a698-b72d82b20d50.title: Guide to Saving Customized Layouts in Interactive Views
9fcf4305-fe13-4210-a698-b72d82b20d50.content:
Problem
The client would like to know how to save interactive views according to their preferences.

Resolution
In Traverse, every interactive view includes an option to save a customized layout for future use. This allows users to personalize views—such as adding/removing columns, adjusting alignment, or applying filters—and preserve those settings.

Example:

Let’s consider the IN Lot Number View. By default, this view displays a standard set of column headers (as shown in the first image).

If a user customizes the view -- such as selecting different columns using the Column Chooser, rearranging them, or changing alignment (as shown in the second image) -- these changes will not be retained after logging out. The view resets to its default state upon the next login.

To avoid this and retain the custom layout, users can save the view either as Private or Public.

Steps to Save a Customized Interactive View:

1.Prepare the View
Customize the layout as desired (column changes, filters, alignment, etc.).

2. Access the Save View option

Click on the View button (represented by an inverted triangle in the menu bar).

3. Name the View

In the widget box that appears, enter a name for your custom view (e.g., Sample Test).

Hit "Enter" on your Keyboard to Save the View. You can also click on the View tab again to save.

You will get the Popup Message stating that the View has been saved successfully.

3. Edit Views

If you would like to make the view public, click "Edit Views" in the View Menu list.  Click the "Public" button to make the view available to others. You can delete views here too by clicking the minus button.

4. Reuse the Saved View

When you log in again, simply select your saved view from the list to restore your preferred layout and filters.

By saving views this way, users can retain a consistent, personalized view in Traverse.

22de2dd7-8bd2-4b4c-a128-ae7cbb509c15.title: Why does a SO Prepayment is not visible in the AR Cash Receipts screen
22de2dd7-8bd2-4b4c-a128-ae7cbb509c15.content:
Problem
The Prepayment that was entered and posted for a Sales Order is not showing in a new AR Cash Receipts transaction screen.

When we look for the Cash Receipts for that customer in the new AR Cash Receipts transaction screen, the Prepayment is missing.

Resolution
The missing of the Cash Receipt is because the user was trying to create a New Cash receipt in a AR Cash Receipt screen which does not list all pending Cash Receipts.



When a Prepayment is entered in the Sales Orders screen under the Payments tab and then posted, a corresponding cash receipt is automatically created in the AR Cash Receipts screen. Therefore, there is no need for the user to manually create a new cash receipt.

However, this is sometimes overlooked. When the user then tries to create a new receipt manually, the Prepayment may not appear, leading to confusion or the perception that the Cash Receipt is missing.

To resolve this issue, rather than creating a new receipt, it is recommended that the user find and retrieve the existing receipt, by using the ellipsis (…) button next to the Receipt No field. The user should then pull up the correct receipt based on the Customer ID that is associated with the transaction.

And this ensures that the prepayment is properly accounted for, and the cash receipt is correctly processed without duplication.

a5fb18ca-cc77-46e3-a965-27cb945e4acc.title: AR Customer De-Duplication - Skutt Ceramics, Inc.
a5fb18ca-cc77-46e3-a965-27cb945e4acc.content:
Problem
Under Accounts receivable, interactive views, there is the Customer duplicates view, which is supposed to pull any duplicate accounts. It does not appear to be functioning the way we anticipated it to.

Resolution
The problem is due to a poorly constructed SQL Statement in the view setup in Design Studio.

The view looks at all customers and returns all the ones where the name, phone number, and email address are the same. The problem is that it just uses an "=" to do the comparison. Equals signs do not work in the case of NULL entries. So if you say "where Email1 = Email2" that will return true if both email addresses have the same non NULL value in them. But it will return false if both contain NULL, where in this case you want to consider it true. So in cases where the customer information is the same be both phone numbers or email addresses are NULL it doesn't correctly identify them as being duplicates.

This can be corrected by changing the select statement to check to see if the values are equal OR if both values are null. Below is the original SQL select statement in Design Studio followed by the corrected statement. The view ID is ArCustomerDuplicates_Custom

WRONG

SELECT * FROM

(

SELECT c1.CustId, c1.CustName, c1.Phone, c1.Email

FROM dbo.tblArCust c1

INNER JOIN

(

SELECT CustName, Phone, Email, COUNT(*) AS [count]

FROM dbo.tblArCust

GROUP BY CustName, Phone, Email

HAVING COUNT(*) > 1

) c2

ON c1.CustName = c2.CustName AND c1.Phone = c2.Phone AND c1.email = C2.email

) ds



CORRECTED

SELECT * FROM

(

SELECT c1.CustId, c1.CustName, c1.Phone, c1.Email

FROM dbo.tblArCust c1

INNER JOIN

(

SELECT CustName, Phone, Email, COUNT(*) AS [count]

FROM dbo.tblArCust

GROUP BY CustName, Phone, Email

HAVING COUNT(*) > 1

) c2

ON c1.CustName = c2.CustName AND

(c1.Phone = c2.Phone or (c1.Phone is NULL and c2.Phone is NULL)) AND

(c1.email = C2.email or (c1.email is NULL or C2.email is NULL))

) ds

1a40a8c6-bd01-4d32-8069-40f44e460c69.title: Inventory item error- Error : Value [] does not exist in [ABC Class].
1a40a8c6-bd01-4d32-8069-40f44e460c69.content:
Problem
please see the attached file with the error Bob is receiving. Please call him at 812-583-4656; bobyoung@hawkins-bailey.com

Resolution
You just need to assign the ABC call, please refer the below screenshot.



ABC Class is a relative value of items in the database, ranking items according to multiple criteria, and grouping items into classes that represent the relative value of the items.



ABC Classes are generally used when physical inventory is done using cycle counting. This means a portion of your inventory is counted on a daily basis. The ABC class can be used to classify your items into value or usage classes to determine how often they should be counted in your cycle. Usually higher value and higher volume items are counted more frequently, so they would be classified with the same ABC class.



You will see the ABC Class as a selection or filtering criteria in these and other places:

Item Locations Maintenance
Item Locations Inquiry
Item Locations List
Freeze Quantities
PO - Calculate Reorders
MFG-MF - MRP Processing (multiple reports)
RP Processing (multiple reports)
WM Physical Counts View




ABC Code    Sequence No    Allocation %    Notes

A    1 (highest value; counted most frequently)    20 (Assigns the top 20% of total items to the code after being sorted by the value matching the criteria selected in the Assign ABC Codes function.)    Comprised of inventory that makes up 70-80% of your overall inventory value.

B    2 (second highest value; counted second most frequently    30 (Assigns the next 30% of total items to the code after being sorted by the value matching the criteria selected in the Assign ABC Codes function.)    Accounts for the next 10-15% of inventory value

C    3 (third highest value; counted third most frequently)    50 (Assigns the next 50% of total items to the code after being sorted by the value matching the criteria selected in the Assign ABC Codes function.)    Represents the bottom 10-15% of inventory value Percent must total 100%

d705cca0-0aad-458a-a479-e88bec973db8.title: Is there a way to turn off Leave Accrual for certain employees?
d705cca0-0aad-458a-a479-e88bec973db8.content:
Problem
Is there a way to turn off Leave Accrual for certain employees?

Resolution
There is a way in which the employees can be added without automatically accruing leave?

If the company has the Business Rule for, "Automatic Accrual of Leave Time" set to No, then no employees will acquire leave automatically. Rather, leave is added manually for each employee.

If the company has the Business Rule for, "Automatic Accrual of Leave Time" set to Yes, and has leave codes set up, this can still be accomplished for select employees.

To accomplish this, the employee needs to be set up with a leave code that does not accrue leave.

1. Go to Payroll

2. Go to Code Maintenance and create a leave code with a Maximum Accrual of 0 hours (or as appropriate), and 0's in the Min Accrual column. Leave the box "Include Leave Hours in Accrual Calculation" unchecked.

(For existing Leave Codes, tiers can also be set up in which employees Up to Year 1 do not accrue leave with a Minimum Accrual of 0, etc. if these employees will eventually accrue leave.)

3. Add this leave code to the employee's setup, so leave assigned to this code will not accrue. When entering transactions for employees, this leave code would be selected.

4. You would add this code in the Employee Information>> Pay tab>> under the Leave codes section. Remove any leave codes that do not apply.



If needed, leave can be added manually to this leave code using the Periodic Processing > Leave Adjustments screen.

e61247ec-5c40-4d09-8642-a62c1411a97d.title: How to Restore Multiple Environments
e61247ec-5c40-4d09-8642-a62c1411a97d.content:
Problem
This document will outline the process to keep multiple customer environments loaded on the same SQL instance at the same time.
As a support representative, we may find we have multiple customer environments restored at the same time. We are unable to use the same SYS for the db name as most users use the software this way and it absolutely works for them. It's been recommended. However, if you have 4 customers with the SYS named SYS, you will overwrite the one that was there before and that can be a problem.

It is also a risk to use the same SYS database as each customer can have their own customizations and thus they need to have their physical SYS database restored.

Lastly, it is also ideal to keep environments isolated so you do not risk contamination issues that lead to false testing results or evaluation.

Resolution
We currently have a customer environment restored FSC and their database is FSCSYS. I now have a new customer issue to investigate and their company database is PPX. Here are some recommendations and process to follow to restore this.

First, it is ideal when working with multiple customer environments to keep things very organized. You may want to consider creating a work folder to organize each customer environment in use:

You may also want to consider organization within each client directory, lets look at Perfect Precision as we intend to restore their data shortly.

We have a client directory which contains the client folder for this customer. It really contains the customer's client folder from their server. This ensures I have everything the customer is using, so I will encounter the issue they reported to me. I am looking at everything through their eyes.

The QA folder is a consideration depending on your work. If you have hotfixes, install packages, special files you are reviewing, you may want to  house that here so you have a clean record of what was provided to you. Perhaps you tested a hotfix and there was still an issue, you might have two more directories inside here, one for the first hotfix so you know what was given, and a second directory for the corrected hotfix. You never know what you need until you don't have it.

The updates directory is optional, but may be used for testing updates in this environment. Perhaps the customer is on an old build and you want to test out going to the latest one. Or perhaps you are QAing the latest install package and want to make sure the updater works properly. Maybe its none of that, but contains the customer's live updates so you can seek out issues in that directory.

Lastly, and also optional, the Work Notes directory. Perhaps you have app data files here related to your case, other scripts for investigation, really anything, but it helps prevent your loss and encourages organization for all the little things.

Let's get to the restore portion of this process.

We already have one customer environment, FSC. Their SYS database has been restored as FSCSYS so there is no worry about overlap unless another customer gets restored that also has FSCSYS for their SYS db name. Then we'd need to pick a different name for the restore and adjust the config file for the client. So adjusting Traverse.exe.config and DesignStudio.exe.config in that customer client folder.

Let's proceed with Perfect Precision. We already have their client folder in our work directory, organized in that client folder from our shot above.

Next, we'll need to restore the data in SQL Server Management Studio.

Login to your instance on SSMS and right-click on Databases > Restore Database:


Click Device > then the box with three ellipses on it to navigate to your backup file.

Click your first database to restore and then OK:

If we wish, we can rename the Database in the 'Database:' field.

We can click OK to start the process, or navigate more on the left pane for other items to change.

For example if you click on 'Files' you can choose to relocate the files to another destination folder (MDF and LDF files.)
You may also adjust the file name and/or location you are restoring as in the 'Restore As' column.


Do the same for the SYS database, we're restore AS PPXSYS and that has been renamed in the shot below:



Now that the data is restored, we need to add this as a company in the Traverse Global Server Manager. Login, changing the SYSdb name to what you used. In our example, logging in as PPXSYS.

Next, navigate to 'Database' > 'Add Company'

Click OK.

Finally, add a user so you can login, and create a security group so you can grant permissions to your user.

At this point in time, you are able to log in to the customer client and proceed with work.

Overall, this process is optional, however you will find with many customer environments at the same time it can be a challenge to keep things organized and decontaminated. And again, you also avoid the risk of a custom mismatch or vanilla mismatch if you use what the customer has instead of sharing that database.

cb4cbfa8-4998-485d-8134-3260d4e3f95b.title: How to Restore Design Studio View without Metadata
cb4cbfa8-4998-485d-8134-3260d4e3f95b.content:
Problem
A scenario may arise where a Design Studio view was reverted to an old design, or possibly lost. If a metadata backup does not exist but a database backup does, you are able to get the design of the old view back with some minor work. Let's read on to look at the solution.

Resolution
To use a database backup to restore a Design Studio view to a previous design, we will need a backup. If we do not have this, or if the view does not exist as desired in that backup, it must be recreated. If it is not known if there is a backup, check any sandbox environments or other test environment, there may be changes to the view there. If they made a change and sent it in, it is possible something was checked in to custom source control for this customer and there may be a correct design there we can obtain and put in place.

Sometimes customers create a view on their own, or modify an existing one on their own; sometimes they modify a view that was already custom and there could be further changes to it that are different than the original custom design. Their changes may not be something we have on file in that scenario.

Note: be sure to gain agreement with the customer that:
- The current view really is wrong. You don't want to replace something that one person thinks is wrong but others agree it is correct. Perhaps the case contact is not aware of someone else making intended changes.

-Once the old, correct view is put back in place, be sure the customer agrees this is correct.

We will look at two scenarios:
- They already have the needed change in their sandbox environment
- You have a database backup that does indeed contain the view they need reinstated

View is in the sandbox
If the view is correct, and confirmed correct by the customer in their sandbox, we can grab that design and paste it in to production, provided we get approval from the customer to do so.

Since a sandbox environment is isolated and on another SQL instance, you won't be able to use the 'Copy To' button. However if the view was an issue in production and another production company had the correct version of the view, you could consider copying in that scenario.

First, identify the incorrect record in Design Studio. In Design Studio > System Data > Views Table to see all views.

From here, it may be best to have the sandbox environment open on another screen. The overall idea is that you want to copy the Datasource, and/or Available columns, and/or Default columns, and/or other columns for this view from the sandbox into production.

NOTE: If the view was customized for just one company, you will see the 'Customized' column show a value of 'Company.' If it was Customized for all, you need to find the record for the view that has a ReplaceID.

If you are fixing the view and it was for one company, click customize and then make your changes there:
Be sure to click OK and then save the record after.

If the change was for all companies, access the record for the view with a ReplaceID value. You may get confused here as the vanilla view will say 'System' in the 'Customized' column, that is to note the view was altered for all companies, for the whole system. But you will not change that record, you will need to make changes to the record that replaces it:

So in this example, the InDetailHistoryCustom view is replacing the InDetailHistory view, I need to make my changes to the InDetailHistoryCustom record in this case. You do not need to hit the 'Customize' button here, just make the changes directly to the record.

Once you make the changes and save, verify the view is correct again and also make sure to get agreement from the customer. Read on if you did not have a sandbox that had the change but it was in a backup.

A backup has been obtained and we can use this
This process is essentially just us restoring the backup that has the correct view in it, setting it up to be able to open Design Studio, and then using the process we outlined above for sandboxes.

To keep things cleaner, you may just want to obtain a backup of the company and SYS databases and while you're at it, a client backup. We just need to be able to open Design Studio. You could manipulate your own environment to point to the customer backup and SYS that you restored as well. Another option is to grab the information out of the data but you need to know the tables to be sure you're getting the correct values. Restoring a backup can be a quick way to do this however, and with less risk.

Once you have the backups (company, SYS, and client folder) bring them to your VM or local machine where you use customer data.
Restore the company and SYS databases and then set up security.
Next, double check the client config file to make sure the license machine name and port are not issues, if so adjust them and save.
Then you can launch and log in to Design Studio. Lastly, follow the process above for copying from the sandbox.

NOTE: Work with the customer on this last part, it is ideal to put it in the sandbox first if they have one so they can confirm the design is correct and working. Its possible the change that was reported broken was intentional, so it might be ideal to consider if other resources can also confirm this is correct, or that the customer contact you have is aware of anyone else making changes. Then proceed to copy from the sandbox to production when given permission to do so. Once that is complete, make sure to get confirmation from the customer that the view is functioning properly.

dd6ff355-78de-4de6-bb02-432b30b3fa87.title: Testing Modified Customers with a Vanilla Database
dd6ff355-78de-4de6-bb02-432b30b3fa87.content:
Problem
A scenario may arise where you have restored a customer's client and data on your VM or local machine and suspect a data issue. One thing you can quickly do is point your client environment to a vanilla database and see how it behaves. This is only practical in certain scenarios, but is something that can help quickly narrow things down when it fits the scenario. We'll talk about how to do this below.

Disclaimer, if the customer has customizations in the area you need to test, you may encounter errors because you are in a customization mismatch. The vanilla database (db) you restore won't have any of their mods applied to it.
If you have a copy of their updates folder, you could consider applying their custom server update against the vanilla database to test if that's the case. If unsure, the update history will tell you the custom updates that have been applied so you know what you might need.
Depending on the issue you are investigating, you may or may not want to do this. It all depends on how you want to test this.

Resolution
First, we'll want a vanilla backup. In our example, the customer is a ProcessPro Global customer using build 21347. We'll want a vanilla backup of ProcessPro Global 21347 which we can obtain from VM26, or other resources may also have a backup if needed.

Once we have our backup and its placed on your VM or local machine, wherever you have the customer data restored, open SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS.)

Proceed to restore the database as usual. In our example we'll restore it as PPX because that is the db from VM26 for PPG 21347:


Next, you need to access the SYS db and add an entry for the vanilla db in there. So we need to access tblSmCompInfo.
Doing this will allow us to setup security and log in to the PPX company and test what we need.

In this environment, the SYS db is named FSCSYS, so we will expand that db and then expand Tables and navigate to tblSmCompInfo.
Right click on tblSmCompInfo and click Edit all Rows (It might say Edit Top 100 Rows depending on your SSMS settings.)

Add your vanilla db in the CompID column, with a name of your choosing, arrow up or down off the field to auto populate the defaults and also finish writing the record.

Next, we need to set up security, let's navigate to the Traverse Global Server Manager and log in.

Click on Database > Add Company

Because we entered the PPX CompanyID in SSMS it will be availalbe for us to choose in the Traverse Global Server Manager.
We'll select it and then hit Apply and OK:


Next, proceed to set up security for PPX (or your company db that you restored.) You could copy security from the existing company to the one you just restored or simply create a group, place your user in it and grant permission.

At this point you should be able to log in to the software and continue your testing pointed to the vanilla database.

Again, an important reminder, if this customer has mods in the area you are testing, you may want to consider also applying the mods to the vanilla database you just restored. The idea is that there might be a data issue, so testing with vanilla data first might be a good idea, and then apply the custom server update(s) to the vanilla environment and test again.

If you are unsure what server updates might be needed, the update history for the customers database should provide this information.

5c34f49d-8347-458d-af72-3fb005f116f4.title: Testing Modified Customers using Vanilla Assemblies
5c34f49d-8347-458d-af72-3fb005f116f4.content:
Problem
A customized customer has encountered an issue. You are troubleshooting and trying to figure out what is going on, and suspect it might be due to a customization. With Traverse based solutions, there can be a few layers of customizations in play. ProcessPro Global, for example, modifies some Traverse functions to provide the features of ProcessPro Global. A ProcessPro Global customer might also have a modification in one of those areas so there could be a custom DLL that modifies a ProcessPro Global DLL, that modifies a Traverse Global DLL.

While investigation can be more complicated, one option is to try and plug in a vanilla assembly. This allows you to see how it behaves with your backup of the customer data and client. With this process, you may be able to quickly determine if this problem may be customization related or not.

Resolution
In this scenario, we will demonstrate how to test a vanilla assembly when a customer is modified.  We'll complicate things a little and add another level: lets use ProcessPro Global as an example, and then if you're only dealing with Traverse Global with a mod, its more simple.

First, let's get an idea about mods in play. We'll use the case scenario where there is an issue in SO Orders, the customer has a modified SO Orders function, and we need to test vanilla and see how it behaves. Now why not just go to your vanilla environment and do this? The process we'll outline below is a way to to test with the customer data that you already observed the issue in. So this way you can say its an issue in this environment when I have the mod in use, but if I use vanilla it works fine.

In this method, we'll essentially be working with SM Application Menus, and then either in the Traverse Global Server Manager or in SM Groups to grant permission to see the functions we add to the menu.

To start, here is our entry to SM Application Menus for SO Orders:
We see the Replaced checkbox which indicates the vanilla entry is overridden by something custom.

Let's take a closer look and see what it is, we can access Design Studio's Custom Menu function where the MenuID is 1250207. Checking this helps us understand if this is replaced by a customizations, or in the case of ProcessPro Global, maybe there is a special ProcessPro Global assembly in use. Here, we can see a custom assembly so we know when we were testing with the customer's data and client, we were using a custom version of the SO Orders function.


If ProcessPro Global modifies Traverse Global with its own SO Order function, we'll see that in Design Studio if running it for vanilla ProcessPro Global:

Now that we know what is in play, lets test this environment but using the custom version, then the ProcessPro Global version, and then the Traverse Global version. We'll make entries to SM Application Menus to add them back so we can test each layer.
Again, if your scenario is just Traverse Global, then you do not have a ProcessPro Global layer to worry about. Use these concepts to review the layers in your particular situation.

In our first screenshot above, we see the Orders entry. This entry is for vanilla Traverse Global. It has a customization entry that overrides it, and so the Replaced checkbox is checked. Why I bring this up is because we will make another entry that is a copy of this, to add the Traverse Global vanilla function to the menu. Then we will do the same for ProcessPro Global.

Step 1, from the Application Menu screen, create a new record.
In this case we want to enter the record for Orders, just like it appears in the first line.

The plugin name is case sensitive, be sure to type this correctly else you will get an error when clicking on it to launch it.
I used a MenuID of 1250299 out of habit, while we are only testing and this is temporary in our environment, I always start at the top of the range as the lower numbers are reserved for development to use, else updates will replace what you put there. Again, this is in your environment, its not like we are adding a modification for a customer, but I do it this way anyway as that is our process for customizations.

Let's add ProcessPro Global's entry. Remember, I used a vanilla PPG environment and looked at Design Studio to see what ProcessPro Global was using to override Traverse Global with:

In the next step, we'll give our self permission so when we launch the software we can use these functions.
I'll do this in the ProcessPro Global UI instead of in the Traverse Global Server Manager, but it can be done there also.

Navigate to SM > Administration > Groups, and then grant permission to the group your user is in so you can test this:

Click Apply and OK

Close the software and log back in, you should now see the two new functions:


At this point, you can access each one and test to see if it throws the error or not. You may quickly find that the issue stems from one of the layers tested but not all.

As a reminder in the example, the top function is Traverse Global's Order function, then ProcessPro Global's Order function, and then the last one is the customized function that we see overriding the Traverse Global function (the replace check we see) originally.

Some additional notes:
This should work most of the time for a test. Do not do this in a customer's production environment, get backups and do it on your own VM or wherever you work with customer data. There is risk if you do this in a customer's production environment.
Some customers may have some elaborate mods and you might not be able to do this.
Some customers may have Design Studio changes that contribute to the issue you experience, verify that as well as it might be the cause.

1bef254b-a1f1-436e-9d84-d16c649a4973.title: Selecting the UOM for an Item on a Sales Order
1bef254b-a1f1-436e-9d84-d16c649a4973.content:
Problem
How do I select the correct UOM for an item on my Sales Order?

Resolution
You can select the Unit of Measure (UOM) you want to use when creating a new Sales Order or adding new items to a Sales Order.

- Simply follow your normal process for creating an SO.

Once you have saved the item to your Sales Order, the UOM will lock in and resist editing.

accd32a9-1f82-416f-afba-d70a8bdd9826.title: Adding column for Social Security Number to a view in Payroll
accd32a9-1f82-416f-afba-d70a8bdd9826.content:
Problem
Customer would like to add a column for the SSN (Social Security Number) to the Payroll Employee Information View

Resolution
Open Design Studio.
Select Views Table (under System Data)
Scroll down to find the View ID entitled "Employee" for the Employee Information View.
Click into the "Data Source" column to access the drop down box. Under the Data Source column, confirm the "SocialSecurityNo" is listed and copy the exact words.

Add "SocialSecurityNo" in the Available field by clicking on the small, inverted triangle on the right side of these text boxes as shown below to access the drop down box. Copy it into the list that appears in the drop down box.

58d3b6b1-82f1-4137-9cda-a506a66b2b90.title: How to check the Build number of Traverse API?
58d3b6b1-82f1-4137-9cda-a506a66b2b90.content:
Problem
How to check the Build number of Traverse API?

Resolution
There is no direct or user-facing option within the Traverse interface to view the build number of the Traverse API. However, it can be manually located by navigating to the installation directory of the API on the server where it is hosted.



Steps to Identify the Traverse API Build Number:

i. Navigate to the API Installation Path:

- Open the File Explorer on the server where the Traverse API is installed.
- Go to the following default installation path (unless it has been customized): C:\inetpub\TRAVERSE\TRAVERSEAPI\



ii. Locate the 'Bin' Folder:

- Inside the TRAVERSEAPI folder, open the bin directory.
- In the bin folder, locate the file named TRAVERSE.Web.API.dll.



iii. Check the DLL File for Version Information:

- Right-click on the file and select Properties.
- Go to the Details tab. Under the Product version or File version, you will find the build number, followed by the 'Product Version', in the 'Product version' field.

90e50c11-bf7f-4647-953d-610ac53db1ba.title: How To Set Up Advanced Earning Codes in On-Time Web
90e50c11-bf7f-4647-953d-610ac53db1ba.content:
Problem
Question: Does On-Time Web have a way to have time differentials for our weekend and second shift workers?

Resolution
How To Set Up Advanced Earning Codes in On-Time Web

Question: Does On-Time Web have a way to have time differentials for our weekend and second shift workers?

Set up Advanced Earning Codes for the special earning codes with a pay differential.

- Set up the Earning Code
- Navigate to Company Settings>Earning Codes>Earning Codes and create your earning code for your Advanced Earning Code
- Earning Code – enter the Earning Code
- Description of the Earning Code
- Pay Type – Select Straight Time (x1), Premium Time, Double Time (x2)

- Include for Premium – select yes or no if the new Earning Code is to be included for calculation of overtime (Premium time)
- Linked to Premium Code – Select the Premium Code that will be linked to the new Earning Code.
- Sort Order – Select the Sort Order for the order in which the new code will display when listed.
- Status – Enable or Disable the new Earning Code
- Save

- Set up the Advanced Earning Code
- Select the Active Earning Code that was set up above.
- Select the Default Days that the earning code will be used.
- Auto Assign Linked Premium Code – (yes or No) If a straight earning code is selected, this will automatically assign the premium code and make it the default premium code for selected days
- Choose the employees whom this Advanced Earning Code is to be applied
- Overwrite Existing? – (Yes or No) If the employee already has the given Earning Code assigned, this will overwrite the record with the new options chosen.
- Add/Subtract a differential amount to employee base RATE. – If you choose to calculate the Rate in On-Time Web, add the differential amount here.
- Add/Subtract a differential amount to employee base COST. - If you choose to calculate the Cost in On-Time Web, add the differential amount here.
- Save

- Select the Earning Code and apply it to the Employee
- Navigate to Company Settings>Employees>Advanced Earnings Codes Tab
- Click Add New+ and select the Advanced Earning Code and complete the form and Save

dfb77ee6-3c18-4fc4-899a-0b8d71abd7b1.title: Integrating Payroll into Project Costing
dfb77ee6-3c18-4fc4-899a-0b8d71abd7b1.content:
Problem
How to integrate Payroll Transactions into Project Costing

Resolution
-

Integrating payroll with project costing ensures accurate tracking of labor costs per project by linking employee hours and pay directly to project budgets. In order to integrate your Payroll with Project Costing, such that your Payroll Employees are available to select for time ticket entries, go to:



System Manager  > Company Setup > Business Rules and select Project Costing from the list.

Next, in the "Interface - Application" section, ensure that your "Payroll" interface is set to "Yes".  If it is not, then select "Yes" for this option and click "Apply" and "Ok" to save the settings. See the screenshot below.

This will allow the Project Costing screens to pull the employee list from the Payroll employee datasets.



If this option is set to "No", then the the Project Costing screens will pull employees from the System Manager > Company Setup > Employees list and transactions will not flow to Payroll.



Creating a Time Entry in Project Costing:

-
Navigate to Time Ticket Entry
Go to Project Costing > Transactions > Time Ticket Entry.

-
Enter Time Details

-
Select the appropriate Batch Code (e.g., #APTST).

-
Enter the Employee ID and associate the correct Project and Task.  With the Payroll integration set up, this should populate a list of employee ID's from Payroll. Otherwise, it will populate with a list of employee ID's from System Manager, as stated above.

-
Assign the number of hours worked on the project.

-
Note: Filling in the Project/Task and Rate Code fields is mandatory.

-
Save the Time Ticket Entry

-
Preview the Time Ticket Journal
Navigate to the Time Ticket Journal, apply the Project ID filter, and select the relevant batch code to review the entry.

-
Post the Project Costing Transaction
Go to Project Costing > Transactions > Post Transactions and post the time ticket entry.

-
Process in Payroll

-
Navigate to Payroll > Daily Work > Time Ticket Journal. You would be able to notice the time ticket entry that was posted in PC appear in the payroll time ticket journal.

-
Post the transactions as per the standard payroll process.

-
Continue with the usual steps to generate and post payroll checks.

This is how a project costing entry is integrated into payroll for processing payment to the worker.

The screenshot below shows that the entries made in Project Costing have now been successfully integrated into Payroll for further processing.

6b56d596-9acd-42af-8430-2f85934e69e4.title: How to pin Export Locations in Quick Access for easy Access from Traverse
6b56d596-9acd-42af-8430-2f85934e69e4.content:
Problem
In Traverse, users often export reports and documents to specific folders on their local or network drives. Traverse allows setting a default export path through the System Manager > User Defaults screen (available from Build 24031 and above) which can help to simplify this. However, if the Users frequently work with multiple folders and do not wish to restrict themselves to a single default path, Windows allows us to pin multiple folders to Quick Access for easier navigation during report exports.

Resolution
This guide provides a step-by-step explanation of how to pin a folder to Quick Access in Windows File Explorer to simplify navigation when exporting to multiple locations.

Quick Access is a section in Windows File Explorer that shows your frequently or manually pinned folders for quick access. It appears at the top left panel when you open any browser window, including Traverse's export file explorer window.

How to Pin a Folder to Quick Access:

-
Open File Explorer (Windows Key + E).

-
Navigate to the folder you frequently use for exporting.

-
Right-click on the folder.

-
Select Pin to Quick Access. The folder will now appear in the Quick Access panel on the left side of File Explorer.



Once the location is pinned, the user would be able to find it while exporting reports out of Traverse, whenever needed.

4495f1b0-c3ba-4e68-b156-2996ecd96309.title: User Question : Can We Change an Item's UoM Conversion?
4495f1b0-c3ba-4e68-b156-2996ecd96309.content:
Problem
User Question : Can We Change an Item's UoM Conversion?

Resolution
User Question : Can We Change an Item's UoM Conversion?

-
Constraints on Changes: You cannot change the conversion factor for the Base UOM in the Units list. For alternate UOM's, changing an item's Unit of Measure (UoM) Conversion may not be possible if there are open purchase orders, sales orders, or other related transactions using the unit. In these cases, if you try to delete the UOM you want to change, you will get an error message "Current record cannot be deleted."

-
Transaction Processing: Ensure all related transactions are processed or closed before changing the UoM Conversion Factor to maintain data integrity. The Item Availability View, SO Open Order Report, PO Open Order Report, and the MP Material Requirements View can be of assistance in finding related transactions.

-
No Constraints: Other than for the Base UOM, if there are no transactions or constraints, the UoM Conversion Factor can typically be changed without issues.

-
Preparation: Verify that the item is not in use and is removed from any transactions or location transfers before making changes.

-
Change: To change the Conversion Factor, delete the current UOM in the Units list, and replace it with a new UOM with a different Conversion Factor.

Once the UOM Conversion Factor has been changed, it will impact transactions moving forward. This change will not affect the conversion calculations for historical posted transactions, as seen in the Inventory Detail History View.

bc1b3f8e-1da1-4ab6-b869-0424043cd116.title: 2627 : Violation of PRIMARY KEY constraint 'PK_tblApPayment'. Cannot insert duplicate key in object 'dbo.tblApPayment'. The duplicate key value is (1). : Procedure{dbo.trav_ApPreparePayment_proc} (.Net SqlClient Data Provider)
bc1b3f8e-1da1-4ab6-b869-0424043cd116.content:
Problem
While attempting to prepare payments in Accounts Payable - Pay Invoices - Prepare Payments, users are receiving the following error message:



2627 : Violation of PRIMARY KEY constraint 'PK_tblApPayment'. Cannot insert duplicate key in object 'dbo.tblApPayment'. The duplicate key value is (1). : Procedure{dbo.trav_ApPreparePayment_proc} (.Net SqlClient Data Provider)

Resolution
This error can typically indicate that there is a Prepayment present in AP Open Invoices that does not have a Bank ID associated with it. The following are steps that can be taken to identify and update the prepayment record.



- Use the AP Open Invoice View under Accounts Payable > Interactive Views > Open Invoice View to review "Prepaid" status Invoices records to identify transactions with Bank Account IDs missing.

- Once the Invoice Number and Vendor ID have been identified, the Bank Account ID may be added to the prepayment/Invoice record in  Account Payable> Pay Invoices> Hold/Release Invoices by the following:

-
- For the applicable prepaid invoice record, click on the drop-down for Bank ID and select the appropriate Bank that was used for the prepayment.

Once the Bank ID is present for the prepayment, you should now be able to prepare payments and no longer receive the referenced error.

f4ad287d-f9ee-44a3-9af5-7db4d79bad55.title: Fiscal years and payroll transactions
f4ad287d-f9ee-44a3-9af5-7db4d79bad55.content:
Problem
I am accruing payroll back to December that was posted in January. Do I use fiscal year 2023 or 2024?

Resolution
When accruing payroll that was posted in January but should be accounted for in December, you should use the fiscal year that includes December. The Payroll Year will track with the calendar year, while the fiscal year may not. Here’s how to determine which fiscal year to use:

Determining the Fiscal Year

-
Calendar Year Fiscal Year:

- If your fiscal year follows the calendar year (January 1 to December 31), then December 2023 falls within fiscal year 2023.
- In this case, you should use fiscal year 2023 for the accrual.

-
Non-Calendar Year Fiscal Year:

- If your fiscal year does not follow the calendar year (for example, it runs from July 1 to June 30), you need to determine which fiscal year includes December.
- For example, if your fiscal year runs from July 1, 2023, to June 30, 2024, then December 2023 would be part of fiscal year 2024.

Example:

-
Calendar Year Fiscal Year:

- December 2023: Fiscal Year 2023
- January 2024: Fiscal Year 2024

-
Non-Calendar Year Fiscal Year (e.g., July 1, 2023, to June 30, 2024):

- December 2023: Fiscal Year 2024
- January 2024: Fiscal Year 2024

Specific Steps:

-
Identify Your Fiscal Year:

- Confirm your organization's fiscal year dates.

-
Determine the Correct Fiscal Year for December:

- If December is within the fiscal year 2023, accrue the payroll to fiscal year 2023.
- If December is within the fiscal year 2024, accrue the payroll to fiscal year 2024.

By ensuring the accrual is made in the correct fiscal year, you maintain accurate financial records and comply with accounting principles. If your fiscal year differs from the calendar year, adjust the entries accordingly based on your specific fiscal year dates.
