54b34e74-abc6-4e1c-8d26-a7f021736ea5.title: Troubleshooting With the SQL Deadlock Report
54b34e74-abc6-4e1c-8d26-a7f021736ea5.content:
Problem
A time may arise in the software where two processes use and lock the same resources, each process preventing the completion of the other process. This becomes a deadlock in the software and can be quite frustrating and challenging to pursue.This could be a design tendency or a bug. As a design tendency, its best to see if there is anything further that development can do to mitigate this.For an issue example, a payment posting process occurs and needs to update a payment related table. Meanwhile, a user is charging a credit card in Sales Order, also interacting with payments. The first process needs to look at and update records in the payment table, meanwhile the second process needs to look at and add records to the same table in order to complete its work.Both processes have various types of locks on the same table and this becomes a deadlock due to the timing. SQL has a process of its own that will check for deadlocks and break this up, so one process is the deadlock winner and one is the deadlock victim.This diagram is representative of the example issue above, and something SQL can provide us:
In the KB, "Navigating SQL Deadlocks in Support" we learn that the workstation's AppData log may provide information about this, as does SQL's own Deadlock Report. We'll explore the deadlock report to help explain how you can dig into this further for any deadlocks you encounter.

Resolution
Let's start with a disclaimer, deadlocks can be quite tricky and its likely we'll need to involve more technical resources or programmers to investigate this issue. This KB is meant to provide more knowledge on the Deadlock Report and guide us on what we can obtain if we do need to escalate. If you are working on a case and it might be a deadlock, attempt to get a copy of this information as soon as possible as the report could overwrite and become lost.

How can I access the report?
The Deadlock report is part of SQL's system health extended events. You can also have an extended event created that explicitly looks for the deadlock report, however it's likely customers will simply have the system health event and have it enabled.

Navigate to SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) and log in to the SQL instance.
Expand the instance and navigate to Management > Extended Events > Sessions > system_health


Double click on package0.event_file to view the health events.

Navigate to the time of the issue:



In the grid section, the details tab contains the XML report. Click in the value to open this as a new query tab in SSMS or copy that into an enhanced notpad such as NotePad++. NotePad++ as an XML formatting plugin that may make this easier for you to read.
The deadlock tab contains a diagram of the deadlock. Both of these are helpful in their own right, especially for those who appreciate visuals.
We'll explore both of these more below in a case example.

Note: If the extended event is not running, perhaps someone decided to turn it off without realizing what it logs, then nothing will get trapped to report on for the event you are looking for. There may be some information in the workstation's app log but it will not contain the detail of the Deadlock Report.

Parts of the Deadlock Report
The deadlock report contains quite a bit of information. It is split into three sections: the Victim list, Process list, and Resource list. All of the information contained here will help you work a case. It might give you more insight into what you need to test to replicate an issue. It might supplement activity logs and the SM audit. It might point you to a workstation or specific process that is routinely an issue. Whatever the case, this will provide more details to you.

Victim List
This section is short and sweet, providing the ID of the victim, for use later in the report.


Process List
The process list contains information about the victim and winner processes, we'll break this into chunks for review.

To start, you'll see the ID is the victim process ID. All of this information can be helpful, but some of the more immediately useful things are lock mode, spid, hostname, and times.

The lock mode will tell you what type of lock the process is requesting.

The spid is the session ID for the process. It will help tie the deadlock to other areas, like a user session if looking at event viewer from a workstation or server. If you found the appdata log pointing to a deadlock this ID also ties to that log. It helps tie this event to other things you have found to help corroborate a deadlock for your issue.

The hostname is the machine the issue occurred on. This simply helps confirm the event you are looking at came from the machine you encountered the issue on.

We'll look at the remaining portion of the victim process list:

First, we have the execution stack, displaying what context on what code was executing at the time of the deadlock.
In our example "adhoc" is indicating that the SQL code was submitted directly, rather than as say a SQL procedure. File this away for an escalation to a programmer for the most part.

Next is the actual SQL statement at the time of the deadlock. This is more fuel for an escalation for a programmer to review.
Outside of programming, we may use this to anticipate what else was going on at the time to try and replicate the issue.
We might be using a decompiler to look at the code, or possibly debugging things depending on the scenario we're dealing with, and maybe seeing this hit tells us more about what exactly was going on. So perhaps its usable to try and better audit the steps taken leading to the issue. That last part might not be as practical but an option none the less.

Now we'll move on to the winner's process section. Its going to look similar to the victim process, only with information about the winner process:


What do we do with this part? Audit with it! Let's look at it this way, a user called in with a case where their credit card didn't process, just stopped like magic. So we have details about that side of things, but what we don't quite know is what else was running that was related to this, and caused the deadlock. Now that we have more information about the winner process, we can try to audit that side of things and hopefully replicate the issue or explain it.  Worst case, it is programmer fuel in an escalation.

Resource List
The Resource List section helps tie the room together. You will find lock objects in here: the types of locks held and the types requested. This is more helpful to programmers looking at this matter, but it still gives any one else some insight. You will notice the lock types look a little funny, Microsoft has some documentation on this with more detail but here is what some of them mean:

- S (Shared)
- For reading operations of a page or row.
- Multiple S locks can coexist.
- Other transactions cannot modify the record while the lock is active.

- X (Exclusive)
- For writing operations of a page or row.
- Only one allowed on a resource.
- Page or row is reserved exclusively for the transaction, as long as that transaction holds the lock. (SQL transaction, not Traverse Global/ProcessPro Global transaction here.)

- U (Update)
- For writing operations but more flexible.
- Update can be imposed on a record already in a shared lock. Once the transaction is ready to update it changes into an exclusive lock.
- Update can be imposed on a shared lock, a shared lock cannot be imposed on an update lock.

- I (Intent)
- Transaction informs another transaction of intention to acquire a lock. Part of the hierarchical system.
- Other transactions cannot obtain an exclusive lock on it if intent exists.
- SQL's database engine will inspect intent locks at the table level to ensure locks acquired in a safe manner.

- IS (Intent Shared)
- Signals to SQL that the transaction intends to read lower level resources by aquiring a shared lock individually on the resources.

- IX (Intent Exclusive)
- Signals to SQL that it intends to modify a lower level resource with an exclusive lock individually on those resources.

- IU (Intent Update)
- Signals  to SQL that it intends to acquire shared locks on lower level resources as shared locks. Then IU is acquired at the page level when the update takes place and converts it to IX.

- SIX (Shared Intent Exclusive)
- Signals that the transaction intends to read all resources at a lower level and acquire a shared lock on all resources of the lower level, modify some of those and acquire an intent exclusive lock on the lower resources that should be modified.
- In short the SIX lock locks a table and acquires Intent Exclusive locks and exclusive locks to interact with the rows within.

- SIU (Shared Intent Update)
- Signals SQL for shared lock on resources with the intent to update them.

- UIX (Update Intent Exclusive)
- Signals SQL with an update lock and intent exclusive lock at lower resources, and UIX lock occurs at the table level.

There are some other lock types but we'll hold here for now.

Here is the section for our case example for the CC charge and AR Cash Receipt Post at the same time:

Remember the victim ID and the winner processes ID? Use those here to reference the content in this section.

We can see that the winner process holds a SIX lock on tblSmExchRateTrans and the victim process wants an IX lock on it. Meanwhile the victim process has an X lock on tblSoTransPmt while the winner process wants a U lock on it.

So what do we do with this information. We have some options, this could be a great scenario to pose to a developer via an escalation. "Here is what occurred, this is what I see from the audit, what can you tell me about this?" It might be enough information to get us in a spot where we can replicate this and write it up as a bug. It may come to be that this is part of the process and maybe we need to enhance the software to make it handle this better.

In this case example, I was able to have some great dialogue with our developers about the scenario and they were willing to make some changes to avoid occurrences like this. They needed all of this information and more understanding of the scenario, but once they had this things moved rapidly towards a conclusion.

Parts of the Deadlock Diagram

Aside from the Deadlock Report, we also receive a visual of the deadlock scenario. Now that we have discussed the type of locks, the below should add some clarity to the case example's deadlock.

The circle on the left shows the deadlock victim. This is the process that was terminated via the deadlock process.
The circle on the right represents the winner process. This process was allowed to move forward through the deadlock process.
The center boxes contain information about the deadlock. We see the struggle with tblSoTransPmt but no mention of tblSmExchangeRateTrans, we're getting information about the winner's resource in that box.
The arrow direction indicates who is waiting and who is blocking. In the above example, server process ID 154 is in request mode IX and

So as you can see, it still is helpful, but doesn't include all the detail the report has. Remember, this information may not be perfect and may be only so helpful, but we can escalate and work with our programming resources to dig at this further.

0fe3537f-21e2-4cfd-9c7d-d9e7825ca49e.title: Verifying Assemblies in Traverse Global/ProcessPro Global
0fe3537f-21e2-4cfd-9c7d-d9e7825ca49e.content:
Problem
A time may arise where you are dealing with a mismatch and need to review what assemblies are in use so you can investigate further. Perhaps a customer just updated and things are mostly working except when they enter a new SO Order? Maybe a customer reported an issue and it works fine for you, but you need their client and data to review the differences, what do you look for?

Resolution
Verifying the assemblies in use, and the assemblies that should be in use, are a good way to check for issues. One thing to consider is the environment in use, is it really up to date or at the build that it is supposed to be? Users forget to apply a server update or the client side update, strange things can happen, files can get corrupted or quarantined during updates. This also applies to customizations.

If you test something and it works fine for you but not the customer, consider a check of the 'Program Info' to see the version of what is loaded up and compare that to the customer's environment. Here is the 'Program Info' after several things have been used in the software:

Its a lot to take in, right? There's even one more page to scroll through that is not in the shot above. You can clear this list by simply logging out and back in, then go straight to the function you need and do what you need to. That will load everything up in to the 'Program Info' section. It should be more manageable, but more important, now it only includes assemblies related to what you are looking at:


Okay, so we saw these screenshots, how does this help? Let's say that scenario where SO Orders is throwing strange errors on build 25143 but it is not throwing errors for you. You could quickly check what version is loaded up for you, knowing you are updated, and then check that against what the customer has on their screen. If the numbers are different and they are supposed to be on build 25143, you know they don't have the correct assembly in place. This idea also applies to ProcessPro Global assemblies and custom assemblies.

Quick note, yes the assemblies have the build number in them, if you find a customer has the current build number it may still benefit you to verify what the current assembly version is. What if an issue arose with this assembly after a build release and development quickly issued a new one for the build. If you were to simply look at the number, it says 25143, and you stop looking, maybe there was a newer one issued.

One last note before we move on here, there could be multiple files you need to check and we'll talk about that much further below. If you are a fan of NotePad++ their compare plugin really helps with a compare of a customer's Program Info dump vs yours.

Let's take things further. If you question a customer having the correct files, you could review the assemblylist.xml file in their updates folder. That will help set some expectations as to what has been deployed in their environment for vanilla updates. So let's say we checked the program info and it says Traverse.Client.SalesOrder.dll is loaded and its version is 12.2.25143.2288, but it seems a little off still. We can go check the updates folder quick and see this is the version of the file per build update 25143:

You can also compare this to what you are running in your vanilla environment for the same build. We also have a shared VM with some older builds that you may use to review this for older builds.

You can also check for the file version in the client folder to see an assembly version of a specific DLL, in this example Traverse.Client.SalesOrder.dll.

Right-click on the file and view the properties:

Something still weird? Maybe there is some sort of a reason the file you are looking for doesn't have a version, or the version doesn't make sense, try a decomplier:


In all, this is a great way to find out the files in play are not correct. What if there are multiple files? We've had prior cases where a new anti-virus software quarantined a set of files but not all. In that case, you could try checking for client-side updates to see what it thinks it needs. The update process should check the client folder and compare it to the assemblylist.xml file in the updates folder.

A good strategy here is NotePad++ again. There is a compare plugin available in that software that you can use to compare your Program Info to the customer's Program Info when they hit their issue. You can grab their info when in a screenshare, or if you have client and data backups restored use that. Then just compare to a vanilla environment doing the same things so the same stuff is loaded.

If it ends up more complex, we can always reach out to a programmer as an escalation and see what they can tell us to look for.

To make a final note in this document, customizations should have a version and likely do. So custom assemblies could also be reviewed like the above. You won't be able to compare a customer to your environment since you don't have their modifications loaded up on your vanilla environment. You can view the assemblylistcustom.xml file in their updates folder and look at the dates and versions of the files in there compared to the client folder of the customer for the assembly/assemblies in question.

15a3e8b4-8a4f-469f-96c4-91c43a1b5b73.title: How To Approve Time on My Cell Phone

My Supervisors want to know if they can approve employees leave time on their cell phone.

How To Approve Time on My Cell Phone

Question: Is there any way to approve employees' leave time on my cell phone?

On-Time Web provides Supervisors and Company Administrators with the ability to approve time using their smartphones. When someone submits a Leave Request, an email is sent to their Supervisor and/or the Company administrator. Then they can follow the steps below.

514bb4a7-5078-462d-8e03-e8c0bdc3ab07.title: GL Account Invalid for Purchase Order Transaction
514bb4a7-5078-462d-8e03-e8c0bdc3ab07.content:
Problem
When trying to save a PO Transaction, the user is getting a prompt that says the GL Account is invalid for the Transaction.

Resolution
There are a number of GL accounts that are associated with a Purchase Order, beyond the ones that are initially most visible. Follow these steps to look through the various GL accounts associated with the order.

Confirm whether the GL Accounts that are listed for the line items on the PO Transaction are Active by clicking on the ellipse (...) for the GL Account column as below,

If those GL accounts are all active, then check the Accrual accounts.

Right click on any of the Column header to pull up the Column chooser> Drag and drop the column Accrual Acct



Now you can see if the error is caused because of the Accrual account being Inactive



If the Accrual account is Inactive, you would need to select an Active Accrual account or make the Inactive one active to resolve the problem.



If the issue is not the Accrual account either, another place to look is in the System Manager > Company Setup > Business Rules, where you can also verify that all of the Default GL Accounts listed there are active as well.  If a GL account listed there is inactive, update it to an active account, or re-activate it.





Finally, if all these are fine, you can also check to ensure that the GL Accounts setup for the tax location are active as well.

Find the Tax Group ID that is listed on the Totals tab of the Purchase Order.

Go to System Manager > Tax Setup > Tax Location Groups to find the specific Tax Locations that are associated with the Tax Group ID you noted on the Purchase Order.



Go to System Manager > Tax Setup > Tax Locations and look up each of the tax locations that are included in the Tax Group. Look at the GL Accounts that are associated with the tax locations to ensure that they are still active.

Once you have found the Inactive GL account and replace it with the active GL account, you will be able to continue processing the transaction.

b5f564d5-7e8a-4b1c-bbfe-fbb01e0a5e72.title: GL STATEMENT LAYOUT changes
b5f564d5-7e8a-4b1c-bbfe-fbb01e0a5e72.content:
Problem
When running  income statement for a particular month, the column that is supposed to give the year to date totals are the same as month to date totals.

Resolution
The above-described problem is due to the GL Statement layout settings set to print month-to-date totals instead of year-to-date.

- Log in to Traverse. Click on Applications -- General Ledger -- Management Reports -- Financial Statements.
- Select the desired Statement ID from the ID drop-down that is having issues with printing year-to-date values.
- Double click on the Statement ID that appeared in the ID field to launch the GL Statements screen.
- On the GL Statements screen, double click on Layout ID in the Layout ID field to launch the GL Statement Layouts screen.
- On the GL Statement Layout screen, adjust the As of When and How Far Back fields for the applicable columns to get the desired results to appear when the Financial statement is generated.
- Below are the available options to setup a layout for As of When and How Far Back fields.

- As of When

Current Period - Activity for the current period.
Previous Period - Activity for the previous period.
Previous Quarter - Activity for the previous quarter.
Period Relative to Current - Activity for a period relative to the period you select at print time.
YTD Relative to Current - Year-to-date balance relative to the period you select at print time.
Year Relative to Current - Activity for the period/year select at print time (you can also use the How Far Back field to determine the year).
TYD Year Relative to Current - Year-to-date balance relative to the year you select at print time (you can also use the How Far Back field to determine the year).
Year-End Balance - Year-end balance regardless of the row type you select.

- How Far Back

This Period Only Use balance information for only the period selected.
Quarter-To-date Use the quarter-to-date balance.
Year-To-date Use the year-to-date balance. The year-to-date balance is the sum of the changes in the balances in every period through the one specified in the As of When field and the beginning balance.



If you selected Period Rel Cur or YTD Rel Cur in the As of When field, you can select Current Period or a number from the range of periods you are using (for example, enter 1 for the corresponding balance information from one period back, 2 for two periods back, 3 for three periods back, and so on).

If you selected Period Rel Cur or Ytd Rel Cur, the amounts from the last-year column are used if you go back more periods than are in the current year. The system checks to see whether you are using the period after your last period for normal processing, which you indicated in the Business Rules function. Suppose you have a 12-period accounting system. You are in period 8 and you want to print information from 9 periods back. If you are using period 13 for normal processing, the amount from period 12 is printed; otherwise, the amount from period 11 is printed.

If you selected Year Relative to Current or YTD Year Relative to Current, you can select either Next Year (to view budgets and forecasts for the upcoming year) or a number for the range of years you are using (for example, enter 1 for corresponding balance information from one year back relative to the year chosen at print time, 2 for two years back, 3 for three years back, and so on)

If you selected Year-End Balance the How Far Back field is deactivated and you can not enter anything in the field.

In the above situation change How far back from field to Year to date instead of This period only fixes the issue.

b9738d7c-858b-4794-ae98-15c2807585cc.title: How to Resolve Sales Order Line Re-Sequencing Issue
b9738d7c-858b-4794-ae98-15c2807585cc.content:
Problem
A specific user reported that the re-sequencing functionality in the Sales Order screen was not working for them. They could not re-order their line items on a Sales Order. However, other users were able to perform re-sequencing without any issues. This indicated that the problem was isolated to the individual user's environment or preferences.

Resolution
The issue occurred because the affected user had set the line entries in the Sales Order screen to be sorted in descending order. This sorting prevented the user from re-sequencing the lines.





To resolve the issue, the user should right-click on any of the column headers to bring up the menu, then select the "Clear Sorting" option. This will remove the applied sorting and allow the re-sequencing functionality to work as expected.



Note: The Clear Sorting option becomes available only when the entries have been sorted in either ascending or descending order.

Once the sorting has been cleared, the user should now be able to re-sequence their line items.

5b67ff3e-689b-4509-8c3f-beae2ae3faa2.title: How to pull the record of Customer's pending balance through Statements?
5b67ff3e-689b-4509-8c3f-beae2ae3faa2.content:
Problem
How to pull the record of Customer's pending balance through Statements?

Resolution
The Print Statements function in the Accounts Receivable module is used to generate customer statements that reflect transactional activity and current balances.

These statements assist in communicating outstanding obligations and can be printed either on statement forms or plain paper, depending on the configuration set in the Business Rules function.



Instructions to generate a Statement:

Navigate to the AR Print Statements screen, under the path: Applications -> Accounts Receivable -> Open Invoices -> Print Statements



i. Data Filtering:

- We can utilize the Data Filter to narrow down the range of data included in the customer statements. This is useful when wanting to create a statement for just one customer, for instance.
- If no filter is applied, all available data will be included by default.



ii. Date Selection:

- Closing Date: In the Closing field, we need to specify the date by which payment is expected. This date will be printed on the statement as the closing date.
- Statement Date: Set the Statement field to the date used for aging invoices. This determines how invoice balances will be categorized (e.g., Current, 30 days, 60 days, etc.).
- Cutoff Date: Use the Cutoff field to define the last date for invoice inclusion. Invoices dated after the cutoff will be excluded from the generated statements.



iii. Print Selection:

In the Print section, the user needs to choose the appropriate customer grouping to determine whose statements will be printed:

-
-
All Customers: Includes all customers configured with "Statements" or "Both" in the Stmt/Invoices setting in customer setup.

-
All Customers With Activity: Includes customers with open invoices only.

-
With Nonzero Balances: Includes customers whose account balances are not zero (includes both positive and negative balances).

-
With Positive Balances: Includes customers who owe outstanding payments (positive balances).

-
With Balances 30+ Days Old: Includes customers whose balances are at least 30 days old, including 60- and 90-day balances.

-
With Balances 60+ Days Old: Includes customers with balances 60 days or older (also includes 90-day balances).

-
With Balances 90+ Days Old: Includes only those customers whose outstanding balances are over 90 days old.

Note that any applied filters added in the top data filtering section will further limit the group that is selected to only those included in the filter.

iv. YTD Finance Charges:
If needed, we can enable the YTD Finance Charge checkbox, so that the year-to-date finance charges will be displayed on the statements.



v. Sorting Criteria:
In the Sort By section, we can select the criteria by which the customer statements will be sorted (e.g., by Customer ID, Name, or Zip Code).



vi. Dunning Messages
Traverse allows us to modify the Dunning Messages section as needed.

[By default, the messages configured in the Message – Statement Dunning section under Accounts Receivable Business Rules will be prefilled here.]



**Note: The Customer Statement will show those transactions that have been marked as "Released" in the Hold/Release Invoice screen. The Statement will NOT show those transactions that have been marked as on "Hold." This allows for greater control regarding what lines show on the Statement, but also needs to be checked to ensure the correct information is included on the Statement.

dda011da-6291-4362-8d56-5ff7b2be01fa.title: Change UOM in inventory

The client needs to change the UOM of the inventory

-

1a087edd-35c7-4f62-9a44-5713179c5956.title: Reports in OTW
1a087edd-35c7-4f62-9a44-5713179c5956.content:
Problem
Users are unable to view the actual clock-in and clock-out times for employees, as the time summary report automatically rounds entries to the nearest quarter hour. A need was identified for a report or option that displays the exact badge swipe times to ensure accurate time tracking and auditing.

Resolution
Yes, it is possible to view the actual clock-in and clock-out times within the report. To do this, please ensure that the “Show Actual Time” checkbox is selected when generating the report. This option allows the system to display the precise timestamps for each entry—reflecting the exact times employees clocked in and out—rather than rounding to the nearest increment.

This setting is especially helpful when you need to audit detailed time records or verify activity during specific time windows.

Problem
'5.7.1 Unable to Relay’ code error generally occurs when the user tries to send emails outside his domain.

Causes for the error: The outgoing mail server could not identify the sender. There are some issues while authenticating the sender on the server, and thus restricting them from sending emails. The receiver domain’s recipient policy has imposed restrictions on the sender’s domain / department. The Exchange Database is corrupt. A properly configured mail server is extremely restrictive with relaying, to prevent it from being abused by spammers to send mails. So, that's a config issue in the mail server. It doesn't allow you (your IP, your sender address) to send mail to the recipient.

Cause
The outgoing mail server could not identify the sender. There are some issues while authenticating the sender on the server and thus restricting them to send emails. The receiver domain’s recipient policy has imposed restrictions on the sender’s domain / department. The Exchange Database is corrupt. A properly configured mail server is extremely restrictive with relaying, to prevent it from being abused by spammers to send mails. So, That's a config issue in the mail servier. It doesn't allow you (your IP, your sender address) to send mail to the recipient.

This is a problem the company's IT should fix. However, you might try some of these steps below.

Open IIS Manager

Or open "Internet Information Services (IIS) Manager" from Administrative Tools.

-
Navigate to the SMTP Virtual Server

In the left pane, expand:

[Server Name] → SMTP Server → Default SMTP Virtual Server

Right-click on Default SMTP Virtual Server, and click Properties.

-
Go to the Access Tab

-
Click on the Access tab at the top of the Properties window.

-
Set Relay Restrictions

-
Click the "Relay..." button under the Relay Restrictions section.

-

-
Allow Only the Listed IPs

-
In the Relay Restrictions dialog:

Choose: "Only the list below"

-
Click Add → select:

-
Single Computer if you want to add a specific IP

Group of Computers for a subnet

Enter the IP address(es) allowed to relay.

Example:

Confirm and Apply

Click OK, then Apply, then OK again to close all dialogs.

516a4ff1-116c-41d4-8152-796e65543c32.title: How to process an AR external payment
516a4ff1-116c-41d4-8152-796e65543c32.content:
Problem
How to process payment or refund through external payment.

Resolution
Go to Accounts Receivable > Transaction > External Payments

1) Select the Customer ID for whom we need to process the payment/refund.

2) Select the Batch code, PO number if available and fill in the payment dates.

3) Select the payment type: either Payment or Refund.

4) Check the box(es) next to the invoice number(s) to they payment will pay off. If you type in a payment amount and do not select an invoice, the payment will be added to their account rather than paying off an invoice.

5) Click "OK" at the top.

See below for reference:

Once you click, OK, this brings up the external payments pop up screen where you can select the payment service like Vantiv, ApteanPay, etc.

You can add a new card by clicking the check box "Use New Card" and clicking OK. This will bring up a new box to enter the Credit Card details. You can also uncheck that box and click on the "New" button in the bottom box to enter a new card.  If needed, you can choose to delete a card here by clicking the "Delete" button in this box.

Once a card has been entered and selected, click OK at the top.

This will process the payment/refund.

Once the Payment/Refund is processed Traverse will show a receipt:



The transaction will now show up in the Cash Receipt screen in the batch you selected as a non-editable cash receipt to be posted. If you receive an error when processing the payment, go to the Process External Payments screen to review and process the transaction.

0f7be26a-6cfa-4c98-9702-3b076b7cb876.title: How to create Finance Charges for specific Customers on their past due Invoices
0f7be26a-6cfa-4c98-9702-3b076b7cb876.content:
Problem
How to create Finance Charges for specific Customers on their past due Invoices.

Resolution
Finance Charges are a fee that can be charged to customers for not paying their bills on time.  Here is the process for configuring this in Traverse, along with instructions on how to assess these charges in Traverse.

- Set up Business Rules specific to finance charges under System Manager> Company Setup> Business Rules ~ AR - Accounts Receivable.
- Specify the Finance Charge Account, which is the General Ledger revenue account to which the Finance charges are posted.
- Specify the Description - Invoice Descriptions for Finance Charge, which will be displayed in the Ageing report and on statements.
- Specify the Finance Charge Date as either Invoice Date or Due Date.
- Specify the Finance Charge Days, which is the number of days past the due/invoice date at which the customer is eligible for finance charges.
- Specify the Finance Charge Minimum. This amount will be used if the calculated finance charge is not greater than this amount. For example, if you enter 1.00 as a minimum and a customer had a finance charge calculated of .75 they would be charged 1.00 as a finance charge.
- Specify the Finance Charge Percent.

- To specify the customer eligible for Finance Charges,
- Accounts Receivable> Setup and Maintenance> Customers
- Call up the customer> under the Default tab > check mark the Finance Charge and Save.

- To Calculate Finance charges,
- After All payments, Credits and Invoices have been posted for the month. Go into Accounts Receivable> Open Invoices> Calculate Finance Charges.
- Enter Month End Date for the Statement Date and click Ok.



- Print Statements from Accounts Receivable> Open Invoices> Print Statements

- To Post the Finance Charges,
- Run the AR Periodic Maintenance - Perform General Periodic Process in Accounts Receivable> Periodic Processing> Periodic Maintenance to post the finance charges to General Ledger and to customer accounts.

- The Perform General Periodic Process will age all customers, update credit status, update finance charges, compare balances, synchronize the customer balance with outstanding invoices, and clear sales reps' period-to-date totals.

- The amount that was in the New Finance Charges filed on the balance tab will move to Unpaid Finance charges.

ce722b75-603f-4f07-ba47-5f9543e87dcb.title: Navigating SQL Deadlocks in Support
ce722b75-603f-4f07-ba47-5f9543e87dcb.content:
Problem
A time may arise in the software where two processes use and lock the same resources, each process preventing the completion of the other process. This becomes a deadlock in the software and can be quite frustrating and challenging to pursue.

This could be a design tendency or a bug. As a design tendency, its best to see if there is anything further that development can do to mitigate this.

For an issue example, a payment posting process occurs and needs to update a  payment related table. Meanwhile, a user is charging a credit card in Sales Order, also interacting with payments. The first process needs to look at and update records in the payment table, meanwhile the second process needs to look at and add records to the same table in order to complete its work.
Both processes have various types of locks on the same table and this becomes a deadlock due to the timing. SQL has a process of its own that will check for deadlocks and break this up, so one process is the deadlock winner and one is the deadlock victim.

This diagram is representative of the example issue above, and something SQL can provide us:
Let's move to the next section to see how we can obtain more information and what we can do with this.

Resolution
Let's start with a disclaimer, it is likely a more senior or advanced resource is required in order to investigate this issue as it entails some work with XML, SQL, and at times a deeper level of understanding of the software. This KB is meant to provide more knowledge on what we can obtain and look for when this type of issue occurs.



What can we do?
There are two things support resources can obtain and review for deadlocks. There can actually be more than things but we will focus on the two most obtainable things available to us:

- Workstation AppData Log
- SQL's Deadlock Report

Both of these will provide some additional details around what occurred to cause the deadlock. This information may be used in conjunction with SM Audit Explorer information from Traverse Global or ProcessPro Global to better determine steps taken to cause an issue. In turn, we can use that to develop tests to replicate the issue, with or without customer data, and provide more pertinent details to additional resources if the case is escalated.

Let's make an honorary mention of the SM Audit Explorer. While deadlock information will not be found here, this function may be key in your investigation of a deadlock. The audit information contained here can be used to piece together a timeline of events and processes that may help indicate what occurred so you can replicate the issue.



Workstation AppData Log:

There is an XML application log kept on the machines that run Traverse Global or ProcessPro Global that can keep error details. If a customer receives an error referencing a deadlock, there is likely something in the log file for it on the machine that experienced the deadlock.
This log is also useful for scenarios where a user reports an error but did not take a screenshot, missed the details of the message, and we may have the ability to obtain this through the log.

To access the log, on the machine that experienced the issue, navigate to C:\ProgramData\Open Systems, Inc\Traverse Global\[SYS database name here]
The file is named "TraverseGlobal.log"

There may also be an log file at C:\ProgramData\Open Systems, Inc\TRAVERSE.Global\[SYS database name here]
The file is named "TraverseGlobal.log"

Once obtained, search the log file for the word deadlock in the timeframe of the issue. If there are multiple errors you can look for the correct time, this will be in UTC. Factor in adjusting for timezone (EST vs. CST for example.)

What do you do with this once you find something? Look for the message tags for a capture of the issue: <message></message> and review what is between those. for example:
"<Message>Transaction (Process ID 93) was deadlocked on lock resources with another process and has been chosen as the deadlock victim. Rerun the transaction.</Message>"
Having the Process ID also allows you to look at other logs, like the event viewer, and check for any issues with that process.

After the message section is a stack trace: <StackTrace> </StackTrace>. This might not be directly helpful, but it can help indicate what was in use at the time of the issue. If escalated, this could help a programmer get a better picture. Also, if one workstation hit the issue more than others, it could point you in the direction of some files to check to make sure they have the correct version of those files.
You can confirm what files are loaded when running the process in the Traverse Global or ProcessPro Global client and then looking at the Help > Program Info for the version. You can compare that to the file from the client folder in use, sometimes in the file properties. If its unavailable there, you can use a decompiler to load up one of the related assemblies from the list in it and verify the version of that file.

You may also see an additional message as an exception, with the deadlock information, or depending on the circumstances, simply other information about the event. You may have an additional stack trace after that noting the loaded assemblies. Again, all of this can be helpful to programmers if escalated, it might be helpful to support's own investigation.

Lastly, all of this information helps paint you a picture of what a user was doing, and supplements things like the SM Audit Explorer's results.
This log file will likely not resolve the issue with the information it contains, but it is a piece of the puzzle. It may be enough information to drive you to collect the deadlock report, or it might lead you to scrutinize the program files in use, check update history and make sure the proper files are in place. It might be enough information to direct you to develop additional tests with or without customer data to replicate the issue.

SQL's Deadlock Report:
The Deadlock report is part of SQL's system health extended events. You can also have an extended event created that explicitly looks for the deadlock report, however it's likely customers will simply have the system health event and have it enabled. If this is not running, perhaps someone decided to turn it off without realizing what it logs, then nothing will get trapped to report on for the event you are looking for.
If you are working on a case and it might be a deadlock, attempt to get a copy of this information as soon as possible as the report could overwrite and become lost.

What is this report? It's awesome. The Deadlock Report contains process information as to the cause of a deadlock. You'll get a diagram of the deadlock noting when process was the victim, what it was doing, what process was the winner, and what it was doing. The report also gives you an XML output with broken down into areas of highlight: victim list, process list, and resource list.

The victim list identifies what the process was that was the victim. Clean cut and easy to see. We can use that info for the Process List.

The Process List identifies the processes involved. You can find more information about the deadlock victim process and the deadlock winner process in this section. There will be information like the Process ID, the workstation, the lock mode so you can understand what it was attempting to do, and more detailed information about the literal process it was trying to run.

The Resource List provides additional information about the resources involved in the deadlock. Here, you can find details around the objects that are locked, the type of lock they hold, and the type of lock the program is trying to obtain.

This information will give more feedback about what is going on and also lead you to more testing that you can do. By reviewing the victim and winner process, you can see where things went awry and use that with the SM Audit to recreate the scenarios that lead to the deadlock. It might not be easy but it will certainly point you in a direction that you can work through. Its also good to talk with the programmers about what you see as the victim and winner processes as they may have more insight as to what was going on in the code at that time. That may lead to replicating the issue, or they may see something that helps the case.

Closure
To bring things together, you may still be wondering what to do with all of this information. The answer is that it all depends on what you find and see. Everything you have collected may be for an escalation to collaborate with a programming resource and potentially an IT resource. It may give you more of a direction on where to look for issues, maybe there is a bug or customization issue at hand and this information helps point you there. The best next step is to look at what you have and see how it fits with everything going on and determine if you can replicate any issues because of it, or need a deeper analysis.

There is an additional KB available that will discuss the SQL Deadlock Report at a deeper level with more of a case example to it to try and help with guidance on this matter. See the KB "Troubleshooting With the SQL Deadlock Report."

d87e5049-9e69-4449-a84a-b3738aa1b635.title: SQL Profiler for Support - General
d87e5049-9e69-4449-a84a-b3738aa1b635.content:
Problem
An issue may arise that requires deeper analysis on the SQL side. Perhaps a user is getting a SQL error when executing SO Orders, SQL Profiler can help track down what is running and tell you what to look for.

What is SQL Profiler? It is a Microsoft Tool that captures SQL related information based on processes running on the SQL instance you are logged in to. It is excellent to use with SQL heavy processes in the software, like server update processes, report processes, post processes, and interactive views. It may give insight to the software's processes without debugging or using a decompiler, but that can depend on the software design you are tracking down. For the SQL heavy processes, it also trap parameters used so you can see exactly how something is running, and use that to run it yourself for troubleshooting purposes.

In this article, we'll talk about the basics of Profiler and setting up a trace. There will be additional KBs to show a basic example of use and more advanced methods of use.

Disclaimer, this is an internal KB meant for resources that have SQL experience and can wield it as a tool. It also helps having experience and knowledge of the software's tables to best use Profiler as a tool.

Resolution
Navigating SQL Profiler
SQL profiler can be launched from either the start menu with SQL's tools or if you are in SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) it can be launched from the Tools menu in the toolbar. The login screen will appear first and is the same credentials you would use if logging in to SSMS.

Once you are in, a new Trace Properties window appears getting you ready to start a trace.

If you wish you can give it a Trace Name, if you choose to save the trace it will use this name.
You can also choose the template you wish to use, more information further down in this document.
You can also save the trace to a file or save it to a table, these are optional.
You can also configure a stop time for the trace.

We also have the Events Selection tab which we will discuss with the templates below.

A quick note, the toolbar shares similar functions to the icons below them. This is where you can create new traces, new templates, open previous traces as a file or from a table. You also have other options to view and search for information in the trace window as you work with it. Some options are inactive until you have a trace loaded up or in process.

SQL Profiler Templates
Profiler uses templates to determine the kind of information to trap while the trace is playing. There are a few pre-loaded templates that help jump start the process or you may create your own depending on your needs. Since our software uses Transact SQL or T-SQL, those templates are ideal for our product.

If you're not sure exactly what you really need to look for, the TSQL template is a great one to use and it might serve your needs frequently.
The TSQL Duration template can help in evaluation of performance issues, however it is only as helpful as the processes. Profiler is great at trapping SQL information but when SQL is not solely in use it may only contain so much information.
There is more that could be said about the other templates and a good resource is Microsoft's own publication on the templates. In place of a link that may become outdated, searching for Microsoft SQL Profiler Templates will get you to the right place.

You can see what the template is going to gather in the Events Selection tab. Once you have picked your trace template, click on the Event Selection to confirm what you wish to use in your trace. Here is an example for the TSQL template:

In the Events Selection screen you have the option to choose not to capture certain things. For example, many users choose to uncheck Audit Login and Audit Logout, and maybe even the ExistingConnection events to reduce the bloat in the results. If you look at this with other templates you will see these change, so if you are unsure what you want to see or not, it is best to review the template and see what in it meets your needs.

Basic Use
We will cover more practical use in additional KBs, but before we break let's talk about basic use.
A case comes in and a user can't Post SO Orders. Fret not, profiler might get us an answer, possibly very quickly to resolve the case in record time. Profiler can present a challenge for production environments, it has a cost to the server that could cause some performance and it also can trap too much information since so much can be running at one time in a production environment. You will be time ahead if you obtain a company and SYS backup, client folder, and run this in your own environment to use profiler. If you do this, you have a command of what is coming through your trace.

Once you have customer data loaded up, cleared all sensitive items like credit card processing configurations, document delivery configurations, etc. you can proceed to run a trace. You need the software open and ready to go. If it is an SO Transaction Post, have everything loaded up on screen ready to click OK to post.

Next, log in to Profiler and choose your trace template, maybe its just the TSQL one, maybe you do remove some of those bloating events, and then click Run.

Once the trace is running, processed to post. Once the error has been encountered, stop the trace. You can also choose to pause this, its better to stop it so you don't accidentally start it again and more information gets trapped that is irrelevant.

Now that you have your trace in hand you can see what SQL was doing up to the point of the error. What do you do with this? Typically you will read through it and it will give you the temporary tables, SQL procedures and other pertinent items that you can put together in SSMS and run to step through the issue. Best put, it all sets you up so you can step through the issue, but in an organized way. Since Profiler also gives you the parameters in which a stored procedure is run, you will have everything you need to set this up in a SQL query and run. From there, you need to run what you find and analyze where an issue may be.

For example in our SO Transaction Post, perhaps there is an invalid item in play. Perhaps someone was in teh tables and changed an item to a non-lotted item, but the post process finds lot numbers or blank lot numbers and errors there. Profiler will give you what is running so that you can run it and pick at the tables the data is coming from to find that issue.

See "SQL Profiler Troubleshooting - Basic Example of Use " for the next level of information on Profiler and how to use it with a more basic example.

a1fce82e-7771-4c57-97fc-63377627e725.title: Design Studio - How to Add Custom View to Traverse Menu
a1fce82e-7771-4c57-97fc-63377627e725.content:
Problem
A user prepares a completely custom view using Design Studio, how do we actually use this in Traverse Global or ProcessPro Global? This document will tackle just that, adding a custom view to the menu and granting permissions to it.

In the example below, we have already created a custom view in Design Studio and are ready to add this and set permissions.

Resolution
The new custom view can be added wherever you wish. In our example, we'll place our new view with the System Manager Audit views.

The first step is to access System Manager > Setup and Maintenance > Application Menus.

Once you are here, expand the area of the menu where you wish to add the view. In our case, we'll move within the Application Menus function, expand System Manager and click on System Audit:

Click new record/plus sign button to create a new record where we can add our view.

Click new record/plus sign button to create a new record where we can add our view. Here you can see the entry already made, we'll examine this more below here.

The Description is exactly what will be read by other users on the menu. The name should be meaningful and easy to determine what the function is.

The Type must be View. This tells the software to check Design Studio tables and look for your view.

The Menu ID should be in range of the Menu, preferably starting at the top of the range. So in this example, we are in the application "System Manager," and the Menu in play is the "System Audit" menu. That starts at 1000900 and goes to 1000999.
It's advisable to start at the top of the range in case any new features are delivered in future updates. If a new feature is added in a future build, it will replace the custom entry if the Menu ID is too low of a number. So if I use 1000912, I run the risk of it being replaced at some point in the future by a new feature getting added to that same menu.
If a custom addition to a menu disappears after an update, the Application Menus function is a good place to check, to see if there is a conflict with something custom that was added with too low of a Menu ID.

The Document value is the name of your custom view. In Design Studio, if you look at the ID for this view, that ID will be used for the Document when you add this to the menu.

The Order determines where this will appear within the menu. So in this example, we have indicated position 40 for this entry, it will appear last when the user opens the System Audit menu in the software.

Lastly, be sure to save this entry once you have everything typed in.

Grant Permission for View
The last component of this process is granting security permissions for this new view. Since it is new to the menu, we will need to update the group security to allow users access to this new custom view. This can be done using the Traverse Global Server Manager or from within the System Manager application if you have access to do so. We'll cover both options.

To grant permission using the System Manager Application
To use System Manager, navigate to System Manager > Administration > Groups. Group security can be configured in many different ways, you may need to access each individual group and add permission to the new view.

In our example, we will grant this to the "ADMIN" group. Click Permissions to begin the process.

Navigate to the Menu where you added the new view. In our example, we'll navigate to System Manager > System Audit and we can see our new view. Check the box next to it to grant permission to it, and then click Apply.


Click Apply on the SM Group screen as well.

To see the new view, log out and back in.

To grant permission using the Traverse Global Server Manager
Navigate to the Traverse Global System Manager and login.


Once in Permissions, navigate to the area the new menu item was added. For our example, we need to go to System Manager > System Audit and we can see our new view.

Check the box and click Apply. Click OK. Do this for each security group that needs to see the new view.

NOTE: If the view was added to other companies, this must be done for each group that needs access, in each company.
There is a Copy Security function that may assist in this process, but care must be taken to avoid unintentional changes, erasing of current groups, security risks. Not all groups in all companies are set up the same way and IT resources may be needed to ensure security is not compromised and is compliant.

Finally, with either method above used, we can now move to access our new view.
Upon opening the view, click refresh to run it. The refresh button functions similarly to the Apply Filter button in the regular Interactive Views.

cdad4941-af2e-477f-9970-2b975a5cb19f.title: Design Studio - How to Create Completely Custom View
cdad4941-af2e-477f-9970-2b975a5cb19f.content:
Problem
A scenario may arise when a user wishes to have a completely custom view. There are two options for this: obtain a custom solution from services or you may be able to use Design Studio.

It should be noted, if you use Design Studio for a completely custom view, you will not get the filter option in the header of the screen like you do with other Interactive Views. Design Studio does not create that but does allow similar functionality without it.
The filtering is part of larger custom coded functionality and that needs to be created for each new custom view. A custom coded view done by the services team will include filtering similar the other views in the software.

Note: To clarify, this document is for completely custom views in the software. If users wish to customize an existing view in the software they can still use Design Studio, but the process outlined in this document is to create a new view completely.

Resolution
Disclaimer, knowledge of writing SQL statements is needed for this process. Table knowledge is also necessary to ensure you are obtaining accurate information.

For this demonstration, we will create a new view that looks at current transaction activity, so you don't have to look through each transaction batch for activity. This process will consist of using Design Studio to create the view, and then we must add it to the menu and grant access to it.

The first step is to gather information for our view. Since the activity we need is in tblSmTransControl, we will need a SQL statement that selects this information.

Since there will not be a filter in the header of the view, so you may want to consider adding filters, especially if much data is to be returned in your view. We may want to consider a filter for this by using a WHERE clause. For example, if we are only looking for Sales Order transactional activity we could filter accordingly in the WHERE clause of the statement for that type of activity. It all depends on the needs.
We'll use this statement:

SELECT *
FROM tblSmTransControl

Note: This example will be a simple one, however more complex statements can be used to accomplish your tasks.

Next, let's access Design Studio and start our work. Open this and login, then proceed to System Data > Views Table


Next, click on the new record/add a record button and add your SQL statement. You may preview results to ensure this is working as you intend, and then click Execute & Accept Query to complete your change.

Next, add all columns that should be available in the view, you can select and deselect them from the column chooser. Click OK to commit your changes.
Remember, these must be selected in your SQL statement, you cannot pick columns that are not part of your SQL statement.


Finally, enter the default columns that will appear upon opening the view. For our example, we'll include all the fields, but this can be whatever you choose as long as they are listed as available columns.


Last, and most important, save the record at the top of the screen to ensure all changes made are saved with this new view.
At this point we will have a usable view, but we will need to add this view to a menu and then assign permission to be able to see this.

NOTE: If multiple companies exist and need this view, the Copy To button can be used at the top of the screen to expedite the delivery to the other companies.

Add Custom View to Software's Menu
Let's access System Manager > Setup and Maintenance > Application Menus. You can place this view wherever you wish, in this example we'll place it in System Manager > System Audit with some of the other auditing views.

Within the Application Menus function, expand System Manager and click on System Audit:

Click new record/plus sign button to create a new record where we can add our view. Here you can see the entry already made, we'll examine this more below here.

The Description is exactly what will be read by other users on the menu. The name should be meaningful and easy to determine what the function is.

The Type must be View. This tells the software to check Design Studio tables and look for your view.

The Menu ID should be in range of the Menu, preferably starting at the top of the range. So in this example, we are in the application "System Manager," and the Menu in play is the "System Audit" menu. That starts at 1000900 and goes to 1000999.
It's advisable to start at the top of the range in case any new features are delivered in future updates. If a new feature is added in a future build, it will replace the custom entry if the Menu ID is too low of a number. So if I use 1000912, I run the risk of it being replaced at some point in the future by a new feature getting added to that same menu.
If a custom addition to a menu disappears after an update, the Application Menus function is a good place to check, to see if there is a conflict with something custom that was added with too low of a Menu ID.

The Document value is the name of your custom view. In Design Studio, if you look at the ID for this view, that ID will be used for the Document when you add this to the menu.

The Order determines where this will appear within the menu. So in this example, we have indicated position 40 for this entry, it will appear last when the user opens the System Audit menu in the software.

Lastly, be sure to save this entry once you have everything typed in.

Grant Permission for View
The last component of this process is granting security permissions for this new view. Since it is new to the menu, we will need to update the group security to allow users access to this new custom view. This can be done using the Traverse Global Server Manager or from within the System Manager application if you have access to do so. We'll use System Manager to do this since we are already in here, it will look similar to the process for the Traverse Global Server Manager.

First, navigate to System Manager > Administration > Groups. Group security can be configured in many different ways, you may need to access each individual group and add permission to the new view.

In our example, we will grant this to the "ADMIN" group. Click Permissions to begin the process.

Navigate to the Menu where you added the new view. In our example, we'll navigate to System Manager > System Audit and we can see our new view. Check the box next to it to grant permission to it, and then click Apply.


Click Apply on the SM Group screen as well.

To see the new view, log out and back in.

Upon opening the view, click refresh to run it. The refresh button functions similarly to the Apply Filter button in the regular Interactive Views.

On a final note, you can filter on the columns as needed and edit that filter at the bottom of the screen once a column has been filtered on. Consideration should be given in the view's design to ensure that it will run and not time out due to too large of a query. Filtering is recommended in the SQL statement when possible.

f7b3c888-4683-4edc-a552-82189e5d3cbe.title: Why when attempting to print WM Print Inventory Tags it Say "Selected batch code is locked."?
f7b3c888-4683-4edc-a552-82189e5d3cbe.content:
Problem
When the User is trying to print WM Print Inventory Tags, the user is receiving a message that says the "Selected batch code is locked.".

Resolution
The error message "Selected Batch Code is locked" indicates that a specific Batch is currently being accessed or worked on by a user. This situation arises when a user has the 'WM Freeze Quantities' screen open. Having this screen open creates a Batch Lock for the selected Batch Code, preventing other users from processing the Batch as it is still considered "in progress" from the Traverse system's perspective.



Navigate to the WM Physical Count Batch Codes screen under the path: Applications -> Warehouse Management -> Setup and Maintenance -> Physical Count Batch Codes screen:

i. In this screen, check if there are any locks recorded for the specific Batch Code.
ii. If a lock is identified, click on the 'Lock' icon corresponding to the Batch Code to unlock it.



iii. Kindly ensure no users are actively working in the batch or holding any activities related to the Batch Code. We can review the Activity Screen to confirm there is no ongoing user activity associated with the locked Batch Code.



Once this had been confirmed, the User can try printing the 'Inventory Tags' as required in the WM Print Inventory Tags screen under the path: Applications -> Warehouse Management -> Physical Inventory -> Print Inventory Tags

Note:

- This issue occurs because the Batch Lock prevents multiple users from accessing the same Batch simultaneously to avoid data conflicts.
- It is crucial to ensure no users are working on the Batch Code in the WM Freeze Quantities screen to resolve the lock.

62d2aa30-29af-4175-8808-484ce3581681.title: How to reprint Invoice/ Check/ Order/ Receipt/ Voucher using Document Archive
62d2aa30-29af-4175-8808-484ce3581681.content:
Problem
How to reprint a printed Invoice/ Check/ Order/ Receipt/ Voucher using Document Archive in AP, AR, PO, SO, PA

Resolution
In order to utilize the Document Archiving functionality, you must set the System Manager Business Rule to Enable Document Archiving to Yes. If you set the rule to No, the Archive settings in the application's business rules will have no effect.

Each application in which document archiving is available has an Archive section in its Business Rules:

- Set the Use Archive business rule to Yes to archive documents, and allow you to reprint prior printed versions of that document. This also activates the Search Document feature.
- For the Archive Watermark rule, enter the watermark text you would like to appear on the reprinted documents. This is only applicable if Use Archive is set to Yes.

In other words, if Use Archive is set to No, after users print an invoice, order, or check stub, they will not have the capability to reprint prior printed versions of documents, and the Search Document feature will be unavailable. There are still functions that allow users to reprint a document using data from the history files.

Same applies for other Applications.

If the document was printed online or using batching with the new document archiving feature enabled, the Business Rule Archive Watermark text will print. If the document was printed before build 16316, or if the Use Archive option is set to No, the Watermark Text for Reprinted Orders/Invoices will print.

If the Business Rule to Use Archive is set to Yes, each time a user prints an invoice, check, or voucher, or POS receipt, a transaction activity record is saved. To view activity records, users can select the Activity or Search Document button on the toolbar to look for activity records based on specific information. Users can then reprint an activity record that includes the Archive Watermark text entered in Business Rules for that application.

If you use document delivery, that process also uses the same print functionality and treats the document as if it was being printed.

Transaction:

The same functionality available in Transactions is also available when printing by batches in the following application functions:

- AP | Pay Invoices | Print Checks
- AR | Transaction Journals | Print Invoices
- AP | Pay Invoices | Print Vouchers
- SO | Transaction Journals | Print Invoices
- PO | Transaction Journals | Print Orders
- PA | Payday Work | Print Checks
- SD | Work Orders | Print Invoices
- PC | Billing | Print Invoices

Interactive views:
After a transaction is posted, users can reprint Orders, Check Stubs, and Invoices from history. The Print function displays all Document No records for that transaction and users can select which one they would like to reprint.

This functionality is available in the following views:

- PO | Detail History View – Print Order
- AR | Open Invoice View – Print Invoice
- PO | Order View – Print Order
- AR | Detail History View – Print Invoice
- PO | Order LC View – Print Order
- AR | Transaction History View – Print Invoice
- PA | Check History View – Print Check Stub
- SO | Detail History View – Print Invoice
- SD | Order View – Print Invoice

f621162e-ac99-444c-9998-15360f5e3fcb.title: Display resolution recommended
f621162e-ac99-444c-9998-15360f5e3fcb.content:
Problem
An insufficient screen display resolution can cause some problems when using Traverse. Below are a few scenarios where this was the root cause:

- The customer was unable to select the payment type and check number due to visibility issues caused by font size and display resolution settings.
- The customer reported issues where users were unable to see the bottom of the screens, leading to missing menu functions and collapsed fields.

Resolution
Check the display settings in the Windows Settings to ensure they are optimal.

Open your Windows Settings > System > Display settings

(This may look different depending on the Windows version being used.)

Under Scale and layout, In the dropdown for "Change the size of text, apps, etc." > Select the one that has a suffix as "(Recommended)"

Under Display resolution> it is suggested to increase the display resolution to the recommended level from the drop down for best functioning in Traverse as well.

If you are using more than one screen, you will want to look at the display settings for each screen.

Operating at recommended display settings will resolve some display issues when using Traverse.

321f8b36-1fe2-4579-8158-d121ad1ffee0.title: GL Transaction - Effect of Multi-Currency Settings on Debit and Credit Field Labels
321f8b36-1fe2-4579-8158-d121ad1ffee0.content:
Problem
When creating a new General Ledger Transaction, the Debit and Credit Amt columns are not editable - they are not taking up the values, and always show -0- when data is entered.

Resolution
When the multi-currency feature is enabled in Traverse, the field labels in the transaction entry screens will display as:

-
Debit Amt Fgn

-
Credit Amt Fgn

These labels indicate that the amounts should be entered in foreign currency values based on the selected currency ID for the transaction.

If multi-currency is not enabled, the system defaults to a single currency mode, and you will see the standard fields:

-
Debit Amount

-
Credit Amount

Navigate to General Ledger> Transactions> Transaction

Right click on a column heading and select the Column Chooser. Double click or drag in the column labels "Credit Amt Fgn" and "Debit Amt Fgn." Also select "Currency ID" to see the currency associated with the GL account.

Enter the amount in "Credit Amt Fgn" and "Debit Amt Fgn" instead of "Debit Amt" and "Credit Amt" columns.

ebcdffe2-cbe9-41f8-bd0c-277d7181307a.title: How to offset an AR Cash Receipt that was posted to a wrong Period?
ebcdffe2-cbe9-41f8-bd0c-277d7181307a.content:
Problem
How to offset an AR Cash Receipt that was posted to a wrong Period?

For example, let us consider the below AR Transaction: 00000239

Resolution
If a Cash Receipt has been posted to the wrong period, we can offset it by creating a negative Cash Receipt for the same period as the original incorrect entry.

Later, the User can create a new Cash Receipt for the right period and post it through as usual.

Please find the below steps to create a negative Cash Receipt to offset the incorrect Cash Receipt.

1. Go to the AR Cash Receipts screen under the path: Applications -> Accounts Receivable -> Transactions -> Cash receipts

2. Click on the 'New' icon at the top and pull up the same Customer ID [For example: '00007']. Enter the payment amount to match the incorrect original Cash receipt with a 'Negative' sign [-] in front. Make sure to select the same Period and Year to which the original incorrect Cash Receipt was posted, along with the Check number as well.

3. Click on the 'Pay' checkbox for the appropriate line(s) in the list of Invoices to apply the negative Cash receipt against the selected line item(s) in the Customer balance.  Alternatively, check the 'Pay" check box to create a new "On Account" line, and edit the Invoice Date and Invoice No as applicable, and/or edit the amount to be applied to the various lines in the "Payment" column.  Then click on the 'Save' icon at the top.

3. Print the Cash Receipts Journal. You can verify that everything looks correct here, with the correct amount being applied to the customer in the correct period.

4. Then we can post the Cash Receipts from the AR Post Cash Receipts screen under the path: Applications -> Accounts Receivable -> Transaction Journal -> Post Cash Receipts:

Thus, the negative Cash Receipt to offset the Cash Receipt posted to an incorrect Cash Receipt has been created.

NOTE: The screenshots are from Traverse 11.2



You can run the Periodic Processing > Periodic Maintenance, selecting the check box to "Perform General Periodic Process" to clear the balances. Next, create the correct cash receipt.

b7c871f7-4e4a-4e22-b7bf-a13cf1861d22.title: Traverse RDP Login - Getting Certificate Message
b7c871f7-4e4a-4e22-b7bf-a13cf1861d22.content:
Problem
The customer received the message, "The identity of the remote computer cannot be verified. Do you want to connect anyway?" when logging into Traverse via an RDP connection.

Resolution
The attached message is a standard prompt checking for secure connections that appears during the login process. The program is basically asking if you trust the computer that you are connecting to since it does not recognize it. In order to trust the connection to the hosted Traverse server moving forward, select the option "Don't ask me again for connection to this computer" is selected. This will prevent the pop-up window from appearing the next time you log in. Clicking "YES," will indicate that you trust this connection, and once you click this you should be able to proceed with the login successfully.

aae72021-ef5e-4034-8d19-862a7839e4d6.title: Sales Order is 'Verified' but 'Qty Shipped' Not Updated
aae72021-ef5e-4034-8d19-862a7839e4d6.content:
Problem
The user has successfully performed the Sales Order verification process, expecting that the system would automatically update the ‘Shipped Quantity’ field for the respective line items. However, after verification, the ‘Shipped Quantity’ remains at zero (0) for all items on the order.

Due to this, the system does not allow the Sales Order to be posted, as a valid shipped quantity is a mandatory requirement for posting.

Resolution
This scenario typically arises during the Sales Order (SO) Verification process in Traverse when the user is prompted to confirm whether the system should automatically populate the 'Qty Shipped' fields for all line items.



If the user selects ‘No’ at this prompt—indicating an intention to proceed with a partial shipment—Traverse does not auto-populate the 'Qty Shipped' fields. Instead, the system sets the 'Qty Shipped' to zero (0) for all lines and allows the user to manually enter the shipped quantities based on what is actually being shipped.



This behavior may be misinterpreted as a system issue, where the user assumes Traverse failed to update the shipped quantities, when in reality, it is functioning as intended based on the user's input.



To proceed in such cases:

-
The user should manually enter the appropriate shipped quantities for each line item—this can be a partial or full quantity, depending on the actual shipment.

-
Once the 'Qty Shipped' field is updated, Traverse will automatically populate the 'Actual Ship Date' with the current system date, indicating the date of shipment.

If the Sales Order is linked to a Purchase Order, you may need to follow some additional steps to adjust these quantities. See Knowledge Base number 000098864, "Linked Sales Order Quantities Cannot Be Posted Due to Missing Purchase Order Quantities" for further information regarding this problem.





This behavior ensures that Traverse supports both full and partial shipments while providing flexibility and control to the user during the verification process. The User can then 'Save' the order and proceed with posting as required.

f4f38d74-b336-4a7a-9490-0d9ecb0b67d4.title: PO Transaction Error Message
f4f38d74-b336-4a7a-9490-0d9ecb0b67d4.content:
Problem
In "PO Transactions" when the client tries to clear information that was entered in a Custom Field, such as a date that was entered in a date Custom Field, an error message pops up saying, "Object reference not set to a reference of an object".  (Ex. - "ETA" field, a customization field).

===================================Object reference not set to an instance of an object.------------------------------Edition = GlobalBuild = 25080User = XXXXXXXLicenseServer = XXXXXXXXXCulture = English (United States)DefaultCompID = XXXSysDb = XXXXXXSessionID = XXXXXXXXXXMachineName = XXXXXXXXX===================================Object reference not set to an instance of an object. (TRAVERSE.Business.PurchaseOrder)------------------------------Program Location:at TRAVERSE.Business.PurchaseOrder.TransactionHeaderProvider.Update(String compId)at TRAVERSE.Client.PurchaseOrder.POHeaderControl.SaveTransaction()at TRAVERSE.Client.PurchaseOrder.POHeaderControl.UpdateData(Int32 index)

Resolution
Upon thorough investigation in collaboration with the development team, it has been confirmed that the issue encountered was due to a software bug within the Traverse Global application. This was found in Traverse Global Build 25080.

The root cause was identified and has been addressed in Traverse Global Build 25143. This latest build includes a permanent fix that corrects the issue and restores expected functionality.
