bb0ea6c1-c8d9-436a-a79c-9a9ade1499fe.title: Why does the updated W4 forms displays as 2020 W4
bb0ea6c1-c8d9-436a-a79c-9a9ade1499fe.content:
Problem
Why does the updated Federal W4 forms displays as "2020 W4" in Payroll -> Setup and Maintenance -> Employee Information, Taxes tab, Federal Taxes tab, Factors, Employee, and Tax Code: FWH?

Resolution
The W4 form was redesigned in 2020, and that is the reason the prompt reads 2020 W-4.



Beginning in 2020, all newly-hired employees are required to use this updated form for tax withholdings. For employees hired before 2020 who already have a valid W-4 on file as of January 1, 2020, their tax withholding will continue to be calculated based on their most recently submitted W-4, unless they choose to update it. If these employees wish to make any changes to their withholding, they must use the redesigned 2020 W-4 form going forward. This update ensures accuracy in withholding in line with current tax regulations.

65953d1d-2662-457b-89fa-e90dfead31bc.title: Cloud User being kicked out of Traverse within 5 minutes of idle time
65953d1d-2662-457b-89fa-e90dfead31bc.content:
Problem
When the Cloud user is leaving the Traverse unused for 5 minutes or less, the user gets the following error message, and they are kicked out of Traverse:

"Your Remote Desktop Services session ended because the remote computer didn't receive any input from you."

Resolution
This error might happen in one of the following scenarios:

1. When the User has the Power Saver mode enabled in their workstation:

- Power Saver mode will indirectly affect internet usage by optimizing system resources. Thus, the Users will be kicked out of Traverse, due to the lack of activity for even several minutes.
- The User may need to consider turning off Power Saver mode to prevent their session from ending.

2. Not having a stable Internet connection:

- As a result, the User will be kicked out of Traverse due to the lack of connectivity to Traverse.
- The User needs to ensure stable connectivity to prevent their session from ending.

cfdc3e80-6ee1-4660-9e2a-6a746623c0a4.title: Unable to login to Cloud - Steps to Install cloud environment and login
cfdc3e80-6ee1-4660-9e2a-6a746623c0a4.content:
Problem
Unable to login - Need step by step instructions to reinstall the Traverse Cloud environment and to then login.

Resolution
A Saas Cloud user is unable to login.

- If a user is not able to access the Traverse cloud at all:

Missing RDP file – The user does not have the Traverse application downloaded on their desktop and needs it - the user sees that there is no Traverse icon on their desktop nor is one found in a folder.

Step 1: The user can access either of the two below links. The user can download an RDP connection to Traverse from the first link, or can use the second web link to connect directly to the cloud from their browser to log in to Traverse.

Remote Desktop Web Client - (RDP) to get an icon on the desktop to access Traverse.  Instructions for downloading the RDP file can be found in the Knowledge Base article: 000087717, "How to Download RDP file for Cloud/SaaS Users"

RD Web Access - To access Traverse directly from the web browser.

If the user downloads the RDP file, they may need to unblock the application. For this, you would need to navigate to the downloads folder. Right-click on the file for the application, click on Properties, and Check the unblock checkbox. Hit OK



Step 2: Once access is set up either through the RDP icon or the browser, open Traverse on the workstation, and put in the login credentials i.e. Username and password.

If the user does not know their username, they can check their Outlook mail, where they would have received their initial login credentials.

Note: The credentials will have been received from the mail ID: NoReply - TeamNextWave noreply-teamnextwave@aptean.com

If the credentials were initially sent to an admin’s email, the user would have received this information. The user would need to reach out to the admin who received the email, or the Aptean team can reach out to our technical support staff to grab the username information for that specific user.

Step 3: Enter the username and password to sign in to the application.

If the user is unaware of his/her password, then they could reset their password through the AD Self Password reset link.

For this, you can refer to the Knowledge Base article 000092564 "Ad Self portal Password reset - Traverse cloud." This article covers everything on how to reset the password.

If the user cannot reset the password through the Ad Self Portal and they are facing a "Password reset was unsuccessful" error, they will need to reach out to Aptean support to have the technical assist with the password reset.

Step 4: Enter the username and Password to Log in. This should open another sign-in window for Microsoft Authentication. Enter the username and Password again for the validation. Check the “Don’t ask me again” check box and click ok.

Step 5: When the “Show details” button becomes visible from being greyed out, click on that and launch traverse. The Knowledge Base article 000085588 delves deeper into how to log in to Traverse from the “Show details” screen.

5.1 In this "Show details" screen, there is a step where the user will receive a code to their registered email address generally known as an MFA code for Multi-Factor Authentication purposes. If a user does not receive that code to their email address, this will require engaging the Aptean technical support team to see if the user's email address is correctly entered in the system and saved correctly.

5.2 A common issue users encounter is that they are unable to enter the code in the code entry textbox. Why?

- Check if the Num Lock is on: Sometimes the Num Lock light may be on but not functioning correctly. Press the Num Lock key once to turn it off, then press it again to turn it back on.
- Alternatively, use the numbers above the alphabet on the keyboard.

One of these solutions should enable the user to enter the code.



Step 6: Now after following all the above-mentioned steps, the user will get into this screen.

The user should not put in their username and login password here, as they will get an “Invalid login” error. Rather, please check the “Use trusted Connection” and “Save Login” checkboxes to login.

7678aa3b-2778-4ece-80ba-58fd563396de.title: Assistance on adding new Fixed Assets to the Year 2024, after completing the Year End Maintenance
7678aa3b-2778-4ece-80ba-58fd563396de.content:
Problem
Assistance on adding new Fixed Assets to the previous Year, after completing the Year End Maintenance

Resolution
i. Set Up the Asset: Go to Fixed Assets > Setup and Maintenance > Fixed Assets. Click the "+" button to add the new asset. Configure the asset in the system as it would have been initially recorded. Ensure that the depreciation start period is accurately set to reflect the intended start date at the beginning of the prior year.



ii. Calculate the Missing Depreciation: Manually compute the total depreciation amount that should have been recorded for the asset throughout 2024.



iii. Adjust the Accumulated Depreciation: Enter the calculated depreciation amount into the Eligible Accumulated Depreciation field to reflect what should have been recorded for the previous year.



Iv. Recalculate Depreciation: Once all adjustments are posted, click the "Recalculate" button on the Depreciation tab for the Asset. This step ensures that the 2025 depreciation schedule is correctly aligned with the updated asset values.



v. Update General Ledger (GL): Manually enter any 2024 depreciation-related GL entries into the correct period and year to accurately reflect the adjustments in the General Ledger. Remember that you need to change your fiscal year so that you are in the prior year to enter GL transactions in the prior year. Post the GL transactions to the Master when ready.

vi. Run the "Update Current Year" process to ensure that the new balances in the prior year are rolled into the new year correctly.

6ae967fa-5d1b-4ee4-b224-275250eddfe5.title: Add a short period in the general ledger
6ae967fa-5d1b-4ee4-b224-275250eddfe5.content:
Problem
The client’s current fiscal year is configured with 12 monthly periods. They are requesting to add a short 13th period for the year 2025 and would like to know if this adjustment is possible within the system.

Resolution
The current system is configured with 12 GL fiscal periods, which are defined during the initial database creation and setup of SM Business Rules—typically before any GL accounts or transactions are entered. Due to this foundational setup, the number of fiscal periods cannot be modified through the standard user interface once the system is in use.

To add a short period and increase the total number of fiscal periods to 13 for the year 2025, programmatic changes would be required. This adjustment would involve altering the core system configuration and therefore qualifies as a billable customization.

If the client wishes to proceed, we can submit a quote request to the Programming Team. They will evaluate the scope of changes needed and provide a formal estimate for implementing the 13-period configuration in their system.

ae381d45-9760-4da4-956c-c323b24bd1f0.title: Using different e-mail addresses to send different forms in Traverse.
ae381d45-9760-4da4-956c-c323b24bd1f0.content:
Problem
Looking to configure Traverse so that certain email addresses are used to send specific forms in Traverse.

Resolution
This can be accomplished by using SM SMTP Settings to configure different email addresses, then using SM Document Settings to indicate what email address/SMTP Name-ID should be used to send specific forms.



To configure different email addresses in the System Manager -> Document Delivery ->SMTP Settings see the following steps:

- Click the New button on the toolbar to create a new record.
- From the Mail Type drop-down menu, select Microsoft for Microsoft Mail service, else select SMTP for basic authentication.
- Enter an SMTP Name. This is the reference you will choose when configuring document settings.
- Enter your SMTP Server name. This is the name used in email programs to send mail. Some common SMTP servers: smtp.live.com for Microsoft Hotmail/Live/Outlook.com accounts; smtp.gmail.com for Google Gmail accounts; smtp.mail.yahoo.com for Yahoo email accounts. Use your local SMTP server, if available.
- Enter the SMTP Port used for sending mail. The most common SMTP ports are: 25, 465, and 587. Contact your system administrator to determine which port to use.
- Mark the Enable SSL check box if your email server uses the SSL secure transfer protocol.
- Enter the User Name for the account used to send mail from the server. The user name will be the name or email address you use to log into the SMTP Server you designated.
- Enter the Password for that user account. Click in the grid cell on the Browse button () to open the password entry dialog box.
- If you marked the SSL check box, you need to enter the path to the SSL Certificate. Use the Browse button to navigate to the SSL certificate.
- Enter the Sender's Name and the Sender's Email address.
- Enter a Reply To email address, if applicable. This is the address to which the recipient's reply will be sent.
- Click the Save button to save your changes.





Once the SM SMTP Settings have been configure, the System Manager -> Document Delivery -> Document Settings may be configure to set unique settings for each document type, including the subject line, sender information, static attachments, and the body text. You can also set the document type to send (email or fax) automatically when it is printed, or be sent to a document queue where you can review the documents before they are emailed or faxed. To create a new form/document setting follow the following steps:

- Click the New button on the toolbar to create a blank document setting record.
- Select a document type to configure from the Form ID drop-down list.
- If you want the document to send automatically without user interaction, mark the Auto Send check box. If you want to require user interaction before the document is sent, clear the check box. If the check box is clear, the document will be sent to the document queue, from where you can manually send the document.
- If necessary, enter the path to a Fax Cover Page, or use the Browse button () to navigate to the page file. Use the View button () to view the page.
- Enter a Subject for the document. This value will appear in the subject line of the document. You can drag dynamic (merge) fields from the Fields tab into the Subject field. If this field is left blank, the system will use the subject from the Document Delivery setup for the customer or the vendor.
- Select an SMTP ID from the drop-down list. If you leave this field blank, the system will use the default email server settings in the System Manager business rules. Note: The SMTP ID ties to the SM SMTP Settings previously setup, and is what will identify what e-mail address to use when the the specific form is printed/emailed through document delivery.
- If you want to sent the email formatted as HTML, mark the Send as HTML check box. If you clear the check box, the email will be formatted as plain text.
HINT: If, when you select to send the email as HTML, the delivered email is not formatted correctly, you must add HTML tags to the body of the email to ensure correct formatting.

- In the Body section, create the body of the email or fax. Enter any static text you want to appear. To add dynamic (merge) fields to the body, drag the field you want to add from the Fields tab and drop it in the body of the email. Dynamic fields are tied to the database, and change depending on the value of key fields such as invoice number or customer number. To add formatting to fields, add a pipe symbol | to the end of the field name, drag a formatting option from the Formats tab, and drop the format option after the pipe | and inside the closing bracket. On the Misc Fields tab, you can find fields not included on the Fields tab.
- Define the file name for the document in the Document Name field. You can use both static text and dynamic (merge) fields to create a file name. If no file name is defined, the default file name determined by the system will be used.
- If applicable, add static attachments in the Attachment field list. Use the Append button () to add a file to the list. Navigate to the attachment file using the Browse button (). Use the View button () to view the page.
- Click the Save button on the toolbar to save your changes.

c41688ac-fce8-4c59-93ef-94bd3acc5f27.title: No Federal Tax Withheld for Employee with W-4 Filed as Married Jointly
c41688ac-fce8-4c59-93ef-94bd3acc5f27.content:
Problem
A part-time employee working less than 19 hours per week, has submitted a federal W-4 form claiming "Married filing jointly" with one exemption. However, no federal income tax is currently being withheld from his paychecks.

Resolution
This behavior is likely due to the employee's low gross earnings combined with their selected filing status. Employees who earn below the federal withholding threshold will not have federal income tax deducted from their pay. The "Married filing jointly" status further raises this threshold, which can result in no withholding for part-time employees with lower income.

To verify this:

-
Use a Tax Calculator:
You can visit the US government IRS tax website to check the calculations. Visit https://www.irs.gov/individuals/tax-withholding-estimator and enter the employee's details (filing status, exemptions, and gross pay) to confirm whether federal withholding should apply.

-
Test Within the System:
In Employee Information, set up the employee with their correct Federal and State withholdings, and with “Married” status and 0 exemptions. Go to Payday Work > Manual Checks. Create a manual check, enter comparable earnings, and click to "Calculate Tax" to see if the system calculates federal withholding. If the withholding calculates as "0" in this test, it confirms that the employee's current settings and earnings are below the withholding threshold. Once you are done with testing, you can delete the check.



Federal withholding is only applied when an employee’s gross earnings exceed the minimum threshold based on their filing status. In this case, the lack of withholding appears to be correct and expected behavior.

d24d1b91-fb04-4fce-a59b-c775ea7efbbf.title: Sql Error when generating COGS adjustments
d24d1b91-fb04-4fce-a59b-c775ea7efbbf.content:
Problem
In Build 24278 in Inventory -> Periodic Processing -> IN COGS Adjustments, when trying to generate or post, Traverse is giving a SQL server error when trying to generating COGS adjustments. After clicking to calculate and then generate the Cogs entries, the SQL error comes up

242 : The conversion of a nvarchar data type to a datetime data type resulted in an out-of-range value. : Procedure{dbo.trav_InAdjustmentCOGS_AverageCost_proc} (.Net SqlClient Data Provider)If you try to post the entries, the post will go partially through and will send the transactions to the General Ledger as unposted transactions. However, it does not post them to the Inventory history, as seen in the IN Detail History View.

This SQL error was deemed to be a bug in the programming in build 24278. Development created a fix to resolve this issue, associated with change request DEV-269516, available in build 25143.

The fix allows you to generate and post the COGS adjustments correctly.

11f89156-d552-4121-8a55-a26495671703.title: How to Select and Rearrange the Widgets in On-Time Web
11f89156-d552-4121-8a55-a26495671703.content:
Problem
Can I remove/add widgets or at least move them around on the dashboard in On-Time Web?

Resolution
How to Select and Rearrange the Widgets in On-Time Web

Question: Can I remove/add widgets or at least move them around on the dashboard in On-Time Web?



You can easily select the widgets and arrange them on the dashboard in On-Time Web for each type of employee.





How to Select and Arrange On-Time Web Dashboard Widgets

- Navigate to Company Settings>Dashboard Settings

- On the tab Widget Order Tab, click the Login Type to choose which employee type you want to set their dashboard. Choose one of the following: Employee, Supervisor, Division Admin, or Company Admin.

- Move all widgets to the Hidden Dashboard Widgets column, then move the desired widgets in the order that you want on the screen to the Show Dashboard Widgets.

- Then click the Save button.



Widget Settings Tab – you can also edit the In/Out Board, Employee Status, and Employee Message widgets. Set the options and save.



- View In/Out Board – Choose who and what Employee Types see.

- All employees may view their own groups
- All employees may view all other employees

- Employee Status – Choose the number of days to view before it is removed from the status widget.

- Days to Show Employee Messages – Choose the number of days to show employee messages in the Employee Messages widget.

Dashboard Message Tab – This is for company-wide messages that Employees can read on the dashboard. Enter/edit the message and save.

619c36ff-a86a-48cd-ab20-d12e113b8b93.title: Why does the 'Qty' in 'Standard RP report' does not align with the Inventory for a 'Discontinued Item'?
619c36ff-a86a-48cd-ab20-d12e113b8b93.content:
Problem
Why does the 'Qty' in 'Standard RP report' does not align with the Inventory for a 'Discontinued Item'?

Resolution
When an item’s status is changed to Discontinued, Traverse may omit or miscalculate its on‑hand quantities in the Requirements Planning (RP) process, leading to a mismatch between what the Standard RP Report shows and the true inventory levels. To correct this discrepancy, follow these steps:

i. Reactivate the Item and Location:

- Navigate to the IN Items screen under the path: Applications -> Inventory -> Setup and Maintenance -> Items
- Locate the required Item ID and update its Status to Active.
- Likewise, update the associated Location Status from Discontinued to Active. [NOTE: If there are more than one location, make sure to setup the 'Active' status on all the Locations]



ii. Generate RP Data:

- Run the 'Generate RP Data' function under the path: Applications -> Requirements Planning -> RP Processing -> Generate RP Data
- This rebuilds the planning dataset, now including the reactivated item and location.



iii. Re‑Discontinue the Item and Location:

- Once the 'Generate RP Data' function is run, return to the IN Items screen.
- Change the Item Status and Location Status back to Discontinued.



iv. Verify the Report:

- Re-run the Standard RP Report.
- The report will now correctly reflect the on‑hand quantities for the formerly discontinued item, restoring alignment with your actual inventory.



By temporarily reactivating discontinued records during the RP data generation process, we can ensure that Traverse captures the proper quantities and delivers an accurate report, even for items that are no longer in active use.

7196a8ce-c120-4e0a-ab99-f6a7d38a3635.title: Change a Transaction Batch
7196a8ce-c120-4e0a-ab99-f6a7d38a3635.content:
Problem
I entered Accounts Payable transactions in the wrong batch ID and I am unable to print them on the correct checks.  How do I change a batch code without deleting everything.  I have already printed the purchase journal, AP Post Transactions, and the prepare payments.  I am at the next phase of printing the checks.

Resolution
To remove any payments that have already been prepared in a batch, you can use the 'AP Select Payables' screen. This allows you to drop the payments without impacting other processes.

However, if you wish to completely restart the Prepare Payments process, please follow the steps below:

-
Navigate to AP → Prepare Payments.

-
Search for and open the batch that was previously prepared incorrectly.

-
When you attempt to access the batch, Traverse will display a prompt indicating that payments have already been prepared in this batch and will ask whether you want to start over.

-
Click 'Yes' on this prompt. This action will reset the batch, clearing the previously prepared payments.

-
If the incorrect bank account was selected during the initial preparation, you can update it by navigating to AP → Hold/Release Payments.

-
Enter the Vendor ID associated with the payment.

-
Update the Bank Account field with the correct account information.

After completing these steps, you can return to AP → Prepare Payments and proceed with re-preparing the payments as needed.

96b4f43f-a6d3-4a5f-a14e-524d206f431f.title: Illinois Sales Tax rate inquiry/ Update Sales Tax Rate in Traverse
96b4f43f-a6d3-4a5f-a14e-524d206f431f.content:
Problem
Customer would like to know "How to change the Illinois sales tax rate in Traverse to 8%? "

Resolution
Go to System Manager > Tax Setup > Tax Locations.
Select the relevant Tax Location ID.
Then, switch to the Rates tab and update the Sales Tax Percentage column with the desired value.

In general,

- In the Sales Tax Percent column, enter the percentage of tax for sales of the class or use the current value.
- In the Purch Tax Percent column, enter the percentage of tax for purchases of the class or use the current value.
- In the Refundable Percent column, enter the percentage of refundable collected taxes for collection expenses.
- Select a GL Tax Expense Account. If you checked the Use Expense Account from Line Items when Purchasing check box on the General tab, this account will not be used for the tax expense. The account entered on each line item would have the tax expense posted to it.
- Use the ellipsis button () to open the Tax Rate Detail dialog box. This allows you to optionally enter detailed information for a tax class, including multiple tax rates and a choice of gradient or total tax methods.

Use the Tax Rate Detail screen to set maximum tax amounts and "up to" taxable sales amounts.

- Choose 'Gradient' or 'Total' from the Method drop-down list:
- The 'Gradient' method can apply multiple tax rates to a sale, purchase, or refund. For example, if the above tax was applied to a sale of $6,000, using the Gradient method the first $100.00 would be charged no tax, the next $4,999.99 would be charged the 1.5% tax rate, and the last $1,000 would be charged at the 4% tax rate.
- The 'Total' method applies a single tax rate to each item in a sale, purchase, or refund. For example, if the tax above was applied to an item in a sale of $100.00, using the Total method the entire amount would not be taxed. An item that had a price from $100.01 to $4999.99 would be taxed at a rate of 1.5%. An item that had a price of $5000.00 or more would be taxed at a rate of 4%.

- Enter the Amounts Through to indicate the levels of the tax rate for the gradient or total amounts.
- Enter amounts in stages to calculate the tax at the desired rates for the amount steps of the tax calculation. If there is a rate that is above all others with no limit enter '99,999,999.99', or an amount you know will be more than any sale.

8255af98-1c17-4344-8882-be4ef141a65a.title: Commissions are not preparing properly
8255af98-1c17-4344-8882-be4ef141a65a.content:
Problem
Manual commissions were input via AR Commission Detail for an Invoice, but they are not preparing and do not show up in the Commission Edit Register.

Cause
"Net Sales" or "Payments on Inv" are not correctly filled out when basing commissions off of Paid Invoices

Resolution
When you go to Accounts Receivable -> AR Commissions --> Commission Detail and create a new record to input information into the AR Commission Detail Screen manually, when the "Based On" is set to "Paid Invoices", you need to select the Percent of Invoice, Commission %, and whether to take the Percent Of the Gross Profit or the Sales (Net). (If "None" is selected, the commission will be calculated as 0.). Accordingly, the prepare commissions process will utilize the Net Sales and Gross Profit fields in their calculation of the commission that is owed the Sales Rep.

The "Line Items" amount and "Net Sales" amount needs to be filled out correctly according to the sales that were made from the invoice. (The "Net Sales" amount generally includes the Line Items total and the Sales Tax, but not Freight or Misc. charges.) The "Gross Profit" will automatically populate based on the Line Items total minus the Cost of Sales total, however, the Net Sales total will not automatically populate. However, if the Net Sales is not filled out, the commission will not prepare if you have selected "Net Sales" as your method of calculating the commission.

Additionally, the Payments on Invoice field needs to be filled out appropriately for the payments that were paid on the invoice, as this triggers the "Tot Comm Earned" field. If a commission needs to be added to the record that was not calculated based on the amounts that were sold and the payments that were made, an adjustment can be put into the "Comm Adjustment" line to add in the extra commission.

Additionally, the Amount Prepared, while it can be edited, is meant to reflect that amount that has been prepared once the Commissions have been prepared, and does not impact the amount that will be prepared.

ab0d7d6e-2141-4075-959f-e31a64a58335.title: Traverse Frozen for cloud customers
ab0d7d6e-2141-4075-959f-e31a64a58335.content:
Problem
When a Traverse print dialog pop-up box launches from a legacy OSAS Cloud Hosted environment and displays behind Traverse itself, Traverse appears to be frozen and unusable.

Resolution
The following steps are to be followed:

1. Click into the frozen Traverse Global application.

2. While holding the Windows key, press left or right. This should move the client window to the left or right half of the screen.

3. It should also reveal a print dialogue behind the Traverse client. Hit cancel. This should give you access back to the Traverse client application.

NOTE: If the “Win – Left and Win – Right” shortcuts don't work, double click on the Traverse icon in the taskbar and try again, sometimes this has to be performed once or twice.

a08fcf6c-20a8-417a-a026-5de44ef3c36e.title: Seeing All Document Attachments in Traverse
a08fcf6c-20a8-417a-a026-5de44ef3c36e.content:
Problem
Is there a place in Traverse that will allow you to see all the Attachments that have been added into Traverse?

Resolution
The System Manager > Company Setup > Manage Attachments will allow you to view attachments from functions where attachments are available. You can also delete attachments that are no longer applicable.



Select the 'Apply Filter' to view all the attachments.

You may also change the priority and status values of different attachments to aid in filtering the attachments in the future.



Double-clicking on the blue links will allow you to view the document attached.

a3280579-aa70-424f-bcc8-312d1a92094c.title: Setting a GL Account to a Payroll Earning Code
a3280579-aa70-424f-bcc8-312d1a92094c.content:
Problem
How do you change or set the GL Account that is associated to a new earning code that was created in Payroll?

Resolution
New PA Earning Codes are created in Payroll -> Codes Maintenance -> Earning Codes. For demonstration purposes we'll create a new earning code 'bus' with the description 'test'.

Next, to select a GL Account to associated with this earning code navigate to Payroll -> Setup and maintenance -> Departments.

In the PA Departments screen you will be able to select the desired Department ID, and you will see the new earning code description 'test' appear in the Accounts list. There you will see that you then have the ability to select Select the desired GL Account in the GL Account column to associate the new earnings code with the GL account.

02018bda-1b35-464c-ba17-14da87618f2a.title: How to create Account Mask in General Ledger
02018bda-1b35-464c-ba17-14da87618f2a.content:
Problem
How to create Account Mask in General Ledger for a newly created company.

Resolution
Access the GL Account Mask screen by going to General Ledger -> Setup and Maintenance -> Account Mask.

- Select the number of segments from the Number of Segments field.
Note: Once you save your entries, you cannot change the number of segments.
- In the Case field select the whether the letters in the mask should be:
EnterForUpperAll uppercase lettersLowerAll lowercase lettersEitherA combination of upper and lowercase letters

- In the Fill Character field select what to use to separate different segments. Available options are:  None, Space, Hyphen, Period, Colon, or Slash.
- Enter the current fiscal year in the Current Fiscal Year field.
- Select a segment, then enter the account mask in the Mask field using the following characters:
EnterFor0Using digits 0-9LUsing letters A-ZAUsing digits 0-9 and letters A-ZCUsing any characters except spaces

- Specify the length of the segment in the Length field.
- Enter a description of the segment in the Description field.
- Enter an abbreviation for the segment in the Abbreviation field.
- Click the Save button, on the toolbar, to save the account mask.
Note: You can use the Test Format and Test Input Mask fields to test the newly created mask.

c7f931e5-15ec-47a5-8e64-38e92a9ddf59.title: How to Cancel a Work Order in Bill of Material - Kitting
c7f931e5-15ec-47a5-8e64-38e92a9ddf59.content:
Problem
How to Cancel an Issued Work Order in the Bill of Material - Kitting application of Traverse.

Resolution

9587aaac-f4ed-4173-a3e4-e0e7bc921e2c.title: Serialized Items with Trailing Spaces Not Recognized During Pick/Pack in Traverse 11.2
9587aaac-f4ed-4173-a3e4-e0e7bc921e2c.content:
Problem
Serialized Items with Trailing Spaces Not Recognized During Pick/Pack in Traverse 11.2

In Traverse 11.2 (Build 24278), when a serialized item is received through WMS – Receive Orders, and a trailing space is mistakenly entered at the end of the serial number, the system does not handle it correctly in subsequent transactions. This leads to a failure in recognizing the serial number during the Pick/Pack/Ship process. As a result, users are unable to pick or pack the items, and the serial number becomes effectively unusable. Additionally, there is no available option to edit or correct the serial number after it's created.

Resolution
The issue was caused by a limitation in how Traverse handled serial numbers with trailing spaces. While the serial numbers appeared valid during the receiving process in WMS, they could not be used in downstream workflows such as Sales Order picking, resulting in transaction failures.

A hotfix was requested, and the issue has now been resolved in Traverse Build 24355. Serial numbers with trailing spaces are now correctly handled across all related processes.

Until upgraded to Build 24355 or higher, it is strongly recommended to avoid entering trailing spaces when inputting serial numbers during receiving in WMS.

Bug 92081: CR - WMS - Mobile picking bins and Serial items - 04066798 - DEV-248675

e2684dec-7a73-4377-8ad9-c4361a1b2228.title: Post Run Number Not Displayed in IN Detail History for Physical Inventory Adjustments
e2684dec-7a73-4377-8ad9-c4361a1b2228.content:
Problem
Post Run Number Not Displayed in IN Detail History for Physical Inventory Adjustments

In Traverse 11.2, users are encountering an issue during the Physical Inventory process involving serialized items. Specifically, after preparing and freezing a Physical Inventory batch, verifying counts, and running the Update Perpetual Inventory process, the system fails to display the associated Post Run number in the IN Detail History View for entries where the quantity was adjusted to zero.

This issue prevents users from validating that the adjustment has been properly processed, as the post run number seen in the Activity Log does not match what is (or is not) shown in the IN Detail History View.

Resolution
This issue was caused by the system not properly linking the Post Run number to inventory adjustment entries made through the Physical Inventory process for serialized items, specifically when a counted quantity was changed from 1 to 0 and updated through Update Perpetual Inventory.

The problem has been resolved in Build 25080. With this update, the Post Run number now correctly appears in the IN Detail History View, allowing users to accurately track inventory adjustments related to Physical Inventory batches.

Please ensure your environment is updated to Build 25080 or later to receive this fix.

Bug 94052: CR - Error: Post Run Number Not Displaying in IN Detail History View - 04109532 - DEV-256917

1c684ff9-fd09-4943-a806-8662399131e4.title: OSAS Customer Database Backup Procedure
1c684ff9-fd09-4943-a806-8662399131e4.content:
Problem
Need Database backup

company database
SYS database and
Client folder

Resolution
KB Article: OSAS Customer Database Backup Procedure

This knowledge base article provides step-by-step instructions for taking a database backup for OSAS customers. Note: This procedure applies only to OSAS customers. SaaS customers follow a different backup process.

1. Retrieve the RDS and SQL server details from the customer's installation survey.
2. Log in to the RDS server of the customer using administrative credentials.
3. From the RDS server, open a Remote Desktop (RDP) connection to the customer’s SQL server.

4. On the SQL server, navigate to the backup directory:
- `B:\SQLBACKUPS`
- Locate the folder for the specific database.
- Inside the folder, you will find two `.bak` files. These are automatically generated backups from the last two days.
- If a recent backup is not present, take a manual backup using SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS).

5. Open Microsoft Edge or Chrome on the SQL server and go to:
- `https://filetransfer.aptean.com/login`
- Log in using credentials provided by the IT team.
- If you do not have FTP access, use OneDrive as an alternative method.

6. In the FTP portal:
- Create a new folder named after the customer.
- Upload the company and sys database `.bak` files.
- Click **Add File**, select the `.bak` file, and then click **Start** to upload.

7. Back on the RDS server:
- Open the `T:\` drive.
- Locate the customer’s client folder.
- Right-click on the folder and select **Compress** to zip the folder.
- Return to the FTP portal and upload the zipped client folder to the previously created folder.

8. After uploading all files:
- Right-click the customer folder in the FTP portal and choose **Share**.
- Set a link expiration date and password.
- Share the FTP link and password with the requester to complete the backup process.

1e35af34-49c9-4d73-89d8-f7712a2ba96f.title: Handling SQL Connection Error: "Communication Link Failure" in DocUnity
1e35af34-49c9-4d73-89d8-f7712a2ba96f.content:
Problem
How to resolve the below SQL connection error while saving Documents in Doc Unity?



The user encountered an error when executing a SQL query to retrieve blob data from the KMD_BATCH_BLOBS table using a specific KMD_UUID. The error message indicated a communication link failure caused by the SQL Server connection being forcibly closed by the remote host.



Error Message:
SELECT KMD_BLOB FROM KMD_BATCH_BLOBS WHERE KMD_UUID = 'XXXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXXXXXXXXXX'
[Microsoft][SQL Server Native Client 11.0][SQL Server]TCP Provider: An existing connection was forcibly closed by the remote host.
[Microsoft][SQL Server Native Client 11.0]Communication link failure.

Resolution
This is commonly associated with disruptions in the network layer or issues at the SQL Server service level that cause the active session to terminate unexpectedly.

The error specifically included:

-
TCP Provider error: Indicates that the existing connection to the SQL Server was terminated unexpectedly.

-
SQL Server Native Client 11.0: Identifies the client technology being used for the connection.

-
Communication Link Failure: A general connectivity error signaling that the client could not maintain a stable connection with the SQL Server instance.



To address the issue, it was recommended to reboot the SQL Server hosting the database. After the reboot:

-
The error message no longer appeared.

-
The query executed successfully.

-
No further communication link failures were observed during post-reboot monitoring.

This indicates that the server reboot resolved any transient issues impacting the SQL Server's ability to maintain stable connections with clients.

9526683c-a49e-4af8-81e7-83ff582584c2.title: Liability account setup to process AP
9526683c-a49e-4af8-81e7-83ff582584c2.content:
Problem
User question on setting liability account to process AP

Resolution
Setup:



1. Set up a GL Liability account (an AP type account), for the credit card payments. It is best to have a Liability Accounts for each credit card which will be reconciled. If several physical cards are paid from one statement, those would all use the same account.

2. (Optional) You may choose to set up an AP Distribution Code for use when paying invoices with credit cards. The primary difference between this Distribution Code and any other will be that by doing this, a second AP Account can be used for the liability in the period between when the invoice is posted and the prepayment is posted (see below). This should not be the same Account as in Step 1 above. This step can be skipped and the common Distribution Code and AP Account can be used if preferred.

3. Set up a credit card Vendor (“VISA”, or whatever). If the optional Distribution Code was created in step 2, use it when setting up this Vendor. For the Vendor's default GL Account, use the Liability Account set up in step 1.

4. Set up the “Bank” Account, in either System Manager or Bank Reconciliation, noting that it will not be an Account Type of “General” but a “Credit Card” Account Type. You will be required to enter the Vendor (“VISA”, etc.). Unlike “regular” Bank Accounts, you will not enter a GL Cash Account when setting up



Processing the expense:



1. Process an Expense or Item invoice as normal, whether through AP or PO, but if the invoice will be paid by a credit card, make sure to change the Distribution Code to the one related to this credit card account, if you set up the optional Distribution Code in Step 2 above.

2. Enter the lines for Expenses or Items (the bottom section) as you normally would with whatever Expense or Inventory GL accounts are appropriate. Confirm the invoice totals. When entering a PO you will need to enter an invoice prior to entering a payment amount and credit card bank.

3. Click on the Payment tab and enter the amount charged to the credit card as the Prepayment amount. Other payment-related boxes will now become available for entry. Enter the Payment Number (comparable to a check number that would correspond to the payment), Payment Date, and (credit card) Bank Account ID. Verify the other fields. If there is any remaining payment amount, it will be entered in the Payment fields in the lower right of this payment entry area.

4. Process the remaining payables or PO batch, print reports and post. GL entries will be debit to Expense or Inventory, credit to the AP Account (may be a unique GL AP Account if Setup Step 2 was performed.)

5. Remember that because one or more invoices were “prepaid” by credit cards, it will be necessary to run an AP check cycle using the (credit card) Bank Account before these prepayments will be posted through. 6. When prepayments are posted, the GL entries from this post will be a debit to AP, and a credit to the Vendor GL Account. At this point, the Vendor GL Account becomes the AP Liability Account for the credit card balance: the liability is not in the AP GL Account. Bank Reconciliation will show a charge transaction in the credit card Bank Account.

430dca04-3275-497d-a397-1dd06b888b9b.title: ITS Module – Piece Rate Rounding Precision Issue - Reach, Inc
430dca04-3275-497d-a397-1dd06b888b9b.content:
Problem
The client has reported an issue with the Piece Rate rounding logic in the ITS module. Specifically, when the calculated Piece Rate is 0.1442006269592476, Traverse rounds it down to 0.1442. However, the client requires this to round up to 0.1443 if the calculated value exceeds 0.1442 by even the smallest decimal (e.g., 0.0000001), to ensure back-calculated values align with hourly pay.

Example:

-
Piece Rate = 0.1442006269592476

-
Rounded = 0.1442

-
Standard Pieces = 111.65

-
Expected Hourly Rate = 16.1000

-

8242a862-64d7-4ccb-b3cb-07220c021144.title: How to set up GL Budget Import in Traverse?
8242a862-64d7-4ccb-b3cb-07220c021144.content:
Problem
How to set up GL Budget Import in Traverse?

Resolution
Importing GL Budgets in Traverse:

Similar to other import functionalities available in Traverse, GL Budget data can also be imported into the system using the Standard Import Utility. The process involves defining the import structure and mapping, followed by executing the import operation. The primary steps are outlined below:

Process Overview:

To successfully import GL Budgets, the following steps must be completed:

-
Create the SM Import Layout Definition

-
Set up the SM Import Map Definition

-
Perform the import from the SM Import Mapped Data screen

Step 1: SM Import Layout Definition Setup:

Begin by defining the layout of your import file through the SM Import Layout Definition  under the path: Applications -> System Manager -> Company Setup -> Import Layout Definition. This layout serves as the template that specifies the structure and data types expected during the import process.

Required Fields for GL Budget Import:

The following data fields must be included in the .csv file used for importing GL Budgets:

-
Account ID

-
Budget Year

-
Budget Amounts for each of the 12 fiscal periods (Period 1 through Period 12)

-
Budget Name

Important Note:

- Ensure that the data in the .csv file is correctly formatted and aligns with the expected data types.
- If any data format mismatches exist, you may either:
-
- Pre-format the numbers appropriately within the .csv file, (or)
- Utilize the Data Conversion options within the Import Layout Definition screen to handle conversion during the import process.
- A sample Import File looks as follows:



A sample layout configuration appear as follows:



Step 2: SM Import Map Definition Setup

Once the import layout has been created, proceed to map the data fields in the import file to the corresponding fields in Traverse using the SM Import Map Definition screen under the path: Applications -> System Manager -> Company Setup -> Import Map Definition.

-
Select the previously created layout definition.

-
Map each column from your .csv file to the appropriate field within the Traverse data structure.

-
Save the mapping definition with a unique Import Map ID, which will be used during the import process.





Step 3: Perform Import from 'SM Import Mapped Data

After the mapping is complete, you can initiate the actual data import using the SM Import Mapped Data screen under the path: Applications -> System Manager -> Company Setup -> Import Mapped Data.

Steps:

-
Select the appropriate Import Map ID that was created in the previous step.

-
Choose the .csv import file that contains the budget data in the 'File Name' field. [By default, the file setup in the SM Import Layout Definition would populate along with the 'Map ID']

-
Click on "Read Data" – this will read and load the data into the import utility.

-
Click on "Verify Data" – this step checks for any inconsistencies or formatting issues that might prevent a successful import.

-
If errors are identified, make the necessary corrections in either the .csv file or the layout/map definitions.

-
Once the data is verified and no issues remain, proceed by clicking on "Import" to finalize the process.

0f25c137-4505-43e4-8c85-6e83872227ed.title: Understanding "Ship To" Field Behavior and Customization Options in Traverse
0f25c137-4505-43e4-8c85-6e83872227ed.content:
Problem
The customer has observed that the "Ship To" field on the Sales Order (SO Orders) screen is currently optional, which can lead to incomplete order information and potential fulfillment issues. They would like to ensure that this field is always filled out during order entry to prevent errors and ensure accurate delivery.

Resolution
Currently, Traverse does not provide a built-in or configurable option to make the "Ship To" field mandatory on the Sales Order (SO Orders) screen. By system design, if this field is left blank during order entry, Traverse will automatically default the shipping address to match the Bill To address. While this behavior ensures that the order can still be processed, it may not reflect the actual intended shipping destination in all cases.

To enforce mandatory entry of the "Ship To" field and prevent users from proceeding without specifying a shipping address, a system customization would be required. This customization would involve altering the validation rules on the SO Orders screen to trigger a warning or error if the field is left blank.

Please note that such a change falls outside the scope of standard product functionality and would be considered a billable engagement.

54359784-e0e0-4d0c-a0f7-c7b6348652f8.title: SO Post Transactions is timing out with Avalara Integration
54359784-e0e0-4d0c-a0f7-c7b6348652f8.content:
Problem
The client is encountering a timeout error specifically when attempting to post Sales Order batches from the SO Post Transactions screen in Traverse, while integrated with Avalara for tax calculation in Build 24355.



NOTE: Updating the 'Timeout Settings' under the View -> Preferences did not help with this instance.

Resolution
The performance issue related to Sales Order posting has been addressed through the Change request DEV-268118.



The resolution focuses on reducing SQL locking in a multi-user environment. Specifically, the Avalara and customer aging processes have been moved to separate SQL transactions. Additionally, a new SO business rule, 'Commit Transaction During Posting Transactions', has been introduced. This rule defaults to 'Yes', but when set to 'No', users must manually commit SO transactions to Avalara using the 'Commit Tax Integration Transactions' function.



Initial performance tests show an improvement of approximately 10%. The changes were included in the May release, with Build 25143.





Workaround:

In the meantime, as a temporary workaround, running EXEC sp_updatestats (Update Statistics) against the Client's Database from the SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) has shown to improve processing time from 5 minutes down to 20 seconds in testing in a Sandbox.

f4754695-9b59-4812-92a3-66d489577a78.title: How to avoid the usage of duplicate Invoice Numbers in AP?
f4754695-9b59-4812-92a3-66d489577a78.content:
Problem
How to avoid the usage of duplicate Invoice Numbers in AP?

Resolution
To prevent the use of duplicate invoice numbers within the system, we can implement a safeguard by configuring the relevant Business Rule. Specifically, by setting the 'Check for Duplicate Invoice Numbers' option to 'Yes' in the Business Rules settings, the system will automatically check each new invoice number entered to see if it matches an invoice number previously used for that vendor.

This setting ensures that any attempt to create an invoice with a number that already exists in the system will be flagged with a notification, "This invoice number has already been used," alerting the user that it is a duplicate invoice. Traverse will still allow the user to use this invoice number however, if they choose to ignore the message. Traverse specifically checks for duplicate invoice numbers by vendor, and will not flag an invoice number that matches an invoice number used for another vendor. This notification will thus help to prevent the use of duplicate invoice numbers in the future.





In order to get this done, the User needs to follow the below steps:

i. Access the SM Business Rules under the path: Applications -> System Manager -> Company Setup -> Business rules:



ii. Choose the 'AP-Accounts Payable' module under Applications:



iii. Set the Business rule ' 'Check for Duplicate Invoice Numbers' entry to 'Yes'. Then click on 'Apply' and 'OK' to save the changes.

Use the Account Mask function to define or change a company's account numbering structure. Before assigning account masks, choose the number of segments and the type (alphanumeric, numeric, or both) of characters used in the account numbering structure. Segments are generally used to define main account numbers, subaccount numbers, divisions, departments, and so forth.

- Enter the current fiscal year in the Current Fiscal Year field.
- Select a segment, then enter the account mask in the Mask field using the following characters:
- Specify the length of the segment in the Length field.
- Enter a description of the segment in the Description field.
- Enter an abbreviation for the segment in the Abbreviation field.
- Click the Save button, on the toolbar, to save the account mask.Note: You can use the Test Format and Test Input Mask fields to test the newly created mask.

Editing an Account Mask

- Edit the fields as necessary.
- Click the Save button, on the toolbar, to save any changes made to the account mask.

Title: How to Kill a Locked, Hung, or Disconnected User Session on Customer RDS Server

Purpose:
This knowledge base (KB) article provides the steps to terminate a user session that is either locked, unresponsive (hung), or in a disconnected state on a customer's Remote Desktop Services (RDS) server.

Procedure:

- Identify the Correct RDS Server:
- Refer to the customer’s install survey to obtain the RDS server details.
- Use remote desktop to log in to the respective customer’s RDS server with appropriate credentials.
- Access Task Manager:
- Once logged in, right-click on the taskbar and select Task Manager.
- Alternatively, press Ctrl + Shift + Esc to open Task Manager.

- Locate the User Session:
- In Task Manager, click on the Users tab.
- Review the list of active, disconnected, or hung user sessions.
- Identify the specific user session that needs to be terminated.
- Terminate the Session:
- Right-click on the identified session and select Sign Off.
- This will forcibly terminate the user's session and release any locked system resources.

- Post-Termination Steps:
- Update the relevant Salesforce case to inform the user that their session has been successfully terminated.
- Confirm whether the user is able to log in again without issues.

Note:
Use this procedure only when necessary, and always ensure proper authorization before terminating any user session. Unexpected termination may cause data loss if the user had unsaved work.

1c0f6371-2185-4658-80fd-6798ef4f2294.title: SO-Interactive View_Detailed order view
1c0f6371-2185-4658-80fd-6798ef4f2294.content:
Problem
The "SO-Interactive View_Detailed Order View" report on a specific User's Traverse system takes an unusually long time to generate. When attempting to run the report, the screen displays a loading animation (moving circles), but the results never appear.

-
The issue occurs specifically when the user runs the report from her user login on her Traverse installation.

-
When tested using a different user login on the affected user’s computer, the report loads successfully within a few seconds.

-
Additionally, the report functions as expected when run on another computer using the same user credentials.

Other interactive views on that User's Traverse system are working normally, indicating the issue is isolated to the "Detailed Order View" within the SO-Interactive View module.

Resolution
Upon investigation, it was confirmed that the setup and configuration for the "SO-Interactive View_Detailed Order View" were correct.

Since other interactive views were functioning normally on the specific user's Traverse, we proceeded with additional troubleshooting steps focused on potential user-specific cached data.

As part of the resolution process, we cleared the application-specific Appdata stored in the user’s AppData directory. This data can sometimes become corrupted or bloated, potentially impacting the performance or accessibility of specific views in Traverse.



Steps To Follow:

-
Navigate to the following location on the affected user's workstation:
C:\Users\%USERPROFILE%\AppData\Roaming\Open Systems, Inc\TRAVERSE\

-
Deleted the contents of the TRAVERSE folder to clear any cached application data and settings that might have been interfering with the view.

-
Logged out of Traverse and then logged back in with the affected User’s credentials.

- The deleted 'AppData' contents will be recreated once the Client relaunches the Traverse Application.

After completing these steps, the "SO Detailed Order View" within the SO-Interactive View module became accessible and loaded as expected without delay.

This indicates that clearing the AppData folder helped resolve any cached data conflicts or corruption related to that specific view.

c6763d41-cf01-4d8c-a84c-a4926bcdcb19.title: Getting error "Unable to connect to the remote server" while trying to make credit card payments.
c6763d41-cf01-4d8c-a84c-a4926bcdcb19.content:
Problem
We are experiencing issues with setting up USB credit card swipers on two newly installed computers at our store. Previously, we had a fully functional setup with these swipers, but since transitioning to the new machines, the swipers are no longer working as expected. We require assistance in properly configuring the swipers on both computers to restore full functionality for processing credit card transactions.

Resolution
Note: Traverse supports various payment service integrations. Some customers process payments using stored credit card information within Traverse, others enter credit card details for one-time use, and some utilize credit card swipers—commonly referred to as pin pad or EMV devices—to process external payments.

In this particular case, the customer is attempting to process payments through a pin pad device.

Process Overview:
For example, when working with a sales order, the user selects "Payments," prompting the External Payments screen to appear. At this point, they check the box to enable the pin pad device and click "OK." The expectation is that the system will then allow them to process the credit card through the swiper device.

Issue Encountered:
However, upon clicking "OK," an error message is displayed: "Unable to connect to the remote server."

This indicates a failure in establishing communication between the system and the pin pad device, which is preventing payment processing.

Basic Checks:

1. Begin by verifying that the payment service is properly configured in the Payment Service Integration Setup screen within Traverse.

Path for navigation: Application> System Manager> Setup and Maintenance> Payment Service Integration.
A correctly configured setup should reflect all necessary service details and credentials.

In this case, the customer is using OEExpress (OpenEdge) as their payment service provider. Ensure the following:

-
The payment service is selected and active.

-
All required fields (such as service URL, merchant credentials, terminal ID, etc.) are accurately populated.

-
The configuration matches the specifications provided by OpenEdge for EMV or pin pad device integration.

Improper or incomplete setup in this screen can prevent the system from communicating with the pin pad device, potentially leading to errors such as:
"Unable to connect to the remote server."

2.

2.1 Additional Configuration Check – TPS Settings in Business Rules:

Ensure that the setup is properly configured in the TPS (Third-Party Services) settings under Business Rules within the System Manager module.

Important Note:
You must assign an AR Payment Method for each integrated payment provider, including Cayan, OpenEdge, PayPal, and/or Vantiv.
If a value is not selected for the applicable AR Payment Method, external-type credit card payments (including those processed through pin pad or EMV devices) will not function correctly.

A properly configured TPS setting will include:

-
A selected and valid AR Payment Method corresponding to the payment provider in use. Here it would be OEExpress.

-
If you utilize Level 3 credit card processing, enter a Default Commodity Code to use if there is no commodity code assigned to inventory and non-inventory items. Note: If you are unsure whether you use Level 3 processing, contact your credit card processing provider.

-
Select an External Payment Processing Type:

Select Early to collect funds from the payment provider, as well as record the receipt of funds, before the source transaction is posted. Payment processing occurs when saving a shipped order.

Select Delayed to collect funds from the payment provider and record the receipt of funds after the source transaction is posted.

Example of a correct setup:

2.2 Also check whether payment provider has been setup:

In the System Manager Business Rules, in the SM Defaults – Miscellaneous section, or SM Defaults- Services section, the payment provider is setup. Here it would be OEEXpress.



3. If all of the above configurations are correct but payment processing is still failing, there is one more critical item to check.

For OpenEdge Users Only:

If you are using a card reader device (such as an EMV or pin pad), it is essential to install the RCM Windows_GA.exe utility. This software enables proper communication between Traverse and the card reader device.

The RCM program includes a Device Configure option, which allows you to assign or modify the communication port used by the device (e.g., COM4, COM6). Setting the correct port is crucial for successful payment processing.

The executable file required to install the RCM utility is attached to this article.

How to Verify Installation:

-
Look for the RCM icon in the system tray (bottom-right corner of the screen).

-
Alternatively, open Apps & Features in Windows to confirm that RCM Windows_GA is listed among the installed programs.

Once all of the above configurations are properly set and the required components are installed, the specific workstation will be fully equipped to process credit card payments through Traverse using the card reader device.

8287f4d2-949e-492d-990e-03f270c87d58.title: How to resolve the error 'Incomplete Tasks exists' while closing a Project in Project Costing?
8287f4d2-949e-492d-990e-03f270c87d58.content:
Problem
How to resolve the error 'Incomplete Tasks exists' while closing a Project in Project Costing?

Resolution
Resolving the “Incomplete Tasks Exist” Error in Project Closure:

When we encounter the “Incomplete tasks exist” error while attempting to close a project in PC, it indicates that one or more tasks tied to that project remain in an active status. To correct this, we should follow the detailed steps below:

I. A. Review Associated Tasks in the Project Status View:

-
Navigate to Project Costing -> Interactive View -> Project Status View.

-
Use the Project ID filter to display only the tasks belonging to the project we wish to close.

-
In the resulting list, locate any tasks marked as Active. [Tip: We can add or remove columns via the Column Chooser if Status or Task ID is not visible in our current view.]

-
Review if there are any 'Active' Tasks. Expand each line to see a breakdown for each active task. If there is any outstanding work that needs to be done, we need to complete the Active Task first before closing the 'Project'

I. B. Close Individual Tasks (If Necessary):

If the project still will not close:

-
Go back to Project Costing -> Periodic Processing -> Close Projects.

-
In the Tasks sub‑grid, identify any remaining open tasks.

-
Close the Open task (if any) by selecting the Task and clicking OK.

-
After all tasks are closed here, retry closing the overall project.



By ensuring every associated task is first completed or closed, we can eliminate the “Incomplete tasks exist” error and can successfully close our project.









If Traverse still did not allow us to Close the Project, the User might consider doing the below:

II. A. Update the Status of the Task:

-
Navigate to Project Costing -> Periodic Processing -> Change Projects.

-
Select the Project and Task

-
Update the Status to 'Completed' and then click on 'OK'.



II. B. Attempt to Close the Project:

Once all tasks appear as complete:

-
Return to Project Costing -> Periodic Processing -> Close Projects.

-
Select the project and attempt to close it again.

-
The system should now allow the project to transition to Closed without error.

59afe70b-b8fc-47db-87e7-9f180ffe1c28.title: How to resolve the error 'Date/numeric value(s) are outside the acceptable range. Please check the error details for more information.' while posting the PO Purchases Journal?
59afe70b-b8fc-47db-87e7-9f180ffe1c28.content:
Problem
When a user manually creates a purchase order and accidentally pastes a part number (for example, 1234567890) into the EntryNum column of the grid rather than into the Item ID field, the system allows the transaction to be saved without any validation or warning. As a result, the order can be received and invoiced normally. However, when the user attempts to print the PO Purchases Journal, an error is encountered:

Date/numeric value(s) are outside the acceptable range. Please check the error details for more information.



Detailed Error message:

220 : Arithmetic overflow error for data type smallint, value = 1234567890. : Procedure{dbo.trav_PoTransactionJournal_proc} (.Net SqlClient Data Provider)

Resolution
This is due to the presence of the 'Datatype' being configured as 'Smallint' in the stored procedure. [If the Entry number lies within the range of –32,768 up to 32,767, Traverse would process the PO Journals without any issues]



This had been addressed in the Change Request #87926 [DEV-227715] and was fixed in the Traverse Build 24138. In this Build, the Data Type for the 'EntryNum' had been updated to 'Int', referring Integer.



If the Client is below this Build, they would need to upgrade, and subsequently Traverse should let them process the affected purchase order.



Alternatively, they can opt for a Services project to manually update the 'Stored Procedure' in their existing Build.

62c66cbf-49a5-43bc-b406-dd8cbdbcf64d.title: Summary history view not loading in AP, AR, IN and GL, and subsequently causing Traverse to crash
62c66cbf-49a5-43bc-b406-dd8cbdbcf64d.content:
Problem
Summary history view not loading in AP, AR, IN and GL, and subsequently causing Traverse to crash:



When attempting to open the Summary History View under the Interactive View of the enlisted modules, the User is receiving the below error message:
"Attempted to read or write protected memory. This is often an indication that other memory is corrupt"

This causes the entire program to crash.

Resolution
In Change Request #95609, our team addressed a rendering anomaly in 3D reports that emerged following a recent Windows update. This issue, rooted in the way hardware acceleration interacts with certain Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) configurations, has been fully resolved in the May 2025 Service Pack (Build 25143).

Root Cause:
The underlying cause was traced to graphics hardware acceleration settings conflicting with specific RDP display drivers. When enabled, hardware acceleration could trigger visual distortions or failures in the rendering of 3D report components.



Resolution and Enhancement:
To give administrators direct control over this behavior, we have introduced a new setting within Traverse that allows hardware acceleration to be toggled on or off at runtime—no registry edits or external scripts required. Internal testing across diverse RDP hosts and virtual desktop environments has demonstrated that disabling hardware acceleration through this new option reliably restores correct 3D report display, without impacting other system functions.



Implementation Steps:

-
Upgrade to Build 25143.

-
In Traverse, navigate to View -> Preferences.

-
Locate the “Enable Hardware Acceleration” setting.

-
Update the field to 'False' to disable acceleration, and then click Save.

- Now, the User should be able to pull up the 'Interactive Views' without any issues

Once applied, all 3D reports will render correctly, and no further visual artifacts should occur in supported RDP environments.

How to enable Traverse to auto-sync only the 'Active' AR Customers records to CRM?

Resolution
When configuring the automated customer-data synchronization in Traverse Actions, we need to add a filter to ensure that only customers with an Active status are synced to the CRM.



This filter reduces clutter in downstream applications and prevents inactive or legacy records from being unnecessarily synced. In order to add this, the User needs to follow the below steps:

139d9844-abbc-4e57-95aa-9de30578e3d0.title: Changing cost in Inventory
139d9844-abbc-4e57-95aa-9de30578e3d0.content:
Problem
How to Change Costs in Inventory when using Standard costing or needing to update a Base cost. I need to change the cost to a negative cost, how do I do this?

Resolution
-

There are two primary ways to change the cost of an item in the Inventory module when using Standard costing or needing to update a Base cost, depending on whether you're updating a single item or making bulk changes across multiple items. This article outlines both options and highlights when to use each.

Option 1: Change Item Cost via Setup and Maintenance (Single Item)

Use this method when you want to quickly update the cost of a single item.

Steps:

-
Navigate to: Inventory >Setup and Maintenance → Items → [Select Item] → Location Tab

-
Locate the desired item and select the relevant Location.

-
In the cost field, update the Standard or Base costs value directly.

- Update the Standard cost if you are using Standard costing.
- Update the Base cost as needed. The Base Cost is used for calculating prices in the Sales Order pricing setup, as a markup from cost.
- (Average cost and Last cost will automatically change based on the costs of the incoming inventory from purchase orders, etc. Any updates you make to this will get written over as Traverse automatically calculates the cost.)
- You can enter a negative value here if needed.



-
Save your changes.

🔹 Note: This method is ideal for quick, one-off updates. However, there is no audit trail or log of changes when done this way.

Option 2: Change Item Cost via Item Cost Change Screen (Multiple Items + Audit Log)

This method is recommended when updating costs for multiple items or when a log of cost changes is required for auditing or tracking purposes.

Step-by-Step Instructions

Step 1: Open Item Cost Change
Navigate to: Inventory → Periodic Processing → Item Cost Change

Step 2: Apply Filters (Optional)

-
Filter by Item ID, Location ID, or leave blank to include all items.

-
Choose how to sort the list: Item ID or Location ID.

Step 3: Configure Settings

-
Check Allow Negative Costs to permit costs to fall below zero.

-
Select Adjustment Base:

-
Base – modifies the current base cost.

-
Standard – modifies the standard cost.

Step 4: Select Adjustment Type

-
Amount – Specify a fixed dollar value increase or decrease.

-
Percent – Specify a percentage-based adjustment.

Step 5: Enter Adjustment Value

-
Enter a positive number to increase cost.

-
Enter a negative number to reduce cost (including making it negative).

Step 6: Execute Cost Change

-
Click OK to apply the cost adjustments.

🔹 Why use this method?
This screen is especially useful for:

-
Making bulk updates to multiple items.

-
Keeping a record of changes for compliance or review.

Upon making the changes the negative cost would reflect for the specific Item under IN Items

c8a7c612-326c-4533-bd36-6db892dea259.title: How Do I Use Work Schedules in On-Time Web?
c8a7c612-326c-4533-bd36-6db892dea259.content:
Problem
Do I need to create work schedules in On-Time Web?  How do I create work schedules and why?

Resolution
How Do I Use Work Schedules in On-Time Web?

Work Schedules in On-Time Web is an optional feature that allows you to provide work schedules to your employees and report when they are early, late, or miss their scheduled time (Scheduled vs. Actual Report).

You can set up as many Work Schedules as needed, from shifts to part-time schedules.  The process is simple.

- Create a Master Schedule
- Navigate to Time Management>Work Schedules>Master Work Schedules
- Click the New button on the bottom of the screen
- Name the Master Schedule in the Master Schedule Name Field and complete the Master Description.
- Complete the Shift Times
- Start Time – The time the shift starts.
- Go Lunch – The time the employee's lunch time begins.
- Return Lunch – The time the employee’s lunch time ends.

- Enter Breaks – enter the number of breaks that the employees are allowed for the shift.
- Days Off – Select the Days Off for the work week.
- Save

- Create Employee Work Schedules – Once the Master Schedule has been created, then you can apply the Master Schedule to Employees.
- Navigate to the Create Employee Work Schedules tab.
- Date Range – Click the date field and enter the range you would like to create the schedule for.  You can create them for a Day, Week, Month, Year or a Custom Range.
- Master Schedule – Click the drop-down and select the Master Schedule you are using to create the Work Schedule.
- Employees – Select the Employees that you want to create the work schedule for.  You can select Supervisor Groups as well to expedite the creation of the work schedule.
- Overwrite Existing Schedules – Select Yes/No whether you want to overwrite previously created for the employees.
- Preview the Work Schedule
- Once you preview the Work Schedule, click Create Schedules.

- Edit Employee Work Schedules – There will be times that after you create the work schedules, you will need to edit or update an Employee Work Schedule. This will make your Scheduled vs. Actual Report more accurate.
- Employees – Select the Employee whose schedule you would like to edit.
- Date Range – Click the calendar field and find the date that you need to edit. The work schedule should appear in the table, then edit the work schedule.
- Edit Schedules – After you have edited the table then click Edit Schedules to save the edits.

198aae79-1bf7-4752-af73-2d0e27631cf3.title: How to resolve the error: 'Requirement ID' does not exist' in 'Record Labor Time' function?
198aae79-1bf7-4752-af73-2d0e27631cf3.content:
Problem
How to resolve the error: 'Requirement ID' does not exist' in 'Record Labor Time' function?



Detailed Error message:

===================================

'Requirement ID' does not exist.

===================================

'Requirement ID' does not exist. (TRAVERSE.Business.MfgProduction)

------------------------------
Program Location:

at TRAVERSE.Business.Manufacturing.LaborTimeProvider.UpdateOrders()
at TRAVERSE.Business.Manufacturing.LaborTimeProvider.UpdateData()
at TRAVERSE.Client.Manufacturing.LaborTimeControl.UpdateData(Int32 index)

When we encounter the error indicating that the Requirement ID field is mandatory in the MP Record Labor Time function, it means that this key identifier (mandatory field) has not been entered before saving the record.

How to Correct It?

i. Open the MP Record Labor Time screen. And pull up the required 'Employee ID':



ii. Right‑click any column header and select Column Chooser.



iii. From the list of available fields, drag Requirement ID back into your grid view.



iv. In the newly visible Requirement ID column, enter the appropriate identifier for each labor entry.
