a513127f-a3fb-48ba-b63e-9fee3e7d5d5b.title: "Unit is Invalid" while processing or deleting a Purchase Order
a513127f-a3fb-48ba-b63e-9fee3e7d5d5b.content:
Problem
A "Unit is Invalid" error message with no details can occur during Purchase Order processing.  It can happen when receiving an item, deleting an item, or when deleting the entire Purchase Order.  Once cause of this is when a Non-Inventory Item is created on a Purchase Order, and then subsequently an Inventory Item with the same Item ID is created in Inventory.  To determine if this is the case, call up the Purchase Order in the PO Order View, and add the column for Item Type.  If any of the line items have an Item Type of 0 (Non-inventory Item), but you can also find the Item ID in Inventory, then this is the cause of the error.

Resolution
The line item with the Non-inventory item needs to be deleted.  To do this Accounts Payable must first be unintegrated with Inventory.  Follow these steps.

- Confirm that there are no users in the system processing in Purchase Order or Accounts Payable.
- Go to System Manager -> Company Setup-> Business Rules
- Go to the Accounts Payable module section
- In the Intergration section, change the Integration between Accounts Payable and Inventory to "No".
- Go to Purchase Order, call up the order, and delete the line item with the Non-inventory Item on it.
- Go back to the Business Rules program and change the integration setting between Accounts Payable and Inventory back to "Yes".
- All uses can go back in to Purchase Order and Accounts Payable.

6aa01cce-aed6-4ca9-ba7b-7ef02f309a4f.title: What is the Global Search Bar for and how to enable it?
6aa01cce-aed6-4ca9-ba7b-7ef02f309a4f.content:
Problem
What is the Global Search Bar for and how to enable it?

Resolution
A search engine-style search control is available in the Traverse shell, providing quick access to information with limited data entry.

The global search is based on catalogs, which define the tables and fields to query for a certain type of search. The global search feature includes sales, sales history, purchases, and purchase history catalogs that query sales and purchase order transactions and transaction history. Additional standard catalogs, including AR transaction history, PS transaction history, PC billing history, and SD invoice history will be released in future updates.

Before you use the global search, you need to install the Full-Text Search service on the SQL Server instance you are using. Make sure the service is running.

- The Full-Text Search service is available if you install SQL Server Express with Advanced Services. If you are running a full-featured version of SQL Server, such as SQL Server Standard or SQL Server Enterprise, Full-Text Search is included. See Microsoft's website for more information: https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/cc645993.aspx.

If you do not have the Full-Text Search service installed, you will get a message in Traverse when you try to build the catalog.

- For more information about the Full-Text Search service, see the Microsoft website: https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/ms142583.aspx.

You can manage active catalogs, permissions, and schedule a catalog for refreshing data in the Manage Catalog screen in the Traverse Global Server Manager.

Initialize global search

- Open the Manage Catalog program on the System Manager Company Setup menu. Note, by default the Manage Catalog program is hidden on this menu, and may need to be unhidden on the System Menu program and the System Manage Setup and Maintenance menu. Alternately, Select a company for which you want to manage catalogs in the Traverse Server Manager, right-click and select Manage Catalog from the context menu or select Manage Catalog from the Database menu.

- Initialize the catalog(s):
- On the Catalogs tab, select the catalog(s) to build.
- Click the Execute button. When the catalog is built, a notification pop-up window will appear. Click OK.
- Set permissions on the catalog(s):
- On the Permissions tab, select the catalog on which to set permissions, or use the View button on the toolbar to view a group/role and the catalogs it has permission to manage.
- Mark the Selected check box for the group(s) you want to have access to the catalog.

Configure Catalog Refresh Schedule -- Traverse Server Manager

If you want to set up a schedule to refresh a catalog with new data on a regular basis, use the Manage Catalog screen in the Traverse Server Manager.

- Click the Config button for the catalog you want to work with. The Config Schedule screen displays.

- Select a frequency for the catalog refresh from the drop-down list in the Occurs field, or enter a value in the Recurs Every field. Each frequency selection (Daily, Weekly, Monthly) will have different options:
- Daily: Enter the number of day(s) (interval) for the refresh. A recur value of 1 will cause the refresh to run every day, a value of 2 will cause the refresh to run every other day, etc.
- Weekly: Enter the number of week(s) (interval) for the refresh, then select the day(s) of the week on which you want the refresh to occur. A weekly recur value of 1 will cause the refresh to run every week on the selected day(s), a value of 2 will cause the refresh to run every other week on the selected day(s), etc.
- Monthly: Enter the day of the month (1 - 31) and the number of month(s) (interval) for the refresh. A day value of 15 and a recur value of 1 will cause the refresh to run on the 15th of every month, a recur value of 2 will cause the refresh to run on the 15th of every other month, etc.
- In the Repetition section, select the type of recurrence. Each option will have different settings available:
- At a specific time: Enter a Start Time for the job.
- At a specific interval (Second): Enter an interval, then enter a Start Time and an End Time. The interval is how often the job will run. The Start and End times restrict the time frame within which the job runs. An interval of 30 will cause the job to run every 30 seconds. A Start Time of 8:00 am and an End Time of 5:00 pm means the job will run every 30 seconds between the times of 8:00 am and 5:00 pm.
- At a specific interval (Minute): Enter an interval, then enter a Start Time and an End Time. The interval is how often the job will run. The Start and End times restrict the time frame within which the job runs. An interval of 30 will cause the job to run every 30 minutes. A Start Time of 8:00 am and an End Time of 5:00 pm means the job will run every 30 minutes between the times of 8:00 am and 5:00 pm.
- At a specific interval (Hour): Enter an interval, then enter a Start Time and an End Time. The interval is how often the job will run. The Start and End times restrict the time frame within which the job runs. An interval of 3 will cause the job to run every 3 hours. A Start Time of 8:00 am and an End Time of 5:00 pm means the job will run every 3 hours between the times of 8:00 am and 5:00 pm.
- In the Duration section, select the length of time the job will continue to run:
- Enter a Start Date for the job. This is the first date the job will be scheduled to run.
- If you want the job to end on a particular date, mark the Expire check box.
- If you marked the Expire check box, enter an End Date. This is the last date the job will run.
- Press a command button:

Click

To

Schedule

Set all fields to their default values.

Run the task.

Once the catalog(s) are initialized and the group permissions are set, you should be able to perform global searches.

Using global search

You can use the global search function by entering a transaction number, customer number, order date, etc. into the Search... box, then pressing Enter. The results will display in the Global Search window. Any search terms entered will search all of the user's catalogs.

Double-click the result you want to view. The appropriate interactive view will open and display the record(s) for which you searched. For example, when you use the global search with the Sales catalog and receive results, you can double-click on a result to drill down into the SO Order Interactive View to see more information about the order.

Tips:

- You can search on any value that displays in the search results.
- Use And or Or to expand your search to include multiple criteria. For example, enter MN or WI to find all records that include these regions.
- You can use an asterisk (*) as a wildcard, BUT if you do so, you must enclose the search terms inside double quotes. For example, enter "a*" into the global search box to find data that starts with the letter a.

2bee6841-5ae3-4855-a143-2748bf2b7314.title: Unable to Save BR Transactions While Entering a Deposit
2bee6841-5ae3-4855-a143-2748bf2b7314.content:
Problem
BR Transactions are not being saved while attempting to enter a 'Deposit' entry in Traverse. Despite multiple attempts to save the transaction using the 'Save' icon, the system does not retain the entered data.



Furthermore, when the user tries to exit the 'BR Transactions' screen, Traverse displays the following prompt:

"Do you want to close without saving pending changes?"



This indicates that the system has not recognized or committed the save action.

Resolution
This error typically occurs when one or more mandatory fields are left blank in the Deposits tab of the BR Transactions screen. When attempting to save, Traverse may prompt the user with a warning or fail to respond, indicating that required data is missing.



Mandatory Fields in the Deposits Tab:

To ensure a successful save, the following fields must be completed:

FieldDescriptionDeposit NoA required identifier for the deposit slip or transaction.GL AccountThe General Ledger account associated with the deposit.

Note: Other fields such as 'Description' will auto-populate based on the setup in Business Rules (if configured).



Recommended Process for Entering Deposits:

i. Initiate a New Entry:

- Click on the ‘New’ icon in the toolbar to begin a new BR transaction.



ii. Enter Required Deposit Details:

- Trans No: Auto-generated by the system.
- Deposit No: Enter the slip number or payment ID (mandatory).
- Trans Date: Accept or modify the default transaction date.
- Fiscal Period / Year: Enter or accept the default values.
- Reference: Enter a reference or use the default (posts to GL Journal).
- Description: Enter a description or use the default from Business Rules.
- Currency ID: View-only if multicurrency is enabled. Any active currency ID may be used.
- Amount: Enter the deposit amount.
- GL Offset Account: Optional—use to split the deposit across multiple accounts.



iii. View and Edit Detail Entries:

- Expand the entry using the ‘+’ icon beside the 'Trans No' field.
- Line 1 (Debit): Auto-filled; not editable.
- Line 2 (Credit): Auto-filled with the same amount; editable if needed.
- Update Description and Reference fields for distribution if necessary.
- Total Debit / Credit / Balance fields will auto-calculate and display accordingly.





iv. Save the Entry:

- Click the ‘Save’ icon on the toolbar.
- If mandatory fields are missing, when we attempt to close the 'BR Transactions' screen, 'Traverse will display a warning such as:
“Do you want to close without saving pending changes?”



Common Issue: Missing 'Deposit No' Field:

In some cases, the 'Deposit No' column may have been accidentally removed from the screen layout. Since this is a mandatory field, Traverse will block the save action until it is re-added.

Resolution:

i. Right-click on the column headers in the Deposits tab. And select ‘Column Chooser’.



ii. Drag and drop the 'Deposit No' field back into the layout.



iii. Enter the required deposit number. Attempt to save again. And Traverse would then 'Save' the entries and allows the User to post



iv. The User can now close the 'BR Transactions screen, and Traverse will no longer throw the error : ''Do you want to close without saving pending changes?'



v. The User can now proceed with previewing/printing the ' BR Transaction Journal' to confirm the same.



Key Takeaway:

-
Always ensure that the Deposit No and GL Account fields are populated when entering a deposit.

-
If saving fails despite completing all visible fields, verify the screen layout for hidden mandatory fields using the Column Chooser.

43a73fba-efb1-40a4-a517-d06da1766afd.title: How to Prioritize ACH Payments While Excluding Other Posted Transactions from Payment Preparation?
43a73fba-efb1-40a4-a517-d06da1766afd.content:
Problem
How to Prioritize ACH Payments While Excluding Other Posted Transactions from Payment Preparation?

Resolution
To process only ACH (Electronic) payments during a payment run, while leaving all other posted transactions untouched for future processing, we can follow the steps outlined below.



We can achieve this by either manually updating Invoice statuses (or) by using the Vendor Priority Code to facilitate filtering.

Option 1: Manual Status Update for ACH Invoices

i. Post Transactions:
Once the transactions are finalized, post them using the 'AP Post Transactions' function. Then, they will appear in the 'AP Hold/Release Invoices' screen.

ii. Manually Update Status for ACH Payments:

- Review the list of invoices and manually update the status to 'Released' only for those associated with ACH vendors.
- And update the status of rest of the 'Invoices' as either 'Hold' or 'Temp'(Temporary Hold, that is the transactions will be held only for one Payment run, and will automatically turn into 'Release' status after the Payment run)
- This ensures only those invoices are picked up during the 'AP Prepare Payments' step.

- Alternatively, filters can be applied on the 'AP Prepare Payments screen' to include only one Vendor ID for the 'Payment Run':





Option 2: Use Vendor Priority Code to Isolate ACH Payments

This method is recommended for efficiently managing larger volumes of payments:

i. Create a 'Priority Code' for assigning it to 'Vendors' that uses 'ACH':

- Navigate to 'AP Priority Codes' screen under the path: Applications -> Accounts Payable -> Setup and Maintenance -> Priority Codes
- Create a new Priority Code for assigning it to the ACH Vendors. For example, 'A'



ii. Assign Priority Code to ACH Vendors:

- Navigate to 'AP Vendors' screen under the path: Applications -> Accounts Payable -> Setup and Maintenance -> Vendors
- In the 'Defaults' Tab, assign a Priority Code 'A' to all vendors, who will be using ACH (electronic payment).
- Click on the 'Save' icon to save the changes



iii. Navigate to 'AP Change Invoice Status':

- Navigate to 'AP Change Invoice Status' screen under the path: Applications -> Accounts Payable -> Pay Invoices -> Change Invoice Status
- Enter a Vendor ID range that covers all vendors (from the first to the last in our system).
- Ensure the Invoice Due Date is set (default is the current date).



iv. Change Status from 'Released' to 'Hold':

- This step sets all invoices—regardless of vendor—to a 'Hold' status.
- Alternatively, use the 'Temp' status if we prefer a short-term hold for just one payment cycle.
- Click on 'OK' to update the 'Invoice status'



v. Filter by ACH Priority Code and re-release ACH Invoices Only:

- Update the Priority Code range to be from 'A' to 'A', which isolates all ACH vendors.
- Set the Invoice Due Date again (default is today’s date).
- Change the Status from 'Hold' to 'Released', and then click on 'OK'
- Now, only invoices related to ACH vendors will be marked as 'Released'.



vi. Prepare ACH Payments

- Proceed to 'AP Prepare Payments'.
- The system will now include only ACH invoices in this payment run.
- All other invoices remain on hold and will be available in the 'AP Hold/Release Invoices' screen.

NOTE: This method helps segregate ACH payments from others and ensures better control over mixed payment types during your processing cycles. And the rest of the Payments (those involving Paper Checks) can be processed later, based on the User's preference

9a0ce5a5-a468-41cf-bc73-09cb15c3c978.title: Receiving "Nothing to Process" Error in SO Batch while Sales Journal shows entries
9a0ce5a5-a468-41cf-bc73-09cb15c3c978.content:
Problem
The customer encountered the following error message when attempting to print invoices via Sales Order > Transaction Journals > Print Invoice:

"Nothing to process."

Resolution
The Print Invoice option under Sales Order > Transaction Journal > Print Invoice is only enabled if the invoice has not been previously printed or output from the Sales Order.

If the invoices were already printed through Sales Order > Transactions > Order, this option becomes unavailable.

The “Nothing to Process” message you’re seeing in Sales Order > Transaction Journal > Print Invoices appears because the invoices for those Sales Orders have already been printed. This function is intended only for Sales Orders with a Verified transaction type that have not yet had their invoices printed.

If you need to reprint an invoice, please navigate to Sales Order > Order > Print > Invoice.

665b03f2-5ef7-4c31-b3b4-2294f5dc97a3.content:
Problem
How to exclude Zero Balance Customers from the AR Aged Trial Balance Report?

Resolution
To ensure that customers with a zero balance do not appear in the Accounts Receivable (AR) Aged Trial Balance Report, users can make use of a configurable option within the report setup. This option allows clients to generate a more concise and relevant report by omitting customers who have no outstanding balances.



To apply this setting, we need to navigate through the AR Aged Trial Balance Report under the path: Applications -> Accounts Receivable -> Open Invoices -> Aged Trial Balance Report.



Within the Aged Trial Balance Report screen, locate the checkbox labeled “Zero Balance Customers.”



By default, this checkbox may be selected, which includes customers with a zero balance in the report output. To exclude such customers, ensure this checkbox is unchecked before generating the report.



This adjustment helps in refining the report data, allowing the focus to remain solely on customers with pending receivables, thereby making the report more actionable and relevant for financial analysis.

0a0ffb6c-87dc-4213-8020-e8935d5bedd1.title: How to create and modify a copy of an existing Financial Statement without altering the original one?
0a0ffb6c-87dc-4213-8020-e8935d5bedd1.content:
Problem
How to create and modify a copy of an existing Financial Statement without altering the original one?



The User is having a GL Financial Statement, which is already a part of Statement Batch, that includes all the Revenue Accounts. Now, the Client would like to pull up a Financial Statement which is quite a replica but with some tweaks, and they want to retain the original one.

Resolution
When managing financial reporting in Traverse, users may wish to use an existing GL Financial Statement as a baseline but tailor it slightly for alternate reporting needs, such as a department-specific breakdown or exclusion of certain accounts, without altering the original structure used in standard reporting or batches.



In order to get this done, we can create a new setup of the existing Financial statement, but using the 'Copy' feature to transfer the contents over to the new Statement ID and the new Statement Content ID. Then the User can make changes to the GL Statement Contents as required. Now the User can have the updated Financial Statement printed, without disturbing the Statement within the Batch



This process involves:

-
Identifying the original Statement and its associated Content ID

-
Create a new Statement Content ID by copying the existing one and modifying it

-
Create a new Statement ID linked to the modified 'Statement Content ID'

-
This ensures the new version meets our reporting needs without impacting the original

Steps to be followed:

i. Identify the 'Statement ID' to Copy:

-
Begin by reviewing the existing setup within the Statement Batch to locate the Statement ID currently being used.

-
Note the associated Statement Content ID, as this defines the report’s layout and structure.



ii. Create a New Statement Content ID:

-
Navigate to GL Statements and identify the associated 'GL Statement Content ID'



-
Go to GL Statement Contents under the path: Applications → General Ledger → Management Reports Setup → Statement Contents

-
Click the ‘New’ icon to start creating a fresh Statement Content ID.

-
In the ‘Copy From’ field, enter the original Content ID to duplicate its structure and line items into the new ID.



-
Once the copy is created, begin making your modifications:

-
To edit existing rows:
Double-click on the row to open the detail, and adjust the filters, account IDs, or row descriptions as needed.

-
To add a new row:
Use the ‘Add’ or ‘Append’ button and follow these steps:

-
Assign a Sequence Number to determine its placement. (For example, use 110 to insert between lines 100 and 120)

-
Choose the appropriate Row Type (e.g., Detail, Heading, Total)

-
Provide a description (optional)

-
Click the ellipsis (...) button to configure account ranges, filters, or conditions [In this example, we have left only the Revenue generated, and excluded the rest of the entries]

-
After making all desired changes, click ‘Save’ to finalize the new Content ID.



iii. Create a New Statement ID:

-
Navigate to the GL Statements screen:
Applications → General Ledger → Management Reports Setup → Statements

-
Create a new Statement ID and use the ‘Copy’ function to duplicate the statement setup. [We can always start from scratch, if we need to create a new one, different from the existing one]



-
Update the 'Statement Content ID' field with the new Content ID and a relevant description for the duplicate (e.g., "Income Only Statement").

-
Click on 'Save' to save the changes



iv. Observe the Changes:

- Navigate to Applications → General Ledger → Management Reports → Financial Statements

- Pull up the required 'Statement ID' and preview the report.

- And this new Statement should not be affecting the existing Statement sitting within the Statement Batch ID

5dc520fa-c122-432e-bb3a-c772123acd33.title: How to reverse an Invoice with Kitted Item, that has incorrect details of the Kit Components?
5dc520fa-c122-432e-bb3a-c772123acd33.content:
Problem
How to reverse an Invoice with Kitted Item, that has incorrect details of the Kit Components?

Resolution
In Traverse, when a Sales Order (SO) Invoice involving Kit Components is posted, but the invoiced contents differ from the original standard Kit definition [may be due to manual updating of 'Kit Detail'], it is necessary to reverse the transaction to maintain accuracy in financial and inventory records.



To correct the discrepancy, it is recommended to issue a Credit Memo that offsets the original invoice. This ensures that the incorrect invoice is nullified properly and that accounting records remain consistent. And then the User can proceed with creating a new Transaction record with the correct entries in it.



Creating a Credit Memo manually can be prone to errors, especially when the invoice contains multiple Kit Components with complex configurations.



To ensure accuracy and simplify the process, Traverse provides a 'Copy' function that allows users to replicate the contents of an existing invoice.

Steps:

i. Navigate to the SO Orders screen under the path: Applications -> Sales order -> Transactions -> Orders:



ii. Create a new 'Transaction' record using the 'New' icon and then switch the Transaction Type to 'Credit Memo'



iii. Select the appropriate 'Customer ID' in the 'Sold To' field to automatically populate the other mandatory fields that have been configured as default values for that Customer ID.



iv. Use the ‘Copy’ feature to select the original invoice that needs to be reversed.



v. Once copied successfully, Traverse throws the following confirmation message: 'Record(s) successfully copied'



vi. Traverse will auto-populate the Credit Memo with all line items from the original invoice—including kit components, quantities, and prices. Traverse would auto-populate the original Invoice number appropriately in the Credit Memo to maintain traceability.



vii. Review the auto-filled Credit Memo and proceed with saving the Transaction. Now if the User can verify the same by printing the 'Miscellaneous Credits Journal' under the path: Applications -> Sales order -> Transaction Journals -> Miscellaneous Credits Journal:



viii. Then we can proceed with regular process of the Transaction and we can observe that the Items are returned back to the Inventory.

1208f1d1-1bf6-4ea9-89ba-b2879a7bbeab.title: How to Set Up SO Contract Pricing for 'Per Item Pricing'?
1208f1d1-1bf6-4ea9-89ba-b2879a7bbeab.content:
Problem
How to Set Up SO Contract Pricing for 'Per Item Pricing'?

Resolution
The Contract Pricing function in Traverse allows businesses to define custom pricing agreements for their customers, based on specific items, customers, and time periods. One of the supported methods is "Per Item Pricing", where pricing is specified for individual items and item locations.

Important Note: Ensure the business rule Use Contract Pricing SO is set to 'Yes' for the feature to be active.

Steps to Set Up Contract Pricing – Per Item Pricing

i. Launch the Contract Pricing Screen:

-
Navigate to the SO Contract Pricing under the path: Applications -> Sales Order -> Pricing -> Contract Pricing

ii. Create a New Contract Price Record:

-
Click the New button on the toolbar.

-
In the Contract Price ID field, enter a unique ID for the new contract

-
(Optional) Use the Copy From button to duplicate details from an existing Contract Price ID:

-
Choose the source contract.

-
Select which components to copy: General Information, and/or Customers, and/or Items.



iii. Enter General Details:

-
Description: Provide a meaningful description for reference.

-
Per Item Pricing:  Check this box to enable pricing setup for specific items and locations.

-
Start Date / End Date: Define the effective period of the contract. Leave blank for no expiration.



iv. Define Item-Level Pricing (Item Detail Tab):

The Price Detail tab is renamed Item Detail when Per Item Pricing is enabled.

-
Click the Append button to add a new row.

-
Item ID: Select the specific item for which contract pricing should apply.

-
Location ID: Choose the item’s location (if applicable).

-
Break Quantity: Set the quantity threshold for the contract price to take effect.

-
Break UOM: Choose the Unit of Measure applicable for the price break.

a42ada6a-d729-4afd-a094-95516e224a00.title: Why Is the Remittance Section Missing Invoice Details on the Printed Check?
a42ada6a-d729-4afd-a094-95516e224a00.content:
Problem
Why Is the Remittance Section Missing Invoice Details on the Printed Check?

Resolution
To ensure that the remittance information is printed on the bottom half of the check itself (commonly referred to as the check stub), it is important to review and update the relevant business rule configuration.

If the client would prefer the remittance details—such as the list of invoices being paid—to appear directly on the same page as the check, then the business rule setting for ‘Check Saver’ must be set to ‘No’.



Please note:

When the ‘Check Saver’ option is set to either ‘Single’ or ‘Multiple’, Traverse is designed to suppress remittance information on the check page. Instead, it generates a separate remittance advice as an additional report output. This approach is intended to minimize check paper usage or to accommodate printers that require simplified layouts—but may not suit all use cases.



In order to update the changes, we would need to follow the below steps:

-

i. Navigate to Business Rules: Go to the SM Business Rules under the path: Applications -> System Manager -> Company Setup -> Business Rules.

ii. Select Accounts Payable Application: Under the Application section, select Accounts Payable to view the relevant settings. From there, locate the Business Rule labeled "Check Saver" under the Miscellaneous section.

iii. Configure Check Saver Options:

We have three options [No, Single, Multiple] to choose from for the Check Saver function. If we have it set at Single or Multiple, Traverse won't print anything on the original check and will instead print out all the stub information on a second report.

In order to meet our requirements of having the 'Remittance' information printed on the same Check paper, we need to update this setting to 'No' and then click on 'Apply' and 'OK' to save the changes

8ab4c056-6715-493a-90bf-cce7d20183e9.title: Post to masters in OSAS
8ab4c056-6715-493a-90bf-cce7d20183e9.content:
Problem
How to Post the transactions before you produce financial statements or reports

Resolution
Using the Post to Master Function in GL

The Post to Master function transfers transactions from the GL Journal (GLJRxxx) file to the GL Master (GLMAxxx) file for a specified range of periods. This step is essential before generating financial statements or reports.

Note: You can post transactions as often as needed. The system ensures that no transaction is posted more than once.

Transaction Allocation

For each allocated transaction, the system distributes the amounts to the appropriate accounts based on the percentages defined in the allocation record.

Before You Post

Ensure the following precautions are taken:

-
✅ In a multiuser environment, confirm that no other user is accessing the GLJRxxx or GLMAxxx files.

-
✅ If you plan to print the GL Posting Log, make sure the printer is online.

-
✅ Print and review the GL Journal and GL Activity Report to verify that debits and credits are balanced and accurate.

-
✅ Back up all data files to prevent data loss in case of interruptions such as power failure.

Accessing the Post to Master Screen

-
Navigate to the Journal Transactions menu.

-
Select Post to Master.

Posting Steps

-
Enter the range of periods for which transactions should be posted.

-
Enter the range of source codes to post.

-
Select whether to post allocated transactions:

-
Check the box or enter Y to include allocations.

-
Leave unchecked or enter N to skip allocation entries.

Note: Posting allocations takes longer, as the system checks every unposted transaction for allocation details.

-
Choose to print period totals:

-
Select the box or enter Y to print total debits and credits by period.

-
Leave unchecked or enter N to skip totals.

-
Choose to print detail:

-
Select the box or enter Y to include transaction details in the log.

-
Leave unchecked or enter N to omit detail.

-
Select the output device for the GL Master Posting Log.

3da27ed6-6089-4646-8d46-d218bb0850a3.title: Resolving Incorrect Fiscal Year for Depreciation Printout in OSAS
3da27ed6-6089-4646-8d46-d218bb0850a3.content:
Problem
KB Article: Resolving Incorrect Fiscal Year for Depreciation Printout in OSAS

Issue:

A customer reported that when printing January depreciation, the fiscal year was showing as 2026 instead of 2025, even though they were working in General Ledger 2025. They didn't proceed with posting the data due to this issue.



Cause:

This issue occurred because:

-
The Accounting Period Tables for Fixed Assets were mistakenly updated to 2026, likely due to running the Year-End Processing multiple times in Fixed Assets.

-
OSAS may have defaulted to the incorrect year during the depreciation printout due to these settings.










Solution:

-
Verify Accounting Period Settings:

-
Navigate to RM Accounting Periods and check the values there. If the periods are set to 2026, that is likely the source of the issue.



-
Editing Accounting Period Table:

-
The values in the Accounting Period Table (ACPRD) need to be edited. Here’s how:

-
Access the relevant table, ACPRD + Company ID (e.g., ACPRDH for Company ID "H"). Edit the table values to reflect the correct fiscal year (2025).

-
Edit the table values to reflect the correct fiscal year (2025).

-
If you are unsure of the table, locate it by checking the Company ID in the top of the screen or in the MDI menu or in the bottom.










-
To save changes, press Page Down or the equivalent save function.







-
Year-End Processing:

-
If Year-End Processing was run multiple times, the accounting periods may have been updated unintentionally. In such cases, check the table after each run and correct the values as needed.



-
Confirm the Update:

-
Once the table is updated, the correct fiscal year should be displayed when printing the depreciation.

-
Retest the process by running the depreciation printout again to ensure the correct year (2025) is shown.



Additional Notes:

-
Always ensure that Year-End Processing is only run once for each fiscal year. Running it multiple times can inadvertently update tables and cause such issues.

-
If you encounter problems with tables not saving or displaying the incorrect fiscal year after the edit, double-check that the correct Company ID and Accounting Period Table are being accessed.


Conclusion:

This issue can be resolved by manually editing the Accounting Period Table to the correct year and ensuring proper year-end processing. If the issue persists, or if multiple year-end runs have caused inconsistencies, further investigation into the Fixed Assets module and system logs may be required.

6349311a-1c3b-4f8c-ba8e-86cd88ccd15c.title: Need to remove the Lotted records from the SQL DB
6349311a-1c3b-4f8c-ba8e-86cd88ccd15c.content:
Problem
The customer, Laibe Corporation, has reported a discrepancy in their inventory system. According to their records:

-
They do not have any inventory items marked as lotted.

-
They have not assigned any lot numbers to inventory items.

Despite this, entries are still present in the IN Lot Numbers section of their system. As a result, Laibe Corporation has raised a concern and wishes to execute a SQL query against their database to delete one or more records from the IN Lot Numbers table.

This action is intended to clean up unused or orphaned lot number records

Resolution
Executing a query directly against a database is a highly sensitive action and should only be performed when there is a clear and valid business justification. It is not recommended without thorough consideration and appropriate safeguards in place.

We must approach this matter with extreme caution. TRAVERSE Support does not support, recommend, or advise customers to directly execute DELETE operations on database tables. This is not a part of normal processing and poses a significant risk to data integrity, with consequences that are unpredictable and potentially irreversible.

To be clear:

-
We do not suggest this approach.

-
We do not support executing DELETE statements on this table.

-
We advise against performing this operation.

If the customer chooses to proceed, they do so at their own discretion and risk.

That said, the customer’s inquiry essentially pertains to how the SQL DELETE statement works in general, which is within our scope to explain from a language and syntax perspective.

SQL Query:

USE [LAB]
DELETE FROM tblInItemLocLot
WHERE ItemId = ' ' AND LocId = ' '



-
USE [LAB]
Sets the context to the LAB database, ensuring all following operations are executed within this database.

-
DELETE FROM tblInItemLocLot
Executes a DELETE operation on the tblInItemLocLot table. This is the table where the IN-Lot Numbers are stored in the Database.

-
WHERE ItemId = ' ' AND LocId = ' '
(Optional) If the goal is to delete data for a specific item and location, values for ItemId and LocId can be entered here (e.g., ItemId = '12345' AND LocId = 'MN').

-
Omitting the WHERE clause
If the WHERE clause is removed or not specified, the DELETE statement will remove all records in the table — this includes all items that have a lot number.

Before running the query, the data would look like.

1.1 Query execution (with WHERE clause)



1.2 The record containing Item ID "125B-AL" and Loc ID "0" has been deleted.

1.3 Query has been executed to delete all the records from the table.

1.4 Output after execution.

1.5 All records have been deleted.

Final Note:

This information is provided only for internal reference and documentation. If the customer proceeds with this query, they accept full responsibility for any resulting data issues.

bebcae2d-04f1-46b1-a544-61917b1581c2.title: SQL Error while Updating perpetual inventory " Link ID cannot be more than 8 Characters"
bebcae2d-04f1-46b1-a544-61917b1581c2.content:
Problem
when user attempting to update perpetual inventory... Error message reads.
Link ID cannot be more than 8 Characters
**************************************************************
Source contains invalid items. Check item collection to determine invalid entities.



How to resolve?

Resolution
Script:

USE BMS;

GODBCC CHECKIDENT ('tblInPhysCount', NORESEED);

GODBCC CHECKIDENT ('tblInPhysCount', RESEED, 1);

GODBCC CHECKIDENT ('tblInPhysCountDetail', NORESEED);

GO

____________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________

When the user attempts to update Perpetual Inventory, they encounter this error:

"Link ID cannot be more than 8 characters, Source contains invalid items. Check item collection to determine invalid entities."

This error is typically caused by corruption or inconsistencies in the internal identity columns of certain tables involved in the inventory update process—specifically, tblInPhysCount and tblInPhysCountDetail.

These tables often use auto-incrementing identity columns to assign unique Link IDs or other internal identifiers. If the identity value becomes misaligned—such as when records are deleted manually or via a process that doesn’t reset the identity counter properly—then the system might attempt to assign a value that violates constraints (e.g., exceeding the allowed 8-character length or referencing invalid items/entities).

What the Script Does

The script is used to check and reset identity values on the affected tables to ensure that new entries get valid, properly sequenced IDs.

Here's a breakdown:

USE BMS;
GO

Sets the context to the BMS database.

DBCC CHECKIDENT ('tblInPhysCount', NORESEED);
GO

Checks the current identity value in tblInPhysCount without changing it. This is mainly for informational purposes.

DBCC CHECKIDENT ('tblInPhysCount', RESEED, 1);
GO

Resets the identity seed in tblInPhysCount so the next inserted record will have an identity value of 2 (since 1 is the seed and it increments after that). This helps resolve issues where the identity has jumped to a high or invalid value.

DBCC CHECKIDENT ('tblInPhysCountDetail', NORESEED);
GO

Again, checks the current identity value of tblInPhysCountDetail without reseeding, used for diagnosis or confirmation.

In Summary

-
The issue arises due to misaligned or corrupted identity values in physical count tables.

-
The error about the Link ID suggests that a new ID being generated may be too long (e.g., more than 8 characters due to an inflated identity value).

-
The DBCC CHECKIDENT commands are used to check and reset these identity values to restore normal behavior and prevent errors during updates.

405322b8-45bb-46bc-b987-403e6db2aae5.title: DocUnity integration with Microsoft Dynamics 365 – SQL NOLOCK error
405322b8-45bb-46bc-b987-403e6db2aae5.content:
Problem
A customer utilizing DocUnity to connect with Microsoft Dynamics 365 is encountering a recurring error due to the use of the NOLOCK SQL hint. The issue arises during the generation of a report within DocUnity that retrieves the Part ID by referencing the associated Party ID linked to an Account Number.

Microsoft Dynamics 365 operates on Dataverse, which supports a subset of SQL but does not support the NOLOCK hint. This incompatibility is resulting in execution errors when DocUnity attempts to run queries that include NOLOCK.

The core objective is to determine whether the NOLOCK hint in the query generated by DocUnity can be removed or conditionally bypassed when interacting with Dataverse, to ensure seamless data retrieval and compatibility.

Resolution
The DocUnity query builder generates standard T-SQL queries based on setup parameters, but it automatically includes the NOLOCK optimizer hint in all queries. This behavior is currently hardcoded and cannot be disabled.

To address the resulting incompatibility with Microsoft Dataverse—which does not support the NOLOCK hint—two potential workarounds are recommended:

-
Establish a Linked Table or External SQL Connection:
Create a linked table or establish an external connection within a SQL Server instance. This may allow the query to execute properly, but further evaluation is needed to determine whether SQL Server processes the query directly or routes it through the Dataverse query engine.

-
Replicate Dataverse Data into SQL Server:
To avoid compatibility issues and support more flexible reporting, the Dataverse dataset can be replicated into a SQL Server–compatible environment. This approach would allow full control over query structure and eliminate the limitations caused by the NOLOCK hint.

These options provide paths to maintain functionality while ensuring compatibility with Dataverse.

To process customer refunds effectively in Traverse, it's essential to configure a dedicated payment method. This ensures that refund transactions are accurately recorded and directed to the appropriate accounts.

It's recommended not to select our cash account for these types of transactions. Instead, we can use a dedicated account, such as a 'Refund Clearing' or 'Write-Off' account, to accurately reflect the nature of the transaction.

i. Navigate to AR Payment Methods under the path: Applications -> Accounts Receivable  -> Setup and Maintenance -> Payment Methods

ii. Pull up the required 'Payment Method' tied to refunds, and update the 'Payment Type' and the 'GL Acct Debit' fields accordingly

7. Confirm the new password, then check the option to **Unlock the user account**.
8. Click **OK** to complete the process.

- Send the updated credentials to the user’s official email address.
- Alternatively, use a secure communication method, such as a **private note link** within the associated **Salesforce case**, to share the username and password.

TO unlock the user account:

Right click on the user account and click on properties and go to account tab there check the unlock account check box and click on apply and ok.

87de99b6-ffca-4632-92bf-9c73bdfb16e0.content:

Sandbox refresh in Aptean SaaS with production Data

Open Azure Storage Management.

Find the SQL Server name and select the Company DB listed in the Excel file.

Click on the most recent backup.

Select Generate Shared Access Signature (SAS).

c42f2e31-df7a-469c-b79a-7662b20cfa06.title: YayPay Expired

ecccc57d-1c62-4f30-88dd-ff4459eab936.title: How to resolve the error 'Print Status' showing as 'Failed' while attempting to print from Traverse?
ecccc57d-1c62-4f30-88dd-ff4459eab936.content:
Problem
How to resolve the error 'Print Status' showing as 'Failed' while attempting to print from Traverse?

Resolution
This error typically occurs when the Form Printer record for the associated form is either missing or not correctly configured with the appropriate printer. It prevents the system from properly routing the print job, especially for processes such as check printing, remittance, or other forms printing.



Steps to Resolve:

i. Navigate to the Form Printers Setup Screen:

Access the SM Form Printers configuration screen by following the path below: Applications -> System Manager -> Company Setup -> Form Printer



ii. A. Check for Existing Printer Record:

- If a record already exists for the Form, that we attempted to print, verify that the correct printer is selected in the 'Printer' dropdown for the specific 'Form' record
- If the printer listed is incorrect or outdated, select the correct printer from the available dropdown options.



ii. B. Add a New Form Printer Record (if none exists)

-
If no record is found for the form, click ‘New’ to add a new entry.

-
Enter the Form ID and select the appropriate printer from the ‘Printer’ dropdown.



iii. Save the Configuration

9c2db6be-3363-46e6-a856-3301f3d7f4ec.title: How to Create a Production Order in MFG - Production
9c2db6be-3363-46e6-a856-3301f3d7f4ec.content:
Problem
How to Create a Production Order in MFG - Production

Resolution
Go to MFG-Production > Production Orders > Production Orders, and click the “+” button to create a new production order.
Accept the system-generated number or enter your own (based on business rule settings).

Select an assembly that has a valid manufacturing BOM (not a planning bill).

Choose the inventory location where the finished product will be stored.

Select the person responsible for the order.
Select the revision from the Revision Number field.

The default revision will populate automatically — update if necessary, Description populates based on the assembly; edit if needed.

Enter or accept the Release Number, select the Customer ID (if applicable), enter the Quantity, and choose the Unit of Measure.

Set the Estimated Finish Date — the system will auto-calculate a suggested Estimated Start Date, which you can accept or override.

Finally, choose the appropriate Status (New, Planned, Firm Planned, or Released) based on the production stage.

The production order has been successfully created.

3b5df3c5-2903-41d0-8a66-22a4a69cda4d.title: How a Production Order Impacts the General Ledger
3b5df3c5-2903-41d0-8a66-22a4a69cda4d.content:
Problem
How a Production Order Impacts the General Ledger

Resolution
To demonstrate how Production Orders affect the General Ledger and which GL accounts are impacted, for testing, we created a Production Order in our test environment and posted it. Below, you can find the Transaction History and the corresponding Post Log:

Transaction View:

Account ID for Finished Good (Item) is 01, and for Raw Material, the Account ID is: LM (Which can be found under the IN Items set-up):

Note the Operation ID for the Assembly (Bill of Materials) that we have used is:

When we go into that Operations ID, we can find the Labour Setup Type ID and Machine Group ID:

When you go into those then you can be able to find the GL Offset Accounts for those:

To explain in detail how General Ledger (GL) entries are created from Production Orders based on the above provided screenshots: (Taking this scenario as an example)

1. Raw Material Consumption

When raw materials are issued to production:

- Debit: Finished Goods Work in Process GL Account: 123000 (Account Code: 01, refer to the above image)

- Machine Group ID: GL Offset Account for machinery (e.g., Machine Overhead Account).

When labor/machine resources are consumed:

- Debit: Finished Goods Work in Process GL Account: 123000 (Account Code: 01, refer to the above images)
- Credit: As per the GL Offset setup under the Labor Type (GL Account: 503000) and Machine Groups (GL Account: 610000), refer to the above images.

3. Completion of Finished Goods

When production is finalized:

- Debit: Finished Goods Inventory GL Account: 120000 (Account Code: 01, refer to the above images)
- Credit: Finished Goods Work in Process GL Account: 123000 (Account Code: 01, refer to the above images)

196a8a92-6a87-4f80-97ed-9094d0135062.title: How to Define ACH File Names with Application ID or Timestamp or both?
196a8a92-6a87-4f80-97ed-9094d0135062.content:
Problem
How to configure 'Dynamic File Naming' for ACH Files being exported out of Traverse?

Resolution
When setting up ACH file generation in Traverse, we have the option to define a default file name format that will be used each time an ACH file is created.



This setup can include both:

- Static text
- Dynamic components using wildcards

This allows the system to automatically insert details such as the application ID (AP or PA or AR) and the current date/time.

Step to be followed:

i. Navigate to SM Bank Accounts:

Access the SM Bank Accounts screen under the path: Applications -> System Manager ->Company Setup -> Bank Accounts:



ii. Pull up the required Bank Account ID:

Load the required 'Bank Account ID' for which the ACH File will be created.



iii. Navigate to the 'ACH' Tab and observe the current setup:

- Access the ACH tab and locate the 'Default File Name / Prefix' field.
- The current configuration generates a file named 'DDEPOSIT.CPU', where 'DDEPOSIT' represents the Direct Deposit file name and 'CPU' indicates the Company ID, appended automatically by the system.
- We can view a preview of the resulting file name in the 'Sample File' field for confirmation.



iv. Update the Desired Default File Name Format:

- In the 'Default File Name / Prefix' field, the User can input the base 'Filename', that we want Traverse to use when generating the ACH file. For example, 'DDFILE'
-  Traverse will automatically append our Company ID to the file name as a suffix (extension), so there’s no need to enter it manually.



Using Wildcards for Dynamic File Naming:

We can include Wildcards (special characters) to make the file name dynamic based on the context of the transaction:

-
? (Question Mark): Inserts the Application ID into the file name.

-
* (Asterisk): Inserts the current workstation date and time into the file name (in the format YYYYMMDDHHMM).

The User has the option to add either the 'Application ID' or the 'Timestamp' or both 'Application ID' and 'Timestamp' together



Example Format and Output:

Input Format: ?_DDEPOSIT_*

Output File Name: AP_DDEPOSIT_202505092051.CPU

Breakdown of the File name:

-
-
-
AP = Application ID (Accounts Payable)

- _ = It is used as a separator between the 'Application ID', 'Base File Name' and the 'Time Stamp'
-
DDFILE = User-defined portion of the file name

-
202505092051 = Timestamp (Year 2025, Month 05, Day 09, Hour 20, Minute 51)

-
.CPU = Company ID automatically appended by Traverse



The 'Sample File' field shows as follows:



Sample Output:

The AP Create ACH File screen looks as follows, when the User tries to create the 'ACH' File for the Bank Account 'MAIN', that we saw in the example:



The exported ACH File will be available in the destination folder with the configured name:

75536029-b6ae-475c-af62-66f808edf972.title: Logging in to Traverse via RDP with MFA Authentication
75536029-b6ae-475c-af62-66f808edf972.content:
Problem
User having trouble with Signing in, stuck at MFA

Resolution
Summary:
This article provides step-by-step instructions on how to log in to Traverse using a Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) file while completing Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA).

Instructions:

When initiating a connection to the Traverse environment via the provided RDP file, the session will begin by attempting to establish a secure link with the remote server. After a few seconds, the RDP login interface may transition to a state that displays a “More details” option. Click on More details to expand the authentication window.

You will then be presented with a prompt asking you to select the email address to which the MFA verification code should be sent. Choose the correct email address and wait for the verification code to arrive in your inbox. Once received, enter the code into the prompt and proceed to sign in.

Before finalizing the sign-in process, ensure that you check the box labeled “Trust this device for 180 days.” This will reduce the frequency of MFA prompts on the same machine. After selecting this option, click OK to complete the login.

Following these steps correctly should allow you seamless access to the Traverse environment via RDP.

62823abe-37ba-4eb1-a051-7802ff4cbe85.title: Setting the Geo Location in On-Time Web
62823abe-37ba-4eb1-a051-7802ff4cbe85.content:
Problem
On top of my dashboard, the Geo Location is not correct.  It is showing a different city or even a different state. How do I correct this?

Resolution
On top of my On-Time Web dashboard, the Geo Location is incorrect.  It shows a different city or even a different state. How do I correct this?



Setting the Geo Location in On-Time Web

This can happen when an ISP (Internet Service Provider) purchases a block of IP addresses registered from a different area or state.  When they assign that IP address to your location, it still shows the original IP address location. Do the following to correct this within On-Time Web.

- Navigate to Company Settings>Geo IP Info – and enter the following information:
- IP Address – Enter the Public Gateway IP address for your Business Location – This can be found by using a web browser and asking the search engine “What is my IP”
- Street Address – this would be your physical street address for your business.
- City – The City where your business is located.
- State – the State where your business is located.
- Postal Code – The Postal Code for your business location.
- Country – Select the Country for your business location.
- Select Find Coordinates – this will search the internet for your specific Latitude and Longitude for the address you have entered. The system will then enter the location in the Latitude and Longitude fields below
- Select Save.

Once you log out and back in, the  Geo Location will be correct on the dashboard.

c4ee9ecd-ebe4-45ad-8231-a51c2b531bd1.title: Double Sided Printing to Single Side
c4ee9ecd-ebe4-45ad-8231-a51c2b531bd1.content:
Problem
Printers Printing in Double sided from Traverse

Resolution
In many cases, a printer will default to use print duplexing which is not always desirable.

To disable duplex, open the Control Panel > Devices and Printers (or use cmd line “control printers”).  Right click on the desired printer and click Printer Properties.



Within the Properties screen, click “Preferences”.



Each printer will have a different named setting.  It will either “Duplex Printing”, “Print on Both Sides”, “2-sided printing”, or similar.  Deselect duplex or set to 1-sided printing and click “OK”.



Back in the Printer Properties window, go to the “Advanced” tab and click the “Printing Defaults” button.  This will bring up the same preferences window from before.  Change the settings here as well.

eb97f6ee-c8f0-49b1-8e18-f0e47be7d301.title: IP Address Rules in On-Time Web
eb97f6ee-c8f0-49b1-8e18-f0e47be7d301.content:
Problem
We want to prevent people from logging into On-Time Web from anywhere other than their place of employment.  Can we do that?

Resolution
How do I ensure people can only log in at work on our network and nowhere else in On-Time Web?



IP Address Rule in On-Time Web and How to Set Them Up

You can set up IP address Rules in On-Time Web to limit employees to only being allowed to log into On-Time Web from inside your network. The following is the way to set up IP Address Rules in On-Time Web. You can set up as many IP Rules as you wish.

- Navigate to Company Settings>IP Address Rules
- Select a Policy Type

- Global Policy – This policy prevents anyone from accessing your On-Time Web website outside your Internet gateway
-  Supervisor Group Policy - This policy prevents employees from specific Supervisor Groups from accessing your On-Time Web website outside your Internet gateway.
- Employee Policy - This policy prevents specific employees from accessing your On-Time Web site outside your Internet gateway.

- IP Address – Enter the IP address that you would like to be allowed the policy group selected to access On-Time Web.  This would be your Public Gateway of your network or the public IP address from wherever you want the group to access On-Time Web.
- Enter the CIDR – the CIDR (Classless Inter-Domain Routing, sometimes known as supernetting) is a way to allocate and specify the internet addresses used in inter-domain routing with more flexibility than with the original system of Internet Protocol (IP) address classes. If uncertain, leave this blank.
- Status – you can enable or disable this rule at will.
- Save

The saved IP Address rules will be listed in the table below and can be edited as needed.

db23835e-e1bb-4c28-aea0-19af872809bd.title: How Traverse handles the 'Scrap %'?
db23835e-e1bb-4c28-aea0-19af872809bd.content:
Problem
How Traverse handles the 'Scrap %'?

Resolution
Handling Scrap in Production Activity:

In Traverse, when recording production activity, it is important to understand how scrap quantities are managed within the system to ensure accurate inventory relief and costing.

Best Practice for Entering Production Quantities:

When entering a production activity in Traverse, the Quantity field should reflect the full amount of material actually used in production, which includes both the usable output and any scrap generated during the process.

-
The Qty Scrapped field is used purely for reference and tracking and does not impact inventory levels.

-
The entire quantity entered in the Quantity field is relieved from inventory and is used in the costing calculation for the finished good.

Example:

Let’s consider an item “Salt” used in a Bill of Materials (BOM), which has a 2% scrap rate defined. The desired quantity to be produced (usable output) is 10 units.

System Behavior:

-
Traverse calculates the total quantity of salt needed as:
10 / (1 - 0.02) = 10.2041 units

-
This means:

-
Total issued quantity from inventory: 10.2041 units

-
Expected scrap: 0.2041 units

-
Net usable quantity after scrap: 10.0000 units

The total quantity, deriving from the quantity times the scrap %, are set up in the Bill of Material in the detail for each component:



Production Activity Entry:

-
When the production order is generated, the system expects 10.2041 units to be consumed.

- If the order is Backflushed, the expected total quantity is the amount that will Traverse will enter for the Quantity produced.
-
Whatever amount gets recorded as produced in the production activity (whether manually or by backflushing) is deducted from inventory and used in calculating the finished good’s cost.

-
The 0.2041 units identified as scrap may be optionally recorded in the Qty Scrapped field for auditing or tracking, but it does not influence the inventory deduction.

NOTE:

If users manually enter 10 units in the Quantity field and expect Traverse to automatically calculate and add 2% as scrap, that is not how the system is designed to function.

Instead:

-
The user must manually enter the full production quantity, including scrap (e.g., 10.2041).

- Or, the user may use the backflush function to automatically enter in the full production quantity. (Lotted or serialized entries will require manual entry, however.)
-
The scrap amount (e.g., 0.2041) should be recorded separately in the Qty Scrapped field if manually recording activity, as needed.



Summary:

FieldValueDescriptionQuantity Entered10.2041Full quantity used in production, including scrapQty Scrapped0.2041Scrap portion (for tracking only, does not affect inventory)Inventory Impact-10.2041Inventory is relieved by the full amount used

b40e8607-36a3-41d0-b5ca-71ed25307d55.title: How to export a EDI 810-Invoice from Traverse Global History
b40e8607-36a3-41d0-b5ca-71ed25307d55.content:
Problem
There was a transmission issue when the original EDI 810-Invoice was processed, and now the 810-Invoice needs to be resent from history to the Trading Partner.

Resolution
The 810-Invoice may be resent/re-exported from history by following the steps:

- In EDI Connector < Invoice-810 < Resend Invoices from History.
- Set any applicable filters in the Data filter section to help narrow down the returned results to the desired invoices.
- Select the "Apply" button to return data results.
- Check the checkbox in the "Select" Column for the applicable 810-Invoices that are desired to be resent from history.
- Once the desired 810-Invoices have been selected, select the "Add to Queue" button in the top toolbar.

- A popup will be receiving asking, "Are you sure you want to resend the selected Item(s)?", select yes to resend the 810-Invoice from History.

- In EDI Connector < Invoices-810 < Process Invoices, You will want to ensure the Invoice passes validation and is in a released status for it to be exported from Traverse.
- If needed, set any needed filters to narrow down the specific returned results.
- Select Apply to return the invoices that are in the queue.
- In the "Show Invoices" drop down, select "Released" to see the Invoices that are in a released status, or select "On Hold" to see the Invoices that are On Hold from being able to be exported from Traverse.
- To perform the Invoice Validation, select the Check Box for the desired invoice(s). Then Select the Validate button in the to toolbar.
- A "Validation Complete" pop up message will appear once the validations executes, Select OK to close the pop up.

- Check the Status column to ensure the Invoice passed validation.

- In order for an 810 Invoice to be exported from Traverse the Invoice must be in a released status. If the Invoice needs to be changed from On Hold to Released, or from Released to On Hold, the "Change Status" feature will allow you to change the Invoice Status.
- When the Show Invoices field is set to "Released" any Invoices in a Released status will appear.
- When the Show Invoices field is set to "On Hold" any Invoices in an On Hold status will appear.
- To change the status of the Invoice, select the desired Invoice records by checking the Checkbox then Selecting the Change Status button.

- Once the Invoice has Passed Validation and is in a Released Status, the EDI Connector < Invoices-810 < Export Invoices feature may be used to export the 810 Invoice file(s) from Traverse and to be processed through EDI. To export all queue 810 Invoices that are in a released status select the OK button. Once Processed a message will appear indicating how many invoices exported and the file name it was saved as.

12eda179-77ce-4d7e-ad25-7e02c77f2a80.title: Midnight Shift End in On-Time Web
12eda179-77ce-4d7e-ad25-7e02c77f2a80.content:
Problem
Why are some of my time entries are appearing on the wrong day.

Resolution
Why Is My Time Showing On The Wrong Day in On-Time Web?



One Possibility for why your time is showing on the wrong date in On-Time Web is that the Midnight Shift End is not set correctly.

What is Midnight Shift End?

Midnight Shift End is a setting in the Employees Settings.  It is used to record time past midnight that should be a part of the previous day’s transactions.  People who work a third shift when their shift that begins on one day and then ends on the next day.

For example, an Employee works from 3:00 PM to 1:00 AM the next day.    In this example, I would set the Midnight Shift End to be 2:00 AM.  This represents the very latest the Employee can work till and have it appear on the previous day. If the Employee works till 3:00 AM, the entire punch record will appear on the day they clocked out.

How Can I Fix My Midnight Shift End?

Edit the Employee record by navigating to Company Settings>Employees>Settings Tab and editing the Midnight Shift End to the very latest time an employee would be allowed to work. For example, if the employee works day shift, set it to 2:00 AM.  This would allow for possible overtime work up to 2:00 AM that would appear on the previous day. Then save.

You can also set the Midnight Shift End in the Settings and Defaults>New Employees Tab and set the Midnight Shift End to a default time, and Save.  Now all new employees that is added to the system will default what was entered.

f810d98f-5bd9-49a8-88ff-d343876c70b5.title: Traverse Crashes Out after 30 Secs due to Printer Driver
f810d98f-5bd9-49a8-88ff-d343876c70b5.content:
Problem
Traverse Crashes Out after 30 Secs

Resolution
Traverse Crashes Due to LMFX1N4Z.DLL Printer Driver

Symptoms:

When attempting to launch Traverse, the application crashes immediately after it gets opened.

Event Viewer logs display an error similar to:

Faulting application name: mstsc.exe

Faulting module name: LMFX1N4Z.DLL Exception code: 0xc0000005

Fault offset: 0x000000000003b59b Faulting module path: C:\Windows\System32\spool\DRIVERS\x64\3\LMFX1N4Z.DLL



Root Cause:

The crash is caused by the LMFX1N4Z.DLL, a third-party printer driver DLL located in the Windows spooler directory.

This driver is likely incompatible or corrupted and is triggered when printer redirection is enabled during Remote Desktop sessions.

The 0xc0000005 exception indicates an access violation due to faulty memory handling within the DLL.

Resolution:

Update Printer Driver from Vendor Identify the printer model associated with LMFX1N4Z.DLL.

Visit the manufacturer’s official support site (Lexmark, Ricoh, etc.).

Download and install the latest WHQL-certified driver compatible with your OS version.

Reboot the system after installation.

1c4dcf4f-937e-44ec-a8fb-ce11682bfe19.title: Setting Up Punch Overrides in On-Time Web
1c4dcf4f-937e-44ec-a8fb-ce11682bfe19.content:
Problem
Need to stop employees from punching in too early in On-Time Web.

Resolution
Can I stop people from punching in early in On-Time Web?

Although On-Time Web will not restrict people from punching, you can set up Punch Overrides.

Punch Overrides allows you to set an override time to move the time punch to the accepted time. For example, if you have someone who comes in early, let’s say 7:40 AM, but they are not allowed to start work until 8:00 AM, you can set up a punch override that will move early IN punches to 8:00 AM.

Note: The Punch Overrides take effect after the Punch Override is set up.  It does not go back and change punches.

How to set up Punch Overrides.

- Go to Company Settings>Punch Overrides.
- Choose a Policy Type
Global Policy – This is a company-wide Punch Override.  The punch override will be
applied to all employees.
Supervisor Group – The Punch Override will be applied to specified Supervisor Groups.
Employee – The Punch Override will be applied to only the employee(s) selected

- Start Time – Enter the Start Time that you want the Punch Override to begin.  Select a time that would encompass the earliest that people usually come to work when they are early. With the example earlier, the employee came in about 20 minutes early, so to make sure that I cover that time, I would enter 7:30 AM.
- End Time - Enter the End Time that you want the Punch Override to end.  Select a time that would encompass the latest that you want to apply to the Punch Override. You may choose to extend this a few minutes past the time work starts. For example, if they are supposed to start work at 8:00 AM, you could set a grace period of 8:03 AM.  But if you do not want a grace period, set it for 8:00 AM.
- Override Time – The time you want the punch to be.  (8:00 AM)
- Status – You can either Enable or Disable this Punch Override.
- Save

In the screenshot above, you can see examples of many Punch Overrides.  You can also edit any of the punch overrides at any time.

b11e6680-be67-467a-88d4-f4b4c93be72e.title: On-Time Web Bulk Time
b11e6680-be67-467a-88d4-f4b4c93be72e.content:
Problem
I need to enter time for all or a group of our employees for the holidays.  How can I do that?

Resolution
Can I enter time for many of my employees at one time?

Yes, On-Time Web has a feature called Bulk Time.  It is a method for Supervisors and Administrators to enter time for multiple employees for multiple hours and days.  For example, entering the time for a national holiday for everyone who will be paid for that holiday.

How To Enter Bulk Time

- Navigate to Time Management>Bulk Time
- Select from Available Employees by clicking on the employee's name.  You can also click the supervisor group name, or you can click Select All, then everyone in that group will be selected and moved to the Selected Employees.
- Set the date range for the time you will be entering.
- Enter the Start Time. This is the time of the In Punch that will show on the timesheets.
- Enter the End Time.  This is the time of the Out Punch that will show on the timesheets.
- The total hours of the punch record will show in this field.
If you enter a start time and skip to this field, you could enter an hour amount, the system will calculate the End Time punch and automatically enter it in the End Time Field.
- Select the correct earning code for this time punch.
- The department field will default to the Employees Department but can be edited.
- Notes – You can add specific notes on the Punch Record that you are making.
- Click the Create Bulk Time button. This will create the identical punch for the employees selected for these records.

89ec2079-2993-4d1f-884e-85741693575d.title: Why Certain Payment number Do Not Appear in AP Detail History View
89ec2079-2993-4d1f-884e-85741693575d.content:
Problem
Users want to know if it’s possible to print some checks without them appearing in the AP Detail History View.

Resolution
Yes, there is a distinction in how the system logs checks based on how they are entered:

-
Checks/payments entered using the "Prepay" or "Print Checks" functions
These check/payment numbers do not appear in the Accounts Payable> Interactive view > Detail History View.

-
Checks/payments entered through "AP > Transactions > Transactions > Payments" tab
These check/payment numbers do appear in the Accounts Payable> Interactive view> Detail History View.

-
Even though checks printed through Prepay or Print Checks won't appear in the AP Detail History View, they will be visible in the AP Payment History View.

-
This behavior is by design and helps distinguish between manually entered and system-processed payments.

If you need the Payment number/check number to appear in the Detail History View for reporting or tracking purposes, enter them manually via Accounts Payable > Transactions > Transactions > Payments.

For all other cases where visibility in the Payment History View is sufficient, using Prepay or Print Checks is acceptable.

d5c156ab-6212-4188-84e6-a332c77e4697.title: How to set up the SAME printer to print the check and remittance when Check Saver is being used?
d5c156ab-6212-4188-84e6-a332c77e4697.content:
Problem
How do you set up the SAME printer to print the Check and remittance when the Check Saver is being used?

Resolution
To configure one printer to print both the checks and the Check Saver remittance, you will need to update the Business Rule for "Check Saver" to the "Single" option. This allows you to assign one printer for checks and the remittance copy.

1. Navigate to Business Rules: Go to the System Manager (SM) Business Rules by following this path:Applications -> System Manager -> Company Setup -> Business Rules.

2. Select Accounts Payable Application: Under the Application section, select Accounts Payable to view the relevant settings. From there, locate the Business Rule labeled "Check Saver" under the Miscellaneous section.3. Configure Check Saver Options: We have three options to choose from for the Check Saver function:

- None: This option disables the Check Saver function entirely.
- Single: Select this option to use the same printer for both the checks and the Check Saver remittance.
- Multiple: Select this option if you want to use one printer for Checks and a separate printer for the Check Saver remittance.

Click "Apply" and "OK" to save the setting.



4. Set Up Form Printers: After configuring the Business Rule to "Single," we can proceed to set up the printer entries for both the checks and the check saver remittance. To do this, navigate to SM Form Printers by following this path: Applications -> System Manager -> Form Printers.

Click into a blank line and select "AP Check" and/or "APChSave" from the drop down list to create settings for those forms have not been set up to print from a specified printer yet. Select the same printer for both the AP Check and APChkSave lines to have them print from the same printer.  Select the appropriate Tray for each one.

If you only set up the AP Check form and not the APChkSave form in SM Form Printer, Traverse will print the AP Checks to the selected printer, and the Check Saver remittance to your computer's default printer.

Go back to Accounts Payable -> Pay Invoices -> Print Checks to print your checks.

When you print your checks, Traverse will print your checks, then you will get this message before the printer prints your check remittance:

Click "OK" and the Check Saver Remittance will print.

By following these steps, we’ll be able to effectively manage which printers to use for the Checks and the Remittance.

4bbb8691-0520-4b45-8792-205994896687.title: How to print Labels for only a group of Customers or Vendors?
4bbb8691-0520-4b45-8792-205994896687.content:
Problem
How to print Labels for only a group of Customers or Vendors?

Resolution
Traverse provides the ability to generate Customer and Vendor Labels through the Accounts Receivable and Accounts Payable modules. This document outlines the available filtering options for standard label printing and introduces an alternative approach using CRM Contact Groups when more granular selection is needed.



Standard Label Printing (Accounts Receivable / Accounts Payable):

Traverse allows label printing for customers and vendors directly from their respective modules using built-in filters. Users can:

-
Print labels for a specific Customer or Vendor.

-
Print for a small, defined group based on manual selection.

-
Apply Data Filters to filter labels based on Name, Status and so on

These options are suitable for environments with fewer records or when printing needs are limited to manageable subsets.





Limitations:

When dealing with a large volume of Customers or Vendors, and labels are required for only a specific segment (e.g., based on custom criteria like transaction history), the built-in Data Filters may not provide the necessary flexibility.





Using CRM Contact Groups for Label Printing:

If the CRM module is in use, an alternative method involves creating a Contact Group containing only the desired Customers or Vendors. Labels can then be generated specifically for this group.

Steps to Generate Labels via CRM Contact Group:

i. Create and Configure a Contact Group:

-
-
Navigate to the CRM module.

-
-
Create a new Contact Group and assign a meaningful name for easy identification.



ii. Manually Add Customers or Vendors:

- Select each record that meets the required criteria (e.g., Customers with sales between 2020 and 2025).
- And then click on 'Generate' to create the 'Contact Group'

b4d12040-2986-45f4-a5b1-0a21021f624c.title: User question on Secure Act 2.0
b4d12040-2986-45f4-a5b1-0a21021f624c.content:
Problem
Partner has few clients asking if Traverse is going to make any changes in regard to the Secure Act 2.0?

SECURE Act 2.0 would require employers that offer 401 (k), 403 (b) and SIMPLE IRA plans to automatically enroll all newly eligible employees at a 3% deduction level that ticks up by 1% annually until it reaches 10%. Employees do have the choice to opt out, if they prefer, and existing plans wouldn’t have to change anything.

Resolution
This legislation was initially implemented in 2022, with some updates introduced more recently. At this time, Traverse does not currently support automated processes for these specific requirements. The setup for newly eligible employees would continue to follow the current manual process, as has been done previously.

Additionally, given the ongoing changes from the IRS and the current administration, it’s still unclear how these requirements may evolve or if they will remain in place long term.

We’ll continue to monitor any developments related to this legislation and will keep our customers informed if there are any updates or product changes in the future.

433cad07-4370-4f3a-8b71-8c273c0d008f.title: How Does Punch Rounding Work in On-Time Web and How To Set up Punch Rounding
433cad07-4370-4f3a-8b71-8c273c0d008f.content:
Problem
what is Punch rounding in On-Time Web?  How do I set it up and use it?

Resolution
What is Punch Rounding?

Punch Rounding in On-Time Web allows punches to be rounded forward or backward based on simple rules. This makes time calculation easier and can save the company money from accidental overtime. For example, if someone comes in and the line at the time clock is long, they reach the clock one or two minutes late, the punch is automatically rounded back, not penalizing the employee due to overcrowding at the time clock.  If someone comes in earlier to beat the rush and clocks in 3 or 4 minutes early, their time will be rounded up to 8:00 AM

How do I Set Up Punch Rounding?

Navigate to Company Settings>Settings & Defaults>Punch Settings

Complete the setup of Punch Rounding by setting the following:

- Enable Time Rounding - Set to Yes if you want to use Time Rounding
- Set the Button Rounding Options: Select the punch buttons that you want to use rounding. IN, OUT, Switch, Return Lunch, Go Lunch, Return Break, Go Break.
- Set your Time Rounding Intervals. Select one of the following: 5 Minutes, 6 Minutes, 10 Minutes, or 15 Minutes.
- Enter the Required Work Time.  This is the amount of time required to be worked before rounding occurs.  for example, If we have the rounding interval set for 15 minutes and require 8 minutes of work time. If someone is due to work at 8:00 AM, and comes in before 8 minutes, their time would be rounded back to 7:45 AM.  If they come to work after 8 minutes till 8:00 AM, their punch would be rounded to 8:00 AM
- Then save your settings.

974d6052-1ca2-4770-a47c-52fc99856d8e.title: How to Set Up a Period Definition ID for Forecast Generation by Item ID
974d6052-1ca2-4770-a47c-52fc99856d8e.content:
Problem
How to Set Up a Period Definition ID for Forecast Generation by Item ID

Resolution
Go to Setup and Maintenance > Period Definitions

1. Open a New Period Definition:
Click the New button on the toolbar to open a blank period definition form.

2. Enter Basic Details:
In the Period Definition ID field, type a unique name or code for the new period definition.
In the Description field, write a short explanation of what this definition is for.

3. Set the Time Fence:
In the Demand Time Fence Periods field, enter how many periods should be included within the time fence.

This time fence is an artificial way to divide reports into two sections based on time (time periods within the time fence and time periods after the time fence). The number you enter is the number of periods you want to include within the time fence.

Time fences are important when you’re looking at orders vs. forecasts on reports. The system uses actual orders vs. forecasts within the time fence and the greater of the two beyond the time fence. For example, imagine that the sales forecast for next March is 300 units, while actual sales are 275. If March lies within the time fence, the system uses the actual sales number of 275 on reports. If March is beyond the time fence, the system assumes 300 (the greater of the two) to be correct.

Example: If you enter 3 and have 8 total periods, the first 3 use actual values and the last 5 use the higher of forecast or actual.

4. Define Each Period:
In the Period field, type the period number (like 1, 2, 3, etc.).
In the Increment field, enter how long that period should be.
In the Units field, choose if that length is in Days, Weeks, or Months.

5. Save the Period Definition:
Click the Save button on the toolbar to finish and save your setup.
