c40d99d2-6db9-4886-b19a-ecac32bad497.title: How to set up a Traverse Alert/Actions from Traverse?
c40d99d2-6db9-4886-b19a-ecac32bad497.content:
Problem
How to set up a Traverse Alert/Actions from Traverse?

Resolution
Traverse Actions (or) Traverse Alerts is a system that monitors data and sends alerts when specific criteria are met. Alerts can trigger actions such as sending emails or generating files, using Traverse’s Document Delivery functionality.



Pre-Requisites:

-
Traverse Version: Ensure Traverse Global Build 21307 or higher is installed.

-
Alerts Service: The Alerts service must be running on the Traverse Server (typically on the same server as the Traverse License Server). This Windows service requires a Traverse user account to operate. [Refer to the Article for the Alerts/Actions Service Setup:
https://connect.aptean.com/s/article/Installing-Traverse-Actions-Previously-referred-as-Traverse-alerts]

-
User Permissions: Assign permissions to users who need access to Alerts via System Manager > Administration > Groups.

-
SMTP Settings: Configure Document Delivery SMTP settings to enable email notifications.



Actions/Alerts Setup in Traverse:

i. Create a new Alert/Action:

- In Traverse, go to System Manager > Actions > Actions:
- Select the Actions to assign actions.
- Click "+" to create a new action or select an existing one to edit.

ii. Define the 'Action Type':

- None: Disable Alerts and Processes
- Notification: It enables the 'General', 'Output', 'Email' and 'Schedule' Tabs
- Process: It enables the 'General', 'Process Automation' and 'Schedule' Tabs



iii. Enter the required details in the 'General' Tab:

-
Description: Name the action, that best defines the 'Actions/Alerts'

-
Group By: Choose a field to group data (e.g., Sales Rep ID to send one email per rep).

-
Renotification Period: Set how often repeated data should be reported (e.g., avoid sending the same alert daily for the same customer).

NOTE: Last Run: This field represents the last time, the Alert/Action ran successfully. It is not the part of the set up

- Define the Parameters:



iv. Configure the 'Output' Tab:

Once the setup is completed on the General tab of the Action, the next step is to configure how the results from the Alert’s dataset should be handled. This is done through the Output tab, where users can specify the file format, destination, included fields, and their order of appearance in the report.

- File Type: Choose the desired file format for the report output. Common file types include: Excel (.xlsx), CSV (.csv), PDF (.pdf), etc.
For example, if the intention is to generate a spreadsheet, select Excel.
- File Name: Enter the preferred base name for the output file. Traverse will automatically append the appropriate file extension (e.g., .xlsx) to the file.
- Output File Checkbox: Enable this option if we wish to save the generated file to a specific location on the server or a network-accessible shared folder. This ensures that the file is stored in a location accessible to designated users.
- Overwrite File Checkbox: Enable this option to replace the existing file with the same name each time the alert runs. If left unchecked, Traverse will create a new file each time, appending a counter to the filename to distinguish versions (e.g., AR Outstanding.xlsx, AR Outstanding (1).xlsx, etc.).
- Folder Path: Specify the full path to the target folder where the output file should be saved.
For alerts that are grouped by a specific column (e.g., SalesRepID), a separate file will be created for each group. The resulting filenames will follow the defined file name format, appended with the group identifier.
Example: If the filename is set as AR Outstanding, and the Sales Rep ID is ABC, the final file would be named: AR Outstanding-ABC.xlsx.

Output Field Setup:

The grid in the Output tab is used to select the fields to include in the output file, define their captions, and set the display order.

-
Column Name: Displays the list of all available fields derived from the query defined earlier in the Query Builder. These represent the potential columns in your report.

-
Add to File: Check this box next to each field we wish to include in the final output.

-
Caption: Enter the desired display name or title for each selected field. This is the label that will appear in the column header of the exported report file.

-
Display Order: Determines the order in which the fields appear in the report. The system will auto-generate order numbers based on the sequence of field selection. However, users can manually adjust these numbers to reorganize the column sequence as desired.



v. Configure the 'Email' Tab:

From the Email tab in Traverse Alerts, users can configure how alert results are sent via email. This includes defining recipients, attaching output files, customizing the subject and body of the email, and including additional attachments if needed.

a. Email Recipients:

-
We can choose to:

-
Send emails to dynamic recipients (i.e., email addresses from the dataset).

-
Enter static email addresses manually for specific recipients.

Note: To enable email functionality, an SMTP ID must be set up in Document Delivery.

b. Key Email Configuration Fields:

-
Email: Click on the lookup icon to select the field from our dataset that contains the recipients’ email addresses.
Example: If we're grouping data by Sales Rep ID, each rep will receive a personalized email with their relevant information and attachments.

-
Send Email:
✔️ Check this box to enable sending emails.
❌ Uncheck it if no emails should be sent for this alert.

-
Send To: Add additional recipients manually here (e.g., a Sales Manager who should receive a copy of all alert emails).

-
Output File:
✔️ Check this to attach the output file (e.g., Excel report) to the email.  [Each recipient will receive only the file relevant to their data.]

c. Customizing Subject and Body:

-
Subject: Enter the Subject line for your email. We can include fields from the alert by dragging them from the "Fields" tab into the Subject line. These fields will appear in square brackets (e.g., [RepName]).

-
SMTP ID: Select the SMTP configuration that was previously defined in Document Delivery. This determines the server used to send the emails.

-
Body: Compose the email message here. We can insert fields from the alert data by:

-
Double-clicking the field name from the right-hand panel (Fields tab).

-
Or dragging and dropping the field where needed in the message.

-
We can also include dynamic fields like:

-
Company information, Current date, etc

-
These can be found under the Misc tab next to the Body section.

d. Attachments:

-
If needed, upload and include additional files along with the alert output in the email.



v. Configure the 'Schedule' Tab:

Once the alert’s purpose and the 'Output' are configured, the final step is to set up a schedule for when the action should run.

a. Choose the Frequency (Occurs Field):

We can schedule the action to run:

-
Every few minutes

-
Hourly

-
Daily

-
Weekly

-
Monthly

b. Schedule Details:

- Hourly or Minutes Schedule:
- Select Hourly or Minutes in the Occurs field.
- Use the Recur Every field to set the interval.
Example: If we set it to 3 hours, the action will run every 3 hours and generate output if applicable.

Note: Previously reported data will not be included again if a Renotification Period is set on the General tab.

- Daily Schedule:
- Select Daily in the Occurs field.
- Recur Every set the frequency in days.
Example: 1 = daily, 2 = every other day.
- Enter the Start Time (in 24-hour format).
Example: 07:00 = 7:00 AM and 17:00 = 5:00 PM

Note: The Time zone refers to the 'Server' in which the 'TRAVERSE Actions/Alerts' areconfigured



- Weekly Schedule:
- Select Weekly in the Occurs field.
- Set the Start Time and Recur Every week(s).
- Choose the days of the week the alert should run.
Example: Every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.



- Monthly Schedule:
- Select Monthly in the Occurs field.
- Choose the Start Time and enter the day of the month in the Recur Every field.
Example: Enter 15 to run the alert on the 15th of every month.

- Set the Duration:
- We can leave the End Date blank if you want the alert to run continuously.
- Alternatively, set both Start Date and End Date to define a limited time range.



vi. Save the setup:

- Once the setup is complete, click on the 'Save' icon to have the setup saved.



vii. Review the 'Activity View' to confirm the working of Alerts:



Summary:

-
Confirm prerequisites (version, service, permissions, SMTP)

-
Create or edit an alert

-
Define data source and key columns

-
Set up parameters. Validate and save the alert

-
Assign and configure actions in Traverse

-
Set output and scheduling

e188160a-f5ca-4c83-9b54-18cab2fe42f6.title: How to delete a 'Credit Memo' that has Qty returned updated, but not posted?
e188160a-f5ca-4c83-9b54-18cab2fe42f6.content:
Problem
How to delete a 'Credit Memo' that was verified, but not posted?

Resolution
In Traverse, creating a Credit Memo does not automatically mark the transaction as finalized. Instead, the system continues to treat the Credit Memo as a draft until it has been fully or partially posted within its associated batch.



Deleting an Unposted Sales Order (SO) Credit Memo:

If the Sales Order Credit Memo has not been posted—either fully or partially—then it remains in a draft state. In this case:

-
The Credit Memo can be safely deleted from the system without any complications.

-
Upon deletion, Traverse will automatically remove the associated record from the batch or transaction list, ensuring there are no residual entries.



Process of Deleting a Credit Memo:

i. Navigate to the SO Orders screen under the path: Applications -> Sales Orders - > Transactions -> Orders:



ii. Pull up the required 'Credit Memo' from the drop-down list:



iii. Click on the 'Update' icon:



iv. Use the 'Delete' option to delete the Credit memo:



Important Note on Transaction Numbers:

When a Credit Memo is deleted, its original transaction number cannot be reused unless the batch in which it was originally included has been posted.

-
This restriction is due to Traverse’s internal batch management logic, which tracks and reserves transaction numbers until their associated batch is finalized.

-
Therefore, if the batch containing the deleted Credit Memo remains unposted, the system considers the transaction number as still in use, and it will not be available for reassignment or reuse.

66b74066-a1ef-458c-afc6-493c44a9bb43.title: How to exclude the zero-dollar entries from a GL Financial Statement?
66b74066-a1ef-458c-afc6-493c44a9bb43.content:
Problem
How to exclude the zero-dollar entries from a GL Financial Statement?

Resolution
By default, when a GL Financial Statement is generated in Traverse, it includes all account sections that are defined within the statement setup, regardless of whether those accounts have balances. This means accounts with a zero-dollar balance will still appear in the report, which may not always be desirable for reporting clarity or readability.



To enhance the report’s usability, especially for review and analysis, Traverse provides an option to exclude accounts with zero balances. This ensures the report only displays accounts with financial activity, making it more streamlined and easier to interpret.



Steps to Generate a Financial Statement Without Zero-Balance Accounts:

i. Navigate to the GL Financial Statements screen:

- Go to Applications → General Ledger → Management Reports → Financial Statements:

ii. Access the Report Settings:

- Select the desired Statement ID that you want to generate.
- Ensure all other parameters are set appropriately (Fiscal Period, Fiscal Year and the Company IDs).



iii. Uncheck the Option ‘Accounts with Zero Balances’:

- Locate the checkbox labeled ‘Accounts with Zero Balances’ in the 'View' section.
- Uncheck this option to exclude accounts that have no activity (i.e., a balance of $0.00).



iv. Preview or Output the Report:

- Click on the ‘Preview’ icon to view the report on-screen.
- Alternatively, choose from:
-
-
‘Output’ to export the report in a digital format (PDF, Excel, etc.)

-
‘Print’ to generate a hard copy directly.

2a5257af-6c6e-4490-a42a-ef39778f7219.title: Idle_Timeout_Update
2a5257af-6c6e-4490-a42a-ef39778f7219.content:
Problem
Customer requested to extend Traverse time out from 15 min to 1 hour in Prod & Staging.

Resolution
Extending Timeout for Traverse Sessions

This knowledge base article provides a step-by-step guide to extend the timeout duration for Traverse sessions using Group Policy Management. This helps avoid unintended disconnections during idle periods while ensuring administrative control over session durations.

To extend Traverse time out

Login to the Domain controller server and open group policy management

In Policy management inside Forest: Apteancloud.local go to domain open prod001.apteancloud.local and open Traverse OU search for the respective customer’s OU and double click on it.

Inside the particular customer’s OU select the Idle session limit group policy under Linked group policy Objects and right click onit and click on edit it will open group policy management editer from there go to user configuration -> policies -> Administrative templates -> windows components -> remote desktop services -> session time limits

Double click on the session time limits and right click on set time limit for active but idle remote desktop services sessions and click on edit and select the time limit you want and click on ok

Go back to customer’s OU and edit the GPO’s name according to the time you setup by right click on it and rename the GPO

Then open command prompt as an administrator and enter gpupdate /force to apply the changes.

f0977e58-103e-44ba-a15f-d43001ad9746.title: How to enter the new W4 for a new employee
f0977e58-103e-44ba-a15f-d43001ad9746.content:
Problem
The customer would like to know how to enter the new W4 for a new employee?

Resolution
- Go to payroll, setup and maintenance in the employee information screen.
- Call up the employee and go to the tax tab.
- If the employee has submitted a new W4 form and wants a tax status other than single or married, change the tax status accordingly. The available tax statuses are head of household, single, married, and head of household with two jobs.
- To enter additional information from the W4 form, click the factors button on the top right hand side to access the override factor screen.

- Click on the employee tab, then hit the plus button at the bottom of the screen to call up new override factors for tax code. Specify federal withholding.

- You will be prompted to enter extra information from the newly redesigned W4 form. If the employee submitted a 2020 or later form, enter 1 for the first prompt; otherwise, enter 0. If you enter 0, no other information needs to be entered.
- For the next prompt, regarding "2 jobs," if the employee marked the checkbox in Step 2(c) of the W4 form, enter 1; otherwise, enter 0.
- The next three pieces of information needed are dependence, other income, and other deductions, found in steps 3, 4A, and 4B on the W4 form. Enter this information accordingly.
- Once all information has been entered, close the override factor screen and click the save button in the top left hand corner of the screen.

815c70b8-5d10-4650-bd03-c250e64e07b1.title: Is there a way to disable Canadian Currency
815c70b8-5d10-4650-bd03-c250e64e07b1.content:
Problem
Request to disable the Canadian Dollar (CAD) from appearing or being used within the Exchange Rates setup screens. This change is required to prevent selection or use of the CAD currency for exchange rate configurations.

Resolution
It is not possible to fully disable or remove the Canadian Dollar (CAD) from the Exchange Rates setup due to system constraints. The following limitations and considerations apply:

-
Transaction History Restriction:

-
CAD cannot be deleted from the Active Currency list if there is any historical transaction associated with it.

-
Vendor/Customer Currency Restriction:

-
The default currency for existing vendors or customers set to CAD cannot be changed.

-
Exchange Rates Setup Limitation:

-
There is no option to selectively remove or hide CAD from the Exchange Rates setup screens.

-
Potential Workaround:

-
Setting GL accounts linked to CAD to Inactive may reduce the risk of future CAD transactions.

-
This workaround is not guaranteed and should be thoroughly tested in a non-production environment.

-
Ongoing Impact:

-
Any vendors or customers already configured to use CAD will remain in CAD.

-
Functional restrictions based on specific setups may still need further analysis.

Disabling CAD entirely is not feasible through standard configuration. The workaround using inactive GL accounts may offer partial restriction

05290a0e-5908-4f70-ade3-94fb26091932.title: Error "The smtp server requires a secure connection or the client was not authenticated. The server response was 5.7.0" when sending email from Traverse
05290a0e-5908-4f70-ade3-94fb26091932.content:
Problem
We are getting error "the smtp server requires a secure connection or the client was not authenticated. The server response was 5.7.0" when trying to send email from Traverse. Customer has tried to reset password and still same error. Suggested to Turn ON the toggle to "Allow less secure apps." under their Gmail account, still same error.

Resolution
As of May 30, 2022, Google permanently removed the option to turn on “Less secure app access” for most personal Gmail accounts for security reasons. However, Google recommends using: OAuth 2.0 authentication, or App Passwords (if you enable 2-Step Verification)

Here's how to enable "Less secure apps" from the admin console:

Step 1: Sign in as Admin

Go to: https://admin.google.com/

Step 2: Navigate to Security Settings

-
Click on Security

-
Scroll down and click on Access and Data Control > Less Secure Apps

-
Select "Allow users to manage their access to less secure apps"

Step 3: Allow for Individual User

Then, the user can go to:

https://myaccount.google.com/lesssecureapps

Turn ON the toggle to "Allow less secure apps."



To Use App Passwords (Recommended Way)

Step 1: Enable 2-Step Verification

Go to: https://myaccount.google.com/security
Turn on 2-Step Verification

Step 2: Generate App Password

Go to: https://myaccount.google.com/apppasswords

-
Select the app (e.g., Mail) and device

-
Google will give you a 16-character password

-
Paste this password (no spaces) into the application (Traverse> under System Manager> Document delivery> SMTP Settings) or device you're connecting to Gmail, in place of your regular password.

Note: App Passwords are only displayed once. If you lose it, you'll need to generate a new one.

c5be9127-9813-4f73-a1c0-5820db687ba4.title: How to turn off the feature that opens the WM Pick list print when an order is released in SO
c5be9127-9813-4f73-a1c0-5820db687ba4.content:
Problem
How to turn off the feature that opens the WM Pick list print when an order is released in Sales Order

Resolution
Under System manager> Company Setup> Business Rules> Expand Sales Order on the left and change the Business Rule under Miscellaneous for "Release for Picking" to "None." When you hit the Release button in Sales Order, this will bring up the below error message instead of releasing the order and opening the WM Picking List to trigger the Pick List print.

In the Business rules, the Release for Picking gives three options.

Release for Picking: Select one of the three options:

- None(default) - The Release button on the SO Transaction screen has no effect.
- Manual - When the Release button on the SO Transaction screen is used and the transaction type is ' New', 'Picked', or 'Backordered', the items on the order, if eligible, will be released for picking. This is the same functionality provided by the New tab in the WMS Release Items function.
- Auto - When the Save button on the SO Transaction screen is used and the transaction type is ' New', 'Picked', or 'Backordered', all SO line items will be released, or if a line item has been removed from the SO and the item is released with a status of 'Released' or 'Assigned', it will also be removed from the released items list in WM.

3baf70aa-377f-461e-8a3a-ac1f7666339b.title: Backup Traverse Preferences
3baf70aa-377f-461e-8a3a-ac1f7666339b.content:
Problem
Client wants to back up their TRAVERSE Settings and Preferences.

Resolution
Settings and Preferences are stored locally on the workstation in the user's folder.  If the folder containing these settings is backed up and later restored, it will restore back any settings or preferences that have changed since the backup was made.

To create this backup, navigate to the following folder.  Note, depending on certain Window's settings the AppData folder might be hidden.  Replace <UserName> with the login account on the workstation whose settings need to be backed up.

C:\Users\<UserName>\AppData\Roaming\Open Systems, Inc

Within this folder will be a folder named either TRAVERSE for 11.0 or TRAVERSE Global for 11.2.  Make a copy of this folder and save it somewhere.  Later, if the Preferences and Settings need to be restored this can be done be coping the backup of the folder back to the same location and overwriting all files.

504c2890-43c4-45b7-80f9-766816d7242d.title: How to Run a Timesheet Report by Various Criteria in On-Time Web
504c2890-43c4-45b7-80f9-766816d7242d.content:
Problem
How do I run a timesheet report in On-Time Web for a specific employee or date?

Resolution
In On-Time Web, you can add conditions and filter the data in your reporting. This provides the user with significantly more functionality from a single report.  For example, a time sheet can become a vacation report, a Department report, a Division report, or any type of report based on the conditions (s) that are selected for filtering the data.

The example below is a vacation report.  This would be a report that lets the user know who has taken leave for the data range selected. Follow the steps below.



- Go to the Reports menu item and select Timesheet

- Select ADD CONDITION to start the report filtering process.
- Start by selecting Date from the dropdown.

- Then select the word equals or select any filter method that you would like to use for the date.  For example, I want a report that will run from the beginning of the year until now, so I will select Is greater than or equal to
- Then enter the date for the first day of the year.

Then, repeat the process to add the Straight Earning Code for vacation.  In my system, that would be VAC.  Now that you have filtered your report by the date range and the Straight Earning Code you would like to have shown on the report.



You may also choose to select how the report is sorted as well as any other Reporting options that are allowed.

If you would like to save the criteria for this report, you can add a filter name and select Options to save. This will save the criteria that you created, and you can re-run the report at any time without the need to re-enter the criteria.

fef8c87f-c79d-4e0d-a9be-bed43f7b3f9b.title: How to exclude the 'Retired Assets' from the FA Depreciation Summary Report?

How to exclude the 'Retired Assets' from the FA Depreciation Summary Report?



(or)



Why does the retired assets, still show in the FA Depreciation Summary even after retiring the asset?

Resolution
The Depreciation Summary Report in Traverse is designed to display all assets—including active, fully depreciated, and retired assets, depending on how the report is filtered and generated.

Key details about the FA Depreciation Summary Report:

-
The Depreciation Summary Report pulls asset records and displays their base costs, accumulated depreciation, year-to-date depreciation, and remaining depreciable base, regardless of whether the asset is currently active or retired.

-
Unless the report is explicitly filtered to exclude retired assets, they will continue to appear.

-
Even though the asset has no remaining value, the system includes it in the report for historical and audit trail purposes, especially if depreciation was taken in previous periods.

Advance Ship Notices (ASNs) were not transmitted to the distribution center.

Initially, we should attempt resending the ASNs. It appears that the Sales Orders (SOs) haven’t been posted yet, which prevents them from being resent through Traverse.

System Archive Folder

Advance Ship Notice File Path

a591897d-f9a6-497a-a71e-4ab8189283fd.title: How to resolve the error 'Bill To customer is not valid' when processing a Sales Order?
a591897d-f9a6-497a-a71e-4ab8189283fd.content:
Problem
How to resolve the error 'Bill To customer is not valid' when processing a Sales Order?

Resolution
Significance of 'Bill To ID':

The ‘Bill-To ID’ in Traverse plays a critical role in determining how Accounts Receivable (AR) and Sales Order (SO) transactions are billed, especially in scenarios where the invoicing entity differs from the customer placing the order.

This field is configured within the AR Customers setup and provides the flexibility to direct billing to a different customer account when needed.

A. Behavior When ‘Bill-To ID’ is Left Blank:

If the Bill-To ID field is left blank, Traverse assumes that the customer placing the order is also the billing customer. In this case:

-
-
The invoice generated will reflect the same customer information in both the Sold-To and Ship-To fields.

-
The customer ID displayed on the Header tab of the SO or AR transaction screen will be used for all purposes.



B. Behavior When ‘Bill-To ID’ is Populated:

When a different Customer ID is entered in the Bill-To ID field of an AR Customer record:

-
The Sales Order transaction will pull this ID into the Bill-To tab automatically.

-
The invoice will display the Bill-To customer’s information in the Sold-To field.

-
The original customer information from the Header tab will appear in the Ship-To field on the invoice.

Example:
If Customer ID ‘00002’ has Bill-To ID set as ‘00005’, then:

-
00005’s details will populate the Sold-To field on the invoice.

-
00002’s details will appear in the Ship-To field.

Resolution:

When a customer is configured with a Bill-To ID, Traverse provides a dropdown selection when creating a Sales Order. This allows the user to choose between:

-
The Customer ID itself, or

-
The Bill-To ID set up under the AR Customers screen.



For example, let's consider the Customer ID 00002, with 'Bill To ID' as 00005:



Now, when the User attempts to create a new Sales order, Traverse allows the User to specify the 'Bill To ID' as either of the two: 00002 or 00005:

[NOTE: Traverse will not allow the User to update the 'Bill To' information once the order is saved]





Now, While the Sales Order is still in open status, the Bill-To ID (‘00005’) is removed from the AR Customers screen under the path: Applications → Accounts Receivable → Setup and Maintenance → Customers:

[NOTE: The same happens, even if the 'Bill To ID' was updated to a different Customer ID as well]





At this point, Traverse will no longer allow processing of this Sales Order, as the referenced Bill-To ID ‘00005’ is no longer valid in the system, and will throw the mentioned error message: "Bill To customer is not valid"





In order to proceed with processing the Sales order, the User must review the 'Bill To ID' existing on the Sales Order under the Tab 'Bill-To' and update the same in the AR Customers screen:



Then navigate to the AR Customers screen under the path: Applications -> Accounts Receivable -> Setup and Maintenance -> Customers.



Once the 'Bill To' information had been updated in the AR Customers screen and saved, Traverse would allow the user to process the Sales Order without any issues:



Key Takeaway:

The Bill-To ID must remain valid throughout the lifecycle of a transaction. If removed or invalidated while a Sales Order is still active, the system will block further processing until a valid Bill-To ID is restored or reassigned.

453fff14-2a90-455e-b4f4-bd798ba066d1.title: How to reset the Digital ID in On-Time Web Timeclock
453fff14-2a90-455e-b4f4-bd798ba066d1.content:
Problem
On-Time Web Punches are not making it to the On-Time Website from the time clock. We have checked the IP address and the network settings. What else can I check?

Resolution
How to check and or reset your Digital ID in your On-Time Web Time clock.  Send a request for your Digital ID to support@on-timeweb.com along with the serial number, which can be found in your clock setting in On-Time Web (see below.)

Here are the steps to do so.
- Press the Lock button on the device.
- Enter the security code, 14153625319. Do not press enter, it will accept it once the code has been fully keyed.
- Use the arrow buttons to scroll to View Digital ID. Press enter. It will then show the Digital ID and some other information.
- Verify the Digital ID. It should be <digital ID from Admin Site> for this clock.
- If it is not, use the arrow buttons to scroll to Enter Digital ID. Press enter.
- Follow the on-screen prompts to key in the digital ID and write it.
- Use the arrow keys to scroll to Do Callback. Press enter. The clock should have now have connected.

Problem
How to create a schedule on On Time Web

A Master Work Schedule must be created before it can be applied to individual employees. To build a Master Work Schedule complete the information and save. You may also edit a Master Work Schedule by selecting it from the drop down menu.

c23a2ba2-fc35-479a-8378-1986092cd7ec.title: Newly setup Local Payroll Tax Not Being Withheld when calculating Payroll checks
c23a2ba2-fc35-479a-8378-1986092cd7ec.content:
Problem
Customer has entered a new local payroll tax with its formula set up in in the Formulas and Formula Tables functions, but it is not being withheld from an employee's payroll during processing.

Resolution
Verify the formula in Payroll Formulas and Formula Tables to ensure that the setup is correct there. If everything looks good, then ensure that the formula ID has been assigned to the local Tax Authority.
Navigate to Payroll> Codes maintenance> Tax Authorities
Switch to Local for the Tax Authority drop-down.

The Formula ID is empty. Assign the respective Formula ID and Save.

Navigate to Payroll> Payday work> Manual checks> Ok.
Pull up the Employee ID in question> Select the Earning code and hit Calculate and Calculate Tax at the top.

Upon calculating, navigate to Withholdings tab,

Here you should now be able to see the local taxes calculating.

9616eb78-9fcf-4871-af02-b4517ca9c9f6.title: How to Use the Standard RP Report for Purchase and Assembly Planning
9616eb78-9fcf-4871-af02-b4517ca9c9f6.content:
Problem
Users need to identify which items must be purchased or assembled within a specific time frame, but are unsure how to correctly generate and interpret the Standard RP Report.

Resolution
Generate RP Data

-
Navigate to Requirements Planning > RP Processing > Generate RP Data.

-
Apply filters as needed, or leave them blank to include all items.

-
Click OK to start the process.

-
Once completed successfully, a confirmation message will appear: “Process is complete.”

Open the Standard RP Report

-
Go to the Standard RP Report screen.

-
Apply a filter for Item ID, if required ,leave it blank to generate the report for all items.



Set Reporting Parameters

-
Period Definition ID: Select the desired time frame for the report.

-
Start Date: Choose the starting date for the report period.

-
Include Items: Select one of the following options:

-
Required – Includes only items that have shortages.

-
Active – Includes items with any recorded activity.

-
All – Includes all items based on the data filter applied.

To prevent the system from automatically generating planned orders:

-
Go to Business Rules > Reports Section > Options Tab.

-
Ensure the checkbox for “Suggest Planned Orders” is unchecked.

4a09cc8f-0e85-4c2d-9a01-a1dbeec08f75.title: Need understanding of the tradmin account
4a09cc8f-0e85-4c2d-9a01-a1dbeec08f75.content:
Problem
The customer has informed us that their security team is currently conducting a User Access Review and has raised a query regarding the tradmin account. They are seeking clarification and a deeper understanding of this account to effectively communicate the information to their team.

Resolution
The tradmin account is a system account created by Aptean during the SSMS and server manager setup at the start of the installation process. Its primary purpose is to provide administrative access to Aptean for performing tasks, troubleshooting, and managing any emergencies related to the Traverse system during the installation. This account has high-level administrative privileges and is strictly used for system purposes, ensuring the smooth operation of the Traverse environment. It is a secure account and does not affect other users or any other processes.

It is important that this account is not deleted, as it is required for accessing various administrative processes. The account is created in the server manager specifically to facilitate system checks and maintenance within the Traverse system.

8b93ed1d-45c1-4c01-a23b-94b8b4bf0ceb.title: How to resolve the error 'The application has failed to start because its side-by-side configuration is incorrect. Please see the application event log or use the command-line sxstrace.exe tool for more detail' while launching Traverse?
8b93ed1d-45c1-4c01-a23b-94b8b4bf0ceb.content:
Problem
How to resolve the error 'The application has failed to start because its side-by-side configuration is incorrect. Please see the application event log or use the command-line sxstrace.exe tool for more detail.' while launching Traverse?

Resolution
This error typically occurs when the application's configuration file becomes corrupted or contains incorrect values, preventing the program from launching successfully. A common symptom is the following error message:

The application has failed to start because its side-by-side configuration is incorrect.
Please see the application event log or use the command-line sxstrace.exe tool for more detail.

Root Cause:

The root cause is often tied to an invalid or improperly configured application configuration file (TRAVERSE.exe.config). This file governs essential settings, including server connection details. Corruption or inaccuracies in this file can lead to the side-by-side configuration error.



The Config file can be found in the path: C:\Program Files\Open Systems, Inc\TRAVERSE Global\ [The file can be located by filtering or sorted through the 'File Type' being 'Config File']



A frequent scenario is observed when the client folder is copied directly from the server. In such cases, the Config file may still reference the server's name as "localhost", which works on the server itself but fails on end-user workstations, as "localhost" points to the local machine.

Resolution Steps:

i. Review the Configuration File:

-
-
Navigate to the application folder under the path C:\Program Files\Open Systems, Inc\TRAVERSE Global\ and open the TRAVERSE.exe.config file.

-
Verify that all entries, particularly the Server name and License Port, are accurate.



ii. Compare with a Working Workstation:

-
-
If the error persists despite the configuration appearing correct, obtain the TRAVERSE.exe.config file from another workstation where the application is functioning properly.

-
Replace the existing file on the problematic workstation with this verified working version.





iii. Replace Entire Client Folder (if needed):

-
-
In cases where replacing the configuration file alone does not resolve the issue, it is recommended to replace the entire client folder.

-
Ensure the new folder is sourced from a verified working environment and that all configuration files are updated accordingly.

NOTE: Always back up the existing configuration file and client folder before making replacements.

6a790dae-187e-48f6-9b3a-d919392e649f.title: New General Ledger account number
6a790dae-187e-48f6-9b3a-d919392e649f.content:
Problem
We need to set up a new general ledger account number.

Resolution
Use the Chart of Accounts function to set up and maintain the chart of accounts. Make sure that the General Ledger tables and records in other applications interfaced with General Ledger match the appropriate accounts in the chart of accounts. If they do not match, you cannot properly post the entries from those applications.





Creating a Chart of Accounts

Click the New button, on the toolbar, to open a blank chart of accounts record.

Enter the segment ID for the different segments from the Segment ID field to create the new account ID.  Either select a Segment ID from the drop down list or type in a new Segment ID. (You can also create a new Segment ID in the Account Segments screen, where you can edit the Description for the segment as well.)
Note: To copy account information from a similar record for a new chart of accounts record, select the existing account from the Copy From field. The Copy From field only appears when you are entering a new account.

Enter a description of the new account ID in the Description field.

Select the Currency ID: If you use multicurrency, select the currency to assign to the account from the Currency ID field.
Note: When an account uses a currency other than the base currency, Traverse automatically converts transaction amounts entered into that account using the exchange rate you specify.

Select the status of the account from the Status field: Active, Inactive, or Discontinued. This status appears in all account combo boxes throughout Traverse and controls whether transactions entered for the account post to the GL Journal; active accounts post to the GL Journal, inactive and discontinued accounts do not.
The inactive and discontinued statuses prevent entries to accounts that are no longer used while preserving historical and audit trail information. If an account will never be used again, assign it a status of Discontinued.
The system treats inactive and discontinued accounts as invalid accounts during processing. If transaction amounts exist for inactive or discontinued accounts when you post, the system does not post those amounts to the GL Journal and alerts you with an error message that invalid accounts exist.

Print the Invalid GL Accounts List (available in the System Manager, System Audits menu and the Invalid GL Accounts List function) to identify invalid, inactive, or discontinued accounts if you encounter problems when posting. Within GL, print the Chart of Accounts List to identify inactive or discontinued accounts.
Note: The status entered controls whether transactions entered for the account post to the GL Journal. Only active accounts post to the GL Journal.

Select an account type from the Account Type field. NOTE: It is very important to select the correct account type when setting up the Account ID. The account type will determine if the account ID is a debit or credit balance account. Once journal transactions have been posted to Master, you will not be allowed to change the account type to one that has a different balance type

.For a revenue or expense account, select the account to which to clear the new account, if applicable, from the Clear To Account field. If you do not want to clear the account at the end of the year, make sure that you leave the Clear To Account field blank.

If you select an account in the Clear To Account field, you also need to enter a step to clear the account in the adjacent Step field. The account you select must match currencies with the Account selected in step 2.

If you want to consolidate the account with an account in a different company, enter that account number in the Consol To Account box. If you do not want to consolidate the account, leave this field blank. The system uses this information in the Consolidate Chart of Accounts function.
Consolidating an account does not affect the balance of the account.

If you select an account in the Consol To Account field, you also need to enter a step to consolidate the account in the adjacent Step field. The account you select must match currencies with the Account selected in step 2. If you enter 0, the account will not be consolidated. To consolidate all accounts in one step, enter 1.

Click the Save button, on the toolbar, to save the new record.

6d43b086-51fa-4f1c-995e-98138473b386.title: Attachment/Notes in GL Transactions
6d43b086-51fa-4f1c-995e-98138473b386.content:
Problem
If you write Multiple GL Transaction with the Notes/ Attachment and Apply filter to Refresh the SM Manage Attachments> It will just update the existing values with new values and will not create a new entry. The Attachments should be specific to each GL Transaction, similar to the working of AP or AR Transaction.

Resolution
Attachments will be linked to each batch code rather than individual transactions. Since batch codes must be unique, having identical batch codes would result in duplicate entries in SM Manage Attachments. To avoid this, we need to generate unique batch codes instead of relying solely on the default batch code #####.

To create new Batch code, navigate to General Ledger> Setup and maintenance> Transaction batch code

Upon this, when creating Transaction from Application> General Ledger> Transactions> Transactions> under the Notes section> Leave the existing Notes undisturbed and use the + icon at the bottom to enter the notes for the specific new Transaction. click ok and Save.

Write the GL Transaction. Now, if you navigate to System Manager> Company Setup> Manage Documents> you will find the GL notes/Attachments as a unique line entry

5a69d1a3-5b08-4d62-b0ff-718d62ee8f1e.title: Print checks and post Payments in AP
5a69d1a3-5b08-4d62-b0ff-718d62ee8f1e.content:
Problem
What is the procedure for preparing and posting payments, as well as printing checks in Accounts Payable (AP)?

Resolution
Use the Transactions function to enter or edit invoices and miscellaneous debits for vendors.

If Accounts Payable interfaces with Inventory, when you enter transactions in Accounts Payable, item location information, detail history, and lot and serial information in Inventory get updated if the Inventory options are set to retain this information.



Follow the below steps to create a new transaction in AP

Step 1: Navigate to Applications > Accounts Payable > Transactions > Transactions

Step 1.1: Click the New button [+] to open a blank accounts payable record. The system will generate a new transaction number with some default details.

Step 1.2: For the new transaction, the transaction type would be an Invoice by default.

Step 1.3: In the Batch Code field, select a batch code for the transaction from the drop-down list. The description of the batch appears for verification. This field only appears if you elect to use batch processing in the Business Rules function.

Step 1.4: If you entered a default Location ID when you set up company information in System Manager, that Location ID appears and can be changed; otherwise, select the location ID you are purchasing the items for. Leave this field blank for transactions that do not involve an inventory item.

Step 1.5: Select the Vendor ID you are purchasing goods from or returning goods to. The vendor’s name, default terms code, distribution code, tax group ID, and currency (if you use multicurrency) appear.

Step 1.6: Enter the vendor’s Invoice Number for the items you purchased or returned. A warning message appears if you enter the number of an open invoice or an invoice that is in history. If you selected Yes to the check for duplicate invoice numbers, you will be prompted to enter a different invoice number.

Step 1.7: Invoice Date - Use the default workstation date, or enter the date of the vendor’s invoice. If you change the Invoice Date, an invoice message appears stating that the due date has been adjusted.

Step 1.8: Enter your Notes about the transaction. Notes are saved in history information. If you selected Yes to the option to print notes on remittance, the text in the notes field will be printed on the check stub or check saver remittance report.

Step 1.9: Select the Terms and Distribution Codes. Code descriptions appear.

Step 1.10: If you use multicurrency, you can change the distribution code only if no open invoices or transactions exist for the vendor and if the Payables account associated with the new distribution code is in either the vendor’s or the base currency.

Step 1.11: The Tax Group ID from the vendor's record appears. If you change this ID, sales tax for the transaction is recalculated. Mark the Taxable check box if the transaction is taxable. Clear the check box if the transaction is nontaxable.

Step 1.12: If the vendor is set up to receive a 1099-MISC form, the 1099 Invoice check box is marked. If you want the purchase to update the 1099 Payments Year-to-Date field in the vendor’s record, leave the box selected; if not, clear the check box. This check box appears only if the vendor is set up to receive a 1099-MISC form.

Step 1.13: The Fiscal Period and Year are calculated from the invoice date but can be changed.

Step 1.14 In the PO Number field, enter the purchase order number.







Step 1.15: After entering all the required details in the Header tab, enter the ItemID field from the drop-down that appears when you place your cursor on the new line entry.

Adjust the number of quantities as required and the amount as well. Once you fill in the Unit cost and quantity, the Ext cost automatically gets updated accordingly.



Step 1.16: After making all the necessary adjustments, Click the Save button on the toolbar to save your changes.



Step 2: We would now need to preview/print the Purchases Journal and verify the transaction that we have just saved.

2.1 Navigate to AP> Transaction Journal > Purchases Journal

2.2 Save your changes and close out your AP Transaction screen. Apply the filters as required and select the batch code. Here the batch code would be KBTST.

2.3 Click on the Preview button on the toolbar. A window opens with the preview screen. Verify if the transaction details that we just entered in the AP Transactions screen are correct.

Step 3: This is an additional step. Please note if you encounter the error “The following batches are either in use or locked (batchname)” this can occur because the AP Transaction screen is still open. If all AP Transaction screens are closed, then you would need to unlock any locks by navigating to the AP> Setup and Maintenance > Transaction Batch Codes. If there is a Lock there, click the "Lock" button to unlock. Also, click the Activity column of your batch and delete the line entry that comes up in the dialog box. Hit Save.

Now Go back to the AP Purchases Journal screen and do the Preview. At times, clients may encounter such errors. Only during that time, this step is required to troubleshoot. If not, this can be skipped.



Step 4: Once the preview is done and verified, we can Post the transactions.

4.1 Navigate to AP> Transaction Journal > Post Transactions.

4.2 Check the box “Do the following, then check the box”. This ensures that the following things within the box have been completed before you post those transactions.

4.3 If you check the box “Post all invoices as held” the invoices will come into the "Hold/Released Invoices" screen in the status of “Hold.” You would need to go to this screen and release them in order to pay them. If you choose not to hold all invoices, use the Hold/Released Invoices screen to mark the invoices you want to put into a "Hold" status.

4.4 Select the required batch code. (If using batch processing according to the Business rules settings.) Here it is “KBTST”

4.5 Now hit the button “OK” on the toolbar to successfully post the Transaction.

4.6 Once done successfully, you will get a prompt stating “Post has been successfully completed”. A preview window will open where you can view the posted transaction.





Step 5: Now the transaction will be available on the AP Hold/Release Invoices screen for them to be paid.

5.1 Navigate to AP > Pay Invoices > Hold/Release Invoices

5.2 Select the Vendor ID from the drop-down available when you click the ellipses …

5.3 This will show up all the invoices for this particular vendor.

Now, if you wish to pay the invoice(s) that you have created and posted, you can change the status of all other invoices to "Hold" and the selected invoice(s) that you wish to make a payment for to be "Released." You will need to prepare this invoice in the following steps to create a payment for it, print it, and post it.

If you wish to create a pre-payment for an invoice from this screen, you can click on the "Prepay" button and enter in the payment details - payment number, payment date, fiscal period/year, and bank and click OK. The Status of the line item will change to "Paid." You will need to prepare this payment in the following steps to print this payment and post it.



Step 6: After making the necessary adjustments in the AP Hold/ Release screen, the next step would be to prepare the payments.

6.1 Navigate to AP > Pay Invoices > Prepare Payments screen

6.2 Use the Data Filter to select the range of filtering options or leave the filter blank to include all available data.

6.3 Select a batch code to represent the group of payments to prepare from the Batch Code field. The Batch Code you select will NOT automatically correspond to the same batch that was used to post the transactions, pulling in the same group of transactions. This is a completely separate, new batch into which to group the payments you wish to prepare.

6.4 Select a due date for the invoices from the Invoices Due field. All invoices with a due date on or prior to this date will be included in the prepare payments, for the range of vendors selected, and have a status of released.

6.5 Enter the Discounts Due date up to which to take discounts. Discounts are calculated for invoices with a discount due date after or equal to the entered discount due date.

Note: The dates you enter determine which invoices to prepare. Payments are prepared for invoices with a net due date before or equal to the invoice date entered. Also, the system prepares invoices on which the discount due date, stored in the Open Invoice table, is less than or equal to the Invoices Due date entered on the Prepare Payments screen, but greater than the Discounts Due date entered here.

Select the date to print on the payments from the Payment Date field.

6.5 Enter the fiscal period and year for which to post payments in the Fiscal Period/Year fields. The fiscal period and year will default to the period the payment date falls in.

6.6 Select a bank account ID from the Bank Account ID field. Payments prepared in this check run are flagged with this bank account ID. (*If a pre-payment you wish to prepare has a different Bank Account ID selected (see the Hold/Released screen - Bank ID column) than this one, it will not be included in this check run. If the payment you wish to process is not being included in this batch, check this field.

6.7 Enter any applicable comments about the payment in the Comments field. For now, I have left the field blank.

6.8 Now, click the Prompt “OK” command to prepare the payments.

6.9 Once done successfully, you will get a prompt stating “Payments prepared successfully”. A preview window will open where you can view the prepared payments.





Step 7: Additional Step. If you feel like you have posted the payments in the wrong date or there are certain changes that you would need to make to that payment before it gets posted, you can use the Select Payables screen to drop those particular payments. Select the Batch Code, and the Vendor, check the "drop" box for the Invoice and click "Write." Once you drop it, you can go back to the AP Hold/ Release screen, make the necessary changes, prepare it again, and post it.



Step 8: Preview the Edit Register

8.1 Navigate to AP > Pay Invoices > Edit Register

8.2 Select the batch code, and the corresponding data filter will automatically update, appearing in a greyed-out state. Hit Preview

8.3 This will open a Preview Edit Register screen. Ensure that the payment amount and the corresponding details are correct.



Step 9: Print Checks

9.1 Navigate to AP > Pay Invoices > Print Checks

9.2 Use the Data Filter to select the range of filtering options or leave the filter blank to include all available data.

Select the batch code containing the checks to print from the Batch Code field. This box is only available when you select yes to the use batch processing in the business rules function.

The Invoices Due Date, Vendor IDs, Currency, Discounts Due Date, Check Date, Fiscal Period and Year, Bank Account, and Payment Exchange Rate (as applicable) you selected when you prepared checks are displayed.

Enter the number of the first check to print in the Check Number Starting field.
Note: If you are reprinting checks, specify the last good check number in the Last Good field. Hit Preview to view the check and print to print it. You select, "Output" to output the checks to a PDF file from which you can print as needed.





(If you are using ACH to process payments, then you would go to the Payment Vouchers screen to print vouchers for those payments.)

Create the Positive Pay file to submit payment verifications to the bank if you are using this function.

Create the ACH File to submit the payment records for your ACH payments to your bank if you are using this function. This process is detailed in other Knowledge Base articles.



Step 10: View Payment Register

Select the Batch Code you are processing, and click "Preview" to preview the register of payments you just printed for any errors. Click "Output" to save this file as a PDF to your computer, or select "Print" to print the file.

***Traverse checks whether this Payment Register has printed before posting the payments. If the Business Rule setting, "Post Without Printing Journals" is set to "No", then if this Payment Register has not been output to PDF or printed, the posting screen will prompt that not all reports have been printed and will not allow you to post. If you are having printing problems, you can output to PDF to be able to post.



This register will show the payments grouped by type, with printed paper checks showing first followed by any EFT/ACH payments. **You will want to check the dates and the Payment Numbers that appear, which indicate the dates and check numbers that will be posted and stored in the history views in Traverse. You will want to ensure that these match any reprinted checks in particular. (If any payment or check number needs to be corrected, checks can be re-prepared if the business rule "Allow Re-prepare After Printing" is set to yes.)



Step 11: Post Payments

10.1 Navigate to AP > Pay Invoices > Post Payments

10.2 Select the batch code and Do the Following check box and Hit OK to post the payments.

**It is important to note your business rules regarding what payments Traverse will process. If you have the "Allow Posting Without Check Numbers" set to "Yes", you will be able to post checks that have no payment numbers on them, but if this is set to "No" you will not be able to post any checks that have no payment number. If you do not want blank payment numbers in your payment history, it is recommended to set this setting to "No."

If you need to post a payment without printing it (ex. a zero balance creating no check), the option "Allow Posting without Printing Checks" can be set to "Yes" to allow this processing.





10.3 Click Yes when the following prompt appears

10.4 Once posted, you will receive a prompt stating “Post Payments has successfully completed” and a report showing that those payments as posted.

d4221140-33a9-4a20-b1e2-b493d328b33d.title: Retrieving Assembly and Component Details Using SQL Joins
d4221140-33a9-4a20-b1e2-b493d328b33d.content:
Problem
The requirement is to extract specific details related to Assemblies and their corresponding Components from two SQL tables:

- tblMbAssemblyHeader – Stores high-level information about assemblies.
- tblMbAssemblyDetail – Stores detailed information about the components within each assembly.

Resolution
The requirement is to retrieve the following fields:

- Assembly ID (from tblMbAssemblyHeader)
- Component ID (from tblMbAssemblyDetail)
- Description of Component (from tblMbAssemblyDetail)
- LocId (from tblMbAssemblyDetail)
- UOM (from tblMbAssemblyDetail)
- ScrapPct (from tblMbAssemblyDetail)

However, the Assembly ID is only present in the tblMbAssemblyHeader table, whereas the Component ID and other details are stored in tblMbAssemblyDetail. To retrieve a meaningful dataset, we need to establish a relationship between these two tables.



Relationship between the 2 Tables:

The common key that links both tables is:

-
- Id from tblMbAssemblyHeader

-
- HeaderId from tblMbAssemblyDetail

- Using this relationship, we can perform an INNER JOIN to combine relevant data.



In order to meet the Client's requirements, we would need to run the below query:

SELECT
h.AssemblyId AS [Assembly ID],
d.ComponentId AS [Component ID],
d.Description AS [Description of Component],
d.LocId AS [Location/Work Center],
d.UOM,
d.Qty AS [Quantity],
d.ScrapPct AS [Scrap %]
FROM [CPU].[dbo].[tblMbAssemblyDetail] d
JOIN [CPU].[dbo].[tblMbAssemblyHeader] h
ON d.HeaderId = h.Id;

[Please note that the Company name 'CPU' should be overridden by the Client's Company Name]

This Query provides us with the below Output:



This information can be exported by right-clicking on the 'Data' and choosing 'Save Results As...', and then saving the File in the required Location:



Output File: [Please note that the Headers will not be present, and we can add those as needed after exporting]:



NOTE: There are multiple fields available in each SQL Table, and we need to tweak the query accordingly to pull the required information:

Table: tblMbAssemblyHeader

Id, AssemblyId, RevisionNo, Description, EffectiveDateFrom, EffectiveDateThru, DrawingNumber, LotSize, UOM, MrpCode, Engineer, Backflushed(Y/N), DfltRevYn, LastUpdated, Instructions

Table: tblMbAssemblyDetail

Id, RoutingId, HeaderId, Sequence, ComponentId, CompRevisionNo, LocId, UOM, UsageType, Qty, ScrapPct, UnitCost, CostGroupId, DetailType, Backflushed(Y/N), Notes, Component Description

03a67e11-6904-4035-94ec-623b08dedfbd.title: How to Enter Estimates in Project Costing
03a67e11-6904-4035-94ec-623b08dedfbd.content:
Problem
How to enter Estimates in Project Costing

Resolution
Use the Estimates function to enter cost and income Estimates, for Materials, Expenses, Other costs, and Time, for Projects, Phases, and Tasks.

You also can copy Estimates that have been previously entered, to duplicate past Estimate records. Time Estimates do not require an Employee ID to be entered for more general Estimating of time projected for a Project/Phase/Task.

To set up Estimates, follow these steps:

1. Select Estimates from the Setup and Maintenance menu

2. Select the Project/Task for which you want to apply the estimates. You will see a row in the search box for each Project, Project and Task, and Project, Task and Phase combination set up.

Expense:

3. Use the Expense area to enter Material, Expense and Other type of expense estimates.

4. Select the Estimate Type to apply the estimate to the Project/Task: Material, Expense, and Other.

5. Select or enter the Item ID for the Estimate. When you select Material you will be able to search for Inventory or System Manager Description Items. When you select Expense and Other types enter an Item ID or skip this field and enter a Description.

6. Select or enter the Location ID for the Estimate. When you select Material you will be able to search for Inventory Location IDs. When you select Expense and Other the Location ID search is not available

7. Enter a Description or accept the Description from your Item selection. When you select Material for the Type and select an Item the Description will fill in from the Item ID selected. When you select Expense and Other for the Type, enter a Description for the line entered.

8. Enter the Quantity for the Estimate.

9. Enter the Unit of Measure to use for the Estimate, or accept the Unit brought in from the Item selected. If you enter Material and select an Item from the Item ID list the, Unit set up for the Item will be displayed, and you may select an alternate Unit if one is set up. If you select Expense or Other, you may enter the Unit of Measure to which you want the item to refer. You may leave this field blank for Expense and Other Types of Estimates.

10. Enter the Unit Cost to use for the Estimate, or accept the Cost brought in from the Item. If you select Material and an Item ID from Inventory, you will not be allowed to change the Unit Cost. If you select an Expense or Other Type, enter the Unit Cost.

11. Enter the Unit Price to use for the Estimate, or accept the Price brought in from the Item. If you select Material and an Item ID from Inventory, you may change the Price. If you select an Expense or Other Type, enter the Unit Price.

12. The Extended Cost is calculated from the Quantity times the Unit Cost. This field is not allowed to be edited.

13. The Extended Price is calculated from the Quantity times the Unit Price. This field is not allowed to be edited.

14. The Profit is calculated from the Extended Cost minus the Extended Price. This field is not allowed to be edited.

Time

15. Select an Employee ID to enter Estimated Time for the Project. If you are interfaced to Payroll you will see Payroll Employees in the list. If you are not interfaced to Payroll you will see System Manager Employees. You may leave this field blank if you are entering general time to be used for the Estimate that is not tied to an Employee. You will use the Time Ticket entry to record the actual time spent on the Project.

16. Select a Rate Code if this is applicable.

17. Enter the Location ID for the Project Estimate. You may type any Location you wish into this field, there is no link to any Inventory Location IDs. You may leave this field blank.

18. Enter a Description for the Time Estimated for the Project.

19. Enter the Quantity for the Estimate.

20. The Unit of Measure for a Time Estimate is always recorded in Hours and cannot be changed.

21. Enter the Unit Cost per hour to use for the Estimate.
22. Enter the Unit Price per hour to use for the Estimate.

23. The Extended Cost is calculated from the Quantity times the Unit Cost. This field is not allowed to be edited.

24. The Extended Price is calculated from the Quantity times the Unit Price. This field is not allowed to be edited.

25. The Profit is calculated from the Extended Cost minus the Extended Price. This field is not allowed to be edited.

Use the Estimates View function to produce a list of the Estimates you defined in the Estimates function on the Setup and Maintenance menu.

e602505b-f887-4a46-bd2c-6150ee3a1846.title: SQL Error WM Order Inquiry View
e602505b-f887-4a46-bd2c-6150ee3a1846.content:
Problem
It appears to be only affecting WM. We have checked our Server and rebooted it with no change. This error occurs when customer tries to open WM Order Inquiry view and apply the filter.

SQL Server error encountered. Please check the error for details for more information.

Details:
SQL Server error encountered. Please check the error for details for more information.

5000: 515 : Cannot insert the value NULL into the column 'ReqDate'. table tempdb.dbo.#OrderList______________________________________________________________0000000017AF'; column does not allow nulls. INSERT fails. : Procedure {dbo.trav_WMPickReleaseOrders_BuildOrderList_MP_proc} : Procedure {dbo.trav_RaiseError_proc} (.Net SqlClient Data Provider)

For help, click: http://go.microsoft.com/fwlink?ProdName=Microsoft%20SQL%20Server&ProdVer=16.00.4185&EvtSrc=MSSQLServer&EvtID=50000&LinkId=20476

Server Name: MXXXXXXP\TXXXXXXBAL
Error Number: 5000
Severity: 16
State: 2
Procedure: dbo.trav_RaiseError_proc
Line Number: 17

Program Location:

at TRAVERSE.Client.ViewControlBase.OnProcessCompleted()
at TRAVERSE.Client.ViewControlBase.TaskCompleted(Exception processError. Boolean cancelled)

Resolution
Let break this down.

- 5000: 515 : Cannot insert the value NULL into the column 'ReqDate'. table tempdb.dbo.#OrderList______________________________________________________________0000000017AF'; column does not allow nulls. INSERT fails. : Procedure {dbo.trav_WMPickReleaseOrders_BuildOrderList_MP_proc} : Procedure {dbo.trav_RaiseError_proc} (.Net SqlClient Data Provider)
- Procedure {dbo.trav_WMPickReleaseOrders_BuildOrderList_MP_proc} - This tells you the Stored Procedure where the code is getting run that is generating this error.
- Cannot insert the value NULL into the column 'ReqDate'. table tempdb.dbo.#OrderList - This tells us that table where the insert is failing is #OrderList, and the column it is trying to insert the null into is ReqDate

So, if we go into SSMS, find that stored procedure and view it, you should see somewhere in that where something happens to insert data into #orderList, and it should include the ReqDate column.  Then we want to see what it is trying to insert, and where it is getting that information from.

Below is the part of stored procedure code.

.... Select s1.TransId, isnull(e.SeqNum, 0) SeqNum, s1.ComponentType, s1.ComponentId, s1.LocId, s1.UOM
, req.EstStartDate AS RequiredDate, rel.OrderNo, rel.ReleaseNo, req.ReqId
, e.LotNum, e.ExtLocA, e.ExtLocB, (e.QtyRequired - e.QtyFilled) ExtQtyReq, s1.EstQtyRequired
From dbo.tblMpMatlSum s1
INNER JOIN  tblMpRequirements req ON req.TransId =s1.TransId
INNER JOIN  tblMpOrderReleases rel ON rel.Id=req.ReleaseId.....

From the above code, we can understand that we are getting the values from tblMpMatlSum, tblMpRequirements and tblMpOrderReleases.

Use below query to review,

- SELECT * from tblMpRequirements WHERE EstStartDate IS NULL

We will find something like this.

Also review tblMpMatlSum,

- SELECT * from tblMpMatlSum WHERE RequiredDate IS NULL

Use the Release ID to look into tblMpOrderReleases in order to find the Order Number, look up that production order and see if you can see on it where these screwed up lines are. Else we may need to delete the order entirely and create it again. This will resolve this issue.

939d97bd-3de9-4e45-ad7c-0dbf3868aec1.title: Reprinting a Check (ex. Accounts Payable)
939d97bd-3de9-4e45-ad7c-0dbf3868aec1.content:
Problem
The customer wants to know where to go in Traverse to get a copy of a check that was printed?

Resolution
If Document Archiving is on, then documents that have been sent can be found in:



System Manager -> Document Archive -> Manage Documents

You should be able to see the documents in SM Manage Documents.



If Document Archiving is not turned on, then this can be changed in the business rule settings.

This can be updated under the path: System Manager -> Company Setup -> Business Rules:

Choose the 'SM-System Manager' section again and locate the 'Miscellaneous' section.

Find the below highlighted option 'Enable Document Archiving' and set it to 'Yes'. Then click on 'Apply' and 'OK' to save the changes.

Each application in which document archiving is available also has an Archive section in its Business rules that you will want to check as well, for example - Accounts Payable:

The following applications include an option to define if you would like to use document archiving and the Archive Watermark feature.

- Accounts Payable
- Purchase Order
- Accounts Receivable (Note: Sales Order and Service Director use the AR business rule)
- Point of Sale
- Project Costing
- Payroll

Once these settings have been set, the corresponding documents that have printed out of Traverse will be saved in the system and will be available for reprinting.

For certain applications, such as Payroll, you can also access reprints from a history view (ex. PA Check History View) by selecting the transaction in the list, and clicking the "Print" drop down in the menu.

aad3d6f1-74e7-4797-9d8f-bf29fb037bd7.title: Individual Tracking report is not working
aad3d6f1-74e7-4797-9d8f-bf29fb037bd7.content:
Problem
The IT Tracking > Management Reports > Attendance report is not pulling the necessary information, it looks blank, as shown below, with no information.



Whereas the same data is successfully retrieved from the IT Tracking > Inquiry > Attendance report. But we do not have an option to export to PDF in this report.



Now that the client would like to retrieve the data in the Management report -> Attendance report. How can it be done?

Resolution
- We would need to make sure that the setup is correct. The first place where we would need to look at is the business days setup.

Why?

In the context of IT attendance reports, business days typically refer to the standard working days of an organization (usually Monday through Friday, excluding weekends and holidays). The relationship between business days and an IT attendance report is that the report often tracks attendance, leave, and working hours based on business days rather than calendar days.



Without setting up business days in the setup and maintenance of the system, the attendance report may fail to generate because the system relies on business days to define the scope of data to be included.

Here in this case, the setup has been missing for the year 2025 under Business days < Setup and Maintenance < Individual Tracking.

So, made entries on the Business days screen for months 1, 2,3 of the 2025 fiscal year by clicking onto the add + icon at the bottom of the screen. (It is ideal that we setup all 12 fiscal period to avoid facing this problem in the future)

After adding the required fields, ensure to save the data.

Now, if you could go back and generate the attendance report from the Management report screen, the PDF file containing the data will be displayed.

d09ca344-f5f5-413d-8d4e-19697dcdaed4.title: Purchase order receiving
d09ca344-f5f5-413d-8d4e-19697dcdaed4.content:
Problem
Material was received in March, using the same receipt # as a different line item that was receiving in February. Period 2 has already been posted yet the period 3 material go attached to the period 2 receipt, unposted, yet we cannot delete it. We need the two receipts separated.

Resolution
Here are a few possible solutions:

-
If the receipt can be deleted: You may need to delete the invoice for the incorrectly posted items and then re-enter the receipts and invoice in the correct period.

-
If the receipt line cannot be deleted: Some customers have tried reopening the period and attempting to delete the line again.

Here for the specific case, they were able to resolve the issue by reopening period 2, posting the receipt, and then adjusting it in the GL Ledger to post in period 3 before finalizing.

v. Finalize the Split:

-
-

7a44e2f1-898a-4f0a-acc9-e6d508f2e58a.title: What causes the 502 Bad Gateway Error and how to resolve it?
7a44e2f1-898a-4f0a-acc9-e6d508f2e58a.content:
Problem How to resolve the error: 502 Bad Gateway Detailed Error message: =================================== 502 Bad Gateway

502 Bad Gateway

nginx
(TRAVERSE.Business.SalesOrder) ------------------------------ Program Location: at TRAVERSE.Business.SalesOrder.TransactionHeader.CalculateTaxes() at TRAVERSE.Business.SalesOrder.TransactionHeader.CalculateTotals(Boolean raiseEvent) at TRAVERSE.Business.SalesOrder.TransactionHeaderProvider.UpdateHeader(String compId, TransactionHeader header) at TRAVERSE.Business.SalesOrder.TransactionHeaderProvider.Update(String compId) at TRAVERSE.Client.SalesOrder.TransactionHeaderControl.SaveTransaction() at TRAVERSE.Client.SalesOrder.TransactionHeaderControl.UpdateData(Int32 index) Resolution The 502 Bad Gateway error in the Traverse application generally indicates a communication issue between the web server (nginx) and the application server (in this case, the Traverse backend). Given the stack trace and context you've shared, here’s how you can approach resolving this issue step by step: Root Cause Analysis: - Error occurs during a Sales Order transaction, specifically while calling: - CalculateTaxes() - CalculateTotals() - UpdateHeader() - The issue is not directly related to user input, but rather during a backend process or service call, likely involving the tax calculation or external service. Resolution Steps: 1. Restart Services - Ensure the Traverse Application Services and IIS (Web Server) are running on the server. - Ensure the nginx reverse proxy (if used between web and app servers) is running without errors. 2. Review Tax Configuration - Check if the tax calculation service or integration (like Avalara) is: - Properly configured - Available and responsive - This error might occur if tax calculation is trying to reach an external service which is not responding correctly. 3. Check System Resources - Review CPU / Memory usage on the server. - Check if SQL Server or Traverse processes are overutilized or hanging. 4. Web.config / NGINX Timeout - If using NGINX between web and app layers, review: - proxy_read_timeout - proxy_connect_timeout - These might need to be increased if backend services take longer to respond. 5. Review Logs - Look into Traverse Application Logs and Windows Event Viewer on the application server for detailed stack traces or related failures. [For SaaS Clients, kindly have the CXT Technical team to review this] 6. Workaround: - Ensure the 'Network Connectivity' of the User, and re-attempt the step that was taken, and Traverse should be able to process without any issues. NOTE: If the issue occurs momentarily, for one user, it was due to a temporary connection issue. At this point, the User can ensure their connectivity, and re-attempt the process he/she was trying, and it would be resolved

3a3c1e82-9d7a-4400-9baa-229ce30df1a3.title: How to reverse PO receipts
3a3c1e82-9d7a-4400-9baa-229ce30df1a3.content:
Problem
The customer has several open purchase orders where the products have been received but not invoiced. They are seeking assistance to determine if there is a way to clear these transactions and receipts other than issuing a debit memo.

Resolution
If the receipts have been posted but no invoices have been received, and you wish to delete the transaction, please follow these steps:

- Navigate to Purchase Order → Transactions.
- Select the orders you want to remove.
- Click Update.
- Go to the Receipts/Invoices section.
- Reverse the receipt to the appropriate fiscal period and year, then confirm the action by clicking OK.
- Delete the receipt by clicking on the line and pressing the "-" button down below.
- Click to save your changes and exit the Receipts/Invoices box.
- Finally, in the main transaction, click on the trash can to delete the transaction.

9691044c-b0bd-4b35-a5f7-6449b833051b.title: Changing the Item Type of an Item, that has a history tied to it
9691044c-b0bd-4b35-a5f7-6449b833051b.content:
Problem
Is there a way to change the Inventory Item Type of an Item, for example, from Serialized to Service? The Item that is desired to have the adjustment made has already been created and has posted history associated with it.

Resolution
Traverse doesn’t allow the item type to be changed after an item has been created and saved in the Traverse User Interface. With the Item already having posted history associated with it, the Item cannot be deleted in Traverse and recreated with the updated Item Type.



If it is determined that the specific Item ID that is currently being used needs to exist with the alternate Item Type for future processing, the current Item could be marked as obsolete, have the Item ID renamed, and a new Item created with the desired Item ID and Item Type by following the following steps.



- Remove the Item ID from any opened Sales Orders, Purchase Orders, Inventory Transactions, etc. for this item.

- Confirm with the Inventory Valuation Report and the Interactive Views that this item has no quantities or extended costs tied to it. (Something to consider: if there is qty on hand for the Item, you may want to issue and post WM Adjustments or IN Inventory Transactions to remove the qty on hand and any extended costs.)

- Under the IN Items setup screen, set the item to a status of Obsolete

- (Optional step) Use the SM Change IDs feature (System Manager->Setup and Maintenance->Change IDs) to change the now Obsolete Item ID to an alternative Item ID, so the original Item ID can be re-used when a new Item ID is created in the next step.

- Recreate the Inventory Item with the type set correctly.

- Perform any necessary IN Transactions or WM Adjustments to add Inventory to being back On Hand with the proper costs, which were removed from being on hand in step 2. (If the new Item is a Service Item type, you may want to consider performing GL Transactions to add the Cost back to the Inventory GL Account associated with the Service Item ID.)
- Add the item back to any SOs, POs, etc which was previously removed from in Step 1.

3ee68390-ab10-4661-a48b-14f2728e9699.title: How to confirm if a specific entry was cleared in a BR Statement?
3ee68390-ab10-4661-a48b-14f2728e9699.content:
Problem
How to confirm if a specific BR entry was cleared in a BR Statement?

Resolution
Steps to Verify if a Bank Reconciliation (BR) Entry Has Been Cleared in a Statement:



Step 1: Access the 'BR Register View':

-
Navigate to BR Register View under the path: Applications → Bank Reconciliation → Reconciliation → Register View. This view provides details of all the transactions and their statuses.



Step 2: Select the required 'Bank Account ID':

- Pull up the required 'Bank Account ID' from the lookups (...):



Step 3: Add the 'Date' range (optional) and click on 'Apply':

-
If needed, add the 'Date Range' and then click on 'Apply' option to show the data.

-
If the 'Date' range was left blank, Traverse will pull all the entries available.



Step 4: Add the 'Cleared' Column:

-
Open the Column Chooser within the BR Register View.

-
Select and add the 'Cleared' column to the view to display its status.



Step 5: Verify the Cleared Status:

-
Locate the specific entry in question.

-
Check if the 'Cleared' checkbox is selected for that entry.



Interpretation of the Cleared Checkbox Status:

-
If the 'Cleared' checkbox is checked  => The Transaction entry has already been cleared as part of a previous BR statement.

-
If the checkbox is unchecked => The Transaction entry is yet to be cleared and it will be available for clearing

-
