Resolution
Under Traverse Server Manager> got to Help> Get Latest Template.

Ensure the Templates files are up to date

When TRAVERSE Server Manager creates a new company, it checks the SYS database to determine the available modules for installation. It then attempts to insert these modules into the tblSmApp_Installed table. Based on the current templates, this table initially appears to be created with only a two-digit AppID column.

The list of applications is sourced from the tblSmApp table in the SYS database, where most applications have two-digit IDs, except for EDI. To resolve this issue, update the tblSmApp table by either deleting the EDI entry or modifying its AppID to "ED" using the following query:

update [SYS].[dbo].[tblSmApp] set appid = 'ED' where appid = 'EDI'

If the client is actively using the EDI module, after the new company database is created, update the AppID in the tblSmApp_Installed table back to "EDI." This is necessary because, after creation, the AppID field in this table supports up to 10 characters.

Now try to Create New Database again, and it will create without any error.

01a21a58-d4ab-4df5-a92e-a6695f98553d.title: Bank Account Setup for ACH Payments
01a21a58-d4ab-4df5-a92e-a6695f98553d.content:
Problem
How to setup Bank Account Setup for ACH Payments

Resolution
- Navigate to Bank Reconciliation>Setup & Maintenance>Bank Accounts
- Select the Bank Account ID that you are setting up the ACH for from the list
- Select the ACH tab
- Choose the information that is included in the ACH file you send to the bank (the bank can provide information about which selection is appropriate)
- Select the Default AP File Format (ADV, CCD, PPD, CCDO, etc.). (You will need to get information from your bank regarding which file format to use. If your bank requires a format that is not included in the defaults, you will need to get a file format configured for your particular needs.)
- If your bank does not want the Offset/Balancing record included, then check the box, "Exclude Batch Offset (Balancing) Record." If they do want the Offset/Balancing record included, check the box.

- Enter the Default File Name/prefix (? will add the Application ID to the file name, * will add the date and time to the file name). This will set the file name for the ACH file that will be created.

- Select the Default Folder to save the ACH files to
- The Sample File field will show an example of the file path and filename for new ACH files
- Enter a security code if your bank expects a security code at the beginning of the ACH file
- If your bank expects a security code, enter the required length of the security code in the Pad Security Code To A Length Of field.
- Save the Bank Account record.

eb8f8c53-7a85-4b30-9faf-ef71e5ceaf33.title: How to Create A New Payroll Year in Traverse
eb8f8c53-7a85-4b30-9faf-ef71e5ceaf33.content:
Problem
How to create the new payroll year in the Traverse application.

Resolution
To create the new payroll year, please follow these steps:

- Navigate to System Manager → Administration → Payroll Year.
- In the "Year" field - put in the year you wish to create
- "From Year" - Select the previous year (Ex- if you are creating a year 2026, the previous year is 2025).

- Click 'OK' to complete the process.

a1c20be6-2a4f-415d-a062-afaba2e24b69.title: How to create a Positive Pay File
a1c20be6-2a4f-415d-a062-afaba2e24b69.content:
Problem
How to create a Positive Pay File

Resolution
Use the Create Positive Pay File function on the Pay Invoices menu to generate an ASCII file to transmit to your bank for check payment authorization.

NOTE: You must print checks prior to running the Create Positive Pay File function. The check number is required to display the payments that will be output into the file.

To use the Create Positive Pay File function, follow these steps:
1. Select Create Positive Pay File from the Accounts Payable> Pay Invoices menu.

2. The Create Positive Pay File screen appears.

3. Select the Bank Account ID for which you will be creating the positive pay file. You must have an AP Positive Pay ID selected in the Bank Account setup to be able to output your positive pay file.

4. The File Name of the file you set up in the Positive Pay Export Definition setup in System Manager, is displayed, if set up. Accept the default or change the path and file name if you want a new file name. Click the Browse button, to browse to the path for which you want the file output. You must enter a file name after the path to generate a new file.

5. The Checks that have been printed for the bank selected will be displayed in the detail area.
The default display is a summary display which has the Check Date, Amount, and Transmit Date columns. You may sort any of these columns by clicking on the column heading once to sort ascending and again to sort descending.

6. The Select check box is marked, by default, for all checks that have not had the positive pay file generated. Accept the selections or clear the checks you do not wish to include in the positive pay file.

7. Select the type of checks you want to Show, from the combo box selections:
•New will display any checks that have not had the positive pay file created for them yet
•Sent will display any checks that have had the positive pay file created for them (the Select box was checked and the file was created).

8. When the Create button is clicked to output the file you will be prompted to overwrite the file if it exists. If you select No, you will be returned to the screen to change the file name in the File Name field.
If you have already output any of the checks selected, you will get a message stating that some of the checks have already been output, do you want to continue and output them again.

9. Once the file has been output, you can navigate to the saved file to upload it to your bank.

eab7a9b4-b588-429a-b188-6dda08a7140a.title: How to resolve the error: "50000 : The post has been aborted." while posting AP Transaction?
eab7a9b4-b588-429a-b188-6dda08a7140a.content:
Problem
The Client is getting the below error when trying to post the AP Transactions:



===================================
50000 : The post has been aborted. Please review and correct the listed transactions before posting again. Errors were detected in the following transactions: 00000793. : Procedure{dbo.trav_ApTransPost_Prepare_proc} (.Net SqlClient Data Provider)
------------------------------
For help, click: http://go.microsoft.com/fwlink?ProdName=Microsoft%20SQL%20Server&ProdVer=14.00.3223&EvtSrc=MSSQLServer&EvtID=50000&LinkId=20476

------------------------------
Server Name: DGA1APP58OSACS\TRAV112
Error Number: 50000
Severity: 16
State: 1
Procedure: dbo.trav_RaiseError_proc
Line Number: 17

------------------------------
Program Location:

at TRAVERSE.Client.ProcessControlBase.OnProcessCompleted()
at TRAVERSE.Client.AccountsPayable.TransactionPostControl.OnProcessCompleted()

Resolution
This error occurs when Traverse identifies a transaction as problematic and blacklists it, preventing it from being posted. The system automatically marks such transactions as un-processable, likely due to inconsistencies, missing data, or system validation rules.

To successfully post the transaction, users need to carefully review and take corrective actions as outlined below.



Resolution:

i. Identify the Transaction Causing the Error:

-
-
When the error message appears, note the Transaction Number mentioned. [In the above sample error message, let's consider the example: 00000793]

-
Navigate to the corresponding Transaction record within Traverse under the path: Applications -> Accounts Payable -> Transactions-> Transactions

-
Locate the affected entry, that is the Transaction number '00000793'

-
Open the transaction details and carefully examine all relevant fields, including amounts, accounts, dates, and other required information.



ii. A. Review and Correct Any Visible Issues:

-
-
Compare the transaction against similar successfully posted transactions to identify any discrepancies.

-
Ensure that all required fields are properly filled and formatted.

-
If errors or missing data are identified, make the necessary updates and save the Transaction. Proceed with posting the same.



ii. B. If No Visible Issues Are Found:

-
-
In cases where no apparent discrepancies exist, Traverse may still be blocking the transaction due to system constraints.

-
In such situations, the most effective approach is to delete the existing transaction and create a new one [either Invoice or Debit Memo].

-
When recreating the Transaction, ensure that all details match the original entry to maintain accuracy.

-
Save the new transaction and proceed with posting it.



iii. Reattempt the Posting Process

-
After recreating the transaction, initiate the posting process once more, under the path: Applications -> Accounts Payable -> transaction Journals -> Post Transactions [Since the system no longer recognizes the newly created entry as blacklisted, Traverse should allow the transaction to be processed without errors.]

cfc7ee59-6b3e-4b25-bfca-fa784517657c.title: How to Update ACH File to Populate Vendor-Specific Routing Number
cfc7ee59-6b3e-4b25-bfca-fa784517657c.content:
Problem
The customer is experiencing an issue where the vendor-specific routing number is not populating in the appropriate field in the ACH file. Instead, the company routing number is being populated. They want to resolve this issue so that the system correctly pulls the vendor’s routing number instead of the company’s routing number when generating the ACH file.

Resolution
To resolve the issue where the vendor-specific routing number is not populating correctly in the ACH file, follow these detailed steps:

-
Navigate to System Manager:
First, open the System Manager in your application and proceed to the Company Setup section.

-
Access Export Layout Definition:
Under the Company Setup, locate and click on Export Layout Definition. This is where the various file formats and layout configurations are managed.

-
Identify the Relevant Layout ID:
Find the Layout ID that is being used for the ACH file export. This layout defines how the ACH file is structured and which data fields are populated.

-
Expand the 3rd Sequence:
Once you’ve located the correct layout ID, expand the 3rd sequence, which is labeled CCD Entry Detail (Credit).

-
Modify Sequence 3 Field:
In the expanded view of the 3rd sequence, look for Sequence 3. Here, you will find a field that currently has the value 'OriginatingDFIRoutingNumber', which is the company’s routing number.
To fix the issue, change the value of this field to 'ReceivingDFIRoutingNumber', which will ensure the system populates the vendor-specific routing number instead of the company's routing number.

By making this change, the ACH file will now correctly display the vendor’s routing number in the respective field, resolving the issue the customer is facing.

b991ed16-c03f-4354-a8f7-b8c976dff9c8.title: How can I unblock all the DLL files in bulk?
b991ed16-c03f-4354-a8f7-b8c976dff9c8.content:
Problem
- The client would like to determine whether the large number of .dll files in a specified directory are blocked or unblocked.

- The client would like to know how to unblock a large number of DLL files in bulk, without having to unblock each one individually by navigating to Properties -> Unblock.

Resolution
- This can be done by running the following command in the PowerShell of the workstation.

Get-ChildItem "C:\Path\To\Your\Folder" -Recurse -Filter *.dll | ForEach-Object {
$file = $_
$stream = Get-Item $file.FullName -Stream Zone.Identifier -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if ($stream) {
[PSCustomObject]@{
FileName    = $file.FullName
IsBlocked   = $true
}
} else {
[PSCustomObject]@{
FileName    = $file.FullName
IsBlocked   = $false
}
}
}

Breakdown:

-
Get-ChildItem "C:\Path\To\Your\Folder" -Recurse -Filter *.dll:

-
This command retrieves all .dll files in the specified directory (C:\Path\To\Your\Folder) and all of its subdirectories (-Recurse).

-
ForEach-Object:

-
This cmdlet processes each file ($_) found in the previous step.

-
$file = $_:

-
The current file object is assigned to the $file variable for easier reference.

-
$stream = Get-Item $file.FullName -Stream Zone.Identifier -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue:

-
This command attempts to get the "Zone.Identifier" alternate data stream associated with the file, which is where Windows stores information about the file's origin (such as whether it was downloaded from the internet).

-
If the file has this stream (meaning it was likely downloaded), it is marked as potentially "blocked."

-
The -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue ensures no error is displayed if the stream is not found (i.e., the file is not blocked).

-
if ($stream):

-
If the "Zone.Identifier" stream exists, the file is considered "blocked."

-
[PSCustomObject]@{ ... }:

-
For each file, the script creates a custom PowerShell object with two properties:

-
FileName (the full path to the file),

-
IsBlocked (a boolean value indicating whether the file is blocked or not).

-
Output:

-
For each .dll file, the script will output an object with the file name and whether it is blocked ($true) or not ($false).

The output would be as shown below:





2.

To unblock .dll files in bulk (or any other files) that have been marked as blocked due to being downloaded from the internet, you can use the Unblock-File cmdlet in PowerShell.

Get-ChildItem "C:\Path\To\Your\Folder" -Recurse -Filter *.dll | ForEach-Object {
# Unblock the file if it is blocked
Unblock-File -Path $_.FullName
Write-Host "Unblocked: $($_.FullName)"
}



Explanation:

-
Get-ChildItem "C:\Path\To\Your\Folder" -Recurse -Filter *.dll:

-
This command searches for all .dll files in the specified folder (C:\Path\To\Your\Folder) and all its subdirectories (-Recurse).

-
ForEach-Object:

-
This processes each .dll file found in the previous step.

-
Unblock-File -Path $_.FullName:

-
The Unblock-File cmdlet is used to remove the "Zone.Identifier" alternate data stream (the block) from each file, allowing it to be used without being flagged as potentially unsafe by Windows.

-
Write-Host "Unblocked: $($_.FullName)":

-
This line will print a message to the console indicating which file has been unblocked.

Sample Output:



Unblocked: C:\Path\To\Your\Folder\subfolder1\example1.dll
Unblocked: C:\Path\To\Your\Folder\subfolder2\example2.dll
Unblocked: C:\Path\To\Your\Folder\example3.dll
Unblocked: C:\Path\To\Your\Folder\subfolder3\example4.dll
Unblocked: C:\Path\To\Your\Folder\subfolder4\example5.dll

06664a54-1f07-43bb-8855-009502ae9a1d.title: How to reprint the AP Check that was already posted in Traverse 11.2?
06664a54-1f07-43bb-8855-009502ae9a1d.content:
Problem
How to reprint the AP Check that was already posted in Traverse 11.2?

Resolution
When the Client has enabled the 'Document Archive' business rule for a specific application, previously printed documents can be retrieved from the SM Manage Documents function. For this functionality to work, users must ensure that document archiving is properly configured within Business Rules.



Pre-requisites for reprinting the AP Checks, even if it was posted:

To enable document archiving for an application, follow these steps:

i. Enable the 'Document Archive' option in the Business Rules function under the path: Applications -> System Manager -> Company Setup -> Business Rules:



ii. Configure the Archive business rules for the required application.

-
-
In this case, document archiving needs to be enabled for Accounts Payable.



Filtering Data for Document Management:

Before retrieving documents, users can apply filters to refine the selection:

-
Utilize the Data Filter to specify filtering criteria and narrow down the results. We can add the required filters and click on 'Apply Filters' to observe the resultant

- If no filters are applied, the system will display all available archived documents (Including the AP Checks in Accounts Payable)



Steps to Print Archived Check (Documents):

i. Locate the AP Check (document) that needs to be printed. Click the ellipsis (. . .) button in the Document column next to the selected document.

ii. The system will open the document using the default PDF viewer on the user's computer. Use the PDF viewer’s print function to print the document as required.

486d2b7a-3688-452a-ac40-09a32774f575.title: How to Export Documents from Traverse to Local PC (for SaaS customers)
486d2b7a-3688-452a-ac40-09a32774f575.content:
Problem
How to Export Documents from Traverse to Local PC (for SaaS customers) to be able to save reports exported from Traverse.

Resolution
Method 1: RemoteApp (Redirected Drive)

1. When exporting a document in SaaS application you will need to save the document to your PC. When prompted for the location to save/export the document you will need to expand “This PC” then select a location on your local PC (indicated by “C on YOUR-PC-NAME” - Y0UR-PC NAME being the actual name of your computer).

Do not save files in the “This PC -> Documents” location as this is located on the Cloud server.

e85c6070-dbb6-49ea-a8b6-5a80a0932aab.title: Resolving GL Description Issues When Changing Vendor ID in AP Transactions
e85c6070-dbb6-49ea-a8b6-5a80a0932aab.content:
Problem
Hi, I have an entry that is showing up as voided, but just for the bank account ID, but I did not void this. Also, the GL desc says this is for another vendor that was entered. Can you please help? See screenshots below:

Resolution
Clarification on Void Bank ID & Payment Status:

A Void Bank ID alone does not confirm that a payment has been voided. For a payment to be officially considered voided, it must:

-
Be explicitly flagged as voided in the system.

-
Have a recorded void date.

Root Cause:

It appears that the user initially selected the wrong Vendor ID in the AP transaction and added a line item. Since the GL description defaults to the vendor name, updating the Vendor ID later did not override the GL description of the existing line item.

Prevention & Resolution:

To avoid this issue in the future, users should carefully review the GL description after changing the Vendor ID. If needed, they can manually update the description in the GL Edit Transaction screen.

If the journal entry has already been posted to the master, the development team can provide a script to correct it; however, this would be considered a billable engagement.

4417e4ba-2393-4771-a98a-94974440b7de.title: Getting the error message: "System Error 2: The System cannot find the file specified" while updating EPTR forms
4417e4ba-2393-4771-a98a-94974440b7de.content:
Problem
While updating the EPTR forms, the Users are getting the following error message:
"System Error 2: The System cannot find the file specified"

Resolution
This issue can be resolved by replacing the Configuration file in the Aatrix folder, where the updates are getting downloaded.

2. Drop the Install.ini file in the C:\Program Files (x86)\Aatrix directory (To be specific, the place where Aatrix is installed

3. After replacing the existing Configuration file with the text file we just created, open that file and insert the following text:
AppSubDir=Aatrix Software\Aatrix Forms\Open Systems, Inc\

4. Save the file.

5. Now re-run the EPTR Report under Payroll -> Quarter/Year-End Reports > Enhanced Payroll Tax Reports. Then select ‘Automatic Update.’

6. Now, the User will be able to complete the update process without any issues.

c8875567-b4a4-40a5-8f50-dade87bc76b9.title: How to update the Price for a Sales Order that was 'Verified' with a Net Due of '0.00'?
c8875567-b4a4-40a5-8f50-dade87bc76b9.content:
Problem
How to update the Price for a Sales Order that was 'Verified' with a Net Due of '0.00'?



The Sales Journal will be appearing as follows:

Resolution
There might be a few instances, where the User might have added the Line Item and would be shipping the same, without updating the 'Unit Price' field, as a result of which the 'Net Due' might be zero.



At that point, the User will be having the status of the Sales Order as 'Verified', and the Net Due is 0.00, and Traverse will not allow the User to post that Transaction as well.



In Traverse, even if a Sales Order has already been marked as 'Verified' with a Net Due of zero dollars, the system allows users to update the 'Unit Price' for the line items within that order. When the Unit Price is modified, the system automatically recalculates and updates the 'Net Due' accordingly, ensuring that the adjustments are reflected accurately.



To update the Unit Price for a verified Sales Order, kindly follow the below steps:

i. Open the verified Sales Order where the Net Due is currently zero.



ii. Click on the 'Update' icon and edit the 'Unit Price' field for the respective line item(s) as required.



iii. Click on the 'Save' icon to save the changes to the Sales Order and we can observe that the updated price is available in the 'Net Due' field:



iv. We can review the 'Sales Journal' now to observe the Invoice totals:



v. Proceed with posting the updated order, to ensure the Amount is posted in place:



Once the order is posted, the updated total amount will be accurately reflected in the 'Accounts Receivable', ensuring that all financial records are maintained correctly.

02f0b5bd-3981-44c0-a7f8-17ecde1e77b2.title: How to run Accounts Receivables Periodic Maintenace in Traverse
02f0b5bd-3981-44c0-a7f8-17ecde1e77b2.content:
Problem
The client wants to clear old transactions in accounts receivable so that the statements are not long with transactions from several years ago

Resolution
Performing Periodic Maintenance:





-
Backup & Print Reports: Print all statements and reports and ensure a valid data backup before proceeding.

-
Enable Maintenance Options: Check the "Do the following" box.

-
Perform General Periodic Processing (if applicable):

-
Select the "Perform General Periodic Process" checkbox to age customers, update credit status, apply finance charges, compare balances, synchronize customer balances with outstanding invoices, and clear sales reps' period-to-date totals.

-
If left unchecked, only records from invoice history and recurring entry tables will be purged.

-
Roll Balance Forward (for Multicurrency Users):

-
Select the "Roll Balance Forward Balances" checkbox to advance the aging period for balance forward customers and retain a summary invoice for each aging period.

-
If left unchecked, Current Due amounts will not roll to the next period.

-
Delete Paid Invoices (if applicable):

-
Check "Delete Paid Invoices With Invoice Date Before" to remove paid invoices.

-
Enter the last invoice date to retain in the adjacent field.

-
Important: Before selecting this option, you must first run the "Perform the following functions" process and ensure the invoices are marked as paid.

-
Clear Customer High Balance (if applicable):

-
Check this box only when performing year-end maintenance.

-
Clear Sales Rep YTD Totals (if applicable):

-
Select this option to reset sales reps' year-to-date totals during year-end maintenance.

-
Add Comments (if needed): Enter any relevant notes in the Comments field.

-
Initiate Process: Click the "OK" button to proceed.

283005a3-fff9-4a14-a671-c5dea9509cae.title: How to enter the 'Job Piece Work' in Individual Tracking System (ITS)?
283005a3-fff9-4a14-a671-c5dea9509cae.content:
Problem
How to enter the 'Job Piece Work' in ITS?

Resolution
The Piece Work Entry screen in the Traverse Individual Tracking System (ITS) is used to record the number of pieces processed by individuals or the time worked. It is accessible from the Daily Work menu in the ITS module under the Piecework option.



I. Access the IT Piece Work screen:

Navigate to the IT Piece Work screen under the path: Applications -> Individual Tracking -> Daily Work -> Piece Work



II. Selecting an Individual:

On the Piece Work Entry screen, choose the individual whose time or piece work you want to enter.



III. Setting Default Values:

-
Batch ID: Select a default batch ID, which will apply when entering piece work data.

-
Entry Date: Defaults to the current system date but can be changed within a permitted range (controlled by business rules).

-
Override Date Range: If enabled in Business rules, clicking the Override Date Range button allows modifying the range of valid entry dates.

-
Filter Date: Displays only the piece work entries for the selected individual on the specified date. To see all dates, clear the filter.

-
'View Posted' Checkbox: Checking this box displays posted entries along with unposted ones.

-
'Filter by Default Batch' Checkbox: If enabled, it restricts displayed entries to those with the selected batch ID.



IV. Entering Piece Work Data:

Adding a New Entry:

-
Click New Entry at the top or Plus (+) Button at the bottom.

-
Fill in the following details:

-
Work Date: Defaults to the selected entry date but can be changed.

-
Start Time & End Time: If enabled in business rules, entering these values auto-calculates Elapsed Time.

-
Elapsed Time: If Start & End Time fields are not enabled, manually enter the total hours worked.

-
Auto Lunch: If enabled in business rules, a checkbox allows auto-deduction of lunch break time.

-
Hours: This is a read-only field calculated based on entered time.

-
Pieces: Enter the number of pieces processed.

-
Job: Specify the task performed.

-
Batch ID: Defaults from the initial selection but can be modified.

-
Funding Source, Service, and Program: Can be adjusted from default values.

-
Posted Checkbox: Indicates whether the entry is posted.

-
Percentage of Standard (Pct of Standard): Auto-calculated based on pieces entered. If the value exceeds 100%, it must be allowed in business rules to proceed.

-
Adjustments: Enter an adjustment amount if applicable (requires prior configuration in the job/task entry screen).

-
Notes: Add relevant comments, if applicable.

-
Voided Checkbox: Can be used to invalidate a posted entry. Unposted entries can be deleted instead.



v. Navigating Entry Options in the Piece Work Module

Once an entry has been successfully completed, the User may need to either add another entry for the same Employee or proceed to recording an entry for a different Employee. To facilitate this process, the following options are available:

i. New Entry Button:

-
This option allows the User to create an additional Piece Work Entry for the same Employee without having to reselect the individual.

-
It is particularly useful when multiple entries need to be recorded for a single Employee within the same session.



ii. New Individual Button:

-
This option enables the User to select a different Employee and continue with the Piece Work Entry process.

-
It is helpful when moving on to a new Employee without affecting the previously recorded data.



iii. Reset Button: If we need to delete the entries in the entire screen and wish to start over from the beginning, we need to use the 'Reset' button available.

c661fd67-e0fc-47d2-8630-c6909193005f.title: Enquiry about Global Location Number
c661fd67-e0fc-47d2-8630-c6909193005f.content:
Problem
What is the Global Location Number in the Setup and Maintenance> Customer>Ship-To? If this field is informational, could we use it for customer notes?

Resolution
The Global Location Number (GLN) provides flexibility for every level of location identification. As a result, you will be able to track anything moving throughout the supply chain and uniquely identify the locations involved in its business transactions.

A Global Location Number (GLN) is a 13 digit number that acts as a key for identifying the location, whether physical or digital, and the function or entity of a company across the supply chain. There may also be space limitations.

It isn't recommended to repurpose the field for other uses.  Even if it ends up working now, you run the risk of TRAVERSE doing something else with that field later or even getting rid of it entirely.

An alternative to repurposing the GLN Field as a customer notes field would be to use the "Attachments" in AR Customers to add Notes to Customer records that way.

The downfall is, users would need to click the attachment button to know whether or not there is a note.

bb596ab6-d90b-4cc8-bd3a-122f5313cadc.title: How to resolve the 'Invalid Formula' error while calculating the Payroll Checks?
bb596ab6-d90b-4cc8-bd3a-122f5313cadc.content:
Problem
How to resolve the 'Invalid Formula' error while calculating the Payroll Checks?



Invalid formula (TRAVERSE.Client.ReportViewer)
------------------------------
Program Location:

at TRAVERSE.Client.ProcessControlBase.OnProcessCompleted()
at TRAVERSE.Client.Payroll.CalcCheckControl.OnProcessCompleted()

Value cannot be null.
Parameter name: name (mscorlib)
------------------------------
Program Location:

at System.Type.GetMethod(String name, BindingFlags bindingAttr)
at TRAVERSE.Core.MethodCaller.GetMethod(Type objectType, String method, Object[] parameters)
at TRAVERSE.Core.MethodCaller.CallMethodIfImplemented(Object obj, String method, Object[] parameters)
at TRAVERSE.Business.PayrollTax.Formula.ExecFormula(String name)

Resolution
When a client adds new employees to the system and the 'Formula' field is not configured in the 'Deductions' and 'Employer Costs' screens, the user may encounter an error. This occurs because the required setup for deductions or employer costs is incomplete or incorrectly configured.



In order to resolve this error, we would need to review the Employee setup in the PA Employee Information screen under the path: Applications -> Payroll -> Setup and Maintenance -> Employee Information:



I. Navigate to the 'Deductions' Tab and confirm that the appropriate 'Code' for each Pay Period (1-5) has been set up. Please find the purpose of each code enlisted as follows:

1. Code 'N' – No Deduction for This Pay Period:

-
Purpose: This code is used when there is no deduction required for the employee in a specific pay period. This could apply when there is a situation like a temporary exemption, a special allowance, or a case where the deduction is suspended for that pay period.

-
Usage: When this code is selected, the system will skip any deduction processing for the employee during that specific pay period.

2. Code 'Y' – Deduct a Fixed Dollar Amount:

-
Purpose: This code is used when the deduction is a fixed, predefined dollar amount for a given pay period.

-
Usage: The user enters a specific dollar amount in the ‘Amount’ field, and the system will deduct that exact amount from the employee's pay. This type of deduction is commonly used for fixed contributions, such as a set loan repayment, insurance premium, or retirement fund contribution.

3. Code 'P' – Deduct a Percentage of Pay:

-
Purpose: This code indicates that the deduction is based on a percentage of the employee’s pay. The percentage value is specified in the ‘Amount’ field, and this percentage will be applied to the employee’s gross pay for the pay period.

-
Usage: When selected, the system will calculate the deduction as a percentage of the employee's pay. For example, if the deduction is 5%, the system will deduct 5% of the employee's total pay for that pay period.

4. Code 'H' – Deduct per Hour Worked:

-
Purpose: This code is used when the deduction is calculated based on the number of hours worked by the employee in the pay period. The amount in the ‘Amount’ field specifies the deduction per hour worked.

-
Usage: This code is often used for hourly employees or situations where the deduction is tied to the hours worked (e.g., union dues or specific work-related fees). For salaried employees, this code requires a time ticket to be entered so that the system can calculate the hours worked and apply the deduction accordingly.

5. Code 'D' – Deduct until Balance Reaches Zero (Declining Balance):

-
Purpose: This code is used for deductions that need to continue until a specified balance is reduced to zero. The ‘Amount’ field specifies the amount to be deducted each pay period. This type of deduction is typically used when the total amount to be deducted is fixed, but the employee’s balance (e.g., a loan or advance) decreases over time.

-
Usage: Each pay period, the system will deduct the specified amount from the employee's balance. The system will continue the deduction until the remaining balance reaches zero, at which point the deductions stop.

6. Code 'E' – Deduct Percentage until Balance Reaches Zero (Declining Balance by Percentage):

-
Purpose: Similar to Code D, this code is used for deductions that continue until a specified balance is reduced to zero, but the deduction is based on a percentage instead of a fixed amount.

-
Usage: The system calculates the deduction as a percentage of the balance and continues deducting this percentage until the balance is fully reduced to zero. This is commonly used for loans or debts where the repayment is structured as a percentage of the remaining balance.

7. Code 'F' – Formula-Based Deduction:

-
Purpose: This code is used when the deduction is calculated using a specific formula. The formula ID and any associated override factors are defined under the Formula button, and the system uses the formula to compute the deduction amount for each pay period.

-
Usage: The ‘Amount’ field should be set to 0.00 when this code is selected because the formula itself will calculate the deduction. Formula-based deductions are useful for complex calculations that depend on multiple variables, such as tax withholdings, benefits contributions, or custom deduction schemes.

8. Code 'G' – Formula-Based Deduction with Declining Balance:

-
Purpose: This code combines formula-based deductions with a declining balance. The system calculates the deduction using a formula (as in Code F) and subtracts the deduction from a balance that decreases over time.

-
Usage: Similar to Code D, this code applies to scenarios where the employee’s balance decreases with each deduction. However, instead of a fixed amount or percentage, the deduction is based on a formula, and the system continues deducting until the balance reaches zero.

NOTE: If we use code F or G for a formula-based deduction, the user must ensure that the correct Formula ID is selected and any necessary Override factors are specified. The Formula button provides access to the interface where these details can be entered.



II. Navigate to the 'Employer Costs' Tab and confirm that the appropriate 'Code' for each Pay Period (1-5) has been set up. Please find the purpose of each code enlisted as follows:

1. Code 'N' – No Employer Cost for This Pay Period:

-
Purpose: This code is used when there is no employer cost to be applied for the employee in a particular pay period. This might occur when the employee is temporarily exempt from employer costs, or there is no cost associated with their pay for that period.

-
Usage: When this code is selected, the system will not apply any employer costs for the employee in the specified pay period, meaning no deductions or contributions will be made.

2. Code 'Y' – Pay a Fixed Dollar Amount:

-
Purpose: This code indicates that the employer will pay a fixed dollar amount for the employee’s employer cost in the given pay period.

-
Usage: The dollar amount to be paid is specified in the Amount field, and the system will deduct the same fixed amount from the employer’s cost budget for each applicable pay period. For example, this might apply to fixed employer contributions to a retirement plan or a fixed premium for employee health insurance.

3. Code 'P' – Pay a Percentage of Pay:

-
Purpose: This code is used when the employer cost is based on a percentage of the employee’s pay for the pay period.

-
Usage: The percentage is specified in the Amount field, and the system will calculate the employer's cost as a percentage of the employee's total pay for that period. For example, this could be used to calculate a pension contribution or insurance premium that is a percentage of the employee’s earnings.

4. Code 'H' – Pay Per Hour Worked:

-
Purpose: This code is used when the employer cost is calculated based on the number of hours the employee works during the pay period.

-
Usage: The employer’s cost is determined by the number of hours worked, with the amount to be paid per hour specified in the Amount field. This is commonly used for hourly workers or for situations where employer contributions (such as benefits or allowances) are based on hours worked. If this code is used for salaried employees, a time ticket must be entered to allow the system to properly calculate the hours worked and apply the correct employer cost.

5. Code 'D' – Pay Amount Until Balance Reaches Zero (Declining Balance):

-
Purpose: This code is used when the employer cost is a fixed dollar amount, but the cost needs to be deducted until a specified balance is reduced to zero.

-
Usage: The amount to be paid is specified in the Amount field, and the system will subtract the employer cost from the remaining balance. The deduction will continue until the balance reaches zero, which is useful for situations like paying off a loan or a debt owed by the employer on behalf of the employee. This is typically used when the employer has an outstanding balance or obligation that needs to be reduced over time.

6. Code 'E' – Pay Percentage Until Balance Reaches Zero (Declining Balance by Percent):

-
Purpose: This code is similar to Code D, but instead of a fixed dollar amount, the employer cost is based on a percentage of the remaining balance.

-
Usage: The percentage to be paid is specified in the Amount field, and the system will deduct the employer cost as a percentage of the remaining balance until the balance is fully reduced to zero. This is typically used for employer contributions to a debt or balance that is being paid down over time, such as a loan or a benefit program with a declining balance.

7. Code 'F' – Calculate Employer Cost Using a Formula:

-
Purpose: This code is used when the employer cost is calculated using a specific formula rather than a fixed amount or percentage.

-
Usage: When Code F is selected, the value in the Amount field should be set to 0.00, as the formula will compute the employer cost. The formula is defined using a Formula ID, and any necessary override factors can be entered through the Formula button. Formula-based calculations are used for more complex employer cost scenarios, such as contributions based on varying factors like employee eligibility, salary bands, or other dynamic data.

8. Code 'G' – Calculate Employer Cost Using a Formula and Declining Balance:

-
Purpose: This code combines formula-based employer cost calculation (as in Code F) with a declining balance feature.

-
Usage: Similar to Code D, the employer cost is calculated using a formula, and the resulting cost is subtracted from a balance. The system continues to pay the employer cost until the balance is reduced to zero. This is useful in scenarios where the employer has a specific obligation to pay off a balance over time (e.g., a loan or contribution), and the payment amount is determined by a formula rather than a fixed amount or percentage.

NOTE: When using Codes F or G, the employer cost is not determined by a simple dollar amount or percentage. Instead, the amount is calculated dynamically based on a predefined formula, which can take into account multiple variables, such as the employee’s salary, benefits eligibility, or other factors. Here, the user must ensure that the correct Formula ID is selected, and any necessary Override factors are specified. The Formula button provides access to the interface where these details can be entered.



CHECK POINTS:

i Formula Not Added for Code 'F':

If the client uses Code F to indicate a formula-based deduction but fails to add the corresponding formula under the Formula button, the system will trigger the mentioned error.

Resolution: Kindly update the required 'Formula ID' under the Formula screen that appears upon clicking on the 'Formula' icon as shown below:



ii. Incorrect Code Configuration:

If the client mistakenly configures the deduction with Code F (intended for a formula-based deduction) instead of Code P (for percentage-based deductions), the system will also throw an error. Ensure the correct code is selected based on the deduction method intended.

Resolution: Kindly update the required 'Code' for the appropriate Column as required as shown below [The same applies to the 'Deductions' Tab as well]:

2fa444aa-9805-480e-8e79-5711c603c88c.title: How to set up a new Task in the Individual Tracking System (ITS)?
2fa444aa-9805-480e-8e79-5711c603c88c.content:
Problem
How to set up a new Task in the Individual Tracking System (ITS)?

Resolution
The IT Tasks screen records the tasks that are performed by the individuals at the job site are set up. The task screen is where the task that the individual will be performing at the job site and that will be used during the daily work section of the individual tracking system module to track hours for the individual or entered. It could also include things like sick leave and vacation so that they can be calculated into the individual's paycheck.



In order to set up a new Task, the User would need to follow the below steps:

i. Navigate to the IT Tasks screen under the path: Applications -> Individual Tracking -> Setup and Maintenance -> Tasks:



ii. Click on the 'New' icon () to create a new Task record



iii. Enter a Task ID and Description.

-
Task ID: Unique identifier for the task.

-
Description: A brief explanation of the task.



iv. Enable applicable 'Checkbox(es)':

- Counts Towards Attendance: If enabled, the recorded time for this task will be included in attendance reports.
-
Tax Subsidy: Enable if the task qualifies for a tax subsidy.

-
Exclude Task from Overtime: Enable to ensure this task is not considered for overtime calculations.

-
Exclude from Auto Lunch: Enable if the task should be excluded from automatic lunch deductions.



v. Fill out the optional details as per the requirement:

- Attendance Report Code: If applicable, enter a custom code to be used in attendance reports.
-
Wage Category: Assign a wage category to determine the hourly wage for this task.

-
Funding Source ID & Service ID: If the task is associated with a funding source or service, provide the relevant details.



vi. Configure the wage details in the 'Rate List' section:

- Start Date: Define the task’s effective start date (mandatory).
-
End Date: Define an end date if applicable (optional).

-
Prevailing Wage: If provided, this wage will override the wage category.

-
Standard Pieces: Enter the number of standard pieces completed per hour to enable automatic calculation of the piece rate.



NOTE: Even if the User would like to configure a 'Task' that should not be included in any Wage Calculation, it is necessary for the User to specify the 'Start Date' for that Task

f47475c7-840f-4f7b-8352-411a5006838b.title: How to reverse the GL Transactions written to a wrong Year
f47475c7-840f-4f7b-8352-411a5006838b.content:
Problem
How to reverse the GL Transactions written to the wrong Year?
[For instance, let the entries been written to the Year 2023 by mistake, instead of the Year 2022. While the Date of the entries are in 2022, but the Fiscal Year is 2023, instead of 2022]

Resolution
The entries that have been written into 2023 need to be reversed and need to be re-written to the right Year 2022.

1. With the Fiscal Year set as 2023, go to the GL Edit Transactions screen under the Path: Applications -> General Ledger -> Transactions -> Edit Transactions: And click on 'Apply Filter', to see the entries made to the wrong Fiscal Year (2023). [If needed, apply necessary Filters to segregate the wrong entries. For example, here, the Source has been used as a Filter to filter out the Manual entries made in the GL Transactions screen].

2. Review all the entries and ensure that there are only the wrong entries present. Then, rearrange the Columns such that it matches the Column Headers of the GL Transactions screen. Select all the entries (using the 'Shift' key and selecting) and copy the same.

3. Change the Fiscal year to 2022 (as desired).

4. Close and re-open the GL Transactions screen under the Path: Applications -> General Ledger -> Transactions -> Transactions. Paste the copied entries in the GL Transactions screen and ensure they are entered on the right Year (2022) this time and save it. Click on 'Write' to write the entries to the Journal of the Year 2022. So now, the entries has been entered into the right Year now.

5. This can be now observed in the GL Edit Transactions screen of the Year 2022.

6. Now again change the Fiscal Year back to 2023.

7. Close and re-open the GL Edit Transactions screen. In order to counter the entries that were mistakenly written into the Year 2023, select all the entries and then click on the Reverse' icon above the Column header to create the reversing entries on the GL Transactions screen.

8. Now re-open the GL Transactions screen and we can observe the reversing entries present here. Write the reversing entries to the Journal of 2023 by using the 'Write' icon.

9. We can observe that the totals of Credit and Debit would have offset due to the reversing entries. Now we can go to the GL Post to Master and post these entries to clear them off.

[NOTE: Every time when the Fiscal Year is changed, make sure to close and reopen the window to ensure that it sticks to the updated Year]

6ab0b90e-3b56-4079-9e6e-5ebfedaa02d5.title: How to Adjust a field position in Traverse reports.
6ab0b90e-3b56-4079-9e6e-5ebfedaa02d5.content:
Problem
When we try to print any reports like invoices, checks, orders etc. from Traverse and sometimes we feel like the fields are misaligned. Let's take an example of purchase order print order.

Resolution
Open Traverse Design Studio. Click on Form Layout and select PO Purchase Order.

Click on "Open" to make sure there isn't any .repx file for "print order". If you find and .repx file for the layout you are in, select the file and open it.

Once we open the file, select he field that you want to move/adjust. In our case we have to move the "Item Description" field upward so that it matches the same line as that of Units and Entry no.

Click on the Description field and click " Up-arrow button" to move the field upward, similarly, use other arrow keys to move the field in respective directions. Each click will move the field by on grid. Also, we can use cursor to click and drag the field to the required location.

If there's a need where we want to move a field less than a "grid" size, hold "ctrl" and click the arrow button.

Hence, we can adjust the fields in the Design studio.

Then Click "Save" at the top, and this form would save as .repx file.

eee4ddf9-b89b-4a27-925a-704fe2d28323.title: How to void a Cash receipt in Accounts Receivable?
eee4ddf9-b89b-4a27-925a-704fe2d28323.content:
Problem
How to void a Cash receipt in Accounts Receivable?

Resolution
In order to void a Cash Receipt, a negative Cash Receipt must be created the same Invoice number as that of the original Invoice that need to be voided.



The User can review the 'AR Payments View' to have the details about that specific Invoice that needs to be voided, under the path: Applications -> Accounts Receivable -> Interactive View -> Payments View:



In order to void a posted Cash Receipt, the User needs to follow the below steps:

Step 1: Open the Cash Receipts Screen

i. Navigate to the AR Cash Receipts screen under the path: Applications -> Accounts Receivable -> Transactions -> Cash Receipts



Step 2: Create a new Cash Receipt:

i. Click the New button on the toolbar to open a new Cash Receipt record. [If batch processing is enabled in Business Rules, select the relevant Batch Code. This field corresponds to the batch or deposit ID if the system interfaces with Bank Reconciliation. If batch processing is not enabled, this step can be skipped.]



Step 3: Set the Date and Fiscal Period

i. In the Payment Date field, enter the date corresponding to the Cash Receipt we need to void.

ii. Select the Fiscal period and year from the Fiscal Pd/Year fields. [By default, these fields will get adjusted based on the 'Payment Date']

NOTE: Ensure this matches the period in which the original invoice was created.



Step 4: Select the Customer

From the Customer ID field, select the customer for whom the negative Cash Receipt is being created. The system will display all open invoices for the selected customer in the Open Invoice Summary section.



Step 5: Enter Payment Details

i. Payment Amount: Enter the negative amount equivalent to the original Cash Receipt. For example, if the original payment was $10, enter -10 dollars.

-
Payment Method: Select the same payment method used in the original Cash Receipt.

- For Check Payments: Enter the check number.
- For Credit Card Payments: The masked credit card details will appear. Confirm the selection or choose another stored card.
- For Direct Debit Payments: Select the appropriate account from the drop-down.
- Here, Let's consider the example as 'Cash' [As this was the 'Payment Method' used for the original Cash receipt]

-
Remaining Field: The system will display the remaining balance after applying the negative receipt to the invoice.



Step 6: Enter a Line item to void the original Cash Receipt

Click on the new Line Item, in case the original Cash Receipt was already posted, and enter that Invoice number in the 'Invoice Number' field.

Step 7: Assign to an Invoice or On Account

- If the payment is tied to a specific invoice, ensure the Invoice No field reflects the correct invoice number.
- If the payment is not tied to a specific invoice, select On Account to apply the adjustment as a general credit to the customer’s account.



Step 8: Save the Negative Cash Receipt

- Click the Save button to save the negative Cash Receipt.
- The system generates a unique receipt number for the transaction and updates the General Ledger accordingly.



Step 9: Print the Journal and post the Cash Receipts

Now, the user can print the 'Cash Receipts Journal' and post the Cash Receipts.



Step 10: Observe the impact of the posted negative Cash Receipt

The Detail History View will now have a negative entry on this.

7cc1a880-7ac4-4e1d-8912-fdd83128f256.title: Purging data in the PO Approvals
7cc1a880-7ac4-4e1d-8912-fdd83128f256.content:
Problem
Purging data in the PO Approvals

Purpose of Purging:

To remove obsolete purchase order (PO) requests from the system, including declined, pending, new requests, and approval details before a specific date.

Resolution
Steps to Use the Purge Requests Function:

- Back up your data before proceeding.

- Choose the types of requests to purge:
- Declined requests
- Pending requests
- New requests
- Approval details

- For each selected option, enter the cutoff date.

- Only the request types marked with a check box will be purged.
- Declined and pending requests with last activity on or before the cutoff date will be purged.
- New requests with a request date on or before the cutoff date will be purged.
- Approval details with an approved date on or before the cutoff date will be purged.

d5fdadfc-1be0-4bbd-b08b-85b0214df2f7.title: How to add Freight charge on Vendor's Invoice in Purchase Order
d5fdadfc-1be0-4bbd-b08b-85b0214df2f7.content:
Problem
The client needs to enter freight charges that were charged by a vendor for product received. This vendor added a freight charge on the invoice that needs to be reflected.

Resolution
To add freight charges based on the total invoice, find the Purchase Order transaction, and follow these steps using the Invoice Totals button:

- First, create an invoice for the transaction.
- Navigate to the Totals tab and select the Invoice Totals button.

- Enter the required freight charges.

- Click Save to apply the changes.
- Click Save again on the PO Transaction screen.

Note: The Detail button provides additional options, allowing you to:

- View detailed information.
- Enter Freight or Miscellaneous charges for the invoice.
- Adjust tax amounts.
- Enter prepayments.
- Split the invoice into three payments.
- Print an online check.
- Modify Invoice Date, Fiscal Period, and Year fields if applicable.

Payments should be processed through the AP workflow or the Deposits screen. However, payments entered via the Invoice Totals window will still be posted to the General Ledger (GL). Freight, miscellaneous, and sales tax costs should be entered here.

Additionally, invoice exchange rates can be modified for new invoices. For existing invoices, exchange rates can only be adjusted within the Invoice Totals window.

f451849f-b6a9-4af3-97eb-58ba41ad76a8.title: Deleting or Removing a Sales Rep ID from AR Sales Reps
f451849f-b6a9-4af3-97eb-58ba41ad76a8.content:
Problem
When trying to delete or remove a inactive/no longer used Sales Rep ID in Account Receivable - Setup and Maintenance - Sales Reps, a "Delete Validation" warning is received advising that "Current record cannot be deleted." Which will not allow the Sales Rep ID to be deleted.

Cause
The Delete Validation warning message typically indicates that the Sales Rep ID cannot be deleted because of any of the following reasons:

- The Sales Rep ID may be currently listed as the Sales Rep ID 1 or 2 in an AR Customers master setup.
- The Sales Rep ID may be currently listed as the Sales Rep ID 1 or 2 in any AR Ship-To Addresses master setup.
- The Sales Rep ID may be currently listed on an open and active Transactions. This can be in Accounts Receivable Transactions, Sales Order Orders, Service Director Work Orders, Point-Of-Sale Daily Activity, or Requirement Planning SO Blank Orders.
- The Sales Rep ID may be be currently listed on a AR or SO Recurring Entries master setup record.
- The Sales Rep ID may be linked to a Traverse User ID in SM User Mapping.
- The Sales Rep ID may be currently listed as the Sales Rep in PS Users or in PS Terminals.
- There may be commission/invoice records in AR Commission Detail that are present for the Sales Rep in AR Commissions.

Resolution
To resolve the "Delete Validation" warning, any instance of the Sales Rep ID in master setups, active transaction entry, and Commission Detail records of the Sales Rep ID that is attempting to be deleted must be deleted or removed before the Sales Rep ID can be deleted.



The Sales Rep ID cannot be present in any of the following master setup records in the following areas:

- The Sales Rep ID cannot be currently present in the 'Sales Rep ID 1' or the 'Sales Rep ID 2' fields in any master customer setup records in Accounts Receivable-Setup and Maintenance-Customers (Defaults tab). Any Customer ID record that has the Sales Rep ID present in either of these fields will need to have the Sales Rep ID removed before the Sales Rep ID can be deleted in AR Sales Reps.
- The Accounts Receivable-Interactive Views-Customer View may be used to help narrow down what Customer ID records may have the Sales Rep ID may be listed in the 'Sales Rep ID 1' or the 'Sales Rep ID 2' fields.

- The Sales Rep ID cannot be currently present in the 'Sales Rep ID 1' or the 'Sales Rep ID 2' fields in any master ship-to addresses for customer records in Account Receivable-Setup and Maintenance-Ship-To Addresses. Any Ship-To ID record that has the Sales Rep ID present in either of these fields will need to have the Sales Rep ID removed before the Sales Rep ID can be deleted in AR Sales Reps.
- The Accounts Receivable-Interactive Views-Ship-To Address View may be used to help narrow down what Ship-To ID records may have the Sales Rep ID listed in the 'Sales Rep ID 1' or the 'Sales Rep ID 2' fields.

- The Sales Rep ID cannot be currently present in the 'Sales Rep ID 1' or the 'Sales Rep ID 2' fields in any Recur IDs that are set up and present in Accounts Receivable-Setup and Maintenance-Recurring Entries. Any AR Recurring Entries - Recur ID that has the Sales Rep ID present in either of these two fields would need to have the Sales Rep ID removed to delete the Sales Rep ID in AR Sales Reps.
- The Sales Rep ID cannot be currently present in the 'Sales Rep ID 1' or the 'Sales Rep ID 2' fields in any Recur IDs that are set up and present in Sales Order-Setup and Maintenance-Recurring Entries. Any SO Recurring Entries - Recur ID that has the Sales Rep ID present in either of these two fields would need to have the Sales Rep ID removed to delete the Sales Rep ID in AR Sales Reps.
- The Sales Rep ID cannot be currently present in the 'Sales Rep ID 1' or the 'Sales Rep ID 2' fields in any blanket orders that are set up and present in Requirements Planning-Blanket Orders-Blanket Orders (Bill-To tab). Any SO Blanket No that has the Sales Rep ID present in either of these two fields would need to have the sales Rep ID removed to delete the Sales Rep ID in AR Sales Reps.
- The Sales Rep ID cannot be currently linked to a Traverse User ID in System Manager-Administration-User Mapping, if the Sales Rep ID is shown as being linked to a Traverse User ID in SM User Mapping, the entry would need to be deleted or the User ID would need to be linked to a different Sales Rep ID in order for the original Sales Rep ID to be deleted in AR Sales Reps.
- The Sales Rep ID cannot be currently present in the 'Sales Rep' field for any Terminal ID's that have been set up in Point Of Sale-Setup and Maintenance-Terminals. Any Terminals that have the Sales Rep ID present in the Sales Rep field would need to have the Sales Rep ID removed to delete the Sales Rep ID in AR Sales Reps.
- The Sales Rep ID cannot be currently present in the 'Sales Rep ID' field for any User ID's that have been set up in Point Of Sale-Setup and Maintenance-Users. Any User IDs that have the Sales Rep ID present in the Sales Rep ID field would need to have the Sales Rep ID removed to delete the Sales Rep ID in AR Sales Reps.



The Sales Rep ID cannot be listed on any current/active/open Transaction. The following areas will need to be reviewed to ensure the Sales Rep ID that is trying to be deleted/removed in AR Sales Reps is not present:

- The Sales Rep ID cannot be currently present in the 'Sales Rep ID 1' or the 'Sales Rep ID 2' fields of any Transaction Header records in Accounts Receivable<Transactions<Transactions. Any AR Transactions that have the Sales Rep ID present in either of these two fields would need to have the Sales Rep ID removed to delete the Sales Rep ID in AR Sales Reps.
- The AR Transaction View may be used to help isolate which Transaction No's have the specific Sales Rep ID listed.

- The Sales Rep ID cannot be currently present in the 'Sales Rep ID 1' or the 'Sales Rep ID 2' fields of any Transaction Bill-To Header records in Sales Order<Transactions<Orders. Any SO Orders that have the Sales Rep ID present in either of these two fields would need to have the Sales Rep ID removed to delete the Sales Rep ID in AR Sales Reps.
- The SO Order View may be used to help isolate which Active Order No's have the specific Sales Rep ID listed.
- If the Sales Order Business Rule for "Commission By Line Item" is or has ever been set to 'Yes', the Sales Rep ID cannot be currently present in the  'Sales Rep ID 1' or the 'Sales Rep ID 2' fields in the line entry details of the SO Orders for any active transaction. Any SO Orders that have the Sales Rep ID present in either of these two fields would need to have the Sales Rep ID removed to delete the Sales Rep ID in AR Sales Reps.

- The Sales Rep ID cannot be currently present in the 'Sales Rep ID 1' or the 'Sales Rep ID 2' fields of any Work Order Site Information records in Service Director<Work Orders<Work Orders Entry. Any Service Director Work Orders that have the Sales Rep ID present in either of these two fields would need to have the Sales Rep ID removed to delete the Sales Rep ID in AR Sales Reps.
- The SD Order View may be used to help isolate which work order Order No's have the specific Sales Rep ID listed.

- The Sales Rep ID cannot be currently present in the 'Sales Rep ID 1' or the 'Sales Rep ID 2' fields of any SD Edit Billings Header records in Service Director<Work Orders<Edit Billings. Any SD Transactions that have the Sales Rep ID present in either of these two fields would need to have the Sales Rep ID removed to delete the Sales Rep ID in AR Sales Reps.
- If the Sales Rep ID that is trying to be deleted is present in the "Sales Rep ID 1" and/or "Sales Rep ID 2" fields of the line entry details of the SD Edit Billings, the Sales Rep ID will not be able to be deleted in AR Sales Reps. If the Sales Rep ID is present in either of these two fields, and if the Service Director Business Rule for "Commission By Line Item" is set to 'Yes', the Sales Rep ID in the line entry details of SD Edit Billings maybe be changed from the Sales Rep ID that is currently being deleted to alternate Sales Rep ID. If the  Business Rule for "Commission By Line Item" is set to 'No', then the Sales Rep ID may need to be removed from the SD Work Order Entry - Site Information "Sales Rep ID 1" and/or the "Sales Rep ID 2" field, then the Work Order will need to be unbilled, and then re-billed/Prepare Invoices performed to have the new Sales Rep ID pull into the line entry details. Any SD Edit Billings transaction that has the Sales Rep ID present in either of these two fields in the line entry details would need to have the Sales Rep ID changed to a different Sales Rep ID to delete the Sales Rep ID in AR Sales Reps.

- The Sales Rep ID cannot be listed or linked to any unposted Point-of-Sale<Daily Work Transactions. Any Transactions that have the Sales Rep ID present would need to have the transaction processed so the commission record could be later processed to allow the Sales Rep ID to be deleted in AR Sales Reps.
- The PS Activity View may be used to help isolate any unposted Transactions that have the specific Sales Rep ID listed.



The Sales Rep ID cannot have any Commission Detail records present in Accounts Receivable<Commissions<Commission Detail.

- If there are any Commissions Due to the Sales Rep ID that is being removed, and these are still going to be paid out to the Sales Rep, then prepare, process, and post commissions for that Sales Rep as you normally would.
- If there are any Commissions Due to the Sales Rep ID or that aren't completed for the Sales Rep, that is being removed and will not be paid out. These records will either need to be deleted or completed and purged from AR Commissions, along with any Commission Invoice Record that has been completed already.
- The Accounts Receivable<Commissions<Commission Detail View may be used to identify Commission Invoice records that are either on Hold or don't have a Date Complete.
- Once the Commission Invoice records are identified, the "Date Completed" can be selected, and the "Hold Invoice" may be unchecked in Accounts Receivable<Commissions<Commission Detail.

- (Optional) The Accounts Receivable<Commission<Commission Detail List may be printed and/or saved for the Sales Rep ID that is being removed from Traverse to have a record of the AR Commission details that existed for this Sales Rep.
- Once the Commission Invoice detail records have a date completed selected and don't have the "Hold Invoice" checked, the Accounts Receivable<Commissions<Purge Completed Invoices may be used to purge/remove the Commission Invoice records from AR Commissions.
- The Purge Completed Invoices function is used to remove completed commission invoice records you no longer need. An invoice is completed when commissions have been paid to the sales reps on the invoice, or once its physically marked complete in AR Commission Detail by entering a Completed Date.
- Before purging completed invoices, print the Commission Edit Register and the Commission Detail List to serve as an audit trail. Purging completed invoices deletes all commission history data for selected invoices.
- IMPORTANT! Before executing the AR Purge Invoices, a Data Filter should be set to where the Sales Rep ID equals the specific Sales ID. This will ensure that other Sales Rep Commission Invoice records aren't inadvertently purged from AR Commission Details.

- Enter a date value in the "Purge Commission Invoices Completed Before" and in the "Purge Zero Commission Invoices Before" fields. This date should be after the latest corresponding dates for the Sales Rep Commission Invoice detail records.
- Select "OK" to execute the AR Purge Completed Invoices.

- If there is a limited number of Commission Invoice Records that exist in Accounts Receivable<Commissions<Commission Detail that need to be removed. Instead of using the AR Purge Completed Invoices, the individual records may be deleted one by one in AR Commission Details. This is completed by selecting the individual Commission Invoice entry, then selecting the Delete  button to delete the record.

- AR Commission Detail, after all the Completed Invoice records have been Purged.



After removing any instance of the Sales Rep ID in master setups, active transaction entry, and Commission Detail records, the Sales Rep ID should be able to be deleted in Accounts Receivable<Setup and Maintenance<Sales Reps.

0fc1b2f1-5aba-4cba-ac2d-abdb5ee4bab7.title: How to Use the Global Item Replace Function to Replace a Component in Bills of Material
0fc1b2f1-5aba-4cba-ac2d-abdb5ee4bab7.content:
Problem
How to Use the Global Item Replace Function to Replace a Component in Bills of Material

Resolution
Steps to Replace a Component in Bills of Material:

-
Navigate to the Global Item Replace Function:

- Go to Applications > Bill of Material > Setup and Maintenance > Global Item Replace.
- In the Component to be Replaced section, locate and select the Item ID of the component you wish to replace.
- If applicable, modify the Location ID and Unit fields to reflect the correct information for the component being replaced.

-
Select the Replacement Component:

- In the Replacement Component section, select the Item ID of the replacement component.
- Adjust the Location ID and Unit fields in the Replacement Component section if necessary.

-
Adjust Quantity Multiplication:

- Enter a value in the Multiply Quantities By field. This step is critical to ensure the correct quantities are used when replacing the components.
- Note: If the relationship between the original and replacement items is one-to-one, enter 1.
- If the relationship is different, enter the multiplier that adjusts the quantities accordingly. For example:
- If you are replacing a 128 MB memory component with a 512 MB memory component and wish to maintain the same total memory, enter 0.25 to use one 512 MB module instead of four 128 MB modules.

-
Select Bills of Material to Update:

- In the Selection List section, choose the bills of material in which you want the item replacement to take place.

-
Add Comments (Optional):

- If needed, enter any Comments to provide context or additional details about the replacement.

-
Process the Replacement:

- Click OK to process the replacement and update the selected bills of material.

-
View Activity Log (Optional):

- If you want to review the process or check for any issues, click Activity to view the Activity Log for the global item replacement.

-
Reset Fields (Optional):

- If you wish to start over or clear all entries, click Reset to return all fields to their default values.

100ae485-fcc2-4769-95e7-2557e64d7927.title: Hawkins Bailey Warehouse, Inc. - Bulk Updating "Qty On Hand Max" value to zero
100ae485-fcc2-4769-95e7-2557e64d7927.content:
Problem
Customer has two new locations, therefore they performed "IN Copy Items to Locations" to copy the item's information to new locations, but customer wanted the values of "Qty On Hand Max" to be "0" in the new locations. Let's take an example and assume that items are copied from MN to CA and MN02, where CA and MN02 are new locations.

Resolution
Once the customer has run the "IN Copy Items to Locations" below is the item view with non-zero values in "Qty On Hand Max".

To Reduce the value to zero, we would need to run a script in that particular database.

Below is the script that needs to be run.

UPDATE tblInItemLoc
SET QtyOnHandMax = '0'
WHERE LocId IN ('CA', 'MN02');     // Location Id should be the location in which we need to change the values.

Therefore, Login to SSMS. Right click on the database and click on new query.



Copy and paste the scrip in the new query screen. Click execute at the top.

Once we execute the query successfully, go back to item view.

We could see that all their qty on hand max values for the location CA and MN02 are reduced to 0. Hence the issue is resolve.





Note: Make sure to take backups before applying the scrip in the database.

e711d361-277a-4a92-92d8-37bc673ff3f7.title: How to compute Period depreciation in Fixed Assets and generate Period Depreciation report?
e711d361-277a-4a92-92d8-37bc673ff3f7.content:
Problem
How do you compute the Period depreciation in Fixed Assets and generate a FA Period Depreciation report?

Resolution
FA Compute Period Depreciation:

The Compute Period Depreciation function is used to calculate depreciation for active assets, generate the Period Depreciation Report, and post the period depreciation.



We can navigate to the FA Compute Period Depreciation screen under the path: Applications -> Fixed Assets -> Period Work -> Compute Period Depreciation



Prerequisites:

Before proceeding with the calculation or posting of depreciation, the necessary permissions for Fixed Assets Compute Period Depreciation must be updated.

The depreciation methods used and the number of periods in the fiscal year determines whether depreciation should be calculated and posted at the end of each accounting period.

Understanding the Compute Period Depreciation Screen:

The Compute Period Depreciation screen consists of two sections:

a. Informational Section:

-
- Displays Depreciation Types
- Shows the Fiscal Year in process of being computed
- Indicates the Current Status of calculated depreciation
- Displays the number of Periods in Year for the Fiscal Year and of those Periods, the number of Periods that have been processed under Periods Processed



b. Calculation Section:

-
- Used to select the Depreciation Types for calculation
- Allows defining the Beginning and Ending Periods that will be calculated
- Displays the Current Fiscal Period

Steps to Compute Period Depreciation:

i. Select the Depreciation Types:

- Choose the required depreciation types by selecting the corresponding checkbox in the bottom section.

ii. Define Periods for Depreciation Calculation:

- The Beginning Period refers to the first period for which depreciation will be computed.
- The Ending Period is the last period for which depreciation will be computed.
- The Fiscal Period field displays the current period, which can be modified if needed.

Example:

a. If depreciation is computed for the entire fiscal year in one go, set the Beginning Period to 1, the Ending Period to 12, and the Fiscal Period to 12 before calculation.

b. If depreciation is computed for just one period of the fiscal year, set the Beginning Period and, the Ending Period to the Fiscal Period before calculation (For example: 12 for both)



iii. Depreciation Calculation:

- Click on the 'Calculate' icon at the top to calculate the 'Depreciation'



Command Options:

-
- Calculate – Computes depreciation based on the asset setup in the Fixed Assets module.
- Activity – Displays the Activity Log for period depreciation.
- Reset – Resets all fields and selections to default values.
- Select All – Selects all depreciation types.
- Unselect All – Deselects all previously selected depreciation types.
- Report – Generates the Period Depreciation Report with selected depreciation values.
- Post – Posts the calculated depreciation for the selected assets.

Generating and Reviewing the Period Depreciation Report

The Period Depreciation Report provides a detailed journal of the accumulated depreciation taken, along with year-to-date, annual, and current depreciation for active assets. This report should be reviewed to verify depreciation figures before posting.



Once the 'Depreciation' had been calculated, the User can generate the Period Depreciation Report. To generate the 'FA Period Depreciation Report', click on the 'Report' icon at the top:



Once the report is reviewed and verified, the user can click on the 'Post' icon to post the Depreciation.



The Period Depreciation Post Log can be referenced to confirm that depreciation has been successfully posted.

600875b3-0b6c-4f93-b1ca-b2c82c2a8d44.title: Launching Traverse as a web link (RDS Web Link)

a071b1a2-e470-4998-b04f-1d19d8dfc240.title: How is a Manufactured Finished Good disassembled or unbuilt after its been produced and the Work Order has been completed?
a071b1a2-e470-4998-b04f-1d19d8dfc240.content:
Problem
After a Manufactured Production Order has been completed to record production of a Finished Good/Assembly and that finished good ends up needing to be disassembled and the raw material/components returned to On-Hand Stock, how is this recorded?

Resolution
The recommended way to record the unbuild/disassembly of Finished Goods/assembly is by using the Warehouse Management<Daily Work<Adjustments feature. (If not licensed for the Warehouse Manager Application, then it is recommended to use the Inventory<Transactions<Inventory Transactions - Adjustments to accomplish this).



Warehouse Management:

- In Warehouse Management<Daily Work<Adjustments, you will first want to enter a "Decrease" entry for the Item ID of the Finished Good/Assembly ID of which you are looking to disassembly, along with the Adj Quantity being the number of units you are disassembling.
- Next in WM Adjustments you will enter "Increase" entries types, to add the raw material/components IDs back to Inventory On Hand.

(Please note: that when performing WM Adjustments Increases the Unit Cost is an editable value, so you will want to ensure the desired Unit Cost is used when adding the Raw Material back to the On-Hand Inventory. Another thing to consider is if any Machine Run Time Costs or Labor Costs went into the manufacturing of the original Finished Good, you may want to consider reviewing with your Accountant to make sure those costs are properly handled when disassembling a Finished Good/Assembly.)
- Once the entries are entered into WM Adjustments, you may use the Warehouse Management<Reports and Worksheets<Adjustments Journal, to Print the Adjustments Journal to review the entries for accuracy and to have a Journal for Auditing purposes.

- After the Journal has been printed and reviewed for accuracy, the Warehouse Management<Reports and Worksheets<Post Adjustments may be used to post the transactions to history and write the GL Journal Entries.





Inventory:

- In Inventory<Transactions<Inventory Transactions - Adjustments, you will first want to enter a "Decrease" entry type for the Item ID of the Finished Good/Assembly ID of which you are looking to disassembly, along with the Adj Quantity being the number of units you are disassembling.

- Next in IN Inventory Transactions - Adjustment you will enter "Increase" entries types, to add the raw material/components IDs back to Inventory On Hand.

(Please note: that when performing IN Inventory Transactions Adjustments Increases the Unit Cost is an editable value, so you will want to ensure the desired Unit Cost is used when adding the Raw Material back to the On-Hand Inventory. Another thing to consider is if any Machine Run Time Costs or Labor Costs went into the manufacturing of the original Finished Good, you may want to consider reviewing with your Accountant to make sure those costs are properly handled when disassembling a Finished Good/Assembly.)
- Once the entries are entered into IN Inventory Transactions - Adjustments, you may use the Inventory<Transactions<Transaction  Journal, to Print the Journal to review the entries for accuracy and to have a Journal for Auditing purposes.

- After the Journal has been printed and reviewed for accuracy, the Inventory<Transactions<Post Transactions may be used to post the transactions to history and write the GL Journal Entries.

The customer is inquiring whether Traverse Web API has a built-in mechanism to log errors globally. Specifically, they need a solution that automatically captures and saves any errors that occur during API operations to a designated folder.

Resolution
Since the customer is using Swagger, we recommended that they use Postman instead. We advised them to download Postman from www.postman.com and complete the sign-up process.

Once they successfully downloaded, installed, and signed up for Postman, they can proceed with further testing.

Click on import and drop the file from the above link,



ChatGPT said:

Click on import and drop the file from the above link,

Global API Postman v21088.zip

To import the file into Postman:

- Click on Import.

This will load the necessary API documentation for further use.

To import the file into Postman:

After importing the file into Postman, the customer needs to access the Traverse application and update the API security settings as follows:

- Go to API Configuration.
- Open API Security Settings.

Go back to the API in Postman and navigate to the collection.

- Click on "Global API Samples" within the collection.
- Open the Authorization tab.
- Verify that the configuration matches the required settings.

Ensure that all authentication details, such as the authorization type, token, or credentials, are correctly configured as specified.





After configuring the authorization settings, proceed with the environment setup in Postman:

- Click on Environments in Postman.
- Select Global.
- Configure the environment variables as shown in the provided setup instructions.
- Ensure that the Current Value and Initial Value are the same for each variable.

This will ensure consistency in the environment settings for API requests.





Ensure that the Token_URL and Request_URL are correctly configured in the Postman environment settings:

-
Token_URL – This should be the API site URL from the browser, appended with /api_token.

- Example: https://your-api-url.com/api_token

-
Request_URL – This should be the API site URL, appended with /api/v2/.

- Example: https://your-api-url.com/api/v2/

-
Company – This should be set to the customer's database company name (e.g., CPU).

Verify that these values are correctly entered in the Global Environment settings in Postman to ensure proper API communication.

After configuring the environment settings, follow these steps to obtain and apply the access token:
