87a96b11-2abd-4494-9cee-ce5205b33e82.title: How to perform Inventory Adjustment?
87a96b11-2abd-4494-9cee-ce5205b33e82.content:
Problem
How to perform Inventory Adjustment?

Resolution
The Inventory Transactions function allows users to enter sale, purchase, and adjustment transactions. Unposted transactions appear upon selecting a tab. Once a transaction is entered and saved, certain fields such as Type, Item ID, Location ID, and Unit cannot be modified.

Note: The Exchange Rate button on the toolbar enables users to view or edit the exchange rate for the transaction.



The Inventory Transactions function under the Transactions menu can be used for the following purposes:

- Adjusting inventory quantities.
- Recording sales for new orders, shipments, invoiced sales, or returned items.
- Recording purchases for new orders, received items, invoiced purchases, or returned items.
- Editing unposted purchase, sale, and adjustment transactions.



Let us consider the sample Item ID '00059', and we can observe the 'Quantity Available' and 'Quantity On-Hand' being zero.



Working with Adjustment Transactions:

Adjustment transactions are used to correct discrepancies in inventory that do not result from sales or purchases, such as damaged items or adjustments from other applications. These transactions directly update the Inventory.

Note: Adjustments cannot be made to service items.



The Inventory Adjustments can be done in the 'IN Inventory Transactions' screen under the path: Applications -> Inventory -> Transactions -> Inventory Transactions:



Steps to Enter an Adjustment Transaction:

A. Create an Inventory Adjustment:

I. Summary View:

-
Select the Adjustment Type

- Increase: Increases both on-hand and available quantities.
- Decrease: Decreases both on-hand and available quantities.

-
Select the Item ID

- The item description will be displayed automatically.

-
Select the Location ID

- The location description will be displayed.

-
Enter the Adjustment Quantity

- Input the quantity of items in the Adj Qty field.
- The default unit of measure will appear in the Unit field.

-
Adjust the Unit Cost (if needed)

- Increase Adjustment: Displays the last cost of the item (modifiable).
- Decrease Adjustment: Displays the cost based on the selected costing method (FIFO, LIFO, Average, or Standard), which can be modified if required.

-
Verify the Extended Cost

- The system calculates and displays the extended cost.

-
Save the Transaction

- Click the Save button to finalize the adjustment. [Note: If the item is lotted or serialized, click the Lot/Ser No Entry button to enter or view lot and serial number details.]



II. Detail View [If the details are already filled in 'Summary View', the defaults fields will be pulled and displayed here. If not, we need to fill out the details here]:

-
Click the >> button to switch to Detail View.

-
Select the Adjustment Type (Increase/Decrease).

-
Choose the Item ID (description appears automatically).

-
Choose the Location ID (description appears automatically).

-
Select the General Ledger (GL) Account impacted by the adjustment from the COGS Adj field.

- The default GL COGS Adjustment account is pre-configured in the item's account code for the selected location.
- If Inventory is integrated with General Ledger, and the adjustment is an increase, the AR GL Offset account appears automatically.

-
Enter Date and Fiscal Period

- The Date field defaults to the workstation date but can be changed.
- The Fiscal Period and Year default to the workstation settings but can be modified.

-
Unit and Quantity Details

- The default Unit of Measure appears (modifiable).
- Enter the Adjustment Quantity in the Adj Qty field.

-
Adjust the Unit Cost (if needed)

- Increase Adjustment: Displays the last cost of the item (modifiable).
- Decrease Adjustment: Displays the cost based on the selected costing method (FIFO, LIFO, Average, or Standard), which can be modified if required.

-
Verify the Extended Cost

- The system calculates and displays the extended cost.

-
Enter Additional Comments (Optional)

- Any notes regarding the adjustment can be added in the Comments field.

- Save the Transaction

- Click the Save button to complete the inventory adjustment.



Handling Serialized and Lotted Item Transactions: For serialized and lotted items, follow the same adjustment transaction process but ensure that the Lot/Ser No Entry details are recorded before saving the transaction.



B. Print the 'Transaction Journal':

Once the 'IN Inventory Transactions' are created, review and print the 'Transaction Journal' under the path:  Applications -> Inventory -> Transactions -> Transaction Journal:



C. Post the Transactions:

Then we can post the Transactions in the 'IN Post Transactions' screen under the path:  Applications -> Inventory -> Transactions -> Post Transactions:



Now, we can observe the result of Inventory Adjustment in the 'IN Items' screen for that specific entry:

4a537fb2-f2e4-4489-bcff-adc1e79b9477.title: Error: 'Country Code VN is Not a Supported Country' During Tax Calculation in Sales Orders (Example: VN for Vietnam)
4a537fb2-f2e4-4489-bcff-adc1e79b9477.content:
Problem
Error: 'Country Code VN is Not a Supported Country' During Tax Calculation in Sales Orders (Example: VN for Vietnam)

Resolution
When calculating taxes in Sales Orders (SO Orders), users encounter an error stating "The country code VN is not a supported country," despite using the correct country code ("VN" for Vietnam). This issue occurs due to a mismatch between the country code provided and the actual address, for example, when the address is set to Vietnam (VN), but the system has incorrectly set the country code to "US" instead of "VN," which prevents accurate tax calculations.

Follow these steps to resolve the issue and successfully calculate taxes in Sales Orders:

- Go to Applications > System Manager > Setup and Maintenance.
- Locate Tax Service Integration under the setup options.
- In the Tax Service Integration settings, uncheck the option for "Enable Address Validation".
- In the Valid Countries field, ensure you type in VN (Vietnam) or any other country that you want to validate tax for.
- After making these changes, update the settings.
- Go back to the Sales Order (SO) and attempt to recalculate the tax.
- The tax should now be calculated successfully without encountering the "country code VN is not a supported country" error.

4dcffa46-90c8-4f48-9a60-8ba423803bd6.title: Unable to post payments in AP "No EFT payment for the selected batch"
4dcffa46-90c8-4f48-9a60-8ba423803bd6.content:
Problem
Customer is trying to post payments; they get an error message stating that they need to create an ACH file, but when they create the ACH file they get an error shown below.

Resolution
Basically, we get an error as in the screen shot when there are actually no payment records or when there are any debit memos to reverse the invoices in the batch.

In this case, we would need the payment to be posted without creating the ACH file.

Therefore, go to System Manager > Company Setup > Business Rules > click on Accounts Payables

Under Miscellaneous, we have a field "Allow posting without creating ACH file" which would have selected as "No". Change the option to "Yes",

Click apply in the bottom and click Ok. Now go back to AP post payments screen, try to post the payment, the payment will be posted successfully.

Note: Make sure that we change the option back to "No" once we have posted, so that it won't create any trouble for customer in future.

7bdb1fcc-55d2-426e-af3f-4475ed90021a.title: Detail Leave Report does not show all entries, and is missing leave entries from the end of the year
7bdb1fcc-55d2-426e-af3f-4475ed90021a.content:
Problem
When trying to pull the Detailed Leave Report for a new year from Payroll > Personnel Reports> Detailed Leave Report, the report is empty or missing entries created at the end of the previous year.

Resolution
The Detail Leave Report displays leave details coded to the current Payroll Year. If the new Payroll Year was created prior to all the Payroll processing being completed in the old year, leave recorded after the new Payroll Year is created will not have been carried over to the new year. This would cause leave records created after the new year was created to be missing when running the report for the new Payroll Year.

The detail leave records can still be viewed if the Payroll Year is set back to the old payroll year and the Detail Leave Report run from there.

To change the Payroll year, navigate to Payroll> Period Processing> Change Payroll Year> Toggle to prior year and hit Ok.

Now run the report from Payroll > Personnel Reports> Detailed Leave Report; it would display the entries created after the new Payroll Year was created.

c298ca73-bd6d-492d-a501-950b5ee2872e.title: Calculate button is greyed out in FA Compute Period Depriciation
c298ca73-bd6d-492d-a501-950b5ee2872e.content:
Problem
When we try to Compute Period Depreciation in Fixed Assets, the Calculate button is greyed out, therefore unable to calculate

d4acda04-f613-4e94-818a-0cec3cde5311.title: Discrepancy in Net Due and Total Due to Incorrect Receipt and Invoice Processing
d4acda04-f613-4e94-818a-0cec3cde5311.content:
Problem
For a purchase order, the client ordered an item with a total quantity of 9, which was received in two separate receipts—one for 3 quantities and another for 6 quantities, each with different unit costs. The receipt for all 9 quantities has been posted, and the invoice for the 3-quantity receipt is also posted, while the invoice for the 6-quantity receipt remains unposted.

Resolution
Further investigation revealed that the receipts and invoices were processed with incorrect values, leading to a mismatch between the Net Due in the right corner and the Total under the Totals screen. This discrepancy occurred because the receipts and invoices were not entered correctly.

To approximate these two values, we suggest the following approach:

- Create an invoice for the remaining 6 quantities with a unit cost of 21.9733. By doing this, the Net Due will be 6,591.77, while the Total value will be 6,591.87. You can then proceed with posting the transaction.



If this approach does not align with your business requirements, you may instead:

- Create an invoice for the remaining 6 quantities using the original cost of 20.89.
- Post the transaction.
- Return the item (KOP 04010684).
- Complete the debit memo process.

To avoid this scenario in the future, we recommend the following:

- If you are receiving or ordering the same items at different costs, please create a new line item for each cost variation. This will help prevent any confusion or discrepancies in transactions.
- Assign a batch to a specific user to ensure that transactions are not mistakenly posted by different users, reducing the risk of errors.

27ae69b3-06a1-4ed1-ae3d-959aec0b8711.title: Fixed Asset: Year-End Maintenance
27ae69b3-06a1-4ed1-ae3d-959aec0b8711.content:
Problem
Fixed Asset: Year-End Maintenance

Resolution
Year-End Maintenance Process for Fixed Assets

The Year-End Maintenance process allows you to perform essential tasks to prepare your Fixed Asset records for the upcoming year. These actions can be accessed via the Depreciation tab in the Fixed Assets setup. The following tasks can be performed during the Year-End Maintenance process:

- Update Accumulated Depreciation
- Add year-to-date (YTD) depreciation to the accumulated depreciation taken.
- Update Accumulated Eligible Depreciation
- Add annual depreciation to accumulated eligible depreciation.
- Reset YTD Depreciation
- Reset the YTD depreciation field to zero for the new year.
- Calculate Projected Depreciation
- Calculate the projected annual depreciation for the upcoming year.
- Increment Current Year
- Increment the Current Year field by one.
- Reset Period Fields
- Reset the Begin Period, Ending Period, and Process fields to zero.
- Delete Retired Assets (Optional)
- Delete assets that were retired before a specified date.

You can perform Year-End Maintenance for any or all types of depreciation, including:

- A.M.T. (Alternative Minimum Tax): Used for calculating depreciation for federal tax purposes. For detailed information on AMT, refer to the appropriate IRS publications.
- Book: Used for your company’s general ledger. If the Fixed Assets module is integrated with General Ledger, the depreciation calculations for this book are posted to the GL accounts.
- FedTax: Used for federal tax purposes. Depreciation in this book is used to generate the Depreciation Tax Report and for tax filing purposes.
- Other: Used for local tax or informational purposes.

Once the Year-End Maintenance process is completed, a log will be generated automatically, providing a detailed record of each asset processed, along with information on the actions taken for each selected depreciation type.



Year-End Maintenance Process for Fixed Assets: Step-by-Step Guide

- Process All Periods
Ensure all periods are processed before beginning the year-end maintenance.
- Print Year-End Reports
Generate and print the year-end reports to document the depreciation and asset status.
- Print Retirements Journal
Print the Retirements journal for a record of all asset retirements during the year.
- Print Additions Journal
Print the Additions journal for a record of all asset additions made during the year.
- Back Up Data Files
Perform a backup of your data files to prevent any loss during the maintenance process.
- Mark the "Do the Following" Check Box
Check the box next to Do the following, then proceed with the subsequent steps.
- Remove Retired Assets (Optional)
If applicable, select a date to remove all retired assets with a Retirement Date prior to the selected date in the Remove Assets Retired Before field.
- Note: Removing assets prior to this date will permanently delete them from the system, making them unavailable for reports and interactive views.
- Enter Comments (Optional)
Enter any applicable comments in the Comments field to provide additional context or notes.
- Select Depreciation Types for Year-End Maintenance
Select the Process check box for the depreciation types you wish to perform year-end maintenance on.
- Checking the box will process the tasks listed in the introduction and reset the fields in the Period Depreciation Setup for the selected depreciation types.
- Depreciation types that are not selected will not be processed.
- Check Status
Review the Status field for the current status of the Compute Period Depreciation for each depreciation type.
- Warning: If the status shows "Unposted Current Depreciation," do not proceed with year-end maintenance until current depreciation is fully posted.
- Warning: If the status shows "Partial Year," complete any unprocessed depreciation periods before continuing.
- Select an Action Button
Choose one of the following command buttons based on your needs:
- OK: Begin processing year-end maintenance.
- Activity: View the Activity Log to see details of the year-end maintenance activities.
- Reset: Reset all fields to their default values.
- Select All: Mark all check boxes in the Process column.
- Unselect All: Clear all check boxes in the Process column.

Following these steps ensures that all necessary actions are taken to properly complete the Year-End Maintenance for Fixed Assets.

5dc6efab-bbde-4c57-904d-490733bee636.title: SQL error  "Cannot insert duplicate key row in object 'dbo.tblnQtyOnHand" in Sales Order Specific to Allision Medical/ Customers on build 24031
5dc6efab-bbde-4c57-904d-490733bee636.content:
Problem
When trying to Post SO Transaction 00203134, the customer is receiving an error message "Cannot insert duplicate key row in object 'dbo.tblnQtyOnHand\_Ext' with unique index 'UX\_tblnQtyOnHand\_Ext\_ID'. The dupliacte key value is (638767096261494607)"

Resolution
This issue has been addressed in newer builds of the TRAVERSE system. To resolve this, update your TRAVERSE build to the latest version.  Specifically, build version 24094 and later include a fix for this issue. If you are on an older build, such as 24031, upgrading to version 24094 or later should resolve the error.

Customers who have modifications would not be able to update to latest build. Development has issued a script to fix it temporarily.
Test the below script with the restored data and upon testing apply to Production company.

DECLARE @NewID bigint
SET @NewID = CAST(DATEDIFF( MINUTE, '00010101', CONVERT(varchar(8),GETDATE(), 112) ) AS bigint) * 60000000 * 10 + (CAST(DATEDIFF( MILLISECOND, CONVERT(varchar(8),GETDATE(), 112), GETDATE() ) AS bigint)  * 1000 + DATEPART( mcs, GETDATE()) - DATEPART( ms, GETDATE()) * 1000) *10 + ( DATEPART( NANOSECOND, GETDATE() ) % 1000 ) / 100

UPDATE dbo.tblSoTransDetailExt SET QuantityExtID = n.[NewId]
FROM dbo.tblSoTransDetailExt e
INNER JOIN
(SELECT e.SeqNum, @NewID + ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY t.[Id]) AS [NewId] FROM dbo.tblSoTransHeader h INNER JOIN dbo.tblSoTransDetailExt e ON h.transid = e.TransId
INNER JOIN tblInQtyOnHand_Ext t on e.QuantityExtID = t.Id
WHERE h.TransType IN (3, 5)) n --Backordered, Picked
ON e.SeqNum = n.SeqNum

Upon running the script against the AMI database, confirmed the ability to post the Sales Order without any error.

97c2ef5c-4a75-4b65-8f3b-46d10015e49c.title: How does rounding of 'Piece Rate' works in Individual Tracking System (ITS) works?
97c2ef5c-4a75-4b65-8f3b-46d10015e49c.content:
Problem
How does rounding in Individual Tracking System works?

Resolution
Individual Tracking System (ITS) in TRAVERSE:

The Individual Tracking System (ITS) module within TRAVERSE ERP is designed to provide 100% time tracking for organizations. It operates based on a commensurate wage payroll system and complies with the Department of Labor's (DOL) round-up requirements for wage calculations.



The ITS module supports three independent types of tracking:

-
Jobs – Tracks external customer-related tasks and work.

-
Programs – Monitors internal organization activities.

-
Funding Source/Service – Manages governmental or authorization-based funding and services.

Piece Rate Calculation in ITS:

The Individual Tracking System (ITS) in TRAVERSE ERP includes a piece rate calculation mechanism that determines workers' earnings based on the number of pieces produced and an assigned rate per piece. There is a special rounding mechanism designed for these calculations follows labor standards to ensure fair compensation.



Rounding Mechanism in ITS (Before March 2025 Service Pack Release):

Up until Traverse Build 25031, the system applied a rounding mechanism that ensured calculated piece rates did not round down unfairly. The rounding process involved adding 0.000049 to the calculated piece rate before rounding it to four decimal places.

Example Calculations:

Example 1:

-
Calculation: $6.65 ÷ 324 = 0.02052469

-
After adding 0.000049, it becomes 0.02057369

-
Rounded to four decimal places: 0.0206



Example 2:

-
Calculation: $16.10 ÷ 1213.30 = 0.0132695953185

-
After adding 0.000049, it becomes 0.0133185953185

-
Rounded to four decimal places: 0.0133



Example 3:

-
Calculation: $16.10 ÷ 111.65 = 0.1442006269592476

-
After adding 0.000049, it becomes 0.144249626959248

-
Rounded to four decimal places: 0.1442 (since the 4th decimal place isn’t affected)

This method prevented underpayment due to rounding but did not always ensure that the rounded value exceeded the original calculated rate.





Updated Rounding Mechanism (After March 2025 Service Pack Release):

Starting from March 2025 Service Pack Release, the ITS module applies a more refined rounding method. The update increases the adjustment value to 0.0000499, ensuring that the final rounded value more consistently meets or exceeds the original calculated rate.

Example Calculations (After March 2025 Update):

Example 1:

-
Calculation: $6.65 ÷ 324 = 0.02052469

-
After adding 0.0000499, it becomes 0.02057459

-
Rounded to four decimal places: 0.0206 (no change from previous rounding method)



Example 2:

-
Calculation: $16.10 ÷ 1213.30 = 0.0132695953185

-
After adding 0.0000499, it becomes 0.0133194953185

-
Rounded to four decimal places: 0.0133 (no change from previous rounding method)



Example 3:

-
Calculation: $16.10 ÷ 111.65 = 0.1442006269592476

-
After adding 0.0000499, it becomes 0.1442505269592476

-
Rounded to four decimal places: 0.1443 (now rounding up instead of staying at 0.1442)

This improvement ensures that calculations remain in compliance with Labor standards while minimizing discrepancies in wage calculations for employees paid on a piece-rate basis.





Key Benefits of the Rounding Update:

- Ensures compliance with Department of Labor regulations.
- Prevents underpayment due to rounding inconsistencies.
- Provides more precise and fair wage calculations.

573767d0-efa1-42ba-a845-9cd2f683db43.title: How to change the date of ACH file
573767d0-efa1-42ba-a845-9cd2f683db43.content:
Problem
The customer has prepared Payments and printed checks for the Default batch ##### which contains both AP Vendor of check Delivery type as Paper and electronic. When trying, to create ACH file, it is defaulting to the payment prepared date which is today's date. They would like to have the ACH file to be dated as of tomorrow so that the file will be accepted by the Bank.

How to change the date of ACH file?

Resolution
When creating an ACH file, the system uses the file creation date as the value date. This may lead to discrepancies if the desired payment date differs from the file creation date.

-
Change Workstation Date:

- Before creating the ACH file, change the workstation date from File> Date to the desired payment date.
-

-
Create and Export ACH File:

- Proceed to create and export the ACH file with the adjusted workstation date.

-
Revert Workstation Date:

- After exporting the ACH file, change the workstation date back to the current date.
- This step ensures that the workstation date is accurate for future operations.

Reason for Workaround:
The ACH file was originally designed to use the date assigned during payment preparation. This workaround addresses the issue by aligning the workstation date with the desired payment date, ensuring consistency in the ACH file.

5d03dd3a-1726-4eba-bda0-67789d26f479.title: What applications are supported to view documents within Traverse for Cloud users
5d03dd3a-1726-4eba-bda0-67789d26f479.content:
Problem
What applications are available in Saas to open Excel, PDF, and other exported reports and views?

Resolution
In the cloud environment, specific applications like Excel or custom PDF viewers are not supported. The exported documents are automatically opened using Adobe or LibreOffice because these are the default applications installed and supported on the servers in accordance with our security policies. It’s not possible to configure Traverse to open embedded documents with a different PDF reader, as applications are limited to ones that are officially supported in the cloud environment for security and compatibility reasons.

76baf5b6-5853-4464-99e7-1e3860ec9087.title: What is the need of Description Items in System Manager?
76baf5b6-5853-4464-99e7-1e3860ec9087.content:
Problem
The client would like to know the significance of the "Description Items" function in System Manager and how to create it.

Resolution
The Description Items function is used to set up items that you purchase or sell when Inventory is not installed. If Inventory is installed, you should use the Inventory Items and Item Location functions instead. However, you can later convert Description Items to Inventory Items using the IN SM Convert Items function.

Key Features:

- Description items can be selected in transactions, but quantities are not tracked.
- When using description items in other modules, you can change the unit cost and price, but these changes won't impact the cost and price entered in the Description Items setup.
- The cost and price amounts you enter are fixed as approximate values.

Information You Can Specify for Each Item:

- Item ID and Description
- Tax Class
- Unit, Unit Cost, and Unit Price
- GL Accounts: Expense, Sales, COGS, and Inventory accounts

How to Create a Description Item:

- Navigate to System Manager -> Company Setup -> Description Items
- Click the New button on the toolbar to open a blank description item record.
- Enter a new Item ID in the Item ID field.
- Enter a description of the item in the Description field. (Optional: Add additional details in the Additional Description field.)
- Select a Tax Class for the item from the Tax Class field.
- Enter the Unit of Measure in the Unit field.
- Enter the Cost per Unit in the Unit Cost field.
- Enter the Price per Unit in the Unit Price field.
- Choose the appropriate GL Expense Account, GL Sales Account, GL COGS Account, and GL Inventory Account.
- Click Save to save the new item.

How to Edit a Description Item:

- Select the description item to edit from the Item ID field.
- Make the necessary edits.
- Click Save to save the changes.

How to Delete a Description Item:

- Select the description item to delete from the Item ID field.
- Click the Delete button on the toolbar.
- Confirm by clicking Yes at the "Are you sure you want to delete selected record(s)?" prompt.

This process allows for easy management of items without inventory tracking, ensuring flexibility and control over your item setup.

3f727164-9f1a-4921-ac75-9c29996b49e0.title: How to drop an Invoice from the AP Payment Batch that had already been prepared without the need to re-preparing the Batch using "Select Payables" program.
3f727164-9f1a-4921-ac75-9c29996b49e0.content:
Problem
How can an Invoice from the AP Payment Batch that had already been prepared be dropped or removed without the need to re-preparing the Batch using "Select Payables" program?

Resolution
In the Accounts Payable module, the following functions help in reviewing and managing payments before printing checks.

1. Edit Register Function

- The Edit Register function is used to review the details of prepared payment batches before proceeding with check printing.
- It allows users to verify payment amounts, vendor details, and payment methods to ensure accuracy before finalizing transactions.
- Any discrepancies or incorrect entries noted on this report can be corrected at this stage to avoid processing errors.

2. Select Payables Function

- The Select Payables function enables users to filter and review payments based on batch codes and vendor IDs.
- Invoices that need to be removed from the Payment Batch can be dropped using the Drop function.
- This function is useful for confirming that the correct invoices are selected for payment.
- Users can refine their selection criteria to ensure only the intended payments are included in the batch.

3. Drop Check Option

- The Drop check box allows users to remove specific invoices from the prepared payments list before finalizing the batch.
- When an invoice is marked as “Drop,” it is returned to the Open Invoices section, meaning it will not be included in the current payment run.
- This function is helpful if certain payments need to be deferred or re-evaluated before processing.

Here is how you can use these three features and functions to review a batch of payments and then remove any invoices that should not be included in the batch.

- Prepare the batch of payments as normal.
- Run the "Edit Register" to see a list of all invoices that are included in the newly created Payment Batch.
- Make a note of any invoices that should be removed from the batch along with their vendor.
- Open the Select Payables Screen.
- Choose the Batch ID and the Vendor ID for any invoice you want to remove.  After choosing this the screen will list all invoices in the payment batch for this vendor.
- For any invoices you wish to remove from the batch click the "Drop" checkbox on the right side of the screen.
- Once you have chosen all the invoices for this vendor to drop click the "Write" button on the top left hand side of the screen to removed them from the batch.
- Repeat this process for any other invoices and vendors which need to be removed from the batch.
- Once this process is complete, re-run the Edit Register to confirm that the list of invoices to be paid in the batch is correct, and then either run the Select Payables program to drop more invoices or proceed with the rest of the Check Printing process.

99a3d5c1-2b03-4702-ab9c-71c3476a4745.title: How to add Finance Charge in a Customer View
99a3d5c1-2b03-4702-ab9c-71c3476a4745.content:
Problem
Client would like to see whether the Finance Charge is enabled for a customer.

Resolution
The default setup in Design Studio for the Customer View reads in the data for the "Finance Charge" checkbox as part of the script in the Data Source, but it does not include it in the Available Fields column.  Therefore it is not initially available as a column in the interactive view.  Adding the column name in the Available column in Design Studio makes this column appear in the Interactive View.



Launch the Traverse Design Studio Application.

Navigate to Views Table -> Select Customer -> Click on Customize.

In the Available section, go to the end of the list and add the entry CalcFinch.  Note that case is significant here.  You have to type this field in exactly.  Once you have added this field you can click OK in the top left of the Custom View Editor to save the customization.

That will add a column called "Finance Charge" in Customer View, and it can be pulled and added to the view using the column chooser.

Add the Finance Charge.

And the view is ready now.

e9ae9b00-2a5f-4cd6-9ab4-963bd432c0ee.title: Quick access and defaults folder are not available while trying to save reports
e9ae9b00-2a5f-4cd6-9ab4-963bd432c0ee.content:
Problem
The client reports that they no longer have quick access or the default folder available in their file explorer/libraries and are unable to save the report to the desired location.

Resolution
The hidden navigation pane causes Quick Access and folders to suddenly disappear when saving reports in Traverse.

- To resolve this, unhide the navigation pane by clicking on Organize in the dialog box.

- Next, select Layout and expand it.
- Check the option for Navigation Pane by clicking on it.

- Once done, Quick Access and the navigation paths will become visible again.









To unhide the navigation panel in File Explorer on Windows, follow these steps:

Unhiding the Navigation Pane in File Explorer:

- Open File Explorer:
- Press Windows + E to open File Explorer, or click the File Explorer icon on your taskbar.
- Enable the Navigation Pane:
- In the top menu of File Explorer, click on the View tab.
- In the Layout section, look for Navigation Pane.
- Ensure that Navigation Pane is checked. If it isn't, click on it to enable it.

- If the Navigation Pane is Collapsed:
- If the panel is collapsed, you can expand it by clicking the small arrow or icon in the upper-left corner of the File Explorer window (next to the "Folders" label).
- Restore Default View:
- If the navigation panel is still hidden or there are issues with the view, you can reset File Explorer's view settings:
- Click on the View tab.
- Select Options, then choose Change folder and search options.
- In the Folder Options window, go to the View tab.

- Click on Restore Defaults at the bottom.
- Apply the changes and click OK.

This method ensures that the system's default settings are restored.

334aa130-d195-4771-af1a-321d1be6c505.title: Locking and Unlocking a Batch in IN Freeze Quantities
334aa130-d195-4771-af1a-321d1be6c505.content:
Problem
Locking and Unlocking a Batch in IN Freeze Quantities

Resolution
Locking a batch in IN Freeze Quantities ensures that only the user who locked the batch can enter the counts. If the batch is not locked, multiple users can simultaneously enter counts.

Steps to Lock a Batch:

- Navigate to the Batch: Locate the batch you want to lock within the IN Freeze Quantities module.
- Click the Lock button: This action will add the Lock Date and Time, along with the name of the user who locked the batch.
- Save your changes: After clicking the Lock button, make sure to save the changes to apply the lock.

Steps to Unlock a Batch:

- Navigate to the Locked Batch: Find the batch that is currently locked.
- Click the Lock button again: Clicking the Lock button will remove the Lock Date and Time, as well as the Lock By name.
- Save your changes: Ensure you save the changes to unlock the batch and allow other users to enter counts.

By following these steps, you can effectively manage batch locking and unlocking in IN Freeze Quantities.

2cf8c223-391a-4cfc-a1d5-354b9237dc01.title: How to install DocUnity on a Client workstation?
2cf8c223-391a-4cfc-a1d5-354b9237dc01.content:
Problem
How to install DocUnity on a Client workstation?

Resolution
Pre-Installation Checklist:

i. Ensure SQL Server Availability:

-  DocUnity requires Microsoft SQL Standard or Express Edition 2012 to 2016.
- Confirm access to the SQL server name and credentials (System Admin 'sa' Login and Password).

ii. Admin Privileges:

-  Log in to the system with Administrator privileges to ensure sufficient network permissions for the installation.

iii. Installation Files

- Have the DocUnity installer(installdocunity.XXXX) program file (appropriate for the version being installed).
- Ensure that the program can be run from a network share for client workstation installations.



Installation Steps:

Step 1: Run the DocUnity Setup Program:

i. Launch the DocUnity Setup program by right-clicking and selecting Run as Administrator.



ii. when prompted, enter the following information:

-
Installer Name: File name of the DocUnity installer program.

-
SQL Server Name: Enter the name of the SQL Server (e.g., ServerName\InstanceName).

-
Database Name: Typically DocUnity_DB.

-
Trusted Connection: Select this option if using a trusted connection instead of a network login and password.

-
Network Login: Enter the SQL Server login (e.g., sa or another login with admin privileges).

-
Network Password: Password for the above login.

NOTE: Ensure the information entered is accurate, as it will be used the first time a user launches DocUnity.

iii. Click OK to save the configuration into the settings.txt file.

iv. Click Install to begin the installation with the entered configuration.



Step 2: Installation and License Agreement:

i. Once clicked on 'Install', the following screen appears and click on 'Next' to proceed:

ii. Read and agree to the DocUnity Software License Agreement.



Step 3: Choose Installation Type:

i. Select the 32-bit or 64-bit version to match your system’s architecture.

ii. Specify the installation directory. The default directory is typically: C:\Program Files\DocUnity.

iii. Click Install to continue. Once installed, the below screen appears:

Step 4: ODBC Driver Installation: [If the Drivers are already updates, we might not get this prompt]

i. During the installation process, you may be prompted to install Microsoft Native SQL ODBC drivers (v11 or higher).

ii. Click Yes to proceed with the driver installation.

Step 5: Complete the Installation:

i. Once the installation is complete, launch DocUnity from the desktop icon.

ii. Right-click the desktop icon and select Run as Administrator, to launch 'DocUnity'

Step 6: Database Connection Setup:

i. Kindly follow the below steps to connect to the DocUnity database:

-
- Go to Setup Connection (upper-right corner on the DocUnity Home Window).
- Select Connection Setup.

-
- Enter the connection string information for your DocUnity system and click Connect.

ii. If the DocUnity connects successfully, and the DocUnity Home Window will be displayed.

38256bec-cb2e-412e-af6f-61ff1169005d.title: Reversing Project Costing Time Ticket entry that has already Been Posted
38256bec-cb2e-412e-af6f-61ff1169005d.content:
Problem
Customer have posted time ticket entry that should be under Rate ID 165 but has been posted under Rate ID 195. How to reverse the posted Time Ticket entry?

Resolution
Navigate to Project Costing> Transactions> Time Ticket Entry

Make a new line entry for the same Employee ID and fill in the date, Fiscal Year, Fiscal Period, Description, Project/Task and Rate code as 195, set the Hours as negative. i.e In this case it is -5 and Save.

Navigate to Project Costing> Transactions> Post Transaction

Select the appropriate Batch code.

Select Do the Following, and select Post Time Tickets and hit Ok

Now create the correct Time ticket entry from Project Costing> Transactions> Time Ticket Entry.

Make a new line entry for the same Employee ID and fill in the date, Fiscal Year, Fiscal Period, Description, Project/Task, Hours and Rate code as 165 Save.

Post the same by navigating to Project Costing> Transactions> Post Transaction.
You can confirm it from Project Costing> Interactive views> Activities View

b430406c-5790-4db0-a2bc-bc6d0ff9208f.title: How to update the 'Revision Number' for a Subassembly in a Bill of Material?
b430406c-5790-4db0-a2bc-bc6d0ff9208f.content:
Problem
How do you update the 'Revision Number' for a Subassembly in a MFG Bill of Material?

Resolution
To update the 'BOM Revision Number' for a subassembly, please follow the detailed steps below:

i. Navigate to the Bills of Materials Screen:

Access the Bills of Materials screen by navigating through the following path: Applications → MFG-Bills of Materials → Setup and Maintenance → Bills of Materials.



ii. Locate the Required Assembly ID:

In the Bills of Materials screen, retrieve the Assembly ID for which the subassembly details need to be updated. This can be done by selecting the appropriate Assembly ID from the lookups.



iii. Find the Component or Subassembly:

Once the required Assembly ID is loaded, locate the specific Component/Subassembly for which the 'BOM Revision Number' needs to be updated.

[NOTE: If the 'BOM Rev No.' field is not visible in the current view, use the Column Chooser feature to add it to the display. The 'Column Chooser' allows you to customize the fields visible on the screen.]



iv. Update the Revision Number:
a. Click on the existing value in the 'BOM Rev No.' field for the selected Component/Subassembly.
b. A drop-down menu will appear, listing all available Revision Numbers for that specific Subassembly. (This field is only applicable for components which are non-stocked subassemblies and is a required field for those subassemblies.)
c. Select the desired Revision Number from the drop-down list.



v. Save the Changes:

Once the required Revision Number has been updated, click on the 'Save' icon located at the top-left corner of the screen to ensure the changes are updated.

NOTE:

- It is essential to verify that the selected Revision Number is accurate before saving the changes, as it directly impacts the BOM structure.
- If the Revision Number drop-down does not show the expected values, confirm that the Subassembly has valid revisions defined.

50be3aab-bd6d-4015-9c8c-eef4701d1db8.title: How to Utilize Varying Source Codes for Manual GL Transactions?
50be3aab-bd6d-4015-9c8c-eef4701d1db8.content:
Problem
How to utilize varying Source Codes in General Ledger to have distinct 'Source Codes' for manual GL entries.

Resolution
Each transaction is assigned a two-character source code that identifies the origin or purpose of the transaction. Most of these codes are automatically input by Traverse to indicate the module in which the transaction originated and cannot be edited. However, manual entries made in the General Ledger can have unique source codes. Using varying source code for manual entries can allow a user to categorize transactions and select specific types of entries for display in the GL Journal and GL Activity Report.

Source Code for GL Transactions:

- The default source code for entries made using the Transactions function is M1.
- The first character of the source code, M, indicates that the transaction is a manual entry.

Customizing Source Codes:

There is no setup screen to have them set up, but we can start utilizing them by manually entering them in the GL Transactions screen under the path: Applications -> General Ledger -> Transactions -> Transactions:



We can customize the second character of the source code to further differentiate or categorize entries. This second character can be changed to any:

- Number (0–9), or
- Letter (A–Z).

For example:

- The source code M0 could represent a specific category of manual entries, while MA or MZ could represent others.
- This provides 36 possible combinations (M followed by 0, 1, 2, 3...9, or A, B...Z).

NOTE: The first character must always remain M to indicate a manual entry.



Auto-Reversing Transactions:

For auto-reversing accrual transactions, the source code R1 is used. This source code allows the transaction to reverse automatically in the next period.



NOTES:

- The two-character source code serves as a critical identifier for organizing and reporting on transactions.
- We can customize the second character to create unique categories for manual transactions while adhering to the required format for source codes, with the first character being 'M'
- Auto-reversing entries have a dedicated source code (R1) to streamline the reversal process.



By utilizing source codes effectively, we can ensure better transaction tracking, reporting, and overall management of entries within the system.

23e40787-45cb-4c74-9980-44929e6ae4e8.title: Resolving an Object Reference error when printing a Variance Report
23e40787-45cb-4c74-9980-44929e6ae4e8.content:
Problem
When trying to print a Variance Report, the user is getting an object reference error. The issue of encountering an "Object Reference" error when printing a Variance Report was identified to be caused by a deleted Physical Inventory batch that was still appearing in the IN Variance Report screen.

Resolution
The resolution involved addressing this discrepancy in the database tables which requires accessing the SQL tables on the server.

Locate which batch is causing the problem. Compare the list of batches in the Variance Report screen and find the one that is not in the Freeze Quantities batch list. (There is no missing batch in the screenshots below, but this is where you would see which batch is missing.)



Once logged in to the SQL server in the SQL tables:

Input the missing batch that shows on the Variance Report batch screen (e.g., "INV") into the tblInPhysCountBatch table into a new row.

Complete the necessary fields to finish creating the batch in the Freeze Quantities screen within Traverse.

Save the changes in Traverse.
Identify and remove any locks on the batch that may be causing the issue.

Once the missing batch has been successfully recreated, delete the problematic batch.
Verify that the Physical Variance Report runs successfully after these changes.

3f265b79-579e-47a6-b3d5-7400687b405d.title: ACH Payment Processing in Traverse: Setup and Workflow Guide
3f265b79-579e-47a6-b3d5-7400687b405d.content:
Problem
ACH Payment Processing in Traverse: Setup and Workflow Guide

Resolution
ACH File in Traverse



For a Vendor to make use of the ‘ACH File’ setup in Traverse, they need to have the ‘Banking’ module purchased in their License.



I. Setting Up a Vendor for ACH Payments in Traverse:

To enable ACH payments for a vendor in Traverse, follow the steps outlined below:

i. Navigating to Vendor Setup:

- Go to Accounts Payable > Setup and Maintenance > Vendors
- Locate and select the vendor for whom ACH payments need to be configured.

ii. Configuring ACH Payment Details:

- Navigate to the Pay To tab.
- In the Check Delivery field, select Electronic to designate the vendor for ACH payments instead of paper checks. [This option to set the ‘Check Delivery’ type to ‘Electronic’ is possible only when the ‘Banking’ module is purchased in the License]

- In the Account No field, enter the bank account number where ACH payments should be deposited.
- In the Routing No field, enter the corresponding routing number associated with the vendor’s bank account.
- In the Account Type field, select the appropriate account type: Checking or Savings.

iii. Configuring Electronic Document Delivery for Payment Vouchers:

- If required, configure the vendor to receive payment vouchers via electronic document delivery.

iv. Saving the Configuration:

- Once all necessary details have been entered, click Save to update the Vendor record with the ACH payment setup.

This ensures that the selected vendor is properly configured to receive payments electronically via ACH.





II. Setting up Layout for ACH File based on the Bank’s Requirements:

i. Go to System Manager > Company Setup > Export Layout Definition

ii. Select the existing Layout that can be used for ACH transactions.

-
- In case the existing Layouts do not meet the requirements, create a new one from the scratch, meeting the Bank’s requirement.



Steps to Create a New Export Layout Definition:

NOTE: The requirements for the ACH File will be provided by the Bank

- Open Export Layout Definition
- Navigate to: Applications > System Manager > Company Setup > Export Layout Definition
- Click the New Record button.
- Enter Layout Details
- Layout ID: Provide a unique ID.
- Function ID: Select the type of export (ACH, POSPAY, etc.).
- Copy From: Optionally, copy settings from an existing layout.
- Description: Enter a brief description of the layout.
- Configure File Structure
- File Type: Select one of the following:
- Delimited: Choose a field separator (Comma, Tab, Space, or None).
- Fixed Width: Fields will be a fixed length.
- XML: Define header and footer tags.
- Block: Specify a blocking factor and fill character.
- Row Separator: Choose from CR, CRLF, LF, or None.
- Text Qualifier: Choose None, Quote (") or Apostrophe (').
- File Name: Enter or browse for the output file location.
- Select Assembly and Class
- Assembly: Select the integration engine-enabled assembly.
- Class: Choose an export class relevant to your function.
- Define Record Types
- Block: Fills remaining records with a specified fill character.
- Detail: Holds the majority of export information.
- Footer: Groups and summarizes totals.
- Header: Organizes and sorts records into groups.
- Group Value: Defines sorting and grouping for headers and footers.
- Setup Field Details
- Click the + button next to a record sequence to expand the field list.
- Sequence: Define the order of fields in the output.
- Description: Name the field.
- Field Value: Select the data source.
- Field Type: Choose from Text, Number, or DateTime.
- Multiplier: Define a multiplier for number formatting.
- Format: Choose number or date formats.
- Fill Justify: Left or Right alignment.
- Fill Length: Specify character length for block files.
- Fill Character: Used to pad empty spaces in block files.
- Header/Footer Tags: Define XML tags.
- Extended Field Translation: Translate values as needed.
- Apply Special Functions (Optional)
- Use predefined functions such as:
- SUM(value1) – Summation
- AVG(value1) – Average
- COUNT(value1) – Count records
- LEN(value1) – Get field length
- ISNULL(value1, value2) – Substitute when null
- TRIM(value1) – Remove extra spaces
- Save and Finalize
- Click the Save button on the toolbar to store your settings.
- Ensure values in separators and qualifiers meet file format requirements



III. Configuring Bank Account Setup for ACH Payments in Traverse:

To facilitate ACH payments, the bank account must be set up correctly within Traverse. Follow the detailed steps below to configure ACH settings for a bank account:

i. Navigating to Bank Account Setup:

- Go to System Manager > Company Setup > Bank Accounts
- Select the bank account that will be used for ACH transactions.

ii. Configuring ACH Payment Settings:

- Navigate to the ACH tab.
- Choose the specific information that needs to be included in the ACH file sent to the bank.
- Note: The bank can provide guidance on the correct selections based on their ACH processing requirements.
- Select the Default AP File Format from the available options:
- ADV (Advice of Credit)
- CCD (Cash Concentration and Disbursement)
- PPD (Prearranged Payment and Deposit)

iii. Defining File Naming and Storage Preferences:

- In the Default File Name/Prefix field, specify how the ACH file names should be structured:
- Using "?" will append the Application ID to the file name.
- Using "*" will append the date and time to the file name.

- Select the Default Folder where ACH files should be saved upon generation.
- The Sample File field will display an example of the file path and file naming format based on the selected settings.

iv. Configuring Security Settings (If Required by the Bank):

- If the bank requires a security code to be included at the beginning of the ACH file, enter the Security Code in the designated field.
- In the Pad Security Code to a Length of field, specify the required length for the security code if padding is necessary.

v. Saving the Configuration:

- Once all details have been entered and verified, click Save to update the bank account record with the ACH payment setup.
- This configuration ensures that ACH payments are processed correctly based on the bank’s requirements.









Once all these setups are in place, the User will need to follow the cycle below:



I. Creating and posting an AP Transaction:

- Navigate to Accounts Payable > Transactions > Transactions
- Create a new Accounts Payable transaction for the vendor whose 'Check Delivery' was set to 'Electronic'.
- Add the Line Items as needed and proceed with printing the ‘Purchase Journal’

- Now, we can post the Transactions under ‘AP Post Transactions’ screen



II. Payment Processing and Posting:

i. Navigate to ‘AP Hold/Release Invoices’ screen under the path: Accounts Payable > Pay Invoices > Hold/Release Invoices.
The User need to review and ensure that this ‘Invoice’ created is in ‘Released’ status.

ii. Go to ‘Prepare Payments’ screen under the path: Accounts Payable > Pay Invoices > Prepare Payments. Prepare the Payments by entering appropriate details in the ‘AP Prepare Payments’ screen

iii. Payment Vouchers:
Navigate to ‘Payment Vouchers’ screen under the path: Accounts Payable > Pay Invoices > Payment Vouchers:

NOTE: As we have enabled ‘Document Delivery’ such that the ‘Email’ will be sent to the ‘Vendors’, they will be getting a soft copy of the ‘Voucher’ to the designated Email address via email.



- Choose the appropriate Batch Code for the payment processing.

- Verify the starting voucher number to ensure correct numbering before proceeding.
- Preview Vouchers (Optional): Click Preview Vouchers to review the details before printing.

NOTE: Vouchers in the preview will not have an assigned voucher number until they are printed.

Important: Do not print from the ‘Preview’ screen, as this will not generate valid voucher numbers.

- Once reviewed, proceed with printing the vouchers to generate the official voucher numbers.





iv. Create ACH File:
Navigate to ‘Print Vouchers’ screen under the path: Accounts Payable > Pay Invoices > Create ACH File:

Steps to Generate an ACH File:

a. Apply Filters (Optional):

-
- A top-level filter can be applied to generate an ACH file for specific vendors as needed.

b. Select the Batch Code:

-
- Choose the appropriate Batch Code that contains the vouchers to be processed for ACH payments.

c. Review Pre-Populated Payment Details:

-
-
- The following details will automatically populate based on the information selected in the Prepare Payments screen:
- Invoices Due
- Discounts Due
- Payment Date
- Fiscal Period/Year
- Bank Account ID

d. Batch Number Assignment:

-
-
-
-
- If multiple ACH files are generated on the same day, the batch number will increment accordingly to maintain unique identification.

e. Verify File Format, File Name, and Save Location:

-
- These settings will default based on the Bank Account setup but can be modified if necessary:
- File Format (e.g., ADV, CCD, PPD)
- File Name (Automatically assigned but can be changed)
- Save to Folder (Defines the storage location for the ACH file)

f. Review the File Creation Path:

-
- The Create File field displays the full file path and name of the ACH file that will be generated.

g. Enter Comments (Optional):

-
- Additional notes related to the ACH file can be entered in the Comments field for reference.

Output ACH File:

[NOTE: The content of the ACH File can be adjusted once the Bank requirements are available]



v. Print Payment Register:
The Payment Register provides a summary of the payments before posting.

Navigate to ‘Payment Register’ screen under the path: Accounts Payable > Pay Invoices > Payment Register:

Note: This register is only available before the payments are posted, so it is recommended to review or print it beforehand.



vi. Post Payments:



Navigate to ‘Payment Register’ screen under the path: Accounts Payable > Pay Invoices > Post Payments: Once all details are confirmed, proceed with posting the payments to finalize the process.

0f035b8a-dcdf-48ee-b619-5af4cd45f4f2.title: Editing Invoices Included in the 1099 Processing
0f035b8a-dcdf-48ee-b619-5af4cd45f4f2.content:
Problem
When generating the 1099s for a given year, certain Invoices are not being listed under the AP 1099 Processing screen to output the 1099. Other invoices are included that should not be on the 1099. How do you edit the list of Invoices included in the 1099?

Resolution
- Navigate to Accounts Payable> Periodic processing> Manage 1099 Invoices

- The Manage 1099 Invoices function allows you to edit 1099 flags and amounts for 1099 Vendors' individually paid invoices. The screen will display the invoices and payments that have been posted for the Vendors that have been set up as 1099 Vendors.
- Select the range of Filter Criteria to manage 1099 invoices. Leave the filter criteria blank to include all records.
- Select the Calendar Year for which you want to manage invoices.
- Click Apply Filter to display the invoices for 1099 Vendors that meet your filtering criteria.
- Select the record to add the invoice to the amount to include in the 1099, and click the Select button, or select the Clear button to exclude the invoice from the amount to include in the 1099. Alternatively, you can check or uncheck the box in the "Current 1099 Invoice" column. (The Original 1099 Invoice column is not editable).
- If the Invoice amount that applies to the 1099 needs to be edited, this can be edited in the 1099 Amount column.
- Click "Ok" to save the changes.

- Upon making the changes in AP Manage 1099 Invoices screen, navigate to Accounts Payable> Periodic processing> 1099 Processing
- Hit Generate again and you will see the changes reflected in the updated 1099.

bbe3551f-508b-4d72-9b45-0b48a575a5bc.title: How to Use the Copy Recurring Entries Function in Accounts Payable
bbe3551f-508b-4d72-9b45-0b48a575a5bc.content:
Problem
How to Use the Copy Recurring Entries Function in AP

Resolution
-
Navigate to Accounts Payable > Transactions > Copy Recurring Entries.

-
Select the range of run codes you want to copy using the Run Code From and Run Code Thru fields.

-
If you leave these fields blank, it will copy all existing run codes.

-
In the Fiscal Period / Year fields, choose the fiscal period and year for the entries.

-
In the Cutoff Date field, select a date that will set the limit for copying recurring entries. Entries with a cutoff date before this date will not be copied.

-
You can enter a Due By Date to copy only entries due by that date.

-
If batch processing is enabled, select the appropriate Batch Code for the entries.

-
Click the Exchange Rate button to select the exchange rate for alternate currency calculations, if necessary.

-
Use the Comments field to add any relevant notes about the recurring entries you're copying.

-
Click OK to begin copying the entries, Activity to view activity logs, or Reset to clear all fields and return to default values.

c464c321-0f20-43e1-a137-95966deb8aee.title: Print out only new revision in Bills Of Material
c464c321-0f20-43e1-a137-95966deb8aee.content:
Problem
Customer would like to see the current revision printing from “COSTED BILL OF MATERIALS”. they don't want the old revisions to be printed in it.

Resolution

52ab7f3c-98e7-4c16-bcaf-b72806c2ae34.title: Why does GL Activity Report for Retained Earnings Account does not show accurate numbers when run across Years?
52ab7f3c-98e7-4c16-bcaf-b72806c2ae34.content:
Problem
When the GL Activity Report is run across the Years [For example, Year 2021 Period 1 to Year 2025 Period 13], the report shows the same Balance of 2021 for all the ending Balances till Period 13 of 2025. When the Report was run for individual Years, the Balance numbers are different.

Resolution
Clients may observe discrepancies when running the GL Activity Report across multiple years, particularly in relation to the Retained Earnings Account. A key concern is that the opening balance for a new year does not match the prior year's ending balance, which may cause confusion regarding the accuracy of the report.



Understanding the GL Activity Report:

The GL Activity Report calculates balances based on recorded transactions within the system. However, year-end adjustments to the Opening Balance are not recorded as transactions; instead, they are system-driven updates that are not included in the report’s calculations. This results in the following behavior:

- The report begins with an opening balance for the first year selected in the range.
- Ending balances are calculated by accumulating the activity recorded for the account.
- Since the year-end adjustment is not a transaction, the report does not reflect the actual transition of balances from one year to the next.
- As a result, running the Activity Report across multiple years may show the same number across different years, leading to potential confusion.



To ensure accuracy in the ending balances of the Retained Earnings Account, it is recommended that clients run the GL Activity Report separately for each year rather than spanning multiple years. This will ensure that the correct balances are displayed for each specific fiscal period.



NOTE:

The observed behavior in the GL Activity Report is not an error but rather an expected outcome based on how the report calculates balances. So, in order to overcome this limitation, we need to adjust the reporting approach accordingly.

By running the report year by year, we can ensure the accuracy of the Retained Earnings Account balances and maintain a clear financial overview.

b402c424-7fc7-46c4-9828-2f2ed41c8c9e.title: How to setup new AR Recurring Entry
b402c424-7fc7-46c4-9828-2f2ed41c8c9e.content:
Problem
How to enter/ Setup new AR Recurring Entry

Resolution
Navigate to Accounts Receivable > Setup and Maintenance > Recurring Entry

NOTE: AR Recurring Entries are a mirror to SO Recurring Entry – a change or new record in one will result in a change in the other.

Click on New Record
Create an 8 character “Recur ID” and a 6 character “Run Code” to indicate the batch/grouping this transaction will be copied over with.

(Use the same run codes for entries you copy on the same basis. For example, you could use "01" for entries that you copy on the first day of each month or "15" for entries that you copy on the fifteenth day of each month, and so on.)

Setup the recurring type as invoice, credit memo, or open order (SO)

Follow instructions for creating a normal AR transaction

Use the “Billing” tab to setup the billing type as monthly, days, quarterly, yearly, or as needed.

Enter the Starting Date as the date of the first invoice for the entry.

Enter the Cutoff Date as the date after which you no longer want to create invoices for the recurring entry. If creating an open ended recurring entry, this can be left blank.

If using days, define a “Billing Interval” in number of days to indicate the number of days you want between billing cycles.

Assign a cutoff date for the recurring transaction

Select a “Payment Method ID”

Use the “History” tab to follow the copy history for the recurring entry.

Save Record

Navigate to Accounts Receivable > Transactions > Copy Recurring Entries

Select a “From” and “Thru” Run Code

Select fiscal period/year, cutoff date, due by date, and AR transaction Batch code, Deposit ID, and Currency ID.

Click OK

NOTE: A transaction that has already been copied and set to a specific billing type will give you a warning message.

Follow usual procedures to print the journal and post the transactions.

bb68adb7-3453-45db-9cd8-2864d20b9626.title: Setting up Finance Charge
bb68adb7-3453-45db-9cd8-2864d20b9626.content:
Problem
How to Set up Finance Charges

Resolution
Set up a revenue account in the General Ledger Chart of Accounts that will be used for finance charges and add this account to your Accounts Receivable business rules:

Go to System Manager > Company Setup > Business Rules > AR

For the Finance Charge Account, select the General Ledger Account set up for this purpose to use.

- Define the Finance Charge Date as either the Invoice Date or the Due Date.  (To start calculating the finance charges from the date the invoice is generated, select "Invoice Date". To start calculating finance charges from the date the invoice is due, select "Due Date".)
- Enter the Finance Charge Days to use. (When you calculate finance charges there is a "Statement Date" field on the screen. This date and the "Finance Charge Days" will be used to calculate the date put into the field "Finance Charges Will Be Calculated For Items Dated Before." Any open unpaid invoice for customers that have the finance charges box checked prior to this date will have a finance charge calculated.)
- Enter a Minimum Finance Charge amount. (This amount will be used if the calculated finance charge is not greater than this amount.)
- Enter a Finance Charge Percentage. (This is the finance charge percent you want to use each time you calculate finance charges. Enter the percentage as a whole number. For example to use 1.5%, enter 1.5.)



Go to Accounts Receivable > Open Invoices > Calculate Finance Charges.

Use the filter to calculate finance charges only on specific customers or leave blank to include all customers

Review activity log of finance charges and remove from customer accounts (if applicable) prior to periodic processing. Note: New finance charges can be removed until the Periodic Processing is run.





Go to: Accounts Receivable >Periodic Processing > Periodic Maintenance

Perform Periodic Maintenance to make the GL posting for finance charges.

Check only the box labeled “Perform General Periodic Process” process the finance charges and clean up the accounts.

This process moves the finance charges from “New Finance Charges” to “Unpaid Finance Charges” - Credits your GL account set up for Finance Charges and Debits your Accounts Receivable GL account for that customer.

Finance Charges can be paid via a cash receipt with the invoice number defined in AR business rules.

1eb5b43c-26c0-4af0-875f-c87f71fad400.title: AP and PO TransID duplication
1eb5b43c-26c0-4af0-875f-c87f71fad400.content:
Problem
In a client's database, both the Accounts Payable (AP) and Purchase Order (PO) modules are generating the same transaction ID (TransID) number sequences, instead of producing unique, combined sequences for both modules. This issue is causing inconsistencies in tracking and referencing transactions across the system.

How can this be corrected?

Resolution
We identified that setting the same transaction numbers for both the Purchase Order (PO) and Accounts Payable (AP) modules in the Traverse UI setup could cause confusion. To resolve this, Traverse provides an option to configure unique transaction number sequences.

To prevent overlap, follow these steps:

- Navigate to System Manager -> Company Setup -> Transaction Numbers.
- In this section, the Function ID represents the specific function (such as POTRANS for Purchase Orders and APTRANS for Accounts Payable), and the Next ID indicates the transaction ID associated with each function.
- Assign different transaction number sequences to POTRANS and APTRANS to ensure the transaction IDs for each module are distinct.
- For future-proofing, we recommend starting the transaction numbers with separate series, with at least 100,000 digits apart, to avoid any potential overlap down the line.

This solution will ensure that the transaction IDs for AP and PO remain unique and distinct, preventing any confusion as transactions are processed.

45fea6ce-88b4-4ebf-98bf-f34612e43e17.title: How to avoid the split of Columns in the Positive Pay file due to the presence of Field separator within the Field vales (For example: Comma)?
45fea6ce-88b4-4ebf-98bf-f34612e43e17.content:
Problem
How to avoid the split of Columns in the Positive Pay file due to the presence of Field separator within the Field vales (For example: Comma)?



The existing Export Layout Definition looks as follows:



The AP Vendors screen looks as follows:



The Output file is splitting the 'Payee name' (Vendor Name) into 3 cells due to the presence of commas in between the words:

Resolution
When working with delimited files in Traverse, a common issue arises when a comma (',') is used as both:

- The field separator in the file format.
- The thousands separator in numeric values or within text fields such as Vendor Names.

If a comma is present within a field (e.g., inside a number or a vendor name), Traverse interprets it as a field separator, leading to incorrect data parsing. This results in data shifting, where values are moved into unintended fields, causing misalignment in the imported records.



Impact on Data Parsing:

When a delimited file contains commas within values, Traverse incorrectly splits the field into multiple parts based on the number of commas. This misalignment affects data integrity and may result in:

- Incorrect numerical values due to unexpected splitting.
- Vendor names appearing incomplete or spread across multiple fields.
- Fields shifting, leading to data being assigned to the wrong columns.



Original Data (Correct Format): "ABC Industries", Inc., 123,456.78, USA

How Traverse Interprets It (Incorrect Format): ABC Industries | Inc. | 123 | 456.78 | USA



Under this case, we would need to set up the Text Qualifiers as either 'Quote' or 'Apostrophe' in the Export layout Definition. [NOTE: This is needed, only when we have the values in our records that contain our field separator.]



To prevent data misalignment when dealing with comma-separated files, the Text Qualifier should be set to either:

- Double Quotes (")
- Apostrophe (')

This configuration ensures that any value enclosed in the qualifier is treated as a single field, even if it contains commas.

Steps to Configure Text Qualifiers in Traverse:

i. Navigate to the SM Export Layout Definition under the path: Applications -> System Manager -> Company Setup -> Export Layout Definition:

ii. Locate the option for Text Qualifiers.

iii. Set the qualifier to either " (Quote) or ' (Apostrophe).

iv. Save the changes and reprocess the export.



The Output file now looks as follows:

ac1ecf56-a4b3-42ce-b20f-b85819af0cfe.title: File in use error (OSAS)
ac1ecf56-a4b3-42ce-b20f-b85819af0cfe.content:
Problem
The client is experiencing an error message indicating that a file is in use.

Resolution
To resolve the 'file in use' error message, you can follow these steps:

- Identify the Process: Check if there are any processes running for the user associated with the error. This can be done through the Enterprise Manager (EM).
- Terminate Processes: If you find any processes that are still running for a user who is no longer active, terminate those processes.
- Clear Control Files: Clear the control file to remove any locks that may be causing the issue.
- Stop/Start BBj Services: If the issue persists, you may need to run a stop/start on BBj services. This action can help release any locked files.



Retry the Action: After performing the above steps, try to perform the action that was previously resulting in the 'file in use' error again.

866255fe-45de-4dc6-ac09-fe123797332f.title: Vacation Accrual Issues for Employees (OSAS)
866255fe-45de-4dc6-ac09-fe123797332f.content:
Problem
The customer reported an issue where two full-time employees, set up with an accrual code of 04 for sick and vacation, were not accruing any time.

Resolution
Solution Overview: The issue involved two full-time employees who were set up with an accrual code of 04 for sick and vacation time, but were not accruing any time. The problem was identified as an incorrect table definition for the accrual code, which was set to apply only to employees under 1 year of service.

Step-by-Step Instructions:

- Review the table definition for the accrual code 04.
- Check the "years up to" column in the table definition.

- If the definition is set to apply only to employees under 1 year, modify it:
- Add another line to extend the range.
- Alternatively, change the "1" to "99" to cover employees with longer service durations.

- Test the changes to ensure that the accruals are now being calculated correctly.

Important Notes:

3ed96d5d-89a0-4044-8119-5c87480408ba.title: GL Edit Transactions: Features, Limitations, and Best Practices
3ed96d5d-89a0-4044-8119-5c87480408ba.content:
Problem
Understanding GL Edit Transactions: Key Features, Limitations, and Best Practices for Managing Unposted and Posted Entries in General ledger

Resolution
The GL Edit Transactions screen will be available under the path: Applications -> General Ledger -> Transactions -> Edit Transactions:



We can use the GL Edit Transactions function to modify unposted transactions that have been recorded in the GL Journal. Once the GL Transactions are written to the Journal, it will be available in the GL Edit Transactions screen.



The Key features of the GL Edit Transactions screen are as follows:

i.  This function applies only to transactions within the current Fiscal year.

If the User prefers to edit a Transaction from a different Fiscal Period, the user need to switch the GL Fiscal Year to that Year and proceed with the same in the GL Change Fiscal Year function. [The GL Change Fiscal Year function can be found under the path: Applications -> General Ledger -> Periodic Processing -> Change Fiscal Year]. The entries corresponding to a different 'GL Fiscal year' will not be available in this screen, by default.



ii. There are some limitations within the fields that are available for editing. We cannot change the 'Year' corresponding to the GL Entries, as they default from the 'GL Fiscal Year', set up in Traverse when those transactions were written to Journal.

iii. Only the below entries are available for editing:

- Account ID
- Debit Amount
- Credit Amount
- Description
- Reference
- Date
- Period
- Check Box 'A' representing 'Allocate'
- Check Box 'c' representing 'Check reconciliation'

iv. The Source Code cannot be edited in the GL Edit Transactions screen. In addition to that the below fields are also unavailable for editing:

- Debit Amount Base
- Credit Amount Base
- Currency ID
- Entry Number
- Exchange Rate
- Post run

In short, the fields that are available in the GL Edit Transactions, by default will be available for editing, while those fields in the 'Column Chooser' are read-only fields, defaulting from the System based on the existing setup.



Difference between Editing and Reversing Transactions:

-
Editing Unposted Transactions:
If a transaction has not yet been posted, we can directly modify it using the Edit Transactions function. [NOTE: Once the changes are made, the user need to save the changes by clicking onto the 'Save' icon at the top-left of the screen]
TEST CASES:
a. Handling Incorrect Year Without Creating Additional Entries
If a transaction was mistakenly written to the Journal under the wrong Fiscal Period or Year, and we do not want to create additional entries in the incorrect period, we can update both the Debit Amount and Credit Amount to $0.00. This ensures that the transaction does not impact financial reports for the incorrect period while allowing us to proceed with processing without generating additional adjustments.

b. Correcting an Incorrectly Assigned GL Account
If the GL Account was selected incorrectly due to manual entry error, we can modify the entry by updating it to the correct GL Account. This ensures that the transaction is recorded under the appropriate account, maintaining accuracy in financial reporting.

c. Adjusting Fiscal Period and Date
If only the Fiscal Period or Transaction Date was entered incorrectly, we can update these fields within the GL Edit Transactions screen.

- Reversing Unposted Transactions:
To create a reversing entry for an unposted transaction, we can use the Reverse button in the upper-right section of the Edit Transactions screen. [Use the 'Shift' key on the keyboard to select the range of entries as needed]. This action generates a reversal Transaction(s) for the selected entries.

[If batch processing is enabled, a pop-up form will appear. We must select the appropriate batch code from the Batch Code drop-down list and click OK to continue.]

The reversing entry is recorded in the Transactions table, not directly in the Journal table. After creating the reversal, we must use the Transactions function to write the entry to the journal.



-
Reversing Posted Transactions:
If a transaction has already been posted, it cannot be edited. Instead, we must enter a reversing transaction using the Transactions function.
a. Here we can make use of 'GL Transaction View' that lists the existing posted entries. We can arrange the Columns, similar to the ones in the 'GL Transactions' screen and copy-paste the entries. [NOTE: The Debit and Credit Columns should be swapped in either of the screens to create reversal entries].

Audit Trail Considerations:

Editing transactions does not create a separate record of the changes outside of the GL Journal. The organization may prefer to reverse transactions rather than edit them directly to maintain a permanent record in the GL Master.

To ensure a clear audit trail, we should print the GL Journal both before and after making edits. Additionally, we need to print the GL Journal to locate the entry numbers of the transactions that require modification.

ee7c7fe6-ff70-4a90-8b0b-31229ad18e13.title: What is the use of Positive Pay File and how to create it?
ee7c7fe6-ff70-4a90-8b0b-31229ad18e13.content:
Problem
What is the use of Positive Pay File and how to create it?

Resolution
A Positive Pay File is a security feature used by banks to prevent check fraud by verifying issued checks before they are cleared. The company generates and sends this file to the bank, listing details of issued checks, such as:

- Check Number
- Check Date
- Payee Name
- Check Amount
- Bank Account Number

When a check is presented for payment, the bank cross-references it with the details in the Positive Pay File. If there are discrepancies, the check is flagged for further review, ensuring a secure payment process and minimizing fraud risk.

[Note: The format and required fields of the Positive Pay File may vary depending on bank-specific requirements.]



Steps to setup and create a Positive Pay file:

i. Gather information on the Bank's requirements:

Before configuring the Positive Pay File, it is crucial to obtain the bank's file format specifications to ensure compliance.

The bank may provide specific details regarding:

- File format (CSV, TXT, XML, etc.)
- Field order and lengths
- Delimiter type (comma-separated, tab-separated, etc.)

For example, let's consider the below specifications:

Sequence

Field Name

Description

Field Length

1Account NumberUnique account number assigned by the bank122Payment NumberCheck Number with leading zeros if required.103Payment AmountRepresents the total Check AmountNA4Payment DateCheck Date in 'MM/DD/YYYY' formatNA5Payment Status"IS" for issued checks, "V" for voided checks26Payment NameName of the vendor receiving paymentNA


ii. Setup the Export layout Definition, aligning to the Bank's specifications/requirements:

Navigate to the SM Export Layout Definition under the path: Applications -> System Manager -> Company Setup -> Export Layout Definition:

Based on the Bank's requirements, design the Positive Pay File Layout. [The below Layout represents the same requirement listed above]



iii. Configure the Layout to the corresponding Bank:

Navigate to the SM Bank Accounts under the path: Applications -> System Manager -> Company Setup -> Bank Accounts: Select the Bank Account for which the Positive Pay File will be generated. Go to the 'Bank' Tab and configure the 'AP Positive Pay File' Layout that was designed, and then click on 'Save' icon at the top



iv. Create Positive Pay File:

Generally, the Positive Pay file will be created after the AP Checks are printed, and before posting the Payments.

Navigate to the AP Create Positive Pay File screen under the Path: Applications -> Accounts Payable -> Pay Invoices -> Create Positive Pay File: Choose the required 'Bank Account ID' from the drop-down. Then select the required Check numbers that need to be included in the Positive Pay file and click on 'Create':



v. Observe the Output File:

The Output Positive Pay File will be looking as follows, available in the destined location:
