e8c3edab-2224-4e51-84b3-58c2b3c3befd.title: ODBC connection for shipping integration
e8c3edab-2224-4e51-84b3-58c2b3c3befd.content:
Problem
Setup ODBC connection for Shipping Integration.

Resolution
If it is completely a new customer for shipping application we would need to create the SQL user, add tables that it needs, and then would create the ODBC connection.

- To create a new SQL login, Right click on Security > New > Login. (In SSMS).

It's going to pull up your information where you can enter in your login. I'm just going to call this from UPS1.
Here you will notice that it has Windows authentication to the top and SQL equal server authentication. You always want to use the SQL Server authentication as an advantage with more than one user is going to be using.
- In this example we will choose SQL on dedication. Enter the password of your choice. Also uncheck enforce password policy.
- Now we would need to check each option here on the left and we'll start by server roles.
All you have to worry about here is that it is public. Confirm it with the customer or leave it at public and you could be fine.

- User mapping is what databases that you want your shipping integration on. In our case we're going to go ahead and choose V11 as an example.

This part actually goes for all of them. It goes for enterprise. It goes for global 11.2 and version 11. So, this step here leading up to the ODBC connection is no different. Also, no different for FedEx setup as well, because this could potentially be a FedEx.

- In the other two options like securable and status, we need not make any changes and click OK.
- The next step we would do is move select V11 database. Our UPS1 user should be ready, and we can start granting the table permissions here. Expand databases as a next step to create our SQL user. We will locate V11 database that we mentioned. We can expand that. Go down to security and we should see our username in here. So, under users.
- The next thing we should do is select database > Right click > select properties. Now properties windows up. Go to securable here. You're going to see your UPS1 username. Select search. In here you should select the second option and click OK.

- And the second window will come up. Select object types. In this case, we should elect tables. Click OK.

- So, the next step that we should do here is we should grant the necessary tables that we're going to need for the shipping integration examples of some tables that we will grant permissions to tblShippingimport, tblSotransdetail, tblSotransheader and tblSotransheaderframe.
- Those are the ones that you can provide permissions to. But you are able to add permissions to another table as you wish based on the client's environment.
- Select each table and check three boxes to make sure to grant it, and those are delete, insert and select.

- Till this we have completed the SQL user creation.
- Next step here will be to set up our ODBC DNS connections. We will mainly be working in a 64-bit environment for Windows and in that case just the biggest advice is that we should make sure that we're using the 32-bit setup.
- Launch the Start menu > Type in ODBC into the 32 and launch that. You'll notice two sets here. One is the user DSN, the second one is system DSN. It is required now to set them up in the user DSN and DSN.

- Now, to create user DNS. We'll do traverse to UPS as a first Map. Select add > You'll get a list of some drivers here > We're just going to use SQL Server > And click Finish.
- A pop up appears, we should give it a short name, it's going to be travers2ups.

Put in the full description here. Next, go ahead and choose the server's name. It should be the server's name that we are using in our SQL server for our SQL server. Go ahead and move to the next step here > go ahead and select with SQL authentication unless you are using a Windows domain windows authentication. So, go ahead and choose with sequel server authentication, which is only the important part here. Then this is where our UPS user gets entered our username and password.

- Click Next, in this section, we don't have to touch anything to leave it as it is or to the next option. Nothing here either. Finish most important things. Then we test or connection, hit the test data source.

- Test is successful and we'll keep on going here.
- Now we should make our ups to traverse map with the same information we had. Follow the same steps as above.
- Click OK Now we are all set for our user DNS.
- Similarly, we should setup for system DNS again.
- Both the user and the system DNS to enter our incoming and outgoing, which means traverse to UPS, UPS to traverse.
- If you have any issues with connection in the UPS integration interface, you will have to revisit here and make sure your password is correct in here.
You probably want to check as a first step when troubleshooting as well.

88488a20-4be3-40e1-be57-5b2239598895.title: What is the use of 'PA History Adjustments' in Traverse?
88488a20-4be3-40e1-be57-5b2239598895.content:
Problem
What is the use of 'PA History Adjustments' in Traverse?

Resolution
The History Adjustments functionality in Traverse is designed to allow administrators to make corrections to values that have been posted to employee history. This is particularly useful when setup errors are identified after checks have already been posted. It ensures that historical data remains accurate for reporting and payroll processing purposes.



The History Adjustments function operates similarly to the Adjustments function for Tax Locations in the System Manager.



NOTES: All amounts displayed are set to 0 by default. Administrators enter the desired adjustment amounts into the appropriate fields.

- Positive values add to the existing totals.
- Negative values subtract from the existing totals.



Before making any changes to the history, the user needs to ensure that they are on the right Payroll Year [For example, 2024]. If the Payroll Year is in the new Year [2025], the user needs to switch the Year back to 2024 in the PA Change Fiscal Year screen and ensure that the Fiscal Year is also open:



If the User need to make adjustments to the history of an Employee, they need to follow the below steps:



i. Navigate to the PA History Adjustments screen under the path: Applications -> Payroll -> Periodic Processing -> History Adjustments:



ii. Choose the employee for whom the adjustment is to be made from the Employee ID field from the lookups [NOTE: Ensure that the Payroll Year is right, as required]:



iii. If the adjustment pertains to employee-paid deductions, leave the Employer Paid checkbox unchecked. Mark the checkbox to include employer-paid costs.



iv. Choose the appropriate 'Adjustment Type' from the list available, as required. The Adjustment Type field allows users to specify the area in which adjustments need to be made, such as deductions, state tax, local tax, or employer costs:

a. Deductions:

- Purpose: Adjustments to deductions involve modifying employee contributions, such as health insurance, retirement savings, or other benefits.
- Tips for Effective Setup:
- Use the Column Chooser to add the Description column to the grid. This helps you view additional details about the deductions, making it easier to identify specific codes.
- Be descriptive when creating deduction codes. For example, instead of naming a code "INS01," consider naming it "Health Insurance – Plan A." This makes it easier to understand its purpose when viewed in reports or audit logs.

- Adjustment Guidelines:
- Enter a positive value to increase the deduction amount.
- Enter a negative value to decrease the deduction amount.

b. State Tax

- Purpose: Adjustments to state taxes ensure accurate withholding amounts for employees based on their state tax obligations.
- Default Withholding State:
- Each employee must have a default withholding state set up in their profile. This is the state where taxes will be primarily calculated.
- The default withholding state is automatically used when processing payroll.

- Overrides:
- If an employee temporarily works in a different state, the withholding state can be overridden during time ticket entry.
- Ensure that such overrides are documented properly to avoid discrepancies in tax filings.

- Adjustment Guidelines:
- Adjustments can be made to correct over- or under-withholding from previous payroll periods.

c. Local Tax

- Purpose: Adjustments to local taxes cover taxes imposed by municipalities, counties, or other local jurisdictions. These taxes are often based on the employee's work or residence location.
- Default Withholding Locality:
- Similar to state taxes, each employee must have a default withholding locality set up in their profile.
- The locality determines which local tax rates will apply.

- Overrides:
- If an employee works in a different locality than their usual location, the default locality can be overridden during time ticket entry.
- Overrides are particularly useful for employees working in multiple jurisdictions.

- Adjustment Guidelines:
- Enter the adjustment values to correct inaccuracies in local tax withholding amounts.

d. Employer Costs

- Purpose: Adjustments to employer costs involve modifying amounts that the employer pays on behalf of the employee, such as employer contributions to Social Security, Medicare, retirement plans, or insurance premiums.
- Description Column:
- Add the Description column to the grid using the Column Chooser. This ensures clarity when selecting specific employer cost codes for adjustment.
- Similar to deductions, employer cost codes are saved in employee history, but their descriptions are not. It is crucial to create descriptive names for these codes.
- For example, instead of naming a code "EC01," use "Employer Contribution – 401(k)."

- Adjustment Guidelines:
- Enter positive values to increase the employer's contribution amount.
- Enter negative values to decrease the employer's contribution amount.



v. Once completed, click on the 'OK' icon at the top to finalize and saves the entered adjustment to the History of the respective month:



vi. a. Once completed, the log will be appearing on the screen. if needed, the user can print the same.

vi. b. Alternatively, the 'Activity' provides the Activity log of all the adjustments performed, for future reference:

2ecd928b-4f54-44af-aeb7-f3c994ddd89a.title: While trying to import GL account Budget the error pops up "BudgetForecast.Parent is required"
2ecd928b-4f54-44af-aeb7-f3c994ddd89a.content:
Problem
While trying to import GL account Budget the error pops up "BudgetForecast.Parent is required" when trying to click Verify Data

Resolution
The error message you're encountering— “budgetforecast.parent is required for one account ID”—typically means that the system or application you're working with is expecting a specific parent account to be provided for a budget or forecast entry, but it is missing for one of the account IDs you are trying to import.

How to resolve this?

Check the data: Verify the account ID that’s causing the issue and ensure that it’s properly associated with a parent account in the file you're importing.

Here, we should make sure the data is correctly mapped with the proper parent accounts.

Step 1: Navigate to General Ledger > Setup and Maintenance > Account Budgets and Forecasts.

Step 2: On “Budgets” and “Forecasts” tab, click on the ellipses on Detail icon column header. It will open the account inbox where we can notice all the GL accounts that are linked to the budget.



Step 3: Click on Apply Filter on the Account ID column header and search for the account ID for which the error occurred. Here the account ID is “63802010”

Step 4: No ID is found here, which means that GL account is not set.

Step 5: Then, we should make sure that GL account do exist in the existing account list.

Step 6: Navigate to General Ledger > Setup and Maintenance > GL chart of accounts. In the Account ID drop box search the required ID and see if it exist. Here, in this case, it is obviously a No.

Step 7: So, we would need to setup a GL account. For this,

Navigate to General Ledger > Setup and Maintenance > GL chart of accounts

7.1 The Account ID field is nonresponsive i.e greyed out. You cannot fill. The segment ID will be the original Account ID. Setup the Segment ID namely for all the line items in the column header Description.

7.2 Fill the description in the Description field.

7.3 Choose the Account type. The other columns like “Type Description, Class description and Account Type” will autofill once you choose the Account type.

7.4 If needed, fill in the Clear to account and consol to account fields. If not leave it blank.

7.5 Make sure that the account ID is in the status of active.

7.6 Once the required changes are made, save the account.



Step 8: Now, we need to add this account to the GL Account Budget & Forecasts Details tab.

8.1: Go to GL Accounts Budgets and Forecasts tab, In the Budgets tab, click on the Details icon and make sure to click the Select All menu tab and then hit OK.



This approach will automatically add the new GL account ID that was added now.

8.2: Follow the same step for the Forecast tab too.

8.3: Make sure to also hit save on the main Save button.

Step 9: Now, refresh the SM Import Mapped Data tab and reimport again. Now the imports will be successfully completed.

When You hit OK, the screen appears to be cleared which clearly means that the data has been successfully imported.

de95d32b-53bb-49d0-87eb-691451b8c7ec.title: Is it possible to delete a GL account?
de95d32b-53bb-49d0-87eb-691451b8c7ec.content:
Problem
Is it possible to delete a GL account? The client encounters the following error while trying to perform the delete operation:

Resolution
Step 1: Verify if the GL account has a history

You cannot delete a GL account if there is any transaction history tied to it. Verify this by going into GL > Interactive view > GL Transaction view. Filter the view by Account ID for which you want to verify if any transactions exist.

Here there is no transaction history tied to it.

However, you are still unable to delete the account. It is possible that this particular account is linked to Setup and Maintenance. Therefore, you will need to find the link. Follow the next steps to identify the linkage.



Step 2: Turn the GL account status from Active to Inactive

Navigate to GL > Setup and Maintenance > Chart of accounts

Change the status to Inactive

Step 3: Find the Invalid GL account

Navigate to System Manager > System audit > Invalid GL Account list

Select all applications and click OK



Apply the account number = 110002 in the filters of the column header “Account number” and hit OK

You will see that an AR (Accounts Receivable) is linked to this account. Reference: App ID.
You will also see that the account is linked to the AR distribution code table. Reference: Table Name and Reference value, i.e., dbo.tblArDistCode and 05 in this case.

Step 4: Delete the Distribution code from the Table

Navigate to Accounts Receivable > Setup and Maintenance > Distribution Code.

d541b422-10ce-4d39-aad5-71c670866146.title: Unable to delete a new customer record in AR Setup and Maintenance
d541b422-10ce-4d39-aad5-71c670866146.content:
Problem
The user is unable to delete a new Customer record 'XXX' in the AR Customers screen under the path: Applications -> Accounts Receivable ->  Setup and Maintenance -> Customers.



The customer has no open Transactions or posted Transactions for the Customer. yet, when the User attempts delete the Customer ID 'XXX' the user is getting the below error message:



===================================

Current record cannot be deleted.

===================================

Current record cannot be deleted. (TRAVERSE.Controls)

------------------------------
Program Location:

at TRAVERSE.Client.PluginControlBase.DeleteRow()
at TRAVERSE.Controls.TravNavigator.OnDelete(TravNavigatorEventArgs e)

Resolution
When a new Customer ID, such as 'XXX,' is created by a user, the system begins tracking transactions associated with it. If a Sales Order (e.g., 'ZZZ') or an AR Transaction (e.g., 'YYY') is created using this Customer ID and is included in a batch (e.g., '######'), but later that specific Order or Transaction is deleted, the system still considers that a transaction is linked to the batch for the Customer ID 'XXX.' This is because Traverse maintains a history record for the Customer ID within the batch, even though the transaction itself has been removed. As a result, the user will not be able to delete the Customer ID 'XXX' due to this residual historical linkage.



To resolve this and enable the deletion of the Customer ID 'XXX,' the user must process at least one transaction from the same batch '######.' That one Transaction serves as a placeholder to complete the batch. By processing and posting this additional transaction within batch '######,' the system will no longer associate any historical records with the Customer ID 'XXX.' This is because once a batch is posted, only the current transactions inside that batch will be included in the historical records, and the residual history of the Customer ID 'XXX' will be completely wiped off from the system, allowing it to be deleted.



Once the batch '######' has been processed or posted, Traverse will acknowledge that there are no longer any historical records tied to the Customer ID 'XXX,' allowing the user to delete it successfully.



Example:

Let us consider the example, where we have a Customer ID 'XXX', that was created in Traverse, and a Sales Order '00000628' was created in the Default Batch '######':



Later, the user might have deleted the Sales Order '00000628' and we can observe that it is not available in the 'SO Open Order View':



When the user attempts to delete the Customer ID 'XXX' now, the user will be getting the error "Current Record cannot be deleted":



At this point, the User need to post the Batch '######', where that Sales Order 00000628 was existing. [NOTE: If there are no Transactions for now, the user can process just a single Invoice for this. In case the User doesn't want to process all the orders of that Batch '######' for now, they can make use of 'Change Batches' function to have those Transactions moved to a different Batch and then post this Batch with at least an Invoice in it]



Now, when the User attempts to delete the Customer ID 'XXX', the record would get deleted without any issues:

e9356884-5a52-4c5f-9dd3-73ccb8f10970.title: How to avoid Geofencing Issues
e9356884-5a52-4c5f-9dd3-73ccb8f10970.content:
Problem
A user is experiencing problems logging in when within the Geofence. What are some criteria to avoid issues with Geofencing?

Resolution
Geofencing can be highly volatile based on the User's device, network connection and location settings. They may be in a place physically present with the region, but due to accuracy errors, the phone may not report the correct position exactly to the application. As a result, the users might not get access to enter the region.

Development had recommended the following measures to avoid issues with Geofencing:

1. Have the size of a Geofence region to at least 200 meters.
2. If the size is smaller than a 200 meter radius, you need to update this and make sure all users do a full sync with the server (rotated arrows on the main punch screen). This should pull down any new data for the fencing.
3. If there was a configuration change, Users need to sign out/sign back in completely or clear app data if necessary.
4. Users should make sure Wi-Fi is enabled on their device as this helps get better location results.
5. Users should check their location settings on their device to make sure higher resolution location tracking is available.
6. Users should make sure the app has been given requested location permissions.

5704cf4f-9192-4b24-ab58-602bbf99ce7f.title: How to adjust the bucketing in AP Aged Trial Balance View?
5704cf4f-9192-4b24-ab58-602bbf99ce7f.content:

The Aged Trial Balance View is used to retrieve detailed information about vendors and aged invoices. Users can navigate to the AP Aged Trial Balance View under the path: Applications -> Accounts Payable -> Interactive Views -> Aged Trial Balance View:

"Options" Button: The user can use the "Options" button to open the Options Screen, where we can configure cutoff dates, past due dates, and other parameters to tailor the view to our needs.��

-
-
Age By: It is used to select how to age the information:

- By Invoice Date: Age based on the invoice date.
- By Due Date: Age based on the invoice's due date.

-
Transaction Cutoff: It defines the point at which transactions should be included:

- By Date: Specify a date to include unpaid invoices with an invoice date on or before this date.
- By Period: Specify a fiscal period/year to include unpaid invoices with a Fiscal Pd/Year in or before this period.

-
Payment Cutoff: This specifies the point at which payments should be included:

- By Date: Include payment details for fully paid invoices with payment dates between the specified date and the Transaction Cutoff date.
- By Period: Include payment details for fully paid invoices with periods in or after the specified period and before the Transaction Cutoff date.

-
Aging Date: It is used to set a starting point for aging calculations.

-
Aging Breaks (Past Due Fields): This defines the aging buckets or categories for classifying aging statuses.

-
Distribution Code Range: We can enter a range of distribution codes to filter the view. Leave the fields blank to include all distribution codes.

-
Past Due Vendors Only: The user can check this option to restrict the view to vendors with past-due invoices.

-
Report Currency:

- Selecting a currency will generate a report based on the chosen currency.

c3b0614e-310f-45a3-b356-33287e3a3b1d.title: Setting Up Overtime in On-Time Web
c3b0614e-310f-45a3-b356-33287e3a3b1d.content:
Problem
Client needs to setup overtime calculations in On-TIme Web.

Resolution
Setting Up Overtime in On-Time Web.

To set overtime in On-Time Web first, Log into On-Time Web as the company administrator and navigate to Company Settings>Settings & Defaults>Company Settings, then select the drop-down box beside Overtime Method from the first column.

Then you can select the appropriate overtime method you wish to use as your default overtime method. The choices are.
Weekly – This method is based on a set number of hours that an employee works in a week
Daily – This method is based on the number of hours a person works in a day
Daily & Weekly – This method is based on the hours worked in a day and the number of hours worked in a week.
7th Day – This method is based on an employee who works 7 days consecutively, on the seventh day the first 8 hours are calculated as overtime.
None – No overtime will be calculated
Once a method is selected, then complete the number of hours in the Overtime Weekly and/or Overtime Daily based on the selection.  For example, if you are working in California and select Daily & Weekly you would enter the number of hours a person has to work in a week before overtime is calculated as well as the number of hours in a day the person must work before calculating overtime.  This means that even if the employee doesn’t work over 40 hours in the week but does work late one or two days, they will still get overtime pay for those two days.

Once the overtime method and hours are saved this becomes your default overtime settings.  You also can change the overtime method for an individual employee if needed.  This override would be done in the Employees tab on the individual Employees record.

991fd1ee-3b8b-4862-91f6-2ed214dd9bfa.title: How to Setup Employee Punch Settings in On-Time Web
991fd1ee-3b8b-4862-91f6-2ed214dd9bfa.content:
Problem
What are the Punch Settings in On-Time Web and how do I set them up?

Resolution
On-Time Web allows you to customize your Punch Method setting from what to show on the punch screen to auto lunches and punch rounding.
What to show on the Punch Screen

There are many options as to what you want to show on the Punch Screen.
Start in the Company Settings> Settings and Defaults> Punch Settings
You will be able to see the show fields which are:
- Show Lunch Buttons - Choose to show or hide the lunch buttons depending on if you want the employees to punch out and back in for their Lunch Time.
- Show Switch Button - Choose to show or hide the switch button depending on if the employees need to switch between Departments, Jobs/Phases/Tasks, or Earning Codes.
- Show Break Buttons - Choose to show or hide the break buttons. If the employees need to punch out and in from breaks.
- Show Earning Code - Choose to show or hide the earning codes, if the employees need to switch their earning codes. (This is not normally used unless there are various earning codes they need to select for specific jobs responsibilities.)
- Show Notes Field - Choose to show the Notes field to allow notes on specific punches.  There is also a setting to force notes on punches.

Layout and Auto Punches

Button Layout - You can choose between two different layouts of the punch buttons on the punch screen.

- Logical Flow - The logical flow arranges the punch button to be read from left to right based on the actions of start and end of the punch time.
- Grouped - all the IN type punches are grouped on the left and all the OUT type punches are on the right.

Auto Punches

- Auto Lunches - Auto lunches are created automatically for punch employees if the IN punch occurs before the start of the employees lunch time and the OUT punch occurs after the end of the auto lunch time for the employee.


- Auto-in Punches - (NOT RECOMMENDED) When an employee punches OUT, but there is no IN punch, then an auto IN punch is created with 00 time. If disabled then the missing punch will be visible on the Time Approval Screen.
- Auto-Out Punches - (NOT RECOMMENDED) When an employee punches IN, but there is no OUT punch, then an auto OUT punch is created with 00 time.  If disabled then the missing punch will be visible on the Time Approval Screen.

Time Rounding (Punch Rounding)

Time Rounding is the function that will round punches based on the set of rules below.

- Enable Time Rounding - Enable/Disable rounding rules to be applied to Employees set for Punch Entry Mode
- Button Rounding Options - Choose which punch button to apply rounding. Choose IN, OUT, Switch, Return Lunch, Go Lunch, Return Break, and Go Break.
- Rounding Interval - Choose the rounding minutes interval for your punch rounding.  Choose 5, 6, 10, or 15 minutes.
- Required Work Time - The amount of time required to work of the rounding interval before the time is rounded to the next interval.

Example:
Let's say you want to use the rounding rule of Eights. The settings for that would be 15 minute intervals and the employee has to work 8 of the 15 minutes before the time is rounded.

646925be-1aef-40f5-9a1d-b2d812e39592.title: Design Studio - Lookup Table
646925be-1aef-40f5-9a1d-b2d812e39592.content:
Problem
Design Studio offers functionality to change how the lookups in the software work, the various drop-down options throughout the software. This document will discuss the Lookups Table function in Design Studio > System Data and how to use this feature.

Resolution
The Lookup Table function contains all lookups the software uses that are allowed to be customized.
It is recommended to have knowledge of TSQL in order to successfully modify the Data Sources of the lookups.

While some may sound specific, they may be used across multiple software functions. As an example, one might be modifying the Item lookup anticipating changing this for Inventory > Setup and Maintenance > Items. This lookup is used throughout the software and any lookup changes made to the Item lookup will extend to all areas this lookup is used.

This feature allows users to modify a lookup for one company or all companies.
If making changes for one company, use the Customize button in the toolbar.
If making changes for all companies, create a new record and then use a Replace ID to replace the ID of the record you are editing.

Note: If you modify the record directly, the next server update will reset the changes to the vanilla design and any customizations will be lost. Creating a new record and using the Replace ID will ensure no loss of customizations.

If a lookup has been customized, it will indicate this in the Customized field, indicating if the definition has been replaced in the system (SYS database) or company (Company Database.)

This function also allows to to copy to and from other company databases, for example maybe I made a change to the Item lookup and wish to make that change in my AVG and GLB company database. I can use the Copy To button to accomplish this task.

The Copy From button will work similarly where you can copy changes from another company to one you are currently working in Design Studio in.

The Lookup Table consists of 11 columns: ID, Description, Data Source, Key Column, Default Contents, Enumerated Columns, Formats, Database Type, Volatile Data, Replace ID, and Customized.

-The ID is the unique name assigned to each lookup.
-The Description is the description of the lookup itself.
-The Data Source is a SQL query that fetches the data for the lookup.
-Available lists the fields that are available in the lookup. The data source may get many fields, the Available fields limit what users see and work with -in the lookup.
-Default lists the default fields that should display when the lookup is used.
-Enumerated translates numeric values stored in the table, where the data source may return 1,2,3,4 for a column, and translate that to values that make sense such as New, Quote, Picked, Invoiced.
-Formats is used to format information that appears in the results. For example a phone number may get returned in the data and formatted as ###-###-####
-Volatile Data is temporary data, it is put into the table and then removed.
-Customized is the indicator if a definitions has been modified for a company or for the system.

The Customize function allows users to create a custom lookup for the company database. It will not be added for all companies that may exist in the same system.

7690166b-7d7d-4be1-b8a3-60de9374feb9.title: Design Studio - Add Custom Field to View

We will also alias it add it as an available field. Next, preview the change to make sure it executes and shows the desired results.

fd3038fd-32c6-4513-96f8-406ed1d2da0a.title: Design Studio - Views Table
fd3038fd-32c6-4513-96f8-406ed1d2da0a.content:
Problem
Design Studio offers functionality to change how the Interactive Views in the software work. This document serves as an overview of the Views Table function in Design Studio > System Data and what it can do.

Resolution
The Views Table contains all editable Interactive Views in the software. Each view has an ID, Description, Data Source, Available columns, Default Columns, Enumerated Columns, Formats, a Replace ID, and a Customized notifier.

- Each ID is a unique name to a specific view.
- The description helps users understand what the content or purpose of the view may be.
- The Data Source is the SQL statement that generates the data for the view.
- The available columns is a list of columns based on the Data Source that users can pull in to the view and use.
- The Default columns are the columns users will have on screen by default.
- Enumerated columns translate values to more meaningful phrases, such as 1,2,3,4 translating to New, Quote, Verify, Invoiced.
- Formats is used to format data returned, such as a phone number as ###-###-####.
- Replace ID is used to replace a standard view with a customized version.
- Customized indicates that a view has been customized for the company or for the whole system.

If the Customize button is used, it will modify the view for the company we are logged in as.
If a new record is created and Replace ID used, the view will be modified for the system.

Users can also copy changes to other company databases by clicking the Copy To button, the views, then database(s), then OK.


Users can also copy from another company database by clicking Copy From, then select the company to copy from, the view to copy, and click OK.


There are additional KB resources that will dive in to customizing the views in different ways.

c33cc061-5498-41df-a1fe-d1d65fa6a283.title: Design Studio - Adding a Custom Field to Report
c33cc061-5498-41df-a1fe-d1d65fa6a283.content:
Problem
Design Studio offers the ability to add custom fields to some of the reports in the software. This document will look at the process to accomplish this task.

Note: Not all custom fields are readily available and may require a custom schema or custom coded work to make the necessary changes. This overview will cover scenarios where this can be done using Design Studio.

Resolution
To add a custom field to a report, take note of the table where that custom field is stored.

Let's use a Sales Order-related custom field that we have added, called extra notes.

Next, let's look at the Report Designer function and the related schema. We need to verify the schema's primary key field is checked. If its unchecked the schema needs to be customized, or a custom coded customization will be needed to accomplish this task.

Since we wish to add a custom field to SO Invoices, we'll drill into the schema and look now. Double-click on the Function ID for Print Invoices


Next, in the Datasource Definition, click on the Primary Table for the first row for Table. In this example, its tblSoTransHeader. Then click on the button with three ellipsis.

This will display the Primary Table window where we can see In Schema Table is checked. This means our custom fields in this table are available in the schema for the report.


Furthermore, if we click on the Custom Fields tab, we can see our custom fields in this table and the one we want is indeed there.


This means we can proceed back to the Report Designer for Sales Orders Invoices and click Design.

We can see our custom field is available in the Field List in Table, as cf_Extra Notes.

Now we will place the field, for our purposes we want this in the header, under Sold To should work for our needs.

Remember to do some testing with your changes in case you find things overlap or grow unexpectedly.

In this example, is it possible for the Sold-To field to grow and move? Yes. Fields used in the Ship To section may have large amounts of data such as the Address 2 field. Perhaps having a Name, Attention, Address 1 and Address 2 entered push this field around.
There may need to be some trial and error to place this, or a coded customization can help stabilize things. This all depends on the other fields, type and amount of data.

Once the desired changes are made, don't forget to save. This can either be saved as the default layout for all users to see, or as a named save and assigning this report to so only certain users print this way when they are using the function.
Example as a default:


Example as a named layout:

96531a43-831e-4267-8aa0-66392b1a7aee.title: Design Studio - Report Designer
96531a43-831e-4267-8aa0-66392b1a7aee.content:
Problem
Design Studio offers functionality to change how the printed items in the software look, the appearance of Traverse's reports. This document will discuss the Report Designer function in Design Studio > Designers and how to use this feature.

Resolution
The Report Designer has many reports available, let's pick on one and take a closer look at a more commonly altered report, the AP Check Format 1 report.

There are many options and tools available on the screen. Some areas to highlight are the Tool Box, Report Explorer, Field List, and Property Grid. If any of these are closed, they are still available in the menu at the top in the View menu.

If you wish to add anything new, you can use the tool box and drag and place an item on to the report where you wish to have it.


The Report Explorer serves as a navigational tree view of what is currently on the report. You can click on fields this way to quickly find them, or click on the screen as desired.


The Property Grid allows you to interact with each object's properties.


The Field List contains all fields available for this particular report. You may drag and drop fields from this list on to the report.


Changes can be saved to the default layout or to a named layout, to be assigned to specific users.
To save to the default layout click Use Database, then the save icon, leave Use default layout name checked, and then OK


To save to a named layout click Use Database, then the save icon, uncheck the Use default layout name checkbox, type a layout name, and then OK


Some items to note:
- Forms can be reactive in how they expand and contract. It can depend on the form, the type, and amounts of data flowing to them at any time, but they can resize in ways that are unfavorable depending on changes made. As an example a change to the check may not seem to be an issue but if one adds a new label to it, it could get pushed out of the way when a larger than normal address prints on the check. It may never be an issue as well.
- Be sure to thoroughly test any changes you make to be sure they do not cause you any issues. Custom coded changes may be necessary if the desired effect cannot be reached using Design Studio.
- The designer will give hints at issues, for example if two fields are overlapping it will appear red in the designer.

e456738d-cf8f-4af9-9577-8048004f7d89.title: Design Studio - Restore Custom Metadata
e456738d-cf8f-4af9-9577-8048004f7d89.content:
Problem
Design Studio has a mechanism to restore designs from a metadata file if they exist. This may be used to recover an old design that was lost, maybe there is an issue with a current design and users need to roll beck to another design. If metadata is exported regularly in any increment of time, this can be used to restore designs from that point in time.

Note: This will restore all associated changes. For example, perhaps I have an issue with an AP Transactions form previously modified. I also have an IN Items form that has been modified. A metadata import will bring both designs back.

Resolution
Let's see the design that has an issue first:

Next verify you have a metadata files. We do have one file luckily that should have the old design.

To import the metadata in, navigate to Design Studio and then open System Data > Export/Import Custom Metadata.
Make sure Transfer Type says Import and then click on file name to point to your metadata file.

As we can see in this example, only a few type of metadata are in this file. Thats not wrong, there could be more or less. It all depends on what was modified in Design Studio at the time this file was prepared.

As a quick comparison, if we were exporting, this is all the possible metadata that can be exported:


In our case, we want to bring back the custom forms that we know are in this metadata backup. Since we just want the custom layouts (Forms and Reports), we'll check that box and then OK.

Confirm the old designs are back in place and they are.

Lastly, if this method brings too much back, all forms instead of just one for example, you can attempt to get changes from an older backup that has the desired design. We have an additional KB that discusses that process.

91146c05-6ed1-4627-9e9e-0cae367bd6bb.title: Design Studio - Modify a Lookup for All Databases
91146c05-6ed1-4627-9e9e-0cae367bd6bb.content:
Problem
A user would like one of the software's lookups for all of the company databases to have some extra data in the lookup. This document will discuss how to modify an existing lookup in the software using Design Studio.

Resolution
First, open Design Studio and access System Data > Lookup Table.

For our purposes, we wish to add LottedYn to our Item lookup for all of our companies so when we are looking for an item we can include or exclude lotted items in the lookup. As a disclaimer, this will change the Item lookup everywhere it is used for example two places are in IN Items, SO Orders.

First we need to create a new record and copy in the contents from our target record into the new lookup.
In the example, we create the new record as ItemCustom so users easily see this is a custom version of the Items lookup.

In the shot above you can see the ReplaceID has been set as Item, and then the original record reads System for the Customized column.

Lets look at the datasource change. If we click into the datasource of our new record we'll get the Custom Lookup Editor.


Add in the necessary SQL code to accomplish your task and preview results to test your code.
In this example its not necessary to alias the column but was done as a choice to cut down on confusion due to the column name.


After confirmation of your change, click Execute & Accept Query


Now that our field is part of the data source, we'll want to determine if users should see it every time they use the lookup.
For our example, let's also add it as a default in the Default Columns.


Lastly, be sure to save the record.

Now if we check our work, if we were to visit the Inventory > Setup and Maintenance > Items function and look at the Item lookup, we'll see our new column available.

d567c5e3-0d23-4013-9ae1-49f18dd5dc0a.title: Design Studio - Modify a Lookup for Company Database
d567c5e3-0d23-4013-9ae1-49f18dd5dc0a.content:
Problem
A user would like one of the software's lookups for one of the company databases to have some extra data in the lookup. This document will discuss how to modify an existing lookup in the software using Design Studio.

First, open Design Studio and access System Data > Lookup Table.

For our purposes, we wish to add LottedYn to our Item lookup for one of our companies so when we are looking for an item we can include or exclude lotted items in the lookup. As a disclaimer, this will change the Item lookup everywhere it is used for example two places are in IN Items, SO Orders.

If we wish for this to be a company change we can click the Customize button at the top of the screen.

The Custom Lookup Editor will appear where we can make the necessary changes. Since we're adding LottedYn we need to edit the data source.


Add in the necessary SQL code to accomplish your task and preview results to test your code.
Note, the column added does not have to be aliased, this was done to help cut down on potential confusion by any users.


After confirmation of your change, click Execute & Accept Query


Now that our field is part of the data source, we'll want to determine if users should see it every time they use the lookup.
For our example, let's also add it as a default in the Default Columns.

9b15bfe5-b4b0-4b8e-bf17-20ae539e6498.title: Design Studio - Restore Report from Database Backup
9b15bfe5-b4b0-4b8e-bf17-20ae539e6498.content:
Problem
Due to unforeseen circumstances, a report's modified design may have changed improperly and there is no metadata export that can be used to get the desired design back. It may be possible to recover the previous design from a database backup.

This document will describe how to load a SQL backup, gain access to it, and copy the correct Design Studio change from your backup into your production database to get the design back.

Resolution
Restore a database backup from a point in time you know the changes were correct.

First, locate your backup so you know where to direct the restore wizard in the steps below.

In SQL Server Management Studio, Object Explorer, right-click on Databases > Restore Database > General, check Device and then the backup devices button, #5 in the screenshot below.

In Select Backup Devices, select Add and then navigate to and select the backup file to be used, click OK.

Click OK


Change the Database name here, if you fail to change this value, you risk rolling back your production environment and losing data.

In this example we'll change this to TST, click OK to start the restore process.


Next, we need to add this company to our SYS database so we can grant security to it.
In SQL's Object Explorer, navigate to your SYS database. It is likely to be installed as SYS, in this example it is named GLBSYS.

Click on the box to the left of the name to expand the database, then expand Tables.


Scroll down to tblSmCompInfo, right-click on tblSmCompInfo and then click Edit All Rows (It may say Edit Top 200 Rows)


This will open the table to edit.

Next, we want to click at the front of our company database and then right-click and copy.


The right-click at the bottom line and paste, to paste in the contents of the copied record. Change the CompID to TST.


To save the record, move off the row by arrowing down or up a line. SQL will throw a message if you do no do this part.

Log in to the Traverse Global Server Manager application.

Click Database > Add Company


Type TST, click Apply and OK.


Next, we need to add security, we can just copy from our existing company, GLB in this example.
Click Security > Copy Security.


Click your company at the top, this example uses GLB.
In the Copy To, click the checkbox for TST and OK. This will copy GLB's security to TST.


This will give us the ability to open TST in Design Studio and get a copy of our errant report.

Launch Design Studio and change the company to TST in File > Company, select TST.


Navigate to the Report Designer and select the report that you need. In this example we'll load up the AP Check Format 1 report.

Make sure the highlighted dropdown says Use Database, then click open. This allows us to open our previous version of the modified report. In our case the design we need is saved as the default, but remember you may have things saved as named layouts so be sure to verify those if you have them.

Now that the modified report is up and we confirmed the design is what we need we can proceed to copy the change to production.

In Designers > Custom Layouts find your change. Our example is AP Check Format 1 saved as the default so there will be no layout name. The third record is what we want to use in this example.

Next, click Copy To and then select the custom layout you want to copy from. In this case AP Check Format 1 with no Layout Name and then select your database to copy to, in this example it is GLB. Lastly, click OK.

This will copy the design from TST to GLB, restoring it to what it should be.

Note, if its a named layout, be sure to verify and assign permissions in the production company.

As a final note, do not forget cleanup after this. The TST database can be deleted at this point. You can also remove the TST entry made to tblSmCompInfo, simply access the table as done in the steps above and then right click on the TST row and delete.

64dbd414-6215-403d-b520-2baf3f7d520c.title: Design Studio - Form Designer
64dbd414-6215-403d-b520-2baf3f7d520c.content:
Problem
Design Studio offers functionality to change how the screens in the software look, the appearance of Traverse's forms. This document will discuss the Form Designer function in Design Studio > Designers and how to use this feature.

Resolution
Let's take a tour of the Form Designer function in Design Studio.

As seen above, we have our Form Designer function listing all available forms. To access any form and make changes, simply click on a form and then the Design button. Let's pick on AP Transactions.

Open opening, the stock AP Transactions form loads. An important note, if you have any Design Studio modifications to this screen already, you will need to load those changes before making any additional changes or you risk losing previous work.

Review the Custom Layouts function in Designers to verify what existing modifications there are for the function you wish to modify.

In this example, there are two existing modifications to the AP Transactions form. One is a default layout, it has no layout name, and then a named layout, it has a layout name. Named layouts must be assigned to users, whereas the default layout will load for all users. In this case, there may have special changes for some users and general changes for everyone else, hence the need for two or more modified AP Transactions forms.

Back to our AP Transactions form. We can choose to modify either version, or skip loading an existing modified form to exclude the existing changes.
To load the default custom layout:


To load the named custom layout:

To make changes without loading existing modifications, simply proceed to make changes, nothing needs to be loaded.
While it may be unlikely to skip loading existing changes, the ability to do so still exists.

Users can navigate the form through the Layout Tree View in the Customize  Layout window or by clicking on the screen at the various objects and working with the properties as needed.

Closing the Customize Layout window also allows you to use the form and test things out with it. It is connected to the production environment so be sure to be mindful of what you do here in terms of testing.

If you close the Customize Layout screen, you can right-click to bring it back.

To move things around on the form, click and drag the object where you wish to rearrange it.
If custom fields are present on the form (assigned to the related table of the function) you will see them in the designer and can edit and arrange them as you see fit.

Once all changes have been made, you can save it to an existing named custom layout, as a new named layout, or as the default layout.






Additional Notes:
Remember, if saving changes as a named layout, you must use the Custom Layouts function, in Designers > Custom Layouts, to assign users to the custom layout. If they are not assigned they will not see the changes.

You can copy changes made in Design Studio to another company using the Custom Layouts function and the Copy To button.
Remember to assign users to any named layouts that are copied in the Copy To company.

There is much that can be edited in Design Studio Forms, if something is missing it may be something that is unavailable for programmatic reasons. It might be possible to further modify with Python Scripting or may even require custom C# code to accomplish.

Some forms may have conditional fields that appear with certain types of actions such as a new Sales Order vs. an invoiced Sales Order. It is best to verify the features and functions at hand to prepare for changes.

Some forms may grow depending on certain actions. To help with this, it is advised to use empty space items to keep new objects contained in the intended area. In the example in this document, the Hello World custom field had two additional empty space items added to hold it in place to account for growth on the screen, and even resizing of the screen.

It is a good practice to save the Form change as a file (Use File when saving) to keep a backup of the changes made. To deploy the changes, save the change to the database, but for backup purposes saving to a file is ideal also.
Users can also export the custom metadata via Designers > Export/Import Custom Metadata.
As the Form changes are saved to the database, a database backup will also contain the Design Studio changes at the time of backup. It is possible to pull these out, with some work, if needed.

76470163-cf4c-41fa-88fe-dd8458fa4155.title: Design Studio - Use the Form Designer to Add a Custom Field
76470163-cf4c-41fa-88fe-dd8458fa4155.content:
Problem
Design Studio offers functionality to create your own custom fields and add them into various places throughout the software. The Form Designer, overall, is a feature that is used to change how the screens in the software look, the appearance of Traverse's forms. There is an available KB for the Form Designer in general.

This document will discuss the Form Designer function in Design Studio > Designers and how to use that to add a custom field to one of the software's available forms.

In this demonstration, we'll add a custom field to AP Transactions screen. This is done by assigning the custom field to tblApTransHeader.

This results in the custom field getting placed in a band called Custom Fields.

We'll use the designer next to place the field where we desire on the form for a sleeker look.

Resolution
In Design Studio, let's navigate to Designers > Form Designer > AP Transactions, click on Design

NOTE: If AP Transactions is already a modified form, be sure to open the custom layout and modify that version. Failure to do so may lose previous customizations.
You can check in Designers > Custom Layouts for the related form and verify how many different saved versions there are, and which one you need to modify (default layout or named layout.) Once you have identified the modified form, in the Customize Layout screen of the designer, click Use Database and open, then use the dialogue to open either the default save or a named layout and proceed to make your changes.

In our example, we do not yet have any saved layouts to open.

We will move our custom field on to the screen next. Either drag the field from the Custom Fields band on the screen or in the Customize Layout window, find your custom field and drag it on to the screen and place it as desired.


Next, consider adding empty space items to the form to help keep the field's expansion in check. We will pull in a few from the Customize Layout window's Layout Tree View.

Make any desired or necessary changes in the properties.


When ready save the layout. You have two options for the save, use the default layout or a layout name.
If using the default layout name  all users with access to AP Transactions will see this design.


If using a layout name, remember that users must be assigned access to this design on the Customize Layout screen.



Lastly, let's confirm the custom field in the AP Transactions function.

Some parting notes:
Remember, additional changes can be made to existing modified forms, but you must load the designer for the desired form, open the saved layout, and then proceed to make additional changes. If that process is not followed, the previous customizations can be overwritten.

It is also a good practice to backup the metadata (Export/Import Custom Metadata) or save the design to a file, and then make your changes. Doing so ensures if any issues arise, you can always roll back to a previous design.

As these changes are saved to the database, it is also possible to obtain these changes from a database backup. This requires some slightly technical work to restore the database as a different company name, add the company to the SYS database's tblSmCompInfo table, add that as a company in the Traverse Global Server Manager, grant permissions in the Traverse Global Server Manager to the new company, and then access the new company in Design Studio to access the old Design Studio modifications as this new company.

b7ccd772-f97b-4e27-9e19-52a4951e12be.title: Design Studio - Assign Custom Fields
b7ccd772-f97b-4e27-9e19-52a4951e12be.content:
Problem
Design Studio offers functionality to create your own custom fields and add them into various places throughout the software. This document will discuss the Assign function in Design Studio > Custom Fields.

The purpose of the Assign function is to place newly created custom fields into tables. Each data table in Traverse has space to store custom fields, stored as XML. Fields may be stored in multiple tables depending on the design need. For example, extra information added to Sales Orders may need to be present in history, it would need to be assigned to the transaction-related tables and the history related tables to keep continuity for that field.

Assigning fields to a table also places the field in the related Traverse function for use. If I save my new custom field to the Sales Order transaction table, it will become available on the Sales Order's Order screen as a custom field. It would also then be available to place it on the screen and move it/place it as desired within Design Studio's other functions.

Resolution
The Assign function opens into Field View, where users can see all custom fields and the tables each field is assigned to.

The toolbar has 4 buttons: Save, Refresh Views, Preview Report, and Table View.
The Save button will save any changes you have made.
The Refresh Views button is responsible for updating the custom field view as changes are made.
The Report Preview provides users a list of tables assigned to the selected field.
Lastly, the Table View button changes the screen to show tables that custom fields are assigned to.

As an example, we have a custom field called Hello World.
To assign it to a table, click Add and then select the table, and then OK.

Click Save to save the change.

In this example, the field was assigned to tblApTransHeader. This will place the Hello World field on the AP Transaction screen, in the header section of the screen. If we wanted to see this field in AP history, we may also want to consider adding it to tblAPHistHeader. When the transaction is posted, the custom field data would transfer to the history record for a given transaction.

When a custom field is added to a table, it is placed in the related function within Traverse. In the related function, there is a band that will appear on the screen labeled Custom Fields. You may choose to place the field on the screen by editing the related form to move the field where you wish to see it.
In our example, we would access Designers > Form Designer and then access the form for AP Transactions. We will then see our custom field available to place and use as we see fit.

c377b72a-3869-4e0b-9976-59b323ab14c4.title: Design Studio - Manage Custom Fields
c377b72a-3869-4e0b-9976-59b323ab14c4.content:
Problem
Design Studio offers functionality to create your own custom fields and add them into various places throughout the software. This document will discuss the Manage function in Design Studio > Custom Fields.

The purpose of the Manage function is to serve as the general custom field setup. This function handles operations such as creating, editing, and deleting a custom field.

Resolution
The Manage function opens with a default display of the grid and all available columns.

The toolbar is similar to those seen throughout the software with the exception of the Refresh Views button.
Once a field has been created, click this button to refresh the custom field views.

If you wish to focus on one field at a time, click the double arrow icon to change how the fields display.


Let's look at the types of custom fields we can create. We'll focus on one field we just added.

We hit the create new record button  and created a List type custom field. For the list type we entered a description, Field Type as List, and then entered display values users will choose from.


If we decide this should be a text field, we can change the Field Type to Text and enter a Text Length value. This will be the number of characters allowed.


For a Number type field, select Number as the Field Type and then enter a Min Value and a Max Value.


For a date type custom field, select Date as the Field Type. No additional parameters are needed, users will be able to type or pick a date from a calendar for this type.


For a yes/no type field, select YesNo for the Field Type. The field will display a checkbox for users to toggle with this type.


For a color type field, select Color for the Field Type. This will add a color box with the system's color palette available to choose.


If you wish to have multiple values to pick from, select Entity for the Field Type. You can then select a LookupID, or enter Display Values for users to choose from. Select the Limit to List checkbox to allow users to pick only from the lookup or from the Display Values. If left unchecked, users can type in their own value to the field.


For an integer type field, select Integer from the Display Type field. Then enter a Min Value and Max Value to create a range users can enter numbers for.


For an email type field, select Email for the Field Type. Then set a Text Length value. Note: this field is like a text field, there is not validation functionality to check what has been entered as a valid email address.


For URLs, select Url from the Field Type list. Enter a Text Length value. There is no functionality to interact with the address to verify it, what is entered is what will display.


For enumerated lists, select EnumList for the Field Type. Enter a Text Length value to restrict the number of characters allowed.


For a memo, select Memo in the Field Type. There are no additional parameters to select for this type.

4833713b-715f-4388-83fd-d3376bfbeea8.title: Design Studio - Export/Import Custom Metadata
4833713b-715f-4388-83fd-d3376bfbeea8.content:
Problem
Design Studio has a built-in feature called Export/Import Custom Metadata. This allows you to backup Design Studio changes as an XML file. This can then be used to import Design Studio changes to another company, sandbox environment, or to restore changes from a certain point in time.

Note: Design Studio changes are saved to the database and retained in those backups. If a sandbox is refreshed with a production database backup they will have those production designs. This function can help to save any pre-production designs or changes to put back in to the sandbox environment.

Resolution
To use the Export/Import Custom Metadata feature, navigate to System Data > Export/Import Custom Metadata.

Next, change the Transfer Type to Export. In the lower section of the screen you will see all the possible areas that can be exported.
Select all for a full export/backup of the metadata, else check the individual features you with to export.

Select a destination to save this file. Consider adding a date stamp or other meaningful variation to help identify it later.


Next we'll look at the import process. When the time comes to use this file, in the company you wish to import to, navigate to System Data > Export/Import Custom Metadata. This time, we will choose Import for the Transfer Type.

Select the file you wish to use, in this example we only have one file but there could be multiple depending on what was backed up and when.


This will pull in all the Design Studio changes saved to that file into the detail of the screen.

Looking in the details, we only see a few things compared to the Export screen. This is because we only had a few changes made to Design Studio. What you see here represents what was chosen for the export, and of those choices, what has been done in Design Studio.

Click OK to import the selected changes.

Note: Individual modified functions cannot be selected. The whole category is exported and imported.
In our example, if Custom Layout Company is checked for the import, all custom layouts are imported.

28cc905a-982d-467a-9b36-5f8e8c5ded1e.title: Design Studio - Custom Layouts Default Vs. Named
28cc905a-982d-467a-9b36-5f8e8c5ded1e.content:
Problem
Customers may encounter issues where their Design Studio form or report changes do not show for Traverse users. Design Studio changes can be saved as the default or as a named layout. If they are saved as a named layout, they must be assigned to user in order for them to see these changes. If they are saved as the default, all users will see the change.

See the resolution on how to check how a form or report is saved, and how to assign users to it.

Resolution
- Navigate to Design Studio and open this for the company database which you are seeing the issue in.

- Under Designers, click Custom Layouts


- Review the entries and look for the entry related to the issue.
We'll pick on AP Transactions for example.

- There are two custom changes for AP Transactions
- One is a default save, we know this because the layout name is blank. All users in this company will see this change.

- The other entry is a named save as the layout name has a value, in this case Purchasing Dept 1


- If we click on the second record for the named layout, the Assign To button becomes available.
Click the Assign To button in the top-right of the screen to open the users list. This will tell us who can see this change.

- Review the list of user logins, any users with unchecked boxes means they cannot see the change. If they should see it, check the box next to their login and click OK.
In this example, no users can see the change.


If users do not show up in the list, be sure to review their security setup to ensure they are set up in the expected company.
For any additional issues with this topic, please reach out to technical support for further assistance.

33bd1bc7-82ac-4d40-afab-c3498f04cabc.title: Traverse - Is It Modified?
33bd1bc7-82ac-4d40-afab-c3498f04cabc.content:
Problem
One common support challenge with the Traverse platform is customizations, many Traverse customers have customizations present in their environment. When questions and issues arise sometimes we can't easily discern if we have a customization in play. If testing issues, we may be dealing with many layers of programming and only one of those layers is a problem.

Customizations can be present via custom coded modifications, Design Studio changes, active scripts, even custom programs and utilities. We'll discuss some strategies in this article that should help clear up the confusion.

The information in this KB is contextual to the issue at hand. Some of this may be helpful at different points in time, depending on what the individual issue is.

Resolution
SOWs/CBRs
Both of these acronyms are really just services related documents that discuss customer modifications. If you suspect a customer has a modification in an area of the software you are investigating, check our documentation to see if it contains relevant information to your search. The location these documents are stored was changed in 2021 and there are two places to check. For newer work check the first link below. For older work, check the second link. You may need to look in both.

Customization-related information for 2021 and onward: Services New Customizations
Legacy customization-related information: Legacy Customization documentation

Scripting Enabled
If you are investigating an issue and see Scripting Enabled in the bottom corner of the screen, there may be a script added to the form via Design Studio or potentially as custom code as a standalone python assembly.

You may also check within the Traverse client folder for any python (.py) files related to the function.
In this example, Accounts Payable Transactions does have a python script present as indicated by the Scripting Enabled label and the physical file:


Custom Assemblies - Coded Customizations
There are multiple ways to check for coded modifications.

One method is to check the Program Info in Help > Program Info. If Traverse is already open, close it and re-open and go straight to the function in question and open it. The reason for closing this first is in case anything else is loaded up. As a user processes in Traverse, every function loads the assemblies it needs in order to do whatever the user needs to do, closing the software clears this so you can get a more focused picture of what is loaded specifically for the function in question.

This method serves to tell you if what you are using has any related modifications. Load something up in that function, for example if the function is SO Orders, open an order. What you see in Program Info is reactive to what you are doing so for a deeper example, you may need to open an SO Order and add a line item, then check the Program Info to see what is loaded.
This is ProcessPro Global, SO Orders has been loaded up. We can see there are at least two modifications in play, TRAVERSE.Client.SalesOrderPP and TRAVERSE.Data.ARTransactionPP.
There are many assemblies loaded that we do not see in the shot above.

An additional method is to check for custom assemblies in Design Studio, looking in System Data > Custom Menu. If you know the MenuID of the function you are using, you can check in here to confirm it is customized. This function provides you with the MenuID that is customized, in addition to the custom assembly, plugin, and custom description if used.

You may also see this information in tblSmMenuCustom if accessing the SQL database.

Lastly, you can check within Traverse > System Manager > Setup and Maintenance > Application Menus, and then navigate to the function in question. This will tell you if a function is overridden, however it may not provide as much information at the above methods.

Traverse (Global) Server Manager
You can use the Traverse Global Server Manager Application to check if any custom server update has been deployed. In the Traverse Global Server Manager Application, navigate to Help > Maintenance History, and then review the update sources. Consider filtering by database if there are many databases or much history to review.

This won't tell you specifically what is modified, but it will help indicate that something custom to the software has been applied.
If the listed update source(s) are still present on the server, it may be possible to open the related TSMX in notepad and read through what the update processes to to determine more information about the customization. Most custom server updates will contain everything needed so the most recent update is likely the only one you need to open but it can depend on other factors.

Design Studio
You can check for Design Studio changes if you are logged in to Design Studio for the company in question.
Check in Custom layouts for any Report or Form changes that have been saved to the database. Once identified, you can open these to see how the modified versions look.

Any custom fields will exist in the Manage and Assign functions.

Any changes to Lookups, Views, Business Rules, Search Catalogue, Schemas, and Alerts can also be seen in their respective Design Studio functions. Some of these use a Replace ID so the custom entries should have a Replace ID to make them stand out. It is a good practice to check the regular entries as users may improperly make changes to the regular entries as a means to modify the feature.

If unsure, always compare what the customer has to a vanilla environment to better see the differences.
Comparison tools greatly help for folders and files to help you determine what has been changed and how.
Notepad++ has a comparison tool that is quite helpful comparing SQL statements, lists of items, XML, etc.

SQL Profiler
SQL Profiler is a more advanced tool that offers users the ability to watch SQL's processing through traces. It can help users see tables and procedures in use during processing. The trace can help reveal if customizations are in use but depends on the customization design. It may not be useful at times as a result but deserves a mention.

50641ad2-293f-482b-9489-0a44cf8a5f19.title: How to resolve the error "Fiscal period(s) [X/XXXX] are closed. Transactions cannot be written to closed periods" when attempting to write journal entries for the new Year??
50641ad2-293f-482b-9489-0a44cf8a5f19.content:
Problem
How to resolve the error "Fiscal period(s) [X/XXXX] are closed. Transactions cannot be written to closed periods"?



The client is in the Period 12 of current Fiscal Year [For example 2024] and trying to write entries to the Period 1 of the next Year [2025]. Yet, they are getting the below error message pointing to the period 1 that was closed for the Year 2024.

Resolution
This error indicates that the 'Fiscal period' corresponding to the 'Fiscal Year' mentioned in the error message is closed. in order to move further with writing the Journal entries, the user need to ensure that they are on the right 'Fiscal Year'



As the client is in the Period 12 of current Fiscal Year [For example 2024] and trying to write entries to the Period 1 of the next Year [2025], then there are chances that the user did not switch the Fiscal Year accordingly. And Traverse is still pointing to 2024 and the Fiscal period 1 of 2024 had already been closed in the SM Period Conversion [NOTE: The User can open the Period being pointed in the SM Period Conversion to get rid of this error. But the user intends to write Journal entries to 2025, and not 2024]

This can be confirmed by pulling in the 'Year' column from Column Chooser in the GL Transactions screen. Here we can observe that even if the user wanted to write to 2025, Traverse was pointing to 2024:



a. At this point, the user would need to navigate to the GL Change Fiscal Year under the path: Applications -> General Ledger -> Periodic Processing -> Change Fiscal year [The user can also access this screen by double-clicking on the Fiscal Year field at the left bottom of the screen]:



b. Switch to the next Year [in this case 2025] and click on 'OK' at the top of the screen [NOTE: If you would like to switch only for the current session, and need to restore the Year back to the old Year when you re-login later, then please ensure to check the 'Change for this session only' checkbox]:



c. Once this 'Fiscal Year' had been switched, we can observe the change in the Fiscal Year:



d. The user can make the manual entries as needed in the GL Transactions screen and we can observe that now the GL entries are pointing towards the new Year [2025], we can observe from the 'Year' column [In most cases, we need to pull from the Column Chooser], to which Year it is about to be written:



e. Now, the user can proceed with writing theses Journals without any issues:

07d62c52-6188-470b-9349-54ad4d3154c9.title: How to transfer billings in Project Costing?
07d62c52-6188-470b-9349-54ad4d3154c9.content:
Problem
The customer would like to know how to transfer billings in Project Costing.

Resolution
1.Create a New Project: Navigate to Applications > project Costing > Setup & Maintenance > Projects

2.Create a new project using an existing customer ID. Set up a new Project ID and additional fields such as Employee rate and O/H Allocation code from the drop-down menus, then save the project. Make sure to check the boxes “Billable” and “Fixed Fee” and allocate a Distribution code before you hit save.

Once, you hit save, you can see the Project ID titled as “Main Test” visible in the drop down of that specific Customer ID. Here the customer ID that we have chosen is 00001.



Now, we need to create a new task: Click on "New task" in the toolbar and enter the task code and phase code. Hit Save.



3. Create AP Transaction: Create a new Accounts Payable (AP) transaction with an Item ID that is not linked to the inventory i.e. the item should not be an item existing in the Inventory.



When you try to enter such an item, you will get a prompt stating that Item ID “...” does not exist in the Inventory. Click Ok.

The screen will look like this once after you successfully create an AP transaction and save it.

Now, Use the "Project" tab in the sub-menu to associate the newly created project with this transaction.

This will open up the dialog box below. Enter the Project ID from the drop-down to link the created Project ID to this transaction.

4. Preview and Post AP Transaction:

Preview the Purchase Journal to review the AP transaction.

Then, post the AP transaction by checking the required boxes and selecting the specific batch code and clicking on OK to proceed.

5.Navigate to Time Ticket Entry: Go to Project Costing > Transactions > Time Ticket Entry.



Select the appropriate Batch code (e.g. #APTST). Set up the Employee ID and associate the project/task with the employee, assigning hours for the project.



Note: Filling the Project/Task and Rate code is mandatory.



Now, save the time ticket entry.

6.Preview Time Ticket Journal: Navigate to the Time Ticket Journal. Apply the Project ID filter and select the batch code.

Preview the time ticket entry.

7. Update PC Transactions:

Go to PC Transactions by navigating to Project Costing > Transactions > Transactions

Add the specific project (e.g., Main Test). Update the Location ID, GL account, and Unit Cost as needed, then save the transaction.



Preview and Post PC Transaction: Preview the PC Transaction Journal.



Post the PC transaction by navigating to Project Costing > Transactions > Post transactions

Select all the required checkboxes and then click Ok to post as shown below



8.Transfer Billings: Navigate to the billing section and select Transfer Billings.

Filter by Project ID and enter the batch code. Click "Prepare" to view the fixed fee.

Select the project to transfer the billings for and click "Transfer." This will open a dialog box. Mark the Consolidated Billing check box to consolidate billings. This means if you have multiple projects for the same customer, you can combine the projects into one invoice rather than a separate invoice for each project.

Mark the Hold check box to put the billings that you transfer on hold to be reviewed before further processing.

Accept or edit the default Fiscal Period/Year.

Enter any Comments, as applicable.

Click OK to execute the Transfer Billings process



Once done, you will get the below prompt stating “Billing transferred”

e9b5d6db-946b-4416-a1e0-aba64300cae1.title: How to fix the error: 'Unable to process the source information.  The source does not match the requirements of the layout.' while performing Import.
e9b5d6db-946b-4416-a1e0-aba64300cae1.content:
Problem
How to fix the error: 'Unable to process the source information.  The source does not match the requirements of the layout.' while performing Import?

Resolution
This error message indicates that the data type defined for each field in a specific layout (i.e., the module or dataset under consideration) is not being adhered to during the import process. Each field is configured to accept only specific types of characters or values that align with its predefined data type. For instance, a field defined to accept "Numbers" will only allow numeric values; any non-numeric characters will result in an error.



When defining the Import Layout Definition, it is essential to ensure that the data type for each field is correctly set and reflects the intended input requirements. Additionally, the data in the Import File (commonly an Excel sheet or a CSV file) must strictly conform to the data type restrictions specified in the layout.



Key Considerations:

- Ensure there are no empty fields in the Import .csv file.
- Validate the Data type in the Import .csv file is aligned to the Import Layout Definition, to ensure all fields have the correct data type.
- Verify that the data conversion set up in the Import Layout Definition is aligning to the need of Traverse and the ensure if all the fields are properly mapped to the 'Property' fields in the Import Map Definition.



Example scenario 1: The Import .csv file is having an empty Field in it. And this was found by manual verification. [Note: This is an example scenario, so there are limited records in it. In real time, we may have hundreds of records]:

- Import Layout Definition:

- Import Map Definition:
