Resolution: Updated the required data needed on that cell of the .csv file and saved the same. Then, we will be able to proceed with importing the data.



Example scenario 2: The Import .csv file is having the data corresponding to the 'Date' field in an encrypted format, which was not aligning to the Import Layout defined. That is, in the Import Layout, it was defined to read the Data in the 'Date' format, while it is encrypted as Raw data.  [Note: We can also manipulate the Import file to change the format of the 'Date' column. But it is always recommended to update the Import Layout Definition, so that there need not be any manual intervention before importing the file into Traverse]:

- Import Layout Definition:

- Import Map Definition:

- Import .csv file:

Resolution: In this case, we need to update the Layout, such that initially the data need to be read as 'Rawdata', and subsequently converted to the 'Date' format as required. This new field should be then mapped in the Import Map Definition as well.

- Import Layout Defintion:

- Import Map Definition:



Example scenario 3: The Import .csv file is having all the data fields with the right format and the cells are completely filled. Still, we are getting the same error message.

- Import Layout Definition:

- Import Map Definition:

- Import .csv file:

Resolution: Here, the Data mapping might not be aligning to the needs of Traverse. For instance, the 'Property' field might be pointing to the 'DebitAmtFgn', and the expectation is to map it to the field 'DebitAmt', which is converted to the numerical format. But the User might have mapped it to the field 'Debit' which is still in the raw data format, from the perspective of Traverse. Once this misalignment was fixed and the Import Map Definition was saved, the user will be able to import without any issues. [Note: It is just an example. And any input not aligning with the Data type defined will fall under this criterion]

35242b6d-0228-4668-8cf4-ef9afadbdee0.title: Setting up employee in System Manager
35242b6d-0228-4668-8cf4-ef9afadbdee0.content:
Problem
How to setup Employee in System Manager?

Resolution
Use the Employees function to set up employee information such as name, address, birth date, phone, email address, and emergency contact if Payroll is not installed. If Payroll is installed, use the Employee Information function on the Payroll Setup and Maintenance menu.

The Employees screen also allows you to set up mobile profiles for users of Mobile WMS, as well as the mobile apps associated with Field Service and Service Repair.



- Employee Information Tab: First, Navigate to Application > System Manager > Company Setup > Employees



1.1 Click on the + icon to open up a new record.



1.2 Enter an Employee ID.

1.3 Select a Status for the employee. You can select the status to either be Active or Inactive. Active is always preferable if the employee is still in the organization and is an active employee.

1.4 Enter the employees’ information in the remaining fields, as applicable.



1.5 In the Username field, select a SM User to associate with the employee. Use the Browse button to view the drop-down list or click the Plus button to open the SM Users function and add a new user.

1.6 Now, Click the Save button, on the toolbar, to save the new employee record.

2. Technician Tab:

This tab is available only if you have the Service Director application installed.

You can create a technician ID for the employee on the Technician tab. This tab also allows you to create a crew.

There is already a KB with the Number 000092372 for this. Follow the same steps to set up Technicians in System Manager.



3. WMS tab

This tab is available only if you have the WMS application installed.

You can create a WMS user for the employee on the WMS tab.

To add the employee as a new WMS user:

3.1 Use the New button on the WMS tab toolbar to open the Add New User window.

3.2 The employee ID for the current employee appears in the User ID drop-down field.

3.3Select a Location ID from the drop-down list.

3.4Click OK to add the employee to the list of WMS users.

3.5 Save your changes.

NOTE: You will still have to grant WMS user permissions to the employee using the WM Users maintenance screen.

For this you would need to navigate to WM> Setup and Maintenance > Users and assign the required permissions.





4. Employee Default Tab:

The Employee Default section at the bottom of the screen is intended to support employee defaults that may be added in vertical-aligned implementations of Traverse, such as Service Repair or Field Service. The Employee Default section has no use in base Traverse at this time.

b5ef7283-4026-4765-b7d9-fb875d6bbc05.title: Removing Inactive Vendors from Vendor List
b5ef7283-4026-4765-b7d9-fb875d6bbc05.content:

e710c551-a895-45c3-8bfc-de0d8b178773.title: Retiring Assets: Process and Guidelines
e710c551-a895-45c3-8bfc-de0d8b178773.content:
Problem
Retiring Assets: Process and Guidelines

Resolution
Use the Retire Assets function to retire or dispose of the asset when the asset reaches the end of its useful life or when you have taken all the depreciation you can. The Retire Assets function changes the asset's status to 'Retired', enters a retirement date in the asset record, and puts a stop to depreciation calculations involving the asset.

Select an asset to retire from the Active Asset ID field.

- Enter a brief reason for the retirement in the Retirement Reason field.
- Enter the applicable retirement code in the Retirement Code field. This field is user-definable. For example, you might enter S if you sold the asset, D if you donated it, or O if it has become obsolete.
- Enter the date to retire the asset from the Retirement Date field.
- Enter the quantity of the asset you want to retire in the Retirement Quantity field. You can retire part or all of the asset. For example, if the original asset quantity was 4, you can enter 1 to retire one unit of the asset.
Note: If you retire part of a multiple-unit asset, the asset status does not change to Retired until the entire dollar value of the asset has been retired.
- In the Retirement Amount box, the adjusted cost (times the retirement quantity percentage, if other than 100 percent) appears. Accept the cost that appears or enter the dollar value of the asset.
- Enter the amount of funds gained by the retirement of the asset in the Retirement Proceeds field.
- Enter the cost for disposal of the asset in the Retirement Expenses field. Proceeds less Expenses are used in the Gains and Losses Report.
- Enter any other applicable information in the Comments field.
- Select the Depreciation Detail tab to view all four types of depreciation (A.M.T., BOOK, FEDTAX, and OTHER) for the retired asset. This tab is for information use only.

- Click a command button to

SelectToRetire AssetRetire the selected asset.ActivityDisplay the Activity Log to view retire asset activity.ResetReset all fields to their default selections.

33048ecd-cd3d-4c5e-ba6b-c5820c94b5c3.title: Barcode scanner not pulling the Item ID in the IN Physical counts entry screen
33048ecd-cd3d-4c5e-ba6b-c5820c94b5c3.content:
Problem
The Barcode scanner not highlighting the Item ID in IN Physical counts entry screen.

Resolution
A Barcode Scanner is designed to interpret the numbers or text embedded within a barcode. However, if a User attempts to scan a barcode in Traverse where there is no active text input field, it may appear as though the scanner is not functioning.

The Physical Counts Entry screen can be found under the path: Applications -> Inventory -> Physical Inventory -> Physical Counts Entry:



In the Physical Counts Entry screen, users can locate the Item ID by scanning the Barcode into one of the following fields:

- Auto Filter Row Field
- Filter value



i. Auto Filter Row: The 'Auto Filter Row' field is the recommended option as it remains visible on the screen at all times, making the process of updating counts seamless and efficient.

a. In order to add the 'Auto Filter Row', the user need to right click on any of the 'Header' and select the 'Show Auto Filter Row' from the context menu:



b. Once the Auto Filter Row appears, place the cursor in the field corresponding to the Item ID column.

c. Scan the barcode using the barcode scanner, and the corresponding Item ID will be automatically located:



ii. Filter Value: Alternatively, users can utilize the Filter option in the Item ID column to locate items via barcode scanning:

a. Click the filter icon on the Item ID column header to open the filter options. Place the cursor in the text field within the filter dialog box and scan the barcode.

c. The filter will locate the specific Item ID corresponding to the scanned barcode:

a28adf9f-4ce6-40a2-aef7-1e201885343b.title: How to add 'Favorites' in Traverse 11.0?

How to add 'Favorites' in Traverse 11.0?

68039d68-d949-4e9e-9f75-ad5f22c9dc43.title: How to apply Deposits for AR Transactions?
68039d68-d949-4e9e-9f75-ad5f22c9dc43.content:
Problem
How to apply Deposits for AR Transactions?

Resolution
Kindly follow the below steps for creating an AR Transaction and applying deposits to the same:



i. Navigate to the Transactions Screen: Go to the AR Transactions screen under the path: Applications -> Accounts Receivable -> Transactions -> Transactions:



ii. Create a New AR Transaction:

- Click on the '+' icon to create a New Record. Choose the Transaction Type as either Invoice or Credit Memo.
- Enter the Location ID, Batch Code, and Customer ID and Invoice and PO Date. Review the defaulted information from the customer profile and edit the same if needed.
- In the Line Item section, enter the required Item IDs. [Note: The system will use the sales account, COGS account, and inventory account associated with the Item ID]



iii. Add details on the Ship-To Tab:



iv. Navigate to the 'Payments Tab': To include deposits or prepayments:

- Click the "+" icon to add a record.
- Select the appropriate Deposit ID Batch Code.
- Enter the Cash Receipt Amount.
- Choose the appropriate Payment Method ID

Note: All prepayments entered on this screen are applied directly to the invoice but must be posted through AR > Transaction Journals > Post Cash Receipts.



v. Save the Transaction: Once the Payment was applied, the Net Due becomes 0.00



vi. Verify details in the Sales Journal for unposted entries: Navigate to the 'Sales Journal' screen under the path: Applications -> Accounts Receivable -> Transaction Journals:



vii. Post the Transaction: Post the Transaction under the path: Applications -> Accounts Receivable -> Transaction Journal -> Post Transactions:

2a187d85-0a0a-4568-93a5-e285ad8cc4e9.title: How to whitelist IPs on a Firewall?
2a187d85-0a0a-4568-93a5-e285ad8cc4e9.content:
Problem
How to whitelist IPs on a Firewall?

Resolution
If the Client is using Firewall, they can whitelist IPs to grant access to their network resources for several specific users.



In Windows, IP whitelisting is typically done through the built-in Windows Defender Firewall or other security tools.



Step 1: Open Windows Defender Firewall:

- Click on the Start Menu and search for Windows Defender Firewall.
- Select Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security.



Step 2: Click on the Advanced settings:



Step 3: To create a New Inbound Rule In the left-hand pane, click on Inbound Rules.



Step 4: In the right-hand pane, click New Rule....



Step 5: In the New Inbound Rule Wizard, follow these steps:

- Rule Type: Select Custom and click Next.

- Program: Choose whether to apply the rule to all programs or a specific one, then click Next.

- Protocol and Ports: Leave it as default unless you want to specify a particular protocol (e.g., TCP or UDP) or port.

- Scope: Under Which remote IP addresses do this rule apply to? select these IP addresses and click Add.... Enter the IP address or range you want to whitelist and click OK.

- Action: Select Allow the connection and click Next.

- Profile: Choose the profile(s) (Domain, Private, Public) where the rule should apply and click Next.

- Name: Give the rule a meaningful name (e.g., "Whitelist IP XXX.XXX.X.XX") and click Finish.



Step 6: Verify the Rule Locate the rule in the Inbound Rules list. Ensure that it is enabled (check for a green checkmark icon).

9d0d6c1c-52b5-4a40-87f2-c7fd8e008178.title: Aptean Routing in System Manager
9d0d6c1c-52b5-4a40-87f2-c7fd8e008178.content:
Problem
Aptean Routing in System Manager

Resolution
The Routing Mapping function maps data from the Action query to Aptean Routing & Scheduling API fields. A default "Paragon" Mapping is included, but it's recommended to create a custom Mapping to avoid overwriting during updates.

To create a new Mapping:

- Navigate to System Manager > Aptean Routing, click New Record, select the Service, and enter a name for your integration.
- Use Copy From to select the "Paragon" Mapping, then save and adjust as needed.

The Fields tab defines available fields for mapping. You can modify existing fields (e.g., changing the data for TDATA04) or add new fields (e.g., CALL.TDATA12) by adding a new record with the required details (Description, Field Type, Length, and Format).

The Mappings tab allows you to map Action query fields to the API. You can add, remove, or adjust fields as necessary, ensuring only relevant fields are transmitted.

3e6b7e84-61bf-4190-bf74-82e483b574fd.title: Keyboard OSAS
3e6b7e84-61bf-4190-bf74-82e483b574fd.content:
Problem
How to customize the function and editing keys for text screens on your workstation

Resolution
Use the Keyboard function to customize the function and editing keys for text screens on your workstation. You can also use this function to copy a keyboard layout to another workstation or set of workstations during setup. This function is not available if you use the graphical mode for function screens.

Keyboard assignments are stored in the OSKY file in the \sysfil directory. If you delete this file, OSAS creates a new one based on standard defaults. If you experience issues with your keyboard on a UNIX system, use this function to make adjustments to keyboard assignments.

Follow these steps to change the keys assigned to commands:

1. Select Keyboard from the User Setup menu.

2. Enter the workstation ID for which you want to edit the keyboard definition
3. The Copy From field appears if you enter a new workstation ID. To copy the keyboard definition from another workstation, enter that workstation ID. If you have a multiuser system, save time when you set up workstations with similar keyboards by copying a keyboard definition to other workstations. Enter the workstation ID to which you want to copy the current keyboard definition in the Copy To field and press Enter. To copy the keyboard definitions to all workstations, enter *ALL and press Enter. If you are changing keys on one workstation only, press Enter to skip this field. To save time, copy keyboard definitions to all workstations, then edit the few workstations that need differing definitions later.
4. The command description, type (Screen or Edit), default control character or escape sequence, key label, and user label for each command appears in the list. To change a key definition, select the command for the definition you want to edit and press Enter.
5. An asterisk appears next to the key you are changing. To change the key assigned to the command, press the key you want to use. The cursor moves to the User Label field and the label of the key you pressed appears. You cannot reassign a key if that key is already in use for another command. For example, if you want to assign the Delete command to the F6 key, you first need to change the key assigned to the Maintenance command, then assign F6 to the Delete command.
6. To change the key’s description, enter the user label you want to appear when you are prompted for a command response in the User Label field and press Enter. Press Enter if you do not want to change the default entry.
7. To change the definition for another key, use the arrow keys to select the command you want to change and press Enter, then repeat steps 6 and 7.

8. Press W to write your changes to the keyboard definition file and return to the main menu.

5300257a-283f-4cd4-8d2a-bdd79a860a9a.title: Editing Help Screen (OSAS)
5300257a-283f-4cd4-8d2a-bdd79a860a9a.content:
Problem
How to add or change text on OSAS help screens

Resolution
Use the Help Screens function to add or change text on OSAS help screens. Help screen text is stored in the XXHELP file, where XX represents the application ID.

Follow these steps to work with OSAS help text:
1. Select Help Screens from the System File Utilities menu

2. Enter the Application ID and Help Key for which you want to view or edit text.
3. The Copy From field appears if you enter a new help key. You can just enter the help key from which you want to copy the help text or leave the field blank to continue.
4. Enter or edit the name of the field or the title of the help screen in the Field ID field. Use brackets to make the text you enter appear in bold. If you leave the field blank, the Copy From screen appears. Enter a similar field ID to copy help text to this help ID. If you choose a field ID that appears in more than one program, you must select the specific program from which you want to copy. When you press Enter, the field ID and the help text appear.
5. The help text for the field you selected appears in the scrolling region. Use the commands to edit this text.

-  Press Enter to edit the selected line. When the Help Text screen appears, edit the text as necessary and use the Proceed (OK) command to return to the Help Screens screen. Your changes are saved automatically. Use brackets to make the text you enter appear in bold.
- Press A to add a line of help text to the end of the list. When the Help Text screen appears, enter the text to add and use the Proceed (OK) command to return to the Help Screens screen. Your changes are saved automatically. Use brackets to make the text you enter appear in bold.
- Press H to return to the Field ID field in the header section of the screen.
- Press C to copy help text from another field. When the Copy From screen appears, enter the field from which to copy information and use the Proceed (OK) command to return to the Help Screens screen and edit the text you copied.

6. Press F7 to close the screen and return to the menu.

5ffde23c-6eeb-4b4a-a1fc-c6c0dae561c5.title: Purchase Price Variance (PPV) Report
5ffde23c-6eeb-4b4a-a1fc-c6c0dae561c5.content:
Problem
I am trying to put together a Purchase Price Variance (PPV) Report but I don’t see that there is a direct report to pull out of Traverse for this. I did some digging within Traverse and noticed that in Inventory Valuation View, there is a column option for a PPV Amt. Can you please advise what tables/information this column is pulling from? Also, regarding a PPV report, is there a way to prepare a report that I could monitor using our average costing?

Resolution
When it comes to Traverse and PPV, it’s important to note that PPVs are typically observed when using Standard Costing rather than Average Costing. Average Costing inherently adjusts the inventory valuation based on purchase prices, which can make it less suited for highlighting variances.

Regarding the "PPV Amt" column mentioned, it seems to derive its data from a temporary table that is generated when the Inventory Valuation View is executed. Specifically, the "TotPurchPriceVar" value is populated by the procedure that runs during the view's execution.

Also, when we check the Design Studio > view table > under ID InItemValuation.

Click on its respective Data_source we will see only a temporary view name instead of a query.

9fd033a0-3f5b-4860-b42f-00dd11a57849.title: How to perform Inventory Location Transfer?
9fd033a0-3f5b-4860-b42f-00dd11a57849.content:
Problem
How to perform Inventory Location Transfer?

Resolution
The Location Transfers function is used to move items from one location to another. When we enter a transfer, the Traverse system updates the quantities accordingly.

- Source Location: The Quantity on Hand and Quantity Available decrease by the number of items sent to the destination.
- Destination Location: The Quantity on Hand and Quantity Available increase by the number of items received from the source.



The User need to follow the below steps for accomplishing the Location Transfer:



i. Navigate to the IN Location Transfer screen under the path: Applications -> Inventory -> Transactions -> Location Transfers:



ii. Click the New button, on the toolbar, to open a blank location transfer record. Select the location from which we need to transfer the item from the From Location ID field [If we are transferring a serialized item, the serial number must exist.] Select the location to which we need to transfer the item from the To Location ID field. Accept the default Unit of measure for the item or select a different unit of measure. Enter the quantity of the item you want to transfer in the Quantity field. If needed, enter the cost of the transfer in the Transfer Cost field.



iii. Click on 'Save' icon at the top. Once saved, we cannot change the From Location, To Location, Item ID, and Unit fields.



iv. The User can now post the 'Batch', IN Post Transfers screen under the path:  Applications -> Inventory -> Transactions -> Post Transfers. [When location transfers are posted, the transfer cost is recorded in the GL account designated for transfer costs based on the GL account code assigned to the source item location. This transfer cost is incorporated into the extended cost at the destination location, thereby updating the item's cost in the "To" location to reflect the added transfer cost]

29cff5f4-79ff-4f58-a2d0-9b058c76cf2f.title: .NET Installation Error for Traverse Client
29cff5f4-79ff-4f58-a2d0-9b058c76cf2f.content:
Problem
A customer encountered an error message indicating that .NET Framework 3.5 or higher was required during the installation of the Traverse client, despite having .NET Framework 4.8 installed.

Cause
The error message indicating that .NET Framework 3.5 or higher is required, despite having .NET Framework 4.8 installed, is likely due to the need for .NET Framework 3.5 specifically for certain applications. Some software, including Traverse, may require .NET Framework 3.5 to be enabled, even if a higher version is installed. This can lead to installation errors if .NET Framework 3.5 is not activated in the Windows Features settings.

Resolution
Open the Control Panel on your computer.

Navigate to 'Programs and Features'.

Look for the option 'Turn Windows features on or off' and click on it.

In the Windows Features window, check if the box for '.NET Framework 3.5' is selected. If it is not selected, please select it.

After making this change, save the settings and close the window. Try to install the Traverse client again.

d638a500-9ee7-4cec-a1fd-da466674e80f.title: How to activate a Product key with 'Manual Activation' in Traverse Global License Server Manager?
d638a500-9ee7-4cec-a1fd-da466674e80f.content:
Problem
How to activate a Product key with 'Manual Activation' in Traverse Global License Server Manager?



When the Server workstation with TLSM doesn't have the Internet connection to it, the User will get the prompt for Manual Activation:



Upon clicking on 'Yes', the below window will appear:

Resolution
Manual activation is typically required when the server workstation is not connected to the network. In such cases, users need a manual Activation code for License activation processes and need to retrieve the ActivationCode manually using an API tool. To achieve this, API tools like Postman are recommended for their ease of use and functionality.



There are two primary methods to obtain the Manual Activation Code for a given Product ID and Site ID:

- Using Windows PowerShell
- Using Postman



I. Windows PowerShell:

-
Run the Script for Manual Activation Code: Launch Windows PowerShell from the Windows search bar and execute the below script:

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Traverse Global
# Define the API endpoint and parameters
$apiUrl = "https://traverseupdates.osas.com/externallm/api/License/Activate"

# Define the parameters for the API call
$param1 = "999998"
$param2 = "DA915180-3629-40A8-A983-2B516466C7D5"
$param3 = "APT01-BXZ17D3"

# Prompt the user for inputs
$siteId = Read-Host "Enter the SiteId"
$productId = Read-Host "Enter the ProductId"
$machineId = Read-Host "Enter the MachineId"

# Create a hashtable to hold the parameters
$body = @{
SiteId    = $siteId
ProductId = $productId
MachineId = $machineId
}

# Convert the hashtable to JSON
$jsonBody = $body | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10

# Make the API call using Invoke-RestMethod
try {
$response = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $apiUrl -Method POST -Body $jsonBody -ContentType "application/json"

# Extract and display the 'Info' value
if ($response.PSObject.Properties["Info"]) {
Write-Output "Manual Activation Code:"
$response.Info
Write-Output "" # Line break
} else {
Write-Output "The response does not contain an 'Info' field."
Write-Output "" # Line break
}

# Check the 'Status' value and display corresponding messages
if ($response.PSObject.Properties["Status"]) {
$status = $response.Status
if ($status -eq 0) {
Write-Output "Successfully processed the license."
} else {
Write-Output "Manual Activation could not be completed based on this Site ID, Product ID, and Machine ID."
}
} else {
Write-Output "The response does not contain a 'Status' field."
}
} catch {
# Handle errors
Write-Output "Error occurred:"
Write-Output $_.Exception.Message
}

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-
Provide Required Inputs: Once the User hits the 'Enter' key, the script will prompt the User to input the following, one after the other:

- Site ID
- Product ID
- Machine ID

-
Validation of Inputs

- If any of the inputs are incorrect or invalid, the script will display an error indicating activation failure.

-
- For valid inputs, the script will generate and display the Activation Code.





-
Copying the Activation Code

- The Activation Code is a long string that always ends with an equal sign (=).
- Copy the entire code and paste it into the Traverse Global License Server to complete the activation process.





II. Postman is a versatile tool designed for API testing and interaction. It simplifies the process of retrieving the ActivationCode by securely sending data to a server and processing the server’s response.



Prerequisites:

- A valid API endpoint for License activation: https://traverseupdates.osas.com/externallm/api/License/Activate
- The below Parameters consisting of License information and the product version:
- Site ID
- Product ID
- Machine ID [The workstation ID, where the License is about to be activated/Server is hosted]

- Access to Postman (either desktop or web version)



Procedure:

Step 1: Access Postman

- Open Postman Web in your browser or launch the Postman desktop application. [The example illustrates the Browser]
- Log into your account or use it as a guest (if permitted).



Step 2: Create a New Request

- Click + New Tab or go to an existing collection and select Add Request.



Step 3: Configure the API Request:

- Set the Request Method: Select POST from the dropdown menu next to the request URL.

2e36d451-8d7f-4d9c-b735-68e7212ec460.title: "Invalid GL Account(s) exist" error when posting Bill of Material > Work Order
2e36d451-8d7f-4d9c-b735-68e7212ec460.content:
Problem
When trying to post from Bill of Material > Work Order> Post Work Orders, the user is getting the error "Invalid GL Account(s) exist"

50000 : 90026 : Invalid GL Account. : Procedure{trgGlJrnlI} : Procedure{dbo.trav_RaiseError_proc}
Uncommittable transaction is detected at the end of the batch. The transaction is rolled back. (.Net SqlClient Data Provider)

Resolution
Follow the below steps to troubleshoot/ find the Inactive GL Account:

Isolate the Work Order(s) that will not post. Look at the Item ID for a Work Order that will not post.

eg: In this case, it is C720LE

Navigate to Inventory> Setup and Maintenance> Items> Pull up the specific item.
Under Location Tab, select the specific location in the Work Order.
Double click on the hyperlink for Account Code.

For the specific line entry of the desired account code, verify if all the GL accounts specified for the columns "Sales, Cost of Goods Sold, Inventory, Work In Process, Inventory Adjustment, Accruals, COGS Adjustment, Purchase Price Variance, Standard Cost Variance, Physical Count Adjustment, Transfer Cost, In-Transit" are of the Status 'Active' .

If all looks good, Navigate to Bill of Materials -> Setup and Maintenance -> Labor Account Codes.

Check that the Account Code that that Item has been set up with is included in the list of Account Codes that have been set up on this screen. (For example, when loading that screen, we see here that the Acct Codes 70 and 72 have been setup, but this Item for this BOM has an Account code that has not been setup: Account code 20.)

Also, make sure the GL accounts set for "Inventory Labor Account" and "Applied Labor Account" have an "Active" status. If you find a GL Account that has an inactive status, then navigate to the GL Chart of Accounts to activate that GL account, or change the selected GL account to the appropriate account.

If there is an error to the Account Code setup, then either make an entry on the BM Labor Account Codes screen to include the appropriate code that the Inventory Item is using (here Acct Code 20) or change the Acct Code for this item in the Inventory setup to a code that has been set up (here, either 70 or 72) and save. See below screenshot.

Upon making the changes to correct this setup, you should be able to post the Work Order from BM Post Work Orders.  If there is more than one work order that will not post, repeat the above steps until they will all post.

76750ef7-61da-41f2-889c-95f2e6718ab1.title: How to enforce mandatory comments for manual GL transactions
76750ef7-61da-41f2-889c-95f2e6718ab1.content:
Problem
How to enforce mandatory comments for manual GL transactions entered in General Ledger> Transaction> Transaction

Resolution
To enforce mandatory comments for manual GL transactions, there is a Business Rule setting that would need to bet set. You would need to select 'Yes' for the option 'Require Transaction Comment' when entering manual GL journal transactions.

- Go to Application> System Manager> Company setup> Business Rules
- Expand Application> General Ledger> Under Miscellaneous, Set "Yes" for "Require Transaction Comment"
- Select Apply and then Ok to save and exit the Business Rules.
- It is advised to have this set as Yes, so that it prompts to enter comment/description for all Manual entries made.

This setting will ensure that you are not allowed to write transactions until a comment has been entered.

8f3b1489-d811-438b-9586-38250170e24d.title: How to restore the Backups in SQL Server Management Studio?
8f3b1489-d811-438b-9586-38250170e24d.content:
Problem
How to restore the Backups in SQL Server Management Studio?

Resolution
The below steps illustrate the process of restoring the Backups in the Microsoft SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS):



Step 1: Launch SSMS and Connect to SQL Server

- Open SQL Server Management Studio.
- Connect to the appropriate SQL Server instance where the database needs to be restored.

Step 2: Access the Databases Node

- In the Object Explorer pane, expand the server tree.
- Locate and expand the Databases node.

Step 3: Initiate Restore Process

- Right-click on the Databases node.
- Select Restore Database... from the context menu.

Step 4: Specify the Backup Source

- In the Restore Database dialog box:
- Under the Source section:
- Choose Device to restore from a backup file.
- Choose Database to restore from an existing backup on the server.

- If selecting Device:
- Click the ellipsis (...) button to locate the backup file (.bak).

Step 5: Load Backup File

- Click the Add button to load the desired backup file.
- Browse to the directory where your backup files are stored.
- Select the appropriate backup file and click OK.

Step 6: Configure the Restore Destination

- In the Destination for Restore section:
- Select an existing database or enter a new name for the database being restored.



Step 7: Set Restore Options

- Navigate to the Options tab:
- Restore As: Confirm the file paths for the MDF (data file) and LDF (log file).
- Recovery State:
- RESTORE WITH RECOVERY: Finalizes the restoration, making the database operational.
- RESTORE WITH NORECOVERY: Prepares the database for additional restores.
- RESTORE WITH STANDBY: Leaves the database in read-only mode for further analysis.

- If overwriting an existing database, check the Overwrite the existing database (WITH REPLACE) option.



Step 8: Start and Monitor Restoration

- Click OK to begin the restore process.
- Monitor the progress in the Restore Progress dialog box.
- Once complete, a success message will appear.



Step 9: Verify Restoration

- Refresh the Databases node in the Object Explorer.
- Confirm that the restored database appears and is accessible.



Additional Notes:

- Point-in-Time Restore: Use the Timeline feature to restore to a specific moment.
- Restore Sequence: Ensure backups are restored in the correct order:
- Full Backup → Differential Backup → Transaction Log Backup.

This step-by-step process ensures a smooth database restoration while allowing flexibility to meet specific requirements.



[NOTE: The process of obtaining the Backups can be found in the link: https://connect.aptean.com/s/article/Traverse-Global-Database-Backup]

ef3c3832-eeb0-43b9-8779-0ba5f21cbfa5.title: A Purchase Order item is “received” but is not showing up in Inventory as a “quantity on hand”
ef3c3832-eeb0-43b9-8779-0ba5f21cbfa5.content:
Problem
Customer entered a Purchase Order in the system and received an item on the order. The item was “received” in Traverse but is not showing up in Inventory as a “quantity on hand”.

Resolution
One reason why this might occur is because the Inventory interface with Purchase Order has just not been turned “on”. This would be more likely after setting up a new environment (perhaps for testing) or a new company.

The interface can be turned on in the Business Rules. Go to System manager> Company Setup> Business Rules> AP

Under "Interface application" the setting should be set to Yes for Inventory.

Click "Apply" and "OK" below to save the changes and exit the settings.

Log out of Traverse and back in.

Test the change to Traverse by entering a new Purchase Order and verifying that the items now appear in Inventory and show the correct "quantity on hand."

fae191c4-49d0-4327-90a1-7909f5265d39.title: How to set up a Batch Statement?
fae191c4-49d0-4327-90a1-7909f5265d39.content:
Problem
How to set up a Batch Statement?

Resolution
Batch Statements allow users to group similar financial statements for various companies into a single batch, enabling streamlined printing and management of multiple reports simultaneously. Below is a step-by-step guide to setting up a batch statement.



i. Access the Batch Statements Function: Navigate to the Batch Statements function via the path: Applications -> General Ledger -> Management Reports Setup -> Batch Statements:



ii. Create a New Batch Statement: Click on the 'New' icon at the top. Enter a unique Batch ID for the new batch and enter the Description



iii. Add individual Statements:

- Enter a sequence number for the statement in the Seq No field. If we do not enter a sequence number, the numbers will automatically by assigned in increments of 10.
- Add the individual Statement IDs created earlier into this batch by selecting them from the available list. [The Statement IDs should have been created in the GL Statements under the path: Applications -> General Ledger -> Management Reports Setup -> Statements]. Once the 'Stmt ID' was chosen, the Statement Name, Content ID, and Layout ID fields will be displayed.



iv. Define Details of the Statement: Click on the ellipsis (...) field to open the 'Detail' section of the Statements:

- Add required filters corresponding to the 'Account Segments'
- The 'Seq No' and the 'Statement ID' Field will be displayed and can be updated, if needed.
- Specify the company or companies whose information need to be printed if selected during batch printing.
- Sort by Account ID: Drag and move the account segment you want to prioritize to the top. Arrange subsequent segments in descending order of priority. [Sorting by account ID is optional and can be configured as needed]
- Segment Detail: Check this box to print detailed segment information; leave it unchecked to exclude it.
- Accounts with Zero Balances: Check this box to include accounts with zero balances; leave it unchecked to omit them.
- Workstation Date and Time: Check this box to include the workstation’s date and time on the statements; leave it unchecked if not required.
- Close the 'Detail' pop-up, once the details have been entered.



v. Save the Batch Statement: Click on the Save icon to finalize the setup.



vi. Print the Batch Statements: If the User goes to GL Financial Statements screen and choose the 'Batch ID', that was created in the GL Batch Statements, the configured statements will be getting printed all at once.



NOTE: If the User is using the 'Output' option, there will be a combined single PDF will get created

f2a5922f-4dfb-44f3-bf6b-e128405ef97d.title: Not able to receive Line Items in the PO Receipts
f2a5922f-4dfb-44f3-bf6b-e128405ef97d.content:
Problem
The User has a 'Purchase Order', that is in a status of 'New', but when the User tries to create a Receipt for that Purchase Order, the Line Items are not even listing in the 'Receipts/Invoices' screen. [The user is not able to receive it in the WM Receive as well.]

Resolution
This behavior occurs because the PO line item has already been included in a shipment and is currently in process.



The status of the PO shipment may be one of the following:

- In Process
- Received
- Completed.



In order to ensure this, the User can get in the PO Transactions screen under the path: Applications -> Purchase Orders -> Transactions -> Transactions:

i. Pull up the required Purchase Order

ii. Click on the 'Update' icon at the top

iii. Navigate to the 'Receipts/Invoices' screen and click on 'New' icon to create a new Receipt

iv. Enter the required Receipt number in the 'Receipt No' field

v. Pull up the Shipment number in the 'Shipment No.' field

vi. Once the 'Shipment No.' field is filled, the user will be able to see the 'Line Items' and proceed with creating the Receipts as required.



Alternatively, the user can also have a look into the PO Shipments screen and verify if that PO Line Item was linked to any Shipments. The PO Shipments screen can be found under the path: Applications -> Purchase Orders -> Transactions -> Shipments: [NOTE: If multiple PO Line items are linked with a single PO shipment, this process may require significant manual effort. Each line item linked to a shipment may need to be individually checked, particularly in cases where there are numerous associations. This method can provide the necessary visibility into shipment links but may be time-intensive in complex scenarios. ]

18080d21-856d-4602-9f1e-d31059e4cd6d.title: Create a new transaction batch code and Payment batch code in AP
18080d21-856d-4602-9f1e-d31059e4cd6d.content:
Problem
The client would like to know how to create a new transaction and payment batch code in AP.

Resolution
Creating a new Transaction Batch Code:

If you elect to use batch processing in the Business Rules function, use the Transaction Batch Codes function to define codes for posting purchases and miscellaneous debits. You can assign each transaction to a batch code, and then you can post transactions by batch code.

Creating a Batch Code:

1. Navigation: Navigate to Application > Accounts Payable > Setup and Maintenance > Transaction Batch Code.

2. Open a New Record: Click the New button on the toolbar to open a blank batch code record.

3. Enter Batch Code: Input a new code in the Batch Code field. Note: The batch code cannot exceed 6 characters, including special characters, alphabets, or a combination of both. If the limit is exceeded, the following warning message will appear:

4. Add Description: Provide a description for the new batch code in the Description field.

5. Select Permanent Option: Check the Permanent checkbox to retain the batch when posting transactions. Note: This will retain empty batches when processing is complete.  If the permanent box for the batch is not checked, the batch codes will be deleted as soon as all transactions in the batch have been posted.

6. Set Journal Status: Once you create a new batch, the journal status for Purchases and Misc Debits will automatically be set to Not Applicable as shown in the above image. You can manually change this default status if needed. The other options include Unprinted, Printed, and Reprint.

If invoices or debit memos are entered, the default is Unprinted. When you print a journal the status changes to Printed. If you enter a new transaction after you print a journal, the status becomes Reprint.

7. Mark Default Option: Check the Default checkbox if you want to use this batch as the default for the function. This will set it as the default batch for the company.

8. Save the Batch Code: Click the Save button on the toolbar to save the new batch code.

Creating a new payment batch code:

Use the Payment Batch Codes function to define codes to use when creating a record of released invoices due to be paid in the Prepare Payments function. Each payment can be assigned to a batch code, and then payments can be posted by batch code.

Use the Payment Batch Codes function to define codes for posting payments and prepayments, such as when creating a record of released invoices to be paid in the Prepare Payments function. Each group of payments from a bank account can be assigned to a batch code, and then payments can be posted by batch code.

Creating a Batch Code:

1. Navigation: Navigate to Application > Accounts Payable > Setup and Maintenance > Payment Batch Code.

2. Open a New Record: Click the New button on the toolbar to open a blank batch code record.



3. Enter Batch Code: Input a new code in the Batch Code field. Note: The batch code cannot exceed 6 characters, including special characters, alphabets, or a combination of both. If the limit is exceeded, the following warning message will appear:



4. Add Description: Provide a description for the new batch code in the Description field.

5. Select Permanent Option: Check the Permanent checkbox to retain the batch when posting transactions.  Note: This will retain empty batches when processing is complete.

The batch codes will be deleted as soon as all payments in the batch have been posted if the permanent box has not been checked.

6. Set Check Status: Accept the default status of Not Applicable in the Check Status field or change it. If payments are prepared, the status is Prepared. When you enter cash receipts, the status changes to Unprinted. When you print a journal the status changes to Printed. If you enter a new cash receipt after you print a journal, the status becomes Reprint. If you print the payment check and vouchers, the status becomes Printed.

7. Mark Default Option: Check the Default checkbox if you want to use this batch as the default for the function. This will set it as the default batch for the company.





8. Save the Batch Code: Click the Save button on the toolbar to save the new batch code.

23832a4f-3e43-4bd8-8079-f7185b6bcd74.title: Add a New Address to Site ID in Service Director Work Order Entry
23832a4f-3e43-4bd8-8079-f7185b6bcd74.content:

c8c7b58c-fa34-4004-ae90-e6704f983655.title: How to set up a Payroll deduction
c8c7b58c-fa34-4004-ae90-e6704f983655.content:
Problem
You need to set up a deduction like a simple garnish for a paycheck

Resolution
Go to the Codes Maintenance -> PA Deductions/Employer Costs screen to create a new deduction. Click the + button to add a new deduction or simply type into a new line. Fill in the information for the Code, Code Description, GL Liability Account, Formula ID, W-2 Box, W-2 Code/Description, and whether to calculate the deduction on Gross Pay or Net Pay. If this deduction requires a Formula, this will need to be set up under PA Formulas, and its Formula ID would be referenced here.

Once this has been created, then you can input the deduction either in the Employee's record as an ongoing deduction to calculate with future payrolls, or as a one time Payroll transaction. If this is a one-time payment, a Payroll transaction can be created to deduct from the employee's pay one time. Go to Payroll Transactions, select the Employee, go to the Deductions Tab, and put in the date, hours if applicable, and amount.



If this will be an ongoing deduction, go to Setup and Maintenance -> Employee Information and navigate to the Deductions tab to add the Deduction to the Employee Record there. Here you can individually select which pay runs you want the deduction to calculate on (in the "1,2,3,4,5" columns), and whether to take a fixed percent, straight amount, or a formulated amount. For salaried employees, these deductions can be calculated through the "Calculate Checks" screen. For hourly employees, they will apply to the hourly transactions that are created.

30644092-33e8-4d3b-b0f5-4e4045c2dcc4.title: Functionality of Reverse in PO
30644092-33e8-4d3b-b0f5-4e4045c2dcc4.content:
Problem
The client would like to know how the Reverse button works for serialized and non-serialized items in PO

Resolution
1. Why and Where Do We Use This Functionality?

This functionality is used when creating a new PO transaction, adding items, and then reversing or invoicing them. The process begins by creating a PO transaction in Traverse:

- Navigate to Applications → PO → Transactions.

Create a new transaction and add items in the Item ID field. The screen will look like this:

There are two methods to create receipts/invoices for the transaction:

Method 1: Using the Receipts/Invoices section in the menu bar.

Method 2: Using the "All" button in the screen toolbar.

Method 1: Receipts/Invoices

- Click Receipts/Invoices, and a new screen will pop up. Note that the Reverse button on the top bar will be greyed out initially.
- Enter the Receipt Number, ensuring the Date and Fiscal Period/Year reflect the current month and year for the transaction.
- Click on the Entry Number to enter the receipt. When you try to save, you will be prompted to enter the Serial Number for each serialized item.
- Enter unique serial numbers for each item to match the ordered quantity, then click Save.
- Once saved, return to the PO Transactions screen, and the status will change from New Order to Goods Received, indicating that the items have been received.

Method 2: Using the "All" Button

- After adding the line items, click the "All" option in the top toolbar. This will open a dialog box.
- Check the Receive All checkbox and enter a Receipt Number, then click OK. This will take you back to the Receipts/Invoices screen to enter serial numbers for each item.

Note: In this case, the Qty column initially shows 0 instead of 2. You will need to enter the serial number, and once that’s done, the Qty column will automatically update to reflect the ordered quantity, as shown in the image below.

- After saving, the “New Order” status will change to “Goods Received” status as shown in the below screenshot.

- Once you attempt to post this transaction and return to the Receipts/Invoices screen, the Reverse button will now be active (previously greyed out), allowing you to reverse the receipt if necessary.

The transaction has been posted- Proof of Delivery.





The Reverse button is now active and in use, as shown in the image below. Please also note that the Posted checkbox is checked.

Reversing Receipts

The Reverse functionality is mainly used when you need to delete a receipt due to errors or changes that need to be made to the transaction.



The "Reverse" button in the Receipts/Invoices screen is a feature that allows users to reverse a receipt back to the period if the order has not been invoiced.

- Note: If invoices and receipts are created but not posted, you can delete the receipts once after deleting the related invoice.

- Check the Status: Ensure that the purchase order is in a "Goods Received" status, meaning no invoice has been entered or posted. If the order has been invoiced, the Reverse button will be disabled.
- Using the Reverse Button: If the conditions are met (i.e., the order is in "Goods Received" status), you can click the "Reverse" button on the Receipts/Invoices screen. This action will create reversing entries to wash the previous receipts.
- Adjusting Receipts: After reversing the receipt, you can then create new receipts or adjust the previously received amounts as needed.
- Handling Invoiced Orders: If an invoice has already been posted on the order, the Reverse button will not be usable. In this case, you would need to back out the excess quantity using a PO Debit Memo/Return.
- Deleting Invoices: If an invoice has been entered but not posted, you may have the option to delete the invoice first and then use the Reverse button for the receipt.

Avoiding Closed Periods: The reverse process also helps avoid issues with closed periods, allowing for corrections to be made without affecting previously closed accounting periods.

Reverse Functionality for Non- Serialized Items

The reverse functionality works the same for non-serialized items. However, when creating receipts for non-serialized items, there is no need to enter a serial number, as illustrated in the image below.



The only difference between serialized and non-serialized items is that you are not required to enter a serial number when creating receipts for non-serialized items. Apart from this, everything else functions the same.

4169ea59-7936-45ad-852b-b52888a2f89e.title: Why is Budget Information Not Available for a New Year, when copied from the previous Year?
4169ea59-7936-45ad-852b-b52888a2f89e.content:
Problem
Why is Budget Information Not Available for a New Year, when copied from the previous Year? The User is using the 'Copy Account Balances' function to copy over the Balances from the older Year to the New Year. Even after running the function several times, the 'Budget' numbers remain 0.00



When the User pulls a Financial statement for the Fiscal period 1 of the New Year, the Budget numbers look to be 0.00 [The report was pulled for Fiscal Period 1 of Fiscal Year 2025]

Resolution
Budget numbers for a new fiscal year may not be available because the setup for the budget falls outside the Valid period defined in the Budget Ledger settings. This issue arises when the fiscal year or periods for the new year are not included within the range specified during the initial budget setup.



The common causes for such instance are:

-
Valid Period Range Limitation:

- The start and end periods configured for the budget do not cover the new year. For example, if the budget was initially set up for 2023, it may not extend into 2024 or beyond.
- The range of fiscal years or periods was not updated to include future years as part of routine Budget maintenance.

-
Account-Specific Restrictions:

- The accounts linked to the budget may have been restricted or deactivated for the new fiscal year, resulting in missing budget data.



In order to resolve this, the User need to review the GL Account Budgets and Forecasts and review the 'Detail' settings of the Budget that is setup for that Company.



The User need to follow the below steps to get this done:

i. Navigate to the GL Account Budgets and Forecasts screen under the Path: Applications -> General Ledger -> Setup and Maintenance -> Account Budgets and Forecasts:



ii. In the 'Budget' Tab, pull up the 'Budget' that is under consideration.  [The Client might have more than one Budget set up]



iii.  Locate the Company ID [For example: CPU] that is under discussion and click on the ellipsis [...] icon corresponding to the 'Detail' of the same.



iv. Verify the start and end periods to ensure they align with your current requirements. If additional periods are needed, adjust the range to include past or future years as necessary. For example, extend the range to cover beginning balances of prior years or forecast budgets for upcoming years. Ensure that the accounts associated with the budget are active and correctly configured to participate in the budgeting process for the new year.



v. In this example, the report is being generated for the fiscal year 2025. However, the defined period range does not currently include the year 2025, which necessitates making adjustments to ensure the report encompasses the desired time frame. The user has two options to address this limitation:

-
Change the End Year to 2025:
This option is suitable for cases where only the immediate next year (2025) needs to be included. By setting the ending year specifically to 2025, the period range will allow the report to cover data for the year 2025 without affecting subsequent years.

-
Set the Ending Year to 2099:
This option is recommended when the user prefers to define a significantly extended range, effectively eliminating the need to repeatedly update the period range in the future. By setting the ending year to 2099 (or any other sufficiently large period), the user ensures that the report will include all years up to the chosen endpoint. This approach is ideal for minimizing maintenance and allowing greater flexibility in report generation.



vi. Once the necessary changes are made, click on 'OK' at the top.



vi. Now click on the 'Save' icon at the top left of the screen to save the changes.



vii. The User can generate the required Financial statement and observe the Budget numbers getting copied over in the report:

ca22790a-8312-4ca0-8c47-6248a34c4108.title: Setting up authentication for email accounts that email from Traverse
ca22790a-8312-4ca0-8c47-6248a34c4108.content:
Problem
We would like to set up an additional security measures for our email accounts and need a process since Traverse does not currently support MFA (Multi-Factor Authentication) for emails.

Resolution
Traverse does not support MFA enabled accounts since Standard Document Delivery requires basic authentication with security defaults turned off. Here are some other strategies for increasing security:

- An IT team can whitelist the IP address from which their emails would be sending. Hosted clients can request this IP address from our TechHub team.
-  For Traverse builds beginning with Build 23107, Traverse now supports the Open Authentication protocol with Microsoft Online Exchange. If their company is using Microsoft 365, they can setup the Mail Service Integration in Traverse which allows for OAUTH instead of SMTP Authentication which is more secure and supported. This implementation enables secure email sending from Traverse without relying on deprecated SMTP Basic Authentication. Please note that Basic Authentication is still supported in Traverse. The integration of SM Mail Service with Traverse supports open authentication for outgoing emails using Microsoft.

In order to set this up: Go to: System Manager -> Setup and Maintenance -> Mail Service Integration

To configure the integration, perform the following steps: From the Name drop-down menu, select Microsoft. The account credential will be automatically loaded from the registered Azure portal, except for the Base URL.

Note: When an invoice is sent, it will be sent from the sender's email address that is available in the business rule settings or SMTP settings. In case the sender's email address is not configured, the user principal name retrieved from the registered Azure portal will be utilized for email communication. Enter the Base URL of the web API you created for this integration.

Note: For SM Mail Service Integration, update the configuration in the following areas for SM Mail Service Integration: * SM SMTP Settings * SM Business Rules * User Default When attempting to print an invoice, the system prioritizes the SM SMTP Settings over SM Business Rules and User Default settings. If the SMTP settings have not been configured, the system will consider the business rules settings for forms in accordance with the hierarchy.

Note: The maximum email attachment size is limited to 3 MB.

662bb282-d6cf-4cde-bfba-83dec32ee2a0.title: How to create a ‘Prenotification File’ for Direct Deposit in Payroll?
662bb282-d6cf-4cde-bfba-83dec32ee2a0.content:
Problem
How to create a ‘Prenotification File’ for Direct Deposit in Payroll?

Resolution
If the client has the 'Banking' module and intends to use Direct Deposit for payroll, they need to create a Prenotification file. This file needs to be submitted to the respective Banks.



The User needs to follow the below steps for creating the 'Prenotification file':



i. Navigate to the Prenotification Screen: Access the PA Create Prenotification File screen under the path: Applications -> Payroll -> -> Periodic Processing -> Create Prenotification File: Pull up the required 'Bank Account ID'





ii. Select Payroll Period and Check Date: In the Create Prenotification File screen, choose the Payroll Period End date and Date on Checks that will apply to this run. The Fiscal Period/Year will be auto-populated yet can be changed if needed.



iii. Configure Prenotification Options:

a. Resend All Prenotifications: Selecting this checkbox will add all previously sent and verified accounts to the current prenotification file, allowing re-validation of these accounts.

b. Mark All Prenotifications in This Run as Approved: Check this box to mark the Prenote In checkbox in each employee’s record, enabling these accounts to proceed with direct deposit in the upcoming check run.

c. Specify 'File Format': The file format will automatically load from the Default PA File Format field in the SM Bank Accounts screen. If a default format is not set, select the format required by the client’s bank.

- If the Exclude Batch Offset (Balancing) Record check box, in the SM Bank Accounts function, is selected, the File Format should be ADV, CCD, or PPD
- If the Exclude Batch Offset (Balancing) Record check box is not selected, the File Format should be ADVO, CCDO, or PPDO.

d.  Specify the 'File Name': Enter the preferred File name for the prenotification file.

e. Specify the 'Save to Folder': The save location will auto-populate based on the Default Folder field in the SM Bank Accounts screen. To change this, click Browse and select the desired folder for file storage. [Once the 'File Name' and 'Save to Folder' are entered, we can observe that in the 'Create File' section]

f. Enter 'Comments' [Optional]: If the User would like to enter any 'Comments' that might be later used to review the 'Activity', they can enter here.



iv. Generate the Prenotification File: Click on the 'Create' icon at the top left of the screen to generate the prenotification file.

5ad6803e-84bf-4edc-9b0e-b7350b570033.title: Why does the user not able to see the modules on the Traverse screen, even if the necessary Permissions are present?
5ad6803e-84bf-4edc-9b0e-b7350b570033.content:
Problem
Why does the user not able to see the modules on the Traverse screen, even if the necessary Permissions are present?



Let us consider the example where the User has permission to the 'IN Item Information', yet not available for the User in the Traverse Application:



But the Menu Security screen of the corresponding User Group indicates that the User is having access to the 'IN Item Information' under the path: Applications -> Inventory -> Interactive Views -> Item Information:

Resolution
In Traverse, users may occasionally be unable to see specific modules on the main screen, even if they have the required permissions. This issue occurs when a module has been hidden within the Traverse system.



To verify and resolve this, the user need to follow the below steps:



i. Navigate to the SM Application Menus under the Path: Applications -> System Manager ->Setup and Maintenance -> Application Menus:



ii. a) In the Application Menus screen, observe the module checkboxes, specifically in the ‘Hide’ column, to determine if the entire module is hidden. A checked box in the ‘Hide’ column indicates that the module is currently hidden. [In the below example, we can observe that the 'Dashboard' is hidded]



ii. b) Expand the Main Menu to view all associated submodules. Select the corresponding module to ensure if each submodule is also visible by unchecking the ‘Hide’ option where necessary. [In the below example, we can observe that the 'Productivity Reports' submodule is hidden]



ii. c) For each submodule, check the visibility of individual screens by selecting them and verifying their settings. Unhide as required by clearing the checkbox in the ‘Hide’ column for each screen within the submodule. [For this example, we need to make changes only in this step. That is uncheck the 'Hide' Checkbox for the Item Information screen]



iii. Once all visibility adjustments are complete, the user need to log out and then log back into Traverse. The user will now have access to the modules and submodules based on their permissions.



NOTE:

- The visibility hierarchy in Traverse affects module accessibility. For example, if an end screen (For example, “IN Item View”) is not hidden but its parent submodule (For example, “Interactive Views” under the Inventory module) is hidden, the end screen will remain inaccessible to the user. It is essential to verify visibility at each level of the hierarchy to ensure the correct access.
- Additionally, any unsupported modules that were previously in use are also hidden by default during installation and updates, ensuring they remain inaccessible.

04cacbc1-6ca6-4335-80af-d92c505e9b8d.title: Ad Self portal Password reset - Traverse cloud
04cacbc1-6ca6-4335-80af-d92c505e9b8d.content:
Problem
How to reset the password via Ad Self Service Portal?

Resolution
- Clients can reset their Traverse cloud password by visiting the link below:
https://adselfservice.apteancloud.com/showLogin.cc

-  Click on "Forgot Password" as shown on the page.

- Enter your username and the captcha, then click on "Continue"

- After submitting, you'll be redirected to a page with a dialog box displaying your registered email address. Confirm that the email is correct and proceed.

- You will receive a verification code sent to your email. Copy and paste the code or enter it manually. Ensure you enter the code within the time limit, then click "Continue."

-
The next page will allow you to reset your password. Be sure to follow the password requirements listed on the page. If the line does not turn green, it may be because the password you entered does not meet all the requirements. Alternatively, if you believe your password meets the criteria but the line remains red/yellow, it could be due to the use of an old password. In that case, make sure to choose a completely new password.
Password Requirements:

The minimum Password age is 0

The minimum password length is 14

No of passwords remembered is 10

The password complexity property is enabled

Password complexity:

- English Uppercase characters (A to Z)
- English Lowercase characters (a to z)
- Base 10 digits (0 to 9)
- Non alphabetic characters/Special characters (eg: !,@,#,$......)

Once you’ve entered the new password, type the captcha and click "Reset Password."

-
Once the password is successfully reset, you will see a prompt confirming that the password reset was successful.

-
After resetting your password, exit the page and try logging into Traverse using the same user account and your new password. This will grant you access to the application.

510abd2c-a14b-4114-911a-4a98e5e8d48a.title: How to add the column “Gross Profit Margin” available in SO Orders to be listed in SO Open Order Detail View in 11.0
510abd2c-a14b-4114-911a-4a98e5e8d48a.content:
Problem
How to add the column “Gross Profit Margin” available in SO Orders to be listed in SO Open Order Detail View.

Resolution
Open Design Studio,

Click on View Table under System Data

Click the new icon.

Type in “SoOpenOrderDetailCustom” in ID field.

Type in “Open Order Detail View” in Description field.

Copy the below script and paste it for Data Source field,



SELECT * FROM

(

SELECT d.TransID, d.EntryNum, d.LocId, d.ItemId, d.ItemType, d.Descr, d.CatId

, d.GLAcctSales, d.GLAcctCOGS, d.GLAcctInv

, SIGN(h.TransType) * d.QtyOrdSell AS QtyOrdSell

, d.UnitsSell, d.UnitsBase

, SIGN(h.TransType) * d.QtyShipSell AS QtyShipSell

, SIGN(h.TransType) * d.QtyShipBase AS QtyShipBase

, SIGN(h.TransType) * d.QtyBackordSell AS QtyBackordSell

82f1da1d-5e1e-4299-98ce-75d4226bc873.title: How to update the Permissions for a User Group from the Traverse application?
82f1da1d-5e1e-4299-98ce-75d4226bc873.content:
Problem
How to update the Permissions for a User Group from the Traverse application?

Resolution
To modify the permissions associated with a specific User Group in Traverse, users need to have authorized access to the SM User Groups screen. Typically, this access is granted to Admin-level users, allowing them to manage and oversee group permissions effectively.



i. Navigate to the SM User Groups screen, under the path: Applications > System Manager > Administration > Groups:



ii. In the Groups screen, pull up the required Group Name of the User Group whose permissions need to be updated. [Once the ‘Group Name’ is selected, we can observe the list of users belong to that group, which is indicated by the ‘Check box’ on the ‘Users’ section]



iii. To proceed with adjusting permissions, we need to click on the Permissions icon located on the left side of the screen. This action will open the Menu Security pop-up window, which contains the configuration options for setting specific permissions for that group.



iv. In the Menu Security window, we can make the required adjustments to the permissions according to the requirements. We can grant or restrict access to various functionalities as needed. Expand the 'Main Menu' and subsequently the 'Modules' to provide access to each window, after selecting the sub-module. [Checking the checkboxes implies permission been provided]. After finalizing the changes, click on Apply, then OK to confirm and to save and exit the Menu Security window.



v. Then, click on Apply and OK on the SM Groups screen, to save and exit the permissions window. It is essential to inform users within the modified group that these changes will only take effect after they log out and then re-launch Traverse. This logout and re-login process is necessary to ensure that the updated permissions are fully applied across the system, guaranteeing a seamless transition to the new settings.

3683db9c-24ff-4dc6-b7eb-bfbf2875b7a9.title: Old transactions that balance out are not clearing away for Customers in Accounts Receivable
3683db9c-24ff-4dc6-b7eb-bfbf2875b7a9.content:
Problem
Old transactions that balance out are not clearing away for Customers. The negative and positive On Account transactions that balance each other out are not clearing away after running the split/reapply and Periodic Maintenance.

Resolution
The key to clearing away old invoices and payments is to ensure that the invoice total is zero.

In order to see which Invoices still have a balance: Go to the Open Invoice view and group by Invoice Number. (Drag the Invoice Number column header above the rest of the column headers.) See the below screenshot. This will allow you to see the total that is outstanding for any invoices and for the ON ACCOUNT records.  In order to clear out old transactions that are still showing, the invoices (Including the ON ACCOUNT records) need to total zero. Once they total zero, all the records that are attached to them (you can see which those are by expanding them in the view), can be cleared out when you run Periodic Maintenance. This applies to the ON ACCOUNT balances or FIN CHRG balances as well - they act as if they were an invoice. As long as there is a sum total balance for those, everything associated with them will remain. Once the balance for the ON ACCOUNT, for example, comes to zero, then everything associated with it will clear out (after running Periodic Processing). As an FYI, the discount amount does not need to total zero for the group to clear away.

Once you know which invoices have outstanding balances, you can split/reapply payments toward the invoices to get their balances to equal zero. Go to the AR Hold/Release Invoices screen and select a payment, click the Split/Reapply and type the amount from the payment that you want to apply to each invoice.





A trick you can use to clear out old ON ACCOUNT records contributing to the balance is to create a cash receipt for the total outstanding amount (either positive or negative) to zero it out, and then create another cash receipt to recreate the balance in one ON ACCOUNT line to simplify things.

In the default setup, the Payee Name field in the Positive Pay file pulls its value directly from the Vendor Name specified in the Pay To tab within the AP Vendors screen.



i. The user can locate the 'AP Vendors' screen under the path: Applications -> Accounts Payable -> Setup and maintenance -> Vendors: Pull up the required Vendor ID. We can observe a name entered for the Vendor ID in the 'Name' field of 'General' Tab.



ii. Navigate to the 'Pay To' Tab: The user might have a different name in the 'Name' field of 'Pay To' Tab than in the General Tab. The name in the 'Pay To' tab will be mapped to the 'Payee Name' field of the default SM Export Layout Definition for a Positive Pay File:



iii. In case a user wants to update the Vendor name of the 'Positive Pay' File, then the user needs to update the 'Name' field found in the 'Pay To' Tab which will be mapped to the 'Payee Name' field. This name will be reflected in the [PayeeName] field in the Positive Pay File for any transactions created after editing and saving the name. This mapping enables customization of the name that appears on Positive Pay files, providing flexibility if the Payee details differ from their main record name of the 'Vendor'.

56d8710c-1d40-4a7d-a667-d849c0d2f8fe.title: Unable to delete a PO that was mistakenly entered.
56d8710c-1d40-4a7d-a667-d849c0d2f8fe.content:
Problem
The client is trying to delete a PO transaction that was entered by mistake. However, they are encountering an error message that says, "Item ID or location not set," which prevents them from completing the deletion. Please see the attached screenshot for reference.

Resolution
Step 1: If you're unable to delete the transaction directly, try removing the associated line items first. Select the line item and click the minus (-) icon at the bottom of the screen to delete it. You can repeat this process for all line items. When you click the minus (-) icon, you may see a pop-up with the following message:

Step 2: Next, we need to clarify a few points.

-  First, ensure that the line item exists in the inventory. If it doesn't, you should be able to delete the line item and its associated transaction without any issues.
-  If the item is in inventory, verify that it is set up correctly.
- If everything is correctly configured in the inventory but you still cannot delete the line items or the associated transaction, there may be another underlying issue causing the problem.

To investigate further, navigate to Applications -> Purchase Order -> Interactive View -> Order View. From there, apply filters to retrieve the item ID and order/transaction number. This will display the specific PO transaction on the screen. Additionally, you can access the Item Type by using the column chooser to pull it up.

If the selected Item ID is properly set up in inventory, it should indicate an Item Type such as Serialized, Non-serialized, Kitted, or Lotted. However, in this case, it is showing as 0, which suggests that there may be an issue with the item configuration.



This indicates that there is an issue with that specific item in inventory. It appears that it was initially entered as a Non-Inventory Item on the PO. Later, the same Item ID was set up in inventory, but not correctly. As a result, when the PO line item was created, the item wasn’t in inventory, leading to incomplete line-item fields. This is why we’re unable to delete either the line items or the transaction.

Step 3: There are two options on how this can be fixed:

- This can be fixed through a scripting process that would correct the setup for the item in inventory.
- Another option is to temporarily disable the interface between the Inventory and Purchase Order integration. If you choose this method, please ensure that no one else is processing PO transactions during this time to avoid complications.

For this, you would need to navigate to Applications -> System Manager -> Company Setup -> Business Rules.

Under Interface - Applications, change the Inventory setting to "NO" from the dropdown menu. This will temporarily disable the integration between Inventory and Purchase Orders.

Click "Apply" and then "OK" After that, attempt to delete the PO transaction. You should see a prompt asking, "Are you sure you want to delete transaction 00000457?" Click "OK" The transaction should then be deleted without any issues, and you won't find any history of it in the system. As you can see in the PO Order View, there will be no existing transaction.



This process allows the client to delete the desired PO transaction. Important: Be sure to re-enable the integration between Purchase Orders and Inventory in Business Rules after completing this.

3e52bc20-8f87-46b8-9f29-33e4f413fdee.title: Why does the posted AP entries not show up in the BR Cleared Transactions screen?
3e52bc20-8f87-46b8-9f29-33e4f413fdee.content:
Problem
Why does the posted AP entries not show up in the BR Cleared Transactions screen?

Resolution
The primary step to ensure is that the Accounts Payable is interfaced with the Bank Reconciliation module.

If the AP is interfaced with BR, and only few of the entries were missing, then there is a possibility that, the entries got cleared in any of the previous statements.

We can review the BR Register View to observe whether an entry has been cleared or not by the following steps:
i. Go to BR Register View under the Path: Applications -> Bank Reconciliation -> Reconciliation -> Register View:
ii. Pull up the required 'Bank Account ID' from the Lookup
iii. Setup the Date Range
iv. Click on 'Apply'

v. Right click on the Header Tab and go to Column Chooser, and pull up the 'Cleared' column:

vi. Here, we could observe that the entries corresponding to AP had already been cleared, as a result, they will no longer be appearing on any Statements under the Cleared Transactions screen:

Hence, in order to sort this, we need to get into the BR Cleared Transactions screen: Pull up the previous statement and locate the same entry and unclear them, by unchecking the 'Cleared' checkbox and click on 'OK'. [If the entry is not found in the previous statement, it is recommended to review the remaining statements as there is a chance the entry may have been cleared unintentionally.]

Then that entry was available to be cleared in the current month statement.

4d997249-f21d-4ea3-a748-8caa2abd984d.title: How to set up different printers for printing Check and remittance when Check Saver is being used
4d997249-f21d-4ea3-a748-8caa2abd984d.content:
Problem
How to set up different printers for printing Check and remittance when Check Saver is being used?

Resolution
To configure separate printers for printing checks and the Check Saver remittance, you will need to update the Business Rule for "Check Saver" to the "Multiple" option. This allows you to assign one printer for checks and a different printer for the remittance copy.

1. Navigate to Business Rules: Go to the System Manager (SM) Business Rules by following this path:
Applications -> System Manager -> Company Setup -> Business Rules.

2. Select Accounts Payable Application: Under the Application section, select Accounts Payable to view the relevant settings. From there, locate the Business Rule labeled "Check Saver" under the Miscellaneous section.

3. Configure Check Saver Options: We have three options to choose from for the Check Saver function:

- None: This option disables the Check Saver function entirely.
- Single: Selecting this option will use the same printer for both the checks and the Check Saver remittance.
- Multiple: This is the option we need to select if we want to use one printer for Checks and a separate printer for the Check Saver remittance.

4. Set Up Form Printers: After configuring the Business Rule to "Multiple," we can proceed to set up separate printer entries for both the checks and the Check Saver remittance. To do this, navigate to SM Form Printers by following this path: Applications -> System Manager -> Form Printers.

By following these steps, we’ll be able to effectively manage separate printers for Checks and Remittance.

b1aef80c-bf29-404b-8abd-9b5eee0c05e7.title: How to output the whole Bank Account Number in the Direct Deposit?
b1aef80c-bf29-404b-8abd-9b5eee0c05e7.content:
Problem
How to output the whole Bank Account Number in the Direct Deposit?

Resolution
To ensure that the full Payment information is visible, it is essential to update the relevant Business Rule in Traverse.

This can be done by navigating through the following path: Applications -> System Manager -> Company setup -> Business Rules: Once there, under the Application section, select 'Banking'.

Now, update the Payment Information Display to "All". This change will ensure that the full account numbers are displayed in the PA Employee Direct Deposit Information List.

For the field Payment Information Display, there are three available options for users to use:
i. None : This option will fully mask the Payment information, replacing the account number or credit card number with asterisks (***) in order to protect the sensitive data and masking the entire Payment information.
ii. All : Selecting this option will reveal the entire account number or credit card number, providing full visibility of the Payment details as required.
iii. Partial : This setting will show only part of the account number or credit card number, masking the rest with asterisks. It provides a balance between visibility and data protection, allowing users to see part of the account without fully exposing sensitive information.

By selecting the appropriate option, the user can control how Payment information is displayed, to best meet the business needs.
