14f1c618-eb10-4157-b03e-9973803344cb.title: How to set up Document Delivery for PO Requests?
14f1c618-eb10-4157-b03e-9973803344cb.content:
Problem
How to set up Document Delivery for PO Requests?

The Purchase Order Requests must be sent from the requestor to the Approver. And that needs to reach the Approver to get approved.

Resolution
The Email settings need to be configured under the Path: Applications -> System Manager -> Company Setup -> Business Rules: Purchase Orders: Under the Purchase Approvals sections, we would need to configure the SMTP Settings to facilitate sending out the Purchase Order requests via email.


- Allow Approval Processing: Select "Yes" to enable purchase order approval routes for purchase requisitions, facilitating review by authorized personnel with purchasing authority. If this feature is not needed, "No" can be selected.
- Budget Name: If applicable, a budget name can be provided to associate approved purchases with a specific budget.
- Budget Type: Choose the relevant budget type where the purchase requisitions will be allocated. This helps in tracking and managing the expenses against predefined budget categories.
- Budget Visible by Requestor: If desired, "Yes" can be selected to allow the requester visibility into the remaining budget amount. Selecting "No" will restrict this information from being viewed by the requester.
- Email Currency Display: This option determines which currency will be displayed in emails. Selecting "Company Base" ensures that the company’s functional or base currency is shown. Alternatively, choosing "Transaction" will display the currency associated with the vendor in the emails.
- Enable SSL Email: To enhance email security, selecting "Yes" will enable Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) encryption for email communications. If SSL is not required, the "No" option can be chosen.
- Login Name: The Login name required to access the SMTP server should be entered here. This is typically the username for the ISP email service.
- Login Password: The Password associated with the SMTP server login should be entered here. This is used for authenticating access to the ISP email service.
- Portal URL: If applicable, the Web Address for the purchase approval portal should be entered. This allows users to access the portal directly.
- Print Order Assembly: This field displays the names of the plugin and DLL files used for printing the order. These details are crucial for ensuring the correct printing configurations.
- Print Request Assembly: Similar to the Print Order Assembly, this field displays the plugin and DLL names used for printing the order request. Proper configuration ensures accurate document handling.
- Reply to Address: Enter the email address that vendors and customers should use if they need to reply to the email. This is essential for maintaining clear communication and addressing any questions or concerns regarding the forms received.
- Require Comment for Request Decline: By selecting "Yes," it becomes mandatory for users to provide a comment when declining a Purchase Order (PO) Approval Request. This helps in documenting the reasons for declination. If not necessary, "No" can be selected.
- Require Vendor Prior to Submit Request: If "Yes" is selected, the requester must choose a vendor before submitting the requisition. If this requirement is not enforced, an approver within the approval route will need to select a vendor before giving approval.
- Sender's Display Name: This field allows for the entry of the Name that will be displayed when sending forms to vendors and customers via email. It ensures that recipients can easily identify the sender.
- Sender's Email Address: The Email address entered here will be displayed on all outgoing emails sent to vendors and customers with attached forms. This is important for ensuring that replies and communications are directed to the correct address.
- Show Approval Details on Emails: Selecting "Yes" will include the approval history within notification emails, providing transparency in the approval process. If this information is not needed in emails, "No" can be selected.
- Show Approval Trail on PO: When "Yes" is selected, the approval history will be visible on the purchase order itself. This provides a clear record of the approval process. If not required, "No" can be chosen.
- SMTP Port: The SMTP port number for the email server should be entered here. This is essential for proper email routing and server communication.
- SMTP Server name: The internal address or IP address of the SMTP email server should be provided in this field. This ensures that the system can correctly connect to the email server for sending and receiving emails

9cbdab6c-8897-43d9-907c-d7248d3f61c7.title: How to offset a Deposit entry debiting and crediting the same account in BR by mistake
9cbdab6c-8897-43d9-907c-d7248d3f61c7.content:
Problem
The Client made a Bank Reconciliation (BR) Deposit entry where both the debit and credit were applied to the same GL account.

Although the General Ledger (GL) appears accurate since the debit and credit entries offset each other within the same GL account, the issue lies within the BR deposit.

The Bank Reconciliation shows the deposit incorrectly, and it needs to be adjusted to ensure that the reconciliation reflects the intended entries.

Resolution
The Deposit made to an account in BR typically stays in the Deposits Tab of the BR Cleared Transactions screen. In order to resolve the issue caused by an incorrect Deposit made to the same account itself, in the Bank Reconciliation module, we need to create a negative entry of the same amount for the same GL Account, to offset its impact in the Bank Reconciliation. This will offset the impact of the original incorrect deposit. Here's how to proceed:

1. Navigate to BR Transactions screen under the path: Applications -> Transactions -> Transactions: pull up the necessary Bank Account ID:

2. Go to the Deposits Tab and click on the 'New' icon to create a new Deposit.
- The system will generate a transaction number, which will be displayed in the Trans No field.
- Enter the deposit number in the Deposit No field
- Accept or edit the transaction date in the Trans Date field.
- Specify the Fiscal Period and Fiscal Year for the deposit, or accept the default.
- Enter the Reference or use the default deposit reference.
- Provide a Description of the deposit, or use the default deposit code description.
- Enter the same deposit Amount, but with a Negative sign for the same GL Account [For example: In this example, it should be entered as -10.00, to offset the Deposit]
- Click on 'Save' icon at the top.

3. After printing the Transaction Journal, go to BR Post Transactions screen under the path: Applications -> Transactions -> Post Transactions: Post the Transactions:

4. Once posted, we could see the impact made by the offsetting entry available to be cleared in the BR Cleared Transactions screen in the path: Applications -> Reconciliation -> Cleared Transactions:

e4c328e4-aeaa-405b-8a5e-796c76364ae2.title: How to setup a new account in the Chart of Accounts?
e4c328e4-aeaa-405b-8a5e-796c76364ae2.content:
Problem
What steps do I need to follow to set up a new account in the Chart of Accounts?

Resolution
1. Navigation: Go to Applications > General Ledger > Setup and Maintenance > Chart of Accounts.

2. Open New Record: Click the New button on the toolbar to start a blank chart of accounts records.

3. Account ID:

3.1 Enter a new Account ID in the designated field. Note: The Account ID column will be greyed out and cannot be manually entered. To populate this field, you must set up a Segment ID say for example here we enter a 6-digit Segment ID, comprising a 4-digit and a 2-digit entry. Once these entries are made, the Account ID will automatically populate.

3.2 Quick Entry: Use the Quick Entry button for a faster way to create an account.

3.3 To copy information from an existing account, select it from the Copy From field (only visible when creating a new account).

4. Description: Provide a description for the new account in the Description field.

5. Select Account Status: Choose the appropriate status for the account from the Status field. The available options are:

Active: This status allows the account to post transactions to the GL Journal, meaning it will be used in financial reporting and record-keeping.

Inactive: Accounts marked as inactive do not post transactions to the GL Journal. However, they retain historical data for reference and auditing purposes. This status is useful for accounts that are no longer in use but may still need to be accessed for historical records.

Discontinued: This status is for accounts that will not be used again. Similar to inactive accounts, discontinued accounts do not post to the GL Journal, but they help preserve historical information. It’s advisable to assign this status to accounts that you want to permanently retire from active use.

5.1 Inactive and discontinued accounts are treated as invalid during processing. If you attempt to post transactions that include these accounts, the system will generate an error message indicating that invalid accounts are present.



5.2 To troubleshoot posting issues, you can generate the Invalid GL Accounts List report. This report will help you identify any inactive or discontinued accounts that may be causing problems during posting.



6. Currency: If using multicurrency, choose the currency for the account from the Currency ID field. Traverse will convert transaction amounts based on the specified exchange rate.



7. Segment ID: Select the appropriate Segment ID for account segmentation.



Note: Once you set up the Segment ID, you will see the Account ID automatically populate in its designated field.



8. Account Type and Consolidation Options:

8.1 Choose an account type from the Account Type field drop down.

Important: Selecting the correct type is crucial, as it determines if the account will have a debit or credit balance. Once transactions are posted, you cannot change the account type to one with a different balance type.

8.2 Clear to Account (for revenue/expense accounts):

- If applicable, select an account from the Clear To Account field.
- If you do not wish to clear the account at year-end, leave this field blank.
- If you select an account, also enter a step to clear it in the adjacent Step field. Ensure the currencies match those of the selected account.

8.3 Consolidation:

- To consolidate the account with one in a different company, enter that account number in the Consol To Account field. Leave it blank if no consolidation is needed.
-  If you select an account in the Consol To Account field, you must also enter a step to consolidate it in the adjacent Step field. The currencies must match those of the selected account.
- Enter 0 to prevent consolidation, or 1 to consolidate all accounts in one step.



9. Save record: Click the Save button on the toolbar to save the new record.

10. Now, you can view the newly saved Account in GL Simple Chart of Account view.

31b3f47e-20a4-420d-9194-fbd3eef92b78.title: Service Director: Creating a new Activity Status
31b3f47e-20a4-420d-9194-fbd3eef92b78.content:
Problem
Service Director: Creating a new Activity Status

Resolution
Create a new Activity Status:

- Navigate to Service Director >Setup and Maintenance > Activity Status
- Click the New button, on the toolbar to open a blank activity status record, or click in an empty record
- Enter a description for the activity status in the Description field.
- Select a Dispatch Status field drop-down list. This status indicates the state of the dispatch, whether it is 'Open', 'Completed', 'Billed', 'Posted', or none of these.
- Select an Action to be applied to the dispatch when the activity status is selected. The action will apply the appropriate business logic to the dispatch, which may include no actions, or actions the system performs when the dispatch is put on hold, released, completed, canceled, or reopened.
- Select a Status Color to indicate at a glance the activity status of a dispatch. This is utilized on the Dispatch Console.
- Click the Save button to save your work.

Use the Re-sequence button on the toolbar when you drag the activity status records into a new order. This will save the new arrangement.

To delete an activity status, select the status to delete, and click the Delete button on the toolbar. You can only delete the activity status if it is not in use.

26ed6089-5fcf-4ebf-8104-fef964584515.title: How to create Billing Type in Service Director
26ed6089-5fcf-4ebf-8104-fef964584515.content:

How to create Billing Type in Service Director

c569b1d2-1448-474c-a1e1-472fb7a23413.title: How to Clear Cached Data from Traverse?
c569b1d2-1448-474c-a1e1-472fb7a23413.content:
Problem
How to clear Cached data from Traverse?

Resolution
Clearing cached data from the Traverse application serves several important purposes enlisted as follows:

- Cached data can accumulate over time, which may slow down the application.
- By clearing the cache, we can free up memory and resources, allowing Traverse system to operate more efficiently and respond faster to user requests. This is essential for maintaining optimal performance.
- Cached information might become outdated if changes are made in the Traverse system.
- If users encounter problems with the Traverse application, such as incorrect data being displayed or functionality not working as expected, clearing the cache can often resolve these issues.
- The cache might store corrupt or stale data that could be causing the errors, and clearing it allows the application to start fresh with a clean slate, reducing the risk of further malfunctions.

In order to clear the Cached data, the User needs to get into 'View' from the Toolbar and get into 'Preferences', then click on the 'Clear Cached data' icon to clear the Cached Data from the user's workstation:

257e2ecd-dd22-4a72-953a-e767be4ff64a.title: How to have the AP Detail History View to be grouped by the 'Type' column.
257e2ecd-dd22-4a72-953a-e767be4ff64a.content:
Problem
How to have the AP Detail History View to group by Transaction Type. Eg: List of Line item, Sales Tax, freight, Misc?

Resolution
We would need to group the columns instead of using the filter.

To group by column,

Click and drag the column "Type" and drop it over on the top, where it says "Drag a column Header here to group by that column"

Once drag and dropped, you can expand the arrow to have a detailed view.

73b39357-137f-4f42-a47c-755eebe1c249.title: Getting the error: "Failed::Syntax error in parameters or arguments. The Server response was: 5.6.0 Request body validation error. Need either non-empty Html or Plain Text body to be present.[System]"
73b39357-137f-4f42-a47c-755eebe1c249.content:
Problem
When the User is trying to send an email out of Traverse, the User is getting the error: "Failed::Syntax error in parameters or arguments. The Server response was: 5.6.0 Request body validation error. Need either non-empty Html or Plain Text body to be present.[System]"
- The User had ensured that the SMTP Settings has been properly configured.
- The Mail Server is not receiving any emails, even after whitelisting the emails that will be sent out of Traverse.

Resolution
The error message "Failed::Syntax error in parameters or arguments. The Server response was: 5.6.0 Request body validation error. Need either non-empty Html or Plain Text body to be present." indicates that the email being sent lacks a valid message body. This can occur due to several reasons:
- Empty Body: The most common cause is that the email does not contain any content in either the HTML or plain text format. Email servers require at least one of these formats to be present in the message body.
- Incorrect Configuration: If we are using a library like PHPMailer, the Mail administrator must ensure that both the Body and AltBody properties are set correctly.
- HTML Content Issues: If we are sending an HTML email, ensure that the HTML content is valid and not empty. Using methods like msgHTML() should correctly set both the HTML and plain text bodies, but if there's an issue with the HTML content being loaded (such as file read errors), it could result in an empty body.
- Server Validation: Some email servers perform strict validation checks on incoming messages. If they find that both body formats are missing or improperly formatted, they may reject the message with this error.

If the Mail Administrator has setup the configuration to reject emails without body, we can configure the Body of the email under Traverse. [NOTE: At many instances, where we send out Forms such as Invoices, Order Acknowledgments, the email being sent out of Traverse would be just having the Attachment, without a Body]

1. In order to set up the Email Body, go to SM Document Settings under the path: Applications -> System Manager -> Document Delivery -> Document Settings:

2.Click on the 'New' icon at the top. Pull up the corresponding Form ID [For example, SO ACK]. Enable 'Auto Send' to have the emails sent, by the time we print out the same Form. If the check box for 'Auto Send' is cleared, the document will be sent to the document queue, from where you can manually send the document.

3. Pull up the corresponding SMTP ID for this Form. Enter the Subject and Email Body for the Document in the corresponding Fields. [NOTE: The Subject and the Body can have either static Text, or we can also use the Dynamic Fields available on the right side of the screen]. If we want to send the email formatted as HTML, mark the Send as HTML check box. If the check box is cleared, the email will be formatted as plain text

4. Define the file name for the document in the Document Name field. We can use both static text and dynamic (merge) fields to create a file name. If no file name is defined, the Default file name determined by the system will be used. If needed, we can also add static attachments in the Attachment field list. Once the necessary changes are made, click on Save.

5. Now the User would be able to send the Emails without any issues.

6a2afa0c-7363-43f2-8ed4-bc159898eb42.title: Not able to Re Calculate a printed Payroll check, getting pop up "Checks have been printed"
6a2afa0c-7363-43f2-8ed4-bc159898eb42.content:
Problem
Payroll checks have been printed but not posted. Would like to calculate payroll checks again as it was miscalculated. When trying to hit reset on PA Calculate Checks screen, getting pop up "Checks have been printed". How to recalculate payroll checks if the checks are printed already?

Resolution
To recalculate payroll checks after they have been printed, you will need to make a change to the "Allow editing after printing" business rule in TRAVERSE. Here are the steps to follow:

- Hit Apply and Ok.

Go to PA Calculate checks now and click on Reset to recalculate the checks. This time you will receive pop up to start over again> hit Yes and start over again.

7e6dd31b-cad1-4e37-912e-bad498982738.title: Change File Size (OSAS)
7e6dd31b-cad1-4e37-912e-bad498982738.content:
Problem
How to Change File Size function to create a new file and copy the data from the old file the

Resolution
Use the Change File Size function to create a new file and copy the data from the old file into it. You can also use this file under the direction of a qualified support technician to shrink files from which you have deleted records of old customers, vendors, employees, inventory items, and so on. When you use this function, OSAS creates a new data file, reads the information from the existing file, and copies all records it can read to the new file.

- To shrink files, select Change File Size from the Database Utilities menu. The Change File Size screen appears.

- Enter the name of the file. Information about that file appears in the middle portion of the screen. In the Actual File Information column, the File Type should be Vkeyed or Highly Recoverable and the Number of Records should be Dynamic. If different values appear for these fields, consult your software provider or call Open Systems for technical support.

In the fields at the bottom of the screen, change the values to use for the new file, if necessary(as shown in the example):

- In the File Type field, enter 7 to create a Vkeyed (variable-length keyed) file. Most OSAS data files are Vkeyed files for flexibility as well as recoverability in case of data loss or a system crash.
-  In the Number of Records fields, enter he number of records you want in the new file. OSAS automatically sets this field to 0 to create a dynamically allocated file.
- In the Bytes Per Record field, enter the number of bytes of memory to set aside for each record in the new file. OSAS automatically sets this field to 1152.
- In the Key Chain field, enter the key chain number you want to use to select the data to copy from the old file to the new one, or leave the default value as is. A key chain represents a primary key used in the table to sort and organize data. Refer to the OSAS file descriptions manuals for more information on key chains. Use the Proceed (OK) command to save your entries and begin the copy process. After OSAS reads and copies to memory all records in the old file, the n records copied. The old file will be replaced. message appears. Use the Proceed (OK) command again to remove the old file and replace it with the new, resized one.

d153e168-bf60-48b8-8500-f50e7fd20491.title: AP Void Payment OSAS

How to void AP Void Payment

ff39bcb1-9aa7-499f-8b60-f9814f773821.title: Remove Application from OSAS
ff39bcb1-9aa7-499f-8b60-f9814f773821.content:
Problem
How can we remove an Application from OSAS

Resolution
Use the Remove Applications function to remove any application except Resource Manager from the system

Follow these steps to remove an application:

1. Select Remove Applications from the Installation menu under Resource Manager.

2. Enter the two-character code for the application you want to remove, and press Enter
3. Because removing the application also removes all data files for that application, the system prompts you for verification before processing continues. When the verification message(s) appears, verify that you want to remove the specified application and use the Proceed (OK) command to continue. After you verify the application’s removal, OSAS removes the application from the system.

Note: This function removes the entire application from your system, including your data files. If you want to save your data files, back them up, copy them to a new directory, or do not use this function to remove the application.

ca1e8c2b-75d3-416f-b23a-484da4dece09.title: Building Favorite Menu in OSAS
ca1e8c2b-75d3-416f-b23a-484da4dece09.content:
Problem
How to build your own menu of the functions and submenus you use most

Resolution
The Favorites menu allows you to build your own menu of the functions and submenus you use most. You can create and add functions to the Favorites menu automatically by using the Add to Favorites (F10) command:

- To add a menu or a function to the Favorites menu, select the menu or function you want to add and press F10
- To remove an entry from the Favorites menu, select the entry to remove and press F10 again.
- To toggle between the Favorites and main menus, press F2.

To customize the Favorites menu, select Favorites Menu from the User Setup menu



- You can create submenus that group functions together in two ways:
- Press F10 to add an entire existing submenu (like the Sales Order Daily Work menu, for example) to the Favorites menu, then switch to the Favorites menu and remove functions as needed until only the functions you use most often appear on it. Edit the title of the menu, if necessary.
- Enter a new menu ID in the Menu field and give it a Title, then press Enter in the scrolling region to add functions to the new menu. You may need to use the Menus function to note down information about specific functions (such as the programs they call and any parameters they need) before you can enter it here.

530f5caa-e69b-4740-b90a-73cb3dd8d905.title: How do we check which version of SQL does Traverse is using
530f5caa-e69b-4740-b90a-73cb3dd8d905.content:
Problem
How do we check which version of SQL does Traverse is using

Resolution
- To check the SQL Server version in SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS), first log in to SSMS using your credentials.
- Once connected, right-click on the relevant database and select "New Query" from the options. In the query window that opens, type the following query:
SELECT @@VERSION
- Then, execute the query by pressing F5 or clicking the "Execute" button. The result will display the current SQL Server version running on that instance.

756f5a53-4b5e-47b1-84e9-ac31a648adf9.title: How to setup the Default path to export reports?
756f5a53-4b5e-47b1-84e9-ac31a648adf9.content:
Problem
How to setup the Default path to export reports for Traverse Users?

Resolution
In Traverse, the default path to Export documents needs to be configured in the SM User defaults screen. This feature will be available for the Clients who are on the Build 24031 and above.

1. Navigate to Applications -> System Manager -> Company setup -> User Defaults: [If the user is an Admin user, then the user can define the Default path for any user under the 'User Defaults -Admin']

2. Select System Manager from the available Application.

3. In the User Defaults screen, locate the 'Default Document Folder' field. Click on the ellipsis (...) icon at the end of the field to browse for the desired export path.

4. Browse through the file system to locate the folder that we prefer to set as the default export path. Once found, click 'OK' to confirm the selection.

5. Click on 'Save' icon on the 'User Defaults' screen:

NOTE: If the client prefers not to be restricted to a single export folder, it is recommended to pin the frequently used locations under 'Quick Access' in the file explorer. This allows easy access to multiple export folders without needing to reconfigure the default path each time.
By following these steps, the users can ensure that their export paths are set up efficiently and can be easily managed within their environment.

bdd486b1-31c2-4568-9b95-580053f367bc.title: OSAS Append/Edit Inventory Adjustments
bdd486b1-31c2-4568-9b95-580053f367bc.content:
Problem
How to Edit an inventory adjustment

Resolution
- Go to Inventory Module
- Select Inventory Transactions from the Daily Work menu

- Use this screen to choose a transaction type. All transactions are listed on this screen before you post.
- Thie below screen is titled the Edit Inventory Adjustments screen when you edit an adjustment line item and Append Inventory Adjustments screen when you add an adjustment. Use this screen to add or edit an adjustment. You can increase or decrease the unhand quantity of an item.

1. To make an adjustment that increases the quantity available, enter I in the Status box. To decrease the quantity available, enter D.
2. Enter the date and GL period and year of the adjustment.
3. Enter or select from the Loc ID box the ID of the location of the item.
4. Enter the ID of the item whose quantity you want to adjust in the Item ID box. The quantity on hand and available appear at the bottom of the screen.
Note: The Inventory Items screen is available through the maintenance function (F6). Use this screen to add an item ID and information about that item or to maintain information about an item.
5. If the adjustment is an increase in inventory, enter or select a credit account in the Adjust Acct box. If the adjustment is a decrease in inventory, enter a debit account.
6. Enter the quantity you want to adjust in the Quantity box.
7. Enter or select the unit of measure with which you want to work in the Units box.
Note: The Units of Measure screen is available through the maintenance function (F6). Use this screen to add or change units of measure for an item.
8. Enter the cost of the item in the Cost box. The extended cost (quantity x cost) appears.
9. Enter additional information about the transaction in the Comment box.
10. To save your entries and exit to the Inventory Transactions screen, use the Proceed (OK) command. To exit to the Inventory Transactions screen without saving your entries, use the Exit (F7) command.

68b731f6-5442-4a7f-88a5-f8bc17c4791f.title: Item Price Change in OSAS
68b731f6-5442-4a7f-88a5-f8bc17c4791f.content:
Problem
How to change an Items price in OSAS

Resolution
Use the Item Price Change function on the Periodic Processing menu to change the price of items. Use the Item Price Change screen to change prices for selected items, price IDs, locations, product lines, and user-defined fields.

1. Select Item Price Change from the Periodic Processing menu of Inventory Module

2. Enter the range of items, prices, locations, product lines, and user-defined fields whose price information you want to change.
3.If you want to print an audit log that shows the old and new prices, select the check box (or enter Y in text mode); if not, clear the box (or enter N in text mode).
4. If you chose to print the audit log, select the order in which you want to organize the log.
5. Enter the adjustment base for the item price change: base, list, or minimum.
6. Enter % for a percentage adjustment; enter $ for a dollar adjustment.
7. Enter the amount of the adjustment. For negative quantities, use the minus symbol; enter positive quantities without a plus sign.
8. If you elected to print the audit log, select the output device for the log. If you elected not to print the log, use the Proceed (OK) command to begin the price change process.

9f5084d6-afa3-47a6-a223-fe6a494c49f9.title: OSAS Inventory Cost Change
9f5084d6-afa3-47a6-a223-fe6a494c49f9.content:
Problem
How to change the cost for selected items, locations, product lines, and user-defined fields.

Resolution
Select Cost Changes from the Periodic Processing menu of Inventory Module.

1. Enter S if you want to use standard cost as the adjustment base or enter B if you want to use base cost as the adjustment base.
2. Enter the range of items, locations, product lines, and user-defined fields whose cost information you want to change.
3. Select the order in which you want to organize the log in the Print By section.
4. The Cost Code field appears if you selected standard cost as the adjustment base. Enter the range of cost codes for which you want to change costs.
5. In the Adj Type box, enter or select % to use a percentage adjustment; enter $ to use a dollar adjustment.
6. In the Adj Amount box, enter or select the amount of the adjustment. For negative quantities, use the minus symbol; enter positive quantities without a plus sign.
7. Select the output device for the log to begin the cost change process. After the log is produced, the Periodic Processing menu appears.

98a8aec2-56ef-4818-912c-c5c806041542.title: How to create a new Bank account in OSAS
98a8aec2-56ef-4818-912c-c5c806041542.content:
Problem
How to create a new bank account

Resolution
Go to Resouces Manager >> Company setup>> Bank Accounts

1. Enter a unique ID for the bank account in the Bank Account ID box.
2. Choose Bank Account in the Type field.
3. In the GL Account Number box, enter the number of the general ledger account affected by transactions made to the account. (The Inquiry (F2) and Maintenance (F6) commands are available if Bank Reconciliation interfaces with General Ledger.) Assign a unique account number to each bank account record.
4. Select Active or Inactive in the Status field. A bank account must have an active status to be used in any transaction.
5. In the Account Description box, enter a description of the bank account (for example, the name of the bank).
6. Enter the Address, City, State, Zip, and Country for the Bank Account.
7. Enter the bank’s phone and fax numbers using the phone mask that appears.
8. In the Contact box, enter the name of the person you contact when you have questions about the account.
9. Enter the E-Mail Address for the contact, and the Web Site of the bank.
10. Proceed to the Account Information screen

Account Information

The next screen contains the account information associated with bank accounts beginning with the account and routing numbers.

1. Enter the number the bank assigned to the account in the Account Number box. If you enter a number longer than 15 characters, the account number is truncated on deposit slips.
2. Enter the Routing Code for your bank.
3. Enter the number of Signature Lines to print on plain paper checks.
4. Enter the Fraction code for your bank, if needed. Fraction codes were once used by financial institutions to route checks to the proper bank for payment. They are still used by some banks, often as a supplement to other routing methods in case part of the check is damaged or unreadable.
5. Check the Allow ACH Creation? box if this account can be used for ACH electronic payment files; if you do not have either Banking or Direct Deposit installed for this company, this prompt is set to NO and you cannot change it (disabled on graphical screens).
6. If you use the Banking application, enter the Positive Pay Format to use with this bank.
7. Enter the Next AP Check Number to be used when printing checks for this account using AP/PO. If you have set the Use separate check numbers for Accounts Payable/Payroll option set to NO, this field is called Next Check Number, and applies to both AP/PO and PA checks.
8. Enter the Next PA Check Number to be used when printing checks for this account using PA. (This field won’t be displayed if you have set the Use separate check numbers for Accounts Payable/Payroll option set to NO.) The remaining fields on this screen are disabled if they Allow ACH Creation? prompt is set to NO. Otherwise, enter the information required to produce the ACH files for direct deposit/transfer of fund.
9. If you use the Banking application and you enabled ACH creation, enter the Next AP Voucher Number to be used when generating vouchers for this account using AP/PO. (If you have set the Use separate voucher numbers for Accounts Payable/Payroll option set to NO, this field is called Next Voucher Number.)
10. If you use Banking or Direct Deposit and you enabled ACH creation, enter the Next PA Voucher Number to be used when generating vouchers for this account using AP/PO (with Banking) or PA (with Direct Deposit).
11. If you enabled ACH creation, the last electronic check posting date appears in the Last ACH Posted field. This field is updated when you post checks and vouchers.
12. If you enabled ACH creation, the last ACH batch number transferred to the bank appears. Accept this batch number or enter the number of the first batch you want to transfer to the bank if you are transferring several batches posted on different days.
13. If you enabled ACH creation, in the Print Field on ACH File field, enter F to include your company’s federal tax ID number in the ACH file you produce, R to include your company’s routing code, or B to include the federal reserve bank routing code.
14. If you enabled ACH creation and if your bank is a federal reserve bank, enter the Federal Reserve Routing Code. 15. If you enabled ACH creation, enter the identifying code your bank requires for direct deposit records in the Company Identifier Type/Number field:

- Enter 1 if the bank requires your federal tax employer ID number
- Enter 3 if the bank requires your DUNS number
- Enter 9 if the bank requires a different number of the bank’s choosing After you enter the code, enter the corresponding number.

16. If you enabled ACH creation, and if your bank requires the 627 records to be included in your direct deposit media files, select the box (or enter Y); if not, clear the box (or enter N).
17. If you enabled ACH creation, and if your bank expects your ACH file to begin with a security code, enter the Security Code for File Transfer in the field at the bottom of the screen. If your bank does not require a security code, leave this field blank.
18. If you enabled ACH creation, enter the required length of the security code for your bank. If your code is shorter than required, the system appends the required number of characters to your security code. The maximum length you can enter is 94

4df58523-04ce-495e-95e0-0ad48b3c5647.title: How to purge data in OSAS
4df58523-04ce-495e-95e0-0ad48b3c5647.content:
Problem
How to purge data in OSAS

Resolution
1. Select Purge Data Records from the Database Utilities menu.

2. Enter the name of the file from which you want to purge records. The bytes per record, active keys, and key definitions appear.
3. Enter the Key Chain number you want to use to locate the records to remove. A key chain represents a primary key used in the table to sort and organize data. Refer to the OSAS file descriptions manual for more information on key chains.
4. Enter the Starting Key from which to start purging records. To start at the beginning of the file, leave this field blank.
5. Use the Proceed (OK) command to begin the purge process. Each key from the file appears, beginning with the starting key you entered. As each record appears, you can take one of three actions:
- Select Yes or press F3 to delete the record from the file.
- Select No or press Enter to leave the record in the file.
- Use the Exit (F7) command to leave all remaining records in the file and return to the Database Utilities menu.

6. After you process the last record in the file, enter another file name from which to purge records or press F7 to return to the Database Utilities menu

f54257b1-9d3e-4ee4-8ba3-8d96cd304300.title: User doesn't want to scroll through the entire printer list available due to APS Enhancement of Build 24200
f54257b1-9d3e-4ee4-8ba3-8d96cd304300.content:
Problem
The Traverse Build 24200 has an APS Enhancement in which, at the Cloud Printing dialog box, all available printers [That are identified with the APS Credentials] are displayed in the format <Machine name>\<Printer name>. And the user finds it hard to scroll through the list every time they hit 'Print.'

If the User doesn't have any 'Default Printer' set up in the SM User Defaults screen under the path: Applications -> System Manager -> Company Setup -> User defaults, then the list would be sorted based on the entries of the Format <Machine name>\<Printer name>

In this scenario, the Printer name list, in the Cloud Print Dialog box, is sorted alphabetically with all the List of Printers displayed with their machine name and printer names in format <Machine name>\<Printer name>.

Cause
Update to the Build 24200

Resolution
In order to easily access the Printers specific to the User's workstation, it is recommended to have the 'Default Printer' set up in the SM User Defaults screen under the path: Applications -> System Manager -> Company Setup -> User defaults.

Once it is set up, we could observe that the 'Printer name' field drop-down would show the Default printer set up, that is on the user's Machine, and the rest of the printers tied to that workstation will be available just around that printer name position in the drop-down, ensuring the ease of access.

Now, the printer list has been automatically scrolled to the position where the Default printer for that workstation is located. As a result, the other printers associated with that same workstation will appear either just above or just below the Default printer in the list. This arrangement makes it much easier to locate the necessary printers, without the need to scroll through the entire list. This optimized positioning helps streamline the selection process and improves overall efficiency when choosing printers from the list.

64f02903-e0d8-4e7c-928f-25e4ca9c4b74.title: How to perform GL Transactions Import
64f02903-e0d8-4e7c-928f-25e4ca9c4b74.content:
Problem
How to perform GL Transactions Import for the following .csv file?

Resolution
It is a 3-step process that comprises of the following:

I. Set up the SM Import Layout Definition:

- Go to the SM Import Layout definition under the path: Applications -> System Manager -> Company Setup -> Import Layout Definition
- Click on 'New' icon at the top to create a new Layout ID
- Layout ID: Enter the Layout ID as preferred
- Description: Enter the Description for the layout.
- File Type: Select a File Type that describes the plain-text source file. [The most common file type is ‘Delimited’].
- Number of rows: Enter the Number of rows the system should skip before importing the data. [Usually, we will have a title row for the columns, so we would enter ‘1’ to skip the first row].
- Field separator: Select the Field separator used in the source file to separate the fields. A Comma is the most common separator.
- Row separator: Select the Row separator used in the source file. The most common separator is the ‘CRLF' (carriage return line feed)
- Text qualifier: Select the Text qualifier that is used when a field separator occurs within a field. If there are no such entries, enter 'NONE'
- Filename: We can either enter the path and filename where the source file is located or browse to the source file under the 'Filename'. This enables us to use the 'Get Fields' function, which directs the system to read the column names from the source file and fill in the detail grid.
- Get Fields: The Get Fields function will only work if the first row of the source file contains column headings. If we do not have a path and filename selected, enter the column names from the source file into the detail grid with a data Type of ‘RawText’
- All the fields, including numeric or date fields, will be imported as a data type of ‘RawText’, and this needs to be later converted to the desired data type with the help of following functions:

FunctionSyntaxDescriptionLEN=LEN([FieldId])Returns the numeric length the identified field value.TRIM=TRIM([FieldId])Removes leading and trailing spaces from the identified field value. Returns a text value.SUBSTRING=SUBSTRING([FieldId], start, length)Returns the subset of text characters from the identified field value.CONVERT=CONVERT([FieldId])Converts the identified field value to the field type of the current field.ISNULL=ISNULL([FieldId1],[FieldId2])Replaces a null (or empty string) value with the identified replacement value.NULLIF=NULLIF([FieldId1],[FieldId2])Returns a null when the value of field 1 matches the value of field 2.ROWID=ROWID()Returns the sequential id of the source data.GETDATE=GETDATE()Returns the current session date (workstation date).XLATE=XLATE([FieldId])
Extended: val1;xlate1;val2;xlate2Translates the value of the identified field using a set of key/value pairs provided in the Extended properties of the field definition.PARSE=PARSE([FieldId], "mask")
Evaluates the contents of the identified field using a preset mask to specify positional attributes of the field value.



- ​​​​​​​Once everything is set up as desired, click on 'Save' at the top to save the Layout:


II. Set up the SM Import Map Definition:

- Go to the SM Import Map Definition under the path: Applications -> System Manager -> Company Setup -> Import Map Definition
- Click on the New icon to create a new Import Map ID
- Function ID: Select a Function ID for the map definition. [Use the ‘Default’ option unless we are importing IN Item Price (IN Pricing) or SO Customer Pricing (Pricing)]
- Description: Enter the Description for the Map ID.
- Assembly: Browse the assembly as TRAVERSE.Business.GeneralLedger
- Class ID: Use the Class ID as TRAVERSE.Business.GeneralLedger.TransactionImport for GL Transactions Import
- Expand the properties grid of the schema by clicking on the plus sign. Set up the necessary mappings for the GL import.
- Once everything is set up as desired, click on 'Save' at the top to save the Map ID.

III. Import the data into Traverse through SM Mapped data:

- Go to SM Import Mapped Data under the path: Applications -> System Manager -> Company Setup -> Import Mapped Data
- Map ID: Select the Map ID that was set under Import Map Definition.
- File Name: Choose the CSV file containing the GL Transactions. [It may appear by default, if it was already set up in the SM Import Layout Definition]
- Click on the "Read Data" button to Read the data from the File.

- Once the data was read successfully, click on 'Verify Data' button to check the data for errors. If the data has errors, those records will be flagged. If there are no errors, it will appear as follows, and then we can import the data into the GL transactions screen.​​​​​​​

​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

Now we can observe the transactions being imported into the GL transactions screen under the path: Applications -> General ledger -> Transactions -> Transactions:

6a6027c4-5d46-4a98-b965-820d7cb7e626.title: Double-sided Printing issue after changing the Default Printer
6a6027c4-5d46-4a98-b965-820d7cb7e626.content:
Problem
The User had changed their Default Printer recently, and they updated the new Printer in the Form Printers screen as well. Yet, the user is experiencing double-sided printing issue.

Resolution
Traverse doesn’t offer specific settings for controlling single-sided or double-sided printing directly. Instead, it reflects the default Windows printer settings configured on the User's workstation.

In order to resolve this, we need to review the Printer properties, and the Printing Preferences of the corresponding Printer that is set as the Default in the Windows Control Panel. [NOTE: The Printer properties is the usual place that will be reviewed by the User. It is important to pay attention to Printing Preferences as well.]

1. Go to Control Panel -> Devices and printers:

2. Right click on the corresponding printer and go to 'Printer Properties'

3. Review the Printing Defaults under the Printer Properties:

4. If that is alright, right click on the corresponding printer and go to 'Printing Preferences' screen or click on to the 'Preferences' icon on the General tab of the Printer Properties screen:

5. Navigate to find the 'Print on both sides' setting, set it to 'No' and click on 'OK' [Depending upon the Printer Model, the organization of the settings may look different and the "Print on both sides" setting may be located in different places such as the "Printing Shortcuts" tab, or the "Layout" tab or the "Advanced" tab.]

6. This will resolve the Double-sided printing issues, while printing the Checks/Vouchers/Reports out of Traverse.

d3b46f0a-054f-41c9-8d1f-60a5ef942d7a.title: Setting FUTA tax rate to 0%
d3b46f0a-054f-41c9-8d1f-60a5ef942d7a.content:
Problem
When the customer is self-funded or if they are a non profit they will be exempt from Federal Unemployment Taxes (FUTA). If setup is not done correctly, Payrolls can be calculated and posted with a FUTA tax on the checks.

Resolution
Login to Traverse. Go to the respective company.

Since the customer don't want to have Fed/FUT we would need to make the percentage zero in the formula tables.

Go to Payroll > Setup and Maintenance > Formula Tables.

Turn on the Show Company Specific Tax Table checkbox on the right side of the screen.

Click the New button at the top of the screen and fill in a new tax table entry as shown below.  Be sure to choose the appropriate Payroll Year.

Making this change will cause the FUTA tax to calculate to 0$ for all subsequent Payroll checks.  This will not make corrections to any checks that have already been posted.  Incorrect taxes on posted checks will need to be corrected with Manual Checks.

1f3f7ccc-588d-4224-a026-de0ba7065690.title: How to update the System Administrator Password for SQL Server Management Studio?
1f3f7ccc-588d-4224-a026-de0ba7065690.content:
Problem
How to update the System Administrator Password for SQL Server Management Studio?

The User had forgot the password to log into the SSMS and the Traverse Server manager. But SSMS is allowing user to log in with the 'Windows Authentication', and the User would like to update the Password for System Administrator (sa) to enable log in with 'SQL Server Authentication'

Resolution
If we have Admin privilege for the Login associated with the 'Windows Authentication', we can update the credentials as expected as follows:

1. Open SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS): Launch SSMS and connect to the SQL Server instance using appropriate credentials. [Windows authentication]

2. In the Object Explorer panel on the left side, expand the Security folder:

3. Under the Security folder, expand the Logins folder:

4. Locate the 'sa' login, right-click on it and select Properties:

5. In the 'Login Properties' window, navigate to the General page [It will populate by default]

6. Enter the New password in the Password field. Ane re-enter the same password again in the Confirm Password field:

7. If you want to enforce the password policy, ensure the Enforce Password Policy checkbox is checked. This enforces the password to meet the Windows password policy requirements. [NOTE: This step is Optional]

8. Click 'OK' to save the changes.

9. Now, we can 'Disconnect' from the instance and log back in with the updated credentials, and SSMS will let us in with the New credentials with SQL Server Authentication.

a753e633-1e8f-4ec6-af95-5084a51b292f.title: perpetual license re registration failure emails from basis (OSAS)
a753e633-1e8f-4ec6-af95-5084a51b292f.content:
Problem
Steps to check the parameters. when we receive perpetual license re-registration failure emails from basis

Resolution
Basically, there are couple of parameters we need to check here.

1.  We need to check the SAM feature expiration date for the license your system is using. If it's nearing expiration, then you need to get a new license.
2.  If the SAM feature still has validity, then you need to just re-register the license. but this part will happen automatically if you leave your system on so that the license gets automatically re-registered.
3.  Or You can manually re-register the license using the BLM admin utility.
4.  If the SAM feature has passed the expiry date, then you will start getting nag messages while using OSAS and it will make the work difficult.
5.  If it is expired create a fulfillment request for a new license.

The parameters for getting the emails for license registration failure are as follows;

1. BASIS relinquished ownership of the basis.com domain in 2022 and moved most of its operations to the basis. cloud domain.

2. The subdomain that hosts the backend of BASIS’ licensing system moved in 2022 to the license.poweredbybbj.com subdomain.

3. The license.basis.com subdomain redirects to license.poweredbybbj.com till July 31, 2023.

4. All users must ensure that they have either updated their BLM to the most current and secure BLM 21 which is coded to update via license.poweredbybbj.com subdomain        or
They are required to be running the BLS.

5. Make sure the server is running 24X7 so that there is no interruption to obtain the update.

6. Once the BLM is updated to the latest version it's mandatory to register your license using the BLM admin utility. So that the new license will reach out to the new domain Basis. Cloud.
instead of old Basis.com.

9d7d02d8-b307-43fe-a567-984aa9123f7d.title: Form Printers (OSAS)
9d7d02d8-b307-43fe-a567-984aa9123f7d.content:
Problem
How to define the printers and workstations using Form Printers.

Resolution
Use the Form Printers function to define the printers and workstations from which to print forms. If you have set up a form code for the form, use this function to specify which printer should print the copies of the form. To work with form printers, select Form Printers from the Company Setup menu.

Follow these steps to use the screen to add or edit a form printer:

- If you are adding a new printer, select the Form Type that you want to print to a specific printer. If you are editing an existing printer, the form type for the selected line on the Form Printers screen appears.
- To print the selected form for a specific company to the printer you select, enter or edit the Company ID for which to print the form type. Leave this field blank to print this form for all companies to the printer you select.
- To print forms generated by a specific workstation to the printer you select, enter or edit the Workstation ID. Otherwise, leave this field blank.
- Enter the Printer Device ID to use to print the selected form. You can select only from the printers that are set up in the Devices function on the Installation and Configuration menu. The printer's name appears. If you use multiple printers, you need to define each on a separate line.
- Use the Proceed (OK) command to save your entries and return to the Form Printers screen.

a43472d3-51f8-418e-b2dd-62c0777249eb.title: OSAS Batch Control
a43472d3-51f8-418e-b2dd-62c0777249eb.content:
Problem
How to add a new batch ID

Resolution
Use the Batch Control function to inquire about the status of your batches, to set up new batches, and to maintain existing batches. If you did not elect to use transaction batching, you cannot use this function. Select Batch Control from the Daily Work menu. The Batch Control screen appears.

1. Enter the batch ID with which you want to work in the Batch ID box. If you elected to use automatic batch number generation in the Options and Interfaces function, you can create a new batch ID by using the Proceed (OK) command.
2. Enter a description of the transactions in this batch in the Description text box.
3. If a terminal ID appears in the Lock Flag box, the batch is or was produced or posted on that terminal. Do not change it unless you need to release a locked batch.
4. Enter the status of the batch: H if it is on hold, or R if it has been released. If you place the batch on hold, you can print or post it, but you cannot enter or edit transactions in it.
5. Check the Permanent? box to make the keep the batch from being deleted upon processing.
6. For each report listed, toggle the report status. The report status begins as Not Applicable. When you enter purchases or miscellaneous debits, the status automatically changes to Unprinted. When you print the report, the status automatically changes to Printed. If you then add or change transactions, the status automatically changes to Reprint. 7. If you selected a batch that is in use, the terminal ID and the user name of the person entering transactions are displayed. A maximum of 20 terminal IDs can appear at one time. After you save the information, enter information about a different batch ID, or exit to the Daily Work menu.

8907c80d-82e9-4a2d-a11d-e1b30d46f71b.title: OSAS Change Batches
8907c80d-82e9-4a2d-a11d-e1b30d46f71b.content:
Problem
How to manually change the batch ID

Resolution
The Change Batches function allows you to manually change the batch ID for a single transaction or an entire batch of transactions that has not been posted. If you did not elect to use transaction batching, you cannot use this function. Select Change Batches from the Daily Work menu. The Change Batches screen appears.

1. Select the type of change you want to make in the Change section of the screen. You can copy a single transaction to a new batch, or you can move all transactions from one batch to another.
2. Enter the batch number from which you want to change in the Old Batch ID box.
3. If you selected the Transaction Number change option, enter the transaction number for which you want to change batch IDs.
4. Enter the batch number to which you want to change in the New Batch ID box. After the transactions are copied and the corresponding log is produced, the Daily Work menu appears.

f4f1ce06-7ecd-48b9-be50-af59e41b31ce.title: OSAS Copy Recurring Entries
f4f1ce06-7ecd-48b9-be50-af59e41b31ce.content:
Problem
How to copy recurring entries

Resolution
Use the Copy Recurring Entries function to copy entries from the APRHxxx and APRLxxx (Recurring Entries) files to the APTDxxx and APTHxxx (Transaction) files when the recurring entries come due. Use the run codes and cutoff dates that you set up in the Recurring Entries function to copy the transactions according to your schedule. After you copy an entry, it is treated like another transaction. When the APTDxxx and APTHxxx files are posted, the entries are moved to the APINxxx (Open Invoice) file.
Before you copy recurring entries, produce the Recurring Entries List and back up your files. If you are using Accounts Payable on a multiuser system, make sure that no one else is using the Recurring Entries function. You cannot copy recurring entries until the other users exit from that function.
Select Copy Recurring Entries from the Daily Work menu. The Copy Recurring Entries screen appears.

1. Enter the run codes whose recurring entries you want to copy.
2. Edit the period and year to which to copy entries, if necessary.
3. When you entered recurring entries, you may have entered cutoff dates for them. Accept the system date as the cutoff date, or enter a different date. Entries that have cutoff dates before the date you enter here are not copied to the APTDxxx and APTHxxx files.
4. If you elected to use transaction batching in the Options and Interfaces function, enter the Batch ID to which to copy the recurring transactions.
5. Select how to output the Copy Recurring Entries Report. This report lists the total amount of recurring entries that were copied to the APTDxxx and APTHxxx files, and any errors that occurred (such as a recurring entry for a vendor whose record has been deleted from the APVExxx file). After the report is produced, the Daily Work menu appears.

afcf9c17-4661-4754-b801-e473c5d46598.title: Voiding a payroll check
afcf9c17-4661-4754-b801-e473c5d46598.content:
Problem
How to Void a check in Payroll

Resolution
Please follow the steps to Void the checks:

1. Enter the ID of the employee for which you want to void a check.
2. Enter the check number you want to void.
3. If Payroll interfaces with Bank Reconciliation, enter the bank account to which the check was posted. This field appears only if Payroll interfaces with Bank Reconciliation.
4. The current period appears. Press Enter to accept the current period or enter a different GL period to which you want the resulting journal entries posted.
5. If last-year files exist in General Ledger, select the fiscal year to which you want to post.
6. Enter the payroll tax month to which you want to post.
7. If the check originated from transactions you entered in the Transactions function and you want to create a copy of the voided check in the Transactions file, select the box (or enter Y in text mode); if not, clear the box (or enter N in text mode). If the check originated from entries made in the Manual Checks or Calculated Checks function and you want to create a copy of the voided check in the Checks file, select the box (or enter Y in text mode); if not, clear the box (or enter N in text mode).
8. If the check originated from transactions you entered in the Transactions function, choose the Batch ID for the check.

9.Next, run the page and you will get a printout of what was voided

d34e8aff-0814-4991-be15-b9876c5ba2d8.title: How to assign account type to a range of account numbers (OSAS)
d34e8aff-0814-4991-be15-b9876c5ba2d8.content:
Problem
How to assign account type to a range of account numbers in OSAS

Resolution
Use the Assign Account Types function to assign an account type to a range of account numbers.

1. Select Assign Account Types from the File Maintenance menu.

2. Enter the range of accounts to which you want to assign account types.
3. Enter the account type you want assigned to this range.

When you assign an account type to a range of account numbers, the code for the default balance type is also assigned to the range. If an account’s balance type is changed when you use this function, the activity amount for that account is multiplied by -1.
For example, if you assign an account type with a debit code to a range of account numbers that includes an account with a credit balance, the activity amount for that account is multiplied by -1 to produce a debit activity amount.

Instead of including the account in the range when you use the Assign Account Types function, use the GL Accounts function to edit the account. When you are editing the account type in the GL Accounts function, you can override the default code for the balance type. After you use the Proceed (OK) command to assign account types, the File Maintenance menu appears.
