ff0e2714-fd2e-4c9b-a16c-9f98bb9f20e8.title: How to void checks in Payroll
ff0e2714-fd2e-4c9b-a16c-9f98bb9f20e8.content:
Problem
How to Void a check in Payroll

Resolution
Use the Void Checks function to void checks that you have printed and posted but need to reverse or void. You can create a copy of the voided check so that a new check can be printed for the employee. Note: You cannot, however, void a check from a previous version of Payroll. The check you want to void must be posted to history.

When you select a check to void, the system searches for and verifies the check in Check History file. Then the system checks the Checks file; if a batch of checks is in process (that is, calculated and/or entered but not posted), you cannot void a check.


Voiding a check is the reverse of posting. The check is backed out; if Payroll interfaces with General Ledger and Bank Reconciliation, the check history is backed out of those applications. The check remains in the check file but is marked as a voided check.

So, whatever is posted will be reversed and whatever account that it is affected is also reversed.

Use the following steps to create a Void check in PA

Select Void Checks from the Payday Work menu.

1. Enter the ID of the employee for which you want to void a check.
2. Enter the check number you want to void.
3. If Payroll interfaces with Bank Reconciliation, enter the bank account to which the check was posted. This field appears only if Payroll interfaces with Bank Reconciliation.
4. The current period appears. Press Enter to accept the current period or enter a different GL period to which you want the resulting journal entries posted.
5. If last-year files exist in General Ledger, select the fiscal year to which you want to post.
6. Enter the payroll tax month to which you want to post.
7. If the check originated from transactions you entered in the Transactions function and you want to create a copy of the voided check in the Transactions file, select the box (or enter Y in text mode); if not, clear the box (or enter N in text mode). If the check originated from entries made in the Manual Checks or Calculated Checks function and you want to create a copy of the voided check in the Checks file, select the box (or enter Y in text mode); if not, clear the box (or enter N in text mode).
8. If the check originated from transactions you entered in the Transactions function, choose the Batch ID for the check.
9. Select the output device to print the Void Checks Audit Log

cf33e5f9-10ae-4d16-9c2f-35d417cbe5aa.title: OSAS Periodic Maintenance
cf33e5f9-10ae-4d16-9c2f-35d417cbe5aa.content:
Problem
How to use the Periodic Maintenance function to clear your vendor records and prepare them for activity for the next period, quarter, or year.

Resolution
Period-end maintenance clears the period-to-date totals in the APVExxx (Vendor) file and deletes records of temporary vendors you paid in full from the APVExxx file. Quarter-end maintenance performs the period-end tasks and clears the quarterto-date totals in the APVExxx file.

Year-end maintenance performs the period-end tasks for periods 12 and 13, performs the quarter-end tasks, clears the year-to-date totals in the APVExxx file, and transfers those totals to the last-year fields.

If you have a multiuser system, make sure that no one else is using the Accounts Payable system. You cannot run this function while someone else is using Accounts Payable functions

Select Periodic Maintenance from the Periodic Processing menu. The function screen appears

1. The information in the Vendor Analysis Report comes from the APVExxx file. Since the Periodic Maintenance function affects the data in the APVExxx file, print the Vendor Analysis Report and back up your data files before you do period-, quarter-, or year-end maintenance. If you have not printed the report and backed up your data files, clear the check box (or enter N in text mode); you are prompted to return to the Periodic Processing menu. When you have done these things, select the check box (or enter Y in text mode).
2. Select the type of maintenance you want to do. You can perform period-, quarter-, or year-end maintenance.
3. If you are at the end of the calendar year and you want to move the values in the 1099 Payments Year to Date field to the 1099 Payments Last Year field in the vendor records, select the check box (or enter Y in text mode); if not, clear the check box (or enter N in text mode). If you do not transfer the 1099 payments at the end of the calendar year, the system continues to accumulate the next calendar year’s 1099 payments in the 1099 Payments Year to Date field in the vendor records. When you produce 1099 forms, the 1099 payment amounts will be incorrect.
4. The current period and fiscal year from the APPDxxx table appears.
5. To begin processing, use the Proceed (OK) command. When the media is prepared, the Periodic Processing menu appears.

e9289184-d21c-4721-b7e6-f5a345c1f445.title: OSAS Hold/Release invoices
e9289184-d21c-4721-b7e6-f5a345c1f445.content:
Problem
How to change the status of individual invoices using the Hold/Release Invoices function

Resolution
Hold/Release Invoices function is valuable if you need to change the status of a particular invoice from what it was when you entered it. You can put an invoice on permanent or temporary hold so that it is not automatically paid when you prepare and print checks. (An invoice on temporary hold is automatically released when you post checks.) You can also release an invoice that is on permanent or temporary hold.

You can pay off an invoice at once, change an invoice’s due date and discount amount, and split the invoice amount into an unlimited number of payment installments. You can prepay part or all of an invoice and print an on-demand check for prepaid invoices right from the Hold/Release Invoices function.

Select Hold/Release Invoices from the Pay Invoices menu. The Hold/Release Invoices screen appears.

Use one of these commands to perform the associated action:
- Vendor: Press V to view invoices for a different vendor. Then enter the Vendor ID.
- First: Press F to hold or release invoices for the first vendor on file.
- Last: Press L to hold or release invoices for the last vendor on file.
- Next: Press N to hold or release invoices for the next vendor on file.
- Prev: Press P to hold or release invoices for the previous vendor on file.

1.To print an on-demand check for a prepaid invoice, press O. The check printing dialog box will appear, asking you to mount the proper forms.
2. to edit an invoice, select the invoice you want to edit, and press Enter. This screen appears:

3. Either accept or change the default discount date, due date, discount amount, and method of payment. Use the Proceed (OK) command to save your changes and return to the scroll region.
4. To change an invoice’s status by toggling between different statuses, press H. The statuses appear in this order: Temporary, Hold, Released. Keep pressing H until the correct status appears.
5. To change the status of all invoices from one type to another (for the selected vendor), press A and select the new status from this window:

6. To pay an invoice that is not due yet, press R. Then, enter the method of payment, the check number (if applicable), and the payment date of the prepayment in this window:

7. To split payments for an invoice, press S. Then, enter the payment amount and date due in this window:

8. To view totals for the vendor, press T. When you finish viewing the totals, press any key to return to the Hold/Release Invoices scroll region.

9.To view payment totals, press Y. When you finish looking at the payment totals, press any key to return to the Hold/Release Invoices screen.

When you finish working with the invoices for this vendor, press V and enter another vendor ID, or use the Exit (F7) command to return to the Pay Invoices menu.

1bc877f5-65bd-49b2-bcb1-8ff8f8d102ef.title: How to create a Direct Deposit File (OSAS)
1bc877f5-65bd-49b2-bcb1-8ff8f8d102ef.content:
Problem
How to create a Direct Deposit File in OSAS?

Resolution
Use the Create Direct Deposit File function on the Payday Reports and Posting submenu of the Payday Work menu to create an ACH (Automated Clearing House) file. This function is available only if you have Direct Deposit installed.

The ACH file contains all the direct deposit transaction information for your employees. After you have created the ACH file, send it to your company’s bank. You cannot create this file if you are using last-year data, or if employer bank information has not been set up.

- Select Create Direct Deposit File from the Payday Reports and Posting submenu.
- The payroll number, quarter, group code, period end, date on checks, GL period, bank account number, and payroll tax month for the post appear. You entered this information in the Calculate Checks or Manual Checks functions.
- Press Enter to accept the current file name or enter a different name. The system appends your company ID to this file name and lists the file’s path.
- Select the output device to print the ACH File Creation Report summarizing the contents of the file.

749e3d31-8adf-4b47-94c0-7d98d5fc4780.title: How to Calculate Checks in Payroll (OSAS)
749e3d31-8adf-4b47-94c0-7d98d5fc4780.content:
Problem
How to Calculate Checks in Payroll for OSAS?

Resolution
If Direct Deposit is installed, you can also use the Calculate Checks function to calculate direct deposit transactions at the same time you calculate checks. You cannot use the Calculate Checks function if you are working with last-year files.

Please follow the steps to Calculate checks:

Select Calculate Checks from the Payday Work menu.

If you calculated checks or entered manual checks without finishing the payday steps, the following message appears: Checks are already on file. Do you want to start over?
Note: If you calculate checks again, the data that is on file is erased. Make sure that the previous day’s payday work cycle was completed properly. If it was not, do not calculate checks again, because the checks that were issued are not reflected in the payroll totals or in the General Ledger balances. To verify checks that have been calculated, print the Check Register
If you do not want to calculate checks, select No (or enter N in text mode) to exit to the Payday Work menu. If you want to calculate checks again, erasing the checks that are on file, select Yes (or enter Y in text mode).

- Payroll number and Quarter will be auto populated from the PACTLxxx table.
- Enter group codes 0-9. The codes you enter determine which employees are paid. The codes are compared to the group code for each employee in the PAEGxxx (Employee General Information) file. You cannot add a check for an employee who is not in an included group code. If you elect to include salary wages in this check run, salaried employees with the group code you enter are paid their salary amount, less deductions and taxes. Hourly employees with the group code you enter are paid according to the earnings accumulated in the PATPxxx file from transactions entered, less deductions and taxes.
- Enter the date the pay period ends & Date on Checks. The system uses this date and the period beginning date you enter for each group code (and checks each employee’s start and termination dates in the employee records) to verify employment during the pay period.
- The G/L period is used when you post checks. The totals for the checks produced are posted to the General Ledger period you specify. (The totals in the payroll system is affected in the current period, regardless of the period you enter.) Press Enter to post the checks to the current period or enter a different period.
- Then enter the Bank ID which to use for the run checks. After that enter the payroll tax month you want updated by these checks when you post them.
- The system uses Period Beg date and the period ending date you entered above to verify employment during the pay period. For each group code you entered, enter a date for the start of the pay period, or press Enter to accept the current date.
- The period code you entered in the Scheduled Deductions section of the Employee Salary Information screen indicates when and how each scheduled deduction is taken. During check calculation, the period codes are compared to the codes in the employee record to determine which deductions will be taken.
- Select the box (or enter Y in text mode) to include direct deposit transactions in the check calculations. Clear the box (or enter N in text mode) to exclude direct deposit transactions and to produce checks for all employees. If you exclude them, paychecks are produced for employees whose pay is normally directly deposited.
- Select the box (or enter Y in text mode) to include salary wages in the calculation for the group codes entered; clear the box (or enter N in text mode) to exclude the wages. Only time ticket and miscellaneous payroll information is processed, so you can process bonus checks without processing the salary wage.
- Calculate Vacation/Sick Accruals appears if you elected to use this option in the Resource Manager Options and Interfaces function. If you want the system to calculate vacation and sick accruals, select the box (or enter Y in text mode); if not, clear the box (or enter N in text mode).
- Select the output device to print the Calculate Checks Log.

Note: Employees with an inactive status will only have checks calculated for them if they have transactions posted (a warning message will appear on the Calculate Checks log). If the inactive employee is salaried and does not have a time ticket posted, they will not have a check calculated for them during the Calculate Check processing

29af0221-b5ed-41af-a241-d3c9974bf475.title: How to navigate through Menus in RM (OSAS)
29af0221-b5ed-41af-a241-d3c9974bf475.content:
Problem
How to navigate through Menus in RM (OSAS)?

Resolution
Use the Menus function to change the OSAS main menu or the menus for any application that is installed for the current company.

You can also use this function to add documents (word processing documents, spreadsheets, graphic files, and so on) to a menu so that users can open them directly from OSAS. When you add a document to a menu using a Type of A, OSAS uses the associations you set up in the File Types function to launch the appropriate software application and open the file.

Follow these steps to customize the OSAS menus:
1. Select Menus from the System File Utilities menu

2. To work with an application menu, enter the Application. Enter OS to work with the Other Commands (F4) menu. To work with the main menu, leave the Application field blank and press Enter. OSAS automatically enters MAIN in the Menu field and moves you to the Title field.
3. If you selected an application above, enter the Menu you want to customize or enter a new one. If you entered OS above, enter MAIN.
4. Enter or edit the Title, if necessary, and press Enter to move to the menu listing in the scrolling region. The scrolling region is available only after you’ve entered a title.
5. Use the commands to work with the menu listings:
6. Press Enter to edit the selected line. The Edit Menu screen appears. See “Editing a Menu Item”.

- Press M to move the selected line to a different line. When the Move Line prompt appears, enter the line number to which to move the line to and press Enter. The other lines move up to fill the vacant space.
- Press C to copy a line to a selected blank line. When the Copy Line prompt appears, enter the line number you want to copy to the blank line and press Enter. You cannot use this command on a line that already contains an entry.
- Press S to swap the selected line with another, then enter the line number to swap with this one and press Enter.
- Press U to enter a letter of the alphabet before each line item, making each one unique. This command lets you move through the menu faster by entering the letter of the item you want to select from the menu.
- Press T to return to the Title field to change the title of the menu.
- Press W to save your changes. When the verification message appears, enter Y to save your changes or N if you do not want to save.

Editing a Menu Item

1.To edit a menu item, select the line to edit on the Menus screen and press Enter

2. Edit the menu item’s Description, if necessary. This description can be the name of the menu, function, or an informational line.
3. If you use the MDI menu, enter a Short Description for the item. This short description appears as the name on the application’s tab (if you are editing the main menu) or as the name of the function within a menu. If the Short Description field is blank, the system uses the information in the Description field on the MDI menu instead.
4. Select the menu item’s type:

- 0 indicates that the line contains only descriptive comment information.
- 1 indicates that the line is a menu file that uses another menu file.
- 2 indicates that the line is a record using another menu from the current file.
- 3 indicates that the line executes an application program.
- 4 indicates that the line calls or executes a public program.
- 5 indicates that the line executes an operating system command.
- 6 indicates that the line executes a public program directly.
- 7 indicates that the line opens an EIS dashboard.
- 8 indicates that the line opens a GENERAL Report Writer report.
- 9 indicates that the line starts an ODBC function.
- A indicates that the line uses file type associations to launch an application and open the file indicated in the Program field.
- B indicates that the line opens a Jasper report.
- C indicates that the line opens a URL or website in BBj’s Web Browser control within the OSAS framework.

Note: The BBj Web Browser control is only available in BBj 14.10 and higher.

5. If the menu item uses another menu or calls a program or command, enter the program name, menu file name, menu record name, or operating system command to execute in the Program field. If you selected a type of 0, leave this field blank. If you are attaching a document to a menu, enter the document’s file name in the Program field.

6. Enter a parameter for the menu selection. If you selected a type of 0 for the line or if you do not need a parameter, leave this field blank.

7. Select the menu item’s Function Type. The function type is predefined for established menu items and will be blank for menus or submenus. The type selected also determines the icon in the MDI menu and whether reports/ forms/posts are archived.

- 1 indicates that the function is a report in the Jasper Report format.
- 2 indicates that the function is an inquiry.
- 3 indicates a maintenance function.
- 4 indicates a data entry function.
- 5 indicates that the function is a Microsoft Excel spreadsheet.
- 6 indicates that the function is a Microsoft Word document.
- 7 indicates that the function is an ODBC report.
- 8 indicates a miscellaneous function.
- 9 indicates that the function is a form.
- A indicates that the function is a post.
- B indicates that the function performs an update or copies data.
- Z indicates that the function is a report in the traditional character format.

8. Use the Proceed (OK) command to save your changes and return to the Menus screen.

222c64a1-891c-4308-9b95-b6889f5b86bd.title: How to Edit Transaction in the GL (OSAS)
222c64a1-891c-4308-9b95-b6889f5b86bd.content:
Problem
How to edit the entries which is not posted in the General Ledger?

Resolution
Use the Edit Transactions function to change transactions that have not been posted to the GLMAxxx (Master) file. You can change any field except the source code. Because you cannot edit entries that have been posted, only unposted entries appear.

Note: Print the GL Journal before and after you edit transactions so that you have an audit trail of the transactions you changed. You also need the GL Journal to find the entry numbers of the transactions you want to edit.

1. Select Edit Transactions from the Journal Transactions menu

2.Use the commands to edit the transactions that appear:

- Press Enter to edit the selected transaction line.
- Press L to change the allocation flag of the selected transaction line.
- Press G to go to a transaction line, then enter the account number. This command is available only if there is more than one screen of transactions

3.When you press Enter on the command bar, the Edit Line screen appears

Note: you can change except Source.

4. Select the GL Account number that you want to edit from the GL account option.
5. Enter the amount in the Debit or Credit amount column if you want to make changes for that amount.
6. You can add the description of the transaction in the Trans Desc filed.
7. A reference identifies the origin of the transaction. If the transaction originated in General Ledger, the reference entered in the Transactions function appears. If the transaction originated in another application, the application initials appear; for example, if the transaction was posted from Fixed Assets, FA appears.
8. The date the transaction was posted to General Ledger appears in the Post Date filed.
9. The accounting period that corresponds to the transaction date will be shown in the GL period.
10. In the allocate box If the transaction will be allocated when it is posted, the box is selected (or Y appears in text mode); if not, the box is cleared (or N appears in text mode).
11. Use the Proceed (OK) command to save your changes and return to the Edit Transactions screen. Continue editing transactions, if necessary, then use the Exit (F7) command to return to the Journal Transactions menu when you are finished.

193bfb48-0b3f-4418-90bb-24af9d218b4b.title: How to reapply/apply an Traverse standard/ Global License Key

f1155ec6-a299-44d5-900e-992f7c559dd0.title: Options and Interfaces
f1155ec6-a299-44d5-900e-992f7c559dd0.content:
Problem
How to use Options and Interfaces to set up interfaces between certain applications installed on your system and determine the way the applications function.

Resolution
Use the Options and Interfaces function on the Company Setup menu to determine the way the applications function, and to set up interfaces between certain applications installed on your system. To produce a list of the information entered in the Options and Interfaces function, use the Options and Interfaces List function on the Master File Lists menu. Select Options and Interfaces from the Company Setup menu.

Select the Option Table Type: Share or Own. If you have multiple companies and you want them to use the same options and interfaces, select Share. If you want each company to have unique options and interfaces, select Own.

For example, if you want company A to save Payroll transaction history, but not company B, enter Own for A’s option table type. Then set the options accordingly for each company. Enter the Application ID for which you want to set or view options. When you use the Proceed (OK) command, the Options table for that application appears and lists the options and interfaces available. The Resource Manager Options screen is shown below as an example.

Use the commands to work with the options and interfaces:
• Press Enter to toggle between values for the selected line.
• Press G to go to a specific option. This command is available only if there is more than one page of options for the application.
• Press W to save your changes and return to the Options and Interfaces screen.

e00f8489-14db-4dd3-a9e6-7e7e3d94fc85.title: Periodic Maintenance for Payroll (OSAS)
e00f8489-14db-4dd3-a9e6-7e7e3d94fc85.content:
Problem
How to carry out the periodic Maintenance for the Payroll?

Resolution
At the end of each calendar quarter, do quarter-end maintenance to prepare for next quarter’s data. This procedure clears out the quarter-to-date balances in the PADPxxx (Department) file, deletes history records before the date you specify (if you keep history), and increments the current quarter number in the PACTLxxx table.

At the end of each calendar year, do year-end maintenance to prepare your files for next year’s entries. This procedure clears out the quarterly and year-to-date balances in the PAEMxxx (Employee Miscellaneous History) file and the year-todate information in the PADPxxx file, deletes records of terminated employees from the PAEGxxx (Employee General Information) and PAEMxxx files, and creates these last-year files with the .LY extension:
• PACDxxx (Checks Deductions)
• PACExxx (Checks Earning)
• PACHxxx (Checks)
• PACWxxx (Checks Withholdings)
• PADDxxx (Deductions)
• PADExxx (Employee Deductions)
• PADPxxx (Department)
• PADXxxx (Deduction Exclusion)
• PAECxxx (Earning Codes)
• PAEDxxx (Employee Deduction History)
• PAEExxx (Employee Earnings History)
• PAEGxxx (Employee General Information)
• PAEMxxx (Employee Miscellaneous History)
• PAEPxxx (Employee Personnel)
•PAESxxx (Employee Federal/State/Local Withholdings)
• PAETxxx (Earnings Types)
• PAEWxxx (Employee Withholding History)
• PAEXxxx (Employee Exclusion)
• PAINxxx (Payroll Information)
• PALCxxx (Labor Class)
• PATBxxx (Tables)
• PATXxxx (Tax Tables)
• PAWIxxx (Withholdings)
• PAWXxxx (Withholding Exclusion)

The PATB.LY (LY represents last-year data) and PATX.LY files are created so that the system can distinguish differences between prior-year and current-year tax percentages. You cannot use the Periodic Maintenance function if you are working with prior-year files. You must be in quarter 4 of the current year to run year-end maintenance. Because year-end maintenance automatically does quarter-end maintenance, you do not have to perform both quarter-end and year-end maintenance at the end of period 4.

For Processing the Periodic Maintenance

- Select Periodic Maintenance from the Periodic Processing menu.
- Before you perform quarter-end or year-end maintenance, print the reports listed on the screen and back up your data files. Select the box (or enter Y in text mode) when you have completed the listed tasks.
- Select the kind of maintenance you want to perform. You can perform quarter-end or year-end maintenance, or you can purge history only (which does not close the quarter or year).
- If you want to delete history because your files are getting too large or because you no longer need check and transaction history before a particular date, enter the dates for check and transaction history to indicate where the deletion should stop. For example, if you enter 12/31/2001, history before and including that date is deleted. If you do not want to delete history, press Enter to leave the date blank.
- If you want to clear remaining sick and vacation time, select the box (or enter Y in text mode); if not, clear the box (or enter N in text mode).
- If you want to clear positive pay information, enter the transmit date for the files you want to clear. All positive pay files sent prior to that date will be purged.
- Use the Proceed (OK) command to save your entries and begin maintenance processing. When the procedure finishes, the Periodic Processing menu appears.

749fce80-69a3-41da-b0f4-c082e0f7cbc7.title: Unable to print in cloud printing when using Aptean Print Services
749fce80-69a3-41da-b0f4-c082e0f7cbc7.content:
Problem
Form printers, setup and cloud printing is enabled, and Aptean Print Service is installed, but the user is unable to print from cloud printing.

Resolution
Traverse Configuration
Open cmd (Command Prompt) and run “hostname”.  This will output the local workstation’s hostname. (Or go to Windows Settings -> System -> About and note the Device Name)
Document this value.

Make sure the user information is entered correctly in Traverse User Defaults:
In Traverse, go to System manager > Company setup > User Defaults- Admin.
Pull up the user ID and go select "SM - System Manager" in the menu list.
Check that the user's workstation name (documented in previous step), Account ID, Agent Key, and Default Printer are all correct, and Enable Cloud Print is set to Yes.

Windows Services
If these are all correct, check to ensure that the Aptean Print Service is running:

Type "Services" into the Windows search bar and press enter to open up the Services screen.
(or open cmd and run "services.msc")

Confirm “Aptean Print Agent” is set to “Automatic” and is in the “Running” state. If it is not running, then click "Restart" to restart the service.
If “Log On As” does not say “Local System”, make sure the account it is using has the correct password.
Click “Restart” to ensure the Aptean Print Agent has the correct values and is running.

Yaml  Configuration
If the above steps do not resolve the problem, check to ensure that the Print Service has been configured correctly in the yaml file:
Browse to C:\Program Files (x86)\ApteanPrintAgent and open application.yaml.  If prompted, select “Notepad”, check “Always use this app to open .yaml files”, and click “OK”.

Once opened, press Ctrl + A and confirm there are no spaces after the lines.
Confirm that the accountId is the correct value and does not start with “API” or “AGT”.
Confirm the agentKey starts with “AGT”.
Server-url should match below.

f4be703e-c3eb-466c-8739-949e43ea9dfb.title: Request users in Purchase order
f4be703e-c3eb-466c-8739-949e43ea9dfb.content:
Problem
How to add PO Request User?

Resolution
Purchase Order > Approvals > Request Users


- Click the New button, on the toolbar, to open a blank user record.
- Enter a username in the Username field.
- Select a Traverse User to associate with the portal PO request user.
- Enter a display name for the user in the Display Name field.
- Enter a Web Password for the user if you do not use trusted logins.

967e6789-1c1f-4e64-b234-08d6cac98658.title: How to Add Inbound Rules for Traverse Connections in Windows Defender Firewall
967e6789-1c1f-4e64-b234-08d6cac98658.content:
Problem
Customer would like to know how to setup a secure connection to the Traverse necessary ports (ex. 2113, 2114, or 2115) and to SQL in Windows Defender Firewall.
This is also one possible solution to the error message, "Login Failed. Cannot connect to license server: servername: Error: No connection could be made because the target machine actively refused it. ip address: port #" when they are getting this due to a firewall block.

Resolution
Open Windows Defender Firewall - (Type Windows Defender Firewall in the Windows search bar to open it.)
Click on Advanced settings on the left.
Click on Inbound Rules on the left
Click on the right: New Rule

To create an inbound rule to connect to the TCP and UDP ports:
Select, “Port” and click “Next”.
Select "TCP" and "Specific local port": and enter the port number ex: 2113 – the standard Traverse port, but whichever port Traverse is using (Check Traverse License Server Manager to verify). Click Next.

Select: "Allow the connection". Alternatively company settings can be configured under "Allow the connection if it is secure".  Click "Next".
Check at least the Domain box, but they can leave all three boxes checked depending on company security policies. Click Next.

Put in a name:

Click “Finish”.

Second Port: Follow similar steps:
Click - New Rule
Select UDP and Specific local ports and enter the port number (ex. 2113)

Click "Next".
Select "Allow the connection". Alternatively, company settings can be configured under "Allow the connection if it is secure".  Click "Next".
Check the box for at least the Domain connection, but they can leave all three boxes checked depending on company security. Click Next.
Type in a Name, "UDP Port 2113" for example. Click Finish.

To create an inbound rule to connect to the SQL Programs:
Select  - Inbound Rule: New Rule à Program

Select. “This program path” Then put in the path for the SQL Server to sqlservr.exe:

Select sqlserver.exe and click Open. Click Next.
Select to Allow the connection.  Alternatively, company settings can be configured under "Allow the connection if it is secure".  Click "Next".
Check at least the Domain box, but they can leave all three boxes checked depending on company security policies. Click Next.
Enter a Name -  ex.” sqlservr”
Click Finish.

Inbound Rule -> New Rule -> Program
Select “This program path” and enter the path to sqlbrowser from the Program Files (x86) folder:

Click Open. Click Next.
Select to Allow the connection. Alternatively, company settings can be configured under "Allow the connection if it is secure".  Click "Next".
Check at least the Domain box, but they can leave all three boxes checked depending on company security policies. Click Next.
Enter a Name -  ex. “SQL Browser”.
Click Finish.

Those are the main things that need to be allowed through the firewall: 2 Ports, 2 Programs.

These directions specifically apply to Windows Defender Firewall, but permissions need to be set up for these ports and SQL for any firewall the company is using to protect their server. Each company will need to determine its own level of security regarding the specifics of allowing the connection and the profiles for which the rules will apply.

89bf5342-a109-4dc2-873f-e10154451283.content:
Problem
Client requires information on the Key Dates tab in the Payroll Employee Information screen.

Resolution
1. Enter the employee's Adjusted Hire Date. This date would be used if the employee has left the company and comes back within the allotted amount of time to retain the accrued leave time. The start date would remain the same as the original start date so the employee will continue to accrue leave time as if they remained employed by the company.

2. Enter the employee's Start Date. This is the date used by the leave codes setup to determine which line to use to calculate the accrual of leave time when calculating checks.

3. Enter the employee's Birth Date.

4. Enter the employee's Termination Date if they have left the company. If a termination date is filled in you will get a warning message when you enter a payroll transaction. When adding a new payroll year in the Server Manager employees with a termination date will not be copied into the new payroll year database.

5. Use the Last Check Date field to select or edit the date of the last check the employee received. This field updates when you post checks.

6. Use the Last Review Date field to enter the date of the employee's last salary review.

7. Use the Next Review Date field to enter the date of the employee's next salary review.

8. Click the Save button to save your changes.

e9c7639c-7f5d-42cb-8488-1609237d19e4.title: Minnesota Transaction Retail Delivery Fee - Setup for Tax Service Integration
e9c7639c-7f5d-42cb-8488-1609237d19e4.content:
Problem
Background

Effective July 1, 2024, there will be a Retail Delivery Fee of 50 cents that applies to certain transactions involving retail delivery in Minnesota. Avalara will support the calculation, reporting, and remittance of the Minnesota Retail Delivery Fee by July 1, 2024.



- If your company/customers’ company must remit this fee, action must be taken in Avalara Portal and/or your connector to map this code.
- The customer must pass the Tax Code:  OF400000
- The fee name will be “Road Improvement and Food Delivery Fee”
- In Avalara Portal, the customer must Opt-Out of the fee in their Nexus settings if they do not want to enable calculation due to not meeting the threshold, marketplace nuances, etc.


- Additional resources have been provided below to help educate you regarding this change
- Testing will be available in sandbox environments starting on June 18, 2024.
- Change will be released to production on June 25, 2024.

Resolution
How to handle this change using the Tax Service Integration



The following steps can be taken to implement this change in Traverse Global with the Tax Service Integration. Before proceeding below, you will need to be able to access the Items function in Traverse Global to Inventory > Setup and Maintenance > Items. You must also have access to Avalara’s online Admin Console.



Use the following steps to implement this change:

- Access the Traverse Global application, and then navigate to Inventory > Setup and Maintenance > Items

-
- Create a new item, with an Item Type of Service.
- The Minnesota fee will be displayed as “Road Improvement and Food Delivery Fee” in the Avalara portal. The item’s Description can be setup as Road Improvement and Food Delivery Fee
- Please consider adding any additional Locations needed in order to use the item, and taking care to set the appropriate item codes per your business needs.





- Access Avalara’s online Admin Console and navigate to Settings > What you sell





- Click on Add an Item

4. In the Item code field, enter the inventory Item ID created in Traverse.
a.Enter a Description of Road Improvement and Food Delivery Fee
b.Enter an AVALARA TAX CODE value of OF400000
c.Click Add Item


Example



Next, we will view this change in action. First, please find an example below where goods are in process of shipping to a customer in the state of Minnesota. An item has been added at a price of $100.00 and taxes calculated with the AvaTax calculation on screen. Note: Our delivery fee item has not been added to this order.





Next, let’s verify the Tax Calculation. The Tax Calculation screen below indicated the tax breakdown for this invoice, with $8.38 of sales tax and $100.00 of taxable goods.





Next, we will add our delivery charge item to the same order and recalculate taxes.





The Net Due has increased by $0.50. The Tax Calculation will now show an increase in the invoice’s total tax.





The Traverse Global Tax Service will also display the $0.50 Tax Amount on under the Tax Details button.





Next, we will post this transaction and commit this to Avalara. If we view the transaction from the Admin Console, we will observe the $0.50 fee listed out.

0328377c-6ce1-43c6-8767-15470b36e81a.title: How to create a new Earing Code In OSAS
0328377c-6ce1-43c6-8767-15470b36e81a.content:
Problem
How to create a new Earing Code In OSAS

Resolution
An earning code stores pay rate information, the GL account number, the earning type, and other information for a particular kind of work. If you enter an earning code and the number of hours the employee worked when you enter time tickets or manual checks, the system calculates the employee’s pay based on the information you enter here. You can have an unlimited number of earning codes.

You can set up earning codes for types of work and for overtime or double-time work that automatically multiplies or adds amounts to the base pay

To create an earning code please follow the below steps:

- Select Earning Codes from the Codes Maintenance menu
- Enter the earning code
- Enter a description of the earning code
- If the pay should be included in the employee’s paycheck, select the box (or enter Y in text mode); if not, clear the box (or enter N in text mode). Including or excluding the pay from net pay does not affect taxable income. To exclude an earning code from taxable income, use the exclusion switches in your federal, state, and local withholding records.
- If you use a fixed percentage for all withholding (specified in the federal, state, and local withholding formulas), select the box (or enter Y in text mode); if not, clear the box (or enter N in text mode). If you do not use a fixed percentage, withholding is calculated according to the regular federal, state, and local tax routines.
- Enter an earning type for the earning code. Each earning code must be assigned an earning type.
- Enter the number of the GL account to which the earning code is posted. The Maintenance (F6) and Inquiry (F2) commands are available if Payroll interfaces with General Ledger.
- The number you enter in Multiplier is multiplied by the employee’s base hourly pay rate. For example, you enter an earning code with a multiplier of 1.2500. Then you enter a time ticket for an employee who uses that earning code and whose base hourly pay rate is $10 per hour. The system performs the calculations, resulting in a pay rate of $12.50 per hour. You must enter a value in this field. If you do not want to use a multiplier, enter 1.
- The number you enter in Add to Base is added to the employee’s base hourly pay rate. For example, you enter an earning code with an Add to Base factor of 0000.50. Then you enter a time ticket for an employee who uses that earning code and whose base hourly pay rate is $10 per hour. The system adds the factor to the employee rate, resulting in a pay rate of $10.50 per hour for the employee. If both a Multiplier and an Add to Base factor exist for the earning code, the Add to Base factor is added to the employee’s base pay rate first. This new base pay rate is then multiplied.
- After you approve the entries, enter another earning code, or use the Exit (F7)

a873eee4-7e26-44e3-861b-e5fe7c075b0e.title: How to create a new Earning type in OSAS
a873eee4-7e26-44e3-861b-e5fe7c075b0e.content:
Problem
How to create a new Earning type in OSAS?

Resolution
Use the Earning Types function to create groups of earning codes. The payroll system has nine preset earning types:
• Bonus
• Commission
• Fringe
• Miscellaneous
• Overtime
• Regular Earnings
•Sick
• Tips Reported as Federal Earnings
• Vacation

You cannot change or delete the preset earning types, but you can set up additional earning types.
Please follow the below steps to create a new Earning Type:

- Select Earning Types from the Codes Maintenance menu.
- Enter the ID of the earning type you want to add or change. Earning type T has special meaning (Tips) in the system. Tip amounts are accumulated in the FICA Tips field for government reporting. Earning type F also has special meaning to the system. Any earning types F that an employee receives through the year are accumulated and printed as fringe on an employee’s W-2 form. Earning types V and S are used to determine the amount of vacation and sick time taken throughout the year. Any other earning types that use a user-defined type are treated as regular pay, using the Multiplier and Add to Base fields to determine pay.
- Enter a description of the earning type.
- The last field on the screen applies only to salaried employees for whom you enter time tickets. Press A to add pay entered through time tickets to salary amounts for this earning code. Press R to replace salary amounts with pay entered through time tickets for this earning code.
- When you save the earning type, the cursor returns to the Earning Type field. Enter the next earning type you want to work with or use the Exit (F7) command to return to the Codes Maintenance menu.

4059882e-a673-4fae-a97b-25ec1f4e512f.title: How does the GL Account default for the line Items in the AP Transactions
4059882e-a673-4fae-a97b-25ec1f4e512f.content:
Problem
How does the GL Account default for the line Items, in the AP Transactions?

Resolution
1. When the client is using the Inventory setup for the Items, and if Inventory interfaces with Accounts Payable, the GL account defaults from the IN Account Codes screen in Inventory: Applications -> Inventory -> Setup and Maintenance -> Account Codes: [Note: In this case, the GL Account would be Item specific]

This Account code will be configured for the corresponding Item ID in the IN Items screen under the Location Tab for each of the Location.

2. But when the client is not using the Inventory setup for the Items, that is the Items are SM Items, it'll be using the SM Description Items under the path: Applications -> System Manager -> Company Setup -> Description Items: [Note: In this case, the GL Account would be Item specific]

3. If the item is not an Inventory or System Manager item, the GL account defaults from the AP Vendors screen under the Path: Applications -> Accounts Payable -> Setup and Maintenance -> Vendors: [Note: Unlike the other 2 cases, in this case, the GL Account would be Vendor specific]

However, the User can change the GL Account if needed, while entering the AP Transaction.

28df9bcd-f035-476a-9399-05fdb35714a9.title: GL Account is invalid for transaction
28df9bcd-f035-476a-9399-05fdb35714a9.content:
Problem
when we enter a line item in an AP Transaction> type invoice, customer receive an alert saying "GL Account is invalid for transaction".

Resolution
It is possible that the GL Account being entered is marked as inactive.

Places to check/confirm if any of the account associated with the respective invoice is inactive account:

- Invalid GL Account List:

- Navigate to System Manager> System Audit> Invalid GL Account List
- Select Accounts Payable and hit ok > It will provide you with list of Inactive accounts. Verify if the account should be inactive or if it has been made inactive for any reason. If any of the listed account should be Active, Navigate to General Ledger> Setup and Maintenance> Chart of Accounts> Select the appropriate Account from list of Account ID, change the status from Inactive to Active.



2. Conflict with the AP distribution code:  Another possibility is that there may be a conflict with the distribution code and the GL accounts associated with it.

- Under AP> Transaction> Transaction pull up the Transaction in which the error appears.
- Double click on the hyper link of the Distribution code, so that it will take you to the AP Distribution Codes screen

- On the AP Distribution Codes screen, verify each status of account numbers in Payables, Freight, Misc, Accrual, Deposit by pull it up in GL> setup and Maintenance> Chart of Accounts. If any of the account status was Inactive, need to change it to Active.

3. Tax Group ID: Another possibility is that there may be a conflict with the GL accounts associated with the Tax Location (Levels) of Tax Group ID.

- Double click on the hyper link of the Tax Group ID in AP Transaction screen, so that it will take you to the SM Tax Location Groups screen

- Double click on the hyper link of the Levels present > It will take you to SM Tax Locations

- Navigate to Rates Tab in SM Tax Locations, verify each status of account numbers in Tax Expense Acct column by pull the account number in GL> setup and Maintenance> Chart of Accounts. If any of the account status was Inactive, need to change it to Active and Save.

Upon verifying the status of all the Account Number from SM Invalid GL Account List, AP distribution code, and Tax Group ID, we should be able to figure out the Inactive account.

7fa84688-1385-41b4-8a24-140ab9fa2096.title: How to apply a deposit to a Purchase Order
7fa84688-1385-41b4-8a24-140ab9fa2096.content:
Problem
A purchase order requires a deposit before any goods are received. How do I process a deposit from the Purchase Order?

Resolution
1. Click on the Deposit button in your Purchase Order.

2. Click the "+" button at the bottom to create a new deposit and fill in the payment number, date, amount, and Bank Account. Click the checkmark at the bottom to finish it when you are done editing it.  You have the option to print the check from this deposit screen or to wait and print it later in the AP Prepare Payments process.

3. Save the Purchase Order.

58a01aa9-0405-4048-ab09-776c349f279f.title: Geo Fencing set up in OTW
58a01aa9-0405-4048-ab09-776c349f279f.content:
Problem
How to set up Geo Fencing

Resolution
The Geofence Setup screens allows company administrators to create and maintain fenced areas/shapes. Employees can trigger events when entering or leaving the fenced areas depending on the options selected for the geofence record.
- Create fences by finding the desired location on the map using the “Search for Location” field or manually moving the map using your mouse. Use the circle tool to draw a fence with a radius. Click on the stop tool to stop drawing and allows the mouse to drag the map view. Users can create as many fences as they want on a single geofence record.
- There are also color options for each shape to help organize and differentiate locations on the map. Click on a drawn fence shape to select it. Click on one of the colors to change the shape color. Once a shape is selected it may be deleted, dragged to a new location or the size changed by using the shape handles.
- There are alerts and options that can be enabled or disabled for all fence shapes on a single geofence record. If Restricted Time Punches is enabled then employees can only make time punches on their mobile devices inside one of the fences. Once outside a fence they will not be able to make any punches (sheet employees are not affected). The Notify on Enter option will e-mail a detailed notification to supervisors or company admin once an employee enters a fence zone. The Notify on Exit does the exact same thing, but when the employees exits or leaves a fence zone. The Save History option saves all event triggers to history. Admin can then run the Geofence History Report and see all geofence triggers with location and employee information. Note: Mobile phone location service is usually accurate within 50 – 100 meters. When drawing fences make them large enough to handle when location accuracy may be off those margins.
-

ed02f292-da81-4da5-a5ce-9b3f061c7509.title: How to add a new earning Code in OTW
ed02f292-da81-4da5-a5ce-9b3f061c7509.content:
Problem
How to add a new earning Code in OTW

Resolution
The Earning Codes screen is where the pay codes are setup to be used on employee timesheets and on employee records.

- Go to Company Settings
- Select Earning Code
- if you want to find an earning code and make changes use the Find earning code.
- If you want to add a new earning code type the earning code and its description.
- The system comes standard with Straight (x1), Premium (x1.5) and Double (x2) pay type multipliers.
- If you want the earning code to be tracked as a leave code, check the Track as Leave box. If the earning code is unpaid mark the corresponding checkbox.
- You can also enable and disable the earning code.
- After making the changes use the save button at the bottom to save the earning code.

Earning Code – Identification for this Earning Type (i.e., OVT for Overtime, DBL for Double time)

Description – Description of this Earning Type.

Track as Leave – Mark the earning code as a leave code for employees. When calculating overtime, employee time records with leave codes will never split.

Unpaid – Mark the earning code as an unpaid earning code. Time using this code will not be used when calculating hours and will not be exported.

Pay Type – Defines what the multiplier should be.

Include for Premium – Check this box to allow Straight Pay codes to “roll-over” to Premium codes.

Linked Premium Code – Link a specific straight time code to a specific premium code if multiple codes of each exist. This allows employees who use different straight time codes to not have to rely on the employee default overtime code when calculating overtime.

Sort Order – Determines the order in which the earning codes are displayed in the timesheet earning code drop down boxes and timesheet approval and summary.

Status – Enable or disable the earning code for use.

eff9f9d6-256a-4c5f-affa-169fd71b3bf9.title: Cloud Users getting glitch while using Traverse through the RDP icon
eff9f9d6-256a-4c5f-affa-169fd71b3bf9.content:
Problem
User is getting the glitch-like screen while launching Traverse and while opening reports out of Traverse. This issue occurs only when the user uses RDP to launch Traverse and the Web Client works completely fine.

Resolution
This issue is due to the Cache and temporary files that are stored in the User's workstation. In order to get rid of the Cache and temporary files, we would need to delete them from the Workstation.
[Note: Make sure the issue is workstation-specific]

1. Open the Run command [or use Windows key + R] and type in 'temp' and click on 'OK':

2. This will navigate to the path: Local Disk (C:) -> Windows -> Temp: Delete all the temporary files in that location. [Use Shift + Delete to permanently delete them.]

3. Again open the Run command, and type in '%temp%' and click on 'OK':

4. This will navigate to the path: Local Disk (C:) -> Users -> XXXXX -> AppData -> Local -> Temp.
Delete all the temporary files in that location as well:

5. Then delete the existing RDP file downloaded in the workstation. Clear the Browser Cache and cookies as well.

6. Go to the following link and sign in using the User's credentials: Remote Desktop Web Client (apteancloud.com)

7. Once the credentials are entered, it will redirect to a page where all the work resources [Production or Sandbox or both] allotted for that User Account:

8. Double-click on the Work resource needed, and it will take us to the following page:

9. Then choose the 'Download the rdp file' option under Settings and then launch the Traverse application:

[Note: By default, if we access the resource without this change, the application will be opened in the Web Browser]

10. Now, the User can have the RDP file saved on the Desktop and can use that to launch the application:


11. Now the User will no longer be experiencing this issue with using the new RDP file downloaded.

8f478749-eab7-4d66-8217-004c5a93ff56.title: How to create a Credit Memo to offset an AR Invoice
8f478749-eab7-4d66-8217-004c5a93ff56.content:
Problem
How to create a Credit Memo to reverse an AR Invoice that was posted to the wrong Fiscal period or Fiscal Year?

Resolution
If an AR Invoice was posted to the wrong Fiscal period or Fiscal year, we would need to create a Credit Memo in the same Fiscal period and the Fiscal period and post the same.

1. Go to Applications -> Accounts Receivable -> Interactive Views -> AR Open Invoice View: Apply the appropriate filter to pull that Invoice and observe the necessary information such as Invoice number, Fiscal period, Fiscal period, etc. there.

2. Go to Applications -> Accounts Receivable -> Transactions -> Transactions: Create a new Transaction with the Transaction Type as 'Credit Memo' and enter the other details as same as that of the Invoice. Once entered, click on 'Save' at the top.

3. Then print the Credit Memo either through Online printing or Batch printing [from AR Print Invoices screen]:

4. then, print the AR Miscellaneous Credits Journal under Applications -> Accounts Receivable -> Transaction Journals -> Miscellaneous Credits Journals:

5. Then Post the Transaction under Applications -> Accounts Receivable -> Transaction Journals -> Post Transactions:

6. Now we can observe that this Transaction is now available in the AR Open Invoice view:

7. In order to apply this Credit to the Invoice, go to the AR Hold/Release Invoices screen under the path: Applications -> Accounts Receivable -> Open Invoices -> Hold/Release Invoices: Pull up the required Customer ID (For example: 00030)

8. Select the Credit entry and click on Split/Reapply at the top.

9. In the popup window, type the credit memo amount in the Applied Amount next to the Invoice as required. And then click on 'OK.'

10. (Optional)We can run the Periodic Maintenance under the path: Applications -> Accounts Receivable -> Periodic processing -> Periodic Maintenance.

If the Periodic Maintenance is run, this Invoice will be washed off from the AR Open Invoices View.

12. Now, we can proceed with creating the AR Transaction in the right Fiscal Period and the Fiscal Year as required.

8cff24ea-31ac-4214-8b7a-c4efe6a7bb8f.title: Printing multiple Sales Order forms at the same time
8cff24ea-31ac-4214-8b7a-c4efe6a7bb8f.content:

The client needs a way of printing multiple SO forms at the same time (for example for a certain customer and based on the transaction type) rather than opening each order and printing it.
They can print from Sales Order> Transaction Journal> Print picking slip/ packing list/ Invoices >choosing an entire batch and hit print,

The problem is that it would print everything in the batch, not just the ones they wanted.

Resolution
If the SO's are still open and available under SO Transaction, create a new batch code from SO> Setup and Maintenance> Batch codes> hit new and name the batch as of your choice and select permanent and hit save as below,

You will be able to move the required SO's into a separate new batch and then can select the batch (eg. test) from Sales Order> Transaction Journal> Print picking slip/ packing list/ Invoices.

75be2c72-cfb3-4aa5-b4e8-8aefe1c2bf0b.title: How to update EPTR/ Aatrix
75be2c72-cfb3-4aa5-b4e8-8aefe1c2bf0b.content:
Problem
Having the Aatrix Installation done, there is no W2 report listed for 2023/ the recent year under PA> Quater/ Year End Reports> Enhanced Payroll Tax Reports.

Resolution
- It indicates that EPTR has not been updated. We need to update Aatrix to get the recent year report.
- Choose any report to run. When you do that, it will prompt for a form update as shown below:



-

When prompted for an update, the dialog box will include 4 options:

Automatic Update: (Recommended) The automatic update option performs the complete update install without having to navigate to a special web page to grab the update to install. Upon clicking the automatic update button, a screen displaying the progress of detecting all the differences between the forms located on your computer and the forms that are posted for the new install. Once all changes are detected, click Next to begin the install. This update will need to be run on all workstations that use the program.

Download Update: The download update option is available to physically download the update install from the web and then manually install the update on the computer. Upon clicking on the download update button, you will be directed to a partner specific web page where you can click a link to download the update. Clicking the download update button or link will prompt to save the update to the computer. After the file is saved, double click on the file and the update will install. This update will need to be run on all workstations that use the program.

Continue Expired: The continue expired option will skip the update and allow you to continue into the forms to view the information. If you attempt to print any forms without doing the update, the forms will print with an expired watermark and will not be able to eFile any of the non-updated forms.

Cancel: This option will close down the update dialog and will not perform any action. The update dialog will appear again the next time a form is opened.



-
-
- Aatrix update client window would process,

Click Next and continue to proceed with the update process.

Once the update is completed, Click Close.

Now, you will be able to locate the year 2023 in PA Enhanced Payroll Tax Reports

418466a3-3637-43c9-9f55-9399fb9f965d.title: Payments do not prepare properly - Consolidated Checks
418466a3-3637-43c9-9f55-9399fb9f965d.content:
Problem
The customer has invoices that are stuck in the "Prepare Payments" stage. They show up under Hold/Release payments, but when you click OK to choose them for payment, you receive an error message that there are no payments to prepare in the selected range, or they are simply not included in the Payment Batch.

Resolution
One possible reason for this is that the Vendor's Check Option is set to "Individual" instead of "Consolidated."
To fix this, pull up the Vendor from Accounts Payable> Setup and Maintenance> Vendors
Have a look at the Defaults tab and note the Check option. Change it to Consolidated from Individual and Save.

Now go back to prepare payment under AP>Pay Invoices> Prepare Payment and it will prepare now.

There can be other reasons why payments do not prepare such as dates past the Invoices Due date, a Vendor Hold, or the wrong Bank Account listed, etc. However, this is one common reason why checks are not preparing.

48d7ec0d-eb23-45c6-a16f-e27b57d1ebcd.title: Adding the Notes section of SO Orders into the SO Invoices for Traverse 11.2
48d7ec0d-eb23-45c6-a16f-e27b57d1ebcd.content:
Problem
How to add the Notes section available in the SO Orders screen into the SO Invoices.

The default Invoice Layout:

Resolution
1. Go to Traverse Global Studio and click on the Report Designer under Designers.

2. Choose the required Check Layout [Example: SO - Print Invoices] and click on Design.

3. Choose the appropriate report name and click on 'OK' [Here, SalesOrderInvoice is the preferred Layout]

4. Here, we are going to add the Notes section in the highlighted region of the Layout.  [If needed, this space can also be increased by moving the content above and below. But we need to be cautious that this does not push the Invoice to the next page.]

5. Click on Toolbar on the left pane and select 'Label' and drag and place the Text box in the preferred region.

6. Select the text box and click on the  icon at the top of the Label to open the Label Tasks and name the Label as preferred.

7. Choose the Table corresponding to the 'Notes' section under Data Binding. [This can also be done by dragging & dropping the Notes section available under the Table of Field List]

8. Add the Prefix as preferred under the Format string and click on 'OK.' Let the Can Grow and Word Wrap fields be enabled to accept the extending lines that may be entered in the Notes section.

9. If needed the alignment of the 'Notes' section can also be changed. [It has been set to 'Center' for now]

10. Once the changes have been made, save the Layout with the 'Default name' to the Database, to have the change reflected in the Production environment.

11. Close and reopen Traverse. We can now observe the Notes section being part of the SO Invoices, as designed.

1b405c34-badb-45e6-ac7a-4afc8ff1640e.title: Unable to run GL Trail Balance report - 'Invalid exchange rate setup'

-
- Once the missing period is added adjust the rates if necessary.
- Save it and close the SM Exchanges currency rates screen.
- This will resolve the issue with running trail balance report.

Customer is experiencing a pop-up or error message while launching OSAS.

Resolution
The customer received a pop-up or error message – BBj error.
“BBj services not running locally. Please (re)start BBjservices and try again” while launching OSAS.

In most cases, when a customer receives this kind of pop-up, we advise them to Restart the BBj services from the services or Admin.

From Admin:

Go to All programs and find the BASIS program Group this can also be launched from the bin directory OSAS8 -> BBj -> bin Launch the Admin Wizard.

Now select the Start the BBjServices and click on Next.

Then select Restart the BBjServices and click on Next.

Go to control panel -> Administrative tools -> Services.

Restart the BBjservices.

The customer won't receive that popup notice once again when they try to launch OSAS after finishing the entire procedure.

0132df18-cf59-4038-893a-afe5723b083e.title: How to change the Default Path for the Positive Pay File
0132df18-cf59-4038-893a-afe5723b083e.content:
Problem
How to change the Default Path for the Positive Pay File that is being exported out of Traverse?

Resolution
The Default Path and File name needs to be updated in the SM Export Layout Definition of the corresponding Positive Pay Layout.

1. Go to System Manager -> Company Setup -> Bank Accounts: And observe the Layout ID of the Positive Pay File associated with the Bank Account ID.

2. Go to System Manager -> Company Setup -> Export Layout Definition: And pull up the corresponding Layout ID as observed in the SM Bank Accounts screen [For example: Postest]. We can observe the existing Default Path in the File Name field.

3. Now in the File Name field and enter the file path and file name or browse to the file that needs to be used as the Export file and then hit 'Open.'

4. After updating the 'File Name' field, hit on 'Save' at the top.

5. Go to Accounts Payable -> Pay Invoices -> Create Positive Pay File: Now we can observe the updated File path in the File Name field.

System Manger -> Company setup -> User Default -> System Manager -> Setup Mode 'By User ID' or 'By Workstation ID'.

631a10ab-5317-45b6-b2c4-8ea86cbaa013.title: General Ledger year end procedure
631a10ab-5317-45b6-b2c4-8ea86cbaa013.content:
Problem
The customer wishes to perform the General Ledger year-end process.

Resolution
The following procedure is followed for the year-end process of the General Ledger -

Press F9 to access the existing last year files. Verify that all entries for the last year have been posted. (All entries must be posted in the last year, because once you use the Create Last Year function for the current fiscal year, you will no longer be able to post transactions in the existing last year).

BACKUP DATA FILES.

Go to the Accounting Periods function from the Company Setup menu in the Resource Manager and define the upcoming fiscal year.

Resource Manager -> Company Setup -> Accounting Periods.

Select Create Last-Year Data function to create the copies of the GL Journal, Master, Master Key, and Drill Down files used for year-end adjustments.

General Ledger -> Periodic processing -> Create Last-Year Data

Running this function accomplishes two things.

It creates the next year in Resource Manager -> Company Setup -> Accounting Periods and It creates the Next Year’s GL files.

There are three of these the master GLMAx the Journal GLJRx and the keys GLMKx file.  The existing year will receive a file extension .Yxx.

When the process is run it will clear the income statement accounts and close them to the retained earnings account in the new year.

For the balance sheet accounts the ending balance of the current year will become the beginning balance of the new year.  A report will be generated with these entries.

Before running the process, the first thing to do is use F9 and switch to the prior GL year.

Go to Edit transactions and make sure all transactions have been posted to master.

You can only work in the current and the prior year.  Once you run Create Last-Year Data and you will no longer be able to work in this year.

So, if the current year is 2023 and you wish to move to 2024 you need to check 2022 and make sure the work has been completed.

Once you create Last-Year data for 2024 you will no longer be able to work in 2022.

If transactions do exist in the prior year they need to be posted to master and update current year needs to be run before proceeding.

When you enter create Last – Year Data will get the following message and click on OK to proceed.

Mark the check box (or enter Y) - Have You backed Up Your Current-Year Files?

Mark the check box (or enter Y) – Reset Current-Year Journal Entry Number to 1?

Customer will select the Retained Earning Account for Company.

Once the procedure is finished, turn to page down to generate a report that includes the closing entries for retained earnings for the upcoming year. The client is now free to continue with business as usual.

f2484995-7e97-49ec-a74d-e15e9b41de57.title: Instructions to file W-2 Forms with magnetic media.
f2484995-7e97-49ec-a74d-e15e9b41de57.content:
Problem
Instructions to file W-2 Forms with magnetic media.

Resolution
Mentioned below are the instruction for filing W-2 forms.

Change the Payroll Year to 2023 (or previous year) by clicking F9.

Go to Payroll or Payroll with Direct Deposit -> Periodic Processing -> W-2 Forms

Select a range of employee IDs or leave the range fields blank to include all employees.

Select a range of states to include or leave the range fields blank to include all states.

Mark the check box (or enter Y) to Process Magnetic Media.

Select an option for Form processing: W-2 Only, W-3 Only, or Both forms.


Mark the check box (or enter Y) to Print State Laser W-3s.

Select the W-2 form type to print.

Mark the check box (or enter Y) to Print COVID-Related Wage Statements.

Note: You will be prompted to mount paper and produce the corresponding statement for each employee that has non-zero balances in any COVID-related wage fields.

After completing this page enter PgDn (page down) will get 2023 Create Output File.

Enter Tax Year as 2023(or Previous year) and respective User ID, then PgDn.

You will get a verification popup and click on - Yes.

Need to enter Mandatory fields.
Note: All the fields that are checked are mandatory and need to be filled to proceed further.

After entering Mandatory fields Click on next page.

Select Generate Output File.

Select Prefix for the Output File for the W2REPORT.NEW and Include Records for State.
Mark the check box (or enter Y) to Print Audit and Preview it.

4ddb7bdb-ad27-428c-bd62-a6d425f6adaa.title: Creating a Magnetic Media Header for Submitting 1099s Electronically
4ddb7bdb-ad27-428c-bd62-a6d425f6adaa.content:
Problem
Illustrate the process on how to fill out the AP Magnetic Media Header for processing 1099s electronically..

Resolution
1. Go to AP 1099s Processing screen to process 1099s.
2. Make sure that you are running Traverse on the most current build to process 1099s.
3. On AP 1099s Processing screen. Click on Header function to enter Magnetic Media Header.

4. Once the Magnetic Media Header screen pops up. Payer, Transfer Agent and Transmitter information need to be filled where Transfer agent information is not mandatory.
5. Payer tab needs to be filled with the company information.

6. The information on the Payer Tab can be confirmed in SM Company Setup -> Company Information screen.
7. A name control is a sequence of characters derived from a taxpayer’s name that is used by IRS in processing the tax return filed by the taxpayer.  It is important that the combination of name control and taxpayer identification number (TIN) provided on an electronically filed return match IRS’s record of name controls and TINs.  A name control is established by the IRS when the taxpayer requests an Employer Identification Number (EIN).  The IRS creates the name control from the legal name listed on the Form SS-4, Application for Employer Identification Number.
9. Go to Transfer Agent tab where you would fill in information about the person paying on behalf of the company. This is typically a bank.  This information is all optional and not mandatory.
10. Go to Transmitter tab and fill the fields with appropriate valves.
11. 5 Digit Control code will be provided by IRS.
12. Contact email should be filled in with the processor's email address.

13. Go to Software vendor tab to enter the vendor details. Since Traverse is provided by Aptean fill up the Aptean details available from the company website.
14. Use the below link to find the Aptean head quarter address from the website.
https://www.aptean.com/en-US/locations
15.  The contact person field should be filled with the Account Manager's name and if the user don't have the Account's Manager phone number our Support Hotline number can also be used.

16. Close the Magnetic Media Header screen to save it.

7cce70a1-04ad-4b9e-9168-1daae7efeb4e.title: Unexpected error detected, line 1490, GENIRPT.PUB.
7cce70a1-04ad-4b9e-9168-1daae7efeb4e.content:
Problem
The customer is experiencing a pop-up or error message when attempting to print the 941 Worksheet.

Resolution
The customer was receiving an unexpected error found on line 1490 of GENIRPT.PUB when they attempted to print 941 Worksheets in Payroll or Payroll with Direct Deposit. To learn more, view the BBj error logs.

Payroll or Payroll with Direct Deposit -> Periodic Processing -> 941 Worksheet.

In most cases, when a customer receives this kind of popup, we advise them to change the Function type to Z - REPORT - PRE - JASPER report in Resource Manager.

Go to Resource Manager -> System Management -> Menus and open the menus.

To select, press F2, then choose Application Payroll or Payroll with Direct Deposit.

To select, press F2, then choose Menu as DD07 and Title as Periodic Processing and hit enter.

After selecting the 941 Worksheet, select Z - REPORT - PRE - JASPER as the Function type, hit Enter to change, and then click the page down button to continue.

Then click on Write it will ask Write changes? Click on Yes.

The customer won't receive that popup notice once again when they try to print the 941 worksheets after finishing the entire procedure.

cadbfbff-005c-401c-8fed-caa5ac72cf7a.title: Creating a Magnetic Media File for Submitting W-2s Electronically
cadbfbff-005c-401c-8fed-caa5ac72cf7a.content:
Problem
Illustrate the process on how to create a magnetic media file that is able to be submitted electronically to the IRS / SSA.

Resolution
- Set up the Magnetic Media Header
- Verify the Federal Tax ID. You can edit this value in the Tax Authorities function on the Codes Maintenance menu for the Federal tax authority.
- Select the payroll year for which you want to generate the W-2 information from the Year field.
- Select a range of available states by which to filter the employees in the Magnetic Media State Filter From and Thru fields, or leave the fields blank to include employees from all available states. The available states will be the states you have set up in the Tax Authorities function on the State tab.
- Accept or edit the path to which you want to output the magnetic media file in the Save to Folder field. Use the Browse button (…) to navigate to the location in which you want to save the magnetic media file.
- Select a range of employees to include in the magnetic media file in the Magnetic Media/W2 - Forms Employee Filter From and Thru fields, or leave the fields blank to include all employees.
- Filter the forms by control number by selecting a range of control numbers in the W2 - Forms Control Number Filter From and Thru fields, or leave the fields blank to include all control numbers in the magnetic media file.
- Click the Generate button to prepare W-2 information using the selected criteria. The Generate W-2s function must be run before you can create magnetic media.



-
-





- NOTE: Once the W-2 records have been generated, the Employee ID, Last Name, First Name, Address Line 1, City, Region, Postal Code, Country Code, State, and Social Security Number are for display only and may not be edited.
- Add, delete, or edit the employee records to include in the W-2 processing as necessary.
- Click the Header button.



-
-





- Use the Magnetic Media Header screen to edit the submitter and employer records for the W-2 magnetic media.
- The Output File Name and the Federal Tax ID and Payroll Year information are read-only.
-  On the Submitter Record tab
- The Submitter Record tab lists information about the Submitter/Employer.





-
-





- Edit the company name, and address information as necessary. The company entered on this tab will receive the next MMREF-1 publication; this company may not be the one for which you are creating the file.
- Mark the Foreign Address Indicator check box if the address is a foreign address; otherwise, clear the check box.
- Edit the User ID (supplied by the federal government) of the employee authorized to submit this file.
- Mark the Resub Flag check box if you are resubmitting the media; otherwise, clear the check box. If this box is marked, the Resub WFID field becomes available.
- If the Magnetic Media is being resubmitted, enter the Resub WFID number from the notice sent to you from the SSA (Social Security Administration).
- In the Software Code field choose either "IN-House Program" or "Off - the Shelf" software. Traverse is considered an "Off - the Shelf" software, thus you should choose it if you are submitting the magnetic media using Traverse.



-  On the Submitter Record(2) tab

- The Submitter Record(2) tab lists information on the organization submitting the W-2 Magnetic Media. (If your company uses a third party to submit your W-2’s, the name of the third party must be entered here.)





-
-





- Edit the company name, and address information as necessary. The company entered on this tab will receive any notification of data that cannot be processed by the SSA.
- Mark the Foreign Address Indicator check box if the address is a foreign address; otherwise, clear the check box.
- Enter the name of the person to be contacted by the SSA concerning processing problems in the Contact Name field.
- Enter the contact person’s Telephone Number and Extension. For the U.S. and U.S. territories, enter the submitter’s Fax number with area code as well.
- If applicable, enter the contact person's E-Mail address.
- Select a Preparer Code from the drop-down list to indicate who is preparing the W-2 Report file.
-  On the Employer Record tab
- The Employer Record tab is used to list information about the Employer for which employee wage and tax information is being filed.
-





- Select an Agent Indicator Code from the drop-down list: 2678 Agent, Common Paymaster, 3504 Agent, None.
- Enter the EIN of the Employer, for which you are an agent. The Agent EIN field is enabled when you select "2678 Agent", "Common Paymaster", or "3504 Agent" in the Agent Indicator Code field.
- Enter the Employer Name and address information as necessary.
- Mark the Third-Party Sick Pay check box if the employer provided sick pay for another entity; otherwise, clear the check box. When the check box is selected, the Third-Party Tax Withheld field becomes available.
- If applicable, enter the amount of the Third-Party Tax Withheld from sick pay payments.
- Mark the Terminating Business check box if you terminated your business during the filing tax year.
- Mark the Foreign Address Indicator check box if the address is a foreign address; otherwise, clear the check box.
- Enter the name of the person to be contacted concerning processing problems in the Employer Contact Name field.
- Enter the Employer Contact person’s Telephone Number and Extension. For the U.S. and U.S. territories, enter the employer’s Fax number with area code as well.
- If applicable, enter the Employer Contact person's E-Mail address.
- Select the appropriate Employment Code: Agriculture, Form 944 Filers, Household, Military, Medicare Qualified Government Employment, Railroad, or Regular (All Others).
- If applicable, select the appropriate Jurisdiction Code: Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa, Northern Mariana, or Puerto Rico.
- If the W-2 Report file contains multiple Code RE records with the same EIN, use the Establishment field to designate various store or factory locations, or types of payroll. Enter any combination of blanks, numbers or letters. Certain military employers must use this field.
- If the employer used an EIN different than the one entered earlier to submit a Form 941 or a Form 943 to the IRS for this year, or to submit W-2 data to the SSA for this year, enter that EIN in the Other EIN field. Otherwise, leave this field blank.
- Click the X to close the popup window and Yes to save the changes made.
- Once ready click the Output button and select Magnetic Media to output the file.
- Go to the file location that is indicated in the Select the path to output the magnetic media file box.



-
-





- Right Click the file and select Rename to change the file type.



-
-





- Type .txt after W2REPORT to change the file to the SSA approved format and click outside the Rename box to update the file format.



-
-





- Submit the file to SSA per the IRS instructions.
