67f747d2-2d1c-44a4-a516-557d07831399.content:
Problem
When the Client tries to print a Purchase order in the PO Transactions screen [Online Printing], the 'Print' option is greyed out in the PO Print Order screen.

Resolution
In this case, we need to ensure 2 things here:

1. Go to System Manager -> Company Setup -> Business Rules: Under Application -> PO-Purchase Order: Under Miscellaneous section, set 'Allow Online Purchase Orders' field to 'Yes'.

2. As this Print function is Role configurable, we would need to ensure if the same permissions were given to the User's group as well. [Check for the User's group information under System Manager -> Administration -> Users and observe the Groups, the User is in]
Now, go to System Manager -> Company Setup -> Business Rules: Under Role, choose the appropriate Group of the User [Example: admin] and in the Miscellaneous section, set 'Allow Online Purchase Orders' field to 'Yes' and click on 'Apply' and 'OK'

3. Once these permissions were ensured in the Business rules, the user would be able to print the Purchase Orders as preferred.

Problem
Cloud-Hosted clients would like to subscribe to the StatusHub notifications for the Traverse Product to get updates about Traverse

The below steps describe how to add a hosted client user to subscribe Status Hub notifications.

- Go to Aptean Cloud Services. or enter the URL as https://status.apteancloud.com

On the Status Hub dashboard, click SUBSCRIBE (at the top).


- On the Subscriptions page, select Email as the subscription method.



- On the Email page, enter the required email ID to subscribe for email updates.
- Select the I accept terms & services check box and click Next.



-
- On the Customizations page, select Notify about:  Selected services.
- In the Filter Services search box, enter Traverse.


- Scroll to the bottom and click on page 2.

- Check the box that corresponds with Service Name Aptean Industrial Manufacturing ERP, Traverse Edition (US-EAST).

7595356f-6ffe-46f0-aa9f-57e7d02ffecc.content:
Problem
Debit Memos (both a prepayment and a regular debit memo) not due until after a particular date are also picked up in the Payment run when payments are prepared in the AP Prepare Payments screen (Accounts Payable->Pay Invoices->Prepare Payments)

Example:
The below debit memos (both a prepayment and a regular debit memo) have an invoice date of 11/26/2023.
The invoice due date on the Prepare Payments screen was entered as 10/26/2023.

10b89073-2c11-43ea-aa39-4f7f821bd59e.title: How to change the vendor's payment type from checks to EFTs
10b89073-2c11-43ea-aa39-4f7f821bd59e.content:
Problem
How to change the vendor's payment type from checks to EFTs

Resolution
To change the vendor's payment type from checks to EFTs, follow the below steps:

- Open AP Vendors (Applications>>Account Payable>>Setup and Maintenance>>Vendors)
- Select the vendor ID whose payment type you want to change
- Go to the Pay-To tab.
- In the Check Delivery field, change the type to Electronic.
- Enter the Account No of the vendor’s bank account you will be sending the ACH file to.
- Enter the 9-digit Routing No for the routing code for the Vendor’s bank that will be receiving the ACH file for invoice payment.
- Select the Account Type the electronic payment will be coming out of. The selections are Savings and Checkings for EFTs, and None if the Delivery method is Paper.
-Click on Save.

- Now, whenever payments for this vendor are prepared, checks won't get printed.
- Delivery type of Electronic will output your payments to an ACH file using the Create ACH File function (Accounts Payable->Pay Invoices->Create ACH File) for the EFT payments.
- You can print vouchers on the Payment Vouchers screen (Accounts Payable->Pay Invoices->Payment Vouchers) and create an ACH file in the Create ACH File screen (Accounts Payable->Pay Invoices->Create ACH File) for the EFT payments.

256e8f08-a3dc-4b0f-ac82-8780565011df.title: A report to fetch the remaining leave balances for all employees
256e8f08-a3dc-4b0f-ac82-8780565011df.content:
Problem
Client needs a report to fetch the remaining leave balances for all employees

Cause
-

Resolution
There are two reports for looking at the leave balances.

1. Leave Detail Report (Payroll->Personnel Reports-> Detail Leave Report)
Use the Detail Leave Report function to produce an audit trail of your employees' leave time accruals and the amounts of leave they have used within the dates you specify.



- Use the Data Filter to select the range of filtering options or leave the filter blank to include all available data.
- Select the sort criteria for the report from the Sort By section.
- Select a Date range for the report in the From and Thru fields or leave the fields blank to include all dates.
- Select a Leave Code ID range, or leave the From and Thru fields blank to include all leave codes.
- Select the Include Terminated Employees check box, if applicable, to include employees no longer with the company in the report.

2. Leave Report (Payroll->Quarterly/Year-End Reports->Leave Report)

The Leave Report function shows the amounts of leave time used and the pay received during the month or quarter you specify, as well as year-to-date totals and remaining leave amounts for each employee.

- Use the Data Filter to select the range of filtering options or leave the filter blank to include all available data.
- Select the timeframe for which to generate the report from the View For section. Select a Month to view as applicable.

(Note: Both of these reports can be used to query leave balances. One is more detailed and uses date ranges. The other is more summarized and does it by the period)

2c0d80ce-511b-4349-bee2-9262613eff79.title: “There are Unprinted Checks on file for method of Payment CHK.”

3bb1d0fd-944f-4f70-b6be-14a14f82f8df.title: How to create a Landed Cost
3bb1d0fd-944f-4f70-b6be-14a14f82f8df.content:
Problem
How to create a Landed cost

Resolution
Two things have to be taken care of before creating a Landed Cost: From the System Manager menu, select Company Setup. Select Business Rules.

- From the Application Menu, choose Purchase Order. In the Use Accrual During Posting option, choose Yes.
- Choose Yes for the Enable Landed Cost Calculations option. If you would like to allow users to edit landed cost values during transaction entry, choose Yes for the Allow Editing of Landed Costs option.

Next, go to Purchase Order --> Setup and Maintenance --> Landed Cost
For Creating a Landed cost use the following steps:

- Click the New button on the toolbar to open a blank landed cost record.
- Enter a landed cost ID in the Landed Cost ID field.
- Enter a description of the new landed cost in the Description field. This will be the name by which you can identify the parameter set.
- In the detail area, enter the description for the landed cost line in the Description field.
- In the Cost Type field, choose whether you want to apply the landed cost by Percent of Cost, Fixed Amount, Weight, or Quantity.
- Depending on the cost type you chose, enter the amount, percentage, or weight per base unit in the Amount field. If the cost type is 'Percent of Cost', the amount is a percentage of the item cost. If the cost type is 'Fixed Amount', 'Weight', or 'Quantity', the amount is a dollar amount per the cost type.
- Select a level to specify a basis for the calculation from the Level field. Select:

1 - To calculate using the extended cost as a base.
2 - To calculate using the extended cost, plus the level one calculation values.
3 - To calculate using extended cost, plus the level one, plus the level two, calculation values as the base.
4 - To calculate using the extended cost, plus the level one, plus the level two, plus the level three calculation values as the base.
5  - To calculate using the extended cost, plus the level one, plus the level two, plus the level three, plus the level four calculation values as the base.

Next, enter or select the account number in the GL Expense Account field. The landed cost expense gets offset by the invoice from the freight company, using this account as the expense account in the freight invoice.

Landed cost in the PO is an estimate. Actual freight invoices may be different. You will need to reconcile your landed cost expense account for amounts that are different between the estimated cost calculated in the transaction and the actual amount from your freight invoice.

Click the Save button on the toolbar to save the new landed cost.

99201a4c-0607-42b6-8daf-b9d3e48c050c.title: How to enable TLS 1.2 on Windows 10
99201a4c-0607-42b6-8daf-b9d3e48c050c.content:
Problem
How to enable TLS 1.2 on Windows 10

Resolution
Follow the below steps to enable TLS 1.2

- In the windows menu search box, type internet options.
- Under Best match, click Internet Options.

3. In the Internet properties window, on the Advanced tab, scroll down to the security section.
4. Check the Use TLS 1.2 checkbox.

de26b0e1-9156-408d-b1cc-144b0431cdd2.title: How to create and record recurring journal entries instead of having to manually enter it every time
de26b0e1-9156-408d-b1cc-144b0431cdd2.content:
Problem
How to create and write recurring journal entries (Journal entries made regularly -- every week, every month, and so on) instead of having to enter it every time in the GL Transactions screen manually.

Resolution
Go to the GL Recurring Entries screen (GL->Setup and Maintenance->Recurring Entries) Add the details as shown below and click on Save.


- Click the New button, on the toolbar, to open a blank recurring entry record.
- Enter a recurring entry ID in the Recur ID field.
Note: To copy recurring entry information from a similar record for a new recurring entry, select the existing recurring entry from the Copy From field.
- Enter a description of the new recurring entry in the Description field.
- Determine if you want the system to automatically verify whether an allocation exists for the account by toggling the Allocate On/Off button.

SelectToOnSet the system to determine whether an allocation exists for the account and to automatically select the Alloc check box.OffNot perform the automatic check. You need to manually select the Alloc check box for allocated accounts.



- Enter a line number in the Line field. If you do not enter a line number, the system automatically enters line numbers 10, 20, 30, etc. Also, to enter a record between existing records, enter a line number that falls between the existing records. The records re-sequence according to the 10, 20, 30 numbering scheme when you exit and re-enter the screen.
- Select an account from the Account ID field. The account description appears in the Description field and can be edited if necessary.
- Enter a debit or a credit amount in the Debit or Credit fields.
-
The Alloc box is checked if the account is allocated.


- Select the source code from the Source field.

SelectForRENormal recurring entriesR1Automatic reversal in the next period
10. Enter a reference description in the Reference field, as applicable.

- The Total Debits and Total Credits for the recurring entry are displayed. The total debits must equal the total credits when you exit from the screen.
- The outstanding Debit Balance and outstanding Credit Balance is displayed. The Debit Balance and the Credit Balance must equal zero when you exit from the screen.
- Click the Save button, on the toolbar, to save the new recurring entry.
Note: You can click the Totals button, on the toolbar to view the Totals Form, which displays a view-only look at the totals for the selected recurring entry ID. This form also shows a Net Base that provides the functional currency value of all the individual currency subtotals.

Once the Recurring Entry is set up, go to the GL Copy Recurring Entries screen (General Ledger->Transactions->Copy Recurring Entries).

Now,

- Select the range of recurring entries you want to copy from the Recur ID From and Thru fields. Leave these fields blank to copy all existing recurring entries.
- Select a date to use for the transaction date on the new transactions from the Copy Date field.
- Enter the fiscal period to use in the Fiscal Period field.
- If applicable, select a batch code in the Batch Code drop-down list.
- Enter, if applicable, any comments to associate with the recurring entries you want to copy in the Comments field.





(Note: The destination of these transactions generated from this screen will depend on the selection made for the Copy Recurring Entries Directly to the GL Journal business rule. 'Yes' will skip the Transactions function and go directly to the GL journal. 'No' will write the transactions from the Recurring Entries to the Transactions function)



If the above business rule is set to No, these transactions will now appear in the GL Transactions screen.

bffbf0e1-5d82-4a64-a54b-1e323c4b19f5.title: How to change the Date Format of the Check Date in Traverse Global Design Studio

Resolution

b0a7a089-510c-43c1-a135-e7cdf2a42f76.title: Reset Factory Default Installation Theme in Traverse Version 11.0
b0a7a089-510c-43c1-a135-e7cdf2a42f76.content:
Problem
The Traverse end-user has changed the theme in Traverse 11.0 and then tried to change back to the default theme, however, the default theme is not the same as the 'default' theme when Traverse 11.0 is installed, which is the desired theme for the end-user.

Resolution
- Close TRAVERSE on the end user's workstation.
- Rename the "TRAVERSE" folder in the C:\Users\username\AppData\Roaming\Open Systems, Inc\ file path.
- Upon relaunching TRAVERSE the theme will be reverted back to the default installation theme.

Note: In the path C:\Users\username, you may need to type in \AppData in the URL after the username and hit ENTER to get the next folder to appear, or you may need to select show "Hidden items" in the File Explore - View settings.

acd842af-1a15-451a-98cb-392ef95f54a2.title: Vouchers are not created after calculating checks although Direct Deposits are set up
acd842af-1a15-451a-98cb-392ef95f54a2.content:
Problem
I am trying to print out the vouchers and it says there is nothing to process, but I have employees set up with Direct Deposit.

Cause
The "Calculate Direct Deposit" check box was not set up.

Resolution
You may not have checked the "Calculate Direct Deposit" checkbox when Calculating Checks. Accordingly, follow these steps to fix this:
-Click the "Reset" button to redo the check batch:
(- If the checks are printed, you may need to change a business rule to allow this:
-Go to System Manager -> Company Setup -> Business Rules and access the business rules for Payroll
- Turn the rule "Editing after printing checks" to "yes". Save.
-After this, go back to the Calculate Checks screen and press the Reset button on the top.)

You may need to exit out of the screen and reenter it in order to reset.  (The screen should return to defaults and blank out filled out fields, and the check batch is essentially erased)
-From there, click the "Calculate Direct Deposit" checkbox, and calculate a new batch of checks.

The Calculate Checks log should now show vouchers in your list if your direct deposits are set up properly, and you should not be able to print or output your vouchers.

*If you printed checks, you will need to reprint the new set of checks or output them to PDF, ensuring to put in the correct "Starting" and "Last Good" numbers to ensure that the check numbers match. The check numbers that are given with this print will be the check numbers that are posted in Traverse.

56051eb8-3922-4fea-9224-99593b4b0386.title: Installing Aptean Cloud Printing Agent on a workstation
56051eb8-3922-4fea-9224-99593b4b0386.content:
Problem
Installing Aptean Cloud Printing Service

Resolution
Perform the following procedure to download, install ApteanPrintAgentSetup.exe, and configure the Cloud Printing Agent:
1. Download the latest Cloud Printing Agent as follows:
a. Open https://print.api.apteancloud.com in a browser. Each SaaS customer must have an account registered at the cloud printing service with an Account ID, APIKey, and an Agent Key. (Each SaaS customer must have an account registered at the cloud printing service with an Account ID, APIKey, and an Agent Key. If the customer does not have it, our cloud team can provide it for them upon request)

b. Use the newly created AccountId and APIKey to get access. Enter the Account ID as the username and API Key as the password.
c. Click the Print Agent Windows Installer link to download the ApteanPrintAgentSetup.exe file.

2. Double-click ApteanPrintAgentSetup.exe. When the welcome page opens, click Next.

3. In the Select Destination Location page, select the default folder or a folder in a location of your choice to install the Aptean Print Agent, and then click Next.

4. Enter the Account ID and Agent Key provided when signing up for the Aptean Cloud Printing service and then select Production
.

5. On the Ready to Install page, click the Install button.

6. Wait until the installation is completed.

Perform the following procedure to enable cloud printing in Traverse Global. To change the cloud print settings for all users, Go to System Manager > Company Setup > SM User Defaults - Admin. To change the cloud print settings for current user, Go to System Manager > Company Setup > SM User Defaults. The User Defaults - Admin and User Defaults screen allows you to enable Aptean Cloud Printing service.

1. Select 'User' in the Type drop-down list.
2. Select a User ID for which you want to set defaults.
3. You have the option to copy defaults from another user via the Copy From drop-down list.
4. Select the SM - System Manager application in the left-hand panel.

7. Select "Yes" to enable cloud printing in the Enable Cloud Print field.
8. Select the printing mode as Production in the Printing Mode field.
9. Enter your workstation name in the Workstation Name field.
10. Save your settings. Please log out from the Traverse application and log back in to see the changes. The print sync could take up to 10 minutes to complete. Then cloud printers are available for your selection on the Form Printers function.

76e0f631-80f1-4456-b018-a0c16b04c5b2.title: How to change the Statement Date in Bank Reconciliation
76e0f631-80f1-4456-b018-a0c16b04c5b2.content:
Problem
How to change the "Statement Date" in the BR Cleared Transactions screen.

Resolution
The Statement Date cannot be directly changed on the BR Cleared Transactions screen under the 'Statement' Tab. When we attempt to change that, the Beginning Date and the Ending Date would get reset, allowing us to enter a new date for a new Statement.

So, we need to uncheck the Cleared Checkbox of all the Cleared entries under Deposits, Disbursements, Adjustments, and Transfers; then Reconcile the existing (Incorrect) Statement; and then Purge that Statement and create a new one with the correct Statement Date as preferred.

Steps:
1. Go to Bank Reconciliation -> Reconciliation -> Cleared Transactions: Pull up the required Bank Account ID and the Statement Date. [Kindly make note of the Beginning Date, Ending Date, Beginning Balance, and Ending Balance.]

2. Go to the Deposits, Disbursements, Adjustments, and Transfers Tab each and uncheck the 'Cleared' checkbox for all the entries that were cleared in this Statement. [Note: This can be done by getting into each Tab and clicking on 'Unselect All' icon on the Toolbar on the top]

3. Ensure no entries are cleared on this Statement under all the Tabs: Deposits, Disbursements, Adjustments, and Transfers:

4. Now, get back to the Statements Tab and click on the 'Change Status' Icon on the Toolbar to Reconcile the current Statement. Click 'Yes' on the prompt and we can observe the Statement status that got changed from 'Open' to 'Reconciled'

5. Once the Statement is reconciled, go to Bank Reconciliation -> Reconciliation -> Reconciliation Report. Enter the Bank Account ID and the Reconciled Statement Date [29/11/2023 in this case]. Then Print the Reconciliation Report. We can observe from the Report that no entries are Cleared in this Statement.

6. Once the Statement is Cleared, go to Bank Reconciliation -> Reconciliation -> Purge Cleared Transactions: Apply the Data filters such that we are Purging only the current Statement. [Enter the Data Filter for both the Bank Account ID and the Statement Date]. Then, click on the Checkbox below. Now click on OK to Purge the Reconciled Statement. Once it is done, we can also notice that the Reconciled statement is no longer available in the BR Cleared Transactions screen.

7. Now, Go to Bank Reconciliation -> Reconciliation -> Cleared Transactions: Pull up the required Bank Account ID and enter the Statement Date as preferred. Also enter the Beginning Date, Ending Date, Beginning Balance, and Ending Balance [As noted from the previous Statement with the incorrect date]

8. Clear the required entries that are to be cleared in this Statement under all the Tabs by checking on the corresponding 'Checkboxes': Deposits, Disbursements, Adjustments, and Transfers. Then, click on OK to Clear them.

9. Thus, we have obtained the Statement with the correct 'Statement Date' as preferred.

163ad79d-b793-4632-95de-a982ba2a160c.title: Getting the pop-up "Vendor on Hold" while creating new AP Transaction
163ad79d-b793-4632-95de-a982ba2a160c.content:
Problem
While creating the AP Transactions, the User is getting notified of the following error: "Vendor is on hold. Do you wish to proceed with this vendor?"

Resolution
This error implies that the vendor is on "Hold." When we try to enter a new invoice or pay a vendor that is on hold, the system warns us that the vendor is on hold, but allows us to override it.

In order to remove a Vendor from 'Hold', we would need to follow the below steps:
1. Go into the AP Vendors screen through the Path: Accounts Payable -> Setup and Maintenance -> AP Vendors.

2. Navigate to the Defaults Tab: Uncheck the Vendor Hold Checkbox, and click on Save.

3. With this, we would no longer get the warning pop-up indicating the Vendor is On hold.

7c88b7c9-e2bf-4211-aec4-6eca066f12fb.title: Create a new AR Sales Rep
7c88b7c9-e2bf-4211-aec4-6eca066f12fb.content:
Problem
Customer wish to know how to Create a New Sales Rep under Accounts Receivable

Resolution
Applications> AR > Setup and Maintenance > Sales Reps

- Click the New button, on the toolbar, to open a blank sales rep record.
- Enter a new sales rep ID in the Sales Rep field.
- Enter the sales rep's name in the Name field.
- Enter the sales rep's address in the Address, City, Region, Country, and Postal Code fields.
Note: Use the System Manager Country Codes function to set up postal code masks, international prefixes, and international prefix masks.
- Enter the sales rep's contact information in the Phone, Fax, and Email fields.
Note: Use the System Manager Country Codes function to set up phone and fax masks.
- Enter the sales rep's website address in the Internet field.
- Select the applicable invoice type to use to pay the sales rep commissions by placing a check mark in the Line Items, Sales Tax, Freight, or Misc fields.
- Select a run code to assign to the sales rep from the Run Code field. The run code is used to prepare commissions and set sort ranges in the Commission Edit Register and Commission Detail List.
- Enter the sales rep's commission rate in the Commission % field.
Note: Each sales rep can receive as much as 99.99% of a sale.
Note: You can also click on the ... button to open the Sales Rep's detail screen.
- Select Category, Product Line, or Item ID from the Type field.
Note: These selections only appear if you have Accounts Receivable interfaced to Inventory in the Business Rules function.
- Select the corresponding reference for which you want to apply a specific commission percentage from the Reference field.
- Enter the percentage of commission you want to apply to the type and reference in the Commission % field.
- Click the End Edit button () to save any changes.


- Select the base for the commission rate from the Percent Of field.
- Select the basis for commission from the Based On field.
- The Booked Sales method pays commission on posted invoices.
- The Paid Invoices method pays commission on fully-paid invoices.


- Select the payment method for the sales rep from the Pay Via field.
- Mark the check box(es) for the portion(s) of the invoice on which to pay commissions: Line Items, Sales Tax, Freight, and/or Miscellaneous.
- Update, if necessary, the sales rep's year-to-date and period-to-date sales history in the YTD Sales and PTD Sales fields respectively.
Note: These fields update when you post transactions. The information for the Commissions Detail List comes from commissions history. If you change these fields, the history information is not updated.
- Update, if necessary, the sales rep's last sale in the Last Sales Date field.
Note: This field updates when you post transactions. The information for the Commissions Detail List comes from commissions history. If you change this field, the history information is not updated.
- Click the Save button, on the toolbar, to save the new sales rep.

93ae7ae5-23f6-4766-95e7-5452dd5fdb3e.title: Set up a printer to print payroll checks
93ae7ae5-23f6-4766-95e7-5452dd5fdb3e.content:
Problem
Client wants to set up a printer to print payroll checks from their workstation

Resolution
Application> System Manager> Company Setup> Form Printer> Selected PA Checks and the desire printer> Save

Setting up a Form Printer for a form can be done by following the below steps:

- Click the New button, on the toolbar, to open a blank form printer record.
- Select a form from the Forms field drop-down list. (In this case PA Checks)
- Enter the text to print on the invoice or picking slip in the Copy Text field. (only if applicable)
- Enter the order in which to print the copy in the Order field. To print multiple copies of the same form, add multiple rows of the same form with the order number different for each copy. The numbers must be sequential and unique for each copy. For example Customer Copy 1, Office Copy 2 etc... they however can be to the same printer. If the numbers are not sequential the multiple copies of the form will not print.(If you leave each copy default to 1)
- Select the printer for which to print the invoice or picking slip from the Printer field. You can select a different printer for each copy. The printers available are the printers set up in Windows on the workstation.
- Select the tray for the selected printer from which you want the form to print in the Tray field. This selection only applies if the printer has multiple trays.
- Select the Active check box to print the copy; otherwise, clear the check box.
- Close the screen to save the new form.

1f93a2a7-fab6-4ad5-a0e0-b3c3a62fb83f.title: Getting the message while logging into Traverse: "Subscription has expired. You are using the Evaluation version of the software."
1f93a2a7-fab6-4ad5-a0e0-b3c3a62fb83f.content:
Problem
When the Users log into Traverse, all of them are getting the pop-up with the following message:
"Subscription has expired. You are using the Evaluation version of the software."

The error message indicates that the License key needs to be renewed and re-applied at the Traverse License Server Manager for 11.0 or Traverse Global License Server Manager for 11.2.

2. Once the key is provided, the updated license key needs to be re-applied in the Traverse License Server Manager (for 11.0) or Traverse Global License Server Manager (for 11.2) by entering the updated key in the Product ID screen and the Site ID in the dialog box which opens up after clicking on Activate Product as seen below:

4. Now, after restarting the Traverse License Server Manager (for 11.0 ) or Traverse Global License Server Manager (for 11.2) by clicking on Restart Service, the users will no longer get the error message.

246ff898-42bc-4b6a-a174-08e6d690b863.title: Deleting a Vendor in Accounts Payable
246ff898-42bc-4b6a-a174-08e6d690b863.content:
Problem
Need to delete a Vendor in Accounts Payable.

Resolution
1. When the Vendor has historical Transactions tied to it, Traverse doesn't allow us to delete the Invoices and shows the following error message: "Current record cannot be deleted"

- But we can make the Vendor as 'Inactive', in order to avoid the Non-active vendors from being used in a new transaction. When we try to involve the Inactive Vendors into Transactions, "The Selected Vendor is Inactive" pops-up to warn the User.

2. If there are no historical Transactions tied to a Vendor, Traverse allows us to delete the Vendor through the following Steps:

- Go to Applications -> Accounts Payable -> Interactive Views -> Open Invoice View: Ensure there are no Open Invoices for that Vendor.

- Go to Applications -> Accounts Payable -> Setup & Maintenance -> Vendors: Select the Vendor, we wish to delete from the Vendor ID field.

- Click the Delete button, on the toolbar, to delete the selected vendor's record.


- Click Yes at the "Are you sure you want to delete selected record(s)?" prompt.

84bb17a4-e77f-4776-b756-2d4c93a7f02a.title: Set up Multiple Emails in Document Delivery
84bb17a4-e77f-4776-b756-2d4c93a7f02a.content:
Problem
How to email a document to multiple emails using Document Delivery.

Cause
Need to send documents to different emails or to multiple emails.

Resolution
You can set up emails in the Document Delivery section of either the Customer Setup in Accounts Receivable --> Setup and Maintenance, in the Vendor Setup in Accounts Payable --> Setup and Maintenance or the Employee Information screen in Payroll->Setup and Maintenance

You can select various form options from the drop-down in the first column of the setup to allow you to add different emailing options for different forms. You can select one form multiple times in the list to send the form via separate emails to differing recipients. The recipients will see only the email that was sent to them.


Alternatively, if you want to send a form to more than one email per form, you can add an email to the email list in the Deliver To column. Separate each email with a semicolon and space. The recipients will see all listed emails.

Additionally, there is another option if you need to make a quick edit on a one-time basis. If your document is not set to "Auto Send" in the SM Document Settings setup (System Manager -> Document Delivery -> Document Settings), then you can also edit the email list when the email is in the queue to edit a single email. After you click to print the form, the "Document Queue" box will pop up. Then, you can click into the "Edit" button to edit who the email will deliver to before you confirm to send it. See the screenshots below. This will only edit this printing instance, and the delivery settings will revert back to the Document Delivery settings with the next email.

Problem
Client had issues with printing reports and journals. When the client tries to print reports from Traverse on a new workstation the reports were not printed to full size.

- First thing to check is that the Printer Driver for the specified Printer is up-to-date.

- Expand Print queues

- Override the High DPI(dots per inch) Scaling Behavior.

- Go to the TRAVERSE client directory
- Right-click the TRAVERSE.exe, and select Properties
- Select the Compatibility tab
- Click ‘Change high DPI settings’
- Check the box to ‘Override high DPI scaling behavior’
- Select ‘Application’ listed in the lookup, and click OK



7. Print the report again to confirm if the issue is resolved

07f5500b-40f1-4f99-9a3b-d07dd7e7a441.title: Object Reference Error for Document Delivery in Build 23198
07f5500b-40f1-4f99-9a3b-d07dd7e7a441.content:
Problem
When the Customer tries to send Documents electronically through Traverse, they are getting the following error: "Object Reference not set to an instance of an Object"

Resolution
This "Object Reference not set to an instance of an Object" error indicates that Traverse is looking for a printer setup, which is not there. So we need to set that up to resolve this.

1. Go to System Manager -> Company Setup -> Business Rules: Under System Manager, ensure that a setting has been selected for the New Business Rule "Form Printer Setup Mode." For example, "By Workstation" [It can be set as 'By User ID' or 'By both' as preferred by the Client].

2. Then go to System Manager -> Company Setup -> SM Form Printers: Ensure a printer has been setup for Document Delivery. If nothing was there, set up the printer and Save. This helps in resolving the issue.

8873dbe9-5ccd-44b6-83e3-4bcff26db6f9.title: Creating a manual Payroll Check
8873dbe9-5ccd-44b6-83e3-4bcff26db6f9.content:
Problem
Need to create a manual check for an employee

Resolution
- Click the New button () to open a blank manual check record, if necessary.
- Select an Employee ID for whom you want to enter or edit a manual check. The employee's name and salary or hourly rate appear, and the employee's gross and net pay and total deductions, withholdings, employer costs, and employer taxes are listed in the fields at the bottom of the screen. These values are updated as you make changes.
- If available, mark the Calculate Direct Deposit check box to calculate the check for the selected employee as direct deposit.
- Select a pay code to use to calculate deductions and employer costs when the manual check is calculated in the Pay Code field.
- Either re-enter a check number previously issued to an employee or, if you are entering a new check, leave the Check Number field blank to automatically assign a check number.
- Select a date for the check in the Check Date field.
- Enter or edit the number of weeks the employee worked in the Weeks Worked field.

On the Earnings tab:

- In the WH State column, edit the withholding state for the manual check, if necessary.
- Edit, if necessary the Tax Group ID for the manual check. You may select a Tax Group OR a Local Tax Authority, but NOT both.
- Edit, if necessary the Local tax authority for the manual check. You may select a Tax Group OR a Local Tax Authority, but NOT both.
- Edit, if necessary, the withholding SUI State you set up for the employee in the Employee Information screen.
- Edit, if necessary, the Department for the manual check.
- Edit, if necessary, the Earning Code to assign to the manual check.
- Use this field to select a Leave Code to associate with the number of hours entered in the Hours field. Leave this field blank if the employee is working and not using any leave hours.
- Edit, if necessary, the Labor Class for the manual check.
- Enter or edit the number of Hours for the selected Earn Code or Leave Code. If the employee is hourly, the Rate and Amount fields calculate automatically.
- If necessary, edit the employee's hourly Rate. This rate is calculated for hourly employees using the employee's default hourly rate, Add To Base, and Multiplier amounts assigned to the Earning Code.
- Edit, if necessary, the Amount for the check. If the employee is hourly, this amount is automatically calculated by the system, multiplying the number of hours worked by the hourly rate.
Note: If you adjust this amount, the employee's hourly rate is automatically recalculated.
- Edit, if necessary, the number of Pieces for which the employee is being paid.
Note: Pieces are used for management information and are not posted to Project Costing if you interface that application with Payroll.
- Edit, if necessary, the Customer ID to which you want to apply the employee's manual check; otherwise, leave the field blank.
- If necessary, if you want to apply the employee's manual check to a task, select a Task Code.
- If necessary, if you want to apply the employee's manual check to a project, select a Project ID.
- If necessary, if you want to apply the employee's manual check to a phase, select a Phase Code.


In the read-only Total section at the bottom of the screen:

- The Gross Pay field displays the total gross pay amount from the Earnings tab.
- The Deductions field displays the total deductions amount from the Deductions tab.
- The Withholdings field displays the total withholdings amount from the Withholdings tab.
- The Employer Costs field displays the total employer costs amount from the Employer Costs tab.
- The Employer Taxes field displays the total employer tax amount from the Employer Taxes tab.

Deductions tab

- If applicable, select the deduction Code to apply to the manual check. The read-only Description field displays the description of the deduction code.
- Enter the number of Hours on which to base the deduction.
- Edit, if necessary, the deductions Amount for the check.
- The view-only Gross Or Net field displays the type of earnings (Gross Pay or Net Pay) on which the deduction is based upon.
Note: Use the Deduction/Employer Costs function to set up the type of earnings used in deductions.

Withholdings tab

- Use the Tax Authority field to select the type of withholding to apply to the manual check, if applicable.
- Select the tax Code to apply to the manual check, as applicable. The read-only Description field displays the description of the tax code.
- Enter the withholding Amount, as applicable.

Employer Costs tab

- If applicable, select the tax Code to apply to the manual check. The read-only Description field displays the description of the tax code.
- Enter the number of Hours associated with the employer cost.
- Enter, if necessary, the withholding Amount for the check.
- The view-only Gross Or Net field displays the type of earnings (Gross Pay or Net Pay) on which the employer cost is based upon.
Note: Use the Deduction/Employer Costs function to set up the type of earnings used in employer costs.

Employer Taxes tab

- Use the Tax Authority field to select the type of employer tax to apply to the manual check, if applicable.
- Select the tax Code to apply to the manual check, as applicable. The read-only Description field displays the description of the tax code.
- Enter the Amount of tax paid by the employer, as applicable.

Use the Save button on the toolbar to save your changes.

012941f5-fb3a-4a9c-a1aa-dc784f228894.title: Applying filters in the interactive views in Traverse
012941f5-fb3a-4a9c-a1aa-dc784f228894.content:
Problem
Need to apply filters on various interactive views: Example: PO Order View, to fetch the necessary data, as required.

Resolution
Filters can be applied in either of the 2 ways:

1. Click on the red text component: And field (by default). If needed, we can make use of And/ Or/ Not And/ Not Or or even more conditions depending on the need.

- Pull the necessary Header field based on which the filtering needs to be done (The blue text component)
- Enter the Criterion by clicking on Green Text Component.

- Enter a string of text or numbers or pull from the drop-down to complete the condition (if applicable) by clicking on the Gray text component.
- Click on Apply filter

7f1bbf5c-2b4e-42be-8c3e-23a8918e42ea.title: BOM Item ID Setup in Bill of Material
7f1bbf5c-2b4e-42be-8c3e-23a8918e42ea.content:
Problem
How to create a new BOM Item ID in Bill of Material<Setup and Maintenance<Bill of Material?

Resolution
Creating a Bill of Material

From the Bill of Material<Setup and Maintenance<Bill of Material screen.

- Click the New button, on the toolbar, to open a new bill of the material record. The Add Item Locations screen will appear.



- Select an inventory item from the Add Item ID field. This is the parent item for the bill of material.
- Select a location from the Add Location ID field.
- To copy item information from a similar record for a new item location, select the existing item record from the Copy From Item field. To copy location information from a similar record for a new item location, select the existing location record from the Copy From Location field.
- Determine whether to include Component Information, Assembly Instructions, or User Defined Fields (if available) by marking the corresponding check boxes; otherwise, clear the checkboxes.
- Click OK.
Note: Use the Inventory Items and Item Locations functions, if applicable, to edit the item's location or description information, or to categorize the item as kitted, lotted, or serialized.


- Accept or edit the Description for the bill of a material item.
- Accept or edit the Unit of measure for the item.
- Enter the cost of labor in the Labor Cost field.
Note: The Total Cost and Component Cost fields automatically recalculate as you enter items. If a checkmark appears in the Kitted check box, you cannot edit this field because kitted items do not have associated labor costs because assembly occurs at the point of sale.
- Use the Add or Delete buttons to add or remove locations for the bill of the material parent item.
Note: If you delete a location from a bill of material, it does not delete the location from the item record in Inventory.
- Click the Components tab.
- Select a component item to add from the Item ID field.
Note: The item's location, unit, unit cost, and extended cost appear. If applicable, use the Inventory Items function to edit this information.
- Enter the quantity used in the Quantity field.
Note: The Total Cost and Component Cost fields automatically recalculate when you edit this field.
- Click the Instructions button, if applicable, to add assembly instructions to the bill of material. Click Close to save the instructions and return to the Bill of Material screen.
- Repeat Steps 7-9 until you have added all components to the bill of material.
Note: When items are selected, the Type will display as Item. When an item that is already set up as a bill of material is selected, the Type will update as Subassembly.
- Click the Save button, on the toolbar, to save the new bill of the material record.

1c8fd2b0-bd66-4c2f-88d7-41eae54ab5c6.title: Traverse Global SaaS – temporarily turning off Aptean Cloud Printing for a user
1c8fd2b0-bd66-4c2f-88d7-41eae54ab5c6.content:
Problem
How to temporarily turn off/bypass Aptean Print Service/Aptean Cloud Printing in Traverse Global.

Resolution
These temporary steps can be used in the case of a significant duration outage/disruption to the Aptean Print Service that prevents printing from Traverse Global, or in the case of an issue with a local Aptean Print Agent install is resolved. Each user that needs to print would need to follow these steps:

1. Go into User Defaults (System Manager, Company Setup, User Defaults), and select: SM-System Manager defaults.
2. Change “Enable Cloud Print” from Yes to No

3. Exit Traverse completely and log back in
- Advanced Tip: Traverse administrator can instead change this for other users via

User Defaults-Admin (System Manager, Company Setup, User Defaults - Admin). But the user still needs to exit Traverse and log back in.

4. Something to take into consideration is if when using Aptean Print Service and the users were printing certain Traverse documents to "Form Printers" (such as invoices, PO, packing slip) those From Printers will need to be set back up in System Manager, Company Setup, Form Printers. These Form Printers can be set to use {default} printer from the printer dropdown list. This will use redirected printing to your local Windows default printer. This setting is specific to users' login only.
- Advanced Tip: RDWeb does not support redirected printing, RemoteApp login is required.

Note: redirected printing is slower than the Aptean Print Service. You will experience a several-second delay after Traverse completes the printing process before the printer starts printing.

After the Aptean Print Service issue is resolved, repeat steps 1-3 above but set “Enable Cloud Print” back to Yes.

d6611439-9735-41db-bd71-84e60ffab4c3.title: Bank Reconciliation Statement Status OPEN vs RECONCILED
d6611439-9735-41db-bd71-84e60ffab4c3.content:
Problem
- What does OPEN status mean?
- How do the statements get changed to a RECONCILED status?

Resolution
1. - What does OPEN status mean?
Open/Reconciled is a status that can be set for a statement.  It can be changed back and forth at any time.

The functional difference is that if a statement is set to "Reconciled" it will lock the statement and not allow users to make any changes to what is cleared and not cleared on the specific statement.

Generally speaking, statements are left open while working on them.  Once the reconciliation process has finished, users can change the status to "Reconciled" to lock the statement and label it to indicate that a specific statement is complete/reconciled.

It is optional and not required to change the Statement Status to Reconciled.

2. - How do we change Statements to a RECONCILED status?

Application> Bank Reconciliation> Reconciliation> Cleared Transaction

Select the desired Bank Account ID and the desired Statement Date by selecting the statement from the ellipse (this is assuming the Statement has already been created)

Click on Change Status to toggle the status back and forth between Open and Reconciled statuses

4ade4f4b-444c-4151-9c9f-b0a7100213eb.title: How to Void and Reprocess AP Payments
4ade4f4b-444c-4151-9c9f-b0a7100213eb.content:
Problem
Checks were printed and posted with non-matching payment numbers or otherwise incorrectly, and now those payments need to be voided and checks reprinted and reposted.

Resolution
In the AP Void Payments screen, you would filter to find a list of payments, and then select the check box(es) for the payment(s) you wish to void. You will want to ensure that you void the payment into the same period as it was posted in. I recommend using the payment date as the void date for this reason, as opposed to today's date. (You also want to verify currency if you have vendors on different currencies.)

The Status you select will be the status that appears on the Payment when it goes back to the Hold/Released screen.

When ready, click "Write" to void the check.

Once you write the void, it will bring up a log showing you exactly what GL account transactions were made to reverse the initial posting. This log is also available by clicking the Activity button and selecting the three dots under "Print Log" for the log you wish to see:

Then, you can go to the Hold/Released payments screen and you will see your voided payment there ready to process again with the status you selected. You can then Prepare Payments again, print the check/voucher again, create any associated Positive Pay Files or ACH Files for it, and post the payment again from this point - just as you would normally.

The old payment will show up in the AP Payment History View with the void date (you may need to pull in the void date column with the column chooser):

- Got to Payroll -> Codes Maintenance - > Earning Codes screen.

Cause
-

f3a13ca9-0fcf-4db4-8597-92c4ff2591a7.title: TRAVERSE Login Errors and Messages
f3a13ca9-0fcf-4db4-8597-92c4ff2591a7.content:
Problem
Depending on the settings that were used during the installation, or the setup of TRAVERSE Server Manager, License Manager and the client, here are some of the more common errors and their possible causes\solutions.

Resolution
Message: Unable to Switch Database. Check Detail.

Possible Causes:
- The login and password information entered in the TRAVERSE Database section of License Manager does not match the Master Login information entered in Server Manager.
- The company that you are trying to connect to is not associated with the Master Login in Server Manager.
- The company that you are trying to connect to does not have a record in tblSmCompInfo in the SYS database.
- The “SysDbName” value in the TRAVERSE.exe.config file is incorrect.
- The proper protocols or SQL Browser service are not enabled on the SQL Server (TCP\IP).
- Verify that the SQL Browser is running on the server.
- Could also be an issue with the firewall on the sql server. Once it times out still able to select the company from the drop down and connect. Set exceptions in the firewall for both sqlservr.exe and sqlbrowser.exe.
- If this occurs after applying an update to the client, copy the update files manually to the client TRAVERSE folder.  You may also need to download and apply newer updates.
- Verify protocols on the server.  Launch Sql Server Configuration Manager.  Under SQL Server Network Configuration make sure the protocols are enabled.  If the client works on the server but not workstations the Native Client protocols may be enabled but not the Network protocols.

Message: Login Failed. Cannot connect to license server: servername: Error: No connection could be made because the target machine actively refused it. ip address: port #.

Possible Causes:

- The TRAVERSE License Server is not running.
- The TRAVERSE License Manager is not listening on the assigned port (2113 by default). Check event viewer to confirm.
- The login or password information entered in the Membership Database area of License Manager does not match the Master Login and password information entered in Server Manager. If this is incorrect, then the TRAVERSE database section information is most likely also incorrect.
- The “LicensePort” value listed in the TRAVERSE.exe.config file is incorrect.

Message: Login Failed. Invalid Login.

Possible Causes:

- The login name entered is not a valid login or setup in Server Manager correctly.
- The password entered for the login is incorrect.

Message: Login Failed. Input String not correct.

Possible Causes:

- License Server not running. Could be issue with Master Login and Password.
- DEFAULT sql instance can use only the machine name in license manager.
- Make sure Traverse database and Membership database information is same in license server.
- Make sure instance name is included in Traverse License Server screen.

Message: Please enter valid database name or Company ID.

Possible Causes:

- The user is not setup in any groups under the companies in Server Manager.

Message: Login Failed. No such host is known.

Possible Causes:

- The “LicenseServer” value in the TRAVERSE.exe.config file is not the correct server name where the license server was installed. This should just be the machine name, not the SQL server name, localhost (unless installing the client on the license server) or the network path name (\\servername).

Message: Configuration System Failed to Initialize.

Possible Causes:

- This may be caused by bad information in the TRAVERSE.exe.config file. There is a bug where reinstalling the client is doubling up information in that file. To fix, need to take out the duplicate information (between the </customTypeSettings> and </configuration> values) or uninstall the client, delete the TRAVERSE client directory, then reinstall.

Message: Login Failed. Length cannot be less than zero. Parameter name: length

Possible Causes:

When SQL was installed it was not installed using mixed mode so the License server cannot start. You can go to the event viewer to verify. In SQL, change to mixed mode. Stop and start the instance then stop and start the License server should then be able to login. If not, check the master login and password. Also make sure there is a group setup in the company you are logging into and the user that you are logging in with is also setup in that group and there is menu permissions setup.


Event Viewer Messages

You can view the Application log within the Event viewer on the License Server to troubleshoot connection issues. The last entry should be “License Server in listening on port 2113”. If you get this message, then the License Server and the SQL server are communicating and you should be able to login to the client with a valid Traverse login and valid TRAVERSE.exe.config settings. If there are problems, here are some of the more common event viewer messages and possible solutions.

Message: Invalid sql connection or
Could not connect to SQL Server. Login failed for user 'user'.

Possible Causes:

- The login information entered in the TRAVERSE and\or Membership Database area of License Manager is not the same as the Master Login information entered in Server Manager.
- The SQL Server is not configured to use both Windows and SQL authentication. This is required if using the default Master Login, or a SQL login as the Master Login.
- The SQL Server information entered in the TRAVERSE License Manager is incorrect.

Message: Only one usage of each socket address (protocol/network address/port) is normally permitted.

Possible Causes:

- The License server service was stopped, but not enough time went by prior to restarting (15-30 secs). Verify in the Event Viewer that the service is listening on the correct port (2113 by default).


Misc Notes:

The login and password information in TRAVERSE License Manager needs to be the same as the login and password for the Master Login setup in Server Manager.

The Master Login should not be used to login to the Server Manager or the client. This login is just used to establish a connection between the License Server and the SQL Server.

TRAVERSE no longer uses SQL logins to login to the client. Users and Groups must be setup for each company before access to those companies will be granted through the client.

The SA login or a trusted admin login should be used to login to Server Manager.

If you cannot change the Master Login information in Server Manager, verify that you are logged into TSM as SA or a trusted admin user. If so, then may need to go into SQL and delete the user(s) listed under Security-Logins, and also under each database-security-users, then reset up the master login again.

TSM does not have applications for company that has been upgraded from 10.5-
Check to make sure that database is in the tblsmcompinfo. If not add.

License count exceeded – Try stopping the service, activate and then start service.

Input String is not the correct format – Could be trusted connection not being able to authenticate with Domain control (AD).  Try a standard Traverse user.

c3fe8048-52ea-4b2f-86c8-79984a2d7c53.title: Traverse Global 11.2 Year-End Update Process and Compliance Update
c3fe8048-52ea-4b2f-86c8-79984a2d7c53.content:
Problem
How to Apply Year-End Updates

Resolution
Process for Applying Year-End Updates
Applying Year-End Updates in Traverse Global 11.2

Once you have received the Traverse Compliance Release – Tax Update notification email, follow the steps below to apply the Traverse Global 11.2 Year-End update.  (Install this update before you begin processing Payroll for the New Year.)
Note: If you do not want to update to the most current build, or if you cannot update to the most current build, and only wish to install the year-end compliance update, then do not follow these instructions.  Reach out to Support for assistance via Aptean Connect.
Traverse Global 11.2 Build/Service Pack Updates consist of 4 steps:
- Backing up the Traverse client, updates, and databases. If additional web-enabled applications (Portals, WMS, Report Server, APIs) are licensed then back up those installations as well.
- Downloading updates in TRAVERSE Server Manager.
- Applying updates to Databases in TRAVERSE Server Manager.
- Applying updates to TRAVERSE Client.



Downloading updates in TRAVERSE Server Manager

- In TRAVERSE Server Manager (TSM), click Help and Check for Updates.




- The TRAVERSE Folder is the location on the Server where the Updates reside. This folder will need to have permissions set so that All TRAVERSE users have access from their workstations.

- Site ID is the identifying number with Aptean for your company.

- Product ID is the License key that Aptean has distributed to you that controls how many users and what applications are available.

- Click Check for Updates.


- If Updates are available, there will be a notification in the Status Field.

- Verify that the file path is correct and click Download.


- When the download is complete, close the Traverse Updater window.


Applying build updates to Databases in TRAVERSE Server Manager

- Select Database from the Menu bar and select Maintenance Update from the selection


- On the Maintenance Update screen, click the Browse button outlined in red above.


- Browse to the folder location where the Updates were downloaded. In the Server folder, choose the ServerUpdateXXXXX.tsmx file with the most recent date. The numbers in that file name represent the Year and day created. In the screenshot below, 12 is 2012, and 081 is the 81st day of the year.


- After selecting the Update tsmx file, a prompt to back up all the databases will appear. Click OK.  If backups have not been prepared, then pause and prepare backups of the databases.



- Once that is selected, check the Databases that will be updated. Note: Always choose to Include System Update and Security Updates. Choose Payroll Tax Updates if using the Payroll Application.

- After selecting the databases to update, click Next.


- Click OK.



- On the Status tab, the update process will begin updating all of the databases you have selected.




- When the update has completed, it will notify you with a new window, click OK.




- Being that this is a Year-End Compliance Update, the Maintenance Update process needs to be repeated if you have Fixed Assets and Payroll. The only difference is instead of selecting the ServerUpdateXXXXX.tsmx file, TaxRates20YYFA_20YYMMDD.tsmx and TaxRates20YYPA_20YYMMDD.tsmx files need to be selected and applied.

Note: If you have more than one Instance in SQL, you will have to close out of TSM and log back in under your other instances and repeat the Maintenance Update steps for those databases.



Applying build updates to TRAVERSE Client

- Open the TRAVERSE Client. On open, there will be a prompt that Updates are Available. Click OK.


- Select Help from the Menu bar.
- Choose Check for Updates from the list


- The TRAVERSE Client updater will pop up. Verify that the Updated Server Folder is the folder that the Updates were downloaded into. Note: It is important that the local Client location has full access to Updates Destination.

- Click Check for Updates.


- The status field will notify you if there are Updates available or if this client is currently up-to-date. If there are Updates available, Close the TRAVERSE client and click Apply Updates.

-  If you receive the Please close TRAVERSE message and you have already closed TRAVERSE, click OK and click Apply Updates again.


- Once the Updates have been completed, the Status field will notify you of that. Then Close the Updater window.

- Open TRAVERSE and on the splash screen, the current build will be displayed and should match the TSMX file that you selected to update with.


- This splash screen and Build information can also be found when in TRAVERSE by going back to the Help menu and choosing About.


Creating new General Ledger Years

- Use System Manager > Company Setup > Period Conversion to create and configure the New Year.
- Go to System Manager > Company Setup> Period Conversion.
- Type in the New Year you are creating in Fiscal Year.


- Click on Enter, Message will display Do you want to set up periods for: Company:XXX, Year:20YY.

- Click Yes.


- Select whether to Copy Previous Year values.

- Click OK.


- Your New Year will be created.


- While not required, it is suggested to close the periods at the end of the year. A common mistake at the end of the year is to post entries to the end of the New Year accidentally when attempting to post entries to the end of the prior year.  Temporarily closing the periods at the end of the New Year prevents this from happening.

Changing General Ledger Fiscal Year

- General Ledger > Periodic Processing > Change Fiscal Year

- Use the Change Fiscal Year function to change the current fiscal year to any existing fiscal year for viewing and printing statements, journals, and reports.

- Un-check the box for Change for this session only. This will change the Default GL Year for all Traverse users. Click OK.



General Ledger Update Current Year

General Ledger > Periodic Processing > Update Current Year.
This function updates only the beginning balances of the accounts in the current year without requiring you to clear and close, you can easily bring forward initial balances at the start of a new year without closing last year's accounts. (This step can be done multiple times. If the Update Current Year is done and then additional transactions are added to the Previous Year, the Update Current Year function needs to be run again.)

It performs the following functions:

- Copies the ending balances from the Old Year to the New Year for GL accounts with types from 005 - 465. (Balance Sheet Accounts)

- Consolidate the net income (or net loss) amount from the balances of all the GL accounts with account types from 500 - 890. (Income Statement Accounts)

- Updates the balance for the retained earnings account with the net income or net loss if selected. Check the box to consolidate unclosed income (loss) to retained earnings, and select your retained earnings account.



Note: When you run the Update Current Year make sure you are in your NEW YEAR. You can run Update Current Year multiple times as long as you don’t run Clear & Close Last Year.



Creating new Payroll Years

Use the TRAVERSE Server Manager to create new Payroll Years.

- Click on the plus sign next to TRAVERSE to expand the company databases.

- Click on the plus sign next to the Company Database you are creating the new payroll year for.

- Click the plus sign next to Applications.

- Right-click the TRAVERSE Application PA and select Add Year.


- The next TRAVERSE Payroll Year 20YY will automatically populate.

- Copy Data From the Previous Payroll Year 20YY.
Tip: make sure to add/change any employee information prior to creating the new payroll year, so those changes are automatically populated when the new Payroll is created.
Note:  Deleting the newly created year and re-creating the year will not refresh the data from the prior year.  It is critically important the New Year be created once all applicable data entry (employees, earning codes, deductions, etc.) is completed in the prior year.


- Once the payroll is created in the TRAVERSE Server Manager it can now be used in the TRAVERSE Client.


Change Payroll Year

- Payroll > Periodic Processing > Change Payroll Year

- Drop down the arrow for the Change Year and select the New Year.


NOTE: Please be sure to mind the current payroll year. If the year has been changed to the new payroll year and adjustments or payroll processing must occur for the prior year, the year must be changed. It must be changed back to the new payroll year once work has been completed.
