02797ff3-a6ea-484d-b071-f13ab65008c9.title: Colorado Retail Delivery Fee - How to apply this fee using the Tax Integration
02797ff3-a6ea-484d-b071-f13ab65008c9.content:
Problem
Background
As of July 1. 2022, a new delivery fee has been imposed for the state of Colorado on all deliveries by motor vehicles to a location within Colorado. The delivery must contain at least one item of tangible personal property subject to state sales or use tax.

This fee can be handled using Traverse Global with the Tax Integration interfaced with Avalara. This document will discuss how to configure Traverse Global to use a Service type item and configure the Avalara Admin Console to code this item help make the process of adding this fee automated.

Resolution
How to handle this change using the Tax Integration
The following steps can be taken to implement this change in Traverse Global with the Tax Integration. Before proceeding below, you will need to be able to access the Items function in Traverse Global to Inventory > Setup and Maintenance > Items. You must also have access to Avalara’s online Admin Console.

Use the following steps to implement this change:
- Access the Traverse Global application, and then navigate to Inventory > Setup and Maintenance > Items
- Create a new item, with an Item Type of Service. This will ensure the item does not have an impact to the GL as a regular inventory item would.
The state of Colorado requires that the invoice or receipt show “Retail delivery fees.” This can be accomplished if the item’s Description reads “Retail delivery fees.”
Please consider adding any additional locations needed in order to use the item, and taking care to set the appropriate item codes per your business needs.
- Access Avalara’s online Admin Console and navigate to Settings > What you sell
- Click on Add an item
- In the Item code field, enter the inventory item created at step 2 above.
Enter a Description of “Retail delivery fees”
Enter an AVALARA TAX CODE value of OF400000
- Click Add item

The necessary setup is complete. When the shipping destination is within Colorado and the CO DELIVERY FEE item is added to an order, the Avalara tax calculation will now include an additional $0.27 to the order amount. It is not necessary to add $0.27 as the price for the CO DELIVERY FEE item due to the automation.

Example
Next, we will view this change in action. First, please find an example below where goods are in process of shipping to a customer in the state of Colorado. An item has been added at a price of $100.00 and taxes calculated with the AvaTax calculation on screen. Note: Our delivery fee item has not been added to this order

Next, let’s verify the Tax Calculation. The Tax Calculation screen below indicated the tax breakdown for this invoice, with $3.70 of sales tax and $100.00 of taxable goods.

Next, we will add our delivery charge item to the same order and recalculate taxes.

We now observe the Net Due has increased by $0.27. The Tax Calculation will now show an increase in the invoice’s total tax.

Next, we will post this transaction and commit this to Avalara. If we view the transaction from the Admin Console, we will observe the $0.27 fee listed out:

d83d62fc-2dbe-44a0-8587-9c0be0d315e3.title: Emailing in OSAS
d83d62fc-2dbe-44a0-8587-9c0be0d315e3.content:
Problem
Customer getting Time out Reading Socket

Resolution
Resource Manager E-mail setup.
Resource Manager > Installation and Configuration > Email Setup.  The client will need to provide this information.

If this is an ssl smtp email server an entry will need to be made in the config.bbx file
Add this line
alias N1 ssl
This can be done with a text editor or going through RM > Installation and configuration > Devices and choosing other.

You must relaunch OSAS to reread the config file after making an edit.

Email queue
There is an option in the RM options and interfaces Send Emails Immediately?  If this is set to NO the emails will not go out until you enter into the queue and send them.  This option should be set to No for testing when someone first sets up their email.
The Applications
In AP/PO in order to email vouchers you need to have an Electronic Method of Payment.  To be able to set up an electronic MOP you need to have both Bank Rec and Banking installed.
Options and Interfaces for the application must be set to allow emailing of the form type, vouchers, statements, invoices, Purchase orders.

E-Mail Defaults
These are set up under File maintenance for DD and AP/PO and Codes maintenance for AR/SO.  Each application requires the same Information.  Make sure you complete this info to be able to successfully email

User Set up Preferences – RM > User Setup > Preferences, This E-mail Address will be used if the option is set in the applications Email Defaults.

Delivery method
This is set in File maintenance > Vendors > Vendor Codes for AP/PO
File maintenance > Customers > General Information in AR/SO for both Invoices and Statements
File Maintenance > Employees > General Information for Direct Deposit

E-Mail Addresses
You must have an email address entered for each form type for each Employee, Vendor or Customer.  This set up is under File maintenance > (Employee, Customer or Vendor) > E-Mail Addresses.

Issues:
Email not being sent.  Check the option for send emails Immediately? If it’s NO check the queue to see if it is being created.  If it is set to YES, change it to NO While you test.  Go through the Set up To make sure Emailing is allowed and that the Vendor, Customer or Employee has the Delivery method as email and an email address for the form type.
You must pick a printer in order to generate an email.  Printing to a directory or printing to a file will not generate the email.  Even if you are setting Print copies of emailed * to NO you need to pick a printer to generate the email.
Time out Reading Socket.  The Socket is the port set in RM > Installation and configuration >      E-Mail Set Up.  It is either blocked or it is incorrect.

SMTP errors
When you receive an SMTP error OSAS is sending the email and the SMTP server is rejecting it the client needs to contact their email provider to find out why.
If it is an authentication error you can check RM > Installation and Configuration > Users.  If the user has an email Log In and password entered here that is what will be used in place of the Log in and Password that is in RM > E-Mail setup.  Delete it from the Users Screen.  This is only used in certain security set ups where based on the users from address it is required that they have their own login and password.

Gmail smtp error 535-5.7.8

On the gmail accounts security settings enable access for less secure apps.
Office 365
SMTP Server smtp.office365.com
Port is 587

d88c561f-2bd5-4289-8809-e4128251a6d8.title: Post Expense to GL function in OSAS8
d88c561f-2bd5-4289-8809-e4128251a6d8.content:
Problem
Post Expense to GL

After you produce the Department Report at the end of an accounting period, post expenses to General Ledger to create accounting entries for the payroll expenses for the period. If Payroll interfaces with General Ledger, these entries update the GLJRxxx (Journal) file. When you post checks at the end of a payday, accounting entries for withholding, tax and net pay are created. To complete this transaction, the gross pay amount is debited to a payroll holding account. The Post Expense to GL function finishes the accounting entries for the period. It credits the holding account and distributes the amount to various department expense accounts in the ledger.

When the general ledger entries are made, the general ledger post-to-date amounts in the PADPxxx (Department) file are cleared to make way for a new accounting period.

33eec9d3-7957-4dec-9529-377d093a5ee9.title: Voiding a voucher using a negative manual check.
33eec9d3-7957-4dec-9529-377d093a5ee9.content:
Problem
Customer needs assistance with Voiding a voucher using a negative manual check

Resolution
Voiding a voucher using a negative manual check.
You’ll need a record of the voucher.  This can be the Edit register or check register if they were run in Detail and included Employer tax and deduction information.  If these are not available print a check history register in detail and include employer deductions and withholdings.  Once you have this information you can enter the manual check.

Once you have this information Go to Manual checks and enter the Group Code of the employee and the period End and check dates as you would if processing a manual check.  On the next page after you have entered the Employee ID enter the number of the original voucher that you are voiding.  Enter over until the “Create Voucher?” option opens and set it to Yes.

Page Down if this is a salaried employee the Salary will populate.  Choose enter to edit and now enter the hours and amount as negative to reverse those on the voucher you are voiding.

Page Down then choose Calculate checks. You may get this message choose OK. Then Next page

The deduction should populate correctly as negative amounts check this and correct as necessary and choose Next Page.

You will need to correct the tax amounts in the employee Withholdings and the Employer Liability.  Make sure the Net Pay amount is correct.

When you are finished choose Next check then F7 back to the main menu print a check register to check for accuracy then Post checks will complete the void.

a0efb4b1-3e69-4cc6-bbeb-edb19c63b644.title: Installing Osas
a0efb4b1-3e69-4cc6-bbeb-edb19c63b644.content:
Problem
Client needs assistance with installing Osas on workstation

Resolution
Methods of connecting
Starting with OSAS 8 the recommended method of connection is a JNLP connection.  During installation of OSAS 8 on the server the configuration for a jnlp connection is created in the Enterprise Manager.  This configuration is held in the jnlp.ini file, \osas8\bbj\cfg.  This setup was available with the interpreter version 19.23 and under.  Starting with the Interpreter version 20.30 and the use of Java 11 or AdoptOpenJDK 11 a new but similar way of connecting has replaced the JNLP method it is referred to as App Deployment.  The preferred method of connection for versions prior to 8.0 was the thin client.  A thin client connection is still a valid and useful way to connect.
JNLP – Jetty – java Web Start
To make the jnlp connection the URL is available in the Enterprise Manager.

On the workstation you wish to connect you will need to have Java installed then paste this url into the address bar of the browser.  The jnlp, OSAS8.jnlp file components are downloaded over port 8888 and the jnlp file is “built on the fly”.   Once downloaded the file needs to be launched, how this is done will depend on the browser used.  The application will go through a verification process during which screens will open See the Resource Manage Installation Guide, RMINDOC.pdf.
If you need to attempt to re-establish a jetty connection that has failed on a workstation the first step is to make sure you have the url.  You do not need to be on the server to get the url you can find it in the existing icons target line.

You can also connect to the EM from the workstation using the url http://<servername>:8888/bbjem/em
If you retrieve the url from the icon copy and paste it into notepad.  Next clear the java cache by doing the following, Start --> Run -->javaws –uninstall.  This may remove the existing icon, if it does not, delete it.  At some point verify the java version being used.  It needs to be a version 1.8_xx.  Now paste the url into the address bar of the browser.  This should take you through the download and verification process.  A new icon will be placed on the desktop and osas should launch.
To place an icon on the desktop go to Control panel > Java > View highlight the application then choose the arrow.

If you get the icon and osas does not launch, launch it.
To be able to get the jnlp to work you need to have ports 8888, 2003 and 2008 available.
If this fails the first step in troubleshooting is to make sure you can get to the server.  In the address bar of the browser enter http://<servername>:8888 this will take you to the BBj welcome screen.

There are only two variables the server name and the port 8888.  If you can’t get here then drop the firewall on the server as a test.  If that fails then ping the server by name and ip address.
If you can get through on port 8888 and you receive the message unable to launch the application check ports 2003 and 2008.  One way to do this would be from the admin cmd prompt enter
netstat –ab > ports.txt
This will create a text file in the system32 directory that you can then search using notepad++

If there is another app occupying these ports 2003 and 2008 then it will need to be uninstalled.  An application called LogMeIn is known for this.  If you do not see the ports listed it is not an indication of an issue.
If you are stopped from connecting by the Java security set exceptions for the site in the Java Control panel.  Go to the Security tab then Edit Site list.  Make two entries one for just the server and port 8888 and another for the entire jnlp url.

If these all fail to establish the jnlp connection then try installing the thin client.
Thin Client
Installing a thin client could very well connect you if the jnlp connection fails. If it does not it will provide a more addressable error.
There are instructions in the RMINDOC for installing the client.  For interpreter versions 19.23 and under there is a method available in the EM referred to as Remote installers.

If you are trying to install a client because the jnlp connection failed these will fail also.  Installing a client involves installing the interpreter, or a portion of the interpreter on the client.  The interpreter must be the same version as that which is installed on the server so you will need to have installation media local to the client, if you’re solving for a jnlp failure.  Once you know the interpreter version on the server.  You can check the Basis site to see if that version is available for download.  The client may have the original install media, the osas8.iso on the server.
There are some differences when installing the client from the osas8.iso and the download from Basis.
The osas iso will require a product ID the basis download will not.
In the RMINDOC instruction you are installing a partial interpreter I would suggest a full installation of BBj.   If installing from the osas8.iso make these selections for a full interpreter install.
Tip:  If you also install RM you will get an icon.  If you use the Basis download you will need to create an icon

For the BLM chose Designate a BLM then Remote, next enter the server name.


When installing a thin client choose to run BBj services Automatically after user log in.

Once you have the interpreter installed you need an icon.  If you created one by installing RM you will need to edit the target line to point to the server.  The RM install guide provides an excellent example of the target line and explanation of its attributes.  If you used the Basis download you will need to create the icon.
In the progRM of any install is the WINOSAS.ico this will provide the osas icon.  Just copy one over to the client.
The thin client needs to be able to “see” the server and connect on ports 2003 and 2008.

ed9da948-8d09-4fd9-839f-50b1bd7638a2.title: Printing a copy of a Form that is being also being e-mailed through Document Delivery.
ed9da948-8d09-4fd9-839f-50b1bd7638a2.content:
Problem
Forms are being sent as an email. However, would like to have a printed copy as well.

Resolution
This can be accomplished by adding two Form Printers for the same Form ID. Traverse will use the first Form Printer to "Send" the E-mail, and the second Form Printer will have the Form sent to it to Print.

Applications > System Manager > Company Setup > Form Printers

Creating Form Printer Information:
1. Click the New button, on the toolbar, to open a blank Form printer record.
2. Select the desired Form ID from the Forms field drop-down list.
3. Enter the text to print on the Form in the Copy Text field as a Watermark if desired.
4. Enter the order in which to print the Form in the Order field.

- To print multiple copies of the same Form ID, add multiple rows of the same Form. The Order numbers can be sequential for multiple Form entries to print in a specific order. For example Customer Copy 1, Office Copy 2, etc...
- The Same Printer may be used for multiple Form entries.
- If using Document Delivery, Document Delivery will use the 1st from Printer to send the e-mail from, and the remaining Form Entries

5. Select the Printer name from the dropdown to which to print the Forms in the Printer field. You can select a different printer for each copy. The available printers are the printers set up on the Windows workstation.
6. Select the tray for the selected printer from which you want the form to print in the Tray field. This selection only applies if the printer has multiple trays.
7. Select the Active check box to print the copy; otherwise, clear the check box and the Form Printer will not be used when printing.
8. Save.

828aad7b-1f33-4ae2-93a6-f500b20e3fcc.title: GL Financial Reports Not Printing
828aad7b-1f33-4ae2-93a6-f500b20e3fcc.content:
Problem
I am trying to print the Financial reports for a particular period and I get a SQL Server error.

Resolution
This seems to be a SQL error that is happening due to SQL versions not being on the latest CU version.
Check the current version of SQL (Help -> About).
Then go to the Microsoft SQL Cumulative updates download page to download and install the latest CU update:

https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/database-engine/install-windows/latest-updates-for-microsoft-sql-server?view=sql-server-ver15

Once the SQL Server has been updated to the latest version, reboot the server. The error should be resolved.

a86729c6-aff0-4134-a3d1-616e383346a1.title: Unable to Create Prenotification File:  " Access to the path 'C:\Program Files\Open Systems, Inc\TRAVERSE\xxxx.xxx' is denied."
a86729c6-aff0-4134-a3d1-616e383346a1.content:
Problem
An error occurs when attempt to Create Prenotification File in the default TRAVERSE folder.
Error: Access to the path 'C:\Program Files\Open Systems, Inc\TRAVERSE\xxxx.CCS' is denied.

Cause
Permission settings on the workstation can prevent files being created or modified under the C:\Program Files folder.

Resolution
Permission settings on the workstation can prevent files being created or modified under the C:\Program Files folder.  The destination folder for the file needs to be changed to a folder where the user has permissions to create files.  The Desktop folder typically allows this.  Here are instructions for saving the Prenotification file to the Desktop.

To save the file.(On the desktop) Create Prenotification File Use the Create Prenotification File function(Applications > Payroll > Periodic Processing > Create Prenotification File) to create the file necessary for your bank to verify account numbers and routing codes in a trial run. You cannot produce vouchers until you have selected the Prenote In check box on the Employee Information screen's Direct Deposit tab.
Note: This function is available only if you use the Direct Deposit/Banking application.
- Select a bank account ID for which to create a prenotification file from the Bank Account ID field.
- Select the Resend All Prenotifications check box, if applicable, to include all employees' direct deposit information in the prenotification file. Note: Leaving this check box clear includes only those employees whose direct deposit account information has been added or changed.
- Select the Mark All Prenotifications In This Run As Approved check box, if applicable, to mark all of the prenotifications in the run as approved.
- Select the file format for the prenotification file from the File Format field. Note: If the Exclude Batch Offset (Balancing) Record check box, in the System Manager Bank Accounts function, is selected, you must select ADV, CCD, or PPD for the file format. If the Exclude Batch Offset (Balancing) Record check box is not selected, you must select ADVO, CCDO, or PPDO for the file format.
- Enter the name you want for the prenotification file in the File Name field.
- Select the location for which you want to save the prenotification file from the Save To Folder field(In this case the desktop).
- Add any comments for the prenotification file in the Comments field.

d963423e-a068-4ab8-a3cd-82392b4074bc.title: SaaS/Cloud - Printing Information
d963423e-a068-4ab8-a3cd-82392b4074bc.content:
Problem
Understanding printing options and setups available in the Aptean Cloud.

Resolution
There are 2 types of printers available in your Cloud.
-  Remote Desktop Services “redirected printers”
- Redirected printers are automatically created for each user’s session via the Microsoft Remote Desktop RemoteApp application which is used to access your cloud applications.
- All printers set up on the PC will be redirected. The user’s default printer on the PC will always be the default printer for Traverse.
- These printers have some limitations and generally do not perform as well as Direct network printers.


- Direct network printers
- Requires VPN tunnel between the client site and Azure cloud site.
- Need to be specifically set up by Aptean’s Cloud IT Team per the client’s request.
- Provide the best printing performance and consistent results.
- Fully supported for Traverse form printers



There are 2 types of printing that can be used in Traverse.

- Traditional printing

- Provides users the ability to print anything that is not set up for form printing to any printer with a real-time selection of the printer.
- When the user wants to print or export a document, they will be prompted with a print selection window. If the user wants to print a document to a direct network printer, they can select that printer from the window. Users can temporarily set a direct network printer as their default however it will change back to the redirected printer that is set as their computer's default printer.
-


- If the user would like to set that printer as their default printer, they need to do that directly on their computer via the Control Panel or Windows Settings. The new default printer will not become the Traverse default until the user closes and reopens Traverse.


- Form printing
- Allows Traverse users to set up specific forms to print to a specific printer. Please see Traverse HELP for more information on setting up form printers.
- If direct network printers are available on the Traverse Cloud server, the user will need to select the direct network printer from the printer dropdown list.
- SM>From Printers


- Redirected printers are not officially supported for form printing however it is possible to use form printing if there are no direct network printers installed on the Traverse Cloud server via the “{Default}” printer option. When set to {Default} the Form printer will print to the user’s default printer on their computer.
- If the user would like to change the {Default} printer to a different printer they will need to make that change directly on their computer via the Control Panel or Windows Settings. The new default printer will not become the Traverse default until the user closes and reopens Traverse.
- Note that If your Traverse system was migrated to the Traverse Cloud or between Traverse Cloud Tiers all users will need to update their form printers unless they are using the {Default} option.

12011f08-0b94-4146-951d-6245e29a692a.title: Printing to multiple trays
12011f08-0b94-4146-951d-6245e29a692a.content:
Problem
Printer has multiple trays and is not printing to them correctly.
For example, Printing 2 companies with 2 check types each to different drawers in the printer, is not working correctly,

Resolution
In Traverse, go to System Manager --> Company Setup --> Form Printers to see how the printers are setup.
Isolate and test each Printer tray for the desired forms (ie. AP Checks, PA Checks). Try to select the desired trays here and test how they print. If the forms are set up to "Automatically select" a tray, test to find out which tray the "Automatically select" options prints to.

If the tray does not appear as an option in Traverse SM Forms Printer, look into the Printers and scanners setup. Go into the properties of the Printer that printed the form, go to the Device settings to add the appropriate trays. Once the trays have been added and installed the client should be able to print and direct the trays as designed in TRAVERSE with all their forms printing successfully.

Step to be followed:
- On the Windows taskbar, click the Windows icon, and then click Settings - Devices - Printers/Scanners.
- click your product, and then select Manage.
- Then select the Properties.
- From the Device Settings menu, right click on the trays and add appropriate trays (ex. 1 though 4).
-
- Click OK to confirm your selections.

Once this is done, go back to Traverse to the SM Forms Printer screen and select the desired trays.

5f7d2508-cba4-4206-9841-425181269ab7.title: AP Select payables
5f7d2508-cba4-4206-9841-425181269ab7.content:
Problem
AP Select Payable does not show the dropdown for the Batch codes.

Resolution
The cutoff buttons that the client is experiencing are from the user’s magnification settings on their PC. I was able to reproduce it by setting my PC’s display settings to 175%. This is pretty common with users who have 4K monitors as the default is usually around 175% scaling.

Follow the following steps to fix the issue:
Open the View< Preference of the Traverse and set the font size to 8.25(Default).
Open the Display Setting by right-clicking on the desktop and select the display settings. Scroll down to the Scale and Layout. Adjust the scaling in the change in the size of the text, apps, and other items.
Open the traverse back up and see that the drop-down is available in the AP(Select Payable) adjust the font size again if needed/required.

1c6250e8-e072-4200-9244-c2772c5cb8bf.title: How to print 1099 Nec Form
1c6250e8-e072-4200-9244-c2772c5cb8bf.content:
Problem
Printing the 1099-Nec Form.

Resolution
Print the 1099 Nec form going to the AP

Applications > Accounts Payable > Periodic Processing > 1099 Processing:
- Use the Data Filter to select the range of filtering options or leave the filter blank to include all available data.
- Select the fiscal year for which you want to generate the 1099-MISC or 1099-NEC forms from the Year field.
- Click the Generate button to calculate vendors' 1099 payment totals based on the selected criteria.
- Add, delete, or edit the 1099 vendor records as necessary in the grid at the bottom of the screen.
Note: You can only edit the Account Number, Name, Name Control, Amount, 2nd TIN Not, Form Code, and Foreign Addr (Y/N) fields.
- Click the Save button to save any changes made to the 1099 vendor records.

4a0cbe9a-d4c8-41ba-a2df-e18d64c23cb6.title: Font size issue with standard report from all Traverse modules
4a0cbe9a-d4c8-41ba-a2df-e18d64c23cb6.content:
Problem
When the client prints any standard report from traverse the font size is small not fill up the whole page.

Resolution
The issue is caused by changing the workstations Windows Display Settings.  In the Scale and Layout section there is a setting for "Change the size of text, apps, and other items."  If that setting it set higher than 100% it will cause scaling issues with TRAVERSE reports.

To resolve this issue one of two things must me done.  The Display setting can be set back to 100%, but this often isn't a good solution since the user has already decided to increase it to improve screen visibility.  In order to resolve this issue while leaving the setting where it is a new shortcut needs to be created for TRAVERSE which has a setting in it that tells Windows to ignore the Display setting for the launched applications.

- Go to the TRAVERSE client directory (Client Folder).  This is typically C:\Program Files\Open Systems, Inc\TRAVERSE
- Right-click the TRAVERSE.EXE file and choose Send to > Desktop (Create Shortcut).  This will create a shortcut for TRAVERSE on the Desktop.
- Go to the desktop and find the shortcut.  Right click it, and select Properties
- Select the Compatibility tab
- Click ‘Change high DPI settings’ Button at the bottom of the tab.
- Check the box to ‘Override high DPI scaling behavior’
- Select ‘Application’ listed in the lookup, and click OK
- Print the report again to confirm if the issue is resolved

88b2f0e2-4748-4e4f-b0b6-1b9f080393e6.title: Where Does Item Cost Pull From?
88b2f0e2-4748-4e4f-b0b6-1b9f080393e6.content:
Problem
The client wants to know where a cost that populates on a purchase order or sales order is coming from.

Resolution
The cost for an Item is set up in the Business Rules.  Check the Business Rules for Inventory to see what the setup is.

FIFO (“First-In, First-Out”) assumes that the oldest products in a company's inventory have been sold first and goes by those inventory costs. The LIFO (“Last-In, First-Out”) method assumes that the most recent products in a company's inventory have been sold first and uses those costs instead.

Zero Quantity Sales Costing -  When an inventory item has no quantity, this is the price that will show, excluding service items.
Last - Uses the Last Cost
Average - Uses a weighted average cost over time. (Service items always pull this cost regardless of this setting.)
Base - Uses the base cost for Inventory items with quantities
Standard - Uses the set estimate user has put in

With this setup, the cost comes from a combination of places. For the Purchase Order, it comes from the last posted invoice for an item for a specific location, matched by vendors.  For the Sales Order, it will come from the Average Cost.

The cost is displayed in Inventory --> Setup and Maintenance --> Items

Pull up the Item ID for the item in question, and click on the Location tab.


For the Purchase Order:

1. The cost will look at the information based on each given location. Then, for each given location, (ex. CA001) a Purchase Order or Sales transaction will pull from one of two places:

2. The order will look first at the Vendor information.  If the vendor the Purchase Order is created for matches one of the vendors stored on the Vendor tab, the order will give the "Unit Cost" for that particular vendor.  Once an invoice is posted, this information will automatically update. You can toggle through the vendors that are set up using the arrows at the bottom.  This information comes from historical information, so it resists editing.

3. If the Purchase Order is for a vendor not in the vendor list, it pulls the cost from the “Last” Cost box (if that is what is set up in the Business Rules).  This comes from the last posted invoice, however, it can also be overwritten and saved until the next posting.

Sales Order:
If the quantity on hand is not zero, and the Business Rule is set either FIFO, LIFO, or Average, the Sales Order will pull the Average cost for the "Unit Cost".  If the Business rule is set to Standard, it will pull in the Standard Cost for the "Unit Cost."

If the quantity on hand for that inventory item is zero, the sales order will pull the field specified in the Business Rule, "Zero quantity sales costing."

5a8fb3f3-0fdb-43ea-9e21-dbfb80b78682.title: User Groups/Permissions

8c06eb82-529d-43aa-ad49-64165e5172ae.title: Invoicing in PO when multiple receipts are posted
8c06eb82-529d-43aa-ad49-64165e5172ae.content:
Problem
Specify the quantity on PO invoices

Resolution
When multiple receipts have been entered for an order and a new invoice is entered, the receipt totals are automatically used for the new invoice record. The Clear button on the invoice screen will reset the automated receipt quantities to 0 and allow users to specify the quantity.
You must have multiple receipts entered to use the Clear button. When you enter the invoice, the receipt quantities are automatically transferred to the new invoice record.

The Clear button is active at this time. If used, the values in the invoice’s Qty and Ext Cost fields are set to 0 and can be entered as necessary.

215f5cc0-23a9-4dde-8b82-4b859d3d48c3.title: How to run "Update Current Year"
215f5cc0-23a9-4dde-8b82-4b859d3d48c3.content:
Problem
Update Current Year needs to be run in order to get ending balances from one year to update the opening balances of the next year.  Whenever correcting or adjusting entries are made in a prior year after it has been closed then the Update Current Year process needs to run in order to roll the new ending balances forward.

Resolution
When transactions are entered in TRAVERSE into a particular year, it will update a period balance, and that will roll forward all the way to the end of the year to show up as year ending balances.  However, year ending balances do not automatically roll over to become opening balances in the next year.  That process must be done manually by running the Update Current Year program.

There are a few different ways the Update Current Year program can be run.  By far the most common way to run the program will take the ending balances in the old year for Balance Sheet accounts and roll them into the new year as opening balances, and it will take all the balances of Income Statement accounts and roll the sum of them into the opening balance of the Retained Earnings account, and set the opening balance of the Income Statement accounts to zero in the new year.

Here are the instructions for performing the Update Current Year process as outline above.  If the above outline does not describe how you wish to close the old year into the new, or if you have multiple Retained Earnings accounts, then contact support for appropriate instructions.
- Get into the correct company.
-  Make sure the current fiscal year is the year whose opening balances are going to be adjusted.  If you are closing an old year into a new year, you need to be in the new year.  The current fiscal year displays at the bottom left hand corner of the screen.  If it needs to be changed, this can be done so by either double clicking the Fiscal Year cell at the bottom left hand corner of the screen, or by going to General Ledger -> Periodic Processing -> Change Fiscal Year.
- Open the Update Current Year screen by going to General Ledger -> Periodic Processing -> Update Current Year.
- When the screen appears, put a check in the checkbox at the top of the screen confirming that a backup has been made.
- At the bottom of the screen leave the checkbox labeled “Clear unclosed income…” blank.  Put a check in the box labeled “Consolidate unclosed income…”
- In the field labeled “Retained Earnings Account” fill in your retained earnings account.
- Press the button at the top left hand corner of the screen labeled “Ok” to start the process.
- When the process completes a message will appear stating the update has completed successfully.  Press “Okay” to close that message.
- A preview of a report will appear.  This report can be printed, but it is optional.  Close the report.
- The beginning balances of the new year should now be updated.  This can be confirmed by running financial statements, or the Activity Report for period one in the new year, or by running a Trial Balance for period zero in the new year.

70a385ea-80c5-43ea-b683-4438aa4f462e.title: Reprint Misprinted Payroll Check
70a385ea-80c5-43ea-b683-4438aa4f462e.content:
Problem
A payroll check has been printed and somehow gotten messed up, and now needs to be reprinted.

Cause
Error when printing checks.

Resolution
Instructions for reprinting a check for an Hourly Employee:  (See instructions for Salaried Employees below.)

First, void the misprinted check at Payroll > Payday Work > Void Checks. Select the filter as the check date and click on Apply.  The Fiscal Period/ Year and Void to Payroll Tax Month should be the date and month when you have posted the check.
Ensure that when you void the check, the box is checked for "Create transaction from history."
Select the check box for the check you want to void, and click "Write"

For further instructions as to how to void a check see the Knowledge Base Article "How to Find and Void a Check"

Once the check has been voided, because the box was checked to create the transaction from history, the transaction for that check will appear again for hourly employees in particular.

It will then need to be processed through the typical posting and printing process:

Go to Payroll --> Daily Work --> Payroll Transactions
Select the Employee ID for the employee whose check needs to be reprinted. Work with the payroll client to ensure the hours, deductions, and employer costs are correct.
Save.

Next, go to PA --> Daily Work --> Time Ticket Journal to see what Transactions are set to post. You should see the transaction for the employee there.
Then Post the transaction under PA --> Daily Work --> Post Transactions

Next, go to PA --> Payday Work --> Calculate Checks
Click the "Reset" Button.
It is alright for the Payroll Number to be the number after the Payroll they just posted and printed (that the misprinted check was printed with).
The "Include Salary Wages" checkbox needs to be unchecked, otherwise all salaried people will get checks in this check run as well.
Ensure that the Quarter, Period End, and Transaction Cutoff Date, and Fiscal Year reflect the pay period the check should be printed in, rather than the current date.
Check the box for the Group that the Employee is in (You can find that on the PA Payroll Transaction screen if you're not sure.) Select the Period Start date for the payroll that the check was run in, rather than the current date.
Choose whatever Pay Code was used in the original check, to ensure correct deductions are taken out - otherwise you may get incorrect deductions taken.
Click "OK".

Next, you can go to PA --> Payday Work --> Edit Register. Click Preview to see what checks are set to print.  You should be able to see the check you want to print there, as well as what other checks are set to print.

Finally, go to PA --> Payday Work --> Print Checks to print the check.
Work with the Payroll client to ensure the settings are correct for the check - check number, leave codes, etc. Preview the check if you would like to ensure it looks correct.  Then Print.

Salaried Employees:

Void the misprinted check at Payroll > Payday Work > Void Checks.  See instructions regarding voiding checks above or check the Knowledge Base Article "How to Find and Void a Check."

Next, you will need to move the employee into their own private Pay Group in order to calculate salaries for just that group and just that employee, and then move them back once you are finished to reprint their check. This is because when recalculating checks you will need to check the "Include Salary Wages" checkbox which will result in ALL employees in that group who are salaried to get a paycheck.

If you need to find what Pay Groups are currently in use so as to choose an empty group, go to:
PA --> Interactive Views --> Employee Information View.
Right click in the header to get the column chooser. Select the "Group" code to display that column. Note which Groups are not in use.

Next, go to PA --> Setup and Maintenance --> Employee Information
Find the employee, select the Pay tab,
Make a note of what their current Group is so as to remember what to change it back to.
Change their Group code to a group not currently in use and Save.

Salaried employees will likely have no work that needs to be processed on the Transaction screen.  However, check whether they have some vacation hours or other transaction to process:
Go to Payroll --> Daily Work --> Payroll Transactions
Select the Employee ID for the employee whose check needs to be reprinted.
If a transaction comes up for them, work with the payroll client to ensure the hours, deductions, and employer costs are correct.
Save.
Print the Miscellaneous Deductions Journal and Post.

Next, go to PA --> Payday Work --> Calculate Checks
Click the "Reset" Button.
It is alright for the Payroll Number to be the number after the Payroll they just posted and printed (that the misprinted check was printed with).
The "Include Salary Wages" checkbox needs to be checked.
Ensure that the Quarter, Period End, and Transaction Cutoff Date, and Fiscal Year reflect the pay period the check should be printed in, rather than the current date.
Check the box for the Group you put the Employee in only.
Select the Period Start date for the payroll that the check was run in, rather than the current date.
Choose whatever Pay Code was used in the original check, to ensure correct deductions are taken out.
Click "OK".

Next, you can go to PA --> Payday Work --> Edit Register. Click Preview to see what checks are set to print.  You should be able to see the check you want to print there, as well as what other checks are set to print.

Go to PA --> Payday Work --> Print Checks to print the check.
Work with the Payroll client to ensure the settings are correct for the check - check number, leave codes, etc. Preview the check if you would like to ensure it looks correct.  Then Print.

Finally go back to PA --> Setup and Maintenance --> Employee Information.  Change the Employee Group Code back to the group you noted earlier.

4eb87f13-c7c2-468b-8f9d-64974d3ac879.title: How to Stop Sending Zero Dollar Invoices
4eb87f13-c7c2-468b-8f9d-64974d3ac879.content:
Problem
User would like to avoid sending Sales Order 0$ Invoices.

Cause
Traverse offers the solution to the problem, by disabling the auto send feature available and allowing user to manually review the invoice before being sent. However Traverse does not have an algorithm or a notification feature which could identify the zero dollar invoice.

Resolution
Step 1: Stopping all of the Sales Order Invoices being sent

Under System Manager > Document Delivery > Document Settings
1. Use the Form ID drop down and select Sales Order
2. Uncheck the Auto Send
3. Click on Save
4. Since we have cleared the Auto Send check box. The system will not deliver any documents immediately.

Image Description: SM Document Settings

Step 2: Selecting the Sales Order Invoices to be sent
Go to: System Manager --> Document Delivery --> Manage Queue
Click Apply Filter (can filter Document Type for  Sales Order) to see the list of invoices waiting to be sent.

Image Description: SM Manage Queue

Alternatively, you may be able to see the list this way:
Under Sales Order > Transaction > SO Orders
When you print a SO Order invoice setup to send via email, a Print Status window will appear:


Image Description: Print Status

When you close the Print Status window, the Document Queue screen will display showing all documents currently in the queue.

For documents that include Zero Dollar as the invoice value and you do not intend to share, select the documents from Document Queue and click on Mark as Sent from toolbar.
For documents that you intend to share, Select the documents from Document Queue and click on Send button on the toolbar.

Image Description: Document Queue

If the user wants to resend invoices automatically again, they should go to System Manager > Document Delivery > Document Settings and recheck the Auto Send box to continue sending invoices automatically.

3134ba59-f8d9-4652-a009-89cfc43dd7cd.title: Locked Bank Account or Transaction
3134ba59-f8d9-4652-a009-89cfc43dd7cd.content:
Problem
When processing, posting, and printing reports in the Bank Reconciliation module a message may appear stating either than a Bank Account is locked or a Transaction is locked, and the user will be prevented from performing a task.

Resolution
Messages about a locked bank or a locked transaction occurs when TRAVERSE notes that a transaction lock has been placed on a transaction in a bank account.  This happens when a user goes in and either enters a new transaction or edits and existing transaction and then either remains on the screen without closing, or perhaps exits the screen due to an error or the computer shutting down.

When this happens, the lock record remains on, and TRAVERSE prevents further processing on either that Bank Account or the Transaction until the lock is released.  The view the locks records and to get them removed follow these instructions.
- Get into Bank Reconciliation -> Setup and Maintenance -> Bank Activity.
- The screen will list entries for all the lock records, and will include information about who the user is that created it, the transaction, and that date the lock was created.
- Check with the user to see if they are in fact currently entering and editing the transaction.  If so, have them complete their data entry and exit the screen, and the lock will release.
- If the user is not currently in Bank Reconciliation and editing the transaction then the lock record is displaying in error.  It can be removed by highlighting the record and hitting the Delete key at the bottom of the screen.
- Once the lock record has been removed by either method the Bank Account and Transaction will be unlocked and processing can continue.

06a7d930-a7b9-43f3-a11c-add2c8701c47.title: How to display Lookups in report and view filters
06a7d930-a7b9-43f3-a11c-add2c8701c47.content:
Problem
When running a report or an interactive view, and the user is trying to create a filter based on a masterfile id such as a vendor id, customer id, inventory id, etc, the screen does not allow a lookup on the id.

Resolution
To resolve this issue you need to make a change in the preferences.
- Log in to TRAVERSE, and then on the toolbar menu at the top choose View -> Preferences.
- When the Preferences screen appears look for the setting that is labeled "Display Lookups in Filters."
- By default when a TRAVERSE client is installed that setting is set to FALSE.
- Change the setting to TRUE.
- The user will not be able to utilize lookups in report and view filters.
- This setting is specific to individual computers.  If other users on other computers need this setting changed they will need to do it on their individual computer as well.

81afb344-8822-4f5e-bc04-0adee65911c2.title: GL Year End Closing
81afb344-8822-4f5e-bc04-0adee65911c2.content:
Problem
GL Year End Closing

Resolution
1. Setup a new year
2. Do a small audit of the accounts before updating to a new year
3. Change the Fiscal Year
4. Post all transactions to master
5. Update Current Year
6. Verify through the Trial Balance Report

1. Setup a new year
To create a new year, go to System Manager->Company Setup->Period Conversion.
Enter the new year in the 'Fiscal Year' tab and hit Tab.
Enabling the checkbox for 'Copy Previous Year values' in the 'Auto Fill' dialog box copies the beginning and the end dates of the previous year to the new year.
* A recommended step while there: close the last few periods of the new year to prevent accidental edits into the wrong year while still going back and forth between years.

2. Do a small audit of the accounts before rolling balances over into the new year
There are two ways to audit:

A. Go to GL –> Master List à Chart of Accounts List
Leave Data Filter empty
Check “View Clear/Consolidate Accounts”
Click Preview: will show the chart of accounts and the types of information to audit.

B. Alternatively, go to GL->Interactive Views->Simple Chart of Accounts View.
Right click on the Table Header, click on "Column Chooser"; and add the "Account Type" and "Clear-to-Account" column in the table if they are not there.
Click "Apply Filter".

Review the accounts, looking for errors in the Account Type and the Clear-to-Account column:
There are two types of accounts
-  0 - 499:   Balance Sheet Accounts (Roll into the next year as the same account)
- 500 and above: Income Statement (All these accounts roll into Earnings and revenue account
Look for accounts with the wrong type (ex. high Account ID numbers with low account type or vice versa) or with an Account Type over 500 with a missing Clear-to-Account.
* See the Update Current Year step for further clarification. The Clear-to-Account in particular needs to be correctly specified if running the process checking the first box, and the Account Type must be correct if running the process checking the second box.

To correct the account type or clear-to-account, go to GL -> Setup and Maintenance -> Chart of Accounts and change the account type or add a Clear-to-Account in the bottom of the screen. Select the step it will roll over if running the "GL Clear and Close last Year" process. Choose Step 1 unless the company rolls balances over in a multi-step process.

Note: You can change the type from one debit to another debit account and one credit to another credit account but can't change the type from debit to a credit or vice-versa.
In order to fix this error, it is a more complicated change. (Done by special services)

3. Change the Fiscal Year
Make sure that the Fiscal year is in the year you'd like to post a transaction in.
(Double click 'Fiscal Year' in the bottom left / GL-> Periodic Processing-> Change Fiscal Year and change the year)
The checkbox for 'This session only' is turned on when the GL person is moving back and forth between years. It defaults back to the previously set year once Traverse is closed and reopened. Once the checkbox is turned off, all the users will now be in the newly changed fiscal year once they log back in.


Note: Only GL operations require the Fiscal year to match the current date. Other modules like AR, AP, etc., don't reference this Fiscal Year. It directly creates a transaction to the current date by default.
You can see this by going to GL Transactions and adding the 'Year' column from Column chooser.

4. Post all transactions to the master
Preview the unposted transactions for the fiscal year you are closing, go to GL->Transaction Journals->GL Journal. If everything looks good, then you are ready to post.

Now, post all the transactions to Master for the year which is getting closed in GL->Transaction Journals->Post to Master. Click "Apply Filter" to bring up the periods which need posting. Select all the checkboxes for that Fiscal Year under Period List and click on 'OK'.

5. GL --> Periodic Processing --> Update current year
When finishing up the previous year, anything entered in the old year will update the old year’s balances, but they will not automatically update to the new year. Anytime the old year’s balances are updated, someone will need to run this to update the balances into the new year.

Check the box which says, "Do the following, then check the box"
"Unclosed Income (Loss) Accounts Balance" - Ensure the Year is correct. This shows the sum of all of the accounts in your income statement or revenue and expenses.
Never click on both the checkboxes under Unclosed Income Accounts Balance (<previous year>). It will cause a lot of confusion.  See further instructions below regarding which box to check.

(i) Checking the first checkbox (Clear unclosed income (loss) accounts to retained earnings)
- Not the commonly used method

This means that GL checks all accounts under GL simple chart of accounts view to see if it has a 'Clear to account'
- If it doesn't, it rolls the balance forward into the next year into that account itself
- If it does have a 'Clear To' account, it rolls the balance over into that specified 'Clear To' account.

-This method will work correctly if the 'Clear To' account description is set up correctly for all the retained earnings accounts.
-The purpose for using this method is when you roll certain income statement accounts to one retained earnings account and some others to a second, third, etc retained account.

(ii) Checking the second checkbox (Consolidate unclosed income (loss) accounts to retained earnings)
-The commonly used method.

You'd have to enter a Retained Earnings account number in the drop-down box for all the income statements accounts to be rolled over into this account.
This means that GL checks all accounts under GL simple chart of accounts view and checks it by the 'Account Type ID'
- If it is a Balance Sheet Account, (i.e.<500), it rolls the balance into the next year into that account
- If it is a Income Statement Account, (i.e.>500) it rolls the balance into that specified 'Clear To' account.

-This method will work correctly if the 'Account Type ID' is set up correctly for all the accounts.
-The purpose for using this method is when you roll all income statement accounts into one retained earnings account.



Click 'OK' to update current year.

This can be run again if the previous year balances are edited again.

6. Verify through the Trial Balance Report.

Go to GL->Management Reports->Trial Balance Report-Set it to period 0 of the year->Preview
It can be noticed that all the accounts are now rolled over into the new year.

Close periods for the year in SM Period Conversions to be completely done with the year.

3f5156a4-278a-4598-a37e-8e153f76b219.title: Period Closed Error
3f5156a4-278a-4598-a37e-8e153f76b219.content:
Problem
A batch cannot be posted.  When trying to post a message appears saying "The following periods are closed..." and then one or more fiscal periods and years are listed.

Resolution
This happens because the period has been closed in the Period Conversion. Open the closed Period in the period conversion and post the transactions.

System Manager -> Company Setup -> Period Conversion
Select the period in which you want to post the transaction.
Uncheck the box for the appropriate Period from the right column (Close).  Then you can go back and post.

77250668-f472-4ddf-8bb8-2a31bec7e3f5.title: How to Find and Void a Check
77250668-f472-4ddf-8bb8-2a31bec7e3f5.content:
Problem
The user would like to find and void a Payroll check.

Resolution
If you need to find the check:

Step 1: Go to Payroll > Interactive Views > Check History View. Select the filter Payroll Year and Check Date. To get a wider period of time, you could choose the filter Check Date "Is Between"  and two dates, or filter by Payroll Month.

If you don't see the columns for Payroll Month and Check Date, right-click on the Header Titles, click on Column Chooser, and drag and drop the Payroll Month and Check Date into the Header. See the attached sample screenshots.

From this view you will be able to view if and when the check has been posted. If the check has been posted in error, you can void the checks.

**Voiding a check in a previous pay period, especially a previous quarter, may cause imbalances in the General Ledger.  If so, proceed with caution, as adjustments may need to be made in the General Ledger as well.

Step 2: For voiding the checks. Go to Payroll > Payday Work > Void Checks. Select the filter as the check date and click on Apply.

Note: The Fiscal Period/ Year and Void to Payroll Tax Month should be the date and month when you have posted the check.

Step 3: Then select the Void check box of the check, which you need to void, and click on Write.

A dialog box will appear. Click on Ok.

The check will be voided.

To verify the check has been voided: Go to Payroll > Daily Work > Payroll Transactions. Select the respective Employee ID. The check, which has been voided, will appear there.

37aedb56-4ae8-4cff-b91e-21cb0286fcde.title: Create Sample Company Database
37aedb56-4ae8-4cff-b91e-21cb0286fcde.content:
Problem
Need to Create Sample Company Database

Resolution
How to create the sample company:

Login to Traverse Server Manager (Global for Global)

Download the sample company templates first.  Go to Help: Get Latest Templates:

You should see File Names such as Data_SAM.tsmx  and Template.tsmx.  Click "Download."  Once the Download is complete, close out the box.

Then, create a new database. Right click on TRAVERSE and choose New Database (not Add Company – see notes at end of section).

The New Company Database screen appears.

Enter the Name and Description and verify the Template Folder path is correct. (Open up File Explorer - ensure user has permissions to the folder pointed to in the path. If they don't, they will need to get them to continue.) To create a sample company, click on the Copy Data tab and choose Data From: Sample Data.



Verify the data path is correct on the options tab, and that the Currency is correct on the Advanced Options tab.

Once all the settings are correct, click OK to create the database.
Once the company databases are created, you need to add them to the master login file. Right Click on Security in Server Manager and choose Master Login.

Verify all of the databases are selected and click Update.

Once the Database is setup, you will need to create Users and Groups so that you can access TRAVERSE via the client. To create a new user, right click on Security in Server Manager and choose New Login.

The User screen appears.

Enter the User name and password if not using the Is Trusted option.
If you want to use the Is Trusted option, type in the login name of the Windows domain user you wish to add. (It may be in the drop down. If not, go to Start menu à User à “Change Account Settings” to find the Domain and User name (after the slash) there ).  If using this option, you do not need to specify a password. Do not enter the domain\user name, only the Windows user name is required.

Check the Is Active checkbox to allow this user login access to TRAVERSE. Check the company databases and Groups that this user will have access to.
Click Apply to apply the changes, and OK to close the User screen.

Once the user is setup, you will need to create new groups and assign the user to their group with the appropriate menu permissions.

To create a group, expand the company database (ie. CPU)  within Server Manager, right click on Groups\Roles and choose New Group.

The Group screen appears.

Enter the Group Name and check the users that will be part of this group. Click
Apply to apply the changes.

After you click Apply, the Permissions button should become active. Click on this

to bring up the Menu Security Screen.

NOTE: You may not see any applications initially. You may need to setup the License Server and register your product ID before those applications will become available. If you do not see the menus, install License Manager, and then setup the group security.

The Menu Security Screen appears.

Check the menu permissions for the group, click Apply to apply the changes and
OK to close.
Click Apply and OK again to close the Group box.

The Sample Database should be installed!  Open up Traverse with the login you set up, select the sample company from the list, and verify that it is functional.

You will likely need to set up the Current Period year.  If this error pops up you do.



Go to System Manager --> Company Setup --> Period Conversion to set it up.

Place cursor in the Fiscal Year box, and type in each year that needs to be set up: 2020, 2021, etc.  Tab over. This box will come up. Select "Yes".


You can then choose to either copy values from the previous year or not. Select OK.

Click Save, and the years will be set up.  The Sample Company is set up!

ADDITIONAL NOTES:

•    There is an option within Server Manager to Add Company when right clicking on TRAVERSE. This is not to be confused with New Database option. Use the New Database option to create blank databases, to copy from an existing database or to create the sample company.  You would use the Add Company option to add existing databases to the TSM security database, for example.

88bc94cd-cc34-4dfd-8289-137dbb526238.title: Cannot Print Traverse Form
88bc94cd-cc34-4dfd-8289-137dbb526238.content:
Problem
Forms such as Sales Order Picking Slips are not printing to the Printer, but the Printer works for the computer in general.

Resolution
First, check to see what the Business Rules settings are for the application related to the form they are printing.  For Sales Order, Plain Paper Packing Lists and Packing Slips should be set to Yes.  If the Form they are using is in a different Application, check the Rules for that application. Ex. AR --> Miscellaneous --> Plain Paper Invoices and other such settings.  If there is an issue here, change the setting and test printing.  If everything is already set to print to paper, go on to the next step.

In Traverse, Go to:
System Manager --> Company Setup --> Form Printers and check to see what Printer is installed.

Ensure that the Form that they want to print from has been set up and is checked as Active.  If it is there but not Active, check the box to activate it.  If the form is not set up, select the correct form from the dropdown, select the printer from the dropdown, select which Tray it should pull from from the dropdown, and ensure that it is Active.

To know which printer to select:

Verify which printer their computer is using in the Computer Settings --> Devices --> Printers to see which Printer they have set up.  You can also test printing out a paper from their workstation if that is working (Word Doc or a PDF) and check which printer they are using for that.

Once you have set up the settings here, test printing out a form.

If there are still issues printing, you may not have the correct settings for the Printer.  If they are using a Printer over a network, you may need to get the network information for the printer and put the correct path in to get the printer working. This may be the case if the employee is accessing Traverse remotely through an RDP or virtual machine.

6a4b396b-f156-4f02-9514-ed610a2fa91b.title: View Direct Deposit Account Information
6a4b396b-f156-4f02-9514-ed610a2fa91b.content:
Problem
Under Traverse Standard/Global > Payroll > Master Lists > Employee Direct Deposit Information List > Output/Preview. The Account Number appears as masked. We would want the complete Account Number and Routing Code information.

Cause
Banking Business Rules

Resolution
This is because the Banking Business Rules are set to either Account Number to be completely or partially masked. Hence, this issue can be resolved by navigating to Traverse Standard/Global > System Manager > Company Setup > Business Rules > Banking > Set the Payment Information Display to All

Apply > OK

The Business Rules changes are saved, and you can find the complete Account Number and Routing Code information for the Employee Direct Deposit Information List report.

933c7bf6-5e7e-4bc9-bb4c-ff5537fd8819.title: Enter New Fiscal Year
933c7bf6-5e7e-4bc9-bb4c-ff5537fd8819.content:
Problem
New Fiscal Year needs to be created.

Resolution
You must create a new Fiscal Year in order to have periods in which to create a post transactions.  To create a new Fiscal Year you will need to perform the following steps.
- Open System Manager -> Company Setup - Period Conversion.
- When the screen opens it may display a message saying the fiscal year has not been set up.  If this occurs simply close the message and continue.
- When the Period Conversion screen appears it will either be blank, or it will be displaying the most recent fiscal year.  Either way, put the cursor in the Year field at the top and type in the new Fiscal Year you are creating.  It the field is currently displaying an older fiscal year then type over that year.  Press Tab.
- You will receive the following message.  Press Enter.
-
- Next, the following screen will display.  You can either turn on the checkbox for "Copy Previous Year Values" if you wish for the period end and begin dates to match the dates from the previous year, or you can specify the Starting Date of the first day of the first period and let the system calculate the period begin and end dates.  Once you have made either choice you can click the OK button to create the year.
-
- The screen when then display the newly created fiscal year along with the period begin and end dates.  Make changes to the beginning and end dates for the periods of necessary, and when done click the Save button in the top left hand corner of the screen.
- The new fiscal year is now created and saved, and you may begin posting transactions to it.

3b5256b9-bbe3-4249-a0d8-fa16f2992ef5.title: Resolving Negative Quantity On Hand and Cost in Traverse
3b5256b9-bbe3-4249-a0d8-fa16f2992ef5.content: This article provides a step-by-step guide to resolving negative quantity on hand and cost values in Traverse after a physical inventory count. The issue may arise due to incorrect inventory count entries or misconfiguration of the Warehouse Management Module. To resolve the issue, follow these steps: 1. Review the recent physical inventory count entries for accuracy. 2. Verify the Warehouse Management Module configuration for correct cost and quantity calculations. 3. Reconcile any discrepancies found in the inventory count entries and module configuration. By following these steps, engineers can identify and correct the root cause of the issue, preventing future occurrences.
